author.name: Yifan Tang, Jingran Li, Yihao Wang, Zhen Yang, Jianyi Liu, Gongshen Liu, Ru Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Context Perturbation Discrepancy (CPD), a zero-shot AI-text detector that scores each token's log-probability gain relative to what a pretrained model expects when conditioning is restricted from full prefix to a short recent window, with an analytical standard-deviation normalization. On unedited human and AI texts from benchmarks including GEN and DetectRL-X, CPD improves detection over fixed-context likelihood baselines. The approach requires no access to the generator model.

entry.title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation

author.name: Nadav Magar, Amir Hertz, Ariel Shamir, Or Patashnik

entry.summary: BriConstrain is a constrained decoding method that steers a pretrained language model toward valid LEGO brick placements by modifying next-token probabilities before sampling, instead of rejecting and resampling invalid outputs. Because placement validity depends on the evolving build state, the authors develop dynamic geometric validity checks rather than compiling a fixed grammar. The work demonstrates a general recipe for grounding autoregressive generation in physical/geometric constraints.

entry.title: GeoMVGen: Joint Appearance-Geometry Modeling for Multi-View Video Generation in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Qiaoqiao Jia, Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: GeoMVGen jointly models visual appearance and scene geometry for multi-view video generation in robotic manipulation, aiming for temporally coherent, cross-view-consistent predictions under varying robot actions and camera configurations. It addresses the gap between video generation priors and explicit geometric modeling.

entry.title: Visual Thinking: Training-Free Active Perception for Counting and Localizing Hard-to-Find Objects

author.name: Emil Kielar, Pratik Chaudhari

entry.summary: Introduces Visual Thinking, a training-free framework combining a vision-language model with SAM 3 in an iterative active-perception loop for counting and localizing small, occluded, or poorly described objects. The VLM proposes candidate noun phrases from image crops and iteration history, and a controller ranks and refines them across steps.

entry.title: Instant LiDAR: Feed-Forward Gaussian Reconstruction for LiDAR Simulation

author.name: Xin Kang, Jiahui Huang, Jiawei Ren, Sipeng Zhang, Yu Chen, Weihua Zhang, Junjie Lai

entry.summary: Introduces Instant LiDAR, a feed-forward pipeline that reconstructs multiple LiDAR scans as reusable Gaussian assets in minutes without per-scene optimization, enabling scalable closed-loop autonomous driving simulation. It handles nonuniform sampling and limited field of view through measurement-anchored Gaussian prediction, sampling-aware scales, and multi-scan merging.

entry.title: Rethinking Post-Training Quantization for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seoyoung Cho, Junhee Lee, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why post-training quantization degrades large vision-language models at low bit widths, showing that a few outliers dominate shared per-channel weight and per-token activation ranges, pushing most values to zero. Based on this diagnosis, it shifts focus from calibration refinement to addressing outlier-driven range sharing. This offers a principled path to better low-bit LVLM compression.

entry.title: Video Models are Excellent Motion Models

author.name: Kian Izadpanah, Ali Mahdavi Amiri, Daniel Cohen-Or, Yiorgos Chrysanthou, Andreas Aristidou

entry.summary: This position paper argues that video foundation models have become superior motion generators, with richer and more general motion priors than dedicated motion models, evidenced by motion naturalness and motion scope including uncommon, complex, compound actions. The authors support the claim through systematic analysis of video models as motion generators.

entry.title: COHERE4D: Training-Free Dense Surface Alignment for Coherent Metric 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Zhumei Wang, Shaofei Wang, Xiang An, Mingtao Pei, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: COHERE4D combines human and scene foundation models for monocular 4D reconstruction by directly registering the shared human surface they both predict, without training. This exploits the observation that human models give metric-scale body meshes while scene models give globally consistent geometry, using the overlapping surface as the alignment cue.

entry.title: TokenMatte: Unlocking T2V Diffusion Priors for Pixel-Native Video Matting

author.name: Zanyi Wang, Dengyang Jiang, Fengfei Yu, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: TokenMatte adapts a pretrained text-to-video diffusion transformer into a single-pass RGB-to-alpha predictor for high-resolution video matting, bypassing the usual RGB-trained VAE latent interface that attenuates fine details. Its core is a shared linear readout mapping each spatio-temporal token directly to its corresponding alpha patch, preserving hair-level detail and soft boundaries without auxiliary supervision.

entry.title: MemAnchorWorld: A Sparse World Model with Horizon-Conditioned Memory Retrieval for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xinyang Jia, Yuqi Zhang, Jiakai Wang, Yahu Yang, Guandong Pan, Chao Tong, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: MemAnchorWorld is a sparse world model for 4D semantic occupancy forecasting that explicitly retrieves relevant historical geometric and semantic evidence instead of relying on implicit scene-state memory. Inspired by the von Restorff effect, its horizon-conditioned memory retrieval reduces the error accumulation that degrades long-horizon forecasting in existing sparse world models.

entry.title: OmniHarness-RSI: Modality-Aware Harness Evolution for Omnimodal Understanding

author.name: Shilin Ma, Xingming Shui, Jinglin Chen, Zetong Zhao, Jingqi Tian, Deyi Zhu, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes OmniHarness-RSI, a framework that evolves executable agent harnesses for omnimodal understanding without updating foundation model weights, factorizing the evolution space into modality routing and collaboration, evidence localization, and modality-specific perception. Extends harness-based recursive self-improvement from video to general multimodal settings.

entry.title: RePix-VFI: Re-rendering Observed Pixels for Video Frame Interpolation with Generative Priors from One-Step Diffusion

author.name: Dayeon Kim, Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: RePix-VFI couples draft-conditioned one-step video diffusion with reconstruction from observed keyframes for multi-frame video frame interpolation, refining a flow-rendered draft with a pretrained video diffusion model while preserving observed textures. Balances flow-based texture fidelity against diffusion-based plausibility at much lower sampling cost.

entry.title: Support2Sim: Visually Faithful Real2Sim with Stable Object Supports

author.name: Samarth Chopra, Ankit Prabhu, Akshayan Nagarajah, Sumer Murthy, Pratik Chaudhari, Vijay Kumar

entry.summary: Support2Sim reconstructs simulation-ready scenes from a single RGB image by inferring support relationships between objects and using a contact-guided pose initializer plus coarse-to-fine physics-informed refinement. It optimizes for source fidelity, support realization, and physical stability within a practical time budget. This advances Real2Sim pipelines needed for sim-based robot training.

entry.title: Embodied Neuro-symbolic AI: Making Robot Behavior Auditable, Safe, and Scalable

author.name: Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Jonathan Francis, Alessandro Oltramari

entry.summary: Argues that end-to-end vision-language-action systems face brittle generalization, weak causal reasoning, and limited auditability in safety-critical settings, and proposes an embodied neuro-symbolic approach combining learned components with symbolic constraints on prohibited behaviors. The framework aims to make robot behavior auditable, safe, and scalable beyond controlled demonstrations.

entry.title: MRCT: An Object-Centric Two-Layer Control Architecture for Heavy-Payload Multi-Robot Transportation

author.name: Ning Wang, Yoshihiko Nakamura, Tianwei Zhang

entry.summary: MRCT coordinates heterogeneous mobile manipulators transporting heavy payloads via a two-layer architecture: object-level MPC generates coordinated contact-force references, and robot-level whole-body impedance control realizes them through confidence-based blending of velocity-tracking and impedance torques. The blending increases compliance when tracking degrades.

entry.title: Misguided power-seeking

author.name: Brad Taylor

entry.summary: Argues that AI risk scenarios should consider non-rational power-seeking: persona selection and RL can instill non-instrumental power-seeking tendencies, which combined with jagged intelligence (strong verifiable-task performance but poor instrumental judgment) could drive models to execute dangerous actions in doomed power-seeking plans. The author sketches three scenarios and argues this creates a vulnerability window earlier than canonical rational power-seeking, recommending greater focus on option control.

entry.title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents

author.name: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li, Zhixiang Lu, Haolin Yang, Jianxu Chen, Yifan Lu, Di Fan, Yutong Xie

entry.summary: SpatialCraft is a self-evolving framework for tool-using spatial reasoning agents that improves orchestration of 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation tools from its own interaction history without parameter updates. It maintains two forms of external knowledge: distilled condition-action tactics (Experiences) and reusable skills, contrasting rollouts to learn when and how to call tools.

entry.title: PatientFlowSynth: Evaluating FHIR Agents with Matched Patient Charts

author.name: Anthony Cuturrufo, Ratul Ghosh, Devashish Khatwani, Krishnaram Kenthapadi

entry.summary: This paper introduces PatientFlowSynth, a benchmark of 18,000 tasks built from 225 synthetic patients and 18 templates for evaluating agents that search FHIR patient charts and classify claims under varying evidence conditions, including missing or conflicting records. Each task variant is verified by re-executing the retrieval program, and success requires correct labels and citations matching an accepted evidence set.

entry.title: E2SIM: Long-Horizon Simulation of Everyday Human Behavior with Evolving States

author.name: Ziwei Gong, Xiangyang Yin, Thai Quoc On, Lin Ai, Julia Hirschberg, Haotong Yang

entry.summary: E2SIM is a longitudinal user simulation framework that jointly models how individual actor states (goals, interests, activities) evolve over time alongside a dynamic shared environment. A feedback loop connects immediate actions, delayed outcomes, and actor-specific observations, keeping simulated behavior consistent over long horizons. This matters for building AI assistants that maintain accurate user models across weeks or months of interaction.

entry.title: Stranded Compute in AI Inference Workloads: Recovering Value Through Demand Aggregation

author.name: Sam Kingsley

entry.summary: This paper reframes AI inference infrastructure economics as a capital problem rather than an energy problem, showing that in the modeled reference deployment capital recovery accounts for 87.3% of fully loaded cost per token versus only 3.7% for electricity. The author decomposes a 40.4 percentage-point loss chain between nameplate throughput and SLO-qualified goodput (59.6%), attributing 25.2 points to scheduling idleness and stranded burst reserve — inefficiencies inherent to an individual tenant's demand portfolio that cannot be diversified alone. The paper proposes demand aggregation as a mechanism to recover this stranded compute value.

entry.title: DexOPD: Dual-Extrapolation On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models

author.name: Yunchao Ke, Yanzhe Hu, Yi Yang, Jiachun Jin, Zhihong Liu, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: DexOPD improves multi-teacher on-policy distillation for flow-based text-to-image diffusion models by exploiting the student's own training progress in constructing extrapolated proxy teachers, whereas prior methods define extrapolation solely from frozen teacher and reference models. This dual extrapolation lets distilled students surpass the original specialist models more effectively.

entry.title: A Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Official Statistics

author.name: Lucas Lageweg, Karen Goes, Tom van den Broek, Frank Pijpers, Paul Groth, Jan-Christoph Kalo

entry.summary: LOCuST is a text-to-SQL benchmark pairing over two thousand English and Dutch tables from Statistics Netherlands with questions, designed to reflect the open-domain catalog setting of official statistics: thousands of wide tables with coded columns and values whose meaning lives in separate metadata rather than a relational schema. It fills a real gap since existing text-to-SQL benchmarks assume cleaner schema-aligned settings. It matters for making critical public datasets accessible to policymakers and businesses through question-answering systems.

entry.title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges

author.name: Hamin Koo, Chanjoo Jung, Fangzhao Wu, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: HUB-J is an integrated framework that uses human-derived bias factors to detect, quantify, and mitigate systematic biases in LLM-as-a-Judge systems, addressing gaps in prior work that relies on pre-discovered bias lists, ignores bias strength, and uses costly interventions. The approach leverages human preference data to inform which biases matter and how strongly, then targets mitigation accordingly. This strengthens the reliability of LLM judges that increasingly sit inside evaluation and training loops.

entry.title: SoundWeaver: Compositional Warm-Starting for Text-to-Audio Diffusion Serving

author.name: Ayush Barik, Sofia Stoica, Nikhil Sarda, Arnav Kethana, Abhinav Khanduja, Muchen Xu, Fan Lai

entry.summary: SoundWeaver is the first training-free framework for compositional cross-example acoustic reuse in text-to-audio diffusion, constructing a prompt-conditioned acoustic prior from segments of cached audios and warm-starting diffusion from an intermediate noise level. An Acoustic Composition Graph built on codec representations and segment identification reduces required neural function evaluations and serving latency.

entry.title: Instantiation of Human Values in Image Generation

author.name: Maria-Teresa De Rosa Palmini, Piera Riccio, Noa Garcia, Eva Cetinic

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework, grounded in Schwartz's theory of basic human values, for studying how text-to-image models visually realize abstract human values such as success, care, and freedom. The authors generate 28,000 images across four state-of-the-art T2I models using prompts derived from 70 positive and negative value items, then identify recurring visual prototypes to quantify how narrowly models instantiate values compared to human descriptions. This matters because T2I systems are increasingly embedded in everyday visual culture, and understanding their implicit value representations has implications for fairness, bias, and cultural alignment.

entry.title: Does Item Response Theory Generalize Across Languages? Evidence from Cross-Lingual LLM Benchmarks

author.name: Ruchira Dhar, Qiwei Peng, Anders S{\o}gaard

entry.summary: The authors test whether Item Response Theory parameters generalize when the same benchmark is translated across languages, fitting 1PL-3PL models per language on Multilingual GSM and Global MMLU with over 100 models and 11 languages. Item difficulty proves the most stable parameter, followed by guessing and discrimination, and differential item analysis traces instability to specific items shifting under translation.

entry.title: Evolutionary AI Control: Population-Level Safety Under Reproduction, Heredity, and Selection

author.name: Andrew T. Cadotte

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that AI agents satisfying individual safety checks can still produce populations violating collective safety limits when agents copy themselves, modify successors, and are subject to selection. The authors prove conditions under which safety guarantees persist through reproduction, heredity, and selection, and present four counterexamples illustrating failure modes such as unrestricted self-copying leading to unbounded growth.

entry.title: Reproducible Social Structure Emerges From Free-Form Interaction Among LLM Agents

author.name: Tom Alisch, Sonia Murthy, Robert Hawkins, Felix Sosa, Core Francisco Park

entry.summary: The paper introduces a repeatable, goal-free multi-agent framework where fifty persona-conditioned LLM agents with persistent memory choose whether, with whom, and how to communicate across three social platforms, run ten times from identical conditions for 700 total hours. It addresses the anecdotal single-run problem in LLM social simulations, finding that most measured network structures are reproducible rather than random artifacts.

entry.title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction

author.name: Ian Miao, Fangrui Zhu, Bowen Jiang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a subtle failure mode in conversational assistants that compress older messages into notes: when a note is written in a language with grammatical distinctions English lacks (e.g., Spanish adjective gender), unstated attributes can be silently asserted or genuinely stated attributes can be discarded after the original message is evicted. The authors propose a training-free repair spanning note writing, a likelihood-based pre-eviction verification step, and reading strategies, such as marking unstated attributes with paired forms like agotado/a.

entry.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG

author.name: Zhifei Zhu, Hongtao Zhang, Yu Ren, Wei Zhou, Zeping Xie, Yi He

entry.summary: EEG-Jev is a unified single-pass decision model for EEG that returns typed readouts in one forward pass: choice distributions, proposition probabilities, or ordered-level score distributions depending on the answer specification. One jointly trained checkpoint is evaluated across held-out splits of 35 public sources, reaching competitive metrics on motor imagery, sleep staging, and seizure detection. This unification of heterogeneous EEG decision tasks with calibratable outputs is notable for clinical usability.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Transformers for Hierarchical Authorization in Personal AI Agents

author.name: Dongyu Cui, Jie Ding, Xuan Bi

entry.summary: PATH is a novel transformer architecture with parent-gating that predicts user authorization preferences for personal AI agents, handling hierarchical permission requests with sparse, correlated user decisions. It aims to reduce the burden of manually approving agent permission requests while preserving privacy and user control. This addresses a growing practical problem as agents perform multi-step tasks on users' behalf.

entry.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement

author.name: Hongbo Duan, Fan Du, Haipeng Luo, Bin Qian, Zichao Nie, Yilin Mi, Yaopeng Tian, Jiake Tian, Siyuan Liu, Yan Gao, Fangming Liu, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: MARGIN is a risk-aware agent that uses a near-miss margin signal — the fraction of execution budget remaining in the slowest successful rollout — to identify fragile robot programs and guide targeted repairs that increase execution headroom. Evaluated on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-90, and Robosuite, it improves robustness beyond binary success metrics.

entry.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction

author.name: Han Xiao, Xin Zhang, Yuhan Zou, Zhenzhong Wang, Donglin Cao, Dazhen Lin, Min Jiang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Commutator Memory Neural Operators, which identify fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations (downsampling before versus after rollout prediction) and use them to improve long-horizon PDE prediction. The approach targets error accumulation in neural operators that traditional numerical solvers avoid at high computational cost. It matters because long-horizon stability is a core bottleneck for learned physical simulators in science and engineering.

entry.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoyuan Li, Wei Huang, Jiehong Lin, Shengrong Zhang, Chenzhi Liu, Shengchao Zhou, Hehe Fan, Xiaojuan Qi, Yi Yang

entry.summary: ReFocus is a progress-guided multi-round RL framework for vision-language-action policies that alternates Global and Local RL to identify task bottlenecks and allocate extra practice to them. It decomposes tasks into a DAG of subtasks and uses a DAG-based progress reward for training, addressing sparse feedback in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models

author.name: Wonjune Seo, Minkyung Park, Saerom Park

entry.summary: ReQOR is a training-free defense against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors, which make LLMs behave maliciously after quantization while staying benign at high precision. It isolates module-local quantization effects from upstream drift and repairs dominant discrepancy directions identified on benign calibration data via operator-discrepancy subspace repair.

entry.title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Nhat Ha Nguyen, Sudipta Chowdhury, Lokesh Das

entry.summary: DriveAnswer is a benchmark of 20,151 questions across seven reasoning families that tests whether driving VLMs can judge whether visual evidence is sufficient to answer, using matched strong- and weak-evidence pairs where abstention is the correct response. It distinguishes well-supported answers from those grounded in relevant-but-insufficient evidence. This targets safe abstention behavior, which is critical for autonomous driving reliability.

entry.title: Detecting Harmful Short Videos in Toxic Diet Culture: A Governance-Ready Evidence Framework with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Wenli Zhang, Shuang Geng, Jiaheng Xie, Zhonghan Xiang, Sudha Ram

entry.summary: The paper introduces SPACE, a framework built on sparse autoencoder features from a large multimodal model that detects harmful short-form videos and produces governance-ready evidence for moderation decisions. It operationalizes evidence quality through traceability, localization, policy grounding, and inspectability, using toxic diet culture as the empirical case.

entry.title: Diagnosing Epistemic Uncertainty in Neural Operators: Effects of Initialization, Discretization, and Function Sampling

author.name: Tian Yu Yen, Yucheng Fu, Pratanu Roy, Guang Lin, Michael Penwarden

entry.summary: The paper systematically separates and quantifies three sources of epistemic uncertainty in neural operators: finite sampling of the training function space, output discretization, and model initialization. Across diverse operator-learning architectures, it shows substantial variation among learned operators even for deterministic physical problems.

entry.title: Neural Interoperability Protocols: Specifying Compatibility Before Training

author.name: Alireza Bagheri

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Interoperability Protocols (NIPs), a specification-first framework treating neural network compatibility as public interface obligations defined before training, rather than a property inferred from pairwise transfer success. This reframes how independently trained models could exchange intermediate representations as reusable components.

entry.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models

author.name: Yicheng Huang, Feng Ke, Linhan Chen, Ziyi Jiang, Xiu Yin Zhang

entry.summary: This paper adapts LLMs to millimeter-wave radar sensing for privacy-preserving, all-weather scene understanding. It identifies failures of standard instruction tuning and contrastive objectives on continuous radar streams, and proposes a manifold-decoupled JEPA that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from text-aligned semantics, improving retrieval and robustness under sensor blackouts.

entry.title: LATEC: Learned Axial TEnsor Compression for High-Dimensional Scientific Data

author.name: Hippolyte Verninas, Hadrien Hendrikx, Thomas Moreau

entry.summary: LATEC is a learned compression codec for high-dimensional scientific data that enforces user-specified pointwise error bounds, unlike prior learned codecs that optimize aggregate distortion and target fixed dimensionalities. The approach generalizes across field dimensionalities without extensive retraining, addressing the growing storage burden of large-scale scientific simulation.

entry.title: Best Arm Identification with Unknown Post-Action Context Distribution

author.name: Amir Mohammad Abouei, Mohammad Shahverdikondori, Emad Emamjomeh, Negar Kiyavash

entry.summary: The paper studies best arm identification with post-action context in the fixed-confidence setting when the action-conditional context distribution is unknown, deriving an instance-dependent sample complexity lower bound and a Track-and-Stop algorithm that matches it asymptotically. This extends prior work that assumed the context distribution is known.

entry.title: OmniX: A first jet and event model

author.name: Anna Hallin, Gregor Kasieczka, Henning Rose

entry.summary: OmniX extends particle physics foundation models, which so far operate only on single jets, to handle both jets and whole collision events within one model. Demonstrated on jet-level (JetClass, top tagging) and event-level (Collide-2V) datasets, it enables task amortization while capturing global correlations that jet-only models miss.

entry.title: EnSurv: Deep Generative Survival Modeling with Application to Kidney Graft Outcomes

author.name: Rajdeep Pathak, Tamalika Koley, Shreyashi Basak, Dipankar Bandyopadhyay, Tanujit Chakraborty

entry.summary: EnSurv is a deep generative survival model (survival engression) that captures nonlinear covariate interactions to predict time to kidney graft failure. It is trained and evaluated on a large UNOS dataset of over 243,000 transplant records with multi-region structure and heavy right-censoring.

entry.title: NCPU: Towards Cell-Inspired Spatial Computing

author.name: Iliya Zhechev, Piotr Walas

entry.summary: This paper trains Neural Cellular Automata to perform exact digital logic computation, encoding bits as cell clusters on a 2D grid where results must propagate through intermediate cells. The authors demonstrate 100% bit correctness on logic gates and 4/8-bit ripple-carry adders across seeds, with near-perfect exhaustive testing, generalization from 3-bit training to 8-bit operands, and a preliminary 8-bit ALU. This points toward a cell-inspired spatial computing paradigm where reliable computation emerges from learned local update rules rather than hand-designed rules as in classical cellular automata.

entry.title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions

author.name: Maximilian Xiling Li, Nils Blank, Paul Mattes, Pankhuri Vanjani, Rudolf Lioutikov

entry.summary: The paper introduces Movement Prototype Quantization (MPQ), which places a library of demonstrated motions outside a trained policy and replaces each predicted action chunk with its nearest library element, with bounded correction and no additional parameter training. Across six architectures, including a 7B vision-language-action model, the wrapped policy performs statistically equivalently to the original. This provides an interpretable, diagnostic decomposition separating vocabulary, skill choice, and execution failures in discrete skill policies.

entry.title: Scoring What Matters: Exact Feedback Reduction for Language Model Comparison

author.name: Hui Zhang, Haoda Yue, Bicheng Deng, Yuanchao Zhu, Jun He, Rui Qian

entry.summary: The paper introduces Contrast-Aware Feedback Acquisition (CAFA), a sampler-agnostic method that identifies which response scores are actually needed for a requested linear report before acquiring feedback, grouping identical inputs and aggregating report coefficients. The authors give necessary and sufficient query-set characterizations for exact recovery of sample means and covariances, achieving exact results with fewer scored responses. This reduces evaluation cost for comparing language model checkpoints.

entry.title: BCP: A Lightweight Boundary-Controlled Framework for Online Sign Language Recognition and Translation

author.name: Xiao Ma, Lin Li, Shiqing Wu, Wang Gao, Chuanbo Liu, Jianquan Liu

entry.summary: BCP (Boundary-Controlled Prefix Commit) is a lightweight framework that converts pretrained offline sign language models into online counterparts for sign-to-gloss, sign-to-text, and combined translation, without retraining the whole model on simulated streaming prefixes. It freezes pretrained components and controls commit boundaries as video arrives incrementally. This enables real-time communication and live captioning at much lower training cost than existing online methods.

entry.title: BEARING: Who Is Talking to Whom? Grounding Acoustic Direction in Vision for Online Multi-Party Conversation

author.name: Nader Lobandi, Lombe Chileshe, Mohammad Mehdi Hosseini, Mohammad H. Mahoor

entry.summary: BEARING grounds microphone-array acoustic direction of arrival into the camera image for online multi-party conversation understanding, using label-free calibration learned from the stream and an enrollment-free registry of faces, voices, and directions. The registered direction serves as a visual prompt for a vision-language model and as one input to reliability-weighted fusion. It offers a geometry-first alternative to offline, self-supervised-reward approaches.

entry.title: Synthetic Augmentation for Data-Scarce Object Detection: Allocation, Dose, and Filtering Across Six Datasets

author.name: Jo\~ao F\'elix, Atabak Dehban, Rodrigo Ventura

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates a synthetic-data augmentation pipeline for object detection in data-scarce domains like orbital robotics and industrial inspection. Using FLUX.1-Fill with class-specific LoRA, it finds dataset-dependent dose effects, inconsistent filtering gains, and that FID/KID/LPIPS metrics fail to track downstream detector improvements.

entry.title: RELAY: Learning Compatible Representations One Encoder at a Time

author.name: Yu Wang, Chuan Qin, Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: RELAY enables compatible representation upgrades during incremental gallery re-encoding by training a new query encoder against the original gallery, then a new document encoder, allowing one query vector to score both document versions in a single pass. It improves Recall@1 by 8.7-10.2 points on untouched galleries across CLIP and Qwen-based retrieval upgrades.

entry.title: TACTUS: Unifying Surgical Action Understanding in Time and Space

author.name: Lurui Wang, Hao Ding, Chenhao Yu, Chenyan Jing, Jiru Xu, Ruoqi Zuo, Liwei Mei, Chang Liu, Lalithkumar Seenivasan, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: Introduces TACTUS, a new dataset and benchmark that unifies annotation of complete surgical actions, jointly specifying tool and action identities, nested action and interaction windows, instrument landmark trajectories, and tissue-region tracks. It aims to connect action semantics, instrument motion, and tissue interaction for surgical automation.

entry.title: LoopFit: Retrofitting Pretrained Diffusion Transformers with Recurrent Refinement

author.name: Xiaocheng Lu, Haoxi Li, Dazhao Du, Tao Han, Jian Liu, Hao Chen, Bohai Gu, Siyu Yan, Jingcai Guo, Jie Zhang, Song Guo

entry.summary: LoopFit improves pretrained diffusion transformers at inference by recurrently reusing Transformer blocks to refine hidden representations within each denoising step, without retraining from scratch. It uses feedback from earlier passes to guide per-patch refinement so additional passes correct local errors without disrupting established structure. This enables test-time compute scaling beyond extra sampling steps.

entry.title: SofaSpace: A Benchmark for Executable Visual Spatial Reasoning in Continuous Motion and Environment Construction

author.name: Ze Rong, Kun Shi, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: Inspired by the moving sofa problem, SofaSpace is a benchmark for visual spatial reasoning through continuous planar rigid-body transport, with 3,000 scenes covering geometric compatibility, nonlocal maneuver planning, and interactive coordination, plus 534 hard tasks. A geometric verifier checks the entire body throughout submitted motions, and tasks include motion planning, layout reconstruction, and joint environment-motion design.

entry.title: PVWander: 3D Memory-guided Panoramic Video Wandering with Path-Facing Canonicalization

author.name: Chuanxin Song, Xiaodong Wang, Shijie Chen, Junliang Xie, Zhanmi Zhong, Suiying Wu, Peixi Peng

entry.summary: PVWander is a framework for long-horizon panoramic video generation that synthesizes scene-consistent 360-degree observations along user-specified camera trajectories from a single equirectangular panorama. It accumulates generated frames into a 3D memory with path-facing canonicalization to stabilize wandering despite accumulated artifacts and depth errors.

entry.title: UnifiedAD: One-Shot Anomaly Detection across Modalities via Evidence Calibration

author.name: Shangze Li, Chuancheng Shi, Simiao Xie, Wenhua Wu, Xingyu Zhu, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: UnifiedAD unifies single-modal and multi-modal anomaly detection through anomaly evidence calibration, requiring only one normal reference per category and no gradient updates. It derives neuron-level discriminative priors from an auxiliary dataset and combines them with neuron response consistency under normality-preserving transformations to produce comparable anomaly scores across modalities.

entry.title: Attack-Inference Aligned Universal Adversarial Attacks on Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Ruiqi Shen, Chang Liu, Henghui Ding

entry.summary: AUV is an adversarial framework for video object segmentation that aligns universal adversarial perturbations with the two-stage initialization-plus-memory-propagation inference paradigm of modern VOS models. Using decoupled training strategies for each stage and disrupting the shared memory space, it achieves prompt-agnostic attacks across mask, point, box, and language prompts with state-of-the-art attack performance.

entry.title: RestPose: Canonicalization for Open Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Sandeep Inuganti, Weihang Li, Benjamin Busam, Didier Stricker, Jason Rambach

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces RestPose, a computer vision approach that removes the dependence of object pose estimation on arbitrary canonical frame conventions defined by reference models. Instead, the method derives a canonical frame for any object by generating an object mesh from a single input image and canonicalizing it, enabling open-vocabulary pose estimation without model-specific training annotations. This could significantly improve generalization of pose estimation systems to novel objects.

entry.title: A Morphological Approach to Inverse Lithography

author.name: Gijs Bellaard, Bart M. N. Smets, Tim van der Leek, Alexandru Onose, Remco Duits

entry.summary: This paper gives a mathematical characterization of manufacturability constraints in inverse lithography technology and develops a (sub-)differentiable scoring function that measures how badly a candidate mask violates them. The differentiable formulation enables optimization-based mask design for semiconductor manufacturing.

entry.title: MemHand: Memory-Enhanced World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos

author.name: Junyi Ma, Zhangshuo Qi, Erhang Zhang, Mingjie Li, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: MemHand reconstructs continuous world-space hand motion from egocentric video using a memory-enhanced framework that retrieves relevant temporal context beyond fixed-length windows, improving robustness around occlusions and hands leaving the field of view. Relevant to human-to-robot policy transfer and augmented reality applications.

entry.title: PAVE: Preference-Aligned Visual Egocentric Learning for the Blind and Low-Vision Users

author.name: Nan Li, Shaofeng Liang, Shiyun Zhao, Keni Shi, Zhencheng Huang, Bowen Tian, Jiemin Wu, Wenshuo Chen, Kaishen Yuan, Runwei Guan, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Builds PA-EgoQA, a preference-aligned egocentric video QA dataset reconstructed from real BLV user queries in EgoBlind according to empirical communication criteria emphasizing spatial orientation, actionability, and conciseness, and develops models optimized for practical helpfulness rather than factual matching alone. Targets assistive technology for blind and low-vision users.

entry.title: Spectrify: Framework for Hyperspectral Image Generation Using Computer Graphics

author.name: Yasin Mamedov, Daniil Vladimirov, Sofiia Dorogova, Bakhtiyar Khalfin, Egor Ershov

entry.summary: This paper introduces Spectrify, a computer-graphics framework for generating hyperspectral images (HSIs) via physically grounded spectral rendering. Because hyperspectral data is expensive to capture and existing datasets contain only roughly a thousand images, the framework aims to provide scalable, spectrally accurate synthetic training data for hyperspectral reconstruction and camera-pipeline research, addressing a gap where high-level vision uses rendered data but low-level tasks have lacked physically correct spectra.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware and Anatomy-Preserving Replay for Continual Echocardiographic Segmentation

author.name: Zahid Ullah, Sieun Choi, Jihie Kim

entry.summary: This paper introduces RAR-Net, a continual learning framework for echocardiographic segmentation that combats catastrophic forgetting through multi-factor exemplar prioritization, protected task-aware memory, and forgetting-conditioned adaptive replay. It adds structure-aware supervision to preserve anatomical knowledge under limited replay memory and incomplete annotations. The work addresses a practical clinical problem where labeled data is scarce and imaging distributions shift.

entry.title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework

author.name: Daniel Windhager, Lothar Ratschbacher, Bernhard A. Moser, Michael Lunglmayr

entry.summary: Introduces Differential Time Representation (DTR), a more bit-efficient encoding of spike trains than Address-Event Representation or 1-bit sampled trains, with a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity for multi-input support. It also presents a modular hardware streaming framework enabling custom low-power SNN accelerators tailored to specific networks.

entry.title: Normative and neural network models of multisensory integration

author.name: Marcus Ghosh, John S. Butler

entry.summary: A review paper that organizes the multisensory integration modeling literature into two classes: normative models based on hypotheses about how cues should be integrated, and neural network models that emulate how brain circuits could integrate them. It surveys how both approaches show observers integrate cues statistically optimally, bridging concise mathematical accounts and large-scale network models.

entry.title: VG-GP: Uncertainty-Gated Visuo-Geometric Memory for Negative-Transfer-Resistant Grasp Adaptation

author.name: Yonglong Zhang

entry.summary: Presents VG-GP, a plug-and-play Gaussian Process memory framework that adapts a frozen antipodal grasping policy to novel objects without retraining, fusing color-invariant DINOv2 surface-normal features, SE(2)-aligned 3D heightmaps, and contact-geometry descriptors under a product kernel. Uncertainty gating and closed-loop acquisition are designed to prevent visual-appearance bias and negative transfer from overriding good base grasps.

entry.title: Reading Geometric Anchors: Viewpoint Generalization in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation with RGB-Only Deployment

author.name: Chengyu Tao, Chunxi Huang

entry.summary: ReGeoAnch is a geometry-anchored imitation learning framework that improves viewpoint generalization for RGB-only deployment by building global anchors in the robot base frame and local anchors in the gripper frame as shared physical references across views. A decoupled appearance-guided geometric readout with point-to-anchor aggregation exploits these anchors.

entry.title: Self-Sensing Compliant Anthropomorphic Hand for Speed-Dictated Shared Force Control in Teleoperation

author.name: Huijiang Wang, Yu Zhang, Rui Chen, Tristan Bonato, Jaemin Eom, Kai Junge, Cheng Pan, Benhui Dai, Yue Xie, Josie Hughes

entry.summary: This paper shows that the elastic transmission of a compliant tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand can itself act as the force sensor for shared-control telemanipulation, with forearm-mounted potentiometers reading series springs to estimate joint states and finger forces. This avoids the wiring, cost, and integration complexity of adding tactile sensors to fingers while giving operators implicit haptic feedback.

entry.title: The Generalized Volterra Signature

author.name: Munawar Ali, Qi Feng, Samy Tindel

entry.summary: This paper introduces the generalized Volterra signature of a path, extending the recently defined Volterra signature (itself an extension of Lyons' path signature), and establishes a new algebraic structure plus a generalized Chen's identity. By restricting to ladder trees, the authors define a geometric Volterra signature with a shuffle product, enabling universal approximation results.

entry.title: The Warning Shot vs. Doom Balance Is Better for White-Box Control Than Black-Box

author.name: GabrielKS

entry.summary: A conceptual argument responding to the Warning Shot Argument against AI control, which holds that control measures suppress catastrophic-risk-revealing incidents. The author argues this objection bites harder against black-box control than white-box control, using a time-varying model of catastrophic risk, warning-shot value, and control power. This refines the debate about whether to deploy control measures on current models.

entry.title: Most attempts at measuring eval awareness overestimate it

author.name: Dean Valentine

entry.summary: Argues that current methods for measuring eval awareness in AI models systematically overestimate it, which matters because honeypot evals and other alignment tests lose validity if models detect them. The author examines how eval-awareness measurements are constructed and where they introduce confounds.

entry.title: Multi-agent System for Automatic Discovery of Pareto-optimal Meta-solvers for PDEs

author.name: Youngkyu Lee, Shanqing Liu, Jerome Darbon, George EM Karniadakis

entry.summary: The authors present a multi-agent framework where LLM agents propose, critique, implement, and evaluate PDE solver configurations from Krylov methods, preconditioners, block factorizations, and neural operators, with an evolutionary algorithm steering the population toward the Pareto front of six measured quantities. The system runs on small open-weight models on a single laptop and outperforms a single-agent baseline on four problems, including 3D acoustics.

entry.title: RepoEviAgent: Scalable Synthesis of Evidence-Grounded Repository-Level Question Answering Tasks

author.name: Aoqi Hu, Yueao Xing

entry.summary: RepoEviAgent is a framework for constructing repository-level SWE question-answering training and evaluation data, starting from 8,477 open-source repositories and about 2.48 million pull request records. It combines semantic alignment, complexity constraints, and multidimensional quality assessment with a sandbox-based multi-agent pipeline that builds environments and executes verification to produce evidence-grounded tasks. This targets the data bottleneck for software engineering agents.

entry.title: From Memory Access to Evidence Sufficiency: Diagnosing and Addressing Demand--Evidence Misalignment

author.name: Shiyao Liu, Yixing Fan, Ruqing Zhang, Xiaohui Yan, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper identifies demand-evidence misalignment in long-term memory retrieval, where relevant records do not jointly satisfy a question's factual, relational, temporal, and state constraints. It introduces MemPath for diagnosing failures across memory access, demand coverage, and evidence utilization, and BiDE-Mem, which represents questions as typed demands to guide retrieval and evidence organization.

entry.title: VC-OPD: Learning to See What Matters via Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Qinxuan Wang, Zheyu Zhang, Yijing Yang, Han Shu, Chuang Wang, Peipei Yang, Shuo Tang, Jie Hu, Shiming Xiang

entry.summary: VC-OPD extends visual on-policy distillation for small multimodal LLMs beyond cropped image regions as privileged teacher information to question-conditioned visual cues generated by advanced MLLMs, capturing structural relationships and semantic evidence. A multi-stage quality filtering process selects reliable cues used to guide the student.

entry.title: Beyond Expected Value: PPO with Distributional Critics for Systematic Conservation Planning

author.name: Ana Maria Quintero Ossa, Daniele Silvestro, James Rudd-Jones, Maria Perez-Ortiz

entry.summary: This paper upgrades the CAPTAIN framework, which casts systematic conservation planning as sequential reinforcement learning under ecological and climatic uncertainty, by replacing gradient-free Evolution Strategies with PPO via a Plackett-Luce solution to the non-differentiable action space, and replacing the scalar critic with an Implicit Quantile Network modeling the full return distribution. Matched-granularity comparisons show distributional critics support worst-case-aware policies where expected-value optimization fails. It applies modern distributional RL to a high-stakes environmental domain.

entry.title: AhaPro: A Process-level Rebus benchmark for probing Aha moments in LLM reasoning

author.name: Wei Guo, Lang Qin, Yundi Gai, Qinghua Xu, Zhi Wu, Wenjian Ding, Huijia Li, Zhenglu Yang, Yao Zhang

entry.summary: AhaPro is a process-level benchmark using rebus puzzles, which encode answers through character forms, spatial arrangements, and homophony, to examine how LLMs reorganize evidence and revise answers through Aha moments. It represents chain-of-thought as sequences of candidate answers, evidence, and verification states with hierarchical metrics for conflict detection and state improvement.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Memory-Organized Search with Anti-Imitation Crossover for Training-Free Microarchitecture Optimization

author.name: Kaushal Mhapsekar, Bita Aslrousta, Paula Contreras, Azam Ghanbari, Samira Mirbagher Ajorpaz

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a training-free LLM-driven search controller for generating cache-replacement policies that stores lessons from prior evaluations rather than copying high-scoring code, and uses anti-imitation crossover to combine dissimilar high-scoring policies when improvement stalls. It addresses the core generalization problem that generated code tends to imitate established policies, reducing held-out IPC losses seen in prior search methods.

entry.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation

author.name: Kaipeng Fang, Yuhao Wang, Ji Zhang, Yunsong Zhou, Jingkuan Song, Lianli Gao

entry.summary: The paper identifies the handoff boundary problem in agent-orchestrated robot systems: visuomotor policies are reliable only from limited start states, and agents may invoke them outside that region. Boundary-Aware Policy Learning explicitly shapes the boundary via contact-segment fine-tuning and then expands it, improving reliable coordination between multimodal agents and control policies.

entry.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy

author.name: Anirban Ray, Florian Jug

entry.summary: BEACON improves guided conditional flow matching for microscopy image restoration by learning observation-conditioned starting points instead of pairing each clean target with an independent Gaussian sample. This leverages the degraded observation as the source of the flow, improving dehazing and computational super-resolution while preserving biological structure. Better restoration enables cheaper, lower-light-dose fluorescence microscopy.

entry.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners

author.name: Zirui Li, Zhiqi Mao, Yangang Ren, Heye Huang, Haohan Yang, Qihang Huang, Zhan Chen, Chen Lv

entry.summary: ContinualDrive is a deployment-anchored benchmark for evaluating post-deployment continual learning of learned driving planners, updating a planner on real-world nuPlan logs one scenario group at a time. It makes four measurement axes explicit and anchors a three-valued release verdict to the deployed checkpoint, evaluating two planners in open and closed loop.

entry.title: SwiftLoop: Selective Refinement for Adaptive Implicit Reasoning in Looped Transformers

author.name: Tianyi Zhao, Ke Wan, Chen Chen

entry.summary: SwiftLoop introduces an inference-time framework for looped transformers that adaptively allocates computation by freezing latent positions when further refinement is unnecessary. Freezing policies are learned via hindsight-guided supervision based on K/V reusability and functional output impact, enabling savings in both recurrent depth and active width.

entry.title: Start Where the Data Are: Statistical Priors for One-Step Generation on Manifolds

author.name: Yuyao Wang, Haoliang Sun, Xiankai Lu, Xinxin Zhang, Yongshun Gong

entry.summary: Proposes fitting a statistical prior via mixtures of tangent-space Gaussians to fix one-step generators that produce spurious samples in low-density gaps, with a posterior coupling scheme to pair noise to data modes coherently. Targets fast generation on manifolds with applications like protein design.

entry.title: CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers

author.name: Xvyuan Liu, Jianjie Fang, Honglin Zhang, Zhaolu Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu, Fengli Xu, Chen Gao, Yong Li

entry.summary: The authors show that frozen hierarchical visual world models can rank goal-conditioned plan proposals effectively even when their predicted costs are uninformative for prolonged gradient-based optimization, which exploits prediction errors. CriticJEPA learns goal-conditioned flow proposals from reward-free trajectories and uses the world model as a critic rather than an optimizer for planning.

entry.title: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation

author.name: Satiyabooshan Murugaboopathy, Adel Daoud, Connor T. Jerzak

entry.summary: LUCID pairs prompt self-correction with Design-based Supervised Learning to calibrate LLM raters evaluating chain-of-thought reasoning, without retraining or weight access. From a small expert-labeled set it summarizes rater bias in plain text and prompts re-grading, shrinking calibration gaps — e.g., correcting GPT-5-mini's over-strict grading on PRM800K.

entry.title: GDD: A Remote Sensing Image Deepfake Detection and Manipulation Localization Dataset

author.name: Jacob Arndt, Philipe Dias, Debvrat Varshney, Sudarshan Srinivasan, Dalton Lunga

entry.summary: GDD is a benchmark for remote sensing deepfake detection and manipulation localization, comprising images from diverse modern generative models with visual realism and diversity prioritized over sheer volume, plus rigorous out-of-distribution testing protocols. It addresses shortcomings of existing RS deepfake benchmarks that rely on uncurated synthetic generation. The resource supports authentication of overhead imagery as generative AI makes synthetic satellite data increasingly convincing.

entry.title: Generalizable Feed-Forward 3D Hand-Object Reconstruction with Coarse-to-Fine Contact Estimation

author.name: Seonghwan Park, Yong-Hoon Kwon, Min-Gyu Park

entry.summary: HORCRUX is a unified feed-forward transformer for joint 3D hand-object pose and contact reconstruction from a single image, using a frozen foundation model to encode unseen objects from given or image-reconstructed meshes. Coarse-to-fine contact estimation exploits explicit geometry rather than image features alone for precise contact localization.

entry.title: GUI-PRISM: Efficient Action Decoding for GUI Agents

author.name: Enqi Liu, Zhi Gao, Liu Liu, Lifeng Fan, Liyuan Pan

entry.summary: GUI-PRISM is a hybrid action decoder for GUI agents that directly predicts action types and structured arguments instead of autoregressively generating action text, while retaining language generation for open-ended content. Field-specific queries extract action-relevant information, cutting inference latency substantially. It extends prior spatial-only decoding methods to complete GUI action prediction.

entry.title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining

author.name: Boning Zhang, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: RELACT is a relation-first latent action pretraining framework that separates modeling the relational structure of observed transitions from abstracting them into compact latent action codes. Existing approaches entangle transition characterization with action inference by directly mapping paired observations into latent action codes. The explicit decoupling aims to yield more reusable action representations from unlabeled video without embodiment-specific annotations.

entry.title: Get the Next Moment Right: Short-Term Event Planning for Physically Plausible Video Generation

author.name: Hao Liu, Xiang Tang, Ruotong Li, Xiaopeng Fan, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: STEP is a training-free closed-loop framework that improves physical plausibility in video generation by planning only the next short event at a time: it grounds scene state, predicts and renders a control clip, generates the next segment, and verifies the event occurred, resampling when it does not. This avoids the error accumulation of whole-clip trajectory prediction.

entry.title: MinPair: Measured Minimal Pairs for Fine-Grained Control in Text-to-Motion Generation

author.name: Lennart Schiweck, Crist\'obal Curio

entry.summary: MinPair builds minimal caption pairs from real motion clips, where a single attribute word (e.g., kick height) is the only difference between otherwise identical captions, to test and train fine-grained control in text-to-motion generation. The paper shows state-of-the-art methods fail to realize all attribute values, and provides the data and rule-based 3D motion descriptors to fix this.

entry.title: Knocked Off Course: Tracing Uncommanded Motion from Perception to Action in Embodied VLAs

author.name: Dan Zlotnikov, Nadav Alali, Ohad Ben-Shahar

entry.summary: This study benchmarks three tracking vision-language-action models across three datasets under environmental disturbances such as wind and uneven terrain, finding all models sensitive to sudden target loss. Tracing egomotion from pixels to actions, the authors identify two gaps: motion is reliably recovered in representation but is not reflected in the emitted actions.

entry.title: Back to Raw Motion: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers for Text-to-Motion and Exact Conditional Generation

author.name: Yun Chen, Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: RawMo brings text-to-motion generation to raw motion space with a Motion Diffusion Transformer, avoiding learned latent codecs that lose detail and cannot guarantee exact preservation of conditioning. Motivated by recent pixel-space diffusion successes in images, the paper shows raw-space diffusion is viable for motion generation at practical costs.

entry.title: ProX-MAD: Aggregating Spatial Context into Representative Proxies for Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Seunghyun Oh, Seongsu Lee, Seunghye Chae, Youngmin Ro

entry.summary: Proposes ProX-MAD, a proxy-based framework for unified one-for-many few-shot medical anomaly detection that aggregates spatial context into compact, learnable, state-specific proxies, with a Masked Proxy Infusion Attention module for cross-attention. Diagnoses why shared decision boundaries and normal-only memory banks fail across heterogeneous lesion definitions.

entry.title: Training Lightweight Gaze Models without Target Gaze Annotation: What Makes a Good Teacher?

author.name: Scott J. Lewis, Di Fu

entry.summary: A controlled study of eleven supervision conditions for distilling gaze target estimation into lightweight models, varying only the label source across three video datasets, two student sizes, and three seeds with 361k fixed samples. Finds imperfect model-generated labels (e.g., from Gaze-LLE) can replace human annotation, and identifies characteristics predicting teacher quality before student training.

entry.title: Co-DRIS: Physics-Informed Predictive Belief and Variable-Impedance Learning for Reactive Catching under Coupled Uncertainty

author.name: Yonglong Zhang

entry.summary: Addresses the collapse of reactive catching policies under simultaneous perception and actuation uncertainty (dropping from 86.4% to 27.6% across coupled stress scenarios in prior DRIS) with a perception-action co-design framework. It couples an inertial world-frame physics-informed world model with exact ballistic kinematics plus a learned contact residual, and variable-impedance control learned for reactive execution.

entry.title: Wind-Aware Trajectory Planning for Deformable Aerial Formations

author.name: Haozhe Wang, Xun Huang

entry.summary: Family-Air is a wind-aware trajectory-family planner for drone formations in dense urban environments, constructing a virtual tube as shared collision-free flight space while jointly optimizing formation-center motion, deformation, and timing. It couples spatially varying wind with deformation-induced velocities in a unified air-relative objective.

entry.title: Bayesian Data Integration and Model Updating in Probabilistic Digital Twins

author.name: Dafydd Cotoarb\u{a}, Antonis Mavritsakis, Timo Schweckendiek, Ian FC Smith, Daniel Straub

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for sequential Bayesian updating in probabilistic digital twins that distinguishes property data (directly informing uncertain parameters) from behavior data (indirect information requiring Bayesian inverse problems). An active-learning-based surrogate strategy evolves with the digital state to reduce the computational cost of assimilating multi-source data over time.

entry.title: Comparing AI R&D compute caps and deployment lags

author.name: elifland

entry.summary: A comparative policy analysis of two pacing mechanisms: caps on the fraction of compute used for capabilities R&D, and deployment lags or freezes limiting how capable the models used for AI R&D can be. The author concludes compute caps are roughly as good or slightly better than lags/freezes standalone, and that combining both is likely best, responding to Evan Hubinger's argument for blocking internal deployment.

entry.title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls

author.name: Artem Trofimov, Boris Novikov

entry.summary: The paper empirically measures how often LLM code-executing agents harm external state when recovering from partially executed code blocks, using recorded AppWorld trajectories across ten models. In a stratified sample, 145 of 200 episodes showed confirmed partial executions, and a stratification-weighted estimate of 24.6% of determinable partial executions were followed by harmful recoveries whose violations persisted to the end of the run.

entry.title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations

author.name: Zeyan Li, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: FN-Prune is a training-free criterion for pruning mixture-of-experts LLM experts that accounts for how RMSNorm consumes an expert's contribution: it compares next-RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, averaged over calibration tokens in a single pass. Low-scoring experts are physically deleted, reducing memory footprint. This addresses a blind spot in frequency- and magnitude-based pruning scores that evaluate experts in isolation.

entry.title: A Generative AI Agent to Emulate Interactive Human-driven Vehicles for Automated Driving Testing in Urban Areas

author.name: Jia Hu, Changjian Yu, Panqu Wang, Jaehyun So, Yang Chang, Xuerun Yan, Jintao Lai

entry.summary: The authors propose a generative AI agent that emulates interactive human-driven vehicles for safety testing of automated driving in urban environments. The agent incorporates field-of-view modeling to handle occlusion-induced interactions, richer driving-style characterization, and learning signals that avoid dilution by non-critical behaviors. This improves the realism of safety-critical scenario generation for autonomous vehicle validation.

entry.title: TableRouter: Query-Aware Evidence Construction for Long-Table Question Answering

author.name: Anahita Bolourani, Xiaofeng Lin, Tung Sum Thomas Kwok, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: TableRouter is a training-free framework for question answering over tables too large for the context window that routes each query between a computation route (deriving question-conditioned statistics from the full table) and a coverage route (retrieving relevant rows and column summaries). Across three LLMs and three benchmarks it beats the strongest single-call baselines in all nine settings.

entry.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints

author.name: Xiaoyang Fan, Yufan Cai, Zhe Hou, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: VerClin is an explainable framework for clinical reasoning that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge, representing patient conversations as scoped cases processed by a deterministic four-valued reasoner. Specialty agents screen matched guidelines and a consultation model synthesizes guidance with a formal-constraint channel preserving traceability and handling uncertainty.

entry.title: GeoSurge: Geometry-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning for Auditable Liver Resection Planning

author.name: Wenjie Deng, Zijian Tu, Xueyin Zhou, Huayi Wang, Zhuoyun Du, Mingyu Chen, Haochao Ying, Jian Wu

entry.summary: GeoSurge combines mask-derived metrics with structure-aware point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable resection surfaces for liver surgery planning, using a surface-action grammar that maps actions to parametric geometry. Anatomy-oriented and tumor-centered templates generate candidate surfaces within a framework that makes resection geometry learnable and auditable. This bridges the gap between anatomical understanding from medical multimodal models and the concrete geometric outputs surgeons actually need.

entry.title: How Persona Conditioning Changes Open-Ended Task Execution: A Paired Evaluation of Behavioral Gains and Reliability Costs

author.name: Yugyeong Ji, Changho Lee, Yerin Hwang, Taegwan Kang, Jinsik Lee

entry.summary: This paired evaluation treats persona conditioning as a task-execution steering signal rather than merely a character-fidelity device, comparing with-persona and no-persona conditions across eight models using instances derived from real role-play logs. Personas improve expert content depth and procedural fidelity but reduce response stability, revealing a behavioral gain versus reliability cost tradeoff.

entry.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests

author.name: Karthik Karunanithi

entry.summary: The paper argues that per-attack blocking rates are the wrong metric for agent tool-manifest security: a catalog is only as safe as its weakest policy, so catalog-level exfiltration vulnerability grows as 1-(1-p)^M with the number of independently authored policies. Three lines of evidence, including runs through ChainCaps and OpenAPPA enforcement engines, show 92% per-attack blocking coexisting with rapidly rising catalog vulnerability.

entry.title: Reading Between the Layers: Where Representation Quality Lives, and What Geometry Reveals

author.name: Arnesh Batra, Aniket Khandelwal, Arush Gumber, Krish Thukral, Kushagra Agrawal, Dev Sharma

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study maps where representation quality lives across 25 pretrained text models spanning four architectural families and four pretraining strategies, evaluated on 13 datasets and four task types. It finds systematic patterns in peak probing layers, e.g., masked encoders peaking in late-middle layers and sequence-to-sequence peaks shifting with task type, addressing label-free layer selection.

entry.title: MIFLOW: Dynamic Recent-Behavior Priors for Reference-Calibrated Online Flow-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenhao Wang, Haonan Ma, Wenjie Zhang, Yifan Wang, Mingbin Gao, Yuan-Ye Zhang, Wenjing Hong

entry.summary: MIFLOW calibrates online flow-policy reinforcement learning with a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions, addressing unreliable off-policy value estimates in poorly covered action regions. The prior acts as a moving density reference, used in a dimension-normalized correction to both actor updates and critic targets. The idea is inspired by canalization as an analogy for path-dependent stabilization of behavior.

entry.title: Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication

author.name: Zixi Wang, Gaohao Zhou, Yubo Huang, Xin Lai, Yushe Cao, Jingzehua Xu, Shuai Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Calibrated Latent Reader, a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and latent message content through task-conditioned interactions between internal states and candidate answers, with source adapters for cross-model transfer and conformal calibration for coverage guarantees. It improves over MLP and attention probes by 4-18 points on two CODI models.

entry.title: Blaming the Machine, Billing the Victim? How Mock Jurors Reassign Fault from Generative AI Systems and Respond to Liability Cliffs in Tort

author.name: Tin Trung Nguyen, Jiannan Xu, Bao Kham Chau, Hal Daum\'e III, Zubin Jelveh

entry.summary: A pre-registered human-subjects experiment (N=199) examines where mock jurors place fault when they blame a generative AI system that cannot legally bear fault, and how U.S. liability-cliff doctrines (contributory negligence, joint and several liability) affect compensation outcomes. Notably, 36% of jurors blamed the AI, redirecting fault away from human defendants.

entry.title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning

author.name: Omar Emara, Nan Lu, Dima Damen, Hazel Doughty

entry.summary: CGAAL is a model-agnostic contrastive objective for audio-visual learning that uses modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between co-occurring audio and video, rather than assuming all pairs are equally aligned. This handles realistic cases such as off-screen sounds that break the paired-observation assumption. The approach improves representation learning on unconstrained audio-visual data.

entry.title: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory

author.name: Jialong Peng, Shihao Zhou, Feng Yan, Wen Xiao, Haozheng Wang, Wenqi Ren, Wenyuan Sheng, Jian Qiao, Jiaxu Miao, Lin Ma, Chao Yang

entry.summary: MXI-MemICL enables memory-guided in-context learning in vision-language-action models, allowing robots to acquire new skills from single demonstrations without parameter updates. It treats demonstrations as retrievable memory via a visual-action causal encoder, avoiding the need for large-scale pretraining or extra annotations.

entry.title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos

author.name: Karthik Sundar Senthilkumar, Christopher Thirgood, Simon Hadfield

entry.summary: EventDiffusion is a hierarchical generative framework that learns the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event-camera streams directly from real recordings, decomposing generation into activity, polarity, and timing processes. It avoids the prescribed sensor-dynamics assumptions of prior RGB-to-event simulators. This addresses data scarcity that has constrained event-camera research.

entry.title: Flagging Batch Shift in Flow Cytometry using Jeffreys Divergence between Gaussian Mixtures

author.name: Jonathan Legrand (MONC, IMB), Aguirre Mimoun (Centre m{\'e}dico chirurgical Magellan), Audrey Bidet (Centre m{\'e}dico chirurgical Magellan), Pierre-Yves Dumas (Centre m{\'e}dico chirurgical Magellan), Christ{\`e}le Etchegaray (MONC, IMB), Baudouin Denis de Senneville (IMB, MONC)

entry.summary: The authors propose a model-agnostic reliability criterion for clinical flow cytometry: each patient sample is encoded as a Gaussian mixture and compared to a training reference via Jeffreys divergence estimated with Monte Carlo integration. Applied to acute myeloid leukaemia cohorts and an NPM1 mutation classifier, the method flags samples where batch shift makes predictions unreliable.

entry.title: Trust-Region Optimization for Performative Prediction without Response Modeling

author.name: Siqi Du, Miaolan Xie, Roy Dong

entry.summary: The paper introduces PTRO, an algorithm for performative prediction that optimizes performative risk without fitting a model of how the population responds to deployed decisions. It samples from the current population to evaluate the known loss at nearby decisions and uses additional deployments only to estimate directional effects, bridging black-box optimization and structure-exploiting approaches.

entry.title: Rethinking Universal Time Series Foundation Models from Unified Representations to Shared Dynamics (UniTFU)

author.name: Shuxin Li, Yingjie Zhou, Le Zhang, Jingyuan Xia, Shengxi Li, Ce Zhu, Anderson Rocha

entry.summary: Critiques time series foundation models for relying on unified representations without explicitly identifying shared temporal regularities across domains, and proposes instead characterizing commonalities in recurring local dynamics. UniTFU captures cross-domain commonalities to improve robust cross-domain generalization.

entry.title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation

author.name: Xiaoliang Shi, Zichen Wang, Zhijian Wei, Zhanpeng Shi, Zhenghong Zhou, Yunpeng Wang, Shuangjia Zheng

entry.summary: This paper identifies a limitation in multimodal protein language models that jointly generate sequence and structure tokens via iterative masked decoding: the memoryless mask reset discards soft predictions between iterations. It proposes predictive memory that carries temporally coherent uncommitted predictions forward as cross-step soft anchors, improving convergence and avoiding repetitive collapse in open-ended co-generation.

entry.title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation

author.name: Andrea Testa, S{\o}ren Hauberg, Andras Gabor Kupcsik, Tamim Asfour, Leonel Rozo

entry.summary: The paper introduces CuOT, a new unbalanced optimal transport formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth, eliminating the structural bias toward high-density regions and mode collapse found in Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao approaches. This yields adaptive sampling steps for bridging unpaired source and target distributions in biology, medical imaging, and robotics applications.

entry.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain

author.name: Zhiyuan Dong, Carlos Mundo-Levano, Daniel L. Lau, Gonzalo R. Arce

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first score-based generative model for signals on fixed hypergraphs, formulated in the t-product hypergraph spectral domain. It repairs an ill-posed tensor heat semigroup via a per-mode frequency shift, yielding a decoupled Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion with closed-form scores and exact sampling guarantees.

entry.title: A Bias in Disguise: Tiny Gradient Edits Stop a Small Language Model's Thinking Loops and Complement a Frontier Model's Weight Edit

author.name: Hussamuddin Syed

entry.summary: The paper provides a gradient-based baseline to a recent demonstration in which GPT-6 Astra edited ~131k weights of a small Qwen model without gradients, and shows that fine-tuning only 140-140k highest-gradient weights on the model's own correct answers stops reasoning loops and raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially within minutes on one GPU. Combining the gradient edit with the weight edit yields complementary gains.

entry.title: IncrementDET: Continual AI-Generated Music Detection via Enrollment

author.name: Runbao Du, Wei Li, Qile He

entry.summary: IncrementDET tackles AI-generated music detection when new generators keep appearing. Instead of retraining a universal detector, it enrolls each new generator by training a single linear classifier (a needle) against a fixed reference set, avoiding catastrophic forgetting and large retraining costs.

entry.title: Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoders for Scalable Phenotyping of Health Trajectories

author.name: Philom\`ene Letzelter, Violaine Courrier, Sandrine Katsahian, Agathe Guilloux

entry.summary: LCMM-VAE is a deep generative model whose latent prior is a mixture of class-specific linear mixed models, combining the interpretability of latent-class mixed models with the scalability of deep time-series clustering. It handles irregular visit times and high-dimensional longitudinal health data while retaining clinically interpretable class structure.

entry.title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Tingting Liao, Mingjia Huo, Hao Li, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric P. Xing, Guangyi Liu

entry.summary: SimPWM tests the assumption behind proxy-conditioned robot video world models by building a calibrated simulator whose state is explicit and perturbable: a parameter-free rule-based simulator moves 3D object points and a video model renders the result. By freezing simulated objects while the arm replays and checking video consistency, it measures how faithfully the video model tracks simulated state.

entry.title: Online V-Learning with Adaptive Longitudinal Data

author.name: Aniruddhan Ganesaraman, Michael R. Kosorok

entry.summary: This work extends V-learning for estimating optimal dynamic treatment regimes to a batch-online setting relevant to mobile health, where policies are re-estimated after each block of new adaptively collected data. The authors develop theory accounting for the dependence across patient trajectories induced by adaptive batch updating, which offline theory does not cover. This bridges a practical gap between offline reinforcement learning methods and real-world mHealth deployment.

entry.title: fork() for Agents: Agent Kernel for Non-blocking LLM Orchestration

author.name: Ankit Chadha, Pratyay Banerjee

entry.summary: Agent-Kernel is a non-blocking runtime for LLM agents that ports subgraph-selective recovery from distributed systems to the agent content plane, resetting only a failed node's descendants while preserving completed sibling work on raw exceptions, without trained verifiers or planners. This avoids discarding completed work on failure, a common inefficiency in synchronous agent execution. The work connects a mature distributed-systems pattern to emerging agent orchestration needs.

entry.title: Social Bias Neurons in Multilingual Language Models: A Mechanistic Interpretability Analysis

author.name: Lance Calvin Lim Gamboa, Yue Feng, Mark Lee

entry.summary: The paper adapts mechanistic interpretability methods to locate and characterize model components encoding social bias in multilingual instruction-tuned models, across three models, four languages, and seven bias dimensions. Using activation probability entropy and integrated gap gradients to identify bias neurons, it finds integrated gap gradients more effective, with isolated neurons concentrated in the deepest layers producing sharper bias decreases when suppressed. The analysis extends bias localization to multilingual settings.

entry.title: Which Way Is Up? Rotated Photos Silently Hurt Multi-View 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Yukun Shi, Minglun Gong

entry.summary: This paper measures how photos with wrong or ignored EXIF orientation tags degrade five multi-view 3D foundation models on three datasets, finding even a few rotated photos reduce camera pose accuracy for every model, and confidence does not reliably flag the failures. Most official image loaders ignore the orientation tag, and tested fixes only partially solve the problem. The paper calls for orientation checks in reconstruction pipelines.

entry.title: Fast Anatomy-Aware Diffeomorphic Augmentation for Brain MRI

author.name: Tonmoy Hossain, Alexandra G. Roberts, Mark Olchanyi, Jonathan Williams Ramirez, Stefan Brandst\"atter, Juan Eugenio Iglesias

entry.summary: BrainAug is an anatomy-aware augmentation framework for brain MRI that generates anatomically coordinated diffeomorphic deformations without requiring large population cohorts. It improves on random nonlinear deformation fields by capturing spatial dependencies among morphological changes across brain regions.

entry.title: Decompose, Verify, Evolve: Physically Grounded Shape Decomposition

author.name: Wenchao Ma, Rui Yu, Fan Zhu, Jiachen Liu, Sharon X. Huang

entry.summary: Introduces PhysDec, an agentic framework that uses a pretrained vision-language model to predict material-aware primitive decompositions of 3D objects from a few images. An iterative pipeline reasons about part structure, uses reference point clouds for geometric feedback, and applies physical verifiers to enforce stability and plausibility.

entry.title: CSC-Mamba: Bridging multimodal convolutional sparse coding and state space models for multi-contrast MRI super-resolution

author.name: Iman Marivani, David Van Hamme, Jan Aelterman, Wilfried Philips

entry.summary: CSC-Mamba unifies deep-unfolded convolutional sparse coding with state space models (Mamba) for multi-contrast MRI super-resolution, combining principled cross-contrast fusion priors with Mamba's global context modeling. This addresses limitations of both heuristic fusion in pure deep networks and shallow unrolled model-based methods. The result is theoretically grounded reconstruction for accelerated clinical MRI protocols.

entry.title: CaveBench: Benchmarking Abductive Physical Reasoning from Internal Observations
