author.name: Guanxin Lin (Tsinghua University), Chen Yang (Tsinghua University), Shenxiang Zeng (Tsinghua University), Honghui Zhu (Tsinghua University), Xin Li (Tsinghua University), Wenbo Deng (Tsinghua University), Jiansheng Fan (Tsinghua University), Chen Wang (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: CaveBench tests whether vision-language models can perform abductive physical reasoning: given apparatus descriptions and internal observations while external controls are hidden, models must infer the operations causing observed responses. It spans 20 apparatus scenes across five physical domains with 10,200 simulated episodes.

entry.title: LRQ-Cache: Compressing Feature Caches in Video Diffusion via Low-Rank Approximation and Quantization

author.name: Ruizhe Yao, Zhen Huang, Songpan Gao, Danyi Liu, Zijian Cao, Weijie Zheng, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: LRQ-Cache addresses the huge memory footprint of temporal feature caching in video diffusion transformers, where predictive caches can reach 109-346 GiB per video. It compresses cached features via low-rank approximation and quantization so that caching remains beneficial on single GPUs without CPU offloading or multi-GPU sharding.

entry.title: ViDM: Efficient and Order-Robust Parallel Visual Decision Making

author.name: Xudong Tan, Peng Ye, Chenyu Huang, Yaoxin Yang, Huafeng Qin, Tao Chen

entry.summary: ViDM reformulates multi-question visual decision-making as a single parallel forward pass, organizing shared visual context, multiple questions, and decision slots into one sequence. This avoids the token-by-token decoding costs of autoregressive multimodal LLMs and reduces prediction variance caused by question ordering.

entry.title: Smooth Essential-Manifold Residuals for View-Graph Calibration

author.name: Viktor Larsson, Johannes Sch\"onberger

entry.summary: The paper derives a smooth two-dimensional residual formulation for view-graph camera calibration by reducing essential-matrix constraints to 2x2 matrices, replacing the rank-deficient singular-value formulation used conventionally. This yields better Gauss-Newton convergence for jointly estimating camera intrinsics from pairwise fundamental matrices.

entry.title: HazeFlux: Few-Step Generative Priors for Real-World Image Dehazing

author.name: Yunong Liu, Danna Xue, Javier Vazquez-Corral

entry.summary: HazeFlux adapts the generative prior of a few-step flow-matching model to real-world single-image dehazing via a two-stage framework that first fine-tunes the latent backbone with LoRA. The approach tackles the domain-shift problem where models trained on synthetic haze fail on real haze, while addressing generative models' weak pixel fidelity and latent-space detail loss.

entry.title: SplatSeg3D: Efficient Zero-Shot 3D Segmentation via Point Cloud Surfelization and Splatting

author.name: Sandeep Inuganti, Mahdi Chamseddine, Marcel Rogge, Martin R. Oswald, Didier Stricker, Jason Rambach

entry.summary: SplatSeg3D performs open-vocabulary segmentation of bare colored point clouds without needing registered images, camera poses, class supervision, or instance mask proposals. It surfelizes the point cloud into oriented 2D Gaussians, renders views via splatting with a coverage-maximizing view selection, and applies 2D foundation models to achieve zero-shot 3D segmentation.

entry.title: DOPER: Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited

author.name: Hugo Hadfield, Alperen Degirmenci, Jonathan Tremblay

entry.summary: DOPER is an RGB 6D pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction, recovering pose of known objects via Perspective-n-Point with synthetic-to-real adaptation and optional heatmap refinement. Starting from underspecified CAD models, it progressively refines both the object representation and the pose estimator.

entry.title: FocusAnchor: Zero-Shot Metric Depth by Anchoring a Depth Foundation Prior to Focus Cues

author.name: Ashkan Ganj, Hang Su, Tian Guo

entry.summary: FocusAnchor is a recurrent model that uses depth-volume lookups and repeatedly aligns a relative depth prior from a frozen foundation model with current depth estimates, carrying metric scale from strongly textured regions into weak-focus regions in a feedback loop. Includes synthetic training stacks with randomized camera parameters for cross-camera transfer and analysis of synthesis-induced artifacts.

entry.title: E-MAPS: Event-Based Promptable Video Segmentation with Memory-as-Prompt

author.name: Adonay Demewez Gebremedhin, Mohamad Alansari, Wessam Shehieb, Muzammal Naseer, Hasan AlMarzouqi, Sajid Javed, Naoufel Werghi

entry.summary: Formalizes event-based promptable video segmentation (ePVS), where prompts at arbitrary windows initialize, correct, or introduce objects in event streams, and presents E-MAPS, which transfers a pretrained promptable segmenter to events using Event-to-Token alignment and a memory-as-prompt mechanism for propagation and correction. Targets RGB failure cases under fast motion and adverse illumination.

entry.title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models

author.name: Amir Razlighi, Zhuo Ning, Naomi Ken Korem, Nisarg Patel, Yiorgos Chrysanthou, Daniel Cohen-Or, Ali Mahdavi Amiri

entry.summary: RML combines a lip reader, a language model, and an audio-visual generative model to recover speech when audio is missing, noisy, or corrupted by competing speakers. The lip reader proposes articulation hypotheses, the language model resolves ambiguity via context, and the generator reconstructs synchronized speech preserving speaker identity, with reliability-weighted selection among multiple reconstructions. It targets realistic partially-observable speech scenarios.

entry.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation

author.name: Shamak Dutta, Biswadip Dey

entry.summary: Analyzes gradient errors in differentiable simulation of ellipsoid impacts, showing that linear time-of-impact estimates produce errors growing with collision obliqueness, contact curvature, time step, and unmodeled spin. It derives exact collision gradients via continuous collision detection on the Perram-Wertheim contact function, improving reliability of gradients at impact moments.

entry.title: SkillHarness: Execution-Aware Coordination with Plug-and-Play Skills for Long-Horizon Traversal

author.name: Bailin He, Xiting Zhao, Kang Wang, Xinyu Zhou, Yongxing Cui, Haojie Liu, Qiao Sun, Hongyan Zhang, Wenqiang Zhang

entry.summary: SkillHarness is an execution-aware coordination framework that composes a plug-and-play library of locomotion skills for terrain traversal, with a perceptive RL approach that preserves task-relevant environmental references while handling perceptual disturbances and unreliable skill transitions.

entry.title: Keypose or Dense? A Controlled Comparison of Action Representations for Stage-Structured Manipulation

author.name: Haizhou Ge, Mengshuo Wang, Zhixing Chen, Lei Han, Chen Wang, Lu Shi, Guyue Zhou, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: This work presents a controlled comparison of keypose versus dense action representations for imitation learning in stage-structured manipulation, holding chunk length, demonstrations, architectures, and update budgets fixed across simulation and a real robot. It examines robustness when demonstrations are slowed, paused, and rerouted.

entry.title: Frequency-Conditioned Privacy Auditing of Fine-Tuned Language Models

author.name: Aymen Noor, Ke Lyu, Honglu Jiang

entry.summary: This study examines how often sensitive information (emails, phone numbers) must appear in fine-tuning data before it becomes recoverable during generation, varying duplication frequency from 1x to 50x across four language models and comparing standard, gradient-clipped, and differentially private training. It distinguishes memorization from actual recoverable leakage, providing a frequency-conditioned audit framework for privacy risk.

entry.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering

author.name: Ruijie Ma, Haoyue Liu, Mingda Zhang, Dongxu Yue, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: CoverMem addresses episodic-memory embodied question answering under computational budgets via coverage-constrained memory construction that selects compact informative frames, a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy, and retrieval mechanisms to answer questions from recorded visual observations. It tackles growing histories and uneven observation quality across viewpoints.

entry.title: SPARQL-Planned Single-Hop Traversal over a Live Knowledge Graph for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Priyesh Vakharia, Masud Moshtaghi, Pratyay Banerjee, Nicholas Jedema, Amita Misra, Ankit Chadha

entry.summary: The paper interleaves dense retrieval with knowledge-graph traversal for multi-hop question answering, using dense retrieval to locate relevant regions at good recall while planned SPARQL single-hop traversals over a live knowledge graph refine precision, avoiding the cost and noise of naive multi-hop expansion. This breaks the recall-precision tradeoff of standard GraphRAG approaches.

entry.title: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness

author.name: Tigran Fahradyan, Riccardo Ali, Sergio Calvo-Ordo\~nez, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Pietro Li\`o, \'Alvaro Arroyo

entry.summary: The paper connects the massive-activation phenomenon in LLMs, previously linked to attention sinks and signal propagation, to region migration in delayed robustness under a spline-theoretic view of deep networks. It shows massive activations push representations away from nonlinearity boundaries, simplifying the network's input-output map around data points.

entry.title: ArEssays: Towards Robust Arabic Handwritten Text Understanding in Educational Settings

author.name: Hamdy Mubarak, Anas Madkoor, Ehsaneddin Asgari, Majd Hawasly

entry.summary: ArEssays is a large-scale dataset of authentic handwritten Arabic student essays from Egyptian primary to secondary students, with verbatim transcriptions and linguistically corrected versions. Benchmarking 34 vision-language and OCR models reveals large performance gaps on real children's handwriting. The release supports progress in Arabic OCR, document understanding, and educational NLP.

entry.title: FOL-Proof: Verifying LLM Text-to-Logic Translations via Deterministic Semantics

author.name: Yisrael Clark, Guy Katz

entry.summary: FOL-Proof is a semantic firewall pipeline that validates LLM-generated first-order logic translations against independently derived linguistic interpretations. It deterministically obtains candidate translations using the English Resource Grammar and Minimal Recursion Semantics, then applies an SMT solver to check logical equivalence with the LLM's formula, accepting faithful translations. This guards downstream reasoning against semantically unfaithful logic conversions.

entry.title: RISE: Reasoning with Implicit State Embeddings for GUI Agents

author.name: Enqi Liu, Zhi Gao, Liu Liu, Lifeng Fan, Liyuan Pan

entry.summary: RISE integrates action-relevant chain-of-thought reasoning into implicit state representations for GUI agents, avoiding over-reliance on explicit reasoning patterns during training. It uses three complementary supervision objectives: full-CoT state alignment, action-distribution alignment, and reasoning-to-action binding. This aims to improve generalizable action prediction over explicit-CoT training.

entry.title: Beyond Static Charts: Benchmarking Interactive Chart-to-Code Generation for MLLMs

author.name: Yuhan Bian, Haoyu Liu, Siyu Li, Hanpei Guo, Jingrong Gao, Zhixu Li

entry.summary: ChartInt is the first benchmark for interactive chart-to-code generation, with 2,779 annotated examples that evaluate whether generated code behaves correctly across sequences of user interactions rather than just matching a static visual. This shifts evaluation from visual consistency to behavioral consistency, requiring multi-step state-based assessment.

entry.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step

author.name: Zhanwen Chen, Tianchun Wang

entry.summary: The authors model GUI agent failures caused by timing misalignment across four events (environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, action receipt) and introduce ChronotopeGym with Paused, Replay, and Live execution modes to study them. They show agents can fail in live settings despite meeting deadlines, and present an accelerator-resident controller, Chronotope, that selectively keeps interaction history to stay in step with changing interfaces.

entry.title: Verified Proof Refactoring with Codex and Qwen

author.name: Lazar Milikic, Gordan {\DJ}uri\'c, Viktor Kun\v{c}ak

entry.summary: The authors use a locally served Qwen model with the open-source Codex CLI to refactor existing Lean 4 proofs, shortening source and reducing checking cost while preserving theorem statements across Lean versions. Replacements are kept only if they improve the objective and verify on every required version, followed by a deterministic CPU refinement pass. The system placed first in the open-source LLM track of Lean Refactor Arena, passing all 127 proof-version checks.

entry.title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning

author.name: Shanmuga Venkatachalam, Quinn Jacobson, John Paul Shen

entry.summary: NeuTNN-AV is a hardware-amenable spiking multimodal substrate built on the NeuroAI Temporal Neural Network, using neurons with multiple active dendritic segments and low-precision parameters. It matches or outperforms state-of-the-art spiking baselines on audio-visual classification with a fraction of the synapse counts, supporting online learning. It departs from the trend of bolting deep-learning machinery and 32-bit parameters onto SNNs.

entry.title: CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Xiaoxuan Chen, Aijun Yang, Xiaohua Wang

entry.summary: CAPE addresses the problem that tool calls can fail when the receiving tool's hidden configuration (delimiters, date formats, record layouts) differs from the agent's assumptions. It is a training-free compiler that jointly allocates a fixed budget between calibrating candidate calls on candidate configurations and searching for a working policy, always maintaining an executable policy.

entry.title: From Rule-based to Agentic: LLM Agent based Real-time Control of Urban Drainage Systems for Flooding and Sewer Overflow Mitigation

author.name: Wenchong Tian, Shixun Li, Ruozhou Lin, Peng Ye, Zhiyu Zhang, Shi Tao, Yu-Qi Wang, Ling Shi, Mingfu Guan, Haoran Duan, Zhiguo Yuan

entry.summary: AgenticAI-Control is an agentic framework for real-time control of urban drainage systems that assimilates multi-source meteorological early warnings, using two coupled LLM agents to retrieve warnings and fuse them with domain engineering expertise to generate control strategies. It is validated in simulation on a combined sewer catchment in eastern China.

entry.title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Pengyu Hou, Mingfei Han, Haihong Hao, Xiaolong Wu, Bo Dong, Xiaojun Chang, Salman Khan, Bin Shi

entry.summary: PoseVLN proposes using camera pose as a natural geometric representation to unify past experience, current spatial state, and future motion in vision-language navigation, jointly learning navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. It organizes visual memory and current observations in an episode-consistent pose-aware framework.

entry.title: RubikSQL-HB: Agentic Text-to-SQL with Knowledge in the Loop

author.name: Haorui Jia, Zihan Qu, Yundi Dong, Ziyang Mei, Chi Zhang, Zezhi Zheng, Dousheng Zhao, Jiahao Zhang, Zui Chen, Han Li

entry.summary: RubikSQL-HB exposes business meanings, stored values, and reference queries through queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces that agents can access throughout SQL construction, with a downstream Judge reusing the same interfaces to investigate disagreements between candidate agents. On a 500-question BIRD Mini-Dev evaluation the full pipeline reaches 75.2 percent. It demonstrates that interleaving knowledge access with execution beats treating schema alone as the agent context.

entry.title: scOPD: Routed On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM-Based Single-Cell Annotation

author.name: Zhiyin Yu, Yuchen Mou, Songtao Huang, Shuaiyu Zhang, Xing Wei, Chunchun Chen, Wei Ye, Xiao Luo, Zhonghai Wu, Xiangchao Yan, Lei Bai, Shiyang Feng, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: scOPD addresses limitations of scalar-reward training for LLM-based single-cell annotation by introducing on-policy self-distillation with routed supervision, targeting batch-level annotation that must satisfy global one-to-one matching constraints. It adds fine-grained reasoning supervision during training and uncertainty-aware refinement during inference to locate uncertain predictions.

entry.title: Below the Stopwatch: Checking the Performance Claims of Coding Agents in the Kernel

author.name: Yuvraj Sehgal, Sneh Patel, Mahsa Panahandeh, Naser Ezzati-Jivan

entry.summary: Below is a pipeline that verifies whether coding-agent pull requests actually achieve speedups for the stated reasons, by extracting claimed mechanisms from 1,343 performance PRs and mapping them to kernel and hardware signals measured via hardware counters and LTTng traces. It finds that most claims are not measurable as stated, exposing a gap between agent-reported and mechanistically verified performance improvements.

entry.title: What You See Is What You Certify: Concept-Based Certificates for Unseen Compositions

author.name: Phuc Linh Ngo, Thang Nguyen Duc, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Hung Cao

entry.summary: This paper examines when concept-based model decisions can serve as certificates, finding that standard joint concept bottleneck and concept embedding models certify wrong classes 93-94% of the time on unseen attribute combinations despite correct ontologies, due to concept leakage and cross-concept shortcut copying. A gated variant trained only on visible parts improves this to 60%.

entry.title: EventSSM: Causal Spatial-State Modelling for Asynchronous Events Event-Depth Estimation

author.name: Sadiq O. Macaulay, Dipon Ghosh, Hadfield Simon

entry.summary: EventSSM is a causal recurrent state-space framework for metric-depth estimation from event cameras that processes chronological event packets without collapsing them into frame-like representations. It bridges asynchronous predictions and sparse frame-time supervision using geometric transport with calibrated camera poses and differentiable rendering, improving on established event-depth baselines.

entry.title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control

author.name: Jeong Woon Lee, Namho Kim, Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: POISE improves smooth control in actor-critic RL by regularizing the critic rather than the actor, characterizing the greedy-action displacement (greedy shift) across state transitions to first order under local concavity. Its curvature-weighted analysis addresses a limitation of prior critic-regularization approaches like PAVE, where separate penalties on gradient variation and curvature do not measure how the critic's preferred action actually moves.

entry.title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?

author.name: Sajjad Pakdamansavoji

entry.summary: CALVIN-MAX is a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN five-instruction chains, each testing how a single mid-execution change to objects, camera, robot, or instruction affects robot policy success. By comparing matched runs with the change absent, present from the start, or arriving mid-task, it separates the cost of timing from the cost of the altered world. This provides a rigorous diagnostic tool for evaluating robustness of robot policies to dynamics that shift while acting.

entry.title: Calm Agent: Reframing Agent Interaction around Intermittent Human Attention

author.name: Dian Jin, Zixun Fu, Guan Wang, Yancheng Yuan

entry.summary: This position paper proposes Calm Agent, a design framework for AI agents performing ongoing auxiliary tasks around intermittent human attention, connecting Delegate, Adjust, and Check interaction modes through a persistent task representation. It demonstrates the principles with Orvlet, a desktop prototype. The work is significant as agent interaction design becomes central as agentic systems deploy at scale.

entry.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation

author.name: Kevin D. Nguetche, Atif Belal, Lilian Hollard, Eric Granger, Marco Pedersoli

entry.summary: VIDE is a training-free video anomaly detection framework that adapts text-derived anomaly scoring to each test video using frozen CLIP embeddings, estimating normal scene conditions per video instead of using a shared text-based normality reference. This reduces false positives from anomaly bias and prompt sensitivity compared to methods like PRISM.

entry.title: Verify then Steer: Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery for Continuous Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Jiewen Hou, Guanxiang Qi, Meina Kan, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies progress hallucination in vision-and-language navigation, where agents misinterpret off-route observations as evidence of task progress, blocking recovery to earlier sub-instructions. PHAR is a test-time verify-then-steer framework that checks instruction progress and steers the agent back on track. It addresses a specific, well-diagnosed failure mode in embodied navigation.

entry.title: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization

author.name: Yushi Long, Juzhan Xu, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Yin Chen, Sida Peng, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou

entry.summary: RoboRecast augments real robot demonstrations using simulation, jointly optimizing the simulated scene and robot motion so source-task interactions remain executable when objects, layouts, or robots change. An agent diagnoses interaction failures using simulation feedback and iteratively revises scene or motion parameters until the demonstration transfers.

entry.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems

author.name: Guowei Guan, Yurong Hao, Jiaming Zhang, Fuyao Zhang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: The paper shows that multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion, typically viewed as robustness mechanisms in MLLM-based recommenders, can introduce a compression-to-consensus bias where signals salient after compression and consistent across modalities gain disproportionate ranking influence. It introduces C3H, an attack exploiting this bias for content manipulation.

entry.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Xuan Yao, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a world model for embodied visual tracking that conditions latent state transitions on predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion, using a Geometry-Progress module to jointly model route selection and travel progress under uncertainty. This improves future-state prediction when both target motion and viewpoint changes affect observations. It is relevant to robot tracking and embodied decision-making.

entry.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations

author.name: Karl El Hajal, Mathew Magimai. -Doss

entry.summary: ClusterVAD is an unsupervised voice activity detection method built on frozen speech foundation model representations, clustering them once on a small untranscribed set and labeling clusters via sonority, eliminating thresholds and labeled data. It avoids the domain and annotation biases of supervised detectors and the far-field degradation of hand-crafted features. This is a practical improvement for speech pipeline front-ends.

entry.title: Is 4 Bits Enough for EEG Sleep Staging? A Subject-Level Benchmark of MXFP4, NVFP4 and FP8

author.name: Emese Batizi, Hossein Valavi

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks 13 post-training quantization configurations from FP16 to block-scaled 4-bit formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) for single-channel EEG sleep staging, using subject-wise cross-validation, multiple seeds, and value-exact emulation. Eight- and sixteen-bit formats nearly match FP32, and 4-bit quantization costs at most about 1.2 points of Macro-F1 for temporal-context networks, supporting on-device sleep staging.

entry.title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design

author.name: Santiago A. Cadena, Andrea Merlo

entry.summary: CHORD is a conditional variational autoencoder for stellarator fusion-reactor design that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent interpolation conditioning. The goal is to explore trade-offs between feasible designs without repeating expensive PDE-constrained optimization.

entry.title: JevBench: Metamorphic Coherence Testing for Typed Probabilistic Decision Models

author.name: Chen Feng

entry.summary: JevBench tests whether typed probabilistic decision models return coherent probability distributions when the same input is reworded, negated, combined, or given different option sets, using 50 metamorphic relations each encoding a law of probability or choice. The JevBench-240 suite provides 12,000 label-free coherence tests across 240 synthetic cases.

entry.title: Boundary Representation-Driven Graph Transformer Modeling for Machining Operation Sequencing

author.name: Fatemeh Elhambakhsh, Gaurav Ameta, Aditi Roy, Hyunwoong Ko

entry.summary: Proposes a graph transformer framework that predicts machining operation sequences directly from B-Rep CAD geometry, replacing expert-driven rule-based process planning. By exploiting full boundary representations rather than simplified voxels or hand-crafted features, it captures richer geometric and topological information for manufacturing automation.

entry.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Muyun Lu, Jose E Aguilar Escamilla, Huazheng Wang, Ying Lin

entry.summary: Reformulates multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization as a fused Gaussian process bandit problem, jointly modeling dependencies across fidelity levels to avoid oversimplified correlation assumptions and heuristic acquisitions. Provides theoretical performance guarantees for strategically trading off accuracy and evaluation cost.

entry.title: Pando: Noise-Coupled Parallel Draft Trees for Efficient Edge Speculative Decoding

author.name: Joren Dumoulin, Hyoukjun Kwon, Subhankar Pal, Steven Li, Vignesh Vivekraja, Marian Verhelst

entry.summary: Pando improves speculative decoding on edge devices by building dynamic draft trees on top of parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark, removing the block-size cap on draft chains and better exploiting the idle compute and verification budget. This targets the memory-bound nature of autoregressive LLM inference on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Meets t-SNE: Integrated Visualization without Batch Effects in OT-tSNE

author.name: Azhar Akhmetova, Edward Eichhorn, Boris Landa, Dmitry Kobak, Sebastian Damrich

entry.summary: OT-tSNE replaces nearest-neighbor-based cross-batch matching in integrated t-SNE visualization with globally coupled affinities derived from entropic optimal transport. Controlled experiments show nearest-neighbor methods deteriorate under challenging cross-batch geometries while optimal-transport affinities remain robust, improving joint visualization under batch effects.

entry.title: Tabra Blends: Improving the Accuracy--Latency Trade-off with Complementary Tabular Models

author.name: Jing Jia, Guanyang Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows a compact two-model ensemble of tabular foundation models (four-estimator Kumo plus one LimiX) reaches 2063.8 Elo on 816 TabArena splits, 45.4 points above the top published entry, with 15-98% lower fit-and-predict time than its components. Prediction diversity between the models explains the error reduction.

entry.title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks

author.name: Octave Gaspard

entry.summary: GREMLIN explores whether randomly parameterized neural environments can supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm, using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework with sixteen generated games. After 224.8M agent-environment steps, the trained learning rule beats its untrained teacher across 26 games but DQN still outscores it on most games, leaving competitiveness with hand-designed training open.

entry.title: The Recycler: In-Transit Machine Learning on High-Fidelity Data from Simulation Campaigns as an Optimized Approach for Building Frontier Models

author.name: Nikhil Rao, Mark Berrill, Ankush Checkervarty, Alexander Debus, Greg Eisenhauer, Ana Gainaru, Scott Klasky, Julian Lenz, Tapish Narwal, Vedhas Pandit, Richard Pausch, Norbert Podhorszki, Franz P\"oschel, Ulrich Schramm, Klaus Steiniger, Jessica Tiebel, Ren\'e Widera, Nico Wrobel, Yongqi Xiang, Michael Bussmann, Sunita Chandrasekaran, Jeffrey Kelling

entry.summary: This systems paper reports the first realization of in-transit machine learning, training on data streamed from multiple parallel simulations on the same exascale HPC system rather than going through the file system. The workflow targets simulation campaigns for accelerators, fusion, climate, and materials design, where data production rates overwhelm storage-based pipelines.

entry.title: KKT Atlas: Learning Low-Dimensional Local Scenario Models for Contextual Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Zhengzhong Ricky You, Baichuan Mo, Yuan Zhou, Jinhua Zhao, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

entry.summary: KKT Atlas speeds up contextual stochastic optimization by partitioning context space into local charts and learning low-dimensional scenario representations from decision gradients. It provides theoretical guarantees that few scenarios suffice to approximate conditional KKT optimality, with decision and risk bounds.

entry.title: Interpretable Orthogonal Latent Diffusion with Scale-Selective Uncertainty for Medical Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Onkar Jadhav, Tim French

entry.summary: Med-PODiff is a patch-wise proper orthogonal decomposition diffusion framework for brain MRI super-resolution that separates low-rank anatomical variation from fine-detail residual variation. This enables decomposing predictive uncertainty into coarse and fine components, helping identify hallucinated fine-scale content in generative reconstructions.

entry.title: Data-driven Reduced-order Modeling of a Multistable Viscoelastic Flow

author.name: Shaoxuan Chen, Su Yang, Simon J. Haward, Amy Q. Shen, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis

entry.summary: This paper develops a data-driven framework for learning a two-dimensional, parameter-dependent normal form of the bifurcation structure of viscoelastic flow past side-by-side microcylinders, using sparse measurements of stable flow states. By enforcing measured steady states as stable equilibria, the method reconstructs symmetric, converging, diverging, and multistable flow regimes without trajectory data. It matters because it extends learned reduced-order models to bistable and tristable physical systems where only equilibrium data is available.

entry.title: Tablassert: Declarative Extraction of Knowledge Graphs from Biomedical Tables

author.name: Skye L. Goetz, Jared C. Roach, Gw\^enlyn Glusman

entry.summary: Tablassert converts tabular data from biomedical publications, especially supplemental tables, into knowledge graphs compatible with the NCATS Biomedical Data Translator, using YAML declarations mapping table data to subject-predicate-object-qualifier statements. It resolves free text to standard identifiers, enabling structured extraction of knowledge that appears only in tables. This addresses a real gap in biomedical knowledge integration pipelines.

entry.title: Evaluating Latent Knowledge Stability in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Chuancheng Shi, Shangze Li, Wenhua Wu, Zifeng Cheng, Pengyang Shao, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: The paper evaluates how image viewpoint and question formulation changes affect latent knowledge representations in multimodal LLMs, from answer preference and internal support perspectives. It introduces the margin retention score (MRS), measuring first-order degradation of the initial answer's logit margin over competing options across elicitation conditions. This provides a finer-grained probe of representation robustness than output correctness alone.

entry.title: From Grammar Deltas to Token Masks: Incremental Constrained Decoding under Runtime Grammar Evolution

author.name: Hantao Hua, Jiming Su, Yonggang Che, Feng Zhu

entry.summary: GramDelta is an incremental method for grammar-constrained decoding when constraints evolve during generation (from new declarations, inferred types, or runtime feedback), avoiding full reconstruction of parser state when a first-seen grammar update changes state induced by an already committed prefix. It maintains constraint state incrementally as grammar deltas arrive, converting them into token masks. This improves efficiency of structured generation in code and DSL settings.

entry.title: Look Where Camouflage Breaks: Concealment-Guided Observation for Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Dingming Zhang, Fengyang Xiao, Jingjia Feng, Chunming He, Sina Farsiu

entry.summary: CamoBreak introduces an active observation framework for camouflaged object detection built on a Concealment Spectrum that measures regional resemblance and boundary ambiguity across comparison scales. These measurements distinguish persistent concealment from separability emerging at other scales and guide crop selection from the captured image for recognition. This connects the scale structure of camouflage to the evidence a new view can reveal.

entry.title: Adapt, Label, Distill: Foundation-Model Supervision for Efficient Object Detection

author.name: Zhengye Yang, Anthony Wang, Yuyang Li, Mehmet Kerem Turkcan, Beizhan Yan, Zoran Kostic

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline that adapts SAM3 as a teacher on limited labeled data, generates confidence-weighted pseudo-labels, and distills into compact YOLOv11 student detectors for real-time deployment in specialized domains. Zero-gating retains uncertain hypotheses during label assignment without applying their gradients.

entry.title: A Well-Posed Fourth-Order Navier-Stokes Model for Image Inpainting: Theory, Order Selection, and Stripe Decomposition

author.name: Yiwen Dou, Yiqiang Ding, Zhongyun Bao, Senyan Zhao

entry.summary: This paper constructs a well-posed fourth-order extension of the Bertalmio-Bertozzi-Sapiro Navier-Stokes inpainting model, showing that the naive correction is Hadamard ill-posed while a forward-sign gated fourth-order term is uniformly parabolic and energy-stable. An order-dissipation principle and stripe decomposition provide theory and practical guidance.

entry.title: DUALingo: A Dual-Hand Instruction-Guided Dataset for Affordance Grounding on 3D Objects

author.name: Ming-Lun Lee, Yi-En Li, Feng-Dian Su, Ming-Han Lee, Kun-Ru Wu, Krzysztof Czarnecki, Yu-Chee Tseng

entry.summary: Presents DUALingo, a large-scale dataset for task-conditioned, role-aware bimanual affordance grounding on 3D objects, representing tasks as two cooperative hand-agnostic roles grounded as heatmaps. It contains 271K free-form tasks over 71K objects, generated at scale to avoid manual annotation of dual-hand contacts.

entry.title: Distractors are the Real Enemy: Visual Distraction Adversarial Perturbations on SAM2-Based Video Tracking and Segmentation

author.name: Adonay Demewez Gebremedhin, Mohamad Alansari, Wessam Shehieb, Muzammal Naseer

entry.summary: Analyzes adversarial robustness of SAM2-based promptable video tracking, showing existing attacks focus on local mask degradation while distractor interference is underexplored. The proposed DistractAttack is a white-box attack exploiting distractor cues that SAM2 itself exposes when tracking is uncertain.

entry.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition

author.name: Sirui Liang, Xuanlong Yu, Longfei Liu, Xiaodong Cun, Xi Shen

entry.summary: LoopDVR converts pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks by reusing Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and decoder. It selects sharing groups based on inter-layer representation dissimilarity and keeps the final backbone block independent to preserve multi-scale features. This reduces parameters while retaining the original computational structure.

entry.title: What to Change, What to Keep: Experience-Evolving Agents for Video Recasting

author.name: Shiying Zhang, Yuxia Zhu, Huaze Xue, Shengqi Dang, Yizhen Wu, Yijie Li

entry.summary: RecastAgent is an experience-guided agentic framework for video recasting, transforming entities and environments while preserving actions and interactions, all under frozen model weights. An Experience-Guided Planner selects edit prompts and input states with visual critique, enabling backtracking, while an Experience Accumulation module distills completed trajectories across tasks. This addresses coherent multi-step video editing with frozen generators.

entry.title: GUI-WEdit and GUI-SkillEvo: Gradient-Free Adaptation of Small GUI Agents

author.name: Haixia Bi, Yingtian Chen, Sihan Yang, Zuzheng Kuang, Yuzhen Tong, Kai Fu, Zhengyong Wan

entry.summary: The paper presents two gradient-free adaptations of small GUI agent models: GUI-WEdit-4B applies guarded closed-form weight updates from trajectory feedback to a late MLP (changing only 0.535 percent of parameters), and GUI-SkillEvo-2B iteratively refines procedural skills with fixed weights. Evaluation is on a 361-task OSWorld subset.

entry.title: PRC4D: Physical Relation-Constrained Persistent 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Junho Kim, Hyunyoung Choi, Jiseok Kim, Seongwon Lee

entry.summary: PRC4D improves 4D reconstruction by identifying reliable rigid relations between objects and using them, together with 3D contact and relative motion consistency plus sequence-level verification, to maintain spatial coherence through occlusion. It avoids the incorrect motion constraints that arise when short-term contact or shared motion is wrongly treated as persistent rigidity.

entry.title: ObsBridge: Observation-Grounded Conditioning for Ego Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Zhenhao Wang, Shaofeng Liang, Jiemin Wu, Sijia Chen, Keni Shi, Nan Li, Wenshuo Chen, Bowen Tian, Runwei Guan, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: ObsBridge improves pedestrian trajectory forecasting from ego-camera views by conditioning future prediction on both recovered historical states and raw observation evidence, using progressive training. This targets the failure mode where predictors trained on clean histories break down when occlusion and tracking errors corrupt inputs at deployment.

entry.title: SetCon: Setup-Conditioned IMU-Language Learning from 3D Human Motion

author.name: Lennart Schiweck, Alaa Saleh, Crist\'obal Curio

entry.summary: SetCon improves IMU-language models for zero-shot activity recognition by replacing full mounting invariance with selective invariance: it estimates each device's mounting from a few unlabeled windows and conditions the encoder on this estimate. This preserves orientation cues like gravity direction that distinguish sitting, standing, and lying, using the worn body as a calibration target.

entry.title: FewRef-5: Fixed-Reference Test-Time Adaptation for Virtual Staining

author.name: Wenxuan Wang, Liwen Wang, Mingmin Wu, Xingbo Dong, Zhe Jin

entry.summary: This paper proposes FewRef-5, a test-time adaptation method for virtual staining that synthesizes Masson's trichrome images from routine H&E slides. It extracts tissue-masked optical-density statistics from a small set of real reference patches to form a fixed stain target, enabling query-specific correction of stain appearance at deployment without retraining the generator.

entry.title: AnyPrune: Optimization-Free Pruning for Any Feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting Pipeline

author.name: Nicola Leonetti, Federico Stella, Aoxiang Fan, Saqib Javed, Pascal Fua, Luigi Di Stefano

entry.summary: AnyPrune is a transformer-based module that prunes redundant Gaussians from any feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline without costly re-optimization, preserving the single-forward-pass property. It exploits richer information than simple heuristic pruning to drastically reduce memory and storage of the reconstructed representations.

entry.title: Aqua2CAD : Observation-Guided Point Cloud Correction and Completion for CAD Reconstruction from Underwater Stereo Images

author.name: Weizhao Huang, Jiayi Zhang, Pangkit Fong, Chongrong Fang, Jianping He

entry.summary: Presents Aqua2CAD, a two-stage pipeline that reconstructs editable CAD models from underwater stereo images by first correcting and filtering noisy point clouds using cross-view disagreement and ray evidence, then applying a learned shape prior conditioned on multi-view observations to infer missing surfaces. Reports a 60% relative reduction in point-cloud Chamfer distance on an OceanSim-based synthetic benchmark.

entry.title: MESSI: Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration for Physics-Based Character Control

author.name: Xiaogang Peng, Jiaqi Zou, Lei Zhong, Sirui Xu, Huaizu Jiang

entry.summary: MESSI enables smooth transitions between diverse physics-based soccer skills by training eight task-competent experts with motion priors and task rewards, distilling them into a unified skill-conditioned Transformer, and learning a shared context-dependent adaptation for transitions while preserving original skill policies elsewhere. Targets seamless multi-skill control such as dribbling into a shot.

entry.title: Proxy Metrics Can Hide Downstream Collapse: A Case Study on Compressed Cellular Segmentation

author.name: Sebasti\'an A. Cruz Romero

entry.summary: This case study shows that common output-level proxy metrics (NRMSE, cosine similarity, flow angular error) fail to predict downstream mask retention when quantizing Cellpose-SAM for cellular segmentation, with cosine similarity of 0.944 co-occurring with 89 of 245 empty masks. It warns that compression screening pipelines can hide functional collapse.

entry.title: BendGS: Observation-Conditioned Gaussian Self-Modeling for Continuum Robots

author.name: Jeong Woon Lee, Doungjun Kim, Namho Kim, Seungheon Chae, Jongwoo Kim, Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: BendGS uses 3D Gaussians to build visual self-models for continuum robots, estimating a virtual backbone from observations to drive command-conditioned Gaussian deformation without measured joint angles. This enables next-state prediction of 3D shape, appearance, and tip pose together. It extends Gaussian-splatting self-modeling beyond articulated robots to continuously bending mechanisms.

entry.title: Accelerating Dynamic Route Re-solving via Robust Solver Evolution in Automatic Heuristic Design

author.name: Yizhuo Ma, Haoran Sun, Shuang Liang, Muquan Li, Qizhi Chen, Renzhong Wang, Nan Chen, Lunxu Liu, Ke Qin

entry.summary: Studies inefficiencies in LLM-based automatic heuristic design (AHD) for multi-goal route planning when request data changes during execution, attributing re-solving overhead to static-overfitting where evolved solvers repeatedly explore overlapping local neighborhoods. It proposes a robust solver evolution approach that accelerates dynamic route re-solving for TSP-style problems.

entry.title: Delay-Tolerant Formation Tracking for Multi-AGV Systems via Reference-Shift Coupling

author.name: Yunfei Bi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a cascade control design for cooperative AGV formation transport over wireless links with time-varying delays, where delayed neighbor data only shifts each vehicle's reference through a second-order filter rather than entering the tracking loop. Bounded error is proven for arbitrary delays with convergence guarantees for bounded delay.

entry.title: At the Limit: Autonomous Vehicle Drifting under Generative Policies

author.name: Jie He, Meixun Qu, Cheng Hu, Lei Xie, Ezio Bartocci, Radu Grosu

entry.summary: The paper proposes online reinforcement learning for flow policies combining SDE-based sampling with value-based optimization to achieve autonomous drifting under tire-force saturation and highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics. Experiments on circular and eight-shaped drifting in an F1TENTH digital twin show real-time control with tighter tracking and better robustness, supporting both from-scratch training and fine-tuning from expert demonstrations.

entry.title: Neural Implicit Representation for Bathymetry Estimation using Sidescan Sonar Imagery

author.name: Tianxiang Lin, Sacchin Sundar, Fenghao Liu, Onur Bagoren, Katherine A. Skinner

entry.summary: This paper proposes a differentiable neural rendering framework for sidescan sonar that enables high-resolution bathymetry estimation from AUV-deployed sonar imagery, addressing measurement ambiguity and limited observation coverage that degrade state-of-the-art methods. It complements multibeam echosounder measurements with higher spatial resolution near the seafloor.

entry.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations

author.name: Damir Filipovic, Valentin Tissot-Daguette

entry.summary: The authors develop a unified RKHS-based approach for solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints, representing differential, boundary, and integral operators via Riesz representers and solving regularized least-squares at collocation points from a single linear system. Sensitivities follow by direct differentiation, and a Nystrom approximation handles large collocation sets.

entry.title: Given AGI, China could probably outgrow the US and allies

author.name: djbinder

entry.summary: An economic modeling post arguing that once AI and robots can replace workers, economies grow at similar autonomous rates so relative size depends on starting point and reinvestment rate. Under equal reinvestment, China alone ends up roughly five times the size of the US, and higher Chinese saving rates could let it overtake the US and allies within three and a half to five years. It concludes China's chip disadvantage matters less than expected unless AI workloads are extremely compute-heavy.

entry.title: If it's not safe for the public, it's not safe for AI R&D

author.name: Jacob Brinton

entry.summary: Proposes a policy that labs should only use publicly released models for internal AI R&D, arguing the internal-external capability gap hurts transparency and heats up the arms race. Using METR's Anthropic AI R&D speedup report, the author quantifies an average AECI gap of about 5 points (roughly one time-horizon doubling) between internal snapshots and public releases across February to September. The post argues this rule would pace capabilities without kneecapping revenue or ceding ground to China.

entry.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model

author.name: Edo Liberty, Ashwin Padaki, Amir Ingber

entry.summary: The paper proves that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for product quantization on Gaussian data, introduces an Extended Zador estimator of k-means quantization cost accurate at low bit rates, and derives a segmentation algorithm via 1-d bin packing of bit allocations. The resulting EZPQ algorithm matches OPQ empirically while providing per-instance distortion lower-bound certificates, often within 1% of the model optimum at 2 bits per coordinate.

entry.title: XMind: Thinking Twice via Cross-Memory Reasoning for LLM-Based Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zuyi Guo, Xianjie Dai, Lei Yang, Xiaocong Zhao, Jingguang Li, Kitae Jang, Heye Huang

entry.summary: XMind is a training-free framework for LLM-based driving agents that combines working memory of recent traffic states with episodic memory of critical risk events, making an initial decision and then cross-checking it against retrieved historical experience before revising on conflict. This addresses the problem that past outcome-only memories fail to transfer to changed traffic conditions.

entry.title: The Control-Flow Tax: Specialized Decision Routing for LLM Agent Workflows

author.name: Zhikai Cheng (Talkdesk), Shuanghu Wang (Talkdesk), Li Jiang (Talkdesk)

entry.summary: This industry paper from Talkdesk quantifies a control-flow tax, with routing decisions consuming 42.5% of baseline cost in their documentation workflow, and evaluates a heterogeneous architecture where a specialized System 1 decision model (Jev) controls finite actions while a generator (Sol) produces documents. Across four tasks and 480 runs, full specialized routing achieved the lowest mean cost and elapsed time on every task.

entry.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis

author.name: Yifan Duan, Lihuan Li, Chao Xue, Siyuan Zheng, Du Yin, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: RecordRoute couples comparative step localization with local diagnosis for auditing failed agent executions: it ranks records within a trajectory via word- and character-level features to identify the responsible actor and earliest decisive step, then uses the selected record text and metadata to predict the error mode. Unlike prior supervised methods that predict attribution targets from shared representations, it uses localization to select the evidence for diagnosis. Evaluated on controlled-injection Who&When-style data, it targets the practical need for post-hoc agent failure analysis.

entry.title: Capability and Interpretability of Transformers on Multi-task Recurrence

author.name: Xiamin Chen, Linyu Liu, Jiachen Hu, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: The paper studies transformer capability and interpretability through controlled linear recurrence tasks over finite cyclic groups, ranging from executing a fixed rule to identifying latent rules and switching specified rules, with and without input masking. Experiments show switching specified rules is easier than identifying latent rules and reveal how key factors affect generalization.

entry.title: DELTA: Diagnosing Exploration Lineages via Twin-path Alignment - What Can Contrasting Design Paths Reveal About Microarchitectural Behavior?

author.name: Kaushal Mhapsekar, Darsh Asher, Bita Aslrousta, Amna Hassan, Debayan Sengupta, Azam Ghanbari, Samira Mirbagher Ajorpaz

entry.summary: DELTA treats parent-child edges in design-space exploration trees as controlled interventions, mining already-produced exploration data to explain why searches stop improving, such as why a backend-bound design rejects a recommended prefetcher. It uses twin-path alignment of design lineages to reveal causal microarchitectural behavior that Top-Down analysis and DSE alone cannot explain.

entry.title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study

author.name: Tim d'Hondt, Oleksii Furman, Damian Kwolek, Jan Por\k{e}ba, Maciej Zieba, Mykola Pechenizkiy

entry.summary: This empirical study compares joint classification-and-generation models built from four state-of-the-art tabular families — energy-based models, probabilistic circuits, tabular foundation models, and tabular diffusion models — across 29 classification datasets, measured against FLOPs and wall-clock time. It provides guidance on which joint modeling approach is preferable at which compute budget versus training separate models.

entry.title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination

author.name: Guowei Zou, Beiwen Zhang, Haitao Wang, Hong Hong, Zhiquan Chen, Hejun Wu

entry.summary: TeamFlowRL is a two-stage framework that pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online via reinforcement learning, formulating team policy optimization over complete denoising trajectories to avoid intractable action likelihoods. The objective weights each agent's trajectory ratio with a shared team advantage and clipped ratios.

entry.title: OrangeTree: A Linear and Tree-based Time Series Forecasting Model Supporting Multiple Input and Output Lengths

author.name: Yiqi Tang, Zhichen Lai, Yuxuan Yang, Dalin Zhang, Jinpeng Chen, Gang Chen, Huan Li

entry.summary: Proposes OrangeTree, a linear and tree-based forecasting architecture that decouples parameters from sequence lengths, natively handling multiple input and output lengths without padding or autoregression. A Segment Tree Encoder, Inverse Tree Decoder, Range Weighter, and Feature Fuser jointly select and fuse relevant ranges for forecasting.

entry.title: The Teacher Is Already Inside: Self-Distilling Looped Language Models Beyond Their Last Loop

author.name: Linghua Zhang

entry.summary: For looped language models that reuse one transformer stack multiple times per token, the paper identifies limitations of reward-only RL and prior cross-loop self-distillation, then introduces ELPSD: a teacher derived by extrapolating the next-token distribution from the first loop through the last. This enables post-training beyond the last loop without external verifiers or sparse reward signals.

entry.title: Polynomial-Time Learning of Random Automata from One Label per Word

author.name: Yilin Cheng

entry.summary: The paper gives a polynomial-time algorithm for learning randomly generated deterministic finite automata from uniformly sampled words with single-bit acceptance labels, working outside a negligible set of transition tables. It provides PAC-style guarantees with sample size and runtime polynomial in the state count, word length, and accuracy parameters.

entry.title: ModernELECTRA: Replaced-Token Detection with Boundary-Window Reconstruction for Compact Encoders that Classify and Embed

author.name: Mykhailo Shtopko, Ihor Stepanov, Dmytro Vodianytskyi, Oleksandr Lukashov

entry.summary: ModernELECTRA keeps ELECTRA-style replaced-token detection as the main pre-training objective but adds a lightweight boundary-window reconstruction auxiliary task, addressing the known weakness of RTD-trained encoders at embedding tasks like retrieval and similarity. The result is compact encoders that are strong at both classification and embedding.

entry.title: PHM-ensemble: Scalable and Stable Probabilistic Multiresolution Clustering via Ensemble Density Estimation

author.name: Ali Turfah, Xiaoquan Wen

entry.summary: The paper argues clustering methods should satisfy fidelity, interpretability, stability, and scalability, and introduces PHM-ensemble, a probabilistic framework that pools mixture models from an ensemble of fits to estimate the data density and builds a clustering hierarchy via hierarchical merging. Experiments on simulated and real data demonstrate improved stability and scalability over existing methods. It offers a general, principled alternative to single-fit clustering approaches.

entry.title: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement

author.name: Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng

entry.summary: This study tests whether response delivery (speed and streaming) shapes user judgments of LLM answers, using three sources of natural-use variation including compar:IA, a French government chatbot arena. Drawing on labor illusion research, it finds that answers unfolding as they are written are credited differently from the same answer shown at once, complicating blind preference votes used to rank models. The results have implications for model evaluation methodology and product design.

entry.title: E-Waste-Bench: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Visual Triage of Data-Center Hardware

author.name: Nader Lobandi, Mohammad Mehdi Hosseini, Lombe Chileshe, Mohammad Mahoor

entry.summary: The paper audits nine public e-waste collections, finding major gaps like 42% duplicates and almost no data-center hardware labels, and introduces E-Waste-Bench: 328K photographs labeled for class, granularity, condition, and printed part text. It targets practical visual triage for refurbishing retired data-center hardware.

entry.title: View Management with Gaussian Placement and Opacity Regularization for Online 3DGS

author.name: Dong Hwi Kim, Park Sangwon, Chaehyeon Song, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: Improves online 3D Gaussian Splatting coupled with SLAM by addressing map overfitting to sparse keyframe views, adding view management with Gaussian placement and opacity regularization within a real-time budget. The design explicitly accounts for the map's millions of parameters competing for limited views and compute.

entry.title: EvoSearch: Self-Evolving Active Perception for Wide-Area Geospatial Search

author.name: Zhenghao Xie, Jing Xiao, Zihao Yu, Wanyi Yu, Liang Liao, Gui-Song Xia, Mi Wang

entry.summary: EvoSearch is a self-evolving active perception framework for wide-area geospatial search that co-evolves a perception policy and exploration program to compress search trajectories. It addresses the key limitation that final-answer correctness alone gives little guidance on which observations to retain and when to stop. This makes large-area search more efficient for resource surveys and environmental monitoring.

entry.title: LookAnything: A Foundation Model for Holistic Gaze Following

author.name: Jiayu Tang, Yuchen Zhou, Hongsheng Wu, Hanjing Ye, Ke Huang, Cheng Wang, Yuqin Dai, Yufei Huang, Yonggen Ling, Chao Gou

entry.summary: LookAnything is a foundation model unifying diverse gaze-centric tasks into holistic gaze following, removing the auxiliary inputs like head crops and depth maps that cause cascading errors in prior customized architectures. Large-scale multi-task, cross-domain training yields flexible adaptation and free-form outputs beyond heatmaps.

entry.title: Every Edit Its Own Budget: Per-Instruction Token Freezing for Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-Edit Image Editing

author.name: Jyotirmoy Nath, Neeraj Kumar, Brejesh Lall

entry.summary: TIDE accelerates training-free multi-edit image editing by giving each instruction part its own compute budget: it localizes each edit region via unbalanced optimal transport on the editor's attention and freezes tokens only when their drift is small relative to their own instruction budget. This prevents the single global threshold of prior accelerators from silently dropping small, slowly settling edits.

entry.title: HS-OVSeg: Multi-Granularity Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Heterogeneous Supervision

author.name: Wei Huang, Chenying Liu, Xudong Kang, Xiao Xiang Zhu

entry.summary: HS-OVSeg trains open-vocabulary segmentation models for remote sensing by unifying heterogeneous scene-, object-, and pixel-level supervision, generating pixel-wise pseudo-labels with SAM3 conditioned on scene and object annotations. This leverages abundant coarse annotations to compensate for the scarcity of precisely pixel-annotated remote sensing data.

entry.title: ShapeQuest: Towards Granularity-Controlled Edit-Conditioned 3D Asset Retrieval

author.name: Faris Abu-Ali, Sankalp Sinha, Didier Stricker, Muhammad Zeshan Afzal

entry.summary: The authors introduce ShapeQuest, a benchmark and pipeline for edit-conditioned retrieval of 3D assets: given a reference mesh and an instruction such as removing an armrest, find variants that apply exactly the edit. The benchmark controls edit granularity across five surface-area levels and uses a VLM judge to validate edits, with ShapeQuerster as the accompanying model.

entry.title: SAVERA: Bridging Frozen Vision and Language Models via Sparse Alignment and Visual Evidence Reuse

author.name: Jiajun Shen, Chuancheng Shi, Jiayi Lyu, Yanpeng Sun, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: SAVERA connects independently pretrained vision and language models through bidirectional alignment in a shared sparse space plus prompt-guided residual fusion, preserving access to original visual evidence before and after language adaptation. Its SPARE component represents original and adapted visual information for evidence reuse during multimodal fusion.

entry.title: NEST: Uncovering and Nesting Unknown Objects in Open-World Object Detection

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Yuan Gao, Sebastian Schmidt, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Addresses open-world detection beyond the generic unknown label by assigning uncovered objects to broader categories of a given taxonomy, with a class-agnostic ranker that scores how object-like each predicted box is to prevent discarding unknowns during top-k selection. Combines uncovering with taxonomy nesting for more informed downstream decisions.

entry.title: ROVO: Robust Rotation-Only Visual Odometry for UAVs at Low and Moderate Altitudes

author.name: Xiaokai Song, Li Zhang, Xichao Teng, Erting Pan, Yibin Ye, Kun Wang, Leqi Liu, Guangcheng Dai

entry.summary: ROVO is a rotation-only visual odometry method for monocular UAV navigation that estimates pairwise rotations, robustly averages them over overlapping windows, and aligns windows through shared frames, preventing uncertain depth from corrupting translation direction. Simulation shows orientation error reduced to roughly a tenth of comparable approaches.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence

author.name: Nasser Alkhulaifi, Direnc Pekaslan, Christian Wagner

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept treats uncertainty as native data to be preserved and exploited throughout entity resolution pipelines: uncertainty signals captured during named entity recognition (span boundary disagreement, type confusion) are passed to the entity linking stage to improve candidate generation, rather than being collapsed by early hard decisions. Demonstrated on cyber threat intelligence, it argues brittle ER systems fail unpredictably when upstream ambiguity is discarded. The design points toward more robust NLP pipelines for adversarial, high-stakes text.

entry.title: Faithful Persona Steering under Incongruity via Dual-Stream Refinement

author.name: Yu-An Chu, Jen-Ren Pong, Chia-Yao Yeh, Meng-Fen Chiang

entry.summary: QuirkyMind is a personalization framework that disentangles identity definition from expression to handle incongruent personas, where stable traits coexist with context-specific atypical stances. It constructs a dual-stream latent state fusing sentence-level semantic stability with token-level generative control, stabilized via in-context anchoring, addressing context drift in prompting and quirk-suppression in fine-tuning.

entry.title: Who gets the information? An $\alpha$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection

author.name: Zhenzhi Tang

entry.summary: FLIC reframes multi-label feature selection as an alpha-fair social welfare problem, treating labels as agents and greedily maximizing the alpha-fair welfare of per-label information coverage; a single alpha parameter interpolates between utilitarian, proportionally fair, and max-min selection, subsuming many published relevance terms as special cases. The objective is monotone submodular, enabling efficient optimization.

entry.title: Progressive Reliable Supervision for Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation

author.name: Jing Li, Zhe Zhang, Huateng Sun, Yuhui Yang, Wanli Xue, Xu Cheng, Fan Shi, Jianhua Zhang, Qinghua Hu, Shengyong Chen

entry.summary: PReS progressively establishes reliable target supervision for black-box universal domain adaptation, where neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible and label-space relationships are arbitrary. It coordinates knowledge from the black-box source model, foundation models, and the evolving target model to identify reliable known samples and handle unknown classes. This addresses an increasingly realistic restrictive setting for adaptation.

entry.title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand CTs: Testing Anatomical Control in Text-to-CT Generation

author.name: Francesca Pia Panaccione, Eugenio Lomurno, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: CtrlCT is a toolkit that standardizes evaluation of text-to-CT generative models along two axes: Credibility (population-level comparison with real scans) and Control (metamorphic tests checking whether editing the report changes anatomy at a fixed seed). It highlights that existing evaluations rarely test whether reports actually control anatomy. This improves rigor in medical image generation evaluation.

entry.title: Predict Backbone, Graft Dynamics: A Decoupled Paradigm for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Lin Zhang, Zilin Li, Jingmei Zhao, Jiayang Wu

entry.summary: Proposes GRAFT, a decoupled forecasting paradigm in which a base forecaster predicts a stable trajectory backbone while a dedicated grafting path restores historically recurrent local dynamics via retrieval-based evidence and phase-aware release. Unlike post-hoc residual correction, it targets abrupt variations, surges, and turning points directly.

entry.title: Beyond Robust Algorithmic Recourse: Sharing the Burden of Validity through Model Multiplicity

author.name: Prakhar Ganesh, Afaf Ta\"ik, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: The paper shows that robust algorithmic recourse, while keeping recommendations valid under model updates, systematically harms individuals by constraining recommendations to majority-density regions, reducing flexibility and amplifying disparities. It proposes sharing the validity burden through model multiplicity so that individual recommendations need not each be robust in isolation.

entry.title: Training decision models for simulating human respondents

author.name: Davood Wadi, Yu Ma

entry.summary: The paper examines using LLMs as synthetic respondents in market research and conjoint analysis, showing that off-the-shelf generative LLMs bias downstream econometric inference regardless of model size or reasoning effort. Training smaller decision models via choice-based maximum likelihood on historical respondent microdata reduces treatment-effect error by 22-89% on held-out studies.

entry.title: Seeing to Drive on a Single Board: Attention-Free Depth for Onboard Robot Navigation

author.name: Itai Mizlish, Boaz Ben-Moshe

entry.summary: The authors distill Depth Anything V2-Large into an attention-free ResNet-34 U-Net that runs at 27.1 FPS in int8 on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-8L accelerator for robot navigation. They diagnose why direct quantization fails (91% of softmax weights below one int8 step at 449 tokens) and show the distilled student matches its float teacher closely.

entry.title: Change the Base, Change the Game: Rethinking Pan-sharpening

author.name: Jeonghyeok Do, Geunhyuk Youk, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: Questions the common pan-sharpening practice of adding learned residuals to blurry upsampled multispectral inputs, proposing PanBase, a training-free sharper starting point that fuses panchromatic spatial detail with multispectral spectra under sensor-specific blur constraints. Only nine parameters are estimated, and the improved base is shown to benefit downstream residual learning.

entry.title: FlashSegmentator: High-Throughput TotalSegmentator Inference without Loss of Accuracy

author.name: Yosuke Yamagishi, Tomohiro Kikuchi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe

entry.summary: FlashSegmentator is an open-source inference pipeline that increases TotalSegmentator CT/MRI segmentation throughput via static-shape compilation, pipelining, batched sliding-window inference, and GPU postprocessing, with no retraining and no accuracy loss. It was evaluated on public datasets including the TotalSegmentator test split, BTCV, and MRI exams. This has immediate clinical deployment value.

entry.title: Sub-Riemannian structure for Oriented Point Clouds

author.name: Thomas Besnier, Stefan Sommer

entry.summary: This paper defines locality for oriented point clouds using a sub-Riemannian contact metric on position-orientation space rather than Euclidean k-nearest-neighbor graphs, preventing feature leakage between geometrically distinct surfaces that are spatially close, such as the two faces of a thin leaf. Points are lifted to position-normal pairs with motion constrained to a non-holonomic horizontal distribution.

entry.title: DiffAnchor: Anchor-Space Diffusion for Monocular 3D Hand Pose Estimation

author.name: Changlong Jiang, Youci Tang, Haohong Kuang, Hang Xu, Jinghong Zheng, Ran Wang, Zhenghong Yu, Chen Feng, Xiaofeng Yue, Yang Xiao

entry.summary: DiffAnchor reformulates diffusion-based 3D hand pose estimation by diffusing anchor points rather than final joint coordinates, separating stochastic exploration of plausible poses from precise coordinate recovery. This enables few-step inference without multiple hypotheses, reducing the cost typical of coordinate-space diffusion pose models.

entry.title: Beyond Image-Text Pairs: Aligning Semantic Changes for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding

author.name: Yujie Sun, Zeqing Wang, Shuang Liang, Zhenlin Zhao, Kunyu Zhang, Xiaowu Sun

entry.summary: The authors propose a post-training method that learns cross-modal semantic change correspondences through controlled visual and textual variations, using a Semantic Difference Alignment loss that matches directions of visual and textual representation changes. Combined with pairwise sigmoid matching, this yields more fine-grained and discriminative visual representations than standard image-text alignment.

entry.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Minchan Jung, Dimitrios S. Georgiou, Augustinos D. Saravanos, Evangelos A. Theodorou

entry.summary: Presents DS-TO, a distributed sampling-based trajectory optimization architecture for multi-agent teams, built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling methods that addresses the trade-off between handling constraint-induced non-convexity and search-space growth. It targets effective exploration of non-convex landscapes while scaling favorably to large teams.

entry.title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels

author.name: Emir Cem Gezer, Ozan Kaya, Ingrid B. Utne, Roger Skjetne

entry.summary: The paper integrates a Bayesian Belief Network as an online risk model into an RRT* path planner for autonomous surface vessels, aggregating hazard probability and severity into a bounded scalar risk index evaluated along candidate path edges. The planner optimizes distance, heading change, and accumulated risk under a hard risk-acceptance constraint.

entry.title: A detective on demand: the Automated Auditor

author.name: Jasper Blank

entry.summary: A governance proposal for an automated auditor that receives confidential insider information in a secure, wiped environment and publishes only its conclusions, enabling credible signals like verifying that a datacenter is not training frontier models. It motivates the design via the absence of legal audit frameworks for compute verification. The post sketches how AI could substitute for trusted human auditors where no legal regime exists.

entry.title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations

author.name: Yuhan Bian, Zhaokai Liang, Jia Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yu Chen, Jianfeng Qu, Zhixu Li

entry.summary: InfoCon is a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations, going beyond binary deception detection to cover behaviors such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim across six categories. Reliable evaluation requires reasoning about facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context.

entry.title: COGENT: A Modular Cognitive Architecture for Agentic User Simulation

author.name: Yikun Chi, Adam Davies, Debarati Das, Lin Ai, Scott Counts

entry.summary: COGENT is a modular cognitive architecture for simulating human users interacting with desktop interfaces, grounded in theories like Norman's action cycle and ACT-R, with explicit modules for perception, memory, user state, intentions, and action selection. Unlike task-completion computer-use agents, it targets explainable and intervenable user simulation, demonstrated through six intervenability experiments.

entry.title: SciFig2Data: A Workflow for Recovering Structured Data from Scientific Figures

author.name: Xinhe Wu, Yicheng Ye, Yadong Jin

entry.summary: SciFig2Data is an automated workflow for extracting structured experimental data from scientific PDFs, integrating figure localization, compound-figure panel decomposition, two-stage OCR semantic filtering, Swin-based chart classification, and instruction-guided multimodal LLM reconstruction. It enables literature-scale recovery of measurements that are otherwise locked in figures. This supports meta-science, dataset construction, and knowledge extraction at scale.

entry.title: How Much Dependency Can a Marginal Rule See? Total Correlation in Diffusion LM Parallel Decoding

author.name: Dovud Asadov, Rustambek Urokov, Qobiljon Toshnazarov, Abduaziz Kayumov, Mardon Hazratov, Husanboy Mansuraliyev

entry.summary: This analytical paper quantifies how much token dependency marginal-based set selection misses in masked diffusion language model parallel decoding, measured as conditional total correlation. Across four masked diffusion LMs, the best marginal-only predictor of this loss is off by roughly one bit, with most of its accuracy derived from the bound alone.

entry.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification

author.name: Yanbin Gong, Lei Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies how little of a generative verifier output is needed to recover its decision, observing that in a frozen 2B span verifier the choice between an empty error list and its first object precedes all localization. Prefill1 supplies the fixed preceding syntax tokens as input and generates only the unrestricted branch token, cutting eager resident service memory by 84.84 percent on 2,015 code-agent responses while maintaining released-reference F1 of 83.43 versus 83.41. It is an efficiency technique for cheap early-exit verification decisions.

entry.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess

author.name: Victor Dziwniel, Tianxiang Lu

entry.summary: The authors extend a Chessformer-style behavioral cloning model for chess with learned temporal conditioning tokens capturing clock state, time control, and recent tempo, plus behavioral heads for thinking time and resignation. Trained on large-scale online chess data, the model shows that time pressure meaningfully shapes human move quality, though overall accuracy gains over time-agnostic baselines are modest.

entry.title: LLM Genetic Feature Engineering

author.name: Jonathan Thompson, Razvan Stefanescu, Manoj Varma Namburi, Liuxia Wang

entry.summary: The authors introduce a genetic algorithm for LLM-driven automated feature engineering that applies selection, crossover, and mutation at the individual feature level rather than across entire engineered feature sets. This finer-grained search aims to reduce statistical noise and extract meaningful domain-specific quantities from raw datasets.

entry.title: Scoring Recovery-Time Agent Security: Proposals, Effects, and Retry Instructions

author.name: Paul Deepakraj Retinraj

entry.summary: The paper introduces an executable evaluation that scores agent recovery from timed-out tool writes by separately recording proposals, runtime decisions, and committed effects, showing that goal-based scoring hides harmful recovery actions. Across thousands of episodes, it quantifies how clarification wording and separating effect definitions from recovery recipes dramatically change valid-recovery rates.

entry.title: Where Agent Defenses Fail: A Case Study of Policy Compositions and Measurement Limits

author.name: Kunwar Singh Sangram, Krishna Mohan Guda Nagavenkata Srinivasa

entry.summary: Using files and HTTP receipts to measure effects independently of control logs, this case study examines how sandboxing and host mediation compose in coding agents, showing that restrictive sandboxing eliminates observed attack harm but degrades benign utility, while mediation restores uploads but admits disclosure. A boundary study identifies encoded disclosure and observer misses that evade complete-line policy matching.

entry.title: LatentLens: Rethinking Latent Interface in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Ziqing Yang, Kewei Cheng, Mingjie Li, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: LatentLens is a framework that decouples latent (continuous, non-textual) communication in multi-agent systems both externally from the agent harness and internally into realignment compatibility, information accessibility, and propagation dynamics. Across seven benchmarks with Qwen3 models, it clarifies how much of previously reported latent-communication gains actually stem from the interface versus the harness.

entry.title: RePT: 3D Geometry Emerges from 2D Relational Pretraining

author.name: Xize Duan, Binke Hou, Xingqiao Huang, Xinyuan Guan, Jiaxin Huang, Kaiyuan Hu, Zipeng Sun, Hong Kang, Meng Bi, Xue Liu, Yili Jin

entry.summary: RePT learns compact relations between physical points through cross-view 2D point prediction without explicit 3D prediction targets, and the learned relation space develops geometric organization reflecting 3D displacement. A single linear readout fitted on 16 scenes recovers displacement length and angle on 39 held-out scenes with Pearson correlations of 0.72-0.78, suggesting 3D structure can emerge from 2D relational learning.

entry.title: GRUN: Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network for Image Restoration

author.name: Rihan Zhang, Fengyang Xiao, Yuhan Chen, Chunming He, Sina Farsiu

entry.summary: GRUN revisits classical Retinex theory, generalizing illumination-reflectance decomposition into a content-environment factorization prior, and unfolds it into an optimization-inspired network for image restoration. It restores images via two learned factors capturing scene properties and degradation-dependent environmental variation.

entry.title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes

author.name: Seonghwan Park, Min-Gyu Park

entry.summary: The paper addresses the gap between rigid articulated hand meshes and realistic soft-tissue contact, where existing datasets and estimators produce hands that hover above or penetrate objects. The proposed optimization adjusts joints slightly and deforms skin so contact regions settle onto object surfaces, producing contact-consistent hand meshes that stay close to original poses. This improves physical plausibility for hand-object interaction modeling relevant to robotics, AR, and motion capture.

entry.title: When Online Adaptation of Resilience Policies Hurts: Safe Exploration and Measurement Pitfalls in Resilience4j
