author.name: Rajat M. Barot, Arjun S. Borkhatariya

entry.summary: The paper studies whether contextual bandits can tune Resilience4j circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings at runtime in Java microservices, showing that a naive design performed worse than defaults in three of four fault scenarios due to unsafe exploration. Two safeguards, a safe policy menu and modified reward handling, restore performance. It provides a concrete cautionary case for safe online learning in production systems.

entry.title: PreferenceScene: Personalized Indoor Scene Synthesis from Feedback

author.name: Seongrae Noh, RyunHa Lee, HyeongYeop Kang

entry.summary: This paper studies personalized 3D indoor scene synthesis under hidden user preferences, where the system iteratively presents rendered rooms and must infer full-room preferences from brief free-form feedback and satisfaction scores covering only part of the scene. It formalizes a multi-turn feedback loop for text-to-scene generation.

entry.title: Mind the Band: The Hidden Frequency Variable in Geometric RoPE

author.name: Seonghyun Jin, Youngmin Kim, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: The paper shows that the frequency band setting in geometric rotary position encodings for 3D-aware multi-view attention is unstandardized and can reverse benchmark rankings, with RayRoPE matching the strongest baseline at 47M parameters but trailing by 1.2 dB at 25M. It identifies frequency band selection as a hidden hyperparameter in geometric RoPE designs.

entry.title: Validating Multi-Model AI-Generated Acceptance Criteria in Requirements Engineering

author.name: Mateen Ahmed Abbasi, Petri Ihantola, Tommi Mikkonen, Niko M\"akitalo

entry.summary: This paper presents a validation-oriented approach for AI-generated acceptance criteria in requirements engineering, combining retrieval-augmented techniques with multi-model generation to address hallucination, correctness, and traceability concerns. It fills a gap relative to the heavy focus on code generation in AI-assisted software engineering. Flawed specifications propagate errors into design and verification, so validation at the specification level matters.

entry.title: BARE: Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Zihao Li, Tong Chen, Hua Song, Zitong Ding, Zihao Xu, Ce Hao, Weibang Bai

entry.summary: BARE enables humanoid robots to evade rapidly approaching obstacles through small, localized body adjustments rather than whole-body repositioning, exploiting rich body articulation like humans do. The method addresses the challenge of maintaining whole-body stability while rapidly moving threatened body regions.

entry.title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations

author.name: Ida Dencker, Simon Karg, Kenneth Enevoldsen

entry.summary: This work releases a large annotated dataset of English and Danish social media comments labeled for hateful tone, constructive tone, and agreement with parent comments, then fine-tunes multilingual LLMs to classify along these three dimensions. It frames constructive speech detection as a proactive complement to hate-speech moderation. The joint framing and bilingual data are useful for content-moderation research.

entry.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning

author.name: Hanzhao Xi, Zhonghao Li, Suxuan Liu, Shanghan Zhou, Zesheng Chen, Qiufeng Wang, Yaran Chen

entry.summary: CAPER is a framework that grounds VLM-generated assembly plans in product-specific inventory and part-reference information, using PartGround for evidence-guided part ID assignment and PlanRefine for cross-step consistency. It addresses a concrete failure of VLMs in robotic assembly: confusing part identities and predicting unsupported part IDs. This improves reliability of manual-guided robotic assembly planning.

entry.title: Hidden Clues in WM-811K: Uncovering the Spatial Signals Behind Wafer Map Prediction

author.name: Kabir Tolani

entry.summary: The study dissects the widely used WM-811K wafer map dataset to determine which spatial features drive CNN classification accuracy, controlling for duplicates, conflicting labels, and manufacturing-lot leakage. After rigorous data cleaning, roughly 25,000 maps remain, and the analysis quantifies the contribution of layout, failure counts, and die locations.

entry.title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study

author.name: Sayed Amir Karim

entry.summary: The paper studies adversarial retrieval traps where a near-copy of a correct document with a small meaning-reversing edit ranks highly under raw cosine similarity, and proposes small learned projections (to 11-32 dimensions) trained deterministically to suppress such traps. Across four domains and pools up to 100,000 documents, the projections remove traps from top-10 results while retaining correct paraphrases 93-99% of the time.

entry.title: Latent Channel Completion for Forecasting in Sensor Networks with Failed Detectors

author.name: Mehran Shabanpour, Sadaf Khademi, Maryam Hosseini, Haiyan Xu, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis, Arash Mohammadi

entry.summary: The paper addresses forecasting degradation in coupled sensor networks when detectors fail, proposing Latent Channel Completion, a joint-embedding objective that reconstructs missing sensors' latent representations rather than raw values. This prevents corrupted substitutions from propagating through shared representations and degrading healthy sensors' forecasts.

entry.title: Curvature-Equilibrated Policy Optimization for Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Gang Chen

entry.summary: Presents EQUIP, an actor optimization method for deep RL that balances positive and negative curvature of the actor loss using a trajectory-informed search subspace and projected Hessian-based metrics. The approach combines first-order loss matching with gradient mixing and curvature-based selection to improve policy search stability.

entry.title: Scale-Robust and Global-Aware Representation Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Gyuwon Lee, Saejoon Park, Won-Seok Hwang, Bogoan Kim, Yunyong Ko

entry.summary: Proposes STAGER, which jointly learns scale-robust temporal representations capturing anomalies across temporal scales and global-aware relational representations capturing inter-series dependencies beyond local windows for multivariate time series anomaly detection. Addresses two identified gaps in existing representation learning for MTSAD.

entry.title: The Activity Geometry of Discrete Generative Sampling

author.name: Xinlong Guo, Jie Zhang, Lingyou Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical work introduces Activity Geometry, a framework characterizing the coupling between successive sampling states in discrete diffusion and flow models that allow token revision during sampling. Activity decomposes into a minimal transport term and an excess coupling term, providing a principled reference for sampler design in iterative refinement.

entry.title: E(n)-Equivariant Spherical Decision Surfaces

author.name: Pavlo Melnyk, Michael Felsberg, Kostas Daniilidis

entry.summary: The paper derives exactly E(n)-equivariant spherical decision surfaces by extending O(n)-equivariant hypersphere neurons to handle translations, with explicit closed-form matrix representations. Equivariance holds without input centering or pairwise differences, and the derivations are numerically verified.

entry.title: Learning from Human Corrections through Temporal Preferences

author.name: Anjiabei Wang, Tesca Fitzgerald

entry.summary: The paper shows that human interventions with a robot carry information not only in how the behavior was corrected but in when the person intervened, translating pre- and post-intervention behavior into preference pairs for learning value functions approximating latent human reward. This leverages temporal relationships among states leading up to the intervention, which prior correction-learning approaches ignored.

entry.title: Instance-Dependent Bandit Convex Optimization in One Dimension

author.name: Felix Breuer, Alireza Bakhtiari, Kevin Jamieson

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies instance-dependent sample complexity of one-dimensional stochastic bandit convex optimization in fixed-confidence settings, introducing a new quantity capturing the sublevel-set threshold around the minimizer. It proves a matching lower bound with a bisection-style algorithm and identifies a surprising gap in the simple-regret literature.

entry.title: A Minimax Optimal Leave One Out Bound for Bounded Losses

author.name: Peigan Gao, Jian Qian

entry.summary: This theory paper determines the minimax excess loss for proper leave-one-out prediction with M real-valued experts under any bounded loss continuous and nondecreasing in absolute error, giving a rate of order sqrt(Br log M / n) plus a lower-order term. Notably, a single deterministic rule attains this rate uniformly across all best-expert loss levels.

entry.title: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering

author.name: Dengzhe Hou, Kazunori D. Yamada

entry.summary: EEGJev introduces a fast single-pass model and benchmark (EEGJev-Bench) for answering multiple question types about the same EEG recording, testing how EEG foundation models handle changing queries. The model achieves 99.70% attribute selection accuracy across 13 held-out sources with very low response latency.

entry.title: MYSTIQUE: Few-Shot Facial Identity Transfer with Performance Preservation

author.name: Shihan Cheng, David Hyde, Junting Deng, Michael Bao, Paul Debevec, Roshni Cooper, Soshi Shimada

entry.summary: MYSTIQUE is a diffusion-based facial identity transfer method for visual effects that uses separate input streams for identity and driving attributes to prevent identity leakage, a known failure of self-reconstruction training. It comes from a credible author group including Paul Debevec and targets production-grade performance preservation of expression, lighting, and pose.

entry.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators

author.name: Stefano Markidis, Qingxin Yang, Erik {\AA}sgrim, Ivy Peng

entry.summary: The authors propose a theory-informed error mitigation method for Shor's order-finding algorithm that models how circuit noise shifts, broadens, or weakens peaks in measurement distributions. These models guide synthetic training data generation and a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain over Fourier modes, which then scores candidate orders from noisy circuit executions. This combines domain knowledge with neural post-processing to recover latent algorithmic results from noisy quantum hardware.

entry.title: Is Prosody Encoded in the Neural Audio Codec Mimi?

author.name: Nicolas Ballier, Artem Saloev, Erin Pacquetet, Taylor Arnold

entry.summary: This work investigates what phonetic and prosodic information is captured during encoding by the neural audio codec Mimi, used in conversational speech agents such as Moshi and Sesame and in speech-to-speech translation. It addresses a gap: most codec evaluations only assess decoded-speech naturalness, not what phonetic information the discrete tokens retain. Understanding prosody encoding in codec tokens matters for expressive speech-language models.

entry.title: Tornado4D: Physics-Guided 4D Gaussian Reconstruction of a Laboratory Tornado from Sparse One-Sided Videos

author.name: Yucheng Zhu, Maria J. Molina, Christopher Metzler

entry.summary: Tornado4D reconstructs time-resolved 3D models of laboratory smoke tornadoes from sparse, one-sided video by embedding rotational airflow field priors and enclosure geometry into a 4D Gaussian splatting framework. This physics-guided approach addresses a severely underconstrained problem with view-dependent appearance and non-rigid motion. The method could aid tornado research and, more broadly, illustrates how physical priors can constrain neural reconstruction of fluid phenomena.

entry.title: LineEX: Data Extraction from Scientific Line Charts

author.name: VP Shivasankaran, Muhammad Yusuf Hassan, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: LineEX extracts underlying data from scientific line charts using adapted vision transformers and pose detection methods, with a new proposed loss function and a synthetically created 430K-image dataset, the largest of its kind. It reports significant gains over existing SOTA baselines.

entry.title: TANDEM: Temporal Anchor Densification With Reliability-Aware Memory for Lightweight Sparse Depth Completion in Endoscopic Robotic Navigation

author.name: Weikuan Qiu, Jiale Hou, Chongzhao Xu, Jinlian Ma

entry.summary: Proposes TANDEM, a causal, lightweight sparse depth completion framework for endoscopic video that re-projects past metric measurements into the current view and uses reliability-aware memory to recover dense depth. It targets depth perception for endoscopic robotic surgery where only a small fraction of pixels have reliable metric measurements.

entry.title: BodyWeave: Native Body-Conditioned 3D Garment Generation

author.name: Junyi Zhang, Yuanchuan Wang, Qichao Wang, Wenzhe Qian, Shizhuo Cheng, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Presents BodyWeave, a framework unifying 3D garment generation and fitting through native body conditioning, using a Global Body Adapter for garment placement and Local Body Attention for surface refinement. It combines 3D generative priors with explicit 3D body context to preserve reference designs while adapting to target body shape and pose.

entry.title: LiteSTAR: Low-Rank Channel Modulation for Temporally Consistent CVD Video Compensation

author.name: Peiyang Lin, Sichen Lin, Yipeng Liao, Liqun Lin, Xu Wang, Tiesong Zhao

entry.summary: LiteSTAR provides on-device video recoloring for color vision deficiency, observing that color flickering correlates with channel-wise response variations concentrated in a low-rank subspace. Its plug-and-play Lightweight Channel-Adaptive Decoder performs temporal filtering in a low-rank state space and modulates feature channels to achieve flicker-free recoloring without costly cross-frame alignment. This enables practical continuous assistive video processing.

entry.title: SoccerNarrate: Event-Grounded Streaming Soccer Commentary with Macro-Window Preference Alignment

author.name: Zihan Jia, Zhilin Dai, Zhengming Zhang, Min Yang, Zhenpeng Huang, Jiaqi Li, Caixia Sun, Xi Chen, Liang Li, Junlan Feng, Gangshan Wu, Limin Wang

entry.summary: SoccerNarrate enables low-latency, event-grounded soccer commentary on untrimmed full-match videos, combining a large time-anchored dataset with word-level ASR alignment, streaming training, and macro-window preference alignment so that key events like goals and offsides are narrated correctly and on time. It bridges streaming video-language models with professional commentary quality. The work contributes data, training methods, and evaluation together.

entry.title: ST-SfM: Spatio-Temporal Structure-from-Motion for Initialising 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Harshit, Sami Brandt

entry.summary: ST-SfM is a sparse spatio-temporal structure-from-motion method for synchronized multi-camera video that separately recovers static structure from temporal-median images and motion via space-time interest points matched with epipolar and temporal consistency. It produces moving-point initialization that says what moves, where, and when, unlike random or first-frame SfM initialization for dynamic Gaussian splatting. This improves 4D Gaussian splatting initialization quality.

entry.title: StreamCoach: Proactive Sports Coaching via Continuous Visual Reasoning

author.name: Xiaoye Liang, Yiming Huang, Jialu Wu, Yushe Cao, Ruxiang Duan, Yi Sun, Tie Liu, Lai Jiang, Mai Xu, Shikun Feng, Yiheng Zhu

entry.summary: StreamCoach is a streaming action quality assessment framework that couples continuous chain-of-thought reasoning with proactive feedback generation for sports and fitness training. It addresses the latency and fragmented-feedback limitations of prior AQA methods that only assess completed performances or focus on one body part at a time.

entry.title: FlowVecFont: Scalable Vector Font Generation via Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Takumu Fujioka, Gouhei Tanaka

entry.summary: FlowVecFont generates pure vector font outlines using a Transformer-based variational autoencoder combined with latent flow matching, trained solely on vector outlines without external pretraining or bitmap representations. The paper shows that scaling this simple architecture yields high-quality vector font generation without specialized refinement mechanisms.

entry.title: TESS: Query-Guided Temporal Event-Structured Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Qi Lu, Shiyan Tong, Shujie Li, Sen Li, Likun shi, Maofei Que, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu

entry.summary: TESS is a training-free frame selection framework for long-video QA that selects frames jointly showing a reference event and the queried event in the required temporal order, using frozen vision-language models. It moves beyond semantic relevance or coverage heuristics by structuring selection around event relationships.

entry.title: CalibTrack: Exploring Learned Heteroscedastic Covariance for Robust Multi-Camera Pedestrian Tracking

author.name: Jack Roberts, Aditya Iyer, Nora Ayanian

entry.summary: CalibTrack studies replacing heuristic, hand-tuned measurement covariance in analytical multi-view multi-object tracking with a learned per-detection heteroscedastic covariance predictor. It evaluates the approach across multiple tracker cores (GM-PHD, JIPDA, delta-GLMB) on WildTrack and MultiviewX, analyzing calibration and robustness.

entry.title: CoReQ: Condition-Aware Cross-Modal Repair and Quality-Guided Robust Collaborative Perception

author.name: Ziwei Guo, Lingzhi Li, Jin Wang, Yunjiang Xu, Yupeng Ouyang, Benyuan Yang, Yujun Shi

entry.summary: CoReQ improves multi-vehicle collaborative perception under degraded conditions (bad weather, missing or false LiDAR echoes) by condition-aware repair that fuses LiDAR geometry with weather-robust 4D Radar features. It also quality-gates the integration of multi-vehicle features whose reliability differs after repair, targeting robust 3D detection.

entry.title: Completion-Aware Compression for Progressive 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Reagan Koo, Yeong-Gyu Kim, Eun-Seok Ryu

entry.summary: The authors present a progressive codec for 3D Gaussian Splatting that supports usable partial reconstructions before the full scene has been transmitted. A single compact stream allows newly decoded Gaussians to be added at arbitrary received-byte budgets, balancing attribute fidelity against the image-quality benefit of early Gaussian availability.

entry.title: Beyond Static Semantics: Instance-Adaptive Vision-Language Alignment for Building Damage Assessment

author.name: Hang Yin, Jiepan Li, Hongruixuan Chen, Guangyi Yang, Wei He

entry.summary: LAMIA-IBDA is a vision-language framework for instance-level building damage assessment from bi-temporal remote sensing imagery that progressively grounds shared damage semantics in local observations and individual buildings. By adapting language-derived damage descriptions to instance-specific visual evidence, it improves severity discrimination over static semantic alignments.

entry.title: DualSpec: Spectral Reconstruction with Optimized Stereo Cameras

author.name: Luca Cogo, Marco Buzzelli, Simone Bianco, Raimondo Schettini

entry.summary: DualSpec jointly optimizes two external optical filters placed in front of standard RGB cameras plus a reconstruction network, capturing six complementary responses to resolve the spectral ambiguity of RGB-only reconstruction. Offers an accessible alternative to expensive dedicated spectral cameras.

entry.title: Characterizing Datasets to Anticipate Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Performance for Radiographic Pneumonia Detection

author.name: Iftakhar Hossain, Md. Imran Hasan, Salahuddin Ahmed, Eric D. McCollum, Abdullah H. Baqui, Taufiq Hasan

entry.summary: This study examines which structural properties of chest X-ray datasets predict unsupervised domain adaptation performance before adaptation is attempted, finding asymmetric performance gains across dataset pairs. Using class separability from a frozen DenseNet-121 summarized via Silhouette Scores, the authors identify measurable dataset characteristics as predictors. This enables cheaper a-priori planning of clinical domain adaptation efforts.

entry.title: The Self-Assembling Brain: Emergent Routing and Its Open Challenges

author.name: Dongsung Huh

entry.summary: A commentary on the Self-Assembling Motif (SAM) from Liao et al., which reframes credit assignment without backpropagation as a self-organizing process using local synaptic rules and initially random cross-stream connections, eliminating fixed neuron-to-neuron pairing between forward and feedback pathways. The piece situates this against the architectural circularity problem in feedback alignment methods and outlines open challenges for emergent routing.

entry.title: Trading BRAM for LUTs: Hybrid Bit-Level Weight Storage for FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Dimitrios Sekertzis, Giorgos Dimitrakopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid bit-level weight-storage scheme for FPGA-based spiking neural networks that stores selected weight bits in look-up tables while keeping the rest in BRAM, preserving original weight precision and accuracy. This trades underutilized FPGA logic resources for scarce on-chip memory, alleviating the storage bottleneck of synaptic weights.

entry.title: An XR-Based System for Enhanced Spatial Awareness in Mobile Robot Teleoperation

author.name: Subhransu Sourav Priyadarshan, Valentina Pericu, Federico Rollo, Gianni Viardo Vercelli, Navvab Kashiri

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-modal extended reality (XR) teleoperation system for mobile robots that combines immersive visual and haptic feedback, using a fixed dual-camera configuration (forward- and rear-facing) to mitigate motion sickness from 360-degree feeds in head-mounted displays. It targets hazardous-environment operations where situational awareness is critical.

entry.title: How open will the IVO industry be?

author.name: Felix Moses

entry.summary: An analysis of whether Independent Verification Organizations for frontier AI will concentrate like the financial auditing industry, where four firms audit about 90% of large SEC filers. The author argues trust, access requirements, and reputational dynamics push IVO markets toward consolidation, analogous to PCAOB-registered auditors. This matters for predicting the structure of AI governance infrastructure.

entry.title: Elizabeth Holmes, honeypotting, and exploration-hacking

author.name: davidg

entry.summary: A conceptual essay using the Elizabeth Holmes documentary to argue that a perfect mimic is indistinguishable from the thing mimicked, and that honeypotting and exploration hacking in AI should be understood as the same broad mimicry capability. The author suggests this framing deserves more attention in eval and monitoring design. It is a conceptual contribution to AI safety evaluation methodology.

entry.title: Modeling Event-Conditioned Emotional Expression Response with LLM Agents in a Synthetic Social Simulation

author.name: Rebecca Marigliano, Peter Carragher, Kathleen M. Carley

entry.summary: This study introduces a hierarchical prompting framework that conditions LLM agents with demographic, psychological, and contextual cues to generate event-conditioned emotional responses within agent-based social simulations, validated against empirically observed emotional patterns. It addresses the gap of emotion-aware modeling in LLM-driven ABMs relevant to emergency response and public health. The work connects computational social science with LLM agent design.

entry.title: DocPristine: Content-Aware Document Appearance Enhancement under Real-World Mixed Degradations

author.name: Zihan Huang, Junle Liu, Zhonghao Ye, Yuyi Zhang, Peirong Zhang, Hanlin Li, Yongxin Shi, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: DocPristine is a document appearance enhancement method that adaptively fuses multi-layer features from a frozen pretrained document visual encoder — which still attends to text regions even in degraded documents — to handle mixed real-world degradations such as highlights, shadows, and blur. This content-aware guidance improves on input-derived cues and LLM-based degradation diagnosis.

entry.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Kim N. Nolle, Ivana Dusparic, Rhodri Cusack, Vinny Cahill

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether different classes of RL algorithms, including PPO, SAC, and model-based variants, differ in robustness to catastrophic forgetting in a non-stationary autonomous parking environment representing cyber-physical systems. Continual adaptation matters for safety and reliability as RL deploys in changing physical environments. It offers a comparative empirical picture of algorithm classes under environmental shift.

entry.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yanzhe Chen, Zhijun Cao, Ruihe An, Chang Gong, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: MRBench is a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation — determining which robots are truly needed for a task as capabilities, resources, and configurations change. It comprises eight tasks with distinct concurrency and reach constraints evaluated under five configurations.

entry.title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection

author.name: Khalid Akhmouch, Eric Jauer

entry.summary: SOTS is an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregularly sampled, variable-length multivariate time series that maps each sample to a truncated path signature and greedily minimizes Sliced Wasserstein distance to select a representative training subset. It targets industrial monitoring settings where expert annotation is expensive.

entry.title: Metric-Dependent Scaling Laws for Sketched Multiclass Softmax Regression

author.name: Ziyan Chen, Linhe Zheng, Peilin Liu, Zhongzhu Zhou, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: Derives scaling laws for full-batch gradient descent in sketched multiclass softmax regression within a Gaussian teacher-student model with power-law spectra, jointly handling approximation error, nonlinear finite-time learning, and fixed-sample perturbation. Shows cross-entropy excess and zero-one risk share a common spectral scale on typical sketch events.

entry.title: Representation and Model Contributions on Small Molecular Benchmarks: Controlled Comparisons and External Evaluation

author.name: Nora A. M. A. Talkhan, Ibrahim Abdelbaky, Fatma A. Omara

entry.summary: This work disentangles how much of molecular property prediction gains come from the model versus the molecular representation, using a two-by-two factorial design crossing models (random forest, CatBoost, TabPFN, TabFM) with representations (fingerprints, RDKit descriptors) across seven MoleculeNet datasets with paired scaffold bootstrap tests. This exposes confounding in the common practice of benchmarking new models against fingerprint-based random forests.

entry.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Jianliang Ye, Sen Na

entry.summary: The paper develops a sketched derivative-free stochastic sequential quadratic programming method that achieves both computational efficiency (per-iteration cost O((d+m)^2)) and valid statistical inference for equality-constrained problems where gradients are unavailable. It addresses the gap between efficient online optimization and uncertainty quantification without derivatives.

entry.title: Lexical Tone and Word Order Matter in Translation: Prosodic Correspondence Across Languages

author.name: Haopeng Xie, Ismail Rasim Ulgen, Shengying Zhao, Berrak Sisman, Philipp Koehn

entry.summary: The paper presents the first systematic word-level analysis of prosodic correspondence in translated speech across tonal and non-tonal Asian languages, comparing pitch and energy correspondence between English and Mandarin, Thai, Vietnamese, and Japanese. It shows that lexical tone and word reordering significantly shape how prosody maps across translation. This informs more expressive and prosodically faithful speech translation systems.

entry.title: Towards a Multimodal Aesthetic Agent for Photographic Reference Grading

author.name: Kunjie Lin, Haitao Zhang, Bosheng Chen, Lanhui Xu, Gaofeng Pan, Yuxin Lin, Tianjiao Liu, Yi Yang, Yue Huang, Xinghao Ding, Zixu Lin, Yunlong Lin

entry.summary: JarvisAura is a multimodal agent that formulates reference-guided photographic color grading as structured decision-making in an editable parameter space, letting users selectively adopt color and tonal characteristics of a reference photo. Unlike pixel-space generative editors, it preserves editable parameters for subsequent refinement.

entry.title: Rescuing Discarded Boundary Samples in Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Yuzhao Jiang, Meng Zhang, Jie Ma, Xiaohong Guan

entry.summary: The paper proposes Boundary Refinement and Correction (BRC), an add-on for confidence-thresholded semi-supervised learning that recovers useful low-confidence samples near class boundaries that standard pseudo-labeling discards. BRC keeps the base method's pseudo-label selection unchanged while extracting additional training signal from boundary samples to reduce confirmation bias.

entry.title: Diving Deeper into Dense Keypoint Localization in Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Jiahong Chen, Jinghao Wang, Yueneng Yang, Banglei Guan, Zi Wang, Dewen Hu, Qifeng Yu

entry.summary: GHLAPose is a global-to-local framework for 6D object pose estimation that combines hybrid Gray-binary encoding, which alleviates the discontinuity of pure binary keypoint encoding, with local-aware refinement to reduce quantization-induced localization uncertainty. The framework improves training stability at high resolutions and delivers stronger pose accuracy.

entry.title: DAA for an Autonomous Delivery Drone: Maneuver Selection Policies for Near-Collision Risk Avoidance

author.name: Franco Callari, Ishay Kamon, Anthony Narkawitz, Pradeep Yarlagadda, Amir Navot

entry.summary: Presents and compares two detect-and-avoid maneuver-selection strategies for small autonomous delivery drones under sub-km detection ranges, severe decision-time limits, high CPA uncertainty, and constrained maneuver envelopes at low altitude. The strategies include a purely geometric steering approach and a second policy compared across these realistic constraints.

entry.title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Tiago Sim\~ao Ferreira (Federal Institute of Minas Gerais - IFMG), Farzad Fallahi (University of Luxembourg)

entry.summary: The paper proposes an Operational Design Domain-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for rationalizing Level 4 autonomous vehicle architectures, propagating ODD-specific capabilities, fault assumptions, post-fault policies, and sensing requirements through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations (removal, relocation, functional changes) are evaluated to reduce complexity, validation burden, and lifecycle cost while preserving critical driving functions.

entry.title: The new METR time horizon results: basic explainer

author.name: draganover

entry.summary: A companion explainer for METR's latest AI task time-horizon results, translating the plots and takeaways for a general audience, including what time horizons measure and why they matter for forecasting AI research acceleration. The author explicitly defers to the original METR post for methodology and limitations. It is a communication piece rather than original research.

entry.title: ECLIPSE: Embedding-Centered Foundation-Model Federated Knowledge Transfer for Data-Free Edge Intelligence

author.name: S. Kawa Atapour, S. Jamal Seyedmohammadi, Maryam Hosseini, S. Mohammad Sheikholeslami, Jamshid Abouei, Konstantinos Plataniotis, Arash Mohammadi

entry.summary: ECLIPSE proposes an embedding-centered framework for federated knowledge transfer from a server-hosted foundation model to resource-constrained edge clients in data-free settings, where no shared reference dataset exists for aligning distributed knowledge. It aims to bring foundation-model representations to privacy-sensitive edge networks.

entry.title: HiCal: Offline Calibration for Hierarchical Scale Encoding in Accurate HiF4 Quantization

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Yanzhao Li, Hui Dong, Sifan Cheng, Mingen Zheng, Hui Wang

entry.summary: HiCal improves HiFloat4 (HiF4) block floating-point quantization for low-bit LLM inference by offline-calibrating the hierarchical scale encoding, refining rounding rules and scale-extension thresholds across a global scale and two binary extension levels. Better-calibrated scales capture the statistical characteristics of quantized tensors, improving accuracy at 4-bit-class precision.

entry.title: MediaStormBench-CameraLog: Can Multimodal Models Identify a Camera's Log Curve?

author.name: Ming Ma, Wenhao Hu, Qichao Wang, Yuhao Wang, Junpeng Zhao, Qiyi Wang, Fangrui Zhang, Zhiqian Lai, Shanxin Guan, Haoyi Pei, Hongan Chen, Rui Gong

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first subset of MediaStormBench, a multimodal benchmark from real film and TV production, focused on identifying a clip's camera Log curve without metadata, a foundational ingest and color-grading task. It frames a practical, previously unbenchmarked perception problem where a wrong curve choice shifts colors across an entire project. It probes whether current multimodal models can handle production-grade visual reasoning.

entry.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM

author.name: Weicong Zhang, Yuan Huang, Yu Zheng, Lin Chenxiao, Yingying Li, Lilong Fan, Liangdong Zhuang, Yufan Chen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiaming Zhang

entry.summary: GOLD-SLAM is a SLAM system combining panoramic cameras with LiDAR depth priors for Gaussian-splatting reconstruction, performing tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and using visual features where LiDAR coverage is absent. It introduces depth-aware map extension and pruning to handle insufficient surface coverage and floating artifacts.

entry.title: Taxi: Analyzing Agents at (Real) Scale

author.name: Guy Dar

entry.summary: Taxi is a technical report describing a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring LLM agents at scale up to millions of steps, using clustering to build step taxonomies plus full SQL access queried through a hybrid pipeline guided by a coding agent. It also experimentally integrates decision models for low-cost semantic routing and evaluation.

entry.title: CROSS-Calib: Selective Channel Calibration for Ultrasound Reconstruction

author.name: Tongxiao Hu, Junyu Zhou

entry.summary: CROSS-Calib is a channel recovery method for ultrasound imaging that uses predictions from other channels as references for amplitude and phase calibration, with a context-based gate that selectively combines calibrated measurements with predicted echoes. On in vivo test sets it outperforms baselines under gain errors and transient interference, and phantom tests show restored cyst contrast. It targets the practical challenge of repairing corrupted ultrasound signals without discarding usable data.

entry.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations

author.name: Mart\'in Escard\'o, Paulo Oliva

entry.summary: The paper gives a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning combining the continuation and reader monads, recording search bounds in monadic outcomes rather than move types. It also shows the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute both optimal outcomes and optimal plays, providing an alternative to prior typed generalizations.

entry.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective

author.name: Sabrine Aroua, Osama Arouk, Pegah Alizadeh

entry.summary: This survey presents a technique-agnostic taxonomy of AI-native radio access network (RAN) decision-making organized around four complementary capabilities: Representation and Reasoning, Prediction and Simulation, Adaptive Control, and Decision Synthesis. Using this functional lens, it compares AI approaches including foundation models and world models against conventional model-based methods across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. It offers a common vocabulary for designing hybrid AI and conventional control in 6G-era networks.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Iranian Doctoral Entrance Exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering

author.name: Sima Akbari Neisiyani, Hossein Taghizad

entry.summary: The authors evaluate GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Grok 4 zero-shot on 433 multiple-choice questions from 2024-2025 Iranian national PhD entrance exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering, in both Persian and English, yielding 3,464 scored responses. All are well-established frontier models, and the study measures their performance on figure-dependent Persian-language technical questions.

entry.title: GoldiBench: Right Tools, Wrong Amount -- Benchmarking Agents on Effect Judgement in Professional Editing

author.name: Wang Yang, Xinpeng Li, Yanyan Zhang, Chaoda Song, Shouren Wang, Debargha Ganguly, Vikash Singh, Chuang Ma, Xiaoran Cai, Kai Ye, Xiaotian Han, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: GoldiBench is a benchmark of 500 editing tasks across five professional applications where agents must judge how much of each tool to apply to match a target image rendered from a hidden program, with re-rendered outputs compared against ground truth. It exposes that existing VLM-judged benchmarks pass more than half of half- and triple-strength errors, i.e., agents pick the right tools in wrong amounts.

entry.title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators

author.name: Guodan Dong, Qi Qian, Feifei Xue, Jianhua Qin, Chang Xu, Wenzhong Shen

entry.summary: This paper applies a physics-informed Fourier neural operator with 4D spectral convolutions and incompressibility constraints to reconstruct 3D wakes behind floating offshore wind turbines under surge-pitch motion, using LES-generated training data for 5 MW and 22 MW turbines. It demonstrates cross-scale transfer across turbine sizes at motion-based Strouhal numbers of 0.2-0.6.

entry.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA

author.name: Hien Minh Tran, Thi-Thu-Hien Pham, Le Duy Tan, Hieu Xuan Nguyen, Tuong-Anh Mai-Phan

entry.summary: The authors propose an automated cardiac phenotyping pipeline for coronary CT angiography that combines deep learning segmentation with anatomical reasoning, including graph-geometry-based pericoronary adipose tissue sampling and a surrogate epicardial fat compartment that removes the need for expert pericardium contours. It was benchmarked on five public datasets.

entry.title: Part-Set Prototypes for Explainable Mountain Gazelles Sex Classification

author.name: Tali Boneh Shitrit, Amir Kedem, Ilan Shimshoni, Anna Zamansky

entry.summary: The paper introduces set prototypes, an architecture for self-explainable fine-grained recognition where both the number of parts and their spatial layouts are mined from data using truncated Sinkhorn competition over a frozen DINOv3 token grid. It is evaluated on camera-trap imagery of Mountain Gazelles for sex classification under occlusion, camouflage, and environmental shortcuts. The architecture generalizes explainable part-based recognition to unconstrained imagery.

entry.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Atefeh Hemmati Golsefidi, David Pisinger

entry.summary: This paper provides an analytical foundation for decision-guided generative scenario search in two-stage stochastic programming by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve, replacing a previous black-box gradient estimate. It includes a heuristic backup direction when duals are unavailable.

entry.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs

author.name: Amit Jena, Bin Wang, Aoxia Chen, Brad Chadwell, Billy Yancey, Le Xie

entry.summary: The authors use LLM in-context learning to build adaptive digital twins that predict electromagnetic transients in data centers, addressing the non-adaptivity of conventional data-driven surrogates as configurations change. This targets the growing power-management challenge created by AI workloads. It demonstrates LLMs being applied to power-systems simulation rather than text tasks.

entry.title: Local subspace encoding for spectral prediction: from TabPFN to operator-adaptive calibration

author.name: Gregory Beurier, Robin Reiter, Denis Cornet, Lauriane Rouan

entry.summary: The paper reanalyses prior experiments to test whether spectral representations from RamanPFN, particularly Local Vibrational Subspace Encoding (LVSE), improve tabular prior-fitted networks like TabPFN on near-infrared spectral prediction tasks. Across 61 matched prediction tasks, LVSE reduces RMSE relative to raw-spectrum TabPFN by roughly 10-15% depending on the checkpoint.

entry.title: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning enhanced Federated Learning for Predicting Remaining Useful Lifetime

author.name: Rajarshi Chattopadhyay, Chen-Khong Tham

entry.summary: Combines cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with federated learning for transformer-based remaining useful life prediction, adapting client model exchange over lossy UDP wireless links by selecting what to transmit under packet drops. Targets industrial IoT prognostics where data is siloed and privacy-sensitive.

entry.title: Multi-view Random-set Learning

author.name: Mengchi Zuo, Tianyang Wang, Cai Xu, Ziyu Guan, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: This work addresses view degradation in trusted multi-view learning, where individual views carry only partial label information. It proposes representing unresolved class groups as random sets rather than forcing unambiguous per-class evidence, enabling direct cross-view refinement of candidate groups before fusion.

entry.title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction

author.name: Yicheng Song, Zhipeng Yang, Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka

entry.summary: This work builds a minimal-complexity quantum reservoir computing model based on an open uniform XX chain and shows that pure dephasing, usually treated as noise, can guarantee echo-state and fading-memory properties needed for temporal processing. The model demonstrates competitive nonlinear time-series prediction while turning a quantum noise channel into a computational resource.

entry.title: A Piecewise-Linear Activation Function for Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Shahd Hekal, Joram Kim, Jeova Farias Sales Rocha Neto

entry.summary: The paper introduces JaSIN, a family of bounded piecewise-linear activations interpolating between ReLU and a piecewise-linear sinusoid without transcendental operations, to isolate which ReLU property harms implicit neural representations. Ablations attribute gains to boundedness, bump shape, centering, and oscillation, raising ReLU from 24.0 to 37.3 dB PSNR on Kodak images.

entry.title: $\epsilon$-Seg++: Ensembling Across Hierarchy and Training Time for Label-Efficient EM Segmentation

author.name: Edoardo Giacomello, Sheida Rahnamai Kordasiabi, Mehdi Seifi, Florian Jug

entry.summary: epsilon-Seg++ extends a hierarchical VAE segmentation method for electron microscopy by placing semantic experts at every hierarchy level combined via a parameter-free product of experts, and adds leakage-free 3D sub-volume evaluation under sparse supervision. It targets label-efficient segmentation important for cell biology.

entry.title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Yanlin Li, Ganzhao Yuan

entry.summary: NABLA is a stochastic optimizer combining block-diagonal row and column preconditioners from second-moment statistics with a closed-loop feedback rule that adapts the gradient averaging coefficient based on cumulative stochastic-gradient energy. The method is horizon-free and avoids fixed decay hyperparameters for the preconditioner.

entry.title: The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers

author.name: Gendo Kumoi, Hideki Yagi, Manabu Kobayashi, Shigeichi Hirasawa

entry.summary: This theoretical paper derives upper and lower bounds on the excess error rate of error-correcting output codes over the Bayes classifier when binary classifiers produce posterior estimates corrupted by Gaussian noise. Recasting decoding as a test over a Gaussian channel, the analysis shows large Hamming distance is necessary and sufficient for reducing excess error, and characterizes when the error floor becomes independent of the number of classes. It provides clean information-theoretic insight into a classical multi-class classification technique.

entry.title: ArabFake: A multitask deep learning framework for Arabic fake news Detection, Categorization, and risk prediction

author.name: Ahmed Maher Khafaga Shehata, Mohammed Nasser Al-Suqri, Nour Eldin Mohamed Elshaiekh Osman, Faten Hamad, Yousuf Nasser Alhusaini, Ahmed Mahfouz

entry.summary: ArabFake is a multitask deep learning framework built on MARBERTv2 that jointly performs Arabic fake news detection, content categorization, and risk assessment, going beyond binary classification. Multitask learning through shared representations improves efficiency and performance across the three tasks. It addresses underexplored misinformation challenges in Arabic dialectal media.

entry.title: Phoneme-identity depth profiles do not reliably predict LoRA placement for dysarthric ASR

author.name: Bernard Muller, LaVonne Roberts

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests a recently proposed heuristic for parameter-efficient adaptation of speech foundation models: probing encoder layers to find where phonetic information is most decodable and placing LoRA adapters there. Across two ASR models (Qwen3-ASR and Whisper-small) and two dysarthric speech corpora, the authors find the heuristic fails, with probe results varying more by seed than by corpus. The work provides a useful negative result and reproducibility check for the low-resource, dysarthric ASR community.

entry.title: WaveSR: Physics-Inspired Wave Evolution Attention for Efficient Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Xiaoyan Lei, Biao Luo, Wenlong Zhang, Tingwen Huang, Chunhua Yang, Weihua Gui

entry.summary: Proposes WaveSR, an efficient image super-resolution framework built on physics-inspired wave evolution attention. It uses the closed-form solution of the 2D wave equation in the FFT domain so different frequency components evolve independently, achieving linear complexity, paired with a frequency-adaptive feed-forward network.

entry.title: EditText: Structure-Aware Generation and Selective Visual Transport for Fine-Grained Text Editing

author.name: Zhaobin Chu, Guandong Li, Xin Lv, Zhiwei Zeng

entry.summary: This paper introduces EditText, a unified framework for fine-grained text editing in images that accurately replaces text in a specified region while preserving font, color, texture, and visual consistency elsewhere. It combines target character generation with visual transport from the source image, using dual-condition fill inputs (a masked image canvas plus a style reference) and a novel Attention Transport mechanism. The work matters because precise text editing is a common requirement in design, document, and advertising workflows where generative models often distort style or surrounding content.

entry.title: CREDIT: Compositional Reliability Learning for Noisy Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Tiancai Zhou, Yongxiang Li, Suimei Liu, Zhong Yuan, Dezhong Peng, Xi Peng, Xu Wang

entry.summary: CREDIT addresses noisy triplet correspondence in composed image retrieval, where the semantic link between reference image, modification text, and target image is unreliable. It replaces fixed decision rules with compositional reliability learning that models varying degrees of semantic trustworthiness rather than binary correctness.

entry.title: One Subspace Is Not Enough: LocalSubspaceAD for Training-Free Few-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Daniel Pr\"oll, Sebastian Hegenbart

entry.summary: LocalSubspaceAD extends training-free few-shot anomaly detection from a single principal subspace of foundation-model patch features to a mixture of per-region subspaces, partitioning patches via k-means so each semantic group gets its own nominal model. This prevents deviations anomalous in one region from being masked by another region's variability.

entry.title: TDD: Target-Discrepancy Distillation for Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Zefan Feng, Zhaocheng Yu, Laibin Chang, Kui Jiang, Junjun Jiang, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: TDD distills two complementary signals from an underwater vision-language teacher into a lightweight guidance network: reference features for target appearance and paired feature residuals describing the discrepancy between the degraded observation and its target. This explicitly structures the enhancement problem around what to recover and how the input differs from it.

entry.title: On the Capabilities and Limitations of Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Cloud Segmentation

author.name: Jose Sosa, Thomas Gillet, Rim Sleimi, Albert Abello

entry.summary: This paper evaluates twelve open-vocabulary segmentation approaches across six Earth observation datasets for zero-shot cloud detection, covering both binary cloud masks and multiclass separation of thick clouds, thin clouds, shadows, and background. SegEarth-OV3 achieves the best binary detection, revealing substantial performance variation across models and datasets.

entry.title: CityRecast: Suppressing Persistent Artifacts in Generative Satellite 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Shuo Cui, Yingyan Hou, Wanxuan Lu, Hongfeng Yu, Daobing Zhang, Xian Sun

entry.summary: Introduces CityRecast, a method for suppressing ghosting, streaking, and blur artifacts in generative satellite-based 3D Gaussian scene reconstruction, using multi-angle warm-up to constrain Gaussian spatial extent plus surface-guided replacement and supervision calibration during progressive refinement. Targets robust reconstruction under sparse observations and cross-date scene changes.

entry.title: Cif-query bridging for audio-native asr transfer to visual speech recognition

author.name: Chang Sun, Dongliang Xie, Wanpeng Xie, Bo Qin, Hong Yang

entry.summary: CIF-Query Bridge connects a Paraformer visual speech recognition encoder to Qwen3-ASR via a lightweight two-layer cross-attention bridge over CIF-predicted token-rate queries, transferring audio-native speech recognition priors to visual speech. This avoids autoregressive processing of hundreds of video frames while preserving uncompressed visual context. The approach shows results on the CMLR benchmark.

entry.title: A Self-Organizing Swarm Control Model for Underwater Robots Based on Turing-Type Reaction-Diffusion Principles

author.name: Takeshi Ishida

entry.summary: Proposes a decentralized underwater robot swarm control model requiring no leader, GPS, or absolute coordinates, using only the count of received signals from two communication channels of differing range. It extends a Turing pattern formation cellular automaton to continuous space, enabling coordination under severe bandwidth and visibility constraints.

entry.title: A Face Robot which Imitates Human Musculoskeletal Skin System and Its Evaluation on Basic Movement of Facial Expression

author.name: Shun Kaneko, Shunnosuke Yoshimura, Akihiro Miki, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: The authors build an anatomically inspired facial robot that reproduces the layered bone-muscle-skin organization of the human face using 3D anatomical data, wire-driven compliant muscles routed through PTFE tubes, and 65 muscles covering 47 Facial Action Coding System action units. They evaluate the platform on basic facial-expression movements. This matters for human-robot interaction, since lifelike expressive faces are central to social robots, and reproducing FACS action units provides a standardized basis for evaluating facial expressivity.

entry.title: Self-supervised quality evaluation of grid maps without ground truth

author.name: Unal Artan, Manuel Castellano-Quero, Johannes A. Stork, Martin Magnusson

entry.summary: This paper proposes a self-supervised approach to assessing quality of 2D occupancy grid maps using only the map itself as input, independent of the underlying mapping algorithm and without ground-truth labels. It targets robot introspection and assistance for human map editors in large environments.

entry.title: I still don't believe in superintelligence

author.name: Haoxing Du

entry.summary: An argument against the intuition that superhuman AI is vastly beyond the best humans, using handicap-based skill-gap measurements in Go and chess to claim the human-AI gap is smaller than commonly assumed. The author challenges quotes like Noam Brown's characterization of Go AIs as orders of magnitude stronger than humans. This pushes back on a common intuition pump used in AI risk discussions.

entry.title: Gated Concept Adapters: Layer-Wise Concept Bottlenecks for Auditable Text Understanding

author.name: Niloofar Ranjbar, Saeedeh Momtazi, Mohammad Mehdi Homayounpoor

entry.summary: Gated Concept Adapters attach gated, low-dimensional concept-producing readout adapters to selected layers of pretrained Transformers, creating a concept-mediated interface for predictions in text understanding tasks. The approach aims to make predictions auditable and intervenable for sensitive applications like affect inference and content moderation.

entry.title: Evaluating Frontier-Model Agent Skills with Open-Weight Models in a Science Gateway

author.name: Komal Thareja, Mats Rynge, Anirban Mandal, Ewa Deelman

entry.summary: The authors packaged Pegasus workflow-management expertise as skills and specialist agents built with a frontier model, offered to scientists through the PegasusAI Studio gateway, then tested whether those skills transfer to open-weight models served free on research cyberinfrastructure. The paper evaluates how well agent skills written for a frontier model work when users lack frontier-model access.

entry.title: GaokaoMathGen: Chinese Gaokao Mathematics Finale Problem Generation Controlled by Latent Reasoning Structures

author.name: Qian Chen, Kun Zhu, Zhongyi Wang, Ling Chen

entry.summary: GaokaoMathGen generates Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problems by extracting standardized latent reasoning structures (skills, methods, a core identity, a pivot step) from seed problems and using them as structural controls for constrained synthesis. It further estimates realized difficulty through logical-quality filtering rather than relying on prompted difficulty targets. This improves controllability of educational problem generation beyond surface-level specifications.

entry.title: Conformalized Tree-Based Gradient Ensembles for Out-of-Distribution Detection and Plausible Recourse

author.name: Mariam Zakaria Moussa Ali

entry.summary: This work addresses Goodhart-style exploitation in counterfactual recourse for gradient-boosted decision trees, where search against confidence proxies yields implausible out-of-distribution recommendations. It combines conformalized OOD gating using anomaly detectors with actionability-constrained counterfactual search, validated on the Adult and Give Me Some Credit tabular benchmarks.

entry.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study

author.name: Barnabas Juhasz, Rolf Pfister

entry.summary: The authors test whether supplying specific research papers as context improves navigation code that Claude Opus 5, an LLM released in mid-2026, writes for a Go2 quadruped with the locomotion policy frozen. They compare controllers across behavior trees, edited navigators, and from-scratch settings, including scenarios where the maze route is blocked mid-episode. Only partial improvements from paper context are observed, making it a useful exploratory result on in-context knowledge application.

entry.title: From the ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling

author.name: Jan Rohleff, Johannes Schropp

entry.summary: This paper provides convergence guarantees for the VAE-NLME algorithm, which applies variational autoencoders to nonlinear mixed-effects models used in pharmacometrics for dosing and regulatory decisions. It proves almost-sure convergence of the ELBO objective to stationary points without requiring exact encoder training, and connects the ELBO solution to maximum likelihood.

entry.title: On the Effectiveness of Resampling for Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Cyril Perosino (GOAL), Rino Di Chiara (Polito), Hamida Seba (GOAL)

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares class weighting and six oversampling strategies across ten detector configurations (GNNs, tree ensembles, tabular foundation models) on 17 GADBench datasets in the low-label regime. It finds no statistically resolved gains on datasets with organic anomalies, while which nodes are labelled matters as much as the strategy, with Gaussian oversampling helping only on injected-anomaly datasets.

entry.title: When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes

author.name: Gendo Kumoi

entry.summary: The paper characterizes code matrices for which the product decoder of error-correcting output codes agrees with the Bayes-optimal class in the noiseless setting, complementing the known equidistance condition for the sum decoder. It analyzes comparisons via an M-estimator with artanh influence function and specializes to pairwise and one-vs-rest structures.

entry.title: Exact Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphic Shear Splitting: Continuous-Discrete Geometric Bounds, Reversible Memory Backpropagation, and Expressivity Frontiers in Volumetric Mapping

author.name: Alvaro Garcia-Casas

entry.summary: The paper formulates an exact structure-preserving framework for incompressible 3D image registration using cascaded coordinate shears whose convective nonlinearities vanish, enabling closed-form integration and eliminating numerical volume drift seen in SVF/LDDMM methods. It also provides geometric bounds, reversible memory-efficient backpropagation, and expressivity analysis.

entry.title: Measuring Counterfactual Credit in a Replayable Wildfire-Suppression Benchmark

author.name: Alireza Moghaddasi

entry.summary: The paper introduces FLARE, a stochastic, replayable wildfire suppression benchmark for cooperative multi-agent RL that permits replaying any moment under the same random events to isolate each agent's counterfactual effect. It distinguishes return prediction from credit assignment, using simulator credit for training and end-of-episode replay to grade critics across eight seeds.

entry.title: A General Framework for E-process Stopping Rules in Best-Arm Identification

author.name: Donghyun Park, Seohwa Hwang, Junyong Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes e-process-based stopping rules for best-arm identification, offering flexible design that recovers the classical Chernoff rule as a special case. It analyzes asymptotic optimality of delta-PAC algorithms, decomposing conditions into sampling-policy convergence, e-process efficiency, and inherent stochastic behavior, and proves a sufficient condition.

entry.title: Degree-bounded Satisfiability of Local MPNNs with Sum Aggregation is NEXPTIME-hard

author.name: Marco S\"alzer

entry.summary: The paper proves that deciding whether there exists a bounded-degree graph (even degree 3) accepted by a message-passing neural network with sum aggregation and ReLU activations is NEXPTIME-hard. This is a tight computational complexity result for verification of MPNNs on local graph classes.

entry.title: Generating Schema-Aligned Synthetic Dialogues and Measuring Their Diversity

author.name: Konrad Stolte, Toni Fetzer

entry.summary: The authors generate paired dialogue-to-record training data by sampling a schema-valid record first and then writing a dialogue from it, eliminating annotation needs for sensitive domains. To overcome low diversity from naive prompting, they add sampled variation configurations, personas, and a topic plan ordering record fields, and they measure resulting dialogue diversity. This is a practical recipe for creating structured-record dialogue data.

entry.title: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens

author.name: Yi-Jun Chen, I-Tsen Hsieh, Li-Wun Chang

entry.summary: This study examines how supportive versus challenging chatbot interaction styles affect user experience and continuance intention across cultures, testing moderation by people-pleasing tendency with Taiwanese (N=49) and Korean (N=52) participants on a tourism-planning task. Supportive chatbots consistently increased satisfaction, trust, and continued use, while PPT did not moderate effects. It offers empirical evidence on cultural factors in conversational AI design.

entry.title: SynAVID: A Synthetic Audio-Visual Immersive Dataset of Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Jun Xu, Sujing Li, Chunhao Bi, Zhengxue Cheng, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Li Song

entry.summary: SynAVID is a synthetic dataset combining synchronized viewpoint-dependent binaural audio with visual rendering across eight dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes, using shared scene dynamics and sound-source events for geometry-aware acoustic synthesis. It supports evaluation of visual reconstruction, binaural audio reconstruction, and audiovisual editing.

entry.title: FedTumor-IoMT: Federated Learning-Aided Brain Tumor Diagnosis on Resource-Constrained Edge IoMT Devices

author.name: Pranshu Jena, Prajnyajit Mohanty, Umesh C. Pati

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight multitask federated learning framework for joint brain tumor segmentation and classification on edge Internet-of-Medical-Things devices, using a shared LiteMedSAM encoder with TinyViT features, a coordinate-attention segmentation decoder, and selective encoder freezing for efficient local training. Extends edge support beyond classification-only prior work.

entry.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated As Nvidia CEO at Behest of President Trump

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A LessWrong post by Zvi reporting that President Trump publicly pressured and called the Nvidia board, leading to Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO within hours, with markets adding trillions in value and Nvidia surging. The author frames the event as a landmark scandal for rule of law and free markets, and predicts consequences for chip sales to China and adversarial maximization.

entry.title: Drift: government decisions are moving to machines

author.name: Hubert Liège

entry.summary: A forecasting essay predicting with 70% confidence that by 2036, learned AI systems will in fact make most decisions in at least one major area of government decision-making in a high-income country, regardless of nominal human oversight. It frames this as gradual drift rather than deliberate policy, opening with Madison on controlling government. The post explores accountability implications of de facto algorithmic governance.

entry.title: California politics seems like a real hope for an AI slowdown

author.name: Jacob Meyer Cohen

entry.summary: Fleshes out the case that California state legislative or gubernatorial action is an underrated path to forcing major AI developers to pace or pause, contrasting it with lab advocacy and federal lobbying. The author argues the federal route is essentially intractable without a catastrophic incident, and notes only around 15 AI-safety community members currently work on the California path.

entry.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users “DJ their art”

author.name: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers present TangiMap, a system that uses an agentic AI approach to dynamically map digital software widgets onto tangible physical controls on everyday devices, supporting tasks like photo editing, animation, music performance, and 3D modeling. The work aims to restore the efficiency and precision of physical controls that preprogrammed hardware cannot offer.

entry.title: MargEmbed-Akan: Bridging Twi Questions and English Knowledge through Cross-Lingual Score Distillation

author.name: Prince N. Y. Annan, Ali A. A. Aziz, Stephen E. Moore

entry.summary: The paper evaluates eight retrieval systems on Twi-English cross-lingual retrieval tasks and introduces MargEmbed-Akan, a 560M-parameter open query encoder distilled from AfriE5-Large-instruct via cross-lingual score distillation. It targets the gap where Twi speakers seek mostly English-language online information.

entry.title: Off-the-Shelf Autonomous Agents for Game Playtesting

author.name: Ayush Maniar, Eryk Banatt

entry.summary: The paper presents Buddy, an autonomous game-solving agent that pursues long-horizon objectives in an unseen 3D RPG using only off-the-shelf language models, without walkthroughs or training. It demonstrates game solving via exploration, automatic bug ticket logging, and conversational capabilities, showing the paradigm works on novel environments not memorized from pretraining.

entry.title: LimoBench: How Street Smart Are Large Language Models?

author.name: Gautam Choudhary, Jack Peng, Udesh Kumarasinghe, Rachel Rafik, Yousef Hammad, Ahmed Samy, Walid G. Aref

entry.summary: LimoBench is a street-level benchmark of 82 natural-language location queries spanning seven canonical spatial operations including geocoding, reverse geocoding, routing, range search, and k-nearest-neighbor search. It tests whether LLMs can reliably handle real-world coordinates, POIs, and geospatial distances. The small but focused design probes a capability gap relevant to map-based services and spatial database interfaces.

entry.title: Breaking the Binary-Lifting Barrier for DNA Minimizer Density: Exact Optimization of a Native 4-ary Order at (w, k) = (12, 5)

author.name: Stefan G. Creadore, Peyton Berntsen

entry.summary: This paper improves DNA minimizer schemes by optimizing a native 4-ary order at (w, k) = (12, 5) rather than lifting binary orders via bit-plane ranking, unlocking a larger universal hitting set prefix than GreedyMini or OptMini. It reports exact expected DNA density improvements over the state of the art.

entry.title: InletScope: Multiscale pressure-based inlet unstart monitoring under changing sensor configurations

author.name: Jiaming Liu, Fenlou Zhai, Ao Xue, Liangliang Tang, Cheng Ding, Daoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: InletScope is a monitoring system for supersonic inlet unstart that combines shared multiscale pressure encoding, learned scale fusion, and sensor-probability averaging so that measurement sets can change without retraining. Evaluated on seven Mach-2.9 runs with annotated events, it performs unstart detection and new-onset prediction within a 0.5-second horizon.

entry.title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer

author.name: Yanlin Fu, Wei Liu, Liming Zhao

entry.summary: The paper studies why intermediate layers of foundation models often outperform final layers when used as frozen feature extractors, using EEG foundation models as a testbed. Across five models and three tasks, it disentangles readout quality from intrinsic layer utility and shows that layer selections transfer across datasets and task families.

entry.title: Denoising Diffusion with Progressive Posterior Sampling

author.name: Zeyu Luo, Shuai Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes progressive posterior sampling with manifold projection for solving noisy linear inverse problems with diffusion priors, automatically estimating measurement noise variance and avoiding SVD of the measurement operator. During reverse diffusion it constructs closed-form Gaussian posterior approximations and projects guided samples onto a learned manifold.

entry.title: Rapid Exploratory Maps and their potential role in supporting evidence-to-policy dialogues and processes

author.name: Gareth J. Hollands, Ian Shemilt, James Thomas

entry.summary: This position-style paper proposes rapid exploratory maps to accelerate the scoping phase of evidence synthesis for policy, replacing weeks-to-months of mostly manual evidence mapping with faster semi-automated processes. It argues such maps can better connect research question formulation to policymaker needs during evidence-to-policy dialogue.

entry.title: Fusion Gains Depend on the Implementation and the Calibration Target: An 18-Task Study of Prediction Intervals with a Single-Source Fallback

author.name: Liwei Deng, Lu Wang

entry.summary: The paper compares four multi-source fusion implementations against matched single-source learners on 18 regression tasks with prediction intervals. Results show fusion gains are highly implementation- and calibration-dependent, with different methods giving opposite verdicts on most tasks, and a development-set selector with a single-source fallback improving averaged scores.

entry.title: PFedHASNet: A Personalized Federated Hybrid Analog-Spike Network for Multi-Subject Motor Imagery EEG Decoding

author.name: Peijia Li, Ruidong Ma, Xianghong Lin, Xiangwen Wang, Guoyong Shi, Shuai Huang, Hongqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes a personalized federated hybrid analog-spiking network for motor imagery EEG decoding, combining continuous temporal features and leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics in a shared encoder while preserving subject privacy. Aims to leverage multi-subject data without centralizing sensitive recordings.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Classifier Chains

author.name: Romain Poggi, Jesse Read

entry.summary: The authors apply Monte Carlo Tree Search to probabilistic classifier chains for multi-label classification, targeting exact-set-match evaluation where joint label probability estimation matters. This offers a search-based alternative for label-dependence inference, relevant to noisy, large-label-space datasets in domains like medicine.

entry.title: ToneMamaba: Learning Contextualized Tonal Contours with Boundary-Reset State Space Models

author.name: Po-Yu Chiu, Yi-Fen Liu

entry.summary: ToneMamba is a boundary-aware state space model for Mandarin tone recognition that replaces static boundary embeddings with bidirectional state resets at syllable, word, and inter-phonetic-unit levels, plus rhythm-conditioned gating. It achieves 97.9% and 74.8% accuracy on read and conversational speech benchmarks, beating the ToneNet baseline by up to 15.9 points.

entry.title: ExitLUT: Boolean Early Exits for Efficient FPGA-Based Neural Network Inference

author.name: Oliver Cassidy, Marta Andronic, George A. Constantinides

entry.summary: ExitLUT replaces softmax-based early-exit decisions in neural networks with learned Boolean functions mapped directly into FPGA LUTs, cutting exit-decision LUT usage by 2.58x and eliminating decision-path DSP usage while preserving accuracy and exit behavior. This allows better resource allocation to the main datapath and improves design-space exploration outcomes.

entry.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain

author.name: Yongyuan Hu, Jiahao Li, Keqi Ni, Yuqi Ouyang, Hao Qin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid surrogate for terrain radio propagation that uses a deterministic analytical baseline for known physics (free-space spreading, antenna effects) and trains a neural network only on the terrain-dependent residual. This separates tractable physics from learned corrections, enabling fast coverage analysis in mountainous environments versus costly SSPE solvers.

entry.title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset

author.name: Dominique Regli, Brian C. Williams

entry.summary: This paper introduces the R-ADL dataset, a privacy-preserving radar sensing dataset with over eight hours of annotated recordings covering eight activities of daily living, aimed at supporting at-home monitoring for older adults. It addresses key gaps in prior work by expanding data scale and relaxing constraints on room configuration, helping to overcome the data scarcity that has limited radar-based activity recognition.

entry.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report

author.name: Yuchao Wu, XingCheng Liang, Xuanze Wang, Yini Huang, Yue Wu

entry.summary: SAG-Mem is a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and finds complementary evidence through query-time lexical expansion, avoiding model-inference-based construction (no LLM extraction, summarization, or relation building). BM25 retrieves initial candidates and expands queries at query time to surface intermediate evidence with low similarity to the original question. This reduces memory construction costs while retaining source details.

entry.title: HyMTS: A Multiscale Tensor Factorization-Based Network for Hyperspectral Image Restoration

author.name: Lei Xu, Fahad Sohrab, Moncef Gabbouj, Mehmet Yamac

entry.summary: HyMTS is a hyperspectral image restoration network whose backbone is built on Multi-scale Tensorial Summation factorization, embedding a low-rank prior directly into the network operator rather than via auxiliary losses or reconstruction constraints. This exploits the strong spectral and spatial redundancy of hyperspectral data as an architectural inductive bias. The design offers an alternative to dense attention or cross-band feature mixing used in prior restoration networks.

entry.title: DynaCue: Comparing Motion and Timing Between Groups of Videos

author.name: Hao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DynaCue, a two-sample permutation test combining motion, frame continuity, and appearance measurements to compare groups of videos without pre-selecting a single cue. It demonstrates that VideoScore's temporal consistency metric can miss motion-preference differences detectable by DynaCue in VideoGen-RewardBench comparisons.

entry.title: Cross-Version Compatibility of TESSERA Embeddings Through Lightweight Translation

author.name: Yutong Yang, Zhengpeng Feng

entry.summary: The paper tests whether lightweight converters allow a downstream classifier trained on one version of TESSERA satellite embedding releases to consume embeddings from another version, fitting converters between v1, v1.1, and v2 across 25 sites. Converted v1.1 embeddings nearly recover v2 classifier performance, though geographic transfer is less reliable.

entry.title: Which Parameters to Update? An Instance-Specific Adaptation Framework for Real-World Pansharpening

author.name: Jin-Liang Xiao, Liang-Jian Deng, Yu-Xuan Zhang, Hua Meng, Zhengchun Zhou

entry.summary: The paper proposes a test-time adaptation framework for pansharpening that selects and updates only a subset of pretrained network parameters for each observed PAN-LRMS image pair, mitigating distribution shift in real-world scenarios. An instance-specific selection mechanism determines which parameters to adapt per input.

entry.title: Geometric Control Analysis of an Internally Actuated Flying Wing

author.name: Jonathan Becker, Ella M. Atkins

entry.summary: Provides a rigorous geometric accessibility and controllability analysis for a fixed-wing UAV actuated only by an internal moving mass, momentum wheel, and thrust, eliminating traditional control surfaces. Using Lie bracket computations and the Lie Algebra Rank Condition, it proves generic small-time local accessibility, characterizes singular configurations, and addresses stronger controllability properties.

entry.title: The Measurement Problem of Consciousness

author.name: Walter Veit

entry.summary: A crossposted academic essay arguing the central challenge for consciousness science is measurement, identifying two problems when applying human-developed indicators to nonhuman cases: the indicator validity problem and the extrapolation problem. Relevant indirectly to AI welfare and machine consciousness debates. It is a methodological contribution to philosophy of science.

entry.title: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management

author.name: Malay Phadke, Chirath Hettiarachchi

entry.summary: XRL4T1D applies SHAP-based post-hoc explainability to pretrained RL insulin-dosing policies in the UVA/Padova simulator, comparing the importance of glucose and insulin-history inputs and summarizing insulin attributions over 20-minute windows motivated by insulin-on-board physiology. The framework evaluates whether explanations align with clinical intuition without retraining the policies.

entry.title: Geo-SMILE: Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability with Local Explanations for Geospatial Machine Learning

author.name: Shadieh Mohammadi, Koorosh Aslansefat

entry.summary: Geo-SMILE extends model-agnostic local explanation methods to geospatial data by separating substantive feature effects from geographic-position effects through complementary perturbation branches, using Wasserstein-distance-weighted surrogates. The framework explicitly treats spatial context in explanations, which conventional post-hoc methods developed for non-spatial inputs neglect.

entry.title: When Knowledge-Tracing Rankings Depend on Available History: A Source-Correction and Matched-Information Audit on ASSISTments 2009 and 2015

author.name: Devis Wawan Saputra

entry.summary: This audit shows that knowledge-tracing benchmark comparisons on ASSISTments are confounded by data provenance and differing access to learner history: hundreds of learners have different skill-response sequences between a popular mirror and the corrected official 2009 release. It re-evaluates models under matched history constraints on a fresh 4,000-learner 2015 sample.

entry.title: MELODI: Similarity-Identity Decoupling for Lightweight Ranking

author.name: Quoc Phong Nguyen, Vuong Le, Volodymyr Vaskovych, Julien Monteil
