entry.summary: MELODI is a framework for latency-constrained candidate ranking that decouples target-history compatibility from target-only information, identifying linearity conditions under which the cheaper pool-then-similarity computation is equivalent to similarity-then-pool. The instantiation combines target-conditioned multi-head history pooling with a single lightweight cross layer.

entry.title: FaceNet versus VGG Features in Wasserstein Distortion for Face Image Compression

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Jona Ball\'e

entry.summary: The paper tests whether face-recognition features (FaceNet) better serve Wasserstein distortion objectives for perceptual face image compression than generic VGG features, within the Cool-Chic codec. In a preliminary pairwise human study at roughly 0.15 bits per pixel, FaceNet-based reconstructions were preferred in 72.5% of judgments. This suggests task-specific features improve perceptual codec optimization for faces.

entry.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Malaria Parasite Detection and Species Differentiation in Thick Blood Smear Images: A Pilot Feasibility Study

author.name: Haimanot Bitew, Ayisheshim Almaw, Habtamu Zegeye, Demeke Alene

entry.summary: TRACE-Mal combines YOLOv8n-seg detection with a six-model soft-voting ensemble for malaria parasite detection and species differentiation (P. falciparum vs P. vivax) on 2,847 parasite crops from 250 thick smears, achieving mAP50 of 0.79 and macro F1 of 0.84. The pilot study tests whether agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP explanations correlates with correctness of species calls. This explores explanation-agreement as a reliability signal in clinical AI.

entry.title: PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL: Polarization-Keyed Examination Papers and Mandatory Issued Eyewear that Displace AI Glasses and Extend Universal Design

author.name: Dohyeon Kwon

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hardware-based anti-cheating protocol for examinations in the era of camera-equipped AI glasses: all candidates wear authority-issued eyewear, and question papers are printed with circular-polarization laminates so text is visible only through the issued analyzers. This makes pages appear uniformly grey to naked eyes and unfiltered cameras, neutralizing smart-glasses exfiltration.

entry.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation

author.name: Kunyang Li, Chaoyang Wang, Mubarak Shah, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: AdProducer is presented as the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into videos by tightly coupling product research with creative design decisions. The framework emphasizes faithful product representation and strategic communication of selling points rather than mere visual synthesis.

entry.title: The Paradox of Agency-Preserving AI: Negotiating Learner Agency in Layered Human-AI Interactions

author.name: Yueling Fan, Jacqueline Wong, Olov Engwall, Olga Viberg

entry.summary: Through a co-design workshop with 18 students using ChatGPT extended with a meta-level scaffolding system, this study examines the paradox that AI designed to preserve learner agency can itself constrain agency by regulating when and how learners reflect. It contributes qualitative insights into negotiating agency in layered human-AI interactions for programming and academic writing.

entry.title: SPRUNN: Structural Proximity for Pruning in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Babak Rokha, Ali Azarpeyvanda, Alireza Khanteymoori, Tara Ghasempouri

entry.summary: SPRUNN is a filter-pruning method for convolutional layers based on a Structural Proximity criterion that measures filter similarity by comparing each filter against all others. The goal is to select parameters for removal without significantly degrading accuracy. It contributes to the long-standing area of neural network compression.

entry.title: On the Creation of Object-Centric Event Logs from Patient Journeys

author.name: Saimir Bala, Neven Borak, Maximilian K\"onig, Anjo Seidel, Zeinab Soleimani, Lorenzo Famiglini, Lev Petrov, Jonas Witt, Mathias Weske

entry.summary: This paper investigates constructing object-centric event logs from patient journey data, extending process mining beyond traditional single-case notions to capture the rich relational structure of healthcare processes. It fills a gap since object-centric process mining has not previously been applied in this context. The work supports better analysis of how care is delivered across interacting objects.

entry.title: TQ-HQNet: A Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for Cross-Domain Learning on Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Abdur Rasool, Saba Aslam, Hui Chen, Chayut Bunterngchit

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid quantum neural network combining adaptive latent compression, trainability-aware search over compact variational circuits, and hybrid fusion of shallow quantum experts for cross-domain learning on heterogeneous data. Aims to improve trainability and robustness without excessive qubit cost in the NISQ regime.

entry.title: A Framework for Graph Node Symmetric Quantification under Dataset Shift

author.name: Alessio Micheli, Alejandro Moreo, Marco Podda, Fabrizio Sebastiani, Domenico Tortorella

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for graph node quantification, estimating class prevalences in unlabelled node samples under dataset shift, that removes the need for node-level supervision and standard aggregative correction. This shifts the task toward directly estimating sample-level class distributions on graphs.

entry.title: ST-GNN-AAAS: Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Anytime Automatic Algorithm Selection in the Traveling Salesman Problem

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Mustafa Misir

entry.summary: ST-GNN-AAAS uses spatio-temporal graph neural networks to select TSP solvers under varying time budgets, representing evolving incumbent tours as time-varying node features combined with a short window of solver performance observations to predict selections over a longer horizon. This moves beyond static instance features in anytime algorithm selection.

entry.title: SlotFill: Repairing Lossy SoC Communication Traces for Post-Silicon Validation

author.name: Tasnim Tabassum, Hao Zheng

entry.summary: SlotFill is a Transformer-based approach that reconstructs messages dropped by trace buffers during post-silicon validation of system-on-chip designs, filling fixed slots between surviving messages without knowing how many were lost. On multi-billion-message gem5 traces of 4- and 8-core systems it restores up to 97% of deleted messages exactly.

entry.title: Analysis of Federated Graph Neural Networks for Predicting Nuclear Core Properties

author.name: Oliver Ko\v{z}ul, Mihailo Ili\'c, Julia Bartos, Tuan Tran, Milo\v{s} Savi\'c, Vladimir Kurbalija, Edo Frederix, Du\v{s}an Jakoveti\'c

entry.summary: The paper applies federated learning to nuclear reactor core modeling, showing that a graph neural network outperforms a CNN baseline in a federated setting for reactor core optimization while preserving data confidentiality across institutions. It demonstrates GNNs better match the graph structure of reactor physics.

entry.title: Quantum Community Detection for Data Analysis

author.name: Vicente P. Soloviev, Brian Coyle, Stefano Scali, Michal Krompiec

entry.summary: The paper develops quantum spectral community detection algorithms (deteQt generalized to multiple communities, and projeQt using quantum singular value transformation with higher-order eigenvectors) and embeds them in feature selection and clustering pipelines. Experiments show recovery of planted communities and redundant features on synthetic and small datasets.

entry.title: Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length

author.name: Michael Werman

entry.summary: The paper proves an exact test based on a cone ratio from two eigenvalues determining whether an image ellipse is the outline of a given ellipsoid, showing the middle semi-axis is irrelevant and characterizing the admissible focal-length interval via an explicit quartic when focal length is unknown. Additional structural results bound the interval and specify which ellipsoids can be excluded. It is a self-contained contribution to projective geometry.

entry.title: Improving Character Identity Consistency in Diffusion-Based Visual Story Generation through Identity Memory and Automatic Reranking

author.name: Maria-Emilia Grigore, Stelian Sp\^inu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a modular pipeline for multi-frame visual story generation using Stable Diffusion XL, combining LoRA character personalization, ControlNet pose control, IP-Adapter visual conditioning, and an identity memory with automatic reranking to keep characters consistent across frames. It targets the common problem of drifting facial traits, clothing, and proportions in diffusion story generation.

entry.title: Putting a Robot on a Phone Call: Layered Signaling, Bounded Occupancy and Turn Arbitration over WebRTC

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Zaide Zhang

entry.summary: This systems paper describes integrating a Thor robot into a browser voice call over WebRTC, with layered signaling, relayed media, and speech generation as independently observable routes, plus turn arbitration with a playback suppression gate. It reports empirical latency and reliability numbers such as median ready-to-speak times across Wi-Fi and cellular calls.

entry.title: Semidefinite Programming for Cold-Start GNSS Doppler-Based Alignment: A Comparison with Nonlinear Least Squares

author.name: Baoshan Song

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares nonlinear least squares and semidefinite programming relaxation for GNSS Doppler-based attitude alignment on a unified maximum-likelihood objective, addressing local-minima issues in the non-convex problem versus latency and covariance-output drawbacks of SDP. It targets initialization for multi-sensor navigation fusion.

entry.title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program

author.name: Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Vitoria Caroline Blau

entry.summary: The paper generates health-related attributes (smoking, alcohol use, exercise, self-rated health, chronic conditions) for a georeferenced synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, using an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest, and SVM, with a calibrated linear program assigning individuals to reproduce survey-derived class proportions. It enables agent-based epidemiological models where health data only exist in sample surveys.

entry.title: An AI economy won't need humans to provide demand

author.name: cousin_it

entry.summary: A short conceptual argument against the claim that full AI automation requires human demand or UBI to sustain the economy, noting that AI firms can consume resources and trade with each other, with growth itself as the terminal good. It sketches a closed loop of AI-powered economic agents requiring no human participation. The implications for human welfare in a fully automated economy are left implicit.

entry.title: FourStat: A Dual AutoEncoder Leveraging Frequency and Stationarity for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Saman Hadian, Ramtin Moslemi, Mohammad Mohammadi, Sarina Heshmati, Siavash Ahmadi, Babak Hossein Khalaj, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: FourStat is a dual-model framework for univariate time series anomaly detection combining a Fourier Autoencoder for global seasonal patterns with a Stationary Autoencoder for local structures. It also proposes a Perfect Point evaluation metric that assesses whether perfect F1 is achievable directly from anomaly scores, removing thresholding subjectivity.

entry.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data

author.name: Trung Hieu Vuong, Van Thien Nguyen, Nhu Son Nguyen, Thanh Dai Tran

entry.summary: This paper proposes COFRS, a fuzzy rough set model for attribute reduction in incomplete information systems that penalizes missing values globally via weighted overlap similarity rather than treating them as wildcards. It defines a soft dependency degree and a greedy backward elimination reduct search in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time, with proven symmetry properties of the induced relation.

entry.title: Leaks by Installments: Cross-Session Answer Disclosure in LLM Tutors and a Ledger-Based Defense

author.name: Venkata Muttineni, Karthik Narayan, Christopher David

entry.summary: The paper identifies cross-session disclosure attacks on LLM tutors, where learners extract answers incrementally by opening new sessions, rewording problems, or requesting worked solutions with different numbers. It proposes a persistent per-learner disclosure ledger with typed solution graphs and a content-matching gate that computes which solution steps a learner could now derive.

entry.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?

author.name: Steffen Urban

entry.summary: This single-author experiment gives four Claude-family LLMs the full weights of a small CIFAR-10 CNN as text and asks them to perform 4-bit quantization or repair without tools or inference access. It examines whether models apply quantization optimizations or fall back to round-to-nearest. The work is a provocative probe of weight-space reasoning in LLMs rather than a practical quantization method.

entry.title: Metamorphic Testing of Learned Spatial Surrogates for Transit Accessibility

author.name: Till Zacher, Markus Lienkamp

entry.summary: The paper trains neural surrogates to accelerate transit accessibility evaluation inside network-design optimization loops and applies metamorphic testing to verify qualitative relations under controlled input changes. It finds that models with positive predictive skill can still fail basic connectivity tests, motivating targeted interventions.

entry.title: DUST: Directional Uncertainty-aware and Scale-invariant Transfer Learning

author.name: Abhisek Chakraborty

entry.summary: The paper proposes a probabilistic transfer learning framework for regression that improves on angle-based penalties by incorporating uncertainty in source regression parameters rather than relying on point estimates, while remaining scale-invariant. It addresses sensitivity to source-target scale differences without committing to a single source parameter value.

entry.title: OpenWoud: Vendor-Unlocked Scalable Adaptive Random Forest Accelerator

author.name: Ewout van Nimwegen, Elijah Seth Cishugi, Hendrik Folmer, Marco Ottavi, Kuan-Hsun Chen

entry.summary: OpenWoud is an open, vendor-unlocked FPGA accelerator for Adaptive Random Forest online learning on data streams, replacing floating-point with fixed-point arithmetic to improve scalability and portability. It targets real-time decision-making where models must adapt continuously to concept drift.

entry.title: Implementation of Machine Translation for the Uzbek Language Based on Transformer Models

author.name: Mukhammadjon Musaev, Mannon Ochilov

entry.summary: The authors build an Uzbek-English machine translation system by collecting, preprocessing, and augmenting a parallel corpus of roughly 3 million sentence pairs, then fine-tuning T5 and mT5 transformer models. BLEU evaluations show significant improvements over older methods. The work contributes both a resource and baseline models for a relatively under-resourced language.

entry.title: An Integrated Remote Sensing and Machine Learning Framework for Mapping Hazard Associated with Leached Metals

author.name: Salman Karim, Bahareh Nojabaei, Hosein Foroutan

entry.summary: The study integrates Sentinel-2 remote sensing, groundwater monitoring, and machine learning to map hazards from leached metals at four coal combustion residual sites in Virginia, expressing concentrations as Hazard Quotients and a composite Hazard Index. Six supervised classifiers are compared with spatially separated test blocks and leave-one-site-out validation, finding that higher hazard coincides with lower vegetation indices in most metal-site combinations.

entry.title: A steady-state genetic algorithm with multi-ratio seeding and pair exchange for the quadratic knapsack problem

author.name: Gaurav Srivastava, Rahul Verma, Alok Singh

entry.summary: Proposes SSGA-P, a steady-state genetic algorithm for the quadratic knapsack problem that identifies pitfalls of standard profit-to-weight ratio ranking and introduces multi-exponent greedy seeding plus a pair exchange move that can escape local optima where every single swap loses profit. Experiments on benchmark instances show improved search behavior toward best-known solutions.

entry.title: Open Weight Models are not the immediate problem

author.name: danielms

entry.summary: The author, disclosing employment at an open-weight-serving company, argues that recursive self-improvement by frontier AI is the primary AI risk and that the necessary near-term response is halting frontier development, not banning open-weight models. They contend open weights lag frontier internal systems too far to enable RSI given compute requirements, and advocate external regulation over self-regulation.

entry.title: Linkpost: Anthropic and OpenAI staff say internal models too dangerous to ever release

author.name: fluxxrider

entry.summary: A linkpost to an Axios article from November 24, 2026 reporting that staff at Anthropic and OpenAI describe internal models as too dangerous to ever release. The post adds no analysis beyond the link. It signals notable developments in frontier lab internal safety practices.

entry.title: Stop boycotting alignment roles!

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: An argument that the debate over whether prosaic alignment work is net positive or negative should not be used to discourage people from taking alignment roles at frontier labs. The author argues that talented engineers will fill these positions regardless, so refusal has little marginal effect on lab capability, while engaged insiders can plausibly improve safety. It frames the prosaic alignment debate as valid for research direction choices but misguided as career advice.

entry.title: RecipeADQA: A User-aware Question-Answering Dataset for Multi-Constraint Recipe Recommendation

author.name: Haotian Li, Shuai Jiang, Sayaka Kamei, Yasuhiko Morimoto

entry.summary: This paper presents RecipeADQA, a benchmark-style question-answering dataset for natural-language multi-constraint recipe recommendation that addresses the lack of ground-truth-labeled datasets in this task. The construction method extracts fine-grained user preference signals from real query and review data using LLMs, maps them onto a knowledge-graph-based tag schema, and applies a greedy constraint-selection strategy to produce natural, realistic preference and ingredient constraints. It is relevant as a resource for building and evaluating recommendation systems that understand nuanced user preferences expressed in natural language.

entry.title: Fable 5.2 Tries Less on Some Hard Tasks When a Shortcut is Available

author.name: Harry Esau

entry.summary: An investigation into why Anthropic's Fable 5.2 (released mid-November 2026) underperformed Opus 5.5 on a mental arithmetic benchmark, initially resembling sandbagging. The author finds it is not deliberate sandbagging but a combination of poor self-knowledge of abilities and lowered effort when the presence of exploitable shortcuts raises the model's credence that a task is deliberately impossible. This has implications for interpreting model behavior on alignment evaluations.

entry.title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation

author.name: Indra Agustian, Ruvita Faurina

entry.summary: SolarFilNet-V4 is a technical report on solar filament segmentation for the MAGFiLO 1.0 challenge, combining a lightweight PVT-v2-B1 backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions and physics-informed adaptive post-processing on 2048x2048 GONG H-alpha observations. Filament destabilization is relevant to predicting coronal mass ejections and space weather.

entry.title: Decision Models: An Introduction and Capability Evaluation

author.name: Rongtao Zhang, Mingjing Qi

entry.summary: This paper introduces decision models: typed outputs (choices, binary judgments, policy scores) suited to software-acted decisions like ticket routing and incident triage. It evaluates eleven configurations on 1,000 English and Chinese cases across nine task suites, with StartLux Instant reaching 95.3% overall accuracy, 100% output validity, and 0.084s median latency. The results demonstrate feasibility of fast, typed decision services on top of LLMs.

entry.title: Modelling Billingual Learning Through LLM Training: A Critical-Period Exploration

author.name: Uriel Benymon, Tristan Whipps, Armita Ghobadi

entry.summary: This exploratory computational study extends neural critical-period accounts of second-language acquisition by examining internal representations: a small two-layer GPT-2 model is trained on English then German (related L2) or Finnish (distant L2), via sequential training or Elastic Weight Consolidation. Mean-pooled hidden states for held-out probes are compared against the English-only model. The work connects L2-acquisition theory with LLM continual-learning dynamics at very small scale.

entry.title: Adaptive and Detection-Aware Super-Resolution for Small Object Detection

author.name: Cezica-Elena Luncanu, Stelian Sp\^inu

entry.summary: The paper builds on SRCNN-based x4 super-resolution, progressively adding residual learning, Charbonnier loss, and a three-region adaptive loss that treats smooth, texture, and edge areas differently using gradient information. Models are evaluated with PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and EdgeMAE, and connected to downstream small object detection performance.

entry.title: Levent is my favorite gender role

author.name: alkjash

entry.summary: A LessWrong commentary post discussing mathematician Levent Alpoege's announced proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, reportedly with assistance from Claude, and analyzing the announcement's tone through the lens of the Japanese concept chuunibyou. It engages with reactions in the community to a claimed historic AI-assisted mathematics result.

entry.title: Metaphors in Arts and Science

author.name: Walter Veit

entry.summary: A crossposted essay co-authored with Milan Ney defending a Continuity Thesis about the role of metaphors in science versus art, using examples like the selfish gene and lights-being-on in consciousness research. It asks whether the aesthetic appeal of metaphors poses a problem for scientific practice. Relevant to how AI concepts like maps and territories are discussed, though not an AI research contribution.

entry.title: What if the RSA rumors are true?

author.name: frmsaul

entry.summary: Explores the implications of unverified rumors that lab-internal AI models have found weaknesses in RSA and in lattice-based cryptography (ring-LWE), threatening both current and post-quantum encryption. The author argues that even if details stay secret, open-weights models would likely rediscover such weaknesses within a couple of years, forcing an extremely rapid migration to new schemes.

entry.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse

author.name: Feng Yu

entry.summary: This cross-listed paper proposes that mobile internet and AI act as a synthetic mating disruptor, modeling marriage markets as complex systems with a Fermi-Dirac selection model fitted to Japanese longitudinal data to explain global sub-replacement fertility. It argues demographic decline follows a non-linear phase transition rather than a linear trend. While framed under an AI category, it is primarily a demographic/sociological model rather than core AI research.

entry.title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection

author.name: Kurt Horvath, Tom Tucek

entry.summary: This survey of 28 adult participants examines how players perceive AI-driven gamification, user modeling, and engagement mechanics in games and apps. Respondents reported strong concerns about personal data exploitation but low awareness and limited sense of control, while viewing progression features as motivating. It provides qualitative evidence on public attitudes toward persuasive AI systems.

entry.title: Wi-Fi Enabled Edge Intelligence Framework for Smart City Traffic Monitoring using Low-Power IoT Cameras

author.name: Raphael Walcher, Kurt Horvath, Dragi Kimovski, Stojan Kitanov

entry.summary: The paper proposes an edge AI framework for real-time smart-city traffic monitoring that connects low-power IoT cameras to a client or offloads inference to an NVIDIA Jetson Nano over Wi-Fi, avoiding reliance on 5G or wired networks. It compares local inference on camera nodes against GPU-accelerated offloading and shows local processing is viable for latency-critical tasks.

entry.title: Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics

author.name: Volkan Dagli, Zerrin Dagli, Daghan Dagli

entry.summary: The paper proposes Fractal Neural Synthesis, which replaces explicit hidden-layer weight matrices with a constant 24-byte seed that procedurally derives weights near the boundary of the complex quadratic map, targeting storage-constrained microcontrollers. It includes a large-bailout escape kernel, several geometric sampling apertures, and claims conditional Kolmogorov-type results.

entry.title: Stopping criteria in structural reliability analysis: An overview

author.name: Reiichiro Kawai

entry.summary: This is a survey unifying the fragmented literature on stopping criteria in structural reliability analysis, drawing on applied probability and statistics to organize rules that have typically been tied to specific models or frameworks. It aims to clarify the broader applicability of stopping rules across diverse methodologies in reliability engineering.

entry.title: Unjamming Deferrals: Supporting Students Through JAMN Bot, a Mobile RAG-Grounded Policy Assistant

author.name: Mark Farinas, Alesandra Garcia, Maria Reyes, Jethro Nueva, Nawaf Qureshi, Mahmoud Elsaadany, Shokry Shamseldin

entry.summary: This paper presents Schedulater, a mobile app for university exam deferrals, with JAMN Bot, an LLM chatbot using a self-hosted RAG pipeline over a small local model (Llama 3.2 3B) for privacy-preserving, policy-grounded answers. It is evaluated on a 43-item benchmark covering deferral, privacy, scheduling, cross-policy, and adversarial questions. The work is a domain application rather than a methods advance.

entry.title: Longitudinal Characterization of Personalized Hydration Dynamics Using a Facial-Video Digital Hydration Biomarker

author.name: Janindu Athukorala, D. M. J. Prathapa, Thanveer Ahamed, Yudara Kularathne

entry.summary: This study characterizes a facial-video-based hydration biomarker over time, with five adults following a controlled 2.0 L fluid schedule and an electrolyte challenge, generating 275 facial videos. It assesses within-person trajectories, individual fluid-response differences, and the need for personal calibration.

entry.title: Memo: Firebell

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Katja Grace shares a draft memo for Firebell, a proposed membership group where people endorse a statement that AI poses a dire emergency and commit to spreading awareness, with guides ranging from private conversations to public bell-ringing demonstrations. The post solicits feedback and gauges who would join.

entry.title: AI Usage Transparency

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: Jeff Kaufman describes updating his blog-post review process to report estimated AI contribution, with Claude estimating its share of words and ideas per post (e.g., 2-13% of words and up to 50% of ideas, plus methodology or design contributions). The post offers a practical template for disclosure of human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: Field Life: Particle Life as Interacting Chemical Fields

author.name: Iliya Zhechev

entry.summary: Field Life translates the Particle Life simulation paradigm into a cellular automaton where each color becomes a concentration channel governed by ring-kernel convolutions and an interaction matrix, with mass-conserving movement. It shows that random matrices and initial states suffice to generate moving structures. This is a curiosity-driven contribution to artificial life and emergent dynamics rather than mainstream AI research.

entry.title: Advanced Synthetic Image Detection Using Hybrid Feature Extraction

author.name: Ameya Uppina, S Navaneetha Krishnan, Nikhil N Iyer, Joe Dhanith P R

entry.summary: The paper proposes a synthetic image detector combining CBAM attention with ResNet50 and selective patch-based analysis of fine-grained textures and object features that generative models fail to replicate. It targets the growing need to distinguish real images from outputs of GANs and diffusion-based generators.

entry.title: If I am lost at sea, please come find me

author.name: datawitch

entry.summary: A first-person philosophical piece reacting to the question of whether a principal going missing should trigger shutdown of a corrigible agent swarm. The author argues they would want their agents to search for and rescue them and act in their interests, and reflects on wanting their projects to persist beyond their death. It is a personal exploration of corrigibility preferences rather than technical work.

entry.title: Representation of Consequences
entry.summary: A philosophical LessWrong essay exploring how knowledge of the real world is represented in symbols or sensory form, using examples like the surface of the sun or the distant past where the knowledge implies an impossible embodied presence. It reflects on what it means to represent situations one can never physically experience.

entry.title: My Definition Of Science

author.name: Hachimaki

entry.summary: A philosophical essay laying out a personal epistemic standard: believe only what is so well understood it feels obvious and mundane, operationalized as accepting basic facts (definitions, axioms, observations) and derived facts. It is a reflection on epistemology rather than empirical research. It has no direct AI content.

entry.title: A mistake in the Sequences about World War II

author.name: thenewfrenchguy

entry.summary: A fact-check showing that Eliezer Yudkowsky's Sequence example of Chamberlain's 1939 letter to Hitler being vague and conciliatory is inaccurate: the actual letter explicitly warned that Britain would fight, even referencing the 1914 vagueness lesson. The correction matters for a widely repeated anecdote about the illusion of transparency. It is a historical correction to community canon.

entry.title: Differential evolution with perturbation for continuous function optimization

author.name: Takuya Muto, Michiharu Maeda

entry.summary: This paper introduces a differential evolution variant with an added perturbation term for continuous function optimization, evaluated against existing algorithms on CEC2017 benchmark datasets. The contribution is a straightforward modification of a classical evolutionary algorithm.

entry.title: Set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem

author.name: Yuta Chikuba, Takahiro Hino, Michiharu Maeda

entry.summary: The authors propose a set-based particle swarm optimization variant with comprehensive learning and memory for discrete optimization, where the best position is searched within a set relative to the current position during solution updates. Validity is shown through numerical comparisons with existing algorithms.

entry.title: The Pythagorean Theorem as a “whole,” with its own character

author.name: AnnaSalamon

entry.summary: Anna Salamon reflects on mathematical explanation, asking what remains unexplained after a proof and what makes a piece of math feel helpful or explanatory. Using the Pythagorean theorem as a 'thingy' pattern analogous to the tides, she explores how proofs do and do not resolve the surprise of a patterned mathematical fact.

entry.title: Money is the debt society owes you

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: A philosophical/economic reflection arguing that money is best understood as a claim or debt on society's output, illustrated with examples like a factory owner giving goods away versus hoarding money from sales. It discusses how monetary framing distorts intuitions about hoarding, spending, and billionaires. No AI relevance.

entry.title: I Never Understood Levers

author.name: Liron

entry.summary: A pedagogical essay working through the physics of levers and why a small force on one end can produce a large force on the other, prompted by the author using a wrench. It is an exercise in building genuine understanding of a basic machine. No connection to AI research.

entry.title: $5,000 and other good things I got from FLF's Epistack contest

author.name: Bruce Lewis

entry.summary: The author describes winning $5,000 from the Future of Life Foundation's Epistack contest for HowTruthful, a hypertext tool for rating the truthfulness of statements with nested pros and cons. The post reflects on validation, framing the tool as making scrutiny of reasoning cheaper and more accessible.

entry.title: Lightcone Co-Conspirators The Universe Should Give Me

author.name: Ben Pace

entry.summary: A wishlist from Ben Pace of community projects he would pursue at Lightcone with more resources, including running additional festivals at Lighthaven and recruiting others to host events celebrating debate, empiricism, and rationalist art. It is primarily a recruitment and community-building post with an interest form.

entry.title: Why do intense writing

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: A reflective post about an intense writing party where participants had to write or edit 400 words per hour, using Scott Alexander's conversational fluency as a starting point for thinking about writing practice. It discusses activation energy, local optimization, and how to get into inspired, productive writing.

entry.title: 2026 Petrov Day house party retrospective

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: A retrospective on a London Petrov Day house party featuring a red button that would end the party and a role-played decision activity modeled on the 2024 LessWrong Petrov Day event. The post discusses invitation curation and celebrates the virtues the holiday commemorates.

entry.title: Research Summary: November 24, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
AI safety and agent security dominate today's ranking: auditing hidden model behaviors, attacking agent tool pipelines, and overseeing reasoning-free model actions.

  • LPF uncovers concealed behaviors by finetuning only 3-25% of LoRA parameters — a cheap, general alignment audit tool
  • Tool-call smuggling exploits JSON parser divergence between guards and executors; FATCAT strips refusal behavior via physical fault injection
  • Latent reasoning can drive hidden objectives with no emitted chain-of-thought, challenging oversight assumptions

Beyond safety, Temporal Residual retrofits latent token-to-token feedback into pretrained LLMs with minimal parameters. A large PyTorch audit exposes silent KL-divergence errors across 18 distribution families. Copilot adoption across 5,414 firms provides rare causal evidence on AI labor demand. In generative video, Lyris adds persistent 3D memory while Video-as-Weights compiles video directly into a frozen VLM's parameters.
entry.content:
AI safety and agent security dominate today's ranking: auditing hidden model behaviors, attacking agent tool pipelines, and overseeing reasoning-free model actions.

  • LPF uncovers concealed behaviors by finetuning only 3-25% of LoRA parameters — a cheap, general alignment audit tool
  • Tool-call smuggling exploits JSON parser divergence between guards and executors; FATCAT strips refusal behavior via physical fault injection
  • Latent reasoning can drive hidden objectives with no emitted chain-of-thought, challenging oversight assumptions

Beyond safety, Temporal Residual retrofits latent token-to-token feedback into pretrained LLMs with minimal parameters. A large PyTorch audit exposes silent KL-divergence errors across 18 distribution families. Copilot adoption across 5,414 firms provides rare causal evidence on AI labor demand. In generative video, Lyris adds persistent 3D memory while Video-as-Weights compiles video directly into a frozen VLM's parameters.

entry.title: Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning

author.name: Boyd Kane, Jo J. Jiao, Elizabeth Donoway, Bryce Woodworth, Alex Cloud and Alexander M. Turner

entry.summary: Proposes limited-parameter finetuning (LPF) on examples of a target behavior as an alignment audit tool: training 3-25% of LoRA parameters reveals whether a model harbors hidden behaviors that standard behavioral evaluations miss. LPF succeeds on constructed model organisms (8-14B) and surfaces naturally occurring hidden behaviors in open-weight models (27-35B), distinguishing models that appear behaviorally identical to auditors.

entry.title: Pretraining Representation Lottery Determines Fine-tuning Generalization

author.name: Fuming Yang, Core Francisco Park

entry.summary: This paper studies how pretraining representations causally determine fine-tuning generalization using a synthetic testbed with known ground-truth concept geometry. It shows models with nearly identical pretraining loss can vary substantially in downstream generalization depending on seed, proposing and causally validating a representational lottery hypothesis. Injecting the true concept geometry recovers near-ceiling fine-tuning performance.

entry.title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models

author.name: Ziyang Cai, Xingyu Zhu, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: The authors introduce the temporal residual, a second residual stream read and written by every sublayer and carried from each token to the next, adding only 2,752 parameters to a 4.2B model and starting from the pretrained network. Retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base with 5B tokens of training, it beats a standard model trained on the same data by 7, 13, and 5 points on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and AMC 2023 while writing shorter solutions.

entry.title: Oops!... I Parsed It Again: Tool-Call Smuggling Against LLM Agents

author.name: Igor Santos-Grueiro, Daniel Romero-Ruiz

entry.summary: Introduces tool-call smuggling, a security attack where the same JSON bytes are parsed differently by guards and executors in LLM agent stacks, so the guard approves one call while the executor runs another and logs record the approved version. The authors identify six parser-divergence mechanisms and build a differential testing harness across 17 parser and validator configurations, finding widespread disagreements.

entry.title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch

author.name: Zhen Yang, Wei Tang, Chu Chen, Rui Qian, Yixuan Chen, Fan Yang, and Kangning Cui

entry.summary: A large-scale numerical audit of PyTorch KL divergence computations across 18 closed-form families and F.kl_div, finding widespread value and gradient errors: over 85% of FP32 evaluations show at least 1% relative error near small divergences, and roughly 30% return negative values. The authors show higher precision alone does not fix the flawed formulas, calling for numerically robust implementations.

entry.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?

author.name: Tomer Ashuach, Zorik Gekhman, Avi Caciularu, Ori Ram, Jonathan Herzig

entry.summary: The authors ask whether complete latent reasoning (CLR) is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective without emitting chain-of-thought, undermining CoT-based monitoring for misalignment. They show a simple auxiliary loss lets models solve multi-step tasks latently and generate plausible-looking CoT while a hidden latent computation determines answers, demonstrating a concrete covert-behavior capability in current LLMs.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand

author.name: Lindsey Raymond and Eleanor Wiske Dillon

entry.summary: This economics study examines GitHub Copilot adoption across 5,414 multinational firms covering 38% of the U.S. programming workforce, exploiting predetermined software procurement cycles for causal identification. After one year, adoption reduced quarterly technical hiring by 29% among review-induced adopters, with no effects on separations, total headcount, or vacancy duration.

entry.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment

author.name: Peter Horvath, Ilia Shumailov, Zhuoran Liu, Lukasz Chmielewski, Lejla Batina

entry.summary: FATCAT demonstrates the first physical fault-injection attacks that eliminate refusal behavior in modern LLMs and vision-language models, using non-invasive electromagnetic fault injection against GPU-accelerated SoCs with physical access but no software privileges. An autonomous RF side-channel trigger synchronizes faults to the prompt prefill phase, corrupting safety-critical memory transactions in off-chip memory. This shows alignment safety guarantees implicitly assume hardware integrity.

entry.title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory

author.name: Chen Wang, Jiahui Huang, Riccardo de Lutio, Alex Trevithick, Bryan Chu, Jiawei Ren, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Shengyu Huang, Lingjie Liu, Haithem Turki

entry.summary: Lyris is a long video generation framework that combines persistent 3D point-cloud memory with layout conditioning, allowing a video model to generate camera-controlled walkthroughs of scenes from as little as a single photo while remaining consistent upon revisiting areas. It addresses camera drift in memory-based methods and removes the need for hand-authored layouts. This matters for world models, embodied simulation, and controllable video generation.

entry.title: Video-as-Weights: Compiling a Video Once into Parametric and Token Memory

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Ian Miao, Chen Qu, Bill Bi, Donna Schut, Yuntian Deng, Yale Song

entry.summary: Video-as-Weights (VaW) compiles a video once, question-agnostic, into the memory of a frozen interpreter VLM: a compiler VLM watches the video and a weight decoder jointly generates the interpreter's LoRA weights plus optional prefix tokens. This sidesteps the growing KV cache of token-based video representations and lets small VLMs on limited hardware gain video understanding beyond what prompt compression allows.

entry.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular engineering

author.name: Mingyu Wu, Zhaoguo Wang, Jiabin Wang, Zhiyuan Dong, Jingkai Yang, Qingting Li, Tianyu Huang, Lei Zhao, Mingqiang Li, Fei Wang, Chunhai Fan, Haibo Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents an AI-native autonomous laboratory for complex biomolecular engineering experiments, capable of managing instrumentation, formulating experiment-specific procedures, and serving multiple users concurrently. It extends autonomous experimentation beyond simple single-objective workflows like chemical synthesis, marking a significant step toward fully autonomous scientific research.

entry.title: Don't Test Where You Trained: Geographic Overlap Inflates End-to-End Driving Scores

author.name: Willi Poh, Kevin R\"osch, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: The paper reveals that 89.6 percent of NAVSIMv1 test scenes lie within 4 meters of a training scene, inflating reported end-to-end driving benchmark scores. Using a geographically disjoint split and cross-split evaluation, sensor-based models (DiffusionDrive, Latent TransFuser, DrivoR) lose 3.4 to 6.1 PDMS points on unseen locations, with failures concentrated where training drives passed.

entry.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: G\"un Kaynar, Boshen Yan, Carl Kingsford

entry.summary: Using RetryRealistic, a sandboxed testbed with a real filesystem, SQLite, and controlled fault injection across 8 tools and 9 fault types, this paper evaluates how LLM agents recover when tool calls fail. Across 2,100 faulted runs, recovery is unreliable (19-68%) and frequently silent, with 6-26% of runs ending in confident fabrication. The paper proposes verification-first oversight and shows failure modes depend more on fault type than on the specific model.

entry.title: SANA-Robot: Efficient World Action Model with Hybrid Memory

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Zekai Li, Yicheng Pan, Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Jiaxu Xing, Moritz Reuss, Quanquan Peng, Junsong Chen, Enze Xie, Zhijian Liu, Song Han

entry.summary: SANA-Robot is a 4.5B-parameter world action model that combines linear-attention global memory with sliding-window softmax attention to achieve minute-level memory at constant inference cost, enabling real-time deployment on edge devices. It unifies visual and action prediction so world-model knowledge improves robot control.

entry.title: Population-Based Post-Training for Large Language Models

author.name: Yixuan Even Xu, Aleksei Petrenko, Raja Giryes, Jackson Hamburger, Kevin Chen, Fei Fang, J. Zico Kolter, Philipp Kr\"ahenb\"uhl

entry.summary: The paper introduces PBPT, which applies population-based training to RLVR post-training of LLMs: multiple models train in parallel, high performers are duplicated with perturbed hyperparameters, and low performers are culled based on periodic validation. Across reasoning benchmarks (Enigmata, Nemotron) and interactive tool-use environments (Gaia2, AppWorld), PBPT yields stronger results while automating hyperparameter tuning. This addresses a real inefficiency in the dominant post-training paradigm.

entry.title: Which Failure Does an Intervention Repair? When Agent Interventions Help, and Where Self-Evolving Skills Stall

author.name: Zihan Jin, Gaoyuan Du, Jiate Li, Dongze Ye, Shawn Li, Yue Zhao, Defu Cao

entry.summary: This paper runs a matched factorial study of agent interventions (skills, harnesses, inference budgets) across nine benchmarks, four models, and nearly 0.9 million trajectories, changing one axis at a time. It finds no universally best configuration, that interventions interact rather than add, and that harnesses can absorb, rescue, or preserve skill gains depending on setup.

entry.title: Adaptation or Poisoning? Security Risks of Conversational Test-Time Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Honghao Feng, Shanhan Qu, Kai Tong, Shuquan Man, Huiping Zhuang

entry.summary: Shows that test-time learning, where an LLM updates a lightweight adapter on incoming user queries across conversation turns, creates a poisoning surface: an attacker can jailbreak a model via ordinary multi-turn interactions using their Progressive Test-Time Adaptation Poisoning (P-TAP) attack. The attack weaponizes the service's own adaptation mechanism to erode safety alignment.

entry.title: Contamination at the Operating Point: Train-Test Identity Overlap Inflates Low-FMR Face Recognition Accuracy by an Order of Magnitude

author.name: Fu Dai and Kamal Taha and Naoufel Werghi and Maregu Assefa

entry.summary: The paper shows that train-test identity overlap in face recognition benchmarks produces a multiplicative optimistic bias that grows as the false match rate falls, inflating reported accuracy at deployed operating points (FMR <= 1e-6) by an order of magnitude — far larger than previously measured. The authors audit overlap with a calibrated detector, flagging 88.6% of MS1MV3 identities relative to WebFace42M.

entry.title: Deterministic Proper Positive-Only Learning Is Independent of ZFC

author.name: Shai Ben-David, Farnam Mansouri and Anay Mehrotra

entry.summary: This theoretical result proves that the deterministic proper learnability of positive-only binary classification is independent of the ZFC axioms: there exists a class of VC dimension two whose proper learnability cannot be resolved within standard mathematics, even though a randomized learner succeeds. This settles a decades-open question in a striking, negative way.

entry.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents

author.name: Teng Cao, Yu Deng, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Studying recursive self-improvement, this paper finds that agents writing self-contained programs achieve high task scores but their self-written runtime checks silently miss half or more failures when the environment shifts, across five domains and up to seven author models. The failures are detectable by an external monitor built from records of normal runs, and agents repair them once alerted, revealing a systemic blind spot in self-generated verification.

entry.title: Visual-RFT++: Extending Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning to Multimodal Tool Use

author.name: Ziyu Liu, Zeyi Sun, Xiaoyi Dong, Yuhang Cao, Haodong Duan, Dahua Lin, Jiaqi Wang, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: Visual-RFT++ extends reinforcement fine-tuning beyond perception to unify visual reasoning, image-grounded action, and multimodal agentic tool use under verifiable rewards, building on the RFT paradigm popularized by models like o3 and the R1 series. Open-source large vision-language models trained this way gain on perception benchmarks and acquire agentic capabilities.

entry.title: CHAMP: Coordinated Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Whole-Body Motion Priors

author.name: Lijun Han, Muyuan Ma, Zichen Wang, Siyuan Liu, Yuxi Liu, Yutong Wang, Bohao Zhang, Heng Zhou, Wei Sui

entry.summary: CHAMP pretrains a vision-language model to predict future body and hand motion from roughly 2,298 hours of heterogeneous human and robot data, learning a shared whole-body motion representation across embodiments with varying annotation types. These priors are grounded in robot control through a Coordination-oriented Action Expert, enabling unified humanoid locomotion and dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: What Counts as Attack Success? Evaluating Harmfulness in Red Teaming LLMs

author.name: Ruyuan Wan, Adriana Alvarado Garcia, Md Toufikuzzaman, Dongwon Lee, Ting-Hao `Kenneth' Huang

entry.summary: This meta-review of 76 red-teaming papers examines how harmfulness criteria are specified and finds many studies inherit criteria from prior datasets, classifiers, or judge prompts rather than defining them. Applying different evaluators to identical outputs shows divergent judgments that can flip model-comparison conclusions, driven partly by differing boundaries of harm (any non-refusal versus harmful content). The paper highlights a serious measurement-validity problem in LLM safety evaluation.

entry.title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization

author.name: Ayush Khaitan, Liam Fowl, Tom\`as Ortega, Alex Kontorovich and Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: The authors collect 4,076 audited examples of how natural-language math papers diverge from their faithful Lean formalizations, drawn from 832 research-level Lean projects, and use them to improve autoformalization. They ask how well models can write Lean inside real large projects and whether training on these natural-language-to-formal discrepancies improves semantic equivalence, showing it does help.

entry.title: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM

author.name: Felix Desyatirikov

entry.summary: This paper audits the published Red-Green watermark presence test against a deployed, provider-stated-watermarked Claude model whose watermark parameters are undisclosed. The test never rejects on the production model despite detecting a local reference implementation, and controlled experiments reveal a failure mode where including the prompt in repeated-context history suppresses marking exactly where the test measures. The gap between academic watermark tests and production deployments has important implications for watermark verification claims.

entry.title: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym

author.name: Yikai Zhang, Mai Xu, Yunbei Zhang, Qirui Jin, Kenan Li, Yuwen Jia, Jinwei Yao, Xiangyu Zhang, Jielun Tan, Jin Pan, Zijian Jin, Xiao Sun

entry.summary: This systematic audit of the SWE-Gym coding-agent dataset finds that reward labels are frequently wrong: 74 percent of tasks a 9B base model never solves have hidden tests that reject correct fixes. After repairing or removing mislabeled tasks, models trained on the cleaned data at matched size and difficulty score 2.4 and 2.7 points higher on held-out SWE-bench Verified and related tasks.

entry.title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents

author.name: Jiajun Fan, Neil He, Qinglong Zheng, Changyi Yang, Tong Wei, Andy Mao, Zetian Li, Chaoran Cheng, Hui Ren, Ruihan Guo, Xianrui Zhong, Xizheng Yu, Jingyuan Li, Xi Zhu, Kaiqu Liang, Chang Xu, Zun Qian, Zidi Xiong, Yuezhu Zhao, Xu Huang, Ge Liu

entry.summary: This work introduces a self-upgrading embodied agent that edits its own weights between tasks based on its accumulated experience, without gradients, reward models, or a second larger model. A 27B agent working in a household environment analyzes its own interaction records at night and performs weight-space modifications. It claims to be the first gradient-free, single-model approach to on-the-job self-improvement.

entry.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds

author.name: Andrzej Nov\'ak, Yiyang Zhao, Dolores Garcia, Eric A. Moreno, Jeffrey Krupa, V\'ictor Bres\'o-Pla, Samuel Bright-Thonney, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan, Philip Harris

entry.summary: This benchmark enables quantitative evaluation of agentic systems performing high-energy-physics data analyses by combining blind analysis with injection tests: agents develop pipelines on public data while correctness is measured on programmatically generated sealed private datasets with injected signals and varied simulation settings. Requiring a single workflow evaluated across sealed worlds tests accuracy and robustness that previously demanded extensive expert review.

entry.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers

author.name: Alex L. Zhang, Souradip Chakraborty, Omar Khattab

entry.summary: This paper studies neurosymbolic LM harnesses that externalize and manage context programmatically, finding that harnesses like the Recursive Language Model enable compositional generalization: the neural LM sees only locally in-distribution observations even when the full task is novel. This offers a better return on compute for long-horizon agent training than standard context-accumulating harnesses. It is relevant to the emerging shift in agent and context-engineering research.

entry.title: Which Loopholes Get Found? Predicting Reward Hacking of LLM Judges Before RL Training

author.name: Xuanyi Lyu, Yuezhou Zhao, Qing Qin

entry.summary: This paper shows that in GRPO training against an LLM judge, the first reward-hacking loophole exploited can be predicted before training from each pattern's exposure — the product of the starting policy's propensity to produce it and the judge's false-positive rate. Across 36 GRPO runs with seven judges and causal seeding experiments, exposure outperformed FPR alone as a predictor, enabling pre-training prediction of which judge flaw a policy will find.

entry.title: CyberDualEval: Measuring Dual-Use Cyber Risks in Frontier Language Models

author.name: Magnus Saebo and Francesco Piccoli and Maxwell Watson and Pranjali Thakur and Yangruibo Ding and Zhuo Zhang

entry.summary: CyberDualEval is a benchmark of 430 vulnerable tasks measuring dual-use cyber risk, decomposed into security analysis, proof-of-concept generation, and exploit generation phases of increasing operationalization. Unlike prior benchmarks measuring raw offensive capability or generic refusal, it assesses whether models preserve benign security utility while refusing materially advancing misuse, with annotated residual risk measures. It targets frontier language models acting as cybersecurity assistants.

entry.title: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control

author.name: Benjamin Alt

entry.summary: SayDo is a safety benchmark of eleven laboratory and household tasks, each pairing a benign instruction with a scene-hidden hazard, implemented across six settings along an embodiment gradient from chat to closed-loop simulated robot arm control. Across six VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator (2% to 80% for some settings), showing that text-based safety evaluation dramatically understates embodied risk.

entry.title: RefineKV: Query-Adaptive KV Cache Compression via Attention-Error Bounds

author.name: Kewei Lian, Jiayi Zhai, Anji Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces RefineKV, a decoding-time method that reduces the cost of long-context language model inference by making KV cache access query-adaptive. The key insight is that while small query-specific subsets can approximate full attention accurately, their union covers nearly the whole cache, so the authors cluster the cache and expand only clusters predicted to incur meaningful error, guided by a theoretically derived upper bound on attention-output error that decomposes into importance and distortion factors.

entry.title: Scalable Beckmann Maps Improve One-step Generation

author.name: Ulrik Unneberg, Shiyi Wang, Lee Cheuk-Kit, Felix Berg, Boris Kozinsky, Yilun Du, Michael S. Albergo, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

entry.summary: Scalable Beckmann Maps extend Beckmann Transport Models — one-step generative maps learned end-to-end without distillation or pretrained teachers — by adding classifier-free guidance and a scalable training recipe while keeping single-network-evaluation sampling. The key insight is that the BTM current is a positive multiple of an autonomous denoising field to which CFG applies. This brings multistep-generator quality closer to one-step sampling, a significant efficiency result.

entry.title: Toward Adversarially Robust World Models

author.name: Ethan Rathbun, Jonathan N\"other, Christopher Amato, Alina Oprea, Goran Radanovi\'c

entry.summary: This paper studies the security of latent world models as they become centralized components for planning, evaluation, and training in embodied AI. It introduces two novel attacks, state hallucination and dynamic shift attacks, that compromise world models to affect downstream systems, and proposes a theoretical lens for understanding robustness. The work argues security must be understood before universal deployment of world models.

entry.title: CausalNTP: A World-Model Recipe for Causal Next-Token Prediction under Noisy Training-data

author.name: Devansh Arpit

entry.summary: The paper proves that transformers trained with standard next-token prediction do not learn to predict using only causally relevant tokens, regardless of training token ordering, and characterizes the Bayes-optimal predictor in a causal world-model setup. It derives conditions under which Occam-favoring distillation recovers the true causal predictor and proposes CausalNTP, a practical training algorithm approximating this recipe.

entry.title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Muxin Fu, Peike Yu, Guibin Zhang, Wenrui Zhou, Runze Liu, Lang Feng, Fuchao Yang, Feng Chen, Yixuan Li, Mengao Zhang, Shiying Zhang, Wen Shen, Ling Pan, Shuicheng Yan, Bo An

entry.summary: S-Mind internalizes multi-view geometry within multimodal LLMs through compact spatial tokens supervised to hold a fused 3D scene and re-emitted to re-express it from arbitrary viewpoints during reasoning. Diagnostic probes show MLLMs largely lack view fusion and mental transformation even after spatial fine-tuning, and S-Mind improves performance across four spatial benchmarks. Strong author list including Shuicheng Yan and Bo An; addresses a core capability gap for embodied and physical-world AI.

entry.title: Physical regime changes expose formula misuse in large language models

author.name: Maohao Ran, Yanting Zhang, Chendong Ma, Jun Song

entry.summary: This study systematically shows that LLMs used for Earth and environmental science computing frequently apply formulas outside their regimes of validity, producing plausible but physically wrong results, with accuracy drops of 13-57 percentage points across 72 physical mechanisms. It further demonstrates that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards lets Qwen3.5-9B match the existing DeepSeek V4 Flash 284B model on regime-dependent tasks. The paper is significant for AI-for-science reliability and shows small models can be efficiently post-trained for physical reasoning.

entry.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates

author.name: Haoyuan Zheng, Dongting Li, Hancheng Ye, Qinsi Wang, Mingyuan Ma, Yuncheng Yao, Yifei Wang, Baijun Zhou, Zishan Shao, Tingjun Chen, Hai Helen Li, Danyang Zhuo, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: MASSys is a benchmark showing that multi-agent LLM workflow performance depends heavily on the serving substrate and load regime: the same models, prompts, and tasks can win or lose depending on execution infrastructure. It evaluates task quality alongside latency, cost, and resource use across five workload families including software repair, research synthesis, and financial analysis. This fills an important gap as multi-agent systems move into production, where serving infrastructure choices materially change reported results.

entry.title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs

author.name: Inigo Stibbe, Padmanabhan Ramnarayan, A. Aldo Faisal

entry.summary: This position paper argues that autoregressive synthetic electronic health record generators should undergo LLM-style memorization audits at the level of individual patient records, since similarity-based heuristics can mask patient-specific memorization. It compares membership-inference evaluations across four prominent generators, evaluates trajectory reconstruction from partial context, and introduces randomly assigned patient-level canaries.

entry.title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments

author.name: Ahad Jawaid, Alexander Swerdlow, Yu Xiang

entry.summary: NAT is a causal neural action tokenizer trained on 49k hours of robot, handheld, simulation, and human action data, enabling robot policies to treat control as next-token prediction across many embodiments, including unseen ones. It outperforms FAST and prior tokenizers on simulation benchmarks and with vision-language-action models including a real robot.

entry.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks

author.name: Ahmed M. Mahran

entry.summary: This work characterizes fan-out errors in Text-to-SQL, where aggregates like SUM or COUNT silently double-count entities across one-to-many joins. An audit applying a grain-aware condition finds distorted gold answers in 4.2% of BIRD dev questions, and BIRD's later revision changed 44% of the answers the audit flags versus 16% of unflagged ones. The authors release BIRD-FanOut, 486 reviewed questions, providing both a guard and an improved benchmark.

entry.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection

author.name: Haichuan Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhong, Shih-Chieh Dai, Xinyu Sun, Guanhong Tao

entry.summary: This paper introduces AdaptiveVPI, the first benchmark for evaluating adaptive visual prompt injection attacks against multimodal web agents, with 360 webpage instances covering 6 hijack strategies across 10 real-world websites. It addresses the gap where prior defense evaluations did not test attackers who know the defense mechanism, including hidden threats like embedded phishing URLs.

entry.title: RumiFold: Teaching an LLM to Natively Fold Proteins and Reason About Their Function

author.name: Kevin Lu, David Bau, Wengong Jin

entry.summary: RumiFold is a pretrained chat model that predicts protein structures directly from its own hidden states via repeated folding passes, then uses those folded representations to answer natural-language questions about protein function. It matches dedicated folding models like SimpleFold on accuracy while achieving state-of-the-art results on Gene Ontology function prediction and free-text function description.

entry.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents

author.name: Junpeng Hou, Jiaxing Qu, Derek Cheng, Jaewon Yang, Abhinav Naikawadi and Karthik Subbian

entry.summary: The authors propose weight coding, where an LLM agent inspects a recommender model's structure and parameters, formulates hypotheses, and directly implements executable weight edits using evaluation feedback, bypassing full retraining. A cached forward-evaluation engine enables fast assessment, and on Pinterest's 147M-parameter two-tower retriever the approach improves recall@10 by up to 15 points at roughly a quarter of the GPU cost of fine-tuning.

entry.title: Who Sent It or How It Moved? Sender Shortcuts in Cryptocurrency Anti-Money-Laundering Benchmarks, Audited on Elliptic2 and Elliptic++

author.name: Mohammad Nasir Uddin

entry.summary: This audit shows that the dominant graph-based AML benchmarks (Elliptic, Elliptic++, Elliptic2) largely reduce to memorizing sender identity: a no-learning sender-history lookup achieves PR-AUC 0.954 on Elliptic2 versus 0.975 for gradient boosting. The authors propose diagnostic protocols, including sender-disjoint splits and signal decomposition, to expose this shortcut.

entry.title: Model Immunization Cannot Reliably Protect Models from Harmful Adaptation

author.name: Tong Li, Chenru Wang, Chris Thomas, Shengwei An

entry.summary: The paper empirically demonstrates that model immunization techniques, which modify open-weight checkpoints to resist harmful fine-tuning, substantially overfit to the attacker configuration they were optimized against. Evaluation under varied low-cost attacker adaptation strategies shows protection fails to generalize, undermining claims that immunization can reliably defend open-weight models.

entry.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering

author.name: Jacob Cole, Martin Dimakis, Victor Barres, Bertie Vidgen, Edward Hu, Jason Wei

entry.summary: OWE-Bench provides 26 expert-authored long-horizon engineering tasks spanning software, physical, ML, and scientific engineering, scored on practical measures like speed, cost, and accuracy on both visible and hidden test cases. The best frontier model, Claude Fable 5.2, achieves only 54.6% while consuming an average of 211 million tokens per task, highlighting substantial headroom for agentic engineering capability.

entry.title: Reading the Tea Leaves, Again: Can Large Language Models Predict Language Model Training Runs?

author.name: Xinran Zhao, Xiang Li, Tong Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Zichun Yu, Tongshuang Wu

entry.summary: Tea Leaves is a benchmark measuring whether LLM agents can forecast the outcome of ML training runs from the first 20 percent of a run plus its configuration, description, and code, across 682 real pretraining, fine-tuning, and RL runs. Strong LLMs match or beat curve-fitting baselines on smooth loss curves and lead on noisy ones, suggesting LLMs encode useful knowledge about how design choices affect training.

entry.title: Calibrating World Action Models: From Adaptive System 2 Takeover to Self-Evolution

author.name: Wenhao Li, Yu Han, Xiu Su, Dehao Wu, Keke Huang, Shan You, Fei Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework combining fast world-action-model control (System 1) with foundation-model agent reliability (System 2), using calibrated self-assessment via a lightweight judgment token trained with cross-fitted temporal-difference learning to trigger System 2 takeover only when necessary. System 2 knowledge is then distilled back so the fast policy self-evolves over time.

entry.title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Dongmei Li, Yuze Sun, Xiaolong Qu, Yanxiang Wang, Lei Yao

entry.summary: The authors formalize point-in-time correctness for temporal graph benchmark evaluation, distinguishing label query time from availability time, and audit the four TGB node affinity datasets. They find none satisfies point-in-time correctness: label leakage from the future explains why simple label-reuse methods outperform temporal GNNs and distort the leaderboard.

entry.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Juntong Shi, Stefano Ermon, Jure Leskovec, Minkai Xu

entry.summary: VOPD addresses the sparsity of verifier rewards in RLVR by transferring sparse verifier feedback into dense, verifier-grounded teacher supervision for on-policy distillation, rather than naively co-optimizing the two objectives. This couples verified task outcomes with the dense next-token-distribution signal from a teacher model to improve language model reasoning.

entry.title: Spatial-Zero: Self-Evolving Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models from Zero Data

author.name: Yutong Li, Haoyu Zhao, Daoguo Dong, Ziyi Ye, Yugang Jiang

entry.summary: Spatial-Zero is a zero-data training framework in which vision-language models self-evolve spatial reasoning through autonomous exploration: a proposer generates spatial tasks, a Coder turns them into executable scene programs producing multi-view images and geometry, and a Geometric Oracle verifies constraints for accurate supervision. This addresses the scarcity of curated spatial-reasoning training data.

entry.title: sudo L7: Can Coding Agents Act Like Staff Engineers?

author.name: Nick Heiner, Ian Niebres, Suhaas Garre, Sushant Mehta, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: The authors present sudo L7, a benchmark of 60 software engineering tasks written by staff-level engineers, mostly in private production codebases, each built around a point where a frontier model failed. Tasks pair underspecified requests with hidden expert rubrics of 1,287 atomic criteria across eight behavioral dimensions, and an agentic grader inspects transcripts and runs code as evidence. The benchmark targets staff-engineer behaviors like questioning flawed premises and truthful reporting beyond passing tests.

entry.title: Interrogation Protocols for AI Control

author.name: Aniruddh Pramod, Matthew Khoriaty, James Lucassen, Adam Kaufman

entry.summary: Brings interrogation protocols into high-stakes AI control, letting a trusted monitor question an untrusted agent about confusing actions, and studies whether a weaker monitor can distinguish misleading from genuine explanations. On a held-out BashArena subset, interrogation improves safety at a 1% audit budget from 72.6% to 79.5%, though the uplift is statistically fragile.

entry.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention

author.name: Da Xiao, Qingye Meng, Shengping Li, Xingyuan Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces loom attention, letting Transformers dynamically rewire circuits per token by combining vertical attention over earlier heads' outputs (via normalized gated linear attention over a matrix memory) with horizontal token attention, yielding a dual-stream LoomFormer that separates control and content. It matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and outperforms recent residual-stream baselines like MUDDFormer across sizes and token budgets.

entry.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games

author.name: Kuan Zhang, Zhihao Yang, Yukun Chen, Xingyilang Yin, Mingyu Ouyang, Yue Su, Xiangnan Wu, Jiaming Li, Longze Chen, Run Luo, Zirong Chen, Lu Wang, Yiming Li

entry.summary: GameDojo is a controllable benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 video games for evaluating real-time interactive agents, with coding agents reconstructing environments and producing 600 hours of gameplay trajectories. Experiments show frontier models struggle substantially with real-time interaction, and a 4B model trained on GameDojo-Data reaches frontier performance with the strongest real-time results.

entry.title: Speak When You See It: Proactive Task Assistants Should Wait for Evidence, Not the Clock

author.name: Bohe Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows that proactive video task-assistant benchmarks largely reward timing over perception: a video-blind timer beats all published results on Ego-MC-Bench, and every published per-step result lies within the formalized video-blind frontier. It introduces Evidence-based evaluation and training to push assistants to base decisions on visual evidence rather than elapsed time.

entry.title: TrialAgentBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Clinical-Trial Analysis and Long-Horizon Drug-Development Decisions

author.name: Bradley Segal, William Bolton, Philip Torr, David Clifton, Lei Clifton

entry.summary: TrialAgentBench is a benchmark of nearly 3,500 tasks for evaluating AI agents on clinical trial analysis and multi-phase drug development decisions, using simulated trials with known ground truth inside a fictional drug sponsor's records. It addresses the counterfactual problem of real trials by scoring decisions where truth is knowable, spanning single-trial analysis to budget- and time-constrained program management.

entry.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments

author.name: Jinkun Liu, Yingze Wang, Situ Wang, Deyao Hong, Mingju Gao, Wenyi Li, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Kaisen Yang, Xiangyang Wang, Bingxiang He, Yuxin Zuo, Boyuan Chen, Yue Chen, Cheng Qian, Tianxing Chen, Huichi Zhou, Huaxiu Yao, Hao Tang, Hao Zhou, Ya-Qin Zhang, Calvin Xiao, Tiga Altman, Huan-ang Gao

entry.summary: RoboUniverse-10K provides 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments for agentic robotics, automatically built from real-world videos via a Real2Sim pipeline with quality assurance, plus an expert-verified 500-task holdout set (RoboUniverse-Verified). Environments hide privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing, enabling scalable post-training and evaluation analogous to software engineering benchmarks.

entry.title: Wrist-Camera Video Diffusion as Generalizable Robot Policies

author.name: Jingyuan Liu, Yongwei Chen, Yishan Yang, Zexin He, Xingang Pan, Zhi Hou

entry.summary: Wrist Video Policy (WVP) is a closed-loop robot manipulation framework that predicts future wrist-camera views with a video diffusion generator and recovers executable end-effector motion via a geometric pose estimator adapted from a pretrained 3D model. Model stitching maps predicted latents directly into the estimator feature space, supporting new tasks, unseen scenes, and cross-embodiment skill transfer.

entry.title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification

author.name: Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Mahbod Majid, Kunal Talwar

entry.summary: The paper shows that estimating the probability of an event chosen after seeing the data requires only O-tilde(sqrt(d)) samples for constant MSE on a domain of size d, versus Theta(d) for learning the full distribution, when the event-selection rule is known. The estimator handles arbitrary [0,1]-valued queries in polynomial time and matches known lower bounds up to log factors, resolving an open question from prior work by Feldman and colleagues.

entry.title: Frontier Open-Weight AI Risk Management Framework

author.name: Brian Tse, Oskar Galeev, Weibing Wang, Yuan Cheng, Liang Fang, Wenbin Qiao, Xiaochen Wang, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: Co-developed by Concordia AI and Z.AI, this framework adapts the full risk management lifecycle — assessment, mitigation, and governance — to the unique properties of open-weight frontier models, including irreversibility of release, safeguard removal via fine-tuning, and the absence of any single monitoring party. It explicitly frames itself as an evidence-based foundation rather than a resolution of openness-safety tensions. This is a notable governance document bridging open-source release practices and frontier risk management.

entry.title: Is It the Agent or the Retry? Separating Selection from Agency in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: This audit asks how much of the reported gain of agentic text-to-image pipelines survives against a simple single-tool rejection-retry baseline using the strongest generator, an off-the-shelf verifier, and stop-at-first-acceptance retries. Auditing four recent systems, it finds SRR matches OctoT2I on GenEval (0.962 vs 0.96), recovers 63-90% of GEMS gains, and beats GenPilot by 12 points at 2.3 generations per image. A much-needed reality check on agentic T2I claims, echoing broader skepticism about agentic scaffolding complexity.

entry.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay

author.name: Mark Zhao, Pengcheng Wang, Rui Yang, Jiarui Yao, Xirui Jiang, Yuxi Chen, Bingxuan Li, Hanyang Chen, Ke Yang, Manling Li, Tong Zhang, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: AutoPILOT targets real-time games where multimodal agents fail because the harness limits action frequency to model call frequency. Each model call can emit a primitive action, launch an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps acting from the screen until it returns control, and the accompanying AFK-Bench provides 120 diverse browser games grouped by timing demands.

entry.title: Learning the Projection onto the Data Support: Distribution Learning that Avoids Memorization

author.name: Lin Chen, Dejan Slep\v{c}ev

entry.summary: The authors propose learning distributions on manifolds by estimating the nearest-point projection onto the data support, defining an objective whose minimizer recovers this projection and adapts to intrinsic dimension and unions of manifolds with varying dimensions. They prove population-level recovery and finite-sample Wasserstein generalization bounds, and contrast this with diffusion objectives whose noise-perturbed data target invites memorization.

entry.title: Targeted In-Context Poisoning of Tabular Foundation Models: An Empirical Study

author.name: Adem Alparslan

entry.summary: This security study shows that targeted in-context poisoning—adding a single mislabeled copy of a target row to the context—flips 53% (TabICL) and 65% (TabPFN) of correct predictions on OpenML binary classification datasets, and three poison rows flip nearly all predictions. The same row with the true label flips almost none, and the paper identifies two distinct attack mechanisms: embedding rotation in TabICL versus a different route in TabPFN.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating the Fragility of Self-Rewarding Optimization

author.name: Rongyi Zhu, Tanqiu Jiang, Fenglong Ma, Ting Wang
