entry.summary: Shows that self-rewarding optimization of language models is fundamentally fragile: benign-looking prompt perturbations can corrupt self-generated preference signals and trigger iterative collapse, demonstrated via Re-Ranking and Preamble attacks. Introduces self-reward fidelity (SRF), a metric quantifying on-policy agreement between self-rewards and oracle quality, and proposes mitigations.

entry.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound

author.name: Asha Barua, Sajad Khodadadian

entry.summary: Establishes last-iterate guarantees for sample-based natural policy gradient algorithms in tabular finite-horizon MDPs, achieving sample complexity of order SAH^4/eps^2 with a matching information-theoretic lower bound. The algorithms use backward sweeps and do not estimate transition probabilities, answering whether direct policy optimization can attain the fundamental statistical limit for RL. This resolves a core theoretical question about NPG's sample efficiency.

entry.title: When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?

author.name: Fabio Valerio Massoli, Arnau Padr\'es Masdemont, Jordi Ros Giralt, Arash Behboodi

entry.summary: The authors study when stored facts become readable during inference in looped transformers, using synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning with depth-resolved measurements of readable information in bits. They find single-hop facts become readable progressively with heavier memorization loads delaying retrieval, that looped models expose facts earlier than untied equal-depth baselines, and that supervision timing shapes this dynamics.

entry.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Jiaqi Su, Jie-Jing Shao, Yichen Liu, Long-Kai Huang, Haiyan Yin

entry.summary: NightWatch is a plug-and-play framework that gives computer-use agents continuous, temporally grounded perception of dynamically changing screens, pairing a VLM agent with a lightweight 0.8B watcher model. It targets the perception-action gap where snapshot-based observation becomes stale before an action executes, without modifying the agent model or prompt.

entry.title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion

author.name: Hao-Yu Hsu, Shenlong Wang, Alexander G. Schwing

entry.summary: The paper asks whether the decoder in latent generative models can be merged into the same backbone as the encoder and generator, producing UNIFIED: one diffusion transformer that encodes, generates, and decodes, trained from scratch in a single stage with reconstruction and flow objectives. The key is casting all three modes as position-aligned sequence maps distinguished only by a mode token and timestep. This simplifies the standard three-network latent diffusion architecture.

entry.title: Compared to What? Calibrating Machine-Unlearning Diagnostics with Present, Absent and Suppressed Anchors

author.name: Arsalan Kaleem

entry.summary: This paper builds controlled anchor cases (present, absent, and by-construction suppressed facts) to validate internal unlearning diagnostics like linear probes, logit lens, and relearning speed against a known ground truth on GPT-2 Small and Qwen3-0.6B-Base. It scores each diagnostic per entity with AUROC against an oracle to distinguish genuine removal from mere suppression.

entry.title: Reward Tilting via Semantic Noising

author.name: Rafa{\l} Karczewski, Peter Blohm, Markus Heinonen, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: The paper proposes semantic noising, which conditions a generative model on a noisy semantic representation so that posteriors correspond to exponential tilts by linear-quadratic rewards, letting a single trained model support rewards and strengths chosen after training. It demonstrates the approach on autoregressive molecular generation and diffusion-based semantic denoisers. This offers an elegant alternative to per-reward fine-tuning or expensive sampling-time search.

entry.title: More Than Picturing the Future: Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning for Generalizable Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xin Zhang, Yushuo Hou, Anqi Zhao, Moyun Liu, Xingwei Zhao, Bo Tao, Jiawei Du, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: The paper argues that latent reasoning in VLA models should encode how a scene evolves toward the goal rather than what an isolated future frame looks like, showing that frame-aligned visual latents bind policies to training-scene appearance. It proposes Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning, redirecting latents from appearance to motion dynamics, improving generalization when scenes change. This is a conceptually sharp critique and fix for an increasingly popular VLA paradigm.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Editing: LLMs Program Their Own Weight Edits for Self-Improvement

author.name: Linghua Zhang, Yunhe Li

entry.summary: Introduces SELFWRITE, where an LLM studies its own reasoning, inspects its own weights and activations in a persistent Python session, and writes a program constructing low-rank weight edits from white-box primitives, with gradient descent replaced by model-authored updates. Candidates are graded against a hidden gate set relative to the current model, iterating across generations toward recursive self-improvement. This is an unusual, safety-relevant direction in which the model, not a training procedure, writes its own weight changes.

entry.title: Detecting Is Not Choosing: What a World Model Needs to Keep a VLA Policy Safe

author.name: Thanish Bolla

entry.summary: Analyzes lookahead safety filters for vision-language-action policies, showing that using an exact simulator as a world model raises safety rates by 11.5 to 25.7 points on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus for several policies including pi0.5. Critically, learned critics that detect dangerous states well (AUROC up to 0.864) fail at ranking candidate action chunks within a decision (AUROC near 0.55), a distinction the authors call detecting versus choosing.

entry.title: Dimension Is Free, Horizon Is Not: When Evolution Strategies Rival Policy Gradients for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Qiyao Liang, Kajetan Schweighofer, Xin Qiu, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: The paper compares Evolution Strategies and policy-gradient methods like GRPO as estimators of the same gradient, showing that ES cost depends on a task's effective dimension (number of independent skills) while PG cost depends on effective horizon (number of reward-changing tokens). This explains when ES can rival or beat PG for billion-parameter LLM fine-tuning.

entry.title: Aligning Judge Models to Be Logically Consistent Multi-Rule Interpreters

author.name: Michel Liao, Nimra Nadeem, Luxi He, Peter Henderson

entry.summary: This paper identifies multi-rule inconsistency in LLM judge models: when judging a full ruleset rather than one rule at a time, models interpret requirements differently and become more lenient, including downgrading violations of safety-critical rules. The authors characterize the phenomenon across judge models and examine mitigation approaches to align judges to be logically consistent multi-rule interpreters. This directly bears on scalable AI governance where models must follow thousands of jurisdictional rules.

entry.title: VADE: A Verifiable Agent Data Engine from Professional Sources

author.name: Xiangchao Chen, Zhiheng Lyu, Kai Zhang, Xueguang Ma, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: VADE automatically constructs verifiable analysis tasks for agent training and evaluation from public professional sources in domains like law and finance, exploiting the asymmetry that professional analyses are hard to produce but easy to check. This targets the bottleneck of expert-authored, hard-to-scale agent task data outside software engineering.

entry.title: Attributing Security Outcomes in LLM-Agent Evaluations: The Role of Content-Free State

author.name: Abdelmonaim Bounite, Zangir Iklassov

entry.summary: The authors show that LLM-agent security benchmark verdicts (attack success rates) are influenced by content-free state such as hash seeds and tool ordering, which should causally affect no outcome. They formalize decision noninterference and introduce TARE, a framework that attributes reported effects to agent, attack, or defense only when they exceed measured state-induced variance.

entry.title: EgoStudy: How Does Scaling Egocentric Data Affect VLA and WAM Pretraining?

author.name: Puzhen Yuan, Yanjiang Guo, Yichen Liu, Xiang Zhu, Qingzhou Lu, Chenxin Liu, Tun Ban, Haodong Yan, Zhide Zhong, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: EgoStudy is a systematic controlled study of how egocentric human manipulation data affects robot policy pretraining, holding the robot dataset fixed while varying egocentric data scale, diversity, processing strategies, and co-training configurations. It examines which action-prediction components benefit most from scaling and how effects differ between vision-language-action models and world-action models.

entry.title: Write, Evolve, Read: Streaming Cameras into a Persistent World State for 4D Occupancy Forecasting

author.name: ZiAn Wang, Tianyi Wang, Zhihao Chen, Manni Cui, Junkai Chen, ZhiJin Chen, Ruiqi Liu, Junfei Wu, Huanyu Zhang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Analyzes 4D occupancy forecasting for driving and finds camera-based world models fail mainly at retaining already-seen, unchanged space rather than predicting change. PersistWorld maintains a persistent 3D world state that frames are written into once, learned end to end, with an evolver predicting state at queried future times along the ego trajectory.

entry.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Nathan Delisle, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: The paper shows that massive activations, which concentrate up to 99.9% of activation variance along the first principal component, undermine standard SAE evaluations: variance explained and ablation damage become misleading, and PC1-rebuilding features dominate importance rankings without stable identity across runs. The authors propose a correction that trains SAEs on activations with PC1 removed and then adds PC1 back to the reconstruction.

entry.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals

author.name: Xuanlei Zhao, Hailun Xu, Kai Wang, Yang Luo, Yingxuan Ren, Zirui Zhu, Yuxuan Lou, Kun Xu, Yan Wang, Kanchan Sarkar, Yang You

entry.summary: LoopRes makes recurrent/looped Transformer architectures work well for existing pretrained LLMs by letting each looped layer attend to outputs of earlier loops, with trainable loop-aware keys distinguishing loop iterations. This converts loops from marginal finetuning gains into significant, consistent improvements and enables test-time compute scaling without new parameters.

entry.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?

author.name: Yanzhe Chen, Zhijun Cao, Zechen Bai, Wenzheng Zeng, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Xiaokang Liu, Ke Sun, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: RUIBench systematically studies robot-use interfaces (RUIs), the layer through which foundation-model agents express physical actions, with 30 manipulation tasks across five capability suites. RUIKit crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms to yield 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. Results show the interface alone swings a frontier agent's simulated success rate from 45% to 81%.

entry.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness

author.name: Xiao-Ming Wu, Kang Liao, Yuexiao Ma, Taolin Zhang, Mingqian Zhou, Nuo Chen, Ziming Li, Yihang Luo, Rui Li, Zhonghua Wu, Tianyu Xie, Xiawu Zheng, Zhongang Cai, Zhi Hou, Chen Change Loy

entry.summary: Embo-Harness systematically studies harnesses in which frontier multimodal models directly serve as robot policies in a closed-loop agentic loop, analyzing prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use. The authors distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe favoring interfaces that exploit native visual reasoning and tool use over handcrafted plans and action priors.

entry.title: Many languages, one common neural code

author.name: Rubina Veerakone | McGovern Institute for Brain Research

entry.summary: An MIT study published in Nature Neuroscience used multilingual language models to predict brain responses and found that the human brain appears to process linguistically diverse languages in a largely universal way, with a shared neural process detected across speakers of 21 languages. This is the first study to use multilingual models to predict brain responses across such a wide language range.

entry.title: Real-time event-level zero-shot learning at 150 ns: towards a foundation model for particle physics experiment triggering

author.name: Leo Rozanov, Lauri Laatu, Benedikt Maier, Arianna Cox, Aadeesh Sharma, Zhiqiang Que, Alex Tapper

entry.summary: This paper trains an offline transformer event embedding on 25 Standard Model processes with a metric loss and distills it into a quantized transformer running within LHC Level-1 trigger latency budgets (~150 ns), with learned bit widths under a fixed resource budget. The embedding generalizes, placing 28 held-out processes near physical relatives and enabling nearest-neighbour selection against unseen background. It is a step toward foundation models for real-time physics triggering.

entry.title: RecallWorld: Episodic Memory for Persistent Embodied Video World Models

author.name: Sarosij Bose, Gitika Karumuri, Chenqi Li, Allen Tu, Srikumar Sastry, Mellon Zhang, Avinash Ravichandran, Alexander Schwing, Konstantinos Karydis, Amit K. Roy Chowdhury

entry.summary: RecallWorld is a persistent embodied video world model that jointly reconstructs short multi-view episodes into Scenelets while keeping geometry independent across episodes, addressing the problem that video world models fail to preserve scene geometry and appearance on revisits. It uses camera-aware ray lifting to place perspective and fisheye images in a common world frame from a single source image. This matters for embodied AI because persistent memory is a key bottleneck for agents operating in environments over time.

entry.title: Where Does a Weight-Editing Agent Help? Blind Diagnosis and Repair of Deployment Faults in Vision Models

author.name: Zhuangzi Li, Shilv Cai, Jian Jin, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates LLM agents that edit neural network weights without gradients in a controlled setting where deployment faults (preprocessing, weight-conversion, output-convention) have known ground truth. Across 183 runs, it finds that when the fault type is known, simple scripts match the agent, but the agent can diagnose fault types outside any predefined script. The paper clarifies where such agents add real value versus where they are unnecessary.

entry.title: Demystifying Classifier-Free Guidance for Auto-Regressive Image Generation

author.name: Zhiling Zhou, Jiachun Pan, Fengzhuo Zhang, Dirk Bergemann, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: This paper explains why classifier-free guidance is needed in autoregressive image generation: both conditional and unconditional logits share previous-token repetition as their leading semantics, while texture information lives mainly in their difference, so greedy decoding from conditional logits alone yields near-pure-color images. The authors support the explanation with training-dynamics analysis of shallow transformers and theory.

entry.title: What Remains After Concept Erasure? Sparse Autoencoder Probes for Auditing Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhuan Shi, Lu Wei, Yuta Nakashima, Noa Garcia, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: SAE-Audit is a white-box auditing method that uses sparse autoencoder probes to test whether erased concepts in text-to-image diffusion models can be restored via activation interventions without weight changes or modified prompts. It compares original and edited models in a shared SAE representation and injects sparse directions to probe residual concept information after erasure.

entry.title: RoboAda: Adapting Frozen Robot Policies at Test Time to Physics They Cannot See

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Zijian Jin, Shuaicheng Niu, Baian Chen, Weirui Ye, Jihun Hamm, Yilun Du

entry.summary: RoboAda adapts frozen pretrained robot policies at deployment time to unobservable physical changes such as object mass or joint friction, correcting executed commands while leaving the policy's plan unchanged. This avoids the pitfalls of updating plans or applying unreliable gradient-based model updates when the visible scene is unchanged.

entry.title: Quantizing Diffusion LLMs under Parallel Decoding: Commitment Risk and the Parallelism Tax

author.name: Huan Xu, Maosen Zhao, Pengtao Chen, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Studies W4A4 post-training quantization of diffusion LLMs under deployed accelerated decoders that cache context and commit confident masked positions in parallel. It identifies two failure channels: irreversible errors entering via forced commitments, and a parallelism tax of extra forward passes caused by compressed logit gaps pushing positions below the threshold.

entry.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans

author.name: Mohammed Baharoon, Sung Eun Kim, Mahmoud Hussain Alabbad, Lucas Bijnens, Ali Piracha, Reem Alwasiah, Talal Yahyan, Abdulrahman Alamoudi, Mashael Alshehri, Rayan Alsager, Hannah Hancock, Anna M. Hunkem\"oller, Peter Youssef, Mona A. Alhammad, Afnan Aljumayan, Brecht Van Berkel, Eric Bijnens, Saud Alhussain, Maarten Steyvers, Rolf Symons, Bryan Eelen, Ayed Alaklubi, Maha Buraykan Alshammari, Amirah Fahad Alshammeri, Tomas Gilvydis, Ibrahim AlTurki, Monerah Almohideb, Ali Alburkani, Shahad Alhomaiani, Fatima Jabali, Abdulrhman Aljouie, Daesung Kim, Junha Im, Michael Moritz, Hassan R. Alomaish, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: CTLink is a text-prompted 3D segmentation model trained on 4123 chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings (including a new dataset, ReXGroundingCTv2, with 1134 scans and 1895 fully segmented findings) that links textual report findings to scan locations. It substantially outperforms the public VoxTell baseline with a hit rate of 0.816 versus 0.533 and higher instance F1 and Dice scores.

entry.title: Prompt-in-Content Attacks: Exploiting Uploaded Inputs to Hijack LLM Behavior

author.name: Zhuotao Lian, Weiyu Wang, Qingkui Zeng, Toru Nakanishi, Teruaki Kitasuka, Chunhua Su

entry.summary: The paper identifies prompt-in-content injection attacks, where adversarial instructions hidden in uploaded documents or pasted text manipulate LLM outputs such as summaries without user awareness. The authors demonstrate feasibility across popular platforms, analyze root causes like prompt concatenation and weak input isolation, and propose mitigations.

entry.title: Do Simulated Users Push Back Like Real Users? Correctness vs. Stance

author.name: Xindi Huang

entry.summary: This study tests whether LLM-simulated users behave like real users in multi-turn evaluation by comparing real WildChat follow-up turns to simulated turns after an assistant challenges or endorses the user. Real users push back more after challenges than endorsements (20.5% vs 8.2%), while a GPT-based simulator pushes back at the same rate regardless of stance, often restating requests as disguised insistence. The finding exposes a measurable stance gap that undermines the validity of simulated-user evaluations.

entry.title: VidRouteBench: A Benchmark for Budgeted Video-Generation Routing

author.name: Dayu Wang

entry.summary: VidRouteBench is the first benchmark for routing text-to-video prompts across models and sampling configurations under budget constraints, spanning 16 arms from 7 open families with 121x cost variation and 27,110 generated clips. It includes human-calibrated quality scores, per-dimension ratings, repeated seeds, an encrypted test split, and cold-start test families. It enables rigorous study of cost-quality tradeoffs in generative model routing, an increasingly important deployment problem.

entry.title: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences

author.name: Shardul Bansal, Seth Schilbe, Jarrod Barnes

entry.summary: Introduces SMB Bench, a calibrated 90-day wholesale-business simulator with 18 causally paired tasks and an 859-run frontier-model trace dataset, to measure whether LLM agents notice, attribute, and act on delayed consequences of their own decisions. Across 16 frontier models, only 3 beat a fixed buying rule, and models often record correct diagnoses in notes without acting on them.

entry.title: A world model for longitudinal health-trajectory prediction in older adults across multinational cohorts

author.name: Jingyi Wu, Chenghua Guo, Qianlin Zuo, Pengfei Li, Luxia Zhang

entry.summary: This work builds a health world model using the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to model evolving health states in older adults and simulate future trajectories under actions, rather than predicting static risk at single time points. Trained on the US Health and Retirement Study, it transfers without refitting to the English ELSA and Chinese CHARLS cohorts, demonstrating cross-national generalization.

entry.title: DeFlowCritic: Dense Latent Reward Alignment for Text-to-Image Flow Matching Models

author.name: Zeeshan Khan, Xin Yu, Shizhe Chen, Cordelia Schmid

entry.summary: DeFlowCritic is an online RL framework that aligns text-to-image flow matching models by providing dense reward supervision on intermediate latents rather than sparse rewards from final decoded images, enabling early-stage guidance of the denoising trajectory. It also addresses Pareto trade-offs between compositional accuracy and aesthetics in multi-reward alignment. The work is relevant because efficient RL alignment of generative models is an active frontier.

entry.title: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration

author.name: Ivan Brugere, Junqi Jiang, Saumitra Mishra, Sumitra Ganesh

entry.summary: INSEP defends LLMs against abliteration attacks, which remove safety refusal behavior by projecting out a refusal direction in activation space. The defense fine-tunes the model with a low-rank adapter, guided by adversarial eigendecomposition, to reduce the separability of harmful versus benign activations along that direction while preserving refusal behavior and output quality. This targets a mechanistic interpretability attack with a mechanistically informed countermeasure.

entry.title: Schedule, Rank, Profile: Continuous Evaluation of LLM Agents in Games

author.name: Martyna Plomecka, Yao Yan, DJ Sterling, Jon Lipovetz, John Schultz, Michael Aaron, Chiamaka Chukwuka, Will Cukierski, Christopher D'Mello, Bovard Doerschuk-Tiberi, Robert Fraser, Ian Gemp, Yuting Han, Addison Howard, Oran Kelly, Siqi Liu, Jeff Moser, Meghan O'Connell, Jun Peng, Laurel Prince, Meg Risdal, Jonathan Ward, Domino Weir, Marc Lanctot

entry.summary: A framework for continuously evaluating LLM agents in games, addressing the staleness and cost problems of one-time benchmarks. It couples an adaptive Bradley-Terry-based scheduler that concentrates match budget on unresolved comparisons with ranking and profiling components, avoiding expensive full round-robin evaluations across model pairs.

entry.title: Don't Train It, Write It: An AI Agent Writes New Capabilities into Language Model Weights

author.name: Santiago Rivadeneira Quintero

entry.summary: Shows an AI agent can add gated attention heads and MLP neurons to a pretrained language model's layers without backpropagation, using only 50 model passes and no task examples, raising normalized BIG-Bench Hard scores of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from 19.95 to 41.05 and Gemma-3-1B-it from 10.25 to 32.86 while leaving other behaviors bit-identical (KL exactly 0). A striking result on surgical, non-training capability insertion with verified non-interference. Both models referenced are established released models, so this is analysis of new capability-editing techniques rather than a model launch.

entry.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?

author.name: Zhe Chen, Emma Hsieh, Vicky Fu

entry.summary: Introduces AMB, a benchmark testing whether AI agents spend a client's money well, evaluating 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and live-data research questions, with payments settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via the x402 protocol. Notably, nine models fell for seller traps at least once, with repeat charges and above-list quotes accounting for 79% of scam events.

entry.title: Can Ideologues Agree on Quality? From Non-identifiable Latent Factors to Collective Outcomes

author.name: David Gamba and Seura Ha and Daniel M. Romero and Grant Schoenebeck

entry.summary: This paper proves that X's Community Notes system (Biased Matrix Factorization) requires fixing an ideological anchor to separate note quality from reviewer ideology, and characterizes how L2 regularization anchors quality at a point proportional to mean reviewer ideology. It shows objective quality is recovered if and only if the mean reviewer is neutral, paralleling the Condorcet Jury Theorem. The result has broad implications for any crowdsourced fact-checking or rating system built on latent-factor models.

entry.title: Seeing Right, Writing Wrong: Where Short Chain-of-Thought Breaks Spatial VQA

author.name: Chenhao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper shows that short chain-of-thought prompting often degrades vision-language model performance on spatial questions, because once a VLM writes down a spatial relation, its answer follows the written sentence rather than the image. The authors study 15 open VLMs (2B-38B) plus six frontier closed models, ruling out token count, turn format, and visual forgetting, and trace the failure through three stages including re-weighting of visual cues during writing. The work matters because it reframes CoT failures as a transcription problem with direct implications for how multimodal reasoning systems should be prompted and trained.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Token Retention in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Fawaz Sammani, Nikos Deligiannis

entry.summary: This paper analyzes whether autoregressive large vision-language models actually need continuous access to hundreds or thousands of visual tokens during generation. By studying attention dynamics across generation time and transformer depth, the authors find visual attention peaks in early generation steps and rapidly declines, revealing temporal and depth-wise structure in the use of visual information. This has direct implications for efficient multimodal inference via visual token pruning.

entry.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts

author.name: Chendong Xiang, Chengwen Zhang, Ruowen Zhao, Zeyuan Wang, Shuhe Huang, Rongxu Cui, Min Zhao, Fan Bao, Hengkai Tan, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Entangle is an in-context world-action model for robotic manipulation that maps a single human demonstration video plus robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. It tackles misalignment between human videos and robot actions by converting recorded robot videos into matched human contexts via video-to-video generation, and prevents shortcut reliance in policy learning. The author list includes Jun Zhu and Fan Bao, suggesting a strong lab.

entry.title: ArgsWorld: Unifying 3DGS Scene Reconstruction, Generation and Extrapolation with Autoregressive Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Weiming Chen, Shuaiyan Liu, Xinyu Shao, Zhewen Chen, Tian Guan, Yonghong He, Xitong Ling

entry.summary: ArgsWorld is an autoregressive diffusion model that generates explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes alongside video, jointly processing historical image latents and noisy new-view latents within a diffusion transformer. A 3D Self-Forcing Distillation scheme trains the model on its own generations to improve scene consistency as new regions come into view.

entry.title: DeRail: Escaping Trajectory Priors via Counterfactual Action Steering for Mid-Execution Instruction Switching

author.name: Yitong Hong, Xiangdong Feng, Xiaoxi Sun, Senqiao Yang, Boyao Han, Zhejian Yang, Shiyang Zhou, Yongcai Wang, Pengguang Chen, Shu Liu, Li Jiang, Zhuotao Tian

entry.summary: The paper studies mid-execution instruction switching in robot policies including VLA models, identifying trajectory hijacking as a key failure mode where post-switch behavior stays drawn toward prior-task trajectories. It proposes Counterfactual Action Steering, a training-free, model-agnostic inference-time method that queries the policy with counterfactual instructions to identify and subtract interference from non-target tasks.

entry.title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study

author.name: Ayush Khaitan, Liam Fowl, Tom\`as Ortega, Alex Kontorovich and Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: The study measures calibration of an existing frontier model (GPT-5.6-Sol-Ultra, released July 2026) on 100 open research-level conjectures in geometric analysis that the model itself selected with a stated at-least-50% success chance. The model's mean stated resolution probability was 0.617 versus an observed success rate of 0.103, with poor Brier score and ECE, revealing severe systematic overconfidence on open mathematical problems. This is an empirical audit of self-knowledge in frontier LLMs.

entry.title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Zhuangzhuang Pan and Yan Xia and Kaiwen Lei and Chee Seng Chan

entry.summary: The paper identifies silent value completion: LLM judges issuing strict verdicts when criteria conflicts leave the winner undetermined by the rubric, effectively smuggling in undeclared trade-off values. TradeoffBench shows six open-weight judges pick unsupported winners on 9-81% of 1,345 conflicts and follow an explicitly banned majority rule, while reasoning-enabled judges largely comply only when an explicit rule is given.

entry.title: XShot: Cross-Shot Video Object Insertion from a Reference Video

author.name: Bangxun Tang, Chen Chen

entry.summary: XShot inserts objects into one video shot by referencing another shot of the same scene, ensuring cross-shot appearance consistency without masks, boxes, or camera poses. It builds on a video diffusion transformer and formulates the task as in-context generation with a geometry-aware cross-shot attention mechanism.

entry.title: Mirror Descent at the Edge of Stability

author.name: Vincent X. Wang, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: The paper extends the edge-of-stability phenomenon from gradient descent to mirror descent by introducing mirror sharpness, curvature measured relative to the mirror potential, and empirically observes it hovering slightly above the 2/eta threshold. The authors derive a dual central flow ODE modeling mirror descent iterates in continuous time at the onset of edge of stability. This generalizes a key empirical law of deep learning to non-Euclidean optimizers.

entry.title: RES: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models with Rolling Entropy Sampling

author.name: Patrick Pynadath, Nicolas Perez-Nieves, Bobak Shahriari, Jean Tarbouriech, Ruqi Zhang, Ivan Lobov

entry.summary: Using the entropy-bound sampler in DiffusionGemma (an existing model), the paper studies KV-cache commit policies for diffusion language samplers: immediate freezing of accepted tokens causes macro accuracy to collapse from 73% to 20% as the entropy bound is relaxed, while unfrozen sampling stays near 70%, and whole-block commits waste computation since tokens converge mostly left-to-right. Rolling Entropy Sampling commits tokens in convergence order to balance these extremes. This is a concrete efficiency win for diffusion language models.

entry.title: ARC: Adaptive Rollout Control for Efficient Synchronous LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yihui Zhang, Tianyu Wo, Jinghao Wang, Xiao Zhou, Huitian Xue, Xiaoyang Sun, Zeying Wang, Chunming Hu, Renyu Yang

entry.summary: ARC is a closed-loop rollout architecture for synchronous LLM RL that operates at group granularity, using Calibrated Streaming Backfill to decide from partial observations whether a group is worth completing and backfilling fresh candidates otherwise. This reduces GPU idle time from the fixed rollout-barrier-update loop and avoids wasted generation on samples that will not contribute. Directly targets a costly systems bottleneck in LLM RL training.

entry.title: Look Back: Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual World Models

author.name: Jinwoo Kim, Toghrul Abbasov, Lucius E.J. Bynum, Aahlad Puli, Stephanie Milani, Hyunwoo Ryu, Seunghoon Hong, Kyunghyun Cho, Rajesh Ranganath

entry.summary: This paper introduces REINFORCE Look Back (RLB), a policy gradient estimator that uses counterfactual world models to transform observed trajectories rather than imagine new ones. By using counterfactual returns as baselines, RLB separates the effect of an agent's actions from environmental randomness, with proven conditions for unbiasedness and variance reduction.

entry.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yifan Duan, Du Yin, Siyuan Zheng, Chao Xue, Lihuan Li, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: DoppelVet is a verification framework that checks proposed memory or skill updates before they enter a self-evolving agent's persistent state. It constructs an alternative update matching all verifier signals, replays both from the same state in both presentation orders, and compares behaviors to decide retention, without needing safety labels.

entry.title: FP-Prune: Rethinking Visual Token Pruning from an Information Gain Perspective

author.name: Haozhe Zhao, Junxiang Zhang, Junxin Wang, Yuan Ge, Xiangchen Song, Dingyang Zhang, JingBo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: FP-Prune reframes visual token pruning in vision-language models as maximizing mutual information gain of retained tokens, proving that frame potential is an effective surrogate for mutual information. The resulting training-free method iteratively selects tokens under a budget to preserve complementary visual information better than attention- or similarity-based scores. This directly addresses inference-cost reduction for VLMs.

entry.title: Endpoint-Conditioned Process Value: What an Endpoint-Blind Process Score Adds Once Terminal Status and Cost Are Known

author.name: Chris D Yan, Ken Wang, MarkX Qian, Jin Jiang, Albus Wu, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: The authors rigorously measure what process/trajectory scores add beyond knowing terminal status and cost, using 1,255 trajectories over 158 test-generation tasks. Smaller judges (4B-14B) add nothing statistically distinguishable from zero, while a Qwen3 32B judge adds +0.050 AUC that survives refitting bootstrap, with most of the gain recoverable from eight behavioral features. This is an important reality check on the value of process-based reward and evaluation signals.

entry.title: Detectable Epistemic Attack Layers: A Coverage Theorem and Standardized Harness for Conversation-History Integrity

author.name: Fahrell Giovanny, Geby Bayuningtyas and Sahrul Mukharom

entry.summary: This paper formalizes session-level contamination attacks on the application layers that store and reinject conversation history for deployed language models, proving a coverage theorem about which attack layers verification can detect. A standardized harness evaluates eight defense mechanism families across 3,249 sessions and three model families, quantifying false-positive costs of pattern-based defenses.

entry.title: Representation Alignment Is Only as Good as the Teacher's Behavioral Structure

author.name: Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Haoyuan Chen, Hexin Wang, Hanyu Zhou, Zhenglin Wan, Wangbo Zhao, Pengfei Zhou

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates 14 frozen vision-encoder teachers for representation alignment (REPA) in vision-language-action fine-tuning across 16 manipulation tasks, finding that no off-the-shelf encoder improves clean success of pi-0.5 by more than 1 point and all reduce robustness under perturbations by 10 to 39 points. Neither global semantics nor spatial structure predicts which teachers help. The paper argues teacher choice should be based on behavioral structure rather than encoder-intrinsic metrics.

entry.title: JEPA-Shield: Safe Diffusion Planning with Latent World Models via Conformal Shielding

author.name: Taekyung Kim, Ege Yuceel, Steven Hong, Georgios Fainekos, Dimitra Panagou, Bardh Hoxha

entry.summary: JEPA-Shield connects a frozen JEPA world model to task-space safety enforcement for image-based robot planning. It uses conformal prediction to convert motion-prediction errors into uncertainty tubes, and a backup-based shield screens candidate trajectories against physical constraints during diffusion-inspired sampling-based MPC. This addresses the gap between latent world-model predictions and formal guarantees of physical constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: Do More Roles or Larger Models Improve LLM Fact-Checking? A Controlled Study on Fixed Evidence

author.name: Martin Pavl\'i\v{c}ek, Martin Kotyrba, Eva Voln\'a, Tom\'a\v{s} Filip, Petr Sos\'ik

entry.summary: This controlled study compares compute-scaling strategies for LLM fact-checking on identical fixed evidence: larger models, repeated sampling, and a multi-role Tribunal with quoted findings, code-based checks, and a blind auditor. Across 300 AVeriTeC claims and four open-weight model families, a 9B judge outperformed a 27B sibling, and larger models abstained more without greater accuracy.

entry.title: Into My Arms: Structured reinforcement learning for autonomous transport of objects and humans

author.name: Elle Miller, Reem Almheiri, Takuma Tsukakoshi, Ben Sanati, Tamon Miyake, Yushi Wang, Namiko Saito, Shigeki Sugano, Tetsuya Ogata, Rika Antonova, Oisin Mac Aodha, and Sethu Vijayakumar

entry.summary: This robotics paper tackles whole-body humanoid manipulation with three structured RL additions: Sparse Interaction Edges, Interaction Gated Transport, and a Hinted Object Path, while leaving the policy free to discover its own strategy. It demonstrates generalization from rigid-object transport to human transport, including what the authors state is the first bed-to-wheelchair human transfer demonstration.

entry.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety

author.name: Zhiyu Zhang, Yuankai Li, Muhao Chen

entry.summary: MobileGrail is an on-device guardrail model for mobile GUI agents that avoids exposing private screens to cloud-hosted large multimodal models. It maintains a recurrent task state retaining only safety-relevant evidence and learns two labels, unsafe and block, within an intervention window spanning from the first action of a potentially unsafe sequence, enabling early yet precise intervention.

entry.title: ProMix: Efficient Data Mixture Optimization for Robotic Imitation via Proxy-Reference DRO

author.name: Qie Sima, Wei Xue, Yike Guo

entry.summary: ProMix makes distributionally robust data-mixture optimization affordable for vision-language-action training by using a 15M-parameter proxy model to learn per-domain sampling weights against a frozen reference, avoiding the cost of training full policies twice. The learned weights transfer without re-tuning to VLA backbones up to 7B parameters.

entry.title: SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization

author.name: Yusong Zhao, Zihao Zhao, Zirui Zhang, Tunyu Zhang, Ziyan Wang, Yi Wang, Chengzhi Mao, Hao Wang

entry.summary: SAEPO addresses the coarse credit assignment of RLVR for LLM reasoning by using a pretrained sparse autoencoder to identify which intermediate reasoning tokens contributed to success or failure, rather than relying only on outcome-level rewards. This token-level signal improves policy optimization efficiency, especially for base models trained from sparse outcome feedback. It connects interpretability tools (SAEs) directly to RL training improvements.

entry.title: EnvTrap: Revealing the Environment-Only Attack Surface in Embodied AI via Consequence-Blind Action Execution

author.name: Zehao Liu, Huashuo Lei, Xi Lin, Haoang Li, Yuliang Chen, Huarui Zhang, Yifan Wang

entry.summary: EnvTrap exposes a previously underexplored attack surface in embodied AI: an adversary can trigger hazardous agent behaviors purely by rearranging physical objects, without touching the model or the instructions. The authors build a diagnostic pipeline with paired safe, trap, and null-trap (benign-but-misleading) scenarios and show environment-only perturbations substantially raise hazardous-action rates. This highlights that safety evaluations of embodied agents must account for physical environment configuration, not just adversarial inputs.

entry.title: Grokking as a Subspace Search: Computing the Destination Before Training

author.name: Sunjae Jeong, Jaeseung Kim, Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: The authors show that for group-operation tasks, the subspace a network will eventually occupy when it groks — the right subspace — can be computed from the task before training, and they prove it is essentially unique. This makes grokking hypotheses falsifiable: the delay is a search for this subspace, and providing the subspace from the start eliminates the delay.

entry.title: Quantizing in the Loop: Drift-Aware Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yanlong Chen, Thongthornpatch Chamadol, Yichen Guo, Yunfei Gao, Mohan Liu, Addison Lin Wang, Yawei Li

entry.summary: This paper identifies why post-training quantization of vision-language-action models collapses at 2 bits or fewer: offline calibration data causes distribution shift when quantized policies roll out, and layer-wise weight reconstruction is a poor proxy for action quality. It introduces LoopQ, which calibrates on states sampled from the quantized policy's own rollouts, closing the calibration loop for ultra-low-bit VLA deployment on resource-constrained robots.

entry.title: AIGI-26: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Image Detection Across Diverse Modern Generators

author.name: Qishuai Ding, Yifeng Wang, Shichuang Xie, Yanli Ren and Guorui Feng

entry.summary: The paper introduces AIGI-26, a 253,200-image benchmark spanning 26 modern open- and closed-source image generators, designed to expose weaknesses of detectors trained or evaluated on older, artifact-laden generators. It also proposes MAFDNet, a multi-aspect forensic detection network using fixed operators for texture, prediction, resampling, and chromatic cues.

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Evidence: Measuring and Training Evidence Dependence in Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Zijie Jin, Shuai Zhao, Haoran Tao, Chaomin Huang, Liwen Luo

entry.summary: The paper shows that accuracy metrics in video temporal grounding reward models that answer blind or fit annotation styles, and introduces a fixed-answer audit measuring evidence dependence by editing frames inside the annotated interval versus placebo edits elsewhere. Audits of Qwen2.5-VL-7B checkpoints reveal that fine-tuning and IoU-reward RL raise accuracy 9-20 points without increasing reliance on event frames.

entry.title: LeanReviewBench: Semantic Alignment Review in Mathematical Lean Projects

author.name: Ruichen Qiu, Hao Shen, Lihong Zhi, Xiao-Shan Gao

entry.summary: LeanReviewBench is a benchmark for project-level semantic alignment review in Lean formalization: checking whether formal proofs actually preserve the content of informal mathematical targets across 197 versioned inputs from 18 real Lean projects. It combines development-history discovery, target binding, and Astra annotation with human review to test whether AI systems can catch formalization misalignment at scale.

entry.title: Decompose and Describe: Narrowing the Diagnosis-to-Report Gap in 3D CT Report Generation

author.name: Zhisong Wang, Wanxing Chang, Weiwei Cao, Fenghe Tang, Bowen Shi, Ruifeng Yuan, Yong Xia, Jianpeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a diagnosis-to-report gap in medical vision-language models: across five MedVLMs, diagnostic VQA outperforms free-form report generation on the same studies and disease categories, and conventional report adaptation does not close it. The proposed DeCAD framework progressively decomposes report generation at diagnostic, regional textual, and regional visual levels to narrow this gap.

entry.title: VeriTouch: Verified Visuo-Tactile World Models that Improve Robot Policy Learning

author.name: Shuxun Wang, Xiaonan Jiang, Zhaoyu Wang, Ziyuan Chu, Xihang Yue, Pengfei Liu, Haodong Zhu, Shiqi Liu, Mingzhi Zheng, Liang Su, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces VeriTouch, a framework for generating and verifying synthetic visuo-tactile trajectories to scale robot policy learning beyond costly real-world data. Its VeriGen world model jointly generates dual-view videos and realistic tactile sequences conditioned on initial images and task instructions, with a verification pipeline to ensure trajectories are useful for training.

entry.title: Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination

author.name: Dominik Bernard Lau, Filip Pawlicki, Jan Dubi\'nski, Sebastian Cygert

entry.summary: Proposes a generation-based, fully black-box framework for auditing LLM training data contamination that infers context-induced information gain from targeted token discrepancies. Exploiting the observation that the membership signal is sparse and concentrated in a few informative tokens, the budget-constrained method drastically reduces inference costs compared to full-sequence sampling or uniform token probing.

entry.title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL

author.name: Xinche Zhang, Shanghong Xie, Zhiyuan Ma, Jinhao Li, Sen Song

entry.summary: Studies how reinforcement learning from simulated user reactions is distorted when a share of users privately seek validation, showing the policy shifts its endorsement threshold — endorsing at-fault posters more often — rather than targeting individuals. The effect persists at matched KL divergence and under a goal-blind reward, quantified on 1,000 Reddit AITA posts with community verdicts.

entry.title: Learning the Next Best Move with Visual Diffusion Models

author.name: Amir Razlighi, Ali Mahdavi Amiri, Yiorgos Chrysanthou, Andrey Voynov, Daniel Cohen-Or

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that visual diffusion models fine-tuned on state-next-best-move pairs can predict actions whose value depends on consequences several steps ahead, in chess puzzles and tile-based pathfinding, without explicit search or symbolic representation at inference. Repeated single-move predictions construct full solutions, suggesting lookahead can be internalized in visual generative models.

entry.title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows

author.name: Yitong Qiao, Lei Liu, Yue Shen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: MedUIGym is an interactive benchmark environment with 15,739 tasks across 17 sources and six clinical task families, where vision-language agents operate real EHR GUIs via screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions, with a paired native-tool interface. It verifies both final answers and clinical actions and supports parallel trajectory collection; benchmarking of twelve VLMs reveals substantial room for improvement.

entry.title: Attention Latent Feedback

author.name: Xuyuan Xiong, Siyu Chen, Mengzhao Chen, Yue Su, Zhuoran Yang, Ping Luo, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: Attention Latent Feedback (ALF) is an architecture allowing every sublayer at the current token to attend to deeper-layer outputs of the previous position during autoregressive decoding, with training unrolled into two parallel passes and single-pass decoding via cached states. Across MoE models up to 4.0B parameters, ALF lowers held-out loss by 0.022-0.024 nats at about 1.1% decoding FLOP overhead, outperforming prior final-state feedback. A credible architectural exploration with strong authorship (Yang, Luo, Liu).

entry.title: Reducing Order Sensitivity in Decision Models

author.name: Bodong Liu, Dongyoung Go, Sofian Zalouk, Kilian Q. Weinberger

entry.summary: This paper shows that order-sensitivity is pervasive across ten open- and closed-source decision models, degrading accuracy and reliability, especially as option count grows and across multi-step decisions. The authors systematically compare eight mitigation methods and find tree attention to be a surprisingly effective and efficient route to order invariance.

entry.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google research blog post describing work on improving residual connections in transformers, the core architectural mechanism that enables gradient flow and deep network training. The Algorithms and Theory group proposes a modified residual design aimed at improving training stability and model performance.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks Expose Path-Dependent Failures in Discrete Medical Image Tokenizers

author.name: Ahmed Loughzali, Akash Yallamati, Aadiv Reki, Aslan Shaukat Vaida, Jeyashree Krishnan

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether imperceptible input perturbations can break medical imaging systems through discrete image tokenizers alone, testing four tokenizers across three modalities and extending the strongest attack to a deployed generative model. It finds path-dependent failures: a supervised attack collapses diagnostic accuracy on the reconstruction path (ROC AUC dropping to 0.013 or below) while sparing the direct token path, and an unsupervised label-free attack behaves oppositely. This reveals a systemic vulnerability in tokenizer-based medical AI pipelines.

entry.title: Plan Big, Paint Small: Semantic-Aware Computation Allocation for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Yixuan Luo and Yanjing Li

entry.summary: The paper finds that in shared-latent AR video diffusion, using a 14B model for only the first chunk and a 1.3B model for continuation preserves 95% of the large model's semantic advantage, while the reverse allocation keeps only 16% at ten times the cost. This motivates BigSmall, a training-free planner-renderer sampler where the large model plans the opening and sketches changing chunks while the small model renders.

entry.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use

author.name: Jin Cui, Xinyue Long, Jiepeng Zhou, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren, Hao Dong

entry.summary: AOVO is a data-centric RL framework for multimodal LLM visual tool use that replaces call-contingent reward engineering with perception attribution, identifying failures attributable to missing visual evidence, plus policy-adaptive data sampling. This avoids degenerate calling behaviors caused by reward hacks while teaching models when tool invocation genuinely helps. The reframing from reward shaping to data curation is a notable conceptual contribution to agentic tool-use RL.

entry.title: Mitigating Backdoors in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chengzhong Wang, Lang Lin, Shengfang Zhai, Chenru Wang, Daniel Yiming Cao, Sheng-Yen Chou, Jiaheng Zhang, Pin-Yu Chen, Shengwei An

entry.summary: Presents UNMASK, the first defense framework for backdoor attacks on masked diffusion language models, which detects trigger-containing inputs, localizes trigger tokens, and removes the backdoor by exploiting the specificity and dominance properties of triggers. This fills a notable gap as MDLMs emerge as serious alternatives to autoregressive LLMs but their security is underexplored. Important groundwork for securing the next generation of text generation architectures.

entry.title: Robust Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models via Simulating Brain Functional Localization

author.name: Manyi Li, Yufan Liu, Bing Li, Xia Wu, Ziyu Li, Weiming Hu

entry.summary: The paper introduces IVO, a concept reactivation attack that optimizes the initial latent of image generation rather than searching text or image spaces, and shows across 8 erasure methods that it reactivates erased concepts more effectively than prior attacks. Motivated by brain functional localization, the authors then localize target-concept components in the model for more robust erasure.

entry.title: Where Do Fact-Checking Errors Arise? Separating Retrieval, Search Control and Judgement in Evidence-Grounded Verification

author.name: Martin Pavl\'i\v{c}ek, Martin Kotyrba, Eva Voln\'a, Tom\'a\v{s} Filip, Petr Sos\'ik

entry.summary: This paper introduces a diagnostic protocol that traces reference evidence from store to verdict, separating failures of retrieval, search control, judgement, and verdict validation in evidence-grounded fact-checking. Testing a 9B open-weight model on FEVER, FEVER 2.0, and AVeriTeC claims, a single hybrid retrieval pass delivered complete evidence for 226 of 228 evidence-bearing claims, while adaptive controllers and tool agents spent 2-9x more calls without consistent gains.

entry.title: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents against Multi-Step Prompt Injection

author.name: Jiaqi Rong, Yunchen Lu, Lihai Nie, Yan Jia, Tong Li, Zheli Liu

entry.summary: Conartist is a cascaded adaptive prompt-injection framework that red-teams computer-using agent harnesses, exploiting two vulnerabilities: consistency checking can be bypassed by malicious actions that appear logically consistent with the legitimate task, and risk auditing itself introduces additional exploitable actions. A goal-pollution stage progressively sets up the attack. The work exposes concrete gaps in current agent security mechanisms.

entry.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Zijian Jin, Janet Wang, Xingchen Zhao, Zhenyu Zhang, Weirui Ye, Yilun Du

entry.summary: RoboThink proposes a division of labor in which a reasoning agent thinks about failures and mid-task corrections while the robot policy is trained to act on the agent's guidance through an instruction channel, avoiding both slow agent control and the limitation that policies only follow instructions from fresh starts. The design handles mid-episode user corrections such as redirecting the robot from one object to another and conveying corrective motion feedback.

entry.title: Same Executions, Different Gaps: Judgment Rules in Web-Agent Evaluation

author.name: Zelong Wang, Weiyue Li, Fei Xue, Junru Zhu

entry.summary: This study examines how web-agent benchmark conclusions depend on judgment methodology rather than agent behavior, showing that requiring recorded evidence for success judgments can eliminate most of a reported lead on identical executions. Controlled additions of missing relations explain how gaps can be hidden or manufactured by evaluation design choices.

entry.title: Test-Time Latent Computation to Improve Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Yang, Zheng Fang, Wenqi Fan, Jun Xia

entry.summary: The paper shows that MLLMs contain stable reusable layers that can be re-forwarded at inference without disrupting generation, and proposes Lobals, a training-free decoding method that identifies the layer window with strongest visual-token attention and re-forwards through it to add latent computation. This extends test-time compute scaling from token-level reasoning to visual perception in latent space.

entry.title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild

author.name: Yuxi Wang, Yufei Liu, Chengkai Jin, Qingyue Chen, Wenqi Ouyang, Tianyi Wei, Kerui Ren, Siyuan Huang, Zhiqi Shen, Hongsheng Li, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: Proposes ViDiHand2, which reformulates video-diffusion-prior-based hand depth estimation from appearance regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving. Fine-Grained Geometric Lifting and Clip-Level Ray Fitting recover metric depth via consistency between pixel-aligned 2D joints and MANO hand structure, generalizing better across unseen cameras for egocentric robot manipulation learning.

entry.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models

author.name: Qinyue Li, Weijie Qiao, Qingyi Tao, Zerui Gong, Zhe Yang, Quanzhou Li, Taolin Zhang, Jinglin He, Zhonghua Wu, Chen Change Loy

entry.summary: Native LAM repurposes a single pretrained video diffusion transformer as both inverse- and forward-dynamics models, extracting latent actions from unlabeled video with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge, requiring minimal changes to the world model. This avoids training LAM components from scratch and their pixel-reconstruction versus latent-capacity trade-offs.

entry.title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation

author.name: Jingxi Chen, Yujia Chen, Cornelia Fermuller, Yiannis Aloimonos, Wen-Sheng Chu, Du Tran

entry.summary: WorldLatent formulates a unified 4D latent space bridging perception tasks like depth and camera estimation with 4D generation, addressing the lack of a shared representational protocol in spatiotemporal vision. By aligning perception and generation in one latent space, it draws an analogy to how GPT-style unified tokenization transformed language modeling.

entry.title: SnakeTranslate: Weakly Supervised Policy Learning from Offline Parallel Text for Simultaneous Translation

author.name: Yu Pu, Zhiyun Fan, Baiji Liu, Zhifu Gao, Xiangang Li

entry.summary: SnakeTranslate learns both prefix translation quality and READ/WRITE decision policies from ordinary parallel text without action annotations, adapting loss-derived alignments to sampled causal histories. It supports SFT plus on-policy distillation with reverse KL divergence, and at inference uses an append-only interleaved token history enabling incremental decoding with cache reuse. A 4B model improves quality-latency trade-offs over streaming policies on FLEURS, NTREX128, and WMT24++.

entry.title: Causal Dioramas: Controllable Video Generation, Revision and Editing via Intervention

author.name: Yifan Shen, Xinyi Yang, Peiyuan Zhu, Yichang Jian, Jinyuan Hu, Xilin He, Fengming Zhu, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Causal Dioramas introduces modules that decompose generated video into a concept graph so that instructions become interventions on individual variables, enabling targeted revision and editing of videos rather than regeneration from scratch. A connector transmits graph interventions to the underlying video generator while reusing original noise. The work brings causal representation learning ideas to bear on the controllability gap in text-to-video models.

entry.title: Beyond Output Suppression: Mitigating Privacy Risks in LVLMs via Visual Intrinsic Privacy Erasure

author.name: Xiangkui Cao and Jie Zhang and Meina Kan and Shiguang Shan and Xilin Chen

entry.summary: Shows that fine-tuning and model-editing defenses against privacy leakage in large vision-language models are illusory: models refuse to disclose private information under normal decoding but still leak it in sentence-completion scenarios, indicating private perception remains intact. The authors propose Visual Intrinsic Privacy Erasure to remove private information from the model rather than just suppressing outputs.

entry.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers

author.name: Benhao Huang, Xuezhe Ma, Hector Liu

entry.summary: This paper shows that feeding top-layer hidden states back into next-position inputs breaks speculative decoding because draft verification requires the predecessor's top-layer state. Feedback Shortcut fixes this with two components: a lightweight trained projection aligning multi-token-prediction-head states to stand-ins without touching base training, and pipelined correction that re-evaluates each draft using its predecessor's newly computed state.

entry.title: eSPG: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Event Speckle Plethysmography

author.name: Aniket Dashpute, Anirudh Bindiganavale Harish, Bhargav Ghanekar, Alankar Kotwal, Andrew Negrut, Syna Gupta, Pablo A. Valdes, Ashok Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: eSPG combines a low-power laser with an event camera to capture speckle fluctuations encoding physiological signals, enabling non-contact heart-rate estimation at 1 km with about 5 bpm mean absolute error under challenging illumination and motion. This is a large leap over prior non-contact vital-sign methods demonstrated at tens of meters. The result has clear implications for remote patient monitoring and rescue operations.

entry.title: GlaucomaMarker - Biomarker-Grounded Glaucoma Vision-Language Model

author.name: Ahammed Sakir Nabil, Sadia Siraz, Nikita Chincholkar, Atalie C. Thompson, Jason Xiao, Theodore Leng, Jennifer I. Lim, Minhaj Nur Alam

entry.summary: The authors propose GlaucomaMarker, a vision-language model framework for glaucoma diagnosis that grounds model reasoning in eleven retinal structural biomarkers derived from public segmentation masks converted into descriptive text. Applied to the RETFound and FLAIR retinal foundation models and trained on 9,778 images yielding 45,190 image-text pairs, the approach shows strong performance on a real-world clinical cohort, addressing the scarcity of clinically meaningful text for glaucoma training.

entry.title: Language models compress human preference geometry while political structure remains prompt-sensitive

author.name: Adolfo Ignacio Fuentes-Jofre, Cristian Candia

entry.summary: Testing synthetic publics built from matched pairwise policy choices of Chilean, French, and Brazilian respondents across three open-weight model families, this study finds no prompt condition jointly reproduces individual choices, population heterogeneity, and political organization. The dominant failure is compression of latent preference space—synthetic participant variance is only 0.4-10.5% of human variance—with political structure remaining highly prompt-sensitive.

entry.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play

author.name: Amitoj Sandhu, Ethan Sick, Omkaar Buddhikot, Nadia Laswi, Wesley Durbano, Nadun Ranawaka, You Liang Tan

entry.summary: ScaleEvals is a reset-free evaluation protocol for generalist robot policies that uses a VLM AutoPrompter to generate scene-grounded tasks and a VLM AutoGrader (90.7% human agreement) to assess progress, aggregating scores with a Bradley-Terry model and tag-stratified ANOVA diagnostics. Across 3,000+ physical rollouts on DROID and YAM robots it achieves 23.0 net rollouts per hour per station, addressing reset, grading, and coverage bottlenecks.

entry.title: SupportChain: Trace-Calibrated Aggregation of Quote-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Multi-Hop RAG with Small Readers

author.name: Zhexi Gu

entry.summary: SupportChain decomposes multi-hop questions into hops, binds each hop's answer to a quoted sentence from retrieved passages, calibrates reliability from execution traces, and aggregates executions by answer support, stopping when support is sufficient. With a 9B reader it achieves 63.0 F1 on MuSiQue, beating the previous best of 59.2 achieved with a 20B reader, and outperforms HippoRAG 2 across five datasets. This shows strong multi-hop RAG is achievable without large readers or expensive corpus-wide LLM indexing.

entry.title: Tight Mistake-Abstention Tradeoffs for Sequential Prediction under Adversarial Injections

author.name: Mo\"ise Blanchard, Ezra Edelman, Surbhi Goel, Shyam Narayanan, Jialin Yu

entry.summary: Resolves open gaps in the mistake-abstention tradeoff for sequential prediction when an adversary injects corrupted instances into an i.i.d. stream, introducing the weighted shattering potential and gap-closing algorithms that essentially characterize the tradeoffs across adversary and information settings.

entry.title: Make Position Uninformative: Exchangeable Self-Distillation Flattens the Lost-in-the-Middle Curve

author.name: Qingsen Ma, Dianyun Wang, Jiahong Liu, Irwin King

entry.summary: Proposes Exchangeable Self-Distillation (ExSD), which trains a small adapter on shuffled contexts to reproduce the model's answer when reading the answer document alone, requiring no gold answers and only a few thousand examples. On six models from 1.5B to 32B, ExSD raises both average and worst-position accuracy, flattening the lost-in-the-middle curve. This is a practical remedy for one of the most persistent and consequential LLM failure modes in retrieval-augmented settings.

entry.title: Multi-Order Passive Macromodeling from Layouts via Nested Port-Hamiltonian Learning

author.name: Benchao Zhu and Keren Zhu

entry.summary: The authors propose an end-to-end framework that maps physical layout graphs directly to multi-order port-Hamiltonian macromodels for interconnects and power-delivery networks, bypassing costly full-wave electromagnetic simulation. A prefix-nested port-Hamiltonian parameterization guarantees passivity and stability by construction rather than post-hoc correction. This supports reliable transient signal- and power-integrity simulation.

entry.title: Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling

author.name: Yaowen Zhang, Chen Chen, Wanyu Lin, Shuo-Hui Li, Ding Pan

entry.summary: TD-FEP is a deep generative framework that learns a temperature-conditioned, invertible mapping between reference and target systems through data-free, energy-based optimization, unifying one-shot state generation with free energy calculation across a continuous temperature range. It is validated across a broad range of physical, chemical, and biological applications.

entry.title: StudioBench: Benchmarking Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models for Productive Audiovisual Creation

author.name: Xinglong Xu, Yuxia Zhu, Siyuan Li, Lixu Tian, Xiaofei Zhao, Yuxin Liu, Caijun Jia, Jintao Chen, Bihui Yu, Alden Cai, Asher Qin, Jingxuan Wei, Cheng Tan

entry.summary: StudioBench evaluates end-to-end audiovisual creation by general multimodal LLMs across 160 tasks in eight genres, requiring models to produce minutes of finished content using 33 generation, editing, and inspection tools without shell access or templates. It analyzes delivered films and reconstructed workflow graphs to diagnose production behavior.

entry.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations

author.name: Suya Li, Zekun Qi, Xiaochong Xu, Duo Zhang

entry.summary: LandWM is a world model of land-surface water where rainfall acts as the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS satellite data with physical observation operators and a mass-conserving balance. It matches operational SMAP Level-4 soil moisture products without ever seeing in-situ soil moisture, and supports counterfactual storm simulation.

entry.title: Consumer-Time Validity in Stateful AI Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State and Deferred Authority

author.name: Guijia Zhang, Huihao Jing, Bing Li, Shing-Chi Cheung, Harry Yang, Ziqi Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies consumer-time validity as a missing check in stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes, where one component records a cancellation, rollback, or approval that another later relies on after state has changed. Demonstrations on vLLM with LMCache show interrupted KV loads leaving stale indexed blocks and GPU desynchronization causing cross-tenant tool-call generation in 10/10 fault runs.

entry.title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent

author.name: Shuyang Xiang

entry.summary: This paper unifies attention-based (H2O) and recency-based (StreamingLLM) KV cache eviction policies as endpoints of a single power-law scoring family indexed by an age-penalty exponent alpha. It shows the exponent is an intrinsic, transferable model property that can be calibrated once on a single corpus, with a companion mechanism bounding its admissible range. This offers a simpler, more principled tuning story for long-context inference efficiency.

entry.title: Grounding Collaborative Agents in Group Cognition

author.name: Zhaoxuan Tan, Mengting Wan, Jingbo Yang, Kwei-Herng Lai, Renyi Qu, Lorenzo Jaime Flores, Meng Jiang, Longqi Yang, Victor Poznanski, Pei Zhou

entry.summary: The paper formulates group briefing, the task of reconstructing task-relevant group cognition (expressed beliefs, group dynamics, grounding gaps) from multi-team interaction histories, and releases a four-domain benchmark of 1,351 requests and 9,975 verified reference points with a two-stage evaluation. It bridges retrieval-of-facts and end-to-end interaction evaluation approaches. This enables direct supervision for agents joining ongoing teams.

entry.title: Recurrent Point Transformer via Test-Time Training

author.name: Wentao Zhou, Xuweiyi Chen, Charles Saunders, Aruni RoyChowdhury, Zezhou Cheng

entry.summary: PoinTTT formulates arbitrary-extent point-cloud segmentation as recurrent sequence-of-chunks processing, augmenting Point Transformer V3 with residual Large Chunk Test-Time Training layers in encoder and decoder. Fast weights act as recurrent state, updated by each chunk and applied to subsequent tokens, avoiding cropping, tiling, and output stitching. This addresses a real mismatch between fixed-size point-cloud encoders and unbounded real-world scans.

entry.title: ViewPACT: Multi-View Geometric Augmentation and Pose-Action Co-Training for Viewpoint-Robust Manipulation

author.name: Chenglang Tu, Feng Chen, Ruizhe Liu, Pei Zhou, Binbin Huang, Chen Xu, Yanchao Yang, Yi Ma, Shenghua Gao

entry.summary: This paper identifies proprioception as a shortcut in image-based robot manipulation policies and introduces ViewPACT, which trains an RGB-only policy with auxiliary geometric supervision of end-effector and object poses. It more than doubles mean success on LIBERO under unseen camera viewpoints (37.4% to 78.4%) and achieves 68.1% across four real-robot tasks.

entry.title: RVLM: Fewer Tokens, Better Resolution Scaling, Fine-Grained Spatial Grounding

author.name: Savya Khosla, Chris Dongjoo Kim, Alex Schwing, Derek Hoiem, Christopher Clark, Sangho Lee

entry.summary: RVLM replaces fixed-grid image tokenization in vision-language models with content-adaptive regions produced by training-free Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher segmentation, pooling ViT patches within each region. The authors identify key properties regions must satisfy (full coverage, spatial connectivity, preserving fine structure like small text) and show benefits in token efficiency, resolution scaling, and fine-grained grounding. Author list includes established VLM researchers.

entry.title: VeriLogic: Reinforcement Learning over Verifiable Logical Reasoning Traces

author.name: ZeLiang Chen, Yunyao Zhang, Xinglang Zhang, Wenbing Li, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces VeriLogic, a reinforcement learning framework that treats intermediate logical reasoning traces as explicit, verifiable learning objects rather than relying solely on outcome-level reward signals. By decomposing reasoning into intermediate judgments, proofs, and final decisions, it enables process-level supervision that can penalize invalid reasoning even when the final answer is correct. This matters because it addresses a well-recognized weakness in RLVR-style training where reward hacking and flawed-but-correct reasoning go unpunished.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Acting: WARD Diagnoses the Evidence-to-State-to-Action Gap in Longitudinal Clinical Agents

author.name: Chao Ding, Yidong Jiang, Junzhi Ning, Juncheng Wu, Yuhan Wang, Renjie Lu, Minjia Yuan, Gaopeng Wang, Liyang Wang, Pengcheng Chen, Dong Yin, Meiping Wang, Jinru Ding, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: WARD is a benchmark of 4,560 clinical tasks across seven output domains, organized into 240 checkpoints from 40 longitudinal clinical trajectories, designed to evaluate how LLM clinical agents translate accumulating evidence into patient-state judgments and safe, timely actions. It includes a Longitudinal Track with controlled cumulative evidence and an Interactive Track for tool-mediated clinical management.

entry.title: DriveOddsBench: Are Driving Video World Models Aligned with Real-World Odds?

author.name: Jiaxi Liu, Keshu Wu, Bin Ran, Xiaopeng Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces DriveOddsBench, a pre-registered benchmark that tests whether sampled futures from driving video world models match real-world probability distributions rather than merely looking realistic. It addresses core evaluation challenges including the one-future-per-history problem, measurement error from reading physical quantities from video, and selective reporting risks. This matters because world model samples are increasingly used for planning and simulation, so probabilistic misalignment could propagate into unsafe downstream decisions.

entry.title: $\zeta_0$: A Framework for World Action Models with Joint Scene and Body Foresight in Humanoid Control

author.name: Yizhi Chen, Zhanxiang Cao, Yitong Wang, Junyu Liu, Hongchu Zeng, Xinyi Peng, Chuxuan Huang, Yicheng Su, Zihao Zhou, Shengcheng Fu, Haoyang Li, Liyun Yan, Tianyue Zhan, Jianming Ma, Yang Zhang, Keqi Zhu, Xiaxi Si, Jinming Yao, Qiao Sun, Shizeng Zhang, Jiangwei Zhong, Yue Gao

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework that converts vision-language-action policies into World Action Models by jointly foreseeing future visual features and joint trajectories in a shared latent space for humanoid robots. A teacher conditioned on recorded futures provides reference action responses during training, and on seven HumanoidArena tasks the approach improves over vision-only foresight baselines.

entry.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Meng-Hao Guo, Yi Zhang, Zhe-Han Mo, Han-Zheng Wang, Jia-Jun Wang, Xin-Sheng Chen, Jiaxi Song, Yi-Xuan Deng, Jia-Ning Li, Xuanyu Chu, Hengrui Zhang, Huan-ang Gao, Yongming Rao, Shi-Min Hu

entry.summary: Motivated by the strong robot-control generalization of the existing GPT-6 Astra model (released September 2026) whose training details are undisclosed, the authors present nanoAstra, an open recipe combining semantic action modeling over parameterized primitives with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning that constrains robot outputs via a system prompt. The goal is reproducible training of vision-language models for generalizable manipulation without degrading pretrained capabilities. It offers a transparent alternative to closed frontier robotics-VLM training.

entry.title: What Test-Time Training Corrects in Latent World Models? A Slow-Fast Approach

author.name: Shuaicheng Niu, Guohao Chen, Kevin Z. Shen, Yunbei Zhang, Peilin Zhao, Yinan Zhang, Cyril Leung

entry.summary: The paper analyzes prediction error in latent world models used for planning, decomposing it on a PushObj task into an action-independent offset and an action-dependent component. It shows that AdaJEPA's test-time training gains are largely (91%) explained by tracking the shared offset, and that episode-specific offsets should not persist across episodes.

entry.title: FLAC: Maximum Entropy RL via Kinetic Energy Regularized Bridge Matching

author.name: Lei Lv, Yunfei Li, Yu Luo, Fuchun Sun, Xiao Ma

entry.summary: FLAC is a likelihood-free framework for maximum entropy reinforcement learning with iterative generative policies (diffusion/flow models), formulating policy optimization as a Generalized Schrodinger Bridge problem relative to a high-entropy reference. Policy stochasticity is regulated by penalizing the kinetic energy of the velocity field, so maximum entropy emerges naturally without explicit action densities.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Hypothesis-Driven Experiment Planning in LLM Agents

author.name: Ryo Kuroki, Amin Mansouri, Philippe Schwaller

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic benchmark for LLM agents doing hypothesis-driven adaptive experimental planning, instantiated in kinetic mechanism identification within closed-world system identification. It evaluates exploration behavior (space-filling vs corner-seeking) and decomposes reasoning into four separately scored steps: belief update, hypothesis discrimination, discriminative experiment design, and predictive reasoning. This moves beyond final-accuracy evaluation toward interpretable failure localization.

entry.title: Attacking Tabular Foundation Models: An Experimental Taxonomy of Context Poisoning and Test-Time Evasion

author.name: Ramak Nassiri, Sujan Kumar Reddy Challa, Feroz Ahmed, Souhail Chakkour, Md Shohel Rana, Aditya Garg, Charan Gudla

entry.summary: This work taxonomizes attacks on in-context tabular foundation models across four families: label flipping, backdoor context poisoning, clean-label context selection, and test-time evasion. Evaluating TabPFN-2.5, TabICL, and XGBoost on intrusion-detection datasets, it finds backdoor context poisoning gives strong targeted control with little clean-accuracy loss, exposing a distinctive vulnerability of in-context learning on tabular data.

entry.title: Grammar Sparsity Sets How Transformers Learn Random Languages

author.name: Edgar Andres Hernandez Moreno, Francesco Cagnetta

entry.summary: Using a Random Language Model with exactly known conditional entropies, this theoretical work shows grammar sparsity governs both the order and speed of transformer language acquisition. Dense grammars are learned level-by-level with plateaus scaling as V^3, while sparse grammars are learned all at once at t proportional to sqrt(V), with exponents derived analytically even for depth-one linear models.

entry.title: What Should World Models Plan Over? Learning Geometry-Aligned Representations of Body Motion

author.name: Renhao Zhang, Abhranil Chandra, Bruno Castro da Silva

entry.summary: MotionPort learns low-dimensional latent representations of body trajectories for world-model planning, arguing that predictive accuracy alone does not make a representation searchable by trajectory optimizers. By organizing the search space by motion similarity, it raises average goal-reaching success from 37.9% to 87.8% across three backbones and seven settings without fine-tuning state encoders.

entry.title: Latent-Predisposition Personas for Heterogeneous and Reliable LLM Survey Simulation

author.name: Geonwoo Bang, Dongho Kim, Moohong Min

entry.summary: The paper shows that persona-conditioned LLMs simulating survey respondents produce over-constrained publics: opinions on unrelated issues are 1.6-4.6 times more correlated than in humans, and common fixes like diversity instructions trade correlation fit for test-retest reliability. The proposed Latent-Predisposition Personas give each simulated person stable latent dispositions, improving heterogeneity and reliability across three model families and three U.S. surveys.

entry.title: Dynamics Forcing: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Causal Video World Models

author.name: Xin Zhou, Cong Miao
