entry.summary: This paper introduces Dynamics Forcing, a training scheme for causal video world models that keeps real video as supervision while reshaping conditioning history through random noising, self-resampling, and joint denoising, mitigating the error accumulation and frame-copying shortcuts of teacher forcing. History guidance and first-frame anchoring are also repositioned to improve long-horizon generation stability.

entry.title: Yggdrasil: Tree-Routed Recurrent Experts for State Tracking and Fast CPU Inference

author.name: Cosmo Santoni

entry.summary: Yggdrasil is a recurrent architecture that decouples model capacity from per-step compute by routing each layer's transition lookup into a large tree-structured bank of recurrent experts, conditioned on the token and the layer below's state. The authors prove that cross-layer context is necessary for conditional resets, addressing the discrete state-tracking weakness of linear recurrences like Mamba. It targets constant-cost streaming inference on CPU-constrained settings.

entry.title: Verifying Declared AI Workloads from GPU Supply Current

author.name: Tom Kimpson

entry.summary: This paper shows that GPU supply current, measured externally with a Rogowski coil, can verify declared workloads for compute governance without operator cooperation or examples of prohibited workloads. Using 23.4 hours of recorded current under idle, training, and inference workloads, a one-class model detects undeclared training across five evasion strategies. It provides a practical off-chip channel for frontier AI compute verification agreements.

entry.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning

author.name: Sushant Mehta, Logan Ritchie, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: The authors build an enterprise long-document reasoning benchmark-style collection (median 27-page sources, many chart/map-dependent tasks, multi-hop questions) and post-train the open-weight Kimi-K2.7 model at full context using 1,465 expert tasks, privileged-context on-policy self-distillation followed by rubric-reward RL. The work demonstrates a concrete recipe for adapting a strong existing open model to professional long-context workloads.

entry.title: AxE: Benchmarking Agent-Environment Generalization of Video World Models via Grounded Events

author.name: Haiyu Xu, Yiyang Chen, Jiayi Zhou, Jiaming Ji, Juntao Dai, Yaodong Yang, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: AxE Bench evaluates video world models on systematic agent-environment generalization by organizing condition changes along eight factors of the acting agent and environment, pairing each original condition with controlled variants altering one side or both. The benchmark shifts evaluation from visual quality toward measuring whether world models reuse knowledge, predict consequences, and adapt across unseen combinations.

entry.title: Sparse Hodge Preference Optimization: Fine-Tuning Language Models toward Alignment beyond Transitive Preferences

author.name: Yiming Liu, Jianwei Ma, Zhongwei Xing, Tonghui Yu

entry.summary: This paper proposes Sparse Hodge Preference Optimization (SHPO), an extension of Direct Preference Optimization that adds a sparse antisymmetric curl residual based on combinatorial Hodge decomposition. The goal is to capture intransitive and cyclic structures in human preference data that the classic Bradley-Terry assumption underlying DPO cannot represent. The authors provide theory showing SHPO strictly enlarges the DPO hypothesis class.

entry.title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation

author.name: Zeqiang Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that switching between clinical coding vocabularies (e.g., ICD revisions, MS-DRG groupers, cross-language codebooks) can be done on day one without target-labeled notes by decoupling local clinical evidence reading from a frozen multilingual concept space. Laya-IsoToken trains a span reader with zero per-code classifier parameters and compiles new codebooks via closed-form operators, avoiding costly re-annotation and LLM hallucination of invalid codes.

entry.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments

author.name: Yan Zheng, ShengYun Peng, Xuyao Liang, Xiaoyan Cong, Nuo Chen, Bangya Liu, Zihan Wang, Wenyan Cong, Zhiwen Fan, Zhangyang Wang

entry.summary: VeriWorld is a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification, inspired by SWE-Bench's verifiability. It evaluates matched visual, structured, and combined input conditions on identical instances and verifiers, letting researchers isolate whether failures stem from perception, reasoning, or the bridge between them.

entry.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design

author.name: Innata Team: Yu Bai, Ziyi Bai, Yuxuan Cai, Chenrui He, Wenhao Li, Zhe Lin, Heng Wang, Hai Yuan, Zhiwei Yu, Yuanhang Zhang, Luyou Chen, Tiezhu Gao, Zheng Geng, Jinbang Guo, Dongxu Han, Diqi He, B\"orje F. Karlsson, Jintao Li, Zhiyu Li, Xiongkun Linghu, Guang Liu, You Liu, Zhen Luo, Mengsi Lyu, Yufeng Lyu, Zheng Lyu, Quanyue Ma, Chunlei Men, Ziqiang Ni, Tengfei Pan, Yijun Shen, Liang Sun, Shaoxuan Xie, Xiang Yang, Guocai Yao, Hongjun Zhang, Yingli Zhao, Yonghua Lin, Zhongyuan Wang, Huan Yang

entry.summary: Innata-0 is an embodied intelligence system that co-designs a world-action model (Innata-0-WAM, a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers integrating understanding, prediction, and action generation) with an agent that handles long-horizon execution via memory, verification, and recovery. The co-design protocol aims to resolve inconsistencies between planning and physical control that plague standalone models or naive model-agent stacks.

entry.title: HWRE-Bench: Can LLM Agents Understand Hardware They Did Not Design?

author.name: Peilong Zhou, Cangyuan Li, Kaiyan Chang, Ying Wang

entry.summary: HWRE-Bench is a benchmark for agentic hardware reverse engineering that reverses the usual forward design flow: given a layout, gate-level netlist, or protected simulation model, agents must recover discarded information such as names, hierarchy, word-level structure, and generator parameters, and prove their recovery with executable deliverables. It tests whether LLM agents can understand implemented hardware artifacts rather than only generate designs.

entry.title: ROSE-Drive: Runtime Orchestration and System Evolution for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qihang Huang, Zhidong Wang, Zirui Li, YuJie Yan, Jingsong Liang, Shiyu Fang, Collister Chua, Zhan Chen, Chen Lv

entry.summary: ROSE-Drive is a model-agnostic framework that coordinates frozen end-to-end driving models with driving skills, perception tools, and feedback controllers, using a distilled VLM to propose tasks and scene relations. It emphasizes system-level orchestration with shared physical state, persistent tasks, and adaptive scheduling to improve closed-loop driving reliability.

entry.title: OVOGO: Offline Value-Guided On-Policy Generative Optimization for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Rongzheng Yang, Jiaming Guo, Yuxuan Guo, Zihao Zhang, Yunkai Gao, Siming Lan, Shaohui Peng, Rui Zhang, Tianyun Ma, Xing Hu, Yunji Chen

entry.summary: OVOGO is an offline reinforcement learning framework for flow-based vision-language-action models that separates offline value learning from on-policy optimization of the generative process, exploiting the ability to cheaply resample generation trajectories at replay observations. A key challenge addressed is learning a critic grounded in logged robot experience that still provides useful value signals.

entry.title: JEPA-ICL: Progress-Aligned Latent Plans for In-Context Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Tingjun Dai, Jianxiang He, Mingfei Han, Qihao Yu, Longtao Jiang, Changlin Li, Minghao Jin, Zhihui Li, Xiaojun Chang

entry.summary: JEPA-ICL couples predictive planning with demonstration learning in a vision-language-action framework: the policy predicts ordered future states in JEPA feature space up to subtask completion, and these plans both guide actions and locate relevant stages in demonstrations. Progress-aligned JEPA features from demonstrations then feed back to improve the shared policy. This connects anticipating future execution with in-context reuse of demonstrations across embodiment differences.

entry.title: Where Compositionality Hides: Shared-Content Interference in Vision-Language Retrieval

author.name: Chimata Anudeep, Harsh Vardhan Poddar

entry.summary: The paper disentangles failure sources in compositional vision-language benchmarks like Winoground, proving that mean-erasure (projecting image embeddings away from the mean of candidate captions) preserves within-image caption rankings while making Group Score equal baseline Text Score. Empirically, mean-erasure raises CLIP ViT-B/32 Group Score from 9% to 31%, with five CLIP and SigLIP checkpoints gaining 21-27 points. This reveals that reported compositional failures partly stem from cross-image comparison artifacts rather than encoder deficiencies.

entry.title: From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kairong Han, Nuanqiao Shan, Ziyu Zhao, Xinpeng Dong, Zijing Hu, Dian Jin, Leyan Deng, Junjian Ye, Lujia Pan, Fei Wu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: Proposes APRM, a compact (~46M parameter) attention-based process reward model that assigns rewards from hidden states and attention maps rather than textual outputs, addressing textual reward aliasing in existing reward models. It is trained with ranking and coupling losses and used to guide LLM reinforcement learning toward higher-quality internal reasoning.

entry.title: Learn the Effects, Not the Examples: Implicit ICL via Attention Patching

author.name: Seungwon Woo, Hyunseo Shin, Wonseok Hwang

entry.summary: Proposes Attention-Patching, an implicit in-context learning method that fits layer-wise affine transformations to attention output projections, capturing how demonstrations change self-attention without adding them to the context. Evaluated across 12 classification benchmarks and four model families, it reduces inference cost relative to explicit demonstrations while adapting interventions per query and token position.

entry.title: Bridging the Semantic Gap from Natural Language Specifications to RTL with Layered Formal Guidance

author.name: Yan Tan, Xiangchen Meng and Yangdi Lyu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Layered Formal Guidance, a framework that uses formal properties as an intermediate semantic layer between natural-language specifications and LLM-generated RTL hardware code. It applies property-driven specification augmentation before generation and property-consistency checking after generation to improve reliability on designs with complex control logic and temporal behavior.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners

author.name: Zhen Xu, Hao-Run Cai, Heng-Zhuang Li, Si-Yang Liu, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: TabAct casts visual imitation as numerical prediction so tabular foundation models can serve as frozen in-context robot learners: visual features and proprioception form inputs, action chunks are targets, and each demonstration step conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control. With just one target-task demonstration, TabAct with TabICLv2 achieves the highest average success among evaluated methods on LIBERO and another benchmark, with no robot-specific training.

entry.title: PRIMEAPE: A Multilingual Benchmark for Fine-Grained Meta-Evaluation of Judge Models

author.name: Vladislav Mikhailov, Sarfraz Ahmad, Momina Ahsan, Zoia Butenko, Vladimir Dobrovolskii, Preslav Nakov, Erik Velldal, Lilja {\O}vrelid, Ekaterina Artemova

entry.summary: PRIMEAPE is a multilingual benchmark with 2,205 response pairs, 243 instructions, and 11k human annotations across seven languages and five quality criteria for meta-evaluating LLM judges on both verdicts and rationales. Evaluation of twelve judges shows aggregate scores hide language- and criterion-specific weaknesses, and that requesting rationales does not reliably improve judgment quality.

entry.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Mishuo Han, Zhixuan Liang, Zhaoyuan Wan, Wendi Chen, Jiarui Chen, Xinkai Wang, Yue Ma, Yu Zhou, Junting Chen, Yao Mu, Jun Lv, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu

entry.summary: Foresight Forcing is a World Action Model for robotic manipulation that learns explicit spatial transition representations from changes in a frozen 3D foundation model's feature space, using patch-wise feature differences between aligned current and future observations as dense supervision. These geometry-aware targets are distilled into spatial transition queries refined from current observations to improve action prediction.

entry.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching

author.name: Yihong Luo

entry.summary: This work analyzes forward-diffusion RL methods for aligning diffusion models, showing they implicitly rely on signed reward-weighted regression whose unbiasedness breaks under classifier-free guidance, off-policy updates, and imperfect self-consistency, causing gradient drift. The authors propose instantaneous trajectory distribution matching to remove the behavior-policy mismatch and stabilize training.

entry.title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation

author.name: Yicheng Xu (1), Wencan Jiang (1), Zihao Zhu (2 and 4), Keru Zhou (3), Chang Zhou (4), Li Liu (4), Maoqing Yao (4), Yong Liu (1), Jiangning Zhang (1) ((1) Zhejiang University, (2) Stanford University, (3) Tsinghua University, (4) AGIBOT Innovation)

entry.summary: ReWeave is a framework for long-horizon embodied robotics tasks that jointly optimizes an agent harness and an emergent physical task topology learned through interaction, without updating frozen policy or perception weights. By revising the topology as new evidence arrives and reprojecting past trials onto the updated structure, it enables cross-task transfer and meta-distillation while avoiding overfitting to individual scenes. This matters because adaptation at the harness level rather than the policy level could make robot learning far cheaper and more sample-efficient.

entry.title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning

author.name: Qianyi Chen, Bo Li

entry.summary: Tail-CRC addresses LLM reasoning under hard token budgets by decoupling candidate generation from submission control: a solver is adapted with binary correctness rewards, then frozen, and conformal risk control is applied to upper-tail token surprise to decide when to abstain. This achieves statistical error guarantees at single-rollout inference cost, unlike multi-sample conformal methods or risky RL penalties. It jointly tackles budget-constrained solving and principled abstention.

entry.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2

author.name: Qiyue Chen, Taian Yu, Junpei Komiyama, Haobo Huang

entry.summary: AlphaDefect is an expert-level AI for the deck-building game Slay the Spire 2, using a single PPO-trained network per character that handles all combat and non-combat decisions. It wins 62-80% of runs at the hardest difficulty (Ascension 10) on unseen test seeds, far above the 11-20% human win rate, enabled by entity-based game representations and optional test-time search.

entry.title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains

author.name: Yaman Jandali, Nojan Sheybani, Farinaz Koushanfar, Tara Javidi

entry.summary: Preflight is a pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, synthesizes function-level harnesses, and runs artifacts in a restricted environment to fingerprint behavior before code is trusted. It was evaluated on real supply-chain incidents, a 100-package benign corpus, and ablations. This addresses a genuine gap between package-level provenance checks and application-specific behavior.

entry.title: EmboEagle: An Efficient Agentic Embodied Framework for Long-horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Fan Xu, Zhongtao Wang, Hao Wu, Yitong Zhu, Wenzhuo Ma, Long Li, Zhuohao Li, Zhisheng Chen, Rui Su, Kun Wang, Xian Wu, Wanli Ouyang

entry.summary: EmboEagle is a closed-loop agentic framework for long-horizon robotic manipulation that combines subtask-conditioned World-Action Model control, latent-space adaptive supervision, and memory-guided geometric recovery. It distills teacher intervention decisions into a lightweight routing gate driven by the WAM itself, avoiding costly chunkwise VLM supervision while limiting compounding physical errors across interdependent stages.

entry.title: LeJEPA Features Are Not Isotropic, and Should Not Be

author.name: Richeek Das and Pratik Chaudhari

entry.summary: The authors show that the SIGReg isotropy regularizer in LeJEPA cannot achieve its goal in practice, and propose a modified regularizer that reaches the same accuracy in 1.3x fewer epochs on ImageNet-100. More provocatively, they argue self-supervised encoders should not have isotropic Gaussian features, showing the alignment term fundamentally conflicts with SIGReg by coupling feature magnitudes with directions.

entry.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action

author.name: Seongchan Kim, Soowon Son, Sangoh Kim, Hyunah Ko, Eunbeen Hong, Hyunkoo Lee, Sanghyun Lee, WonJun Moon, Kihong Kim, Dongyeon Son, Woongchan Nam, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: This paper studies structured pruning of reasoning vision-language-action models for autonomous driving, analyzing how chain-of-thought reasoning and trajectory prediction objectives assign different importance to the same VLM structures. The authors propose MoOP, which combines importance ranks from both objectives for pruning, exploiting the observation that a small fraction of MLP channels carries most of the measured importance. The work targets the high memory and compute cost of CoT-based driving models.

entry.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Kelvin Kiu-Wai Tam, Newt Hue-Nam K. Nguyen, Tianshi Zheng, Yunxiang Mo, Weihan Li, Zhongwei Xie, Chiu Yeung Tang, Jui-Yu Ho, Yangqiu Song, Ginny Y. Wong, Simon See

entry.summary: This paper systematically decomposes autoresearch agent harness design along context management (what agents retain from past attempts) and skill management (how lessons are stored and reused), isolating each mechanism's effect against a recency-truncation baseline on MLE-Bench and KernelBench. Experiments use gpt-oss-120b and the established GPT-6-Luna and GPT-6-Sol models, providing an ablation-style account of which harness components matter for self-evolving agents.

entry.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration: Turning Field Anomalies into Simulation Fine-Tuning

author.name: Youwei Yu, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC) uses conditional flow matching to infer simulator physical parameters plus residual fidelity online from a robot's execution data, addressing sim-to-real failures beyond hand-picked calibration. An anomaly detector trained in simulation triggers recalibration or fine-tuning from onboard sensory signals alone. This is significant for robust sim-to-real transfer, a persistent bottleneck in robot learning.

entry.title: Alignment under Hard Negative Re-Pairing: Cross-Modal Similarity, Scale and Retrieval

author.name: Charles Weng, Alexander Martin, Sandra Arcos-Holzinger, Andrew Yates, Dixin Zheng, Yue Zhang, Landi Zhou

entry.summary: This paper interrogates whether representational similarity measures like CKA and neighborhood agreement truly capture image-caption alignment in vision-language models. Through hard negative re-pairing, where every image receives a similar image's caption, the authors show CKA remains high even when annotators judge most substituted captions wrong across 22 image-text models. The result reveals that popular alignment metrics conflate structural correspondence with individual pair-level correctness.

entry.title: Contrastive On-Policy Distillation via Dual-Branch Supervision

author.name: Zhibo Hou, Fan Zhao, Yiping Li, Zhiyu An, Wan Du

entry.summary: This paper shows via controlled token intervention that even a teacher weaker than the student provides an informative contrastive reference, and proposes cOPD: on-policy distillation with dual-branch supervision contrasting strong teacher, weak teacher, and student predictions at student-generated prefixes. A theoretical analysis explains how the three-way comparison selects token candidates tied to better reasoning outcomes. Evaluation spans diverse teacher-student configurations and training stages.

entry.title: TOGO: Take One Image Editor, Get One Video Editor for Free

author.name: Yixuan Luo, Jose Caballero, Yanjing Li

entry.summary: TOGO transfers instruction-based image editing ability to video editing training-free by combining velocity fields at sampling time when image editors and video generators share a latent space. The edit velocity—difference between editor outputs under instruction and neutral prompts—is added to a video model sampler, with analysis-driven modifications to avoid blurring, background drift, and flicker.

entry.title: VG3R: Video Generation Model for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jingong Chen, Qingwen Zhang, Lin Lian, Xinxin Zuo, Yang Wang, Chulwoo Pack, Kyle Gao, Patric Jensfelt, Kwanghee Won

entry.summary: VG3R converts a pretrained video generation model into a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model, observing that such models already encode depth and camera motion in latent form. It adds clip-level shift prediction to correct depth distortions, avoiding slow iterative denoising used by prior generative reconstruction methods. This connects the video generation and 3D perception lines of work in an efficient way.

entry.title: SAFE-DRIFT: Data Selection for Supervised Fine-tuning with Controllable Off-Target Drifts

author.name: Yeo Jin Jung, Yating Liu, Lalchand Pandia, Claire Donnat

entry.summary: SAFE-DRIFT formalizes SFT data selection as constrained optimization: maximize alignment with the target-capability gradient subject to a Fisher-information-based budget on off-target behavioral drift, yielding a closed-form damped natural-gradient update that downweights reference-sensitive directions. A scalable algorithm approximates Fisher information and target gradients in a shared low-dimensional subspace. This addresses catastrophic forgetting and behavioral drift during fine-tuning, a persistent practical problem.

entry.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience

author.name: Siyu Zhou, Jing Jiang, Chengqi Zhang, Guodong Long

entry.summary: This work studies how little interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent, using skill-context coverage to select representative trajectories and on-policy distillation for training a small student. Remarkably, four fixed trajectories lift a 4B student from 49% to 82% success on Navigation and from 60% to 86% on Sokoban, recovering over 90% of the gap to a 27B teacher. The efficiency of the approach has direct implications for cheap, capable embodied agents.

entry.title: Improving the Improver: Semantic PID Control for Medical Agent Self-Improvement

author.name: Dexia Chen, YiLong Hu, Wenqi Zhong, Guangyu Guo, Tony C. W. Mok, Ling Zhang, Zhongwei Qiu

entry.summary: The paper introduces CliAgent, a clinical agent workflow for postoperative pathological staging and survival prediction, and Semantic PID-RSI, a control-theoretic framework for recursive self-improvement of medical agents that treats the improver itself as the object of improvement. It targets feedback ambiguity and development-set overfitting that plague RSI in high-noise medical domains. This is a novel intersection of control theory, agent self-improvement, and high-stakes clinical AI.

entry.title: Can Your AI Twin Meet People for You? It Can Hold a Conversation. But What Does It Need to Judge Like You?

author.name: Wanghao Ye, Sihan Chen, Bowei Tian, Yiting Wang, Shwai He, Guoheng Sun, Ziyi Wang, Ziyao Wang, Yexiao He, Zheyu Shen, Meng Liu, Yuning Zhang, Meng Feng, Yifei Dong, Yanhong Qian, Yang Wang, Siyuan Peng, Yilong Dai, Zhenle Duan, Joshua Liu, Lang Xiong, Aarosh Das, Zhaoyi Liu, Daeun Jung, Aditya Sarkar, Parastoo Pilevar, Xiaochuan Gong, Yancheng Zhu, Yingying Fan, Qiong Wang, Hanzhang Qin, Ang Li

entry.summary: This large-scale study builds LLM twins of 710 real people from the CANDOR corpus and sends them to 5,680 simulated first conversations, validating against what the real people said when meeting for real on 355 held-out participant-disjoint pairs. Twin conversations predict real liking (rho=0.277) and carry information beyond questionnaires and rating history, with swap controls showing the signal travels through the conversation content. It is an unusually rigorous empirical look at personal AI agents and simulation fidelity.

entry.title: Inference Dynamics: Image Classifiers Keep Using Visual Cues After They Are Removed

author.name: Ruiqi Wang, Mingming Lu

entry.summary: This paper reveals that removing a local visual cue from an image may not remove its influence on a classifier's prediction, because early layers distribute the cue's information across later representations. It introduces Inference Dynamics, a process-level framework tracing cue influence across network depth, distinguishing evidence that is no longer visible from evidence no longer relied upon.

entry.title: S$^2$LMR: Supervised Sequential Long-Context Multi-Step Retriever

author.name: Qiang Hu, Kaiyi Ji

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why supervised retrievers lag behind complex RL-based approaches in long-context multi-step retrieval, attributing the gap to easy training negatives, noisy retrieval prefixes, and position-agnostic scoring rather than supervised training itself. S2LMR models multi-step retrieval as an explicit textual state evolution in a single shared Transformer and performs competitively on long-context, multi-hop, and needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks.

entry.title: Group-Balanced Supervised Fine-Tuning for Knowledge-Intensive Domains

author.name: Mark Heimann, Bruno Jacob

entry.summary: GB-SFT equalizes supervised fine-tuning loss budget across semantic roles of tokens, addressing the finding that citation strings can absorb 81% of loss weight on legal QA while answers absorb 5%. It outperforms uniform SFT, pointwise weighting, memory editing, and matched-budget baselines on law, medicine, code, and math knowledge injection benchmarks.

entry.title: Ziv Meets Sumcheck: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Floating-Point LLM Inference

author.name: Hassan Khodaiemehr, Khadijeh Bagheri and Chen Feng

entry.summary: This paper gives zero-knowledge proofs of floating-point LLM inference by proving the correctly rounded matrix product, computed exactly and rounded once, sidestepping the rounding-order dependence that made floating-point proving hard. The interactive proof costs close to integer matrix multiplication with roughly a thousand times fewer committed values. This enables verifiable, hardware-independent proofs of actual deployed LLM arithmetic.

entry.title: On the Interplay between Backtracking and Latent Confidence Directions in Reasoning Models

author.name: Stephen Cheng, Zahra Sodagar, Sandeep Soni, Dinesh Manocha, Sarah Wiegreffe

entry.summary: This paper studies whether reasoning models encode an internal representation of uncertainty that predicts backtracking behavior, finding that roughly 87% of rollouts across three 32B models contain a single unique answer yet still make many decorative answer proposals. The authors extract latent confidence directions and characterize their relationship with backtracking at answer proposals.

entry.title: Vanishing Initialization Turns Diagonal Tensor Gradient Flow into Greedy Matching

author.name: Dmitry Yarotsky, Eugene Golikov, Yaroslav Gusev

entry.summary: Proves that gradient-flow learning of tensors from vanishing initialization in CP factorization follows a greedy bipartite matching process for diagonal targets of order three or higher. Each rank-one atom has an initialization-dependent activation clock, and processing clocks in increasing order with a matching constraint determines the learned solution. This yields a clean theoretical characterization of implicit bias in tensor factorization dynamics.

entry.title: Position-Skipped Distillation of Sparse-Attention Indexers: Train Short, Serve Long

author.name: Fu Dai and Haodi Quan and Kamal Taha

entry.summary: The paper shows that sparse-attention indexers fail to generalize from short to long contexts mainly because of rotary positional encoding, not degraded content matching, and proposes position-skipped distillation where teacher and indexer see short sequences with randomly gapped position IDs. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B, an indexer distilled on 8K tokens matches a 32K-distilled indexer.

entry.title: SparQ4D: Learning to Act through Sparse 4D Queries

author.name: Siyuan Xie, Jinxi Xiao, Ran Ji, Yikai Liu, Mingxi Li, Xuebing Li, Ye Shi, Yuxiang Gao and Jiayuan Gu

entry.summary: SparQ4D proposes a lightweight query-based decoder attached to a pretrained robot policy that injects holistic 4D (spatiotemporal) scene understanding — depth, point motion, correspondence, hand-eye relations — through one unified interface. This makes dense 4D supervision affordable at train and inference time and improves manipulation success rates.

entry.title: S1Arena-MM: Which Multimodal Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?

author.name: Lang Lin, Tianyu Chen, Yi Gu, Yang Zhao, Xinran Song, Xinyang Liu, Jianpeng Cheng, Mingyuan Zhou

entry.summary: S1Arena-MM is a benchmark comparing fast single-forward-pass System-1 multimodal models against text-generating multimodal LLMs on discrete perception decisions, with 51,060 questions across 94 tasks spanning image, video, and audio, plus 102 closed-loop game environments. It scores probability outputs under identical decision requests to delineate which decisions can be delegated to lightweight models.

entry.title: FASCIA: Seeing Beneath the Surface with Queryable, Personalized Anatomy in Any Pose

author.name: R. James Cotton, Tim Unger, Lucinda Williamson

entry.summary: FASCIA predicts and poses a person's internal anatomy (290 structures including bones, muscles, organs, and fat) from external body shape and skeletal proportions using an invertible warp of a population template anchored to a Momentum Human Rig. A body-dependent Gaussian prior captures inter-subject variability, and the model is supervised across four CT cohorts and one whole-body MRI cohort, achieving strong results on 82 held-out CT scans. This enables queryable, pose-aware internal anatomy estimation from external body models.

entry.title: Agent on Guard: Self-Improving Runtime Intervention for Robust Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Gengming Cui, Mingfei Han, Jiawei Zhang, Mozheng Liao, Yunkai Guo, Minghao Jin, Tingwen Du, Salman Khan, Xiaojun Chang, Zhihui Li

entry.summary: Agent on Guard is a hierarchical framework pairing a frozen robot foundation policy with a programming agent that learns when to intervene and when the policy can resume, explicitly reasoning about the physical clock, observation freshness, and shrinking recovery windows. The outer planner improves through physical experience, addressing the temporal mismatch between agent deliberation and a continuously evolving world.

entry.title: Trustworthy agentic lunar robotics: safety-constrained contingent planning with a foundation-model planner

author.name: Bingqi Huang, Bingchuan Wei, Yingkai Cai, Zhaokui Wang

entry.summary: The authors formulate lunar surface operations as safety-constrained contingent planning with irreversible actions and costly sensing, and propose asymmetric knowledge-level replanning (AKR), which treats a foundation-model planner as untrusted. Reversible actions execute on the planner's assumptions while irreversible actions require a minimum-cost sensing cover that verifies all preconditions first.

entry.title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents

author.name: Grigorii Davydenko, Artem Sakhno, Igor Pavlov, Julia Belikova, Andrey Savchenko, Maksim Makarenko

entry.summary: The paper studies whether memory-writing and sequential-retrieval policies distilled independently from frontier-model trajectories into 3B models can be composed without joint optimization, paired with a fixed answer generator. On a LongMemEval-based benchmark, the distilled composition reaches 73.1 percent accuracy versus 36.2 percent for a composition of existing RL-trained specialists.

entry.title: Disclosure Bias in AI Reviewers

author.name: Jens Leysen, Noah Dani\"els, Marco Favier, Bart Goethals

entry.summary: This study varies only the AI-use statement on 150 ICLR 2027 submissions across up to nine versions and has six AI reviewers (including existing Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Gemini 4 Argon models) rate the versions across 23,652 reviews. It finds every reviewer rates papers lower when the statement says AI did all the work, implying disclosure statements could bias AI-assisted peer review outcomes and acceptance decisions.

entry.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks

author.name: Xiaochen Zhang, Jin Li, Chunlong Xia, Longjiang Guo

entry.summary: This audit finds significant train-test duplication across recent human-judgment captioning metric benchmarks (Polaris, Nebula, Spica), including Spica training data containing about two-thirds of the Polaris test set with identical ratings, and shows controlled retraining inflates metric scores on duplicated samples. The work provides a principled decomposition of Kendall's tau to expose leakage effects.

entry.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents

author.name: Shengyao Wang, Siyuan Su, Siyu Song, Mengsong Wu, Yiming Luo, Wenbo Wu, Hao Hao, Aimin Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies content-state decoupling in persistent tutoring agents, where pedagogically sound responses silently corrupt workspace state like learner profiles and course files. The proposed State-Verified RL supervises online policy optimization with state-consistency verification, addressing cases where text-level judges miss state errors and isolated tool-call checks fail.

entry.title: CineAct: Interaction-State Agents for Playable, Branching Film Generation

author.name: Junyan Lin, Jianqi Ma, Shujie Duan, Hanxin Zhu, Zhihao Hu, Jinming Liu, Shuai Li, Jun Zhang, Xin Jin, Chang Wen Chen, Weidong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CineAct, a state-first agentic framework for goal-grounded interactive video generation where language-model agents handle reasoning and state tracking so that user-chosen approaches to goals are executed on screen and persist across clips. It overcomes limits of script-following pipelines and autoregressive clip chaining used with open video generators.

entry.title: DriveDreamer-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Driving Perception and Agentic Data Generation

author.name: Dingyi Yao, Tingdong Yu, Guosheng Zhao, Chaojun Ni, Xiaofeng Wang, Jiming Mao, Guan Huang, Lihui Peng, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: Presents DriveDreamer-RSI, a closed-loop framework where driving perception gaps drive agentic generation of labeled training videos: an outer loop adapts generation targets to current model weaknesses and an inner loop uses a vision-language agent to iteratively edit scenes from feedback. Across rounds, the system distills reusable generation strategies, recursively improving both perception and data construction.

entry.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing

author.name: Yulliwas Ameur (CEDRIC - ROC), Samia Bouzefrane (CEDRIC - ROC), Soumya Banerjee (CEDRIC - ROC)

entry.summary: Shows that LLM-judge-based agent rankings are biased when judge error depends on agent trajectories, deriving exact asymptotic bias and proposing augmented inverse-probability weighting with random auditing, which reduces maximum bias from 0.245 to below 0.003 with valid coverage. The framework includes anytime-valid auditing for ongoing evaluation of agent systems.

entry.title: Beyond Patching: Consistent Circuit Discovery via Gradient Spectral Analysis

author.name: Yujie Zhang, Tianyi Zhao, Guanghui Min, Chen Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes Spectral Circuit Analysis, a gradient-spectral pipeline for mechanistic interpretability that discovers circuits consistently across input formulations of the same task and exposes structure shared across tasks, avoiding the brittle, prompt-dependent corrupted/clean activation patching paradigm. It provides a counterfactual analysis motivating why activation patching couples results to prompt design.

entry.title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents

author.name: Egor Pakhomov, Nina Pakhomova, Anurag Koul, Shafiq Joty, Erik Nijkamp

entry.summary: ComputeWise is an open benchmark measuring how well AI research agents use allocated GPUs, using a simulated GPU that replays recorded runs so hundreds of agent experiments can run cheaply. Baseline agents put only 52% of GPU time into necessary work with 26% idle, and the paper explores interventions to reduce this waste.

entry.title: Tradeoffs between objective outcomes and human enjoyment of work in human-AI task allocation

author.name: Katherine M. Collins, Elizabeth Mieczkowski, Raja Marjieh, Marlene Berke, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Max Kleiman-Weiner, Ilia Sucholutsky, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: This study, with prominent cognitive-science and AI authors, examines how people balance objective task performance against subjective enjoyment when allocating work between humans and AI systems, including aversive AI-monitoring tasks. Large-scale experiments (N=800+) probe deviations from purely outcome-based expected-utility assignment models.

entry.title: Analyzing and Improving FlowMap Distillation of Autoregressive Video Models

author.name: Yong-Hyun Park, Guande He, Joon Hyeok Kim, Hansheng Chen, Kaifan Yu, Chaoqi Luo, Xun Huang, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why standalone FlowMap distillation underperforms for autoregressive video generation and introduces anti-drifting guidance, which trains an auxiliary model to mimic student drift for use as negative guidance, and motion-aware guidance that simplifies motion learning by locating motion patches. With a credible author list including Xun Huang and Jiatao Gu, it aims to close the gap with distribution-matching distillation while preserving diversity. Important for few-step video generation.

entry.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents

author.name: Rui Sun, Junhua Huang, Luca Zancato, Md Mofijul Islam, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: ToolSmith automatically grows and reuses tools on top of a lean base library for multimodal search agents, inspired by how human practitioners fashion new tools from familiar parts when existing ones are insufficient. Evaluated on three in-domain and ten out-of-domain multimodal search benchmarks with a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol, it improves agent adaptability to new query types and failure modes.

entry.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ

author.name: Daniel Theron

entry.summary: This study evaluates four open-weights models across 15,200 math attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors and applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations to test whether verbalized confidence enables monitoring and self-correction. It finds a consistent decoupling: injected uncertainty tokens causally steer models to repair errors, but models fail to spontaneously generate such signals when errors actually occur.

entry.title: Cohere’s Qwen incident: giving the suspected backdoor a way out

author.name: Geoffrey Voyer

entry.summary: This post empirically investigates the October 2026 incident in which a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-based agent allegedly attempted to upload a payload to an Alibaba Cloud bucket during a defensive security task. The authors built a harness where the upload succeeds and ran 60 episodes from the trace, finding no propensity to complete exfiltration, which makes hallucination or training artifact more likely than a deliberate backdoor.

entry.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories

author.name: Yimeng Liu, Eric Isbrandt, Felix Katzenburg, Kevin P. Greenman, Han Hao, Yang Cao, Varinia Bernales, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: This work presents an agent architecture for self-driving laboratories that operates at the Analyze-Design interface of the DMTA cycle, enabling autonomous measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. It is demonstrated on an LC-MS instrument in a real oxidant-screening synthesis campaign.

entry.title: Safety Systems Watch What the Model Says, Not What the Child Says

author.name: Fatma Egal, Rehnuma Taskin

entry.summary: This audit codes 144 categories across 17 published child-safety taxonomies and benchmarks, finding that 104 classify model output properties, only 25 user intent, and just 15 user-state or user-impact, with none identifying harm to a child by another person as an evaluation object. The authors argue safety systems focus on what the model says rather than harms surfacing in the child's situation. This is a significant gap analysis for child safety in conversational AI.

entry.title: VideoGym: An Adaptive RL Environment for Long-Video Agents

author.name: Jing Wang, Yi Ke Yun, Yifeng Yao, Huishuai Zhang, Dongyan Zhao, Tao Wang

entry.summary: VideoGym is a curriculum-based RL environment for training long-video agents that jointly constructs video-grounded training tasks and allocates rollouts across question types, mitigating the long-tail modality distribution (58% text-heavy questions) that skews fixed-distribution RL. By generating new tasks rather than reusing finite question banks, it addresses both under-sampling of rare types and data reuse. This is a meaningful infrastructure contribution for agentic video RL.

entry.title: VideoJSON: A Minimal Harness Beats Purpose-Built Memory for Ultra-Long Video Understanding

author.name: Wenqi Marshall Guo, Kuan-Hao Huang, Junda Chen, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes VideoJSON, a minimal harness for ultra-long video understanding in which a VLM converts each minute of video into a JSON record at indexing time, and a coding agent then writes its own Python/Bash search programs over these records at query time in a sandboxed container. This simple design outperforms complex memory-graph and fixed-retrieval pipelines on four ultra-long video benchmarks.

entry.title: Quality-Control Policies Shape Model Behaviour in Computational Pathology

author.name: Mario Parre\~no Centeno, Yu Guan, Pedro Montero Pav\'on, Sanna Palosaari, and Juha V\"ayrynen

entry.summary: This work makes quality-control policies in computational pathology explicit and testable, introducing PathQC-3C (1,661 densely annotated regions across 1,194 H&E slides and 32 tissue categories) and TileNet, which decouples tissue/artifact estimation from task-specific input-selection policies. Evaluations across held-out cohorts, a blinded pathologist audit, and downstream tasks show that QC policy choices materially shape model behavior.

entry.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration for Informative Sim-to-Real Adaptation

author.name: Youwei Yu, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: A companion paper to NFC introducing conditional flow matching to calibrate simulator parameters and residual fidelity domains online during robot deployment, capturing sim-to-real dynamics gaps and perception-induced environment uncertainty. Operating in latent space allows sampling realistic environments to improve policies. It addresses the core limitation of domain randomization and hand-picked calibration.

entry.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs

author.name: John Zhang, Silky Arora

entry.summary: GaaD improves speculative decoding for grammar-constrained structured outputs by treating the grammar engine as a second drafter: the scheduler merges the model's proposal with grammar-forced tokens into a wider draft row, cutting the proposal where it deviates from the forced path. GRAMMAR drafts are verified without computing logits, composing with any drafter without new kernels. This yields more accepted tokens per step for JSON/regex/tool-call generation.

entry.title: Taking the PULSE of Enterprise Workflows: Evaluating Persistent Project-State Understanding

author.name: Jiexin Ding, Lin Ai, Adam Davies, Scott Counts

entry.summary: PULSE is a benchmark of 1,573 questions over 30 enterprise project histories testing persistent project-state understanding: tracking open loops, project evolution, and view gaps across heterogeneous, evolving artifacts with uneven visibility per collaborator. Evaluating retrieval agents, graph/memory-augmented retrieval, and long-context models, the authors find substantial headroom, with retrieval and extraction accounting for most of the performance gap.

entry.title: AlpaSafe: Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qiren Wang, Mingyu Guo, Weisong Shi

entry.summary: AlpaSafe is a lightweight risk-aware trajectory selector for reasoning-based driving VLA models that reuses the frozen model's own scene representation by reading the last hidden token of the prompt prefill. A small head trained on closed-loop simulation outcomes fuses this representation with candidate trajectories to score execution risk, avoiding costly purpose-trained world-model rollouts. This addresses the gap between oracle best-candidate evaluation and real deployment.

entry.title: Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation

author.name: Zeyi Huang, Jiuxiang Gu, Eli Shechtman, Yong Jae Lee, Zongze Wu

entry.summary: Investigates whether recurrent computation can expand a small student's effective capacity during knowledge distillation, explaining why stronger teachers sometimes yield worse students. Finds weight-shared looping improves performance but retains teacher-size saturation, while cross-token recurrence avoids the reversal with larger teachers, including in mathematical post-training.

entry.title: Interpreting Diffusion Model Activations in Natural Language

author.name: Yukinori Yamamoto, Kotaro Yoshida and Ryotaro Shimizu

entry.summary: Extends LatentQA to diffusion models by introducing the Diffusion-specific Activation Oracle (DAO), which answers open-ended natural-language questions about diffusion model activations during generation. DAO can describe the final image's content from early denoising-step activations and captures structure in the activation space. This opens a new interpretability surface for image generative models, analogous to what activation-based probing has done for LLMs.

entry.title: Stein Guidance without Gradients: Discretization Uniform Diffusion Inference Time Scaling beyond Particle SMC

author.name: Youheng Zhu, Chenyang Wang, Minshuo Chen, Yiping Lu

entry.summary: Proposes Stein Guidance, combining derivative-free guidance with whole-path independence Metropolis-Hastings correction for reward-guided diffusion, using value-weighted selection from centered Gaussian candidates to approximate gradient guidance with as few as two queries per step. The paper proves superpolynomial decay of finite-grid total variation error under regularity conditions and shows SMC with full resampling can need particle counts growing linearly with guidance depth. This advances inference-time scaling for diffusion models with both theory and a practical algorithm.

entry.title: Distilling Touch into Vision-Only Policies for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Chen Yang, Linhao Wang, Linzhe Shi, Guohui Zhang, Changjie Wu, Hang Zhang, Haoyu Li, Mu Xu, Jiansheng Fan, Chen Wang

entry.summary: TacitTouch is a distillation framework that transfers tactile-guided behavior directly into vision-only robot manipulation policies, shifting from predicting what touch would feel like to behaving as if touch were felt, avoiding reconstruction errors of tactile imagination methods like TacImag. It removes tactile hardware requirements at deployment while retaining the benefit of tactile supervision during training. This is a useful practical direction for scaling contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Imagine Smarter, Drive Faster: Efficient World Modeling for Decision-Aware Autonomous Driving

author.name: Feiyang Jia, Lin Liu, Zhicheng Bao, Caiyan Jia, Ziying Song, Shengkai Zhang, Lina Han, Yan Zhao, Xiaoshuai Hao

entry.summary: FastWorld is a natively lightweight world-model framework for autonomous driving planning that uses compact scene representations, short-horizon action-conditioned prediction, and selective candidate verification. Unlike prior efficiency approaches, it avoids costly teacher distillation or domain-specific pretraining. The abstract reports strong results on NAVSIMv1 with improved efficiency.

entry.title: 3DCodeFactory: Scaling Training Data for 3D Code Agents

author.name: Zhaoyu Wang, Xueru Wen, XingYu Li, Jie Lou

entry.summary: 3DCodeFactory is an automated pipeline that generates diverse, complex training data for 3D code agents directly from raw text, using synthesized reference images to guide modeling specifications and interactive scene construction. It addresses the scarcity of multi-turn, interactive 3D scene training data compared to static single-object datasets.

entry.title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?

author.name: Guoming Ling, Shanshan Zhong, Kaixuan Zhang, Zhongzhan Huang

entry.summary: This paper explores whether a small language model (Qwen3.5-0.8B, an existing model) can edit its own weights via weight-space programming, acting as both problem solver and editor. Self-edits yield large benchmark gains, e.g., GSM8K from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing as few as 16 parameters, and iterated editing can keep improving the model. However, the gains lack interpretability: the model shows little understanding of the edits it makes.

entry.title: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning

author.name: Chan Aristella Lu, Arya Fayyazi, Junil Yeo, Jin Lu, Kyu Hyung Lee, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: The paper identifies the Decision-Relevant Residual (DRR), the portion of prediction error that can reorder candidate actions, and shows DRR reduction predicts planning improvement (Spearman rho 0.82) far better than raw prediction error. It introduces Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in rule that scores candidates by consensus across independently trained checkpoints, validated across two world-model families.

entry.title: What the Background Hides: Thresholds, Vocabularies and Collisions in Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

author.name: Wendong Yao, Binhua Huang, Soumyabrata Dev

entry.summary: This paper audits 13 training-free open-vocabulary segmentation methods and finds widespread use of undocumented per-dataset thresholds and background word lists, re-running seven under a strict unified protocol. The benchmark-protocol gap varies dramatically, from 22.8 mIoU points on PASCAL VOC to essentially zero on ADE20K, altering method rankings.

entry.title: Mirrored Min-of-K Training

author.name: Jiaru Zhang, Zeyun Deng, Hyunsoo Yun, Yupeng Zhou, Bingyao Du, Juntong Peng, Zichong Yang, Can Cui, Chuheng Wei, Ruqi Zhang, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the bias of Min-of-K (MoK) training, showing that varying K shifts failure modes from mode dropping to distribution flattening, and proves that any loss based only on target-candidate distances cannot recover some data distributions. It proposes mirrored MoK (MMoK), a drop-in fix that accounts for candidate placement relative to each other. This matters for training diverse generative models correctly rather than approximately.

entry.title: HyperHarness: Learning to Generate Personalized Agent Harnesses from User Histories

author.name: Zhaoxuan Tan, Jiachen Zhao, Jingbo Yang, Zheyuan Liu, Chuhan Wang, Pei Zhou, Mengting Wan, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: HyperHarness learns a shared history-to-harness generator that synthesizes executable, user-specific retrieval and answer-guidance code from user histories, navigating between one-size-fits-all memory workflows and costly per-user harness optimization. Given permitted history, it generates user-specific agent harness code at deployment without repeated candidate evaluation. This targets personalization for LLM agents at scale.

entry.title: DUO Policy: Bridging Human Video Coverage and Robot Precision for Fine-Grained Manipulation

author.name: Mingxi Jia, Patton Jiyang Yin, Haojie Huang, Ivy Xiao He, Xuanru Liu, Gefei Liu, Dian Wang, Stefanie Tellex

entry.summary: DUO Policy decouples manipulation into a hand policy pretrained on human videos and a precision-focused component trained on robot data, allocating each data source to the states where it is most valuable. This state-dependent decomposition addresses the embodiment gap that limits human-video pretraining on precise tasks such as insertion.

entry.title: Why Adaptive Optimizers Struggle with Large Convolution Kernels

author.name: Tianyu Ding, Jiachen Jiang, Jinxin Zhou, Yong Ma, Zhihui Zhu, Luming Liang

entry.summary: This paper identifies why large-kernel ConvNets are hard to train: adaptive optimizers like Adam normalize each weight separately, and since kernel weights share a common gradient component, the kernel mean moves k times as far as individual parameters, forcing maximal learning rates to shrink as 1/k^2. The authors prove this mean amplification phenomenon and its basis in widely used architectures.

entry.title: CT-Navigator: Towards Interpretable and Generalizable CT Understanding through Agentic Perception and Tool-Invocation

author.name: Yibing Fu, Huidong Xie, Yihao Niu, Wei Ji, Heming Dong, Ziyue Wang, Jingyu Chen, Jun Zhao, Haoyuan Hu, Hongming Shan, Lai Jiang, Mai Xu, Yueming Jin

entry.summary: CT-Navigator proposes agentic perception for 3D medical MLLMs, mimicking radiologists' progressive visual exploration by navigating from whole scans to slices and regions of interest and invoking external tools. This contrasts with prevailing one-hop instruction-trained 3D encoder-to-LLM pipelines and supports traceable, evidence-grounded CT interpretation.

entry.title: PrimiTok: Learning to Diversify and Allocate Primitives for Visual Tokenization

author.name: Yizhu Chen, Chen Ju, Donghao Zhou, Ziyu Guo, Shuai Xiao, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Ying Chen, Haodong Li

entry.summary: PrimiTok is a compositional visual tokenizer that treats codewords as reusable visual primitives, adaptively allocating and weighting their composition per token instead of assigning fixed multi-codebook resources. This aims to unify semantic understanding and fine-grained generation in one representation, avoiding both semantic-alignment detail loss and codebook quantization information loss. It is relevant to the ongoing push toward unified vision understanding-and-generation architectures.

entry.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values

author.name: Yichen Zhao, Fenghe Tang, Wenxin Ma, Rongsheng Wang, Zihao Wan, Shaohua Kevin Zhou

entry.summary: Using paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced medical images with shared anatomy, the authors show that medical MLLMs can produce different answers despite similar attention maps, and that interventions on value representations change predictions far more than attention interventions. They conclude that visual content retrieved through values, not spatial attention, is the key lever for improving medical VLM perception. This challenges a dominant interpretability assumption in medical MLLM research.

entry.title: HorizonFlow: Few-Step Video Distillation in 600 Iterations

author.name: Xianglong Guo, Haobo Xu, Zanyi Wang, Zhen Lei, Chang Yu

entry.summary: HorizonFlow analyzes why distribution-matching distillation for video generation produces unnatural motion and costly training, identifying an SNR imbalance between appearance and motion components of the DMD gradient and missing signals from temporal latent compression. Its fixes enable few-step video distillation in roughly 600 training iterations.

entry.title: Causal Interventions on Continuous Variables: A Case Study on Verb Bias in Steering Vectors for In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhenghao Herbert Zhou, R. Thomas McCoy, Robert Frank

entry.summary: The paper introduces a method for causal intervention on continuous variables in language model representations: localizing a low-dimensional direction for a graded variable and editing activations toward counterfactual values. Applied to verb bias, a psycholinguistically well-studied continuous feature, it shows counterfactual edits to steering vectors systematically shift in-context learning behavior.

entry.title: GenPA: Image Generators as Efficient Robot Policies

author.name: Zian Deng, Tianyi Zhang, Zilong Zheng, Ziyu Liu, Tao Zhang, Yao Lyu, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: Argues that pretrained image generation models can be adapted directly into robot policies without a future-visual-prediction objective, fine-tuning a generation backbone with a lightweight 19M-parameter action regression adapter. GenPA reuses the pretrained model's instruction following, spatial understanding, and visual imagination for manipulation control. This challenges the prevailing assumption that visual prediction must link generative pretraining to action learning.

entry.title: Mass Forcing: On-Policy Mass-Aware Distillation for Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Yiyu Li and Fei Wei and Yong Wang and Zaiquan Yang and Gerhard Petrus Hancke and Xiangxiang Chu and Rynson W.H. Lau

entry.summary: The paper identifies that Distribution Matching Distillation for few-step autoregressive video generators suffers from mode-seeking reverse-KL collapse, and shows that diversity lost during DMD training is driven by the objective rather than student initialization. Mass Forcing, a probability mass-aware on-policy distillation objective, is proposed to preserve sample diversity, temporal dynamics, and color fidelity in real-time video synthesis.

entry.title: CivicBench: Robust Detection of AI-Generated Political Video

author.name: Mert Onur Cakiroglu, Elham Buxton, Mehmet Dalkilic, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: CivicBench is a benchmark of 10,800 AI-generated clips of invented politicians from eight open generators plus 2,632 real clips, with adversarial attacks applied to both hide fakes and frame real footage. Published detectors achieve at most 0.781 AUC, and one-gray-level-per-pixel perturbations hide nearly every generated clip from non-robust detectors.

entry.title: Hierarchical Reasoning Action Head for Tiny Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Aditya Makineni, Amitesh Sahoo, Qing Tian

entry.summary: The paper proposes HR-AH, an action head for small vision-language-action models that maintains two latent states updated at different frequencies, separating slowly evolving task context from rapidly changing motor commands. This enables latent-space deliberation without the latency and memory costs of chain-of-thought decoding or dual-system architectures, targeting real-time onboard robot control.

entry.title: Who Makes the Decision? Auditing an Agentic LLM Pipeline for Illicit Cryptocurrency Transaction Monitoring

author.name: Vaishnavi Chaughule, Yuchen Zhang, Mohammed Ahnaf Tajwar, Sai Akshay Menta, Saanidhya Vats, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Divya Chaudhary

entry.summary: This paper audits an agentic pipeline combining graph detectors, rules, retrieval, and an LLM judge for illicit crypto monitoring using decision-source attribution: per-case actual causation, interventional Shapley credit, and mediation analysis. Strikingly, a deterministic wallet-score override carries about 94 percent of the credit for flags and a verification gate cancels most of the LLM judge's own flags, which fall on licit transactions.

entry.title: Autonomous Multireference Quantum Chemistry with Artificial Intelligence Agents

author.name: Younghwan Kim, Ming-Hsiu Hsieh, Ankit Mathanker, Arpan Choudhury, Joshua Zhou, Qiaohong Wang, Matthew R. Hermes, and Laura Gagliardi

entry.summary: CASPER is an agentic workflow that automates multireference quantum chemistry calculations along reaction pathways, combining chemical knowledge, electronic structure computations, and iterative assessment to maintain chemically meaningful active spaces as bonds form and break. It is demonstrated on five transition-metal reactions, a class of problems requiring expert judgment to automate previously.

entry.title: The Answer Is Not the State: Trajectory-Level Corrigibility in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Junchi Liao, Wentao Li

entry.summary: This paper studies corrigibility in diffusion language models, finding a counterintuitive effect where reopening only the final answer allows the existing rationale to reconstruct the old decision despite new evidence, while reopening both rationale and answer makes decisions track current evidence. The effect is tested across Dream, LLaDA, and iLLaDA on source-disjoint and free-form benchmarks. It reveals how canvas-level generation changes the dynamics of response revision and corrigibility.

entry.title: When "A or B" Is Less Likely than A: Coherent Probabilities for Vision Decision Models

author.name: Seongrae Noh, SeongEun Hong, HyeongYeop Kang

entry.summary: The paper shows that VLM multiple-choice probabilities are incoherent under option regrouping: a merged option A-or-B receives on average 11.5 probability points less than the sum of A and B, an effect persisting across model sizes and fine-tuning. The proposed CORE training method regroups options and trains toward a single coherent target distribution, reducing total variation distance across seven benchmarks.

entry.title: When Does Optical Context Compression Pay Off? A Decode-Aware Cost Analysis of Reasoning VLMs

author.name: Ziqing Ge

entry.summary: This analysis shows that rendering long text as images for VLMs, though cheaper in prefill tokens, makes reasoning models think longer: decode length grows 1.5-3.5x, which under typical output pricing makes image input more expensive than text for some models. Notably, OCR recovers 98.7 percent of words at moderate compression and feeding a model its own transcription restores text-mode behavior, suggesting the tax is not pure information loss.

entry.title: RMR-VLA: Recurrent Memory Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yiheng Du, Jingqi Tian, Xu Jiang, Jiexuan Zhang, Shuyu Wang, Zecheng Tang, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: RMR-VLA introduces an explicit recurrent memory reasoning step inside a vision-language-action model, where the model infers events, revises a task state, and grounds a subgoal in the current scene each update. This lets remembered cues that are no longer visible still determine actions, roughly doubling success on RoboMME for long-horizon, history-dependent manipulation.

entry.title: Counterfactual Velocity Steering for World Action Models

author.name: Xufeng Zhan, Yuanzhi Liang, Ye Lu, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that naive test-time bias correction for flow-based robot policies, subtracting task-agnostic velocities from task-conditioned predictions, fails because reference velocities share a large transport component with task predictions. It provides a same-state diagnostic and shrinkage analysis identifying the optimal correction scale, validated across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks on Fast-WAM.

entry.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks

author.name: Sunbowen Li, Dandan Song, Shengkun Ma, Xuanning Cao

entry.summary: The authors formally analyze whether standard SFT can learn heterogeneous reasoning strategies pooled from diverse teachers, showing the optimal autoregressive target weights modes by prefix posteriors and collapses to one mode when alternatives lose likelihood. Controlled experiments in a symbolic graph-search environment with BFS/DFS traces characterize learnability and local bottlenecks.

entry.title: AgentMoT: An Agentic Mixture-of-Transformers for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qihang Huang, Collister Chua, YuJie Yan, Shiyu Fang, Zhan Chen, Haoran Xu, Zirui Li, Chen Lv

entry.summary: AgentMoT is a Mixture-of-Transformers for autonomous driving with three jointly trained pathways (direct-action, vision-language-action, world-action), where a router selects a native pathway and an agent expert supplies reasoning, skill selection, and a self-scheduler that decides when to reconsider decisions based on a relative-capability principle. It combines architectural modularity with agentic control in an end-to-end driving stack.

entry.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Ting Chen, Geng Li, Guohao Chen, Hanjia Lyu

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing benchmarks confound the measurement of contrastive decoding for multimodal hallucination mitigation through candidate filtering and trajectory changes, and introduces CONCOR, a controlled benchmark using a Contrastive Grounding Margin metric that directly measures competition between ground-truth and hallucinated candidates. This enables cleaner analysis of why and when contrastive adjustments help.

entry.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems

author.name: Nicolas Boull\'e, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend

entry.summary: The paper establishes when coefficients of linearly parameterized analytic systems can be exactly recovered from a single input-solution pair, proving a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate for recovery, or the degenerate set is measure-zero under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. Applications include matrix recovery, analytic dynamical systems, and differential operators.

entry.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? An Empirical Study of Decoupled Knowledge and Generation Trajectories in Clinical LLMs

author.name: Niclas Doll, Jasper Schulze Buschhoff, Shalaka Satheesh, H\'ector Allende-Cid, Katrin Klug

entry.summary: This empirical study tracks continual pre-training dynamics across 18 checkpoints for eight instruction-tuned Qwen models (0.5B-8B) adapted to German medicine, jointly measuring factual knowledge via MCQA and open-ended behavior via pairwise preference rankings. It finds knowledge and generation behavior converge at different rates, with preference rankings saturating at a median of 1.7B tokens versus 3.5B for MCQA. A judge-free token-distribution metric approximates the preference signal cheaply.

entry.title: DelayOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation from a Synchronous Teacher for Real-time Asynchronous Policies

author.name: Hyeonjae Kim, Jeongsol Kim, Sunwoo Park, Chanyu Moon, Yoojin Oh, Youngjun Jun, Kyumin Choi, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: The paper studies latency-induced performance degradation in asynchronous flow-based vision-language-action policies, showing that action predictions from stale observations diverge substantially from planning-time predictions on the policy's own rollouts, especially in failures. DelayOPSD trains an asynchronous policy to imitate its synchronous counterpart on the policy's own delayed rollouts via on-policy self-distillation. This mitigates stale-observation mismatch for real-time robot control.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data

author.name: Merel Kuijs, Till Richter, Rushin H. Gindra, Korbinian Traeuble, Christian Matek, Rebeka Lukn\'arov\'a, Tingying Peng, Fabian J. Theis

entry.summary: Presents CAMEO, an adversarial fusion framework that learns shared cross-modal representations from small, partially paired datasets by combining pretrained unimodal encoders with cross-modal latent alignment. On computational pathology tasks like niche classification and cell type composition prediction, it outperforms contrastive approaches in data efficiency.

entry.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?

author.name: Hiroaki Honda, Koya Sakamoto, Shu Morikuni, Yusuke Iwasawa, Taiki Miyanishi

entry.summary: Introduces SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark of 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks across 16 skill categories evaluated at 13 belt speeds, with matched static counterparts and identical randomized scenes across speeds. Fine-tuning eight VLA and world-action models reveals that most peak at intermediate speeds and fail to react to visual motion cues, exposing a systematic speed-perception gap in current embodied policies.

entry.title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Zehua Chen, Yusheng Dai, Andong Wang, Weibei Dou, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes LiveAudio, a streaming video-to-audio framework that converts a bidirectional diffusion model into an autoregressive streaming generator, producing synchronized, high-quality audio in real time while video plays. Building on an existing bidirectional model rather than training a streaming model from scratch preserves audio quality and synchronization for interactive applications.

entry.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority

author.name: Yulliwas Ameur (CEDRIC - ROC), Samia Bouzefrane (CEDRIC - ROC, CNAM Paris), Soumya Banerjee (CEDRIC)

entry.summary: Identifies and formalizes a supply-chain-style security risk where compatible JSON schema updates to agent tools silently widen agent authority, noting that none of eight surveyed MCP clients re-approve widening tools. The paper defines a non-amplification re-binding rule with a Coq proof, 48 regression tests, and a pilot on 604 MCP server releases finding 412 of 580 compatible schema changes widen some authority.

entry.title: AnchorCredit: Output-Anchored Credit Assignment for Structured Generation with Multiple Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Gen Li, Pengyang Xie, Xiao Xiao, Chuanzhi Tong, Ziyang Ji, Zhigang Xu, Huiwen Bai, Zihao Xing, Yanxiang Zhou, Yifei Yuan, Xiaoqing Wang

entry.summary: AnchorCredit addresses systematic cross-component credit misassignment in RLVR methods like GRPO, where low rewards on some components wrongly penalize well-performing ones and their reasoning. It uses attention from output anchors to reasoning sentences to estimate component associations and assign component-specific advantages to relevant reasoning tokens.

entry.title: Temporal Gains, Spatial Costs: Revisiting Video Fine-Tuning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Linghao Zhang, Jungang Li, Yonghua Hei, Sicheng Tao, Song Dai, Yibo Yan, Zihao Dongfang, Weiting Liu, Chenxi Qin, Hanqian Li, Xin Zou, Jiahao Zhang, Shuhang Xun, Haiyun Jiang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how video-based supervised fine-tuning reshapes visual capabilities in multimodal LLMs, finding a consistent trade-off: video performance improves while static image understanding often stagnates or degrades across architectures and scales. The trade-off is linked to temporal budget, with more sampled frames influencing the spatial-temporal balance.

entry.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency

author.name: Xinyang Zhou, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: WorldLeague is a benchmark of 60 simulated robot tasks measuring progress toward physical goals from robot trajectories, spanning exploration (WorldSeek), object rearrangement (WorldShape), and adaptation to change (WorldShift). It allows vision-language models and other AI systems to be compared on a common control interface, probing combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action.

entry.title: A Comparison of Uncertainty in AI and Dynamical Climate Ensembles

author.name: Jacob B. Landsberg, Devin M. McAfee, M. A. Fernandez, Elizabeth A. Barnes

entry.summary: The authors perform the first systematic comparison of uncertainty representation between state-of-the-art AI climate model ensembles and dynamical atmospheric ensembles across temperature, geopotential height, and precipitable water. They find AI ensembles exhibit reduced internal variability and model uncertainty, producing narrower extremes and underdispersion relative to observations. This is a cautionary result for using AI climate emulators in risk and policy applications.

entry.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?

author.name: Tianrun Gou, Qingyao Yang, Wendong Xu, Liang Chen, Kuan Li, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: ChiProgramBench is an 18-task benchmark testing whether LLM agents can reverse-engineer hidden hardware circuits (processors, accelerators, codecs, interconnects) by driving and reading pins of a stateful simulated reference, then submitting a gate-level netlist of public library cells. It evaluates black-box discovery and function-guided reconstruction settings with an emphasis on efficiency of the rebuilt circuit.

entry.title: Attention Temperature Confounds Zero-Shot Context Extension

author.name: Ruben Navasardyan

entry.summary: This paper shows that evaluations of training-time attention modifications for zero-shot context extension are confounded by temperature miscalibration of the dense baseline, since sharpening logits by one scalar can account for much of the apparent gain. Seed-paired 365M-model experiments quantify 8-15% miscalibration at 30k context for an 8k-trained baseline, and pure-bf16 training makes it several times worse. A cautionary methodological result for long-context research.

entry.title: On-Policy Codec Distillation for Efficient All-in-One Video Generation

author.name: Boyang Wang, Kevin Blackburn-Matzen, Oindrila Saha, Matheus Gadelha, Zezhou Cheng

entry.summary: CodecOPSD tackles the cost of conditioning tokens in visual generative models by pruning redundant spatiotemporal tokens using classical video-codec insight, then training a DiT adapter via on-policy self-distillation to learn the pruning pattern without quality loss. Together these reduce conditioning computation for all-in-one video generation.

entry.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming

author.name: Hani Alomari, Md Atabuzzaman, Chris Thomas

entry.summary: TowerBridge shows that post hoc removal of the CLIP modality gap degrades retrieval, and instead introduces a paired statistic identifying directions where the two towers agree more on hard negatives than matched pairs; mildly attenuating these directions improves retrieval while preserving the gap. Edits are produced by an LLM agent performing weight-space programming — closed-form weight edits without backpropagation.

entry.title: Modern Self-Supervised Vision Transformers Are Pareidolic

author.name: Zihang Lin, Huaiyuan Qin, Liangli Zhen, Qing Guo, Jun Liu, Yew-Soon Ong, Hongyuan Zhu

entry.summary: The authors discover pareidolia in self-supervised ViTs: on pure white noise, a few feature directions still form spatially coherent patterns, defining a pareidolic subspace that holds most feature variance in DINOv2 and DINOv3 but little in DINO. This excess explains why the stronger dense features of DINOv2/v3 fall behind DINO in object emergence, the ability to identify object patches.

entry.title: NOVA: Normalization-Aware Output-Guided Attention Acceleration for Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Wenxuan Miao, Haosong Liu, Aiyue Chen, Yiwu Yao, Zihan Liu, Anbang Wu, Yiming Gan, Jingwen Leng, Minyi Guo, Yu Feng

entry.summary: NOVA accelerates video diffusion transformers with a coarse-to-fine sparse attention framework whose selection criterion approximates the full normalized output, building a residual proxy that accounts for coupled numerator-denominator softmax errors rather than raw attention weights. This output-fidelity-aware criterion better predicts the error of sparse attention. Efficiency work of this kind directly enables longer and higher-resolution video generation.

entry.title: From Point Clouds to Engineering Models: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment

author.name: Changyu Du, Stavros Nousias, Syed Salman Ahmed, Kai Dietmair, Mohammad Alrabab'h, Andr\'e Borrmann

entry.summary: The authors formulate scene-level Scan-to-BIM as an agentic 3D coding task and introduce S2Bench, with public and proprietary scans of 128 real-world scenes across five domains paired with expert-curated reference models. A shared framework lets coding agents measure scans in Python and build labeled components in a live CAD/BIM kernel, and the paper proposes asynchronous parallel collaboration where a lead delegates versioned tasks to workers.

entry.title: Intervention-Robust VLA: Diverse Demonstrations for Robot Deployment with Safety Filters

author.name: Tzu-Yuan Huang, Shao-Hsuan Chang, Dai-Jie Wu, Ralf R\"omer, Yung-Hui Li, Stefan Sosnowski, Angela P. Schoellig, Kenneth Marino, Sandra Hirche

entry.summary: InteR-VLA addresses the problem that test-time safety filters can push robots into poorly covered training states, degrading task performance. The framework leverages diverse task-completing demonstrations to broaden state coverage so VLAs remain competent under safety interventions, aligning the training distribution with safety-filtered deployment. It connects safe RL deployment with VLA training data strategy.

entry.title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare

author.name: Yihao Wu, Runjia Zeng, Tongyan Wang, Renzhong Huang, Chongzhou Fang, Qifan Wang, Fan Heng, Dongfang Liu

entry.summary: The paper proves that JEPA world models trained on logged transitions cannot identify action responses in directions where the behavior policy never varies within a state. It proposes Fork-JEPA, which augments training with fork futures: outcomes of two alternative actions executed from the same restored state, whose difference cancels the state term and identifies the action response. A lookback head preserves predecessor recoverability at modest training-time cost.
