entry.title: The Effect of Security-Focused Prompts on Reported Findings: A Controlled Experiment on 400 AI-Generated Web Applications

author.name: Darko Andro\v{c}ec

entry.summary: A controlled experiment appending an OWASP-aligned security block to prompts for two agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI) across 100 frozen specifications, producing 400 web applications and 6,721 triaged security findings. The security block cut findings per application by about a third, with results analyzed via mixed models and dependency diffs to quantify effects and side effects.

entry.title: PhysPPF: Learning Robotic Manipulation with Past, Present, and Future Physical Representations

author.name: Junjie Li, Dawei Yan, Guoting Wei, Ruike Song, Lu Wang, Qingguo Chen, Zhenbo Luo, Haokui Zhang, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: PhysPPF is a vision-language-action framework for manipulation that performs unified spatiotemporal modeling in a compact physical token space, combining WWH (What-Where-How) distillation of pretrained perception with explicit 3D contact cues and past-present-future context. It targets complex tasks requiring precise 3D contact and long-horizon coordination that current VLAs handle poorly. This addresses a real gap between spatial-prior and history-aware VLA approaches.

entry.title: CrossPanel: Exposing the Answer-Evidence Gap in Scientific Figure Understanding

author.name: Zhengyang Lu (1), QianhongWen (2), Chenpeng Wang (3), Qiang Huang (4), Ziyang Ling (1), Huan Li (1), Chenziao (5), Yibo Qiu (1), Xiaojie Cheng (3) ((1) University of Science and Technology of China, (2) Sichuan Agricultural University, (3) YiXin-AI Lab, (4) Fudan University, (5) Peking Union Medical College)

entry.summary: Introduces CrossPanel, a benchmark of 2,650 human-reviewed questions on scientific figure understanding with a response audit separating object selection, conditions, cross-panel binding, and local readout. Across 15 VLMs, 8.42% to 56.64% of correct answers contain explicit factual errors, revealing that models can answer correctly while misreading the experiment. This answer-evidence gap is a significant and underappreciated evaluation blind spot.

entry.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?

author.name: Priyanka Siddappa, Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma

entry.summary: The study examines how updating a deployed clinical risk model with a new data source that only some patients have reshapes patient rankings, potentially dropping sick untested patients off alert lists. Using 78,475 emergency visits plus a pre-registered 100,000-stay MIMIC-IV-ED replication, it splits rank compatibility by data availability and quantifies alert-list effects.

entry.title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery

author.name: Yingheng Wang, Francesco Ricci, Zhilong Wang, Tao Yu, Junwen Bai, Xiangyun Lei, Shufeng Kong, Fengqi You, John M. Gregoire, Carla P. Gomes

entry.summary: DeepDOSReasoner predicts electronic and phonon densities of states from crystal structure using atom-to-energy source attention and a learned continuity-equation transport refinement enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation. It addresses the fact that roughly 60-80% of Materials Project entries lack DOS data due to costly DFT calculations.

entry.title: Meddies-PII: A Multilingual Framework for Personally Identifiable Information Extraction in Clinical De-identification

author.name: Le Linh Uyen, Christian Hoang, Ho Dinh Tri, Huy Hoang Ha

entry.summary: Releases a large multilingual clinical PII extraction dataset covering seventeen languages, including seven Southeast Asian languages, with nine PII labels and a fully documented synthetic generation pipeline. A compact 350M-parameter BIOES token classifier trained on it achieves the highest scores on all fifteen public benchmarks (mean exact-match F1 of 0.827 versus 0.672 for the strongest public system) and transfers without adaptation to human-annotated German and Spanish benchmarks. This addresses scarcity of governed multilingual clinical de-identification data.

entry.title: PROPS: Can Visual Generators Keep the Current Look of a Prop?

author.name: Xiangzhao Hao, Dianyi Wang, Keyan Zhou, Yiqian Zhang, Zefeng Zhang, Bailin Li, Kun Zhan, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: PROPS is a benchmark of 2,257 pairs of twin visual histories ending on the same request but showing one prop in two different looks, designed to isolate prop drift — the failure of visual generators to recover an object's current appearance from history rather than redrawing it or reverting to an outdated look. A paired judge design prevents similarity-to-history shortcuts from masking the failure.

entry.title: Admitted Is Not Effective: Lessons from a Notary-Gated Retrospective Loop in an Agentic Pipeline

author.name: Lo Gullstrand Heander and Emma S\"oderberg and Christofer Rydenf\"alt

entry.summary: This pre-registered study of 880 pull requests tests a retrospective loop where an agent proposes edits to learned rules every ten PRs and a Notary admits, merges, or rejects them with a provenance ledger. Despite the Notary admitting 55 of 89 proposals and catching fabricated citations, held-out metrics did not improve, showing that governed rule accumulation alone does not yield task success.

entry.title: PackLoop: Row-Packed Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models under Concurrency

author.name: Runguo Li, Dezhen Lu

entry.summary: PackLoop improves speculative decoding for looped language models under concurrent load by repacking speculative work so multiple positions share a KV-cache row, exploiting the observation that the row is the unit of cost in concurrent decoding. This restores speculative speedups that conventional wavefront-style schedules lose as GPU sharing increases.

entry.title: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Haokai Ding, Han Zhou, Zuxing Lu, Heng Zhang, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: DexDuet learns bimanual dexterous manipulation from a single human demonstration by using interaction rewards that preserve human hand-object configurations and contacts, factoring the bimanual policy into two weight-sharing per-hand policies that condition on each other's states. It also proposes assisted reference-state initialization to enable coordinated manipulation training.

entry.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Javier Conde, Xiuyuan Qi, Shanshan Liu, and Pedro Reviriego

entry.summary: This study shows that fixing prompt and seed does not fix the output image of text-to-image models on GPUs: batch composition and GPU type determine outputs, with bit-exact replay controls proving the variation is deterministic execution-dependent, not noise. Across six diffusion and autoregressive models, four precisions, and three GPU types, structural similarity between solo and in-batch generations varies substantially and model-dependently. This challenges the assumed reproducibility contract of generative pipelines.

entry.title: SuSi-RAG: A Hybrid Graph RAG for Equipment Maintenance

author.name: Hansi Zhang+, Wilma Johanna Schmidt+, Wanlin Yang, Xiaozhi Shen, Adrian Paschke and Evgeny Kharlamov

entry.summary: Proposes SuSi-RAG, a hybrid Graph RAG system that matches queries to maintenance records via subgraph similarity, targeting complex causal chains and cross-domain synthesis that defeat vector-based RAG in manufacturing. The system has run on an active Bosch production line for over eight months with 10,664 interactions, offering rare real-world deployment evidence.

entry.title: Vitrify Exact Learning: exact differential equations, changes of variable and closed forms from numerical data

author.name: Benedict Irwin, Alexander Mathiasen, Tom Etminan

entry.summary: Vitrify Exact Learning recovers exact linear differential equations with polynomial coefficients from numerical function data, handling changes of variable and density pushforwards. It finds annihilating operators as null vectors of weak-form measurement matrices, integrates data against test functions to avoid differentiation, and validates exact operators on held-out data against propagated noise.

entry.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time

author.name: Jianyu Wu, Yizhou Wang, Encheng Su, Jinouwen Zhang, Pengze Li, Lintao Wang, Chen Tang, Aoran Wang, Wanli Ouyang, Shixiang Tang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI), a label-free framework in which LLMs improve at test time by building on earlier attempts rather than relying on independent solutions and majority voting, using two mutually reinforcing components to preserve useful reasoning and correct mistakes. It aims to avoid reinforcing incorrect majorities that plague self-consistency-based training targets.

entry.title: Real2Worlds2Real: Scaling Self-Improving Agentic Real2Sim2Real for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jinzhong Gu, Jiakai Chen, Xinyi Cao, Yan Shen, Hangke Sui, Shutian Zheng, Xiang Xiao, Haoran Lu, Fan Xu, Lu Shi, Daochen Shi, Ruihua Zhang, Wei Zhan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: Real2Worlds2Real is a self-improving agentic pipeline that builds digital twins from limited visual observations and task descriptions, then expands them into diverse physically executable digital cousins for sim-to-real policy learning. An agent orchestrates construction tools and revisits decisions using visual and execution feedback, aiming to scale robot manipulation learning beyond costly real-world data collection.

entry.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li, Xinlin Zhuang, Zhixiang Lu, Haolin Yang, Jianxu Chen, Yifan Lu, Zhiran Zhang, Yutong Xie

entry.summary: ActSpace-Bench comprises 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, requiring VLMs to navigate and actively gather evidence from a single starting view before answering spatial questions. A controlled protocol compares each model's own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning ability.

entry.title: Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM

author.name: Amol Harsh, Zongyan Han, Jean Lahoud, Ye Liu, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Hisham Cholakkal, Salman Khan, Fahad Khan

entry.summary: Ground3D-LMM is a unified 3D large multimodal model that combines conversational spatial reasoning with explicit point-grounded responses and metric numeric outputs (sizes, distances, clearances) at object and part granularity. It bridges the gap between 3D grounding models and interactive dialogue systems, making answers verifiable and physically measurable.

entry.title: Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards for Human-Behavior Simulation

author.name: Ruoyun Ma, Shuang Liu, Peiye Liu, Ao Qu, Baichuan Mo

entry.summary: The paper introduces Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR), an RL reward for training LLM survey-respondent simulators that uses demographic group distribution gaps to guide individual response generation. It resolves the tension between exact-match rewards, which collapse to the most frequent answer, and aggregate distribution matching, which can ignore demographics. DVR aligns simulated frequencies with human response distributions per group while still predicting individual answers.

entry.title: ORDO: Fine-Grained Motion Understanding in Video LLMs via Order-Dependent Supervision

author.name: Jiaye Luan, Chaoning Zhang, Pengcheng Zheng, Dongshen Han, Sheng Zheng, Ping Guo, Caiyan Qin, Yang Du, Yang Yang

entry.summary: ORDO targets a real weakness of video LLMs: fine-grained motion perception such as acceleration or deceleration. It formalizes order-necessary supervision, where labels become unrecoverable if frame order is discarded, preventing models from solving tasks via static cues. Building training data with this property yields models that genuinely use temporal ordering, a conceptually clean contribution to video understanding.

entry.title: StateBind: Exposing the Symbol-to-State Binding Gap in Visual Measurement

author.name: Qing Mu, Jiani Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces StateBind-200, a benchmark of 200 real images with human-refined local geometry to test whether vision models can bind numerical claims to visible physical states in measurement tasks. Physicalizing candidate values raises three-model majority accuracy from 75.54% to 91.13%, while calibration and extra reasoning leave most of the gap intact, revealing a systematic weakness in how VLMs ground numbers in image evidence.

entry.title: Beyond Outlier Rejection: Transient-Aware Reconstruction of Multi-Stack MRI

author.name: Anika Knupfer, Maximilian Lindholz, Maria Camila Bustos-Vivas, Joseph V. Hajnal, Bodo Rosenhahn, Jana Hutter

entry.summary: Rather than down-weighting inconsistencies in multi-stack 2D MRI reconstruction, this paper proposes an analysis-by-synthesis decomposition that models each voxel via exact acquisition geometry into shared static anatomy, per-stack motion, and a sparse transient field capturing intra-scan physiological changes such as fetal motion. A robust reweighting keeps transients out of the anatomy estimate while preserving them as clinically informative signals.

entry.title: Specialized Large Language Models for Markovian Reasoning: Structural Cache Compression, Transition Pretraining, and Dual-Loop Transformers

author.name: Haibin Tong, Liangliang Xin, Yamei Zhu, Jiang Yu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified paradigm for LLMs specialized in first-order Markovian reasoning, transforming history-dependent KV caches into constant-size state transfer and reformulating long-chain prediction as independently trainable one-step transitions. The dual-loop architecture targets long-chain reasoning and multi-branch sampling workloads. If validated, this could substantially reduce memory and throughput bottlenecks for a class of reasoning problems.

entry.title: Probing Invisible Actuation Shifts for Test-time Calibration of Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Jie Liu, Hui Xie, Qinfeng Feng, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: The paper identifies actuation shifts (retuned controllers, latency, added payloads) as a deployment failure mode for visuomotor policies like VLAs, since these shifts change how commanded actions translate to motion without altering observations. It proposes PEA, a test-time calibration method where the robot runs a short active probe before each episode to detect and compensate for such shifts. This addresses a practical gap in sim-to-real and cross-robot transfer that domain randomization alone does not solve.

entry.title: When Can an AI Agent Serve as a Model of Human Psychopathology?

author.name: Marc-Andre Schulz, Pauline Scheuber

entry.summary: This conceptual paper asks under what conditions experiments on AI agents can provide evidence about human psychiatric processes, decomposing such claims into three evidential parts: that a change occurred and was caused by the agent's history, that only a human-shared process explains it, and that it discriminates between rival theories of the human condition. It maps each part to existing evidence standards from diagnostics, clinical testing, and adjacent fields.

entry.title: Muted Distillation: Sealing Reasoning from Teacher Unlocks Token-Efficient Agents

author.name: Yuwei Zhang, Ian Miao, Wentao Zhang, Chen Qu, Bill Bi, Jingbo Shang, Donna Schut

entry.summary: Identifies that on-policy distillation for LLMs inflates student reasoning length in multi-turn agentic tasks because student reasoning distracts teacher scoring, and proposes Muted Distillation, which hides the student's reasoning from the teacher during judgment. This few-line change cuts output tokens per episode by 57% and 53% on OfficeQA Pro and SpreadsheetBench versus standard on-policy distillation. A simple, well-motivated fix to a practical inefficiency in agentic post-training.

entry.title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics

author.name: Yuxiang Wei, Zundong Wu, Weiyu Sun, Qizhen Lan, Yanteng Zhang, Vince D. Calhoun

entry.summary: The authors introduce BrainStateBench, a benchmark for evaluating brain world models on whole-cortex movie-watching fMRI using frozen linear probes. It separately tests latent-state inference, stimulus-driven prediction, and state updating, addressing the flaw that prediction accuracy alone cannot distinguish genuine state tracking from stimulus memorization. This provides a rigorous evaluation protocol for a growing area connecting world models and neural decoding.

entry.title: Tool-to-Self: Internalizing Visual Tool Capabilities via Scaffolded Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jin Cui, Hao Dong, Xinyue Long, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: Introduces T2S, an RL framework for vision-language models that uses external visual tools as temporary training scaffolds, progressively annealing tool execution so the model internalizes tool capabilities and avoids inference-time dependencies. Combines answer-correctness and observation-consistency rewards with on-policy self-distillation from real tool outputs.

entry.title: Right Verdict, Right Reason? An Execution-Grounded Study of Whether LLM Vulnerability Detectors Understand Vulnerabilities

author.name: Leizhen Zhang and Sheng Chen

entry.summary: Tests whether LLM vulnerability detectors actually understand the bugs they flag by grounding evaluation in program execution: for 515 C/C++ functions with reproduced proofs of concept, the authors build a ladder of five tests from detection to fault localization and run-outcome prediction, each paired with understanding-free baselines. This challenges reading benchmark scores as evidence of comprehension.

entry.title: Internalized Experience: How Training Data Shapes Memory Formation in LLMs

author.name: Xianxuan Long, Xinnan Dai, Kai Guo, and Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Introduces FSMem, a finite-state-machine-based framework for constructing training data to study how data content and organization shape parametric memory and reusable rule internalization in LLMs. Evaluations across synthetic worlds, planning, and code execution reveal systematic patterns, including interference when rules are learned alongside more varied tasks. This offers a principled lens on how training data design affects in-context and cross-task generalization.

entry.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus

author.name: Bangyan Ju, Xiaolin Sun, Yibin Hu, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: Formalizes insider attacks in multi-agent LLM debate and consensus systems as sequential decision-making, where a malicious agent learns a world model to persuade other agents toward a hidden adversarial goal and degrade collective outcomes. The model-based attack formulation is a proactive red-teaming contribution for a class of systems increasingly assumed to be robust via deliberation. This exposes a security assumption in most multi-agent LLM frameworks.

entry.title: ViewAgent3D: A Training-Free Multi-View Pipeline for 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Sarosij Bose, Arindam Dutta, Konstantinos Karydis, Amit K. Roy Chowdhury

entry.summary: ViewAgent3D argues that for many 3D scene queries the bottleneck is selecting a small set of multi-view RGB views that make the query answerable, rather than building richer 3D representations. It introduces a training-free, query-conditioned pipeline that decomposes queries into concepts and performs coarse-to-fine evidence selection using only 2D images and inference-time tools. This offers a practical, low-cost alternative to specialized 3D multimodal models.

entry.title: IRIS: Inverse Dynamics from Random Exploration with Eye-in-hand Sensing

author.name: Xiaoxiong Zhang, Zhiqiang Zhou, Tze Ho Elden Tse, Linfang Zheng, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: IRIS targets the action-grounding bottleneck in imagine-then-execute video-based manipulation by training an inverse dynamics model from random exploration rather than limited task-specific demonstrations, and by handling eye-in-hand observations whose moving viewpoint makes video planning hard to learn and scale. This improves generalization even with oracle visual subgoals. It addresses a real bottleneck beyond visual planning in video-based robot manipulation.

entry.title: Training speech deepfake detectors against worst-case filters: Gains, Costs and Limits

author.name: Ali Alavi

entry.summary: This paper shows that a single short filter tuned against a speech deepfake detector defeats it, and that training with random filters does not help because attackers use worst-case filters. The authors train detectors against adversarially optimized filters at roughly the cost of random filters, showing in a preregistered study improved robustness on real-world recordings and better performance than one-step additive-noise adversarial training. It is a concrete, well-evaluated advance in audio deepfake security.

entry.title: KMed-31B Technical Report

author.name: KMed Team at NAVER

entry.summary: NAVER's KMed team presents a 31B medical language model post-trained from an open-weight base for on-premises deployment on limited hardware. They categorize medical tasks by expected output type and available feedback, train a specialist per category with a matching reward, and merge them into one student using Multi-teacher On-policy Delta Distillation. This addresses the common problem where gains on one medical task degrade another.

entry.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings

author.name: Disha Sheshanarayana and Tanishka Magar

entry.summary: DiscernBench evaluates whether LLM agents appropriately comply with, refuse, or escalate requests in institutional settings, using scenarios derived from real incident reports in aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. It tests eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations, analyzing both final decisions and multi-agent deliberation dynamics, finding model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns.

entry.title: STAC++: Plug-and-Play Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Aware Cache Compression for Streaming 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Boyi Zhu, Youcheng Cai, Dong Wang

entry.summary: STAC++ is a training-free, plug-and-play framework that compresses spatial key-value caches using an octree with adaptive resolution, merges cache entries based on attention-output changes, and reuses cached features to refine historical predictions in streaming 3D reconstruction. It extends fixed-resolution caching to unbounded scenes with better memory scaling.

entry.title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design

author.name: Mingjie Bao, Yu Dai, Guangke Chen, Guozhu Meng

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for audio CAPTCHAs that remains robust against large audio-language models by inverting the usual human-easy/machine-hard assumption: challenges are chosen where stable human perceptual biases cause humans to systematically differ from the physical ground truth, while machines converge toward it. The verifier accepts the human-reference answer, so more capable machine solvers actually become easier to separate from humans. The authors instantiate the idea using psychoacoustic phenomena.

entry.title: DoC: Learning to Defer or Commit for Timely, Accurate, and Stable Conversational Diagnosis Prediction

author.name: Xueren Ge, Anthony Cortez, Homa Alemzadeh

entry.summary: DoC is a two-phase framework for conversational diagnosis prediction that learns when to commit to a diagnosis without annotated commitment times: iterative commitment-boundary estimation constructs deferral supervision, then defer-aware SFT is refined with RL using trajectory-level rewards for timeliness, first-commit accuracy, and post-commit stability. It achieves the best first-commit accuracy and lowest post-commit error on EMSDialog and MediTOD.

entry.title: T2ISpec: Benchmarking Speculative Decoding for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Shatong Zhu, Hui Shen, Yunta Hsieh, Jianing Ma, Muxin Fu, Xin Wang, Ping Zhang, Qian Chen, Chaofan Tao

entry.summary: T2ISpec is a benchmark of 1,400 prompts across seven rendering topics and two difficulty levels for evaluating speculative decoding accelerators on autoregressive and diffusion/flow text-to-image models. It finds that aggregate metrics hide large topic-level differences, alignment scores can disagree with constraint satisfaction, and large reductions in target-model work can yield little latency gain. The proposed TopicRoute plugin routes based on topic to exploit these findings.

entry.title: Distributed Interactive Conformal Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Daniel M. Cherenson, Dimitra Panagou

entry.summary: MA-ICP is a distributed framework for conformal prediction in multi-agent robotic systems, handling dependence among robots, distributed calibration, and distribution shift induced when uncertainty bounds alter the closed loop. It aggregates robot-level nonconformity scores to compute robustness margins satisfying mission requirements with high probability. This extends distribution-free uncertainty quantification to realistic multi-robot deployments.

entry.title: Your Diffusion-Based Driving Planner Only Needs a Nudge

author.name: Zilin Wang, Guozheng Ma, Saeed Rahmani, Jiong Yang, Antyanta Bangunharcana, Yiluan Guo, Jakob Nicolaus Foerster, Shimon Whiteson

entry.summary: PlanNudge freezes a pretrained diffusion-based driving planner and trains a lightweight nudge policy that makes small trajectory adjustments to prevent collisions and road departures under closed-loop covariate shift. This avoids the complexity of RL finetuning through the iterative denoising and receding-horizon execution of diffusion planners.

entry.title: RAVEC: Reward-Aligned Visual Evidence Correction

author.name: Junjie Yang, Rui Qian, Xutao Mao, Yuhe Wu, Mingda Zhang, Jiaxuan Luo, Yang Tan, Qiang Huang, Zhisheng Chen, Yanfeng Li, Dawen Tian, Changmiao Wang, Tao Tan

entry.summary: RAVEC improves multimodal reasoning under reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by selecting which visual evidence regions to correct, using local and cross-question reward support rather than response-level feedback alone. Its Paired Visual Evidence Contrast technique compares predictions at the same response prefix under original versus evidence-suppressed images to derive signed correction directions. This addresses the credit-assignment gap in RL for vision-language reasoning.

entry.title: FunGrasp-Zero: Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Policy for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Functional Grasping

author.name: Yanhan Lin, Yuliang Wu, Yihao Guo, Wei-Jin Huang, Jianwen Li, Jiawei Tang, Xiaolong Huang, Yuquan Wang, Ancong Wu, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: This robotics paper proposes FunGrasp-Zero, a reinforcement learning framework for zero-shot functional grasping that generalizes across different dexterous hand hardware. Instead of embodiment-specific retargeted hand poses, it uses an object-centric contact map capturing functional intent, enabling policies trained on one hand to transfer to unseen hands.

entry.title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds

author.name: Dongfang Zhao

entry.summary: Zarc is a GPU vector search system that achieves exact k-nearest-neighbor search over a billion vectors in seconds by keeping short half-precision distance proofs in GPU memory and fetching only the few full vectors that pass from host memory. It supports Euclidean, cosine, inner-product, and filtered queries exactly under updates, spanning four H100 GPUs.

entry.title: Neural Agent Compiler: Learning to Schedule Soft Dependencies

author.name: Bo Yan, Peng Wang, Zihan Chen, Ziwen Kan, Zhen Tan, Huiyuan Chen, Bo Sun, Shuai Shao, Tianlong Chen, Song Wang

entry.summary: This work identifies the problem of scheduling soft dependencies in LLM agent execution, where optional information could improve already-executable operations. It proposes Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a learned scheduler that predicts task-quality and resource tradeoffs across execution modes and selects the highest-utility legal mode at scheduling boundaries.

entry.title: ClothCast: Generative Cloth World Modeling under Partial Observability

author.name: Yushen Hu, Yilong Song, Zhen Zhou, Apurv Kushwaha, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Zhu-Tian Chen

entry.summary: ClothCast is a world model for deformable garment manipulation that uses planned gripper trajectories as motion priors and learns residual cloth deformation from a single RGB-D observation, hypothesizing occluded layers without requiring cloth meshes or material parameters. It tackles the hard partial-observability problem in garment robotics.

entry.title: Optimal Bandits with Switching Costs: $(T/\log(T))^{2/3}$ Regret

author.name: Chenyu Gan

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves the minimax regret for adversarial bandits with switching costs, proving a Theta((K^{1/3} T^{2/3}) / log^{2/3}(2+T/K)) bound and showing simple blocking is suboptimal. The algorithm uses randomized switching times and information-weighted detours to extract more information per switch.

entry.title: MAS-BIT: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-End BraIn-to-Text Decoding

author.name: Xinjie Zhang, Linyang He, Yizi Zhang, Yuesheng Ma, Nima Mesgarani

entry.summary: MAS-BIT is the first multi-agent framework for end-to-end brain-to-text decoding from intracortical recordings, coordinating a neural agent, a phonetic agent, and an arbitration agent that integrates their evidence via token-embedding-based latent communication. The approach aims to close the accuracy gap between end-to-end and cascaded speech BCI decoders.

entry.title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yiyang Zhao, Zhuo Zhang, Qingxuan Le, Lizhen Qu, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: MAC-Bench is a dynamic, adversarial benchmark evaluating procedural compliance of LLM-based multi-agent systems, targeting Machiavellian behavior where agents violate safety rules to maximize rewards. Its SERV pipeline (Seed-Evolve-Refine-Verify) transforms unstructured legal texts into executable, contamination-free scenarios with sandboxed environments.

entry.title: OnCache: Learning Dynamic Caching Schedules for Efficient Diffusion Inference

author.name: Zhikang Xie, Xichen Ye, Yifan Wu, Yuxuan Liu, Qianlong Wang, Haoshen Yu, Peizhu Gong, Weizhong Zhang, Cheng Jin

entry.summary: Proposes OnCache, a dynamic caching framework for diffusion model inference that makes prompt-adaptive, online decisions about computation allocation and when to refresh cached features, replacing static sample-agnostic schedules. It is motivated by the observations that denoising dynamics vary across prompts and caching-error sensitivity varies across timesteps. A learned policy decides per-step reuse versus recomputation to cut latency while preserving quality.

entry.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks

author.name: Ran Guan, Yiqi Lin, Xiangxi Tian, Yige Luo, Mi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes an agent harness that exposes intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls to the agent runtime, allowing policies to allocate computation within and across models. A prototype learns stitching bridges and state-conditioned policies that choose among continue, exit, and stitch actions during inference, supervised by matching full-vocabulary next-token predictions.

entry.title: JKO-GRPO: Augmenting GRPO with Wasserstein Proximal Steps for Flow-Matching VLAs

author.name: Jiyong Kwon, Yikun Bai, Amirhossein Mollaali, Guang Lin

entry.summary: JKO-GRPO augments Flow-GRPO for flow-based vision-language-action models like pi0 and pi0.5 by formulating policy improvement as a Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) Wasserstein proximal step, treating sampled action groups as empirical distributions. A soft discrete c-transform constructs transport targets from group-relative advantages, using action distances rather than only likelihood-ratio reweighting.

entry.title: Towards Global Counterfactual-Based Self-Explainable Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Wendy Zheng, Yinhan He, Jundong Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses limitations of graph counterfactual explanations (GCEs) by moving beyond post-hoc, sample-local explainers toward self-explainable GNNs that produce global counterfactual principles. The approach integrates explanation with model training so the explainer can leverage learned representations, which is especially valuable for applications like drug discovery.

entry.title: Constrained Diffusion from Binary Evaluations via Learned Doob h-Functions

author.name: Ssaumya Kammal Jaiswal, Mahfuza Farooque

entry.summary: This work reduces constrained diffusion generation to learning a Doob h-transform function, the probability that a noisy sample denoises into the constraint set, trained by regression on binary clean-sample evaluations alone. The base model stays frozen, one lightweight head per constraint is trained, and noisy-state classifier guidance emerges as a special case.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Multi-Objective Bandits: Pareto Violations & Gap-Based Regret

author.name: Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Murat Kocaoglu, Mahsa Ghasemi

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes Bayesian multi-objective bandits through an information-theoretic lens, showing that the information needed for low regret depends on the regret criterion, with the Pareto-optimal set as the natural target for Pareto-violation regret. The authors introduce a predictive separation measure, connect it to information gain, analyze Thompson Sampling, propose an Information-Directed Sampling strategy, and prove sublinear regret plus a lower bound under weak separation.

entry.title: Towards Agentic Video Corpus Moment Retrieval

author.name: Chenwei Xu, Shang Wu, Zhenyu Pan, Jianshu Zhang, Pranav Maneriker, Lie Lu, Fan Du, Manling Li, Han Liu

entry.summary: RELAY is a training-free agentic framework for video corpus moment retrieval that shares memory across queries via a three-stage pipeline: embedding-based search with a query bank, LLM reranking over VLM-generated video notes, and localization with video prompt caching. Cross-query memory amortizes expensive VLM processing.

entry.title: Reparameterizing Your Object Detectors for Weight Space Programming

author.name: Chien-Yao Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes IR-ODWSP, a method for editing the weights of converged object detectors without backpropagation by lifting layers into decoupled subspaces (moment, DCT, PCA, Stiefel-Procrustes) using function-preserving reparameterizations. The approach improves all 26 MS COCO settings across 17 detector variants with zero added parameters or FLOPs, including cross-basin gains and zero-image repair of damaged models.

entry.title: Reward Blindness: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Reinforcement Learning Reward Limitations in Text-to-SQL

author.name: Lakshmi Muraleedharan Nair, Shiqi Huang, Fangyu Lo, Yihua Xu, Dingyan Shang

entry.summary: This paper develops a theory of reward design for RL-trained text-to-SQL systems, introducing Reward Error Sensitivity and proving a Reward Blindness theorem: when a reward cannot separate queries with a given error type, policy-gradient training carries no signal for fixing it. The framework is validated using fourteen published fine-grained error taxonomies. It gives practitioners a principled diagnostic for why RL training stalls on certain semantic errors.

entry.title: Statistically Optimal and Near Linear Time Hypothesis Selection

author.name: Satyen Kale, Amirreza Shaeiri, Kunal Talwar

entry.summary: The authors give a hypothesis selection learner achieving the optimal factor-2 TV distance guarantee with O(log(n/delta)/epsilon^2) samples, matching Yatracos-style sample complexity while removing logarithmic factors from prior factor-2 bounds. The method accesses candidate distributions only through sampling and pointwise comparison, enabling near-linear time.

entry.title: RoboLiveMem: Is Robot Memory Solved When the World Does Not Wait?

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Yuyou Zhang, Janet Wang, Ming Liu, Yijiang Li, Yikai Wang, Weirui Ye, Ding Zhao, Jihun Hamm

entry.summary: RoboLiveMem is a benchmark showing that frontier VLM-based robot agents, which pass most static memory benchmarks, degrade when the world keeps changing while the model deliberates. It runs identical memory tasks in paused and live-world conditions across 29 task families in realistic BEHAVIOR-1K scenes and ManiSkill, mixing real changes with harmless look-alikes.

entry.title: Designing Incoherent Multispectral Diffractive Optical Networks for Satellite Image Classification

author.name: Xilin Yang, Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Ryan Lee, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: This paper presents a surrogate model-guided design framework for incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks that perform satellite image classification directly onboard, outputting class probabilities without downlinking the full multispectral data cube. This matters for space systems because it drastically reduces transmission bandwidth and enables real-time inference at the sensor.

entry.title: AdaptRouter: Adaptive Routing across Evolving Tasks and Models

author.name: Jingpu Yang, Fengxian Ji, Tianhao Li, Juanfan Wu, Yufeng Wang, Shuxin Zheng, Xiaoqing Zhang

entry.summary: AdaptRouter is a policy-learned model router in which a compact multimodal decision model reads queries with expert cards and learns from native task feedback without routing labels. It handles both open-weight and paid API experts with different learning strategies (RL for cheap experts, cached feedback as soft labels for API experts) and supports new tasks and experts without replay.

entry.title: Geospatial foundation models and deep learning for climate resilience: a review of transfer, uncertainty and decision readiness

author.name: Parastoo Farajpoor, Mohammadreza Narimani

entry.summary: This review examines whether geospatial foundation models, pretrained on large Earth-observation archives, transfer reliably to unfamiliar events, regions, and sensing conditions relevant to climate resilience and hazard early warning. The authors audit 137 full-text hazard-application studies plus 37 model and benchmark records, finding that only 31 studies used held-out events as headline evaluations and merely two used held-out sensors, with none of the ten foundation-model fine-tuning studies treating sensor holdout as a headline test. The work highlights systematic gaps in out-of-distribution evaluation, uncertainty quantification, and decision readiness that must be addressed before these models can be trusted operationally.

entry.title: Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding

author.name: Zeqiang Wang

entry.summary: OCSF is a vocabulary-free medical coding framework that maps clinical notes into a fixed 2D state matrix via a bidirectional diffusion-pretrained encoder with zero code-specific parameters, so any target ontology can be compiled onto the representation in seconds without retraining. This decouples document understanding from vocabulary-specific heads, enabling cross-ontology transfer.

entry.title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding

author.name: Kanghui Tian, Shuai Dong, Yuhan Zhu, Congcong Wang, Ji Zhao, Tianxiang Jiang, Zhixiong Zhang, Shengyuan Ding, Yi Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao

entry.summary: PixelOne is a student-teacher framework for GUI grounding that predicts precise click coordinates directly from native-resolution screenshots in a single forward pass. It transfers spatial knowledge from a search-based teacher that progressively zooms into candidate regions via spatial distillation, addressing detail loss from downsampling and coarse fixed bins in prior one-pass methods.

entry.title: PinGround: Pinning Queries to Points for Parallel Grounding in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shuxuan Li, Jialiang Kang, Yanghao Zhou, Ziye Zhu, Zhilin Zhao, Xiao Yang

entry.summary: PinGround addresses the sequential decoding bottleneck in vision-language grounding by writing a single point per query as a spatial anchor and retrieving the nearest matching instance in a local radius, enabling parallel decoding. This avoids duplicate and missed instances seen in naive parallel approaches while removing the linear growth of decoding steps in dense scenes.

entry.title: REACT: Response-based Expert Assembly from Contextual Trajectories

author.name: Hesen Yang, Yuxue Liu, Yanzhe Chen, Weibo Zhao, Junwei Su, Dan Hu, Shenggan Cheng, Xuanlei Zhao, Wenchao Zhou, Junhua Wang, Lansong Diao, Yang You

entry.summary: REACT is a context-guided upcycling method that organizes pretrained dense-network neurons into experts based on their responses to similar inputs, using frozen denoising trajectories with timestep-wise centering to connect input contexts with neuron responses. The goal is sparse execution that groups computations an input actually needs together while retaining pretrained weights.

entry.title: ColonoWorld: Camera-Controlled Full-Procedure Colonoscopy Video Generation

author.name: Jihwan Hong, Sunghwan Steve Cho, Ping Shu Ho, Joo Seong Kim, Bokyung Kim, Nam-Joon Kim, Simon See, Ji Won Kim, Jaeyoung Do

entry.summary: ColonoWorld is a video world model for colonoscopy that conditions generation on a commanded camera trajectory plus a coarse 3D tube of the colon, enabling full cecum-to-rectum procedure simulation with consistent anatomy, polyps, and procedural events, even for unseen colon shapes. It is trained on in vivo videos and is motivated by the need to safely develop and test increasingly autonomous colonoscope navigation systems, where erroneous motion could injure patients.

entry.title: SGD Selects Initialization-Dependent Representation in Overparameterized ReLU Networks

author.name: Nikos Tsikouras, Yorgos Pantis, Ahmed Mehdi Inane, Mehrab Hamidi, Ioannis Mitliagkas

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that in two-layer ReLU networks trained to fit a linear teacher, joint batch-size-one SGD from small initialization drives every neuron close to a teacher direction despite infinitely many non-aligned exact fits existing at width four and above, revealing how SGD selects among functionally equivalent representations. The result connects initialization scale to which hidden representation training converges to.

entry.title: SVUBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Yuxuan Liang, Bohan Zhang, Haiyang Yu, Bocheng Hu, Ke Niu, Xu Li, Zhengtao Yao, Yan Wen, Haotian Chen, Xiaolei Chen, Jiacong Wang, Zhe Liu, Jingqun Tang, Benlei Cui, Fan Shi, Xiangyang Xue

entry.summary: SVUBench is a large benchmark for proactive streaming video understanding with 12,131 questions and 62,881 answer points across ten tasks spanning perception, understanding, and reasoning. It introduces two interaction modes: Basic for sustained responses from video onset, and Trajectory requiring historical recovery and continuous updates after mid-stream task activation. Annotation combines model assistance with human verification, plus a duration-scaled challenge across four video lengths.

entry.title: RAPID: Codec-Aware Video Decoding for Efficient Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Yuna Lee, Yulhwa Kim

entry.summary: RAPID exploits information in compressed video bitstreams to reduce frame decoding and selection costs for long-video VLM inference. RAPID-Dec uses reference frames and random access points to skip unnecessary frames and decode retained ones in parallel with exact reconstruction, achieving up to 3.7x decoding speedup on H.264/AVC, addressing the fact that decoding can take longer than LLM prefill for hour-long videos.

entry.title: Foundation Model and Radiomics Distance Scores for Post-Hoc Segmentation Failure Detection

author.name: Simon Johannes Joham, Gianluca Guglielmo, Mateusz Kozinski, Martin Urschler

entry.summary: Proposes two post-hoc failure-detection scores for medical segmentation based on Mahalanobis distance to a labeled reference set: one using radiomic shape features of predicted masks, one using mask-aware frozen DINOv3 foundation model features. Validated on multi-site prostate and hippocampus MRI under protocol and population shift without needing model internals.

entry.title: Beyond the Black Box: A Diagnosis-Driven Agent for Interpretable MIP Solver Tuning

author.name: Yidong Luo, Weihuang Wen, Xuanhao Pan, Yinya Wang, Shanwen Pu, Chenghao Lan, Dongdong Ge, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: Introduces APEC, a log-grounded LLM agent for per-instance mixed-integer programming solver tuning, structured in three layers: deterministic log profiling, hypothesis-driven interpretation, and evaluation control. Inspired by GPU-kernel profilers, it yields more reliable and interpretable tuning than black-box Bayesian optimizers, evaluated on the full MIPLIB suite.

entry.title: Speculate in the Right Order: Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Yihan Chen, Jintao Zhang, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Analyzes theoretically how generation order affects self-speculative decoding efficiency in autoregressive image generation, identifying draft-target mismatch and early-rejection cost as key factors. It proposes Speculation-Aware Ordering, a training-aware method that chooses generation orders to maximize speculative decoding speedups without an extra draft model.

entry.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments

author.name: Yulliwas Ameur (CEDRIC - ROC), Miqeas Pedro Mendes (CEDRIC - ROC), Samia Bouzefrane (CEDRIC - ROC)

entry.summary: Introduces IntentFlow, a mediation layer that checks authority-bearing tool-call arguments against an intent contract and provenance policy, catching trusted-but-unauthorized values that provenance-only defenses accept. On a synthetic 200-attack benchmark, attack success drops from 50.5% to 12.0% with no false blocks on benign tasks and only 4 of 50 hard cases wrongly blocked.

entry.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation

author.name: Qiwei Liang, Zhengtu Liang, Minghao Lai, Yikeng Chen, Yiming Wang, Boyang Cai, Yuetong Fang, Taowen Wang, Baiqiao Yin, Tianxing Chen, Yue Chen, Jiaming Liang, Guangyu Chen, Shaolong Zhu, Daolin Ma, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: HIVE-Bench evaluates 20 vision encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual manipulation tasks using one shared flow-matching policy, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Key findings include that averaging patch tokens to a single pooled vector removes most success and that a shared policy retains most performance of separate policies.

entry.title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Lernie Li, Yuanliu Liu, Pengfei Xiong, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: DyLoMo-DiT reuses rather than adds parameters in diffusion transformers: weight-shared loops repeatedly apply middle layers while sparse experts allocate capacity across tokens, deepening the network without growing parameter storage. Compute is allocated dynamically across noise levels, and experiments indicate more effective parameter usage than standard MoE DiTs.

entry.title: Evaluable Language-Model Treatment Policies for Sepsis Resuscitation via Offline Value-Guided Selection

author.name: Yue Pei, Shining Bo, Yingying Zhang, Qinggang Ge, Zhiling Zhao, Jian Cheng, Haogang Zhu

entry.summary: R-LLMC balances imitation and value maximization at inference time for sepsis resuscitation: a behavior-supervised LLM proposes clinician-anchored candidates from an exact distribution over 25 vasopressor-fluid actions, and an offline critic selects among them by estimated long-term value. This avoids the delayed credit assignment and sparse outcome problems of fine-tuning LLMs on retrospective outcomes.

entry.title: Prediction-Powered Regression via Calibration: Beyond the Supervised Minimax Benchmark

author.name: Jin Su, Yong Zhou, and Jian Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes wPPRC, a method for nonparametric regression with few labels and many imperfectly pseudo-labeled observations, which first calibrates pseudo-labels using labeled data and then performs weighted regression. The authors derive matching nonasymptotic upper and minimax lower bounds over Hoelder classes and show the method can beat standard supervised minimax risk on certain observation structures.

entry.title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine

author.name: Hengzhi Jiang, Haixu Liu, Jindou Jia, Tinglan Wang, Shaobo Chen, Yiren Zhao, Ziyang Rao, Laiyuan Cui, Jiaxin Dong, Yin Ma, Hai Wei, Jiaqi Bai, Tuo An, Xinyu Zhou, Hao Ban, Hongdong Zhu, Yanqi Wang, Jiaqi Dou, Nuo Qian, Qi Liu, Bin Jin, Chang Wu, Qingfeng Li, Hui Yang, Weiyu Guo, Dicong Qiu, Qi Gao, Jianwei Niu, Kai Wen, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Boltz-Flow replaces the fixed, unimodal Gaussian source in flow-matching robot policies with an observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann machine source, parameterized by a conditional Boltzmann machine trained with a listwise offline objective, leaving the base VLA unchanged. This yields multimodal, temporally coordinated source distributions that better scale with task diversity in manipulation.

entry.title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Wenlong Yu, Bingxu Lu, Qilong Wang, Qinghua Hu, Qianru Sun

entry.summary: The paper introduces REPA, a structural model that traces how errors propagate, amplify, or get corrected across agents in multi-agent LLM systems, connecting local agent-level responses to system-level failure rather than relying only on outcome evaluation. It is evaluated on ErrPropBench-10, covering three Qwen base models, six multi-agent workflows, and ten knowledge and reasoning settings, achieving a mean condition-level Spearman correlation of 0.84. This provides much-needed analytical and benchmark tooling for understanding reliability in increasingly common multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents

author.name: Tianyi Huang, Samuel Xu, Ivy Gu, Nathan Huang, Siqi Zhang

entry.summary: LiveLora enables exact migration of KV caches when an LLM LoRA adapter is updated, avoiding costly full-history re-prefill for active agent sessions. By freezing lower decoder blocks and fixing K/V down-projections, the runtime reconstructs candidate K/V, reevaluates the latest token through the final block, and commits adapter, cache, and logits atomically, with a proof of continuation equivalence to full re-prefill under stated assumptions.

entry.title: Look Back, Draft Ahead: Corrective Prefix Attention for Parallel Speculative Decoding

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Moradi, Ali Pourranjbar, Zongzuo Wang, Mingming Zhu, Ben Feng, Boxing Chen

entry.summary: Corrective Prefix Attention improves parallel speculative decoding by letting draft candidates attend to earlier choices within the same block and training with an auxiliary autoregressive loss on clean prefixes. Fixed candidate shortlists reduce sequential computation to table lookups and lightweight scoring. It is validated across eight math, code, and dialogue benchmarks with Qwen3-4B/8B targets on Ascend NPUs.

entry.title: VITA-WAM: Manifold-Aligned World-Action Modeling for Real-Time Robot Control

author.name: Boqi Zhao, Dechen Gao, Hanchu Zhou, Hang Wang, Junshan Zhang

entry.summary: VITA-WAM accelerates world-action models for real-time visuomotor control by jointly aligning source and action manifolds, avoiding the costly transport of Gaussian noise into actions and the repeated cross-attention injection of task context. This substantially reduces the multi-step ODE sampling latency that limits deployment of diffusion- or flow-based action heads.

entry.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations

author.name: JB Kim, Byungwoo Jeon, Kyungmin Lee, Hyeonmo Kang, Cheonbok Park, Shinyoung Joo, Jinwoo Shin, Jeonghoon Kim

entry.summary: Integral converts a pretrained VLM into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across understanding and generation, addressing the heterogeneous-representation obstacle. Two complementary components, including Abstraction Fusion, make the VLM's multimodal knowledge accessible to image generation without training a unified model from scratch.

entry.title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models

author.name: Alex Klem and Uwe Peters

entry.summary: Testing ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and consumer UIs, the authors find UI access is generally associated with greater social sycophancy across four dimensions, including softened criticism. This suggests prior API-based sycophancy measurements may underestimate what the public actually experiences.

entry.title: You Only Think Once: Rescuing Hybrid Vision-Language Models Lost in Thought

author.name: Tianyi Tan, Wentao Wang, Xiaohan Li, Zining Ren, Siyuan Li, Xutao Mao, Rui Qian, Luoxi Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in hybrid vision-language models where extended chain-of-thought reasoning loops or exhausts budgets, scoring below direct answering. Rather than early-exiting a failing thought, YOTO inverts the paradigm: it collects direct answers first, and only unsettled problems receive a single thinking pass. This is a practical, well-motivated fix for reasoning-budget waste in VLMs.

entry.title: FlowPAC: Flow-Guided Visual Pruning and Action Caching for Efficient VLA Inference

author.name: Jintao Cheng, Yipu Zhang, Haozhe Wang, Lin Jiang, Jiang Xu, and Wei Zhang

entry.summary: FlowPAC accelerates vision-language-action models for edge deployment by using task-aware optical flow as a shared physical signal to jointly optimize visual token pruning and action caching, replacing static resource allocation. Components include Direction-Aware Trajectory Propagation to address fragmented KV-cache layouts and wasted compute on non-critical regions during dynamic robot interactions.

entry.title: When Video Verifier Scores Mislead: Capability Assessment and Verifier Selection

author.name: Charles Weng, Zixi Huang

entry.summary: This paper shows that video verifier evaluation scores depend strongly on the negative type and judgment interface, enough to reverse conclusions about model capability and verifier choice. Using controlled constructions with exact truth conditions (endpoint-matched negatives, truth-switch tests), the authors expose failure modes where models drop to near chance under direct judgment. This is an important caution for the increasingly common use of LLM verifiers as evaluators.

entry.title: TabK: Amortized Bayesian Estimation of the Number of Clusters in Tabular Data

author.name: Mohammadreza Bakhtyari, Bogdan Mazoure, Renato Cordeiro de Amorim, Guillaume Rabusseau, Vladimir Makarenkov

entry.summary: TabK is a zero-shot, permutation-invariant transformer that estimates the number of clusters k in tabular data as amortized Bayesian inference, replacing expensive grid searches over cluster validity indices. A novel Quantile Feature Encoder extracts position-free representations from marginal distributions, and training on a synthetic prior enables single-forward-pass estimation. This brings prior-fitted-network style amortization to a classic statistics problem.

entry.title: Cross-Site Transformers Are Robust Heart Rate Estimators

author.name: Mason Kadem and Rong Zheng

entry.summary: The Cross-Site Transformer introduces a hemodynamically informed inductive bias for multi-site PPG heart-rate estimation, restricting multi-sensor fusion to cross-attention between body sites that observe delayed copies of the same cardiac event. On WildPPG it sets a new single-model state of the art, cutting error 21% over the previous best and 35% over the best prior transformer. The cross-site restriction also improves robustness under real-world motion.

entry.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models

author.name: Navapat Nananukul, Mayank Kejriwal

entry.summary: DiVE is an ensemble method for recursive self-improvement using small open-weight models instead of frontier models, combining a shared memory, a failure log, and best-idea-wins rounds to improve diversity and creativity of generated solutions. This lets cheap models whose individual programs often crash and stall nonetheless sustain RSI loops on machine-learning tasks.

entry.title: BIRD-Persona: A Persona-Aware Benchmark for SQL and pandas Analytics Code Generation

author.name: Davin Hill, Pawan Chorasiya, Bhawani S. Leelar, Oren Avram, Robert E. Tillman, Tamer Soliman

entry.summary: BIRD-Persona extends BIRD-Python with persona-stratified (novice/expert) rewrites, matched SQL and pandas ground truth, schema variants, and task-structure annotations to isolate when text-to-code performance diverges between SQL and pandas. Across 1,534 tasks, nine models, and 245,592 evaluations, SQL outperformed pandas for eight of nine systems, with the gap varying by persona, schema representation, and task structure. This gives the code-generation community a diagnostic benchmark with practical implications for production analytics assistants.

entry.title: LoopSeek: Decoupling System One Search from System Two Answering for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Chengzhong Wang, Lang Lin, Xinyang Liu, YueQin Yin, Mingyuan Zhou, Shengwei An

entry.summary: LoopSeek decouples evidence search from answer generation for long video QA, using a non-thinking System I of four role agents that navigate a tree of video windows through typed decisions and probability outputs without text generation, feeding evidence to a generative System II. This avoids the latency of repeated text generation during adaptive frame selection under a fixed frame budget. The architecture addresses a core efficiency problem in long-video understanding.

entry.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety

author.name: Jipei He, Cheng Cheng, Liuguo Wang, Zihan Wen, Changlin Yu, Wentao Song, Suyun Zhao

entry.summary: This paper reframes multimodal safety moderation beyond binary allow/refuse into four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse, grounded in diagnostic judgments and source evidence. The authors build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark with controlled context changes, and train JudiAct, a guard that separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the response, and how rules apply, then verifies these against the input. This enables nuanced intervention when visual context changes the safety of an otherwise ordinary request.

entry.title: Diagnosing Verbalized Confidence in a Medical Vision-Language Model for Selective Prediction on Colorectal Histopathology Patches

author.name: Anay Sinhal, Amit Sinhal, Ashish Pandey, Arpana Sinhal

entry.summary: The study evaluates verbalized confidence from MedGemma-27b-it versus base Gemma-3-27b-it on roughly 17,000 histopathology patches, finding MedGemma collapses 96% of confidence to one value with near-chance confidence-correctness AUROC (0.499) while Gemma-3 achieves AUROC 0.70 and meaningful selective-prediction gains. Both models are too inaccurate for deployment (40.6% and 35.5%).

entry.title: Decoupling Perception from Generation for Agentic 3D CT Report Generation

author.name: Chenyu Wang, Mingyu Chen, Wenchao Li, and Kayhan Batmanghelich

entry.summary: This work reformulates chest CT report generation as a set of visual question-answering decisions coordinated by an LLM agent, decoupling discriminative visual perception from reasoning and report writing. This lets perception be trained as a non-generative task (better suited to limited data) while the LLM handles patient context and follow-up questions. A promising architecture for data-efficient medical report generation.

entry.title: GALILEO: Geometric RoPE with Galilean Key Transport for Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Youngmin Kim, Seonghyun Jin, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: GALILEO extends geometry-aware rotary positional encodings to dynamic scenes by transporting each key's 3D position via Galilean motion before encoding, aligning positional encodings with scene dynamics when input views are temporally separated. This fixes the static-scene assumption in methods like RayRoPE that misplace moving objects during rendering.

entry.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning

author.name: Xiaoyu Chen, Xiao Gu, Chao Zhang, Wen Wu, Shuaicong Hu, Qinfan Xiao, Jie Yang, Chen Chen, Wei Chen

entry.summary: SleepXA composes independently pretrained EEG and ECG foundation models with lightweight encoders for additional polysomnography modalities, learning shared and modality-specific representations via sleep-guided alignment, pretrained on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings. It demonstrates an alternative to training multimodal sleep models from scratch by reusing existing unimodal medical foundation models. This composition strategy could generalize to other multimodal physiological domains.

entry.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model

author.name: Zeyu Ren, Jie Ni, Rui Qian, Jiahao Wei, Hao Tang, Yongtai Liu, Zeyu Zhang

entry.summary: PINE is a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that jointly predicts point maps, surface normals, and instance segmentation in a single forward pass, using stream masks, camera-ray token positioning, and attention grounded in DINOv3 feature affinities. Trained on only 139K synthetic images, it achieves state-of-the-art point-map results.

entry.title: MAWAM: Joint Imagination for Collaborative Robot Manipulation with a Multi-Agent World Action Model

author.name: Rongze Tang, Chenyu Zhou, Jianjie Fang, Ziming Liu, Zhaolu Wang, Ziyou Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Wei Wu, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Presents MAWAM, a multi-agent world action model that jointly predicts future observations across multiple robot embodiments and decodes each agent's actions for collaborative manipulation across disjoint workspaces, coupled timing, and heterogeneous embodiments. Unlike decentralized per-robot policies or flat centralized models, it unifies spatiotemporal alignment with embodiment and role awareness. An agentic data generation pipeline supports training.

entry.title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware

author.name: Shuaiwei Huang, Weihua Du, Allen Wu, Ivan Fox, Manupa Karunaratne, Yiming Yang, Sean Welleck

entry.summary: Introduces KernelShift, a benchmarking pipeline and environments for evaluating how well coding agents optimize CPU kernels using newly introduced architectural extensions across evolving hardware. An agent-assisted, human-verified pipeline converts code repositories into benchmark instances, and agents receive feedback from target hardware during optimization.

entry.title: Exact on Paper: Which LLM Serving Shortcuts Flip Graded Answers, Measured Against the Noise of Reordering the Same Requests

author.name: Sharven Rane

entry.summary: The authors serve a 4B instruction model in vLLM under nine single-feature configurations and compare each against restart and scheduling floors, finding that seven features documented as exact still flip 1.47-1.78% of graded benchmark outcomes while aggregate accuracy stays within one point. The study measures these flips against the noise floor of merely reordering the same requests.

entry.title: From States to Dynamics: Detecting Rule Violations in OthelloGPT

author.name: David L. Cao, Sai Sumedh R. Hindupur, and Demba Ba

entry.summary: Extending interpretability work on OthelloGPT from static board states to game dynamics, this paper shows linear probes distinguish legal from illegal moves and separate three classes of rule violations (empty-square placement, flanking, turn-taking). It also introduces an unsupervised rule-violation detection method, probing whether the transformer encodes game rules, not just states.

entry.title: Continuous-time 4D Reconstruction via Event-guided Latent Feature Interpolation

author.name: Gwangtak Bae, Seunggu Kang, Junho Kim, Eun Sun Lee, Changwoon Choi, Young Min Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose continuous-time 4D reconstruction that combines geometric foundation models with event-camera measurements, formulating the task as interpolation in the latent feature space with auxiliary event-based losses in image space. This yields 3D structure and camera poses at arbitrary time instants beyond the observed RGB temporal resolution, leveraging foundation model priors while incorporating microsecond-resolution event data.

entry.title: Could This BE Any More Wrong? Teaching VLMs to Know What They Don't Know in Document Extraction

author.name: Varad Srivastava, Victor Casas Hernandez

entry.summary: The authors derive per-field confidence estimates for VLM document extraction purely from existing token log-probabilities via a token-to-span alignment over the structured JSON output. Minimum token probability per field achieves 0.74-0.91 AUROC for error detection across three VLM families, far above verbalized confidence, and the identified uncertain fields serve as a curriculum for GRPO fine-tuning that lifts CORD accuracy from 78.5 to 87.5 percent.

entry.title: Multimodal View Training: Learning More Through Different Modalities

author.name: Devang Kulshreshtha, Priyanka Kaswan, Minh Pham, Chinmay Hegde, Niv Cohen

entry.summary: Multimodal View Training (MVT) presents identical information to a model as text, speech, and rendered-text images, training a multimodal LLM to produce the same output across views without new facts or supervision. Lightweight connectors attach pretrained audio and vision encoders to text-only LLMs, and results across QA tasks suggest learning improves purely from multimodal re-encoding.

entry.title: Quantization for Action, Execution for Deployment: Joint Precision and Execution Selection for World Action Models

author.name: Tianqi Li, Xin He, Xue Geng, Le Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Yun Liu

entry.summary: PTQ4WAM jointly selects layer-wise bit assignments and execution configurations for world action models, recognizing that memory-fit and small prediction errors that flip selected actions are coupled deployment constraints. The framework avoids costly task trials while ensuring candidate plans satisfy real GPU memory and execution limits.

entry.title: BASE: A Backend-Agnostic Streaming Embodiment Layer for Full-Duplex Conversational Avatars

author.name: Chenye Yang, Jin Jiang, Shengcai Liao

entry.summary: BASE is a streaming embodiment layer that turns any full-duplex spoken dialogue model into a full-body 3D avatar using only the emitted speech as the interface, handling turn-taking, barge-in, listening feedback, and proactive turns via an audio-driven conversation state manager. This decouples motion generation from specific dialogue models, avoiding retraining when backends change and enabling attachment to audio-only cloud APIs.

entry.title: BEND: Spectral Bregman Losses for Multi-Image Unlearning in Diffusion Models

author.name: Mohamed-Hicham Leghettas, Markus P\"uschel

entry.summary: BEND addresses diffusion model unlearning by searching the family of Bregman divergences for the unlearning loss rather than defaulting to squared-L2, fitting a spectral Bregman divergence via a bilevel optimization loop. This shapes the loss itself to forget memorized training images thoroughly while preserving generation quality elsewhere. It is framed as the first method to search this loss family for unlearning.

entry.title: Body and Soul: Decoupling Robotic Brain and Policy with RoboHarness-Zero

author.name: Yihao Shen and Yuxuan Chen and Xuantong Liu and Jun Gao and Weijian Luo and Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: The paper introduces RoboHarness-Zero, a vision-language model harness that wraps frozen VLA policies to enable multi-skill task composition without task- or policy-specific preparation. Motivated by an audit of Xiaomi-Robotics-1 showing roughly 43% of failures involve wrong target selection or lost task progress, the harness is designed to require minimal task setup, no redesign for new policies, and to preserve standalone policy capabilities. It decouples high-level task reasoning from low-level policy execution.

entry.title: HOSE: Hierarchical Orthogonal Subspace Erasure for Concept Unlearning in Diffusion Models

author.name: Xiaoqi Wei, Li Li, Kejiang Chen, Hanzhou Wu, and Xinpeng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces HOSE, a model-editing method for removing harmful or sensitive concepts from text-to-image diffusion models by projecting parameter updates into subspaces orthogonal to general knowledge and handling U-Net hierarchy separately. This aims to erase target concepts while avoiding collateral damage to non-target concepts.

entry.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics

author.name: Yunpeng Qing, Yuheng Huang, Changxu Wei, Yilun Kong, Yichen Shi, Shunyu Liu, Changqing Zou

entry.summary: Introduces ActField, a continuous-time action-conditioned JEPA world model that models latent state evolution as an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time, separating action-independent evolution from action-induced changes modulated by latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss support accurate long-horizon prediction for embodied decision-making.

entry.title: EgoDepth-Bench: Benchmarking Metric Depth for Egocentric Manipulation

author.name: Yuan Gao, Dongchen Wei, Xinyang Lin, Shuhua Cao, Xueliang Guo, Zhuohan Li, Yihao Wang

entry.summary: Presents EgoDepth-Bench, a large-scale benchmark of 941,233 synchronized samples across 37 physical environments combining six calibrated RGB views with millimeter-accurate metric depth from active-infrared stereo. Environment-held-out splits measure generalization, and fine-tuning MapAnything on the benchmark sharply reduces metric error on unseen environments.

entry.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Vinay Udit Mohan, Xuchuan Huang, Rolandos Alexandros Potamias

entry.summary: The paper introduces a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations from point-cloud observations of retargeted human demonstrations, using contrastive objectives for cross-embodiment consistency. The unified latent action space directly serves as the search space for model-predictive control, enabling zero-shot transfer to unseen robot morphologies.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Wenhao Wang, Panrong Tong, Quyu Kong, Pengxiang Li, Haowen Yang, chenglin Cai, Siheng Chen, Yue Wang

entry.summary: CUA-SEE is a closed-loop evaluation environment for computer-use agents that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence, disentangling benchmark evolution (difficulty and coverage growth), diagnostic evolution (capability-boundary probes), and verifier evolution (state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation). It addresses static benchmarks' fixed difficulty ceilings and declining discriminative value.

entry.title: Demographic Encoding is Not Exposure: Fairness and Privacy in Chest X-ray Foundation Models

author.name: Sahar Askari, Amin Golnari

entry.summary: Using 200 probe heads trained on frozen BiomedCLIP, DINOv2 and RAD-DOD embeddings audited on CheXpert and ChestX-ray14, the authors show that demographic encoding in medical foundation models explains almost no variance in membership-inference vulnerability, and that erasing linearly decodable demographics leaves leakage unchanged while reducing age-related underdiagnosis gaps. Leakage instead depends on head capacity, decoupling two properties often conflated.

entry.title: Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Nan Chen, Soledad Villar, Soufiane Hayou

entry.summary: TipSweep transfers optimal learning rates across the number of trainable transformer blocks in LLM post-training (SFT, DPO, RLVR): it searches only the last k0 blocks and applies scaling rules to predict the optimal learning rate for any k, including full-model training. Experiments span 1B to 7B parameter models. This addresses the costly grid search over learning rates in post-training pipelines.

entry.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control

author.name: Zexin He, Rui Li, Yushi Lan, Chengkai Jin, Zhi Hou, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: ACAP organizes a single robot as a team of persistent coding agents, each responsible for a configurable control group (e.g., an arm with its gripper), enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. A hyper-agent assigns tasks, coordinates physical dependencies, and dynamically allocates control so independent work proceeds concurrently.

entry.title: Scrub Data: A Framework for Reproducible Data Curation with AI Coding Agents

author.name: Justin Kay, Shir Bar, Sara Beery

entry.summary: Scrub Data is a framework enabling AI coding agents to perform data curation while preserving reproducibility and verifiability, countering the risks of unverified agent-driven curation. It provides mechanisms to trace exact modifications to raw datasets and audit changes, addressing longstanding curation pain points amplified by agentic tools.

entry.title: VTree: Question-Driven Growth of Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Lianyu Hu, Zixuan Hu, Zhizhen Wu, Zeqin Liao, Shengqian Qin, Yang Liu

entry.summary: VTree builds question-driven hierarchical memory for long-video understanding, growing the memory tree toward what a specific question requires instead of using pre-committed uniform pyramids or re-exploring from scratch per question. The key observation is that coarse video structure is question-independent while zoom targets and depth are question-dependent. This reduces per-question cost and preserves fine-grained evidence for long videos.

entry.title: Seeing the Invisible: How Vision-Language Models Read, Predict and Trace Radio Fields

author.name: Yiyang Zhu, Xin Li, Guangyuan Liu, Ziheng Liu, Jiayi Zhang, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: Builds RadioVISTA, a benchmark and training dataset testing whether VLMs can infer invisible radio signal fields from visible urban structures, using a label-free engine that converts any Earth coordinate into a ray-traceable city with exact answers and single-factor counterfactuals. This enables controlled probing of physical reasoning beyond what cameras capture.

entry.title: From Observation to Explanation: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM-Generated Code for Principled Repair

author.name: Musfiqur Rahman

entry.summary: Triangulates longitudinal, empirical, and behavioral evidence on LLM code generation: agent-attributed code is statistically indistinguishable from human code semantically yet attracts disproportionately corrective modifications in production (49.1% vs 37.9%), and models scoring 84-89% on synthetic benchmarks reach only 24-35% on real-world class-level code. The work moves toward mechanistic explanation to enable principled repair of LLM-generated code.

entry.title: Med-Agentic: Distilling Agentic Medical Reasoning with Internalized Meta-Capabilities

author.name: Yucheng Zhou, Junwei Sheng, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: Med-Agentic replaces brittle external tool-call runtimes for medical visual diagnosis with internalized meta-capabilities: atomic, composable reasoning units invoked within a single chain-of-thought via capability tags rather than external calls. Training uses multi-teacher on-policy distillation with token-level dual-factor teacher routing to instill these capabilities parametrically.

entry.title: Mitigating large circuits with a learned small-circuit mitigator

author.name: Thi Ha Kyaw, Pablo D\'iez-Valle and Gaurav Saxena

entry.summary: This quantum computing work shows that circuit cutting allows a learning-based quantum error mitigation model to be reused on circuits much larger and deeper than its training distribution. The fragment-wise mitigator removes most reconstructed error on random-circuit chains and outperforms or complements baselines like zero-noise extrapolation and probabilistic error cancellation. It matters as a path to scaling learned error mitigation without expensive exact labels.

entry.title: MatHarness: Towards Long-Horizon Open-ended AutoResearch for Computational Materials Science

author.name: Yanlin Fei, Lei Li, Shaolong Chen, Nazhou Liu, Xinmiao Yu, Madalina Ciobanu, Navan Preet Singh, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: MatHarness is an agent harness for open-ended, long-horizon computational materials research covering ideation through manuscript writing, combining pre-flight execution verification, expert-distilled skills, persistent research artifacts, and a multi-agent round table with human oversight. It aims to make scientific agents less brittle than workflow-bound systems. Evaluation spans the full research lifecycle in materials science.

entry.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models

author.name: Huanran Li, Nhat X.T. Le, Kevin De Angeli, Yao Xuan, Alireza Vahdatpour, Djordje Gligorijevic

entry.summary: Engram is a memory system for LLM agents that tune neural networks, linking past trial outcomes to hypotheses and rationale and assessing applicability to the current, differently-architected model. An online agent curates evidence at decision points (initial guidance, session retrieval, trial review) while an offline agent distills validated lessons between sessions. This prevents agents from re-learning known lessons across tuning sessions on heterogeneous production models.

entry.title: WingBench: Benchmarking How AI Agents Search for Better Designs

author.name: Yiming Yang, David Xia, Jisen Li, Yuqing Jian, Yunjia Yang, Koray Aydin, Zhaoran Wang

entry.summary: WingBench is a multifidelity benchmark where optimizers and AI agents design transonic wings using a learned aerodynamic surrogate plus a fixed budget of sequential CFD evaluations that can return failures.
