It grades recommended designs separately on validity and quality, contributing a study of five optimizers and three AI agent methods across 6,629 CFD evaluation records, revealing how learned-prediction failure modes affect design search.

entry.title: Automated Safety Analysis for Agentic Workflows

author.name: Yanju Chen, Ying Li, Bosi Zhang, Hanzhi Liu, Hongbo Wen, Yufei Ding, Yuan Tian, Yu Feng

entry.summary: Presents Apsis, a static safety analyzer that detects logical design flaws in LLM agentic workflows before deployment by lifting framework-specific code into a common intermediate representation modeled as a semantic graph of steps, data dependencies, and control logic. Addresses a gap since no existing tool statically validates workflow logic across frameworks. Timely and important for safe deployment of agent-based applications.

entry.title: General-purpose language models are neurosymbolic reasoners able to annotate proteins from sequence

author.name: Christopher J. Mungall, Marcin P. Joachimiak

entry.summary: The authors test whether generalist LLMs, previously shown to perform well on next-residue prediction, can also annotate protein function from raw sequence, challenging the assumption that generalist models fail at sequence tasks and protein language models fail at symbolic tasks. The results support viewing general-purpose LLMs as neurosymbolic reasoners for biology. This has implications for gene function annotation, a major open problem across the tree of life.

entry.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries

author.name: Xinyu Cao, Tianjie Ju, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: EvoViM is a self-evolving framework where a frozen multimodal model converts interaction experience into visual programs that retain images and compute on pixels, enabling memory retention before knowing which details will matter. The model traces failures in its visual trajectories to specific operations and revises them along with its notes and analysis tools.

entry.title: DRAM: Memory-Efficient Muon via Rank Reallocation in Principal-Random Subspaces

author.name: Haomin Bai, Dingzhi Yu, Xuling Zhao, Sifan Yang, Yibo Wang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: Improves memory-efficient variants of the Muon optimizer by constructing a principal-random subspace mixing leading singular gradient directions with random directions from their orthogonal complement, and dynamically reallocating rank between exploitation and coverage. This preserves convergence guarantees while reducing storage overhead.

entry.title: VeriLadder: A Multi-Agent Specification Refinement System for Tool-Verified Verilog Datasets

author.name: Saeid Rajabi, Chengmo Yang, Satwik Patnaik

entry.summary: VeriLadder builds a five-level Verilog dataset using a multi-agent pipeline where LLM agents write and revise specifications and EDA tools (synthesizers, formal equivalence checkers) serve as acceptance judges, addressing the scarcity of correct RTL training data. Notably, 28% of RTLCoder designs fail synthesis and are retained as negatives. The tool-verified construction approach is significant for hardware code generation where correctness verification is automatable.

entry.title: Doing More with Less: Complex Manipulation with a Contact-Adaptive Robotic Hand

author.name: Hyung Gon Shin, Sanghoon Jung

entry.summary: This robotics paper presents a robotic hand mechanism designed to sidestep classic anthropomorphic hand trade-offs, offering contact-adaptive finger motion, slender fingers, wide grasping range, and sustained gripping force. It also introduces a motion glove using quaternion swing-twist decomposition to extract human manipulation intentions, plus a forearm-mounted interface. It matters for dexterous manipulation hardware, an area where most progress is algorithmic rather than mechanical.

entry.title: Multimodal LLMs Know the Game but Assume the Real World

author.name: Jianxin Gao, Bohan Chen, Runze Li, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: RuleCraft probes six widely used multimodal LLMs with 1,240 engine-verified questions over 155 Minecraft rules, asked as text, on named-game images, and on bare images. Models know the rules but answer bare images with real-world physics; naming the game lifts accuracy by 8-20 points (up to 50+ on hard sets) where games depart from reality, revealing a context-conditioning failure rather than knowledge absence.

entry.title: RadAG: Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models

author.name: Hyeongchan Jeon, Kwanyoung Kim

entry.summary: RadAG is an inference-time guidance method for diffusion and flow models that steers sampling toward reward models without backpropagating through the entire generator. It builds a reward-aware reference via reward-adversarial attention guidance, combining the efficiency of extrapolation guidance (forward passes only) with reward-directed steering previously requiring gradients.

entry.title: Pixel Auto-Encoder: Reconstructing Language Model Activations Through Pixel Art

author.name: Haru Furuichi, Phan Xuan Tan

entry.summary: This exploratory work converts intermediate LLM activations into 32x32, 32-color pixel art and reconstructs them, encouraging representations to resemble predefined concept images while preserving language capability. It investigates whether images can serve as an interpretable target modality for understanding LLM internal states, as an alternative to natural-language explanations.

entry.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation

author.name: Pujun Zheng, Chengmu Wang, Wanying Ren, Jiacheng Yao, Peizhou Yu, Xiaoqian Zhang, Xiongyao Zha, Guoxiu He

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mechanism, bias cascade, in LLM-based social simulation: models may match knowledge and isolated responses yet still fail to reproduce collective effects of interventions because small individual divergences compound through dynamic interactions. The authors introduce REFLEX, a benchmark of 30 classic human-subject experiments with reproductions, to empirically test whether simulations replicate group-level effects rather than individual judgments. The findings caution against over-reliance on LLM social simulations for causal claims.

entry.title: Eidetic Code World Model

author.name: Wenqing Tian, Zijian Zhang, Qiang Liu, Liang Wang

entry.summary: Paintress is a code-conditioned world model that combines an executable geometric proxy with a persistent 3D Gaussian appearance memory, preventing video renderers from altering previously seen scenes when they leave the camera view. It separates memory writing from reading via confidence-gated updates and a globally refined reader copy, supporting spatially consistent world modeling.

entry.title: A Design Space for Data Agents: Insights from KDD Cup 2026

author.name: Boyan Li, Zhuowen Liang, Yupeng Xie, Xiaotian Lin, Xinyu Liu, Yizhang Zhu, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: The authors analyze final submissions from the ten top-ranked teams in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition, organizing design choices into three layers: workflow orchestration, analytical functions, and working state. They identify recurring patterns for budget-aware computation, evidence structuring, and artifact provenance, and note pitfalls like correlated errors from shared evidence.

entry.title: Elicitation format changes zero-shot classification accuracy in a medical vision-language model: a two-center evaluation on colorectal histopathology

author.name: Anay Sinhal, Amit Sinhal, Arpana Sinhal

entry.summary: Holding a colorectal histopathology prompt fixed except for response format, the authors show MedGemma-27b-it accuracy drops 14.8 and 13.4 points at two centers when asked for nine-class probabilities instead of a ranked top-3, noting the nine-class prompt also forbade commentary, reasoning, and a chosen answer. The study uses preregistered endpoints and randomized tie handling.

entry.title: Hypothesis Generation and Semantic Attribution in Inverse Perturbation Modeling

author.name: Pascal Passigan, Manolis Kellis

entry.summary: Using LINCS L1000 CRISPR perturbation profiles, the authors train a graph neural network over a sparse typed gene network to recover the perturbed gene from baseline and endpoint expression, then use this inverse formulation to nominate inspectable hypotheses for steering malignant transcriptional programs toward favorable-prognosis expression. Nodes combine protein representations with expression features; edges encode signed regulatory relationships. The work aims to connect black-box learned computation to biological knowledge for intervention design.

entry.title: Decoding Transformer Dynamics via Koopman Subspaces

author.name: Subhradeep Kayal, Ali Dashti

entry.summary: This paper applies Koopman operator theory and Dynamic Mode Decomposition to LLM hidden-state evolution, treating layer-to-layer transitions as a dynamical system and using dominant-mode subspaces as topic spectral fingerprints. It finds the depth map is near-linear, fingerprints are topic-discriminative across 57 MMLU subjects, and are reproducible signatures.

entry.title: Fixed or Deleted? External Feedback Lets Cheaper AI Coding Agents Repair Rule Violations

author.name: Laura Wynter

entry.summary: This empirical study tests whether LLM coding agents repair rule violations (layering constraints, required tests) better when an external checker such as CodeAssure reports findings with locations and repair goals. It evaluates small, medium, and large models across 25 pull requests with 31 planted defects in ten open-source projects, comparing against Copilot code review and nine free static-analysis tools. Results indicate external feedback lets cheaper agents match stronger ones on rule repair.

entry.title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics

author.name: Conghan Yue, Yuanjie Chen, Yunyan Xiao, Zeyu Peng, Xingsong Ye, Ya Gao, Yanglin Huang, WeiYao Zhang, Yue Han, Zhineng Chen, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: PhyCoVE is a benchmark of 533 cases on 110 source videos for physical counterfactual video editing, covering rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics across five interaction patterns with removal, quantity-change, and insertion edits. It uses LLM-proposed scene designs built by coding agents with appropriate physics solvers to construct grounded evaluation cases. Substantially broadens counterfactual video evaluation beyond object removal and rigid motion.

entry.title: Edit-Induced Dependency Mismatch: Propagation Omissions, Recovery, and Evaluation Blind Spots in Coding Agents

author.name: Fei Ding

entry.summary: This study examines how coding agents rely on outdated dependency judgments after code edits, causing propagation omissions and consumer defects that standard benchmarks miss. Through blinded human audits of agent trajectories on DeepSWE and SWE-bench Verified using existing models like DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash, it documents terminal mismatches and exposes evaluation blind spots in current coding-agent benchmarks.

entry.title: A2I-VLA: A Two-Stage Vision-Language-Action model with Semantic-Physical Alignment and Integration

author.name: Kun Dai, Tianqi Wang, Haibo Lei, Chaoyang Li, Kai Zhang, Fuyuan Qiu, Lijun Zhao, Ruifeng Li, Chuqing Cao, Tao Xie, Wenming Tan

entry.summary: A2I-VLA is a two-stage vision-language-action framework that first learns semantically aligned force-tactile representations via a cross-modal alignment loss, then integrates them into a VLA model through hierarchical multimodal fusion. It targets contact-rich manipulation where visual observations alone cannot capture physical interaction dynamics.

entry.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?

author.name: Yuechen Jiang, Enze Zhang, Yuyan Wang, Mohsinul Kabir, Chenying Lin, Sijia Li, Qianqian Xie, Stavroula Golfomitsou, Konstantinos Arvanitis, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: Polytropos is a benchmark measuring what VLM descriptions of cultural objects preserve, by reconstructing images from 1,870 model-generated and 230 curator-written descriptions of 374 museum artifacts and comparing them to originals. Strikingly, reconstructions are recognized as the recorded culture more often than the original photographs, yet lose object particulars, revealing how models typify rather than particularize culture. It offers a novel, humanities-grounded lens on multimodal model behavior.

entry.title: Contact Harness: Enabling VLM Agents to Perform Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Shilin Shan, Yuxuan Hu, Chuhao Zhou, Yimeng Dong, Bohan Hou, Jiaqi Bai, Boyu Ma, Jiahua Dong, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Contact Harness enables zero-shot VLM-based robot agents to handle contact-rich manipulation by using reusable optimized skills to interpret force and tactile feedback alongside vision, plus compliant in-contact execution. It requires no fine-tuning, demonstrations, or simulation training.

entry.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction

author.name: Matteo Ciferri, Tonio Weidler, Matteo Ferrante, Nicola Toschi and Elia Formisano

entry.summary: Introduces MAAS, an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer (Stable Audio) directly on ROI-wise 7T fMRI responses using region-specific projections and learned brain tokens via cross-attention. This bypasses the usual step of decoding neural activity into an intermediate stimulus representation. It shows consistent improvements in brain-to-audio reconstruction and offers insight into cortical sound encoding.

entry.title: CompareDR: Benchmarking Deep Research Reports from Individual Quality to Comparative Merit

author.name: Wanli Wu, He Zhu, Yue Xu, Haolin Ren, Yan Chen, XunLiang Cai, Fan Yang, LingChuan Liu, Shizhu He

entry.summary: Introduces CompareDR, a benchmark combining task-specific pointwise audits with guideline-based pairwise comparisons to evaluate deep research report generators. It uses passage-linked representations to locate relevant differences and selective evidence verification, spanning 40 Chinese and English tasks and 360 reports from nine systems.

entry.title: One Checkpoint, Four Converters: Per Input Disagreement After On Device Conversion and a Probe Set That Catches It

author.name: Sharven Rane

entry.summary: This paper shows that INT8 conversion for on-device inference can keep top-1 accuracy unchanged while flipping more than 1% of individual predictions, with each of four converters' recipes moving decisions differently; ONNX Runtime static INT8 flips 4.07% of ResNet-50 decisions while accuracy moves by only -0.15 points. The authors release a probe set designed to catch such per-input disagreements.

entry.title: Reasoning Beyond Imitation: Observation Conditioned Distillation for Video LLMs

author.name: Junzhou Chen, Jindong Wang, Gang Zhou

entry.summary: This work identifies a Reasoning Acquisition-Execution Gap in video-LLM distillation: teacher and student sample videos differently, so teacher reasoning trajectories may rely on evidence the student cannot observe. The proposed acquisition-to-execution framework first distills teacher trajectories into a reasoning prior, then optimizes execution under the student's own observations.

entry.title: When Simpler Beats Learned: Dual-Weighted Sampling vs. Machine Learning for the Pricing Subproblem in Graph Coloring

author.name: Nikolai Antonov, P\v{r}emysl \v{S}\r{u}cha, Mikol\'a\v{s} Janota, Jan H\r{u}la

entry.summary: The paper shows that the state-of-the-art machine-learning pricing heuristic for branch-and-price graph coloring can be matched or beaten by Dual-Weighted Sampling, which replaces learned vertex scores with the dual solution of the restricted master problem, requiring no training or feature engineering. It critically reassesses the value of ML in this pipeline within a unified framework.

entry.title: Memphis: A Case Study in Seeding an Agent Task from a Model's Real-World Attempt

author.name: Ibrahim A. Ahmed, Ahmed Sameh Khalil

entry.summary: The authors propose building agent evaluations by simulating tasks from a model's own real-world attempt, so simulated failures mirror real failures. As a case study, GPT-6.1 Sol, an existing frontier model, managed two human workers in Cairo over five shifts to build USB desk lamps, then the transcript seeded the Memphis evaluation, on which the model repeats its real mistakes such as buying too few stands.

entry.title: Ego2Wrist: Bootstrapping Wrist-View Synthesis from Egocentric Video

author.name: Ziyao Zeng, Xiatao Sun, Hao Wang, Ziyu Guo, Youheng Yao, Jingcheng Ni, Shenyuan Gao, Fengyu Yang, Renrui Zhang, Bangya Liu, Daniel Rakita

entry.summary: Ego2Wrist synthesizes synchronized wrist-camera views from scalable head-mounted egocentric videos and task descriptions, trained on roughly 940 hours of paired head- and wrist-camera recordings and jointly generating three views. The paper also proposes hand-centric cross-view consistency (HCC), a metric for evaluating generated wrist views without ground truth.

entry.title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays

author.name: Tardelli Ronan Coelho Stekel

entry.summary: The paper introduces BRESSAY, a benchmark of 1,000 handwritten Brazilian Portuguese essays with metrics for error preservation, edit markup, and line structure, and trains Escriba-OCR, a 1B-parameter open-weight vision-language model for faithful transcription of student writing. Existing open baselines, even at 235B scale, fail to preserve misspellings and edit marks reliably.

entry.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability

author.name: Himanshu Gupta, Brendan Crowe, Christoffer Heckman, Bradley Hayes, Zachary Sunberg

entry.summary: A systematic study of how to encode particle-filter belief states as inputs to RL policies under partial observability, comparing statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function features, and permutation-invariant set encoders across eight tasks. It finds Set Transformers with appropriate pretraining perform best and characterizes when pretraining helps.

entry.title: Segment Anything In-Context via Visual Demonstrations

author.name: Yuzhu Wang and Manni Duan and Hongliang Ye and Shu Kong

entry.summary: SAYD is a foundation model for in-context segmentation that, given prompt images with segmentation masks, segments coherent regions in a query image via visual correspondences, generalizing to unseen tasks including those hard to specify in language. It is trained on 12 public panoptic segmentation datasets using a lightweight prompt-agnostic mask decoder and mechanisms for recognizing novel query classes.

entry.title: MORSE: Optimizing Streaming Memory Design via Open-World Auto-Research

author.name: Ce Zhang, Jianshu Zhang, Jinxi He, Xiyuan Yang, Pan Wang, Han Liu, Katia Sycara, Yaqi Xie

entry.summary: MORSE is an open-world auto-research framework for streaming video memory design in which an editor clusters recurring failures by cause and searches prior literature and existing solutions before devising repairs. This extends recursive self-improvement beyond predefined toolsets, letting the system reuse knowledge from problems already solved elsewhere.

entry.title: A Polynomial-Time Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Matroid Semi-Bandit Problems

author.name: Botao Chen, Junya Honda

entry.summary: The authors prove Best-of-Both-Worlds guarantees for Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader with Frechet and Pareto perturbations plus geometric resampling in matroid semi-bandits, achieving minimax-optimal O(sqrt(mdT)) adversarial regret and logarithmic stochastic regret. This yields, to their knowledge, the first polynomial-time BOBW algorithm for this setting, avoiding per-round optimization required by FTRL-based approaches.

entry.title: AutoSECO: Automated Skill Evolution for Cross-Problem Combinatorial Optimization with General-Purpose LLM Agents

author.name: Zirui Zhu, Cong Zhang, Ni Zhang, Kuan Xu, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: AutoSECO is a method enabling LLM agents that build combinatorial optimization solvers to accumulate reusable development guidance across problems. It traces solver performance shortfalls back to decisions made during development, revises skill instructions, and retains changes only when a freshly built solver improves. This turns one-off solver engineering experience into transferable knowledge.

entry.title: PathStream: Towards Streaming Diagnostic Copilots for Whole-Slide Pathology

author.name: Dankai Liao, YuFeng Wu, Ziyue Wang, Guanxi Liu, Tianyi Zhang, Zeyu Liu, Linghan Cai, Yueming Jin

entry.summary: PathStream formalizes pathologist-led streaming diagnosis, where the pathologist navigates a whole-slide image while a copilot describes incoming views and accumulates evidence toward a diagnosis. The authors recorded five pathologists viewing trajectories across 1,791 TCGA slides in ten organs and built PathStreamBench to assess response timing, morphological description quality, and diagnostic synthesis.

entry.title: PCC: Pivotal Channel Compensation for Layer Pruning of Large Language Models

author.name: Xiangqian Wang, Yucheng Zhang, Zhaohong Jia, Kun Jing, Chunchun Li

entry.summary: The paper observes that a large share of representational information concentrates in a few pivotal channels and proposes PCC, a post-pruning compensation method for layer pruning that adjusts only these channels. This yields significant performance recovery after multi-layer removal at far lower cost than prior compensation schemes.

entry.title: Uncovering Separable and Composable Skill Mechanisms in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Miaoyu Li and Boyang Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes separability and composability as desiderata for localizing visual reasoning skill mechanisms in VLMs, and introduces DISCO, a multi-skill interpretability framework that identifies mechanisms contributing selectively to target skills and that can be combined to support complex tasks. This enables precise diagnosis and targeted intervention.

entry.title: Seeing Together, Acting Apart: Shared Environmental Understanding for Multi-Robot Navigation

author.name: Haihong Hao, Lei Chen, Mingfei Han, Chenglong Yan, Dong An, Yuqiang Yang, Changlin Li, Minghao Guo, Salman Khan, Xiaojun Chang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Shared Environmental Understanding, a policy-agnostic shared latent world model built from multiple robots' egocentric observations, shifting collaboration from policy space to representation space. Its SEER framework organizes multi-robot observations into shared memory and retrieves relevant context to support decentralized navigation decisions.

entry.title: Learning Teacher Output Preferences from Final Responses for Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Hongli Shen, Shaopeng Fu, Qinbo Zhang, Jian Li, Di Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Final-Output Preference Learning, a model-agnostic approach to reconstructing hidden chain-of-thought traces from arbitrary LLMs using only prompts and visible final responses. A single reconstruction model learns which reasoning patterns match a given final response, generalizing to unseen target models without per-target attackers.

entry.title: Time Series Foundation Models on the Edge

author.name: Marco Pichler, Patrick Podest, G\"unter Klambauer, Sepp Hochreiter

entry.summary: This paper analyzes what time series foundation models require to serve as streaming forecasters on resource-constrained edge devices: bounded latency and memory as streams grow, plus accuracy retention under accumulating history. It establishes that temporal causality is key, distinguishing non-causal recomputation, linearly growing KV caches for causal attention, and constant-time fixed-state updates for causal recurrent models, with implications for model choice in deployment.

entry.title: SCAN: Neural Additive Networks for Scalable High-Order Component Selection and Estimation

author.name: Seokhun Park, Kunwoong Kim, and Yongdai Kim

entry.summary: SCAN extends neural functional ANOVA models by letting the network learn which features each basis function combines, jointly selecting and estimating components of arbitrary order without pre-enumerating candidate interactions. A shared global component-selection parameter and truncation of negligible weights yield sparse, interpretable models.

entry.title: When Do Spatial Plans Help Text-to-Image Generation? Causal Control, System Utility, and Text Responsiveness

author.name: Lu Han, Jingyao Zhang

entry.summary: This controlled study examines when providing explicit spatial plans improves text-to-image generation, finding that plan corrections yield small gains and that direct text is non-inferior at matched training compute. However, a fixed rule layout helps pretrained generators on two-object tasks, and a minimum-gap instruction alone yields up to 37 points of improvement on text-only adapters. The results clarify that the value of spatial conditioning depends heavily on the model's existing text responsiveness.

entry.title: Near-Far Attention: Region-Aware Sparse Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Decoding

author.name: YuanShuo Wang, Jianchao Tan, Lei Gong, Teng Wang, Wenqi Lou and Xuehai Zhou

entry.summary: Near-Far Attention improves long-context sparse decoding by adapting retrieval to regional attention patterns: a Lightweight Gate Estimator during prefill identifies skippable regions at under 1% prefill overhead, while a Calibration-Free Subspace Extractor provides shared features for page- and token-level scoring without offline calibration. A Distance-Aware Two-Level Selector scores near and far context differently, reducing selection overhead relative to uniform page scoring.

entry.title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jiawei Guo, Yu Huang, Dijiang Dong, Yue Liu, Peiran Ren, Wei Shen

entry.summary: RoboInF measures how reliably manipulation policies adapt behavior to instruction changes, using eight tasks with six to twelve expert-validated instruction branches each that vary goal, procedure, or manipulation detail while holding scene and robot state fixed. Task-specific checkers verify terminal goals and recorded execution, separating instruction fidelity from perception, planning, and generalization confounds found in existing benchmarks. This provides cleaner evidence of true instruction following.

entry.title: Reliable Recursive Memory for Causal Multi-scale Video Polyp Segmentation

author.name: Tong Wang, Wenbo Peng, Yaolei Qi, Yuting He, Yutong Xie, Guanyu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes STREAM, a streaming framework for video polyp segmentation in computer-aided colonoscopy, extending prior causal multi-scale aggregation work to online streams. Its Recursive Slot Memory summarizes multi-scale features compactly, handling scale change, blur, and occlusion without cost growing with history length or propagating degraded frames.

entry.title: GSDet: Gaussian Splatting for Oriented Object Detection

author.name: Zeyu Ding, Jiaqi Zhao, Yong Zhou, Wen-liang Du, Hancheng Zhu, Rui Yao

entry.summary: Reformulates oriented object detection as Gaussian splatting in a 3D feature space, where 3D Gaussians representing oriented objects are projected to 2D and transformed into oriented boxes, avoiding predefined anchors or queries. It jointly optimizes Gaussian mean, anisotropic covariance, and related parameters.

entry.title: Omniprediction with the Minimum Number of Linear Scores

author.name: MohammadHossein Bateni, Zahra Hadizadeh, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Shayan Taherijam

entry.summary: Settles an open question from STOC 2025 by proving that a single single-index model (SIM) suffices for exact omniprediction with binary matching losses in the population model, where the prior result required O(1/eps^2) SIMs. The result holds for any compact family of continuous nondecreasing transformations.

entry.title: Hard to Translate, Harder to Detect: Human Analysis Remains Essential in AI Meme Translation

author.name: Olga Zamaraeva, Carla Mart\'inez, Carlos G\'omez-Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Presents a dataset and evaluation setup for translating culturally loaded Soviet comedy quotations that function as memes in Russian, studying whether AI difficulty estimators and web-searching translators can detect and handle these passages. GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5, used as existing frontier systems, improve most with human-validated difficulty analyses, with GPT-6 Sol approaching approved references in human evaluation.

entry.title: Same Seed, Different Picture? Deciding Early at Low Resolution for Seed-Faithful Few-Step Flow Sampling

author.name: Huiran Duan, Weilun Feng, Yuqi Li, Yingli Tian

entry.summary: Traces the loss of seed fidelity in few-step flow samplers for text-to-image models to the first sampling steps, where coarse noise determines image structure at high noise levels. It proposes Decide-then-Render, a training-free sampler that resolves composition in cheap low-resolution steps before rendering at full resolution, preserving seed faithfulness at a third of the cost.

entry.title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It

author.name: Paul Mattes and Ayman Abdeldayem and Denis Shcherba and Wojciech Samek and Marc Toussaint

entry.summary: Proposes WAVE, which extends a pretrained single-object manipulation skill to scenes with many objects without updating its weights, via a selection policy and a warping policy that emits affine multipliers and offsets for every quantity the skill reads and outputs. This reframes object-count generalization as an interface problem solved by warping a frozen expert rather than retraining.

entry.title: PVFormer: Proper Velocity Transformer for Stable and Scalable Hyperbolic Representation Learning

author.name: Xianglong Shi, Nicu Sebe, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Ziheng Chen

entry.summary: PVFormer is presented as the first Transformer that operates natively and intrinsically in hyperbolic space, addressing coupled attention primitives (transformation, similarity, aggregation) that existing Poincare- or Lorentz-based designs handle awkwardly. The goal is stable and scalable hyperbolic representation learning for hierarchical data.

entry.title: Replay Before You Reply: Second-Look Prompting for Unified Multimodal Encoding

author.name: Yicheng Zhang, Xun Zhang, Jingyuan Ma, Tianyu Yu, Yuan Yao

entry.summary: Second-Look Prompting is a training-free method that repeats the image-question pair in a VLM input so every token can attend to the complete multimodal context, yielding a unified encoding under causal attention. Across 12 benchmarks SLP improves performance, and intriguingly, even blank visual tokens in the repeated copy contribute computation beyond re-exposing the image.

entry.title: Personalization of a Commercial Powered Knee Prosthesis Under Clinically Realistic Conditions via Reinforcement Learning: A Feasibility Study

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Atli \"Orn Sverrisson, David Langlois, Ming Liu, Varun Nalam, and He Huang

entry.summary: This feasibility study applies a constraint-embedded reinforcement learning tuning method (PICE) to personalize a commercial powered knee prosthesis for human users in clinically realistic walking conditions. Initialization from an offline-learned policy allowed each participant to reach personalization goals within 8-18 tuning steps, i.e., only 1.7-4.2 minutes of walking.

entry.title: Generalizing Agentic Robotics via Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xinxin Liu, Anh Dao, Wenrui Bao, Rafid Ahmed, Bingxin Xu, Ming Li, Chen Chen, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies whether multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD), borrowed from LLM post-training, can consolidate domain-specialist robot planners into a single generalist planner that issues tool calls, avoiding costly proprietary APIs and per-domain RL. It evaluates MOPD against alternative consolidation methods for agentic robotics.

entry.title: WildAnySplat: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild

author.name: Richard Shaw, Arthur Moreau, Athanasios Papaioannou, Thomas Tanay, Zhensong Zhang, Eduardo P\'erez-Pellitero

entry.summary: WildAnySplat is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for novel-view synthesis from in-the-wild multi-view images corrupted by transient occluders, illumination changes, and camera ISP effects. It uses a student-teacher setup where a teacher on clean images supervises a student on wild inputs toward transient-robust, appearance-consistent canonical 3D representations, with a pseudo-paired data strategy to overcome data scarcity.

entry.title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives

author.name: Nicolas Bolouri and Gaya Mehenni and Daniel Toyama

entry.summary: Habitats is a framework for open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives, maintaining a population of reward-policy pairs evaluated under every population reward to build a cross-fitness matrix exposing self-mastery, transfer, and functional diversity. A population-level Planner selects parent rewards and issues mutation directives, while a separate Mutator implements them. This decouples what to explore from how to implement it, addressing a limitation of task-fixed reward generation.

entry.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting

author.name: Ramraj Chandradevan, Sayontan Ghosh, Vinoth Selvendran

entry.summary: CO-GRAFT is a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework that decomposes RL accuracy gains in LLM search agents into four functional roles (reasoning, decision, query generation, answer extraction) by evaluating all 16 role assignments between an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization within shared trajectories. Shapley values from this cooperative game reveal which capabilities actually improve or interact during training.

entry.title: Efficient Memory-Constrained Video Object Segmentation via Subspace Optimization

author.name: Hai-Anh Le, Le-Trung Nguyen, Enzo Tartaglione

entry.summary: The paper identifies temporal redundancy in memory-based video object segmentation, showing consecutive frames have highly overlapping low-rank subspaces that remain stable over time. It proposes Memory Subspace Iteration (MSI), a training-free, model-agnostic plugin that compresses streaming memory features by exploiting this subspace stability, preserving segmentation accuracy across standard VOS benchmarks while reducing memory and computation. A clean efficiency contribution applicable to existing memory-based VOS models.

entry.title: When Recognition Meets Discovery: Learning Need Not Be Entangled in One Representation Space

author.name: Chenglin Liu, An Tian, Mingxuan Du, Shang Rui Yang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes Generalized Category Discovery and shows via spectral analysis a fundamental asymmetry: old-class discrimination concentrates in dominant singular directions while novel-class structure lives in the residual space, and improving one can degrade the other. It proposes separating recognition and discovery representation spaces rather than entangling them in one shared geometry. This reframes GCD as competing for representation capacity, not just optimization weight.

entry.title: Variable Importance Recovery in Tabular Foundation Models: A Simulation Study

author.name: Vasil Yasenov, Nicholas Adams-Cohen

entry.summary: This Monte Carlo simulation study examines whether tabular foundation models, which now match gradient boosting on prediction, can recover population-level variable importance. The framework distinguishes multiple estimands, pairs each with an aligned model-agnostic estimator, and evaluates ranking, support, and magnitude recovery against established baselines.

entry.title: Defending Vision-Language-Action Models against Transferable Attacks via Visual-Proprioceptive Consistency

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Ming F. Li, Han Xu

entry.summary: Observing that transferable adversarial attacks on VLA models share a common effect of disrupting visual perception of the robot's own state, this paper proposes a defense grounded in trusted proprioceptive information. The robot's proprioceptive state establishes a spatial reference compared against visually inferred position to detect and mitigate attacks. It offers a cheap, sensor-redundancy-based robustness mechanism for VLA systems.

entry.title: SoK: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning

author.name: Zhuotao Lian, Qingkui Zeng, Weiyu Wang

entry.summary: A systematization-of-knowledge that questions the consensus that distributed backdoor attacks in federated learning are stronger due to trigger splitting, running 875 paired federated runs to disentangle adding attackers from splitting the trigger. Findings indicate adding attackers, not trigger splitting, drives the reported success advantage, and prior evaluations never tested whether individual trigger pieces remain effective. A valuable myth-busting contribution to federated learning security.

entry.title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales

author.name: Kun Li, Tian Luo, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Yifeng Chen, Xinfu He, Yunquan Zhang, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu

entry.summary: This paper tackles the simulation-to-engineering-timescale gap in material degradation by learning to identify the rare atomic events that drive lasting structural change, using spatial defect environment and kinetic history as context that instantaneous configurations miss. The approach enables mechanism-resolved predictions across metre and year scales from atomistic events. This is an ambitious cross-scale scientific ML contribution with potential materials-science impact.

entry.title: CHORD: Closed-loop Human-Object Rectified-flow Decomposition

author.name: Yi Wang, Yubo Zhao, Chi-Keung Tang

entry.summary: CHORD is a two-stage rectified-flow framework for text-driven 3D human-object interaction generation that settles interaction variables (object pose, contact regions, limb posture) in a compact draft plan and observes that plan against the object surface during generation. It avoids entangling core interaction variables with dozens of joints or relying on post-hoc contact refinement. This advances generative modeling of physically plausible coupled human-object motion.

entry.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding

author.name: Junyi Yang, Zheng Si, Yilin Zhai, Pengpeng Ouyang, Hongxi Wang, Kangze Li, Mo Chen, Sicong Zhang, Hua Wang, Dongyuan Wu, Dong Chen, Mingliang Xu

entry.summary: HighwayVerse is a benchmark of 14,143 real-world images spanning a four-stage highway inspection chain: anomaly detection, recognition, condition analysis, and maintenance resolution, covering components beyond pavement such as guardrails, glare screens, and drainage. It enables evaluation of MLLMs on progressive diagnostic reasoning rather than isolated tasks.

entry.title: More Is Never Less: Affordable Robustness to Additive Attacks via Monotone Multiple-Instance Learning

author.name: Alexander Herzog, Shae McFadden and Lorenzo Cavallaro

entry.summary: This paper shows that static malware detectors using sum-pooled sparse feature representations are vulnerable to additive evasion attacks where benign content cancels malicious evidence, and that post-training features are invisible under fixed vocabularies. The authors reframe malware detection as monotone multiple-instance learning over set-shaped features, preventing added benign features from outweighing malicious ones. The approach aims to deliver robustness at low deployment cost.

entry.title: From Dense to Sparse: Morton-Ordered Sparse Mapping for Efficient 3D Mesh Generation

author.name: Junjie Yang, Rui Qian, Yijiang Li, Jinyi Xu, Yuhao Yan, Xinjian Yi, Yanfeng Li, Mingxuan Li, Xiang Wan, Jicong Fan, Siqi Liu, Ahmed Elazab, Changmiao Wang

entry.summary: SPAC combines a sparse SDF VQ-VAE with 3D Byte-Pair Encoding over Morton-serialized faces to create compact 3D mesh token sequences preserving spatial proximity. A shared LLM both captions geometry and generates tokens that decode into text-conditioned meshes, supporting unified 3D understanding and generation.

entry.title: RAGA: Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars from a Single Photo

author.name: Sadia Mubashshira, John Quarles, Kevin Desai

entry.summary: RAGA creates animatable full-body Gaussian avatars from a single photo in about one second and can refresh them as new images of the same person become available, without retraining or gradient optimization. New observations are fused in canonical UV space via visibility- and angle-weighted running sums and re-decoded by the original single-image decoder. It outperforms LHM and LHM++ baselines across 163 clips from five datasets.

entry.title: SilentWAM: Planning in the Masked State of a Diffusion World Model

author.name: Ziyu Zhao, Casey Sun, Zeyu Wang, Shicong Ma, Emily T Zhang, Cheng Lu

entry.summary: SilentWAM is a world-action model planner that reads hidden states of masked future tokens without decoding future frames, pretraining on driving video with frame-level masked world modeling built on MMaDA. Planning queries attend to masked positions so trajectories are predicted in a single forward pass, avoiding costly frame generation.

entry.title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images

author.name: Yan Wang, Yiran Song, Zizhuo Gong, Jianxiang Qi, Zhongxing Xu, Lingfei Qian, Minquan Lin

entry.summary: This work formulates cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV): checking whether an agent's magnified observation in a whole-slide image actually originates from its claimed location, with recovery and abstention options. The authors introduce PyraFault, a benchmark of 3.06 million coordinate-supervised examples from 2,200 TCGA cases, and ZoomTrace, a claim-independent verifier. This addresses a real trust and hallucination problem for pathology agents.

entry.title: Tacinf: A Unified Tactile Infrastructure for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Qiwei Wu, Xiangyu Chen, Xin Xiang, Rui Zhang, Yihang Kang, Weiran Chen, Zikang Xie, Yangfan Li, Tao Wang, Xiangzheng Wang, Tianyi Bi, Zhiyan Zhang, Xianpeng Wang, Mingqian Zhou, Yan Yu, Chuanyu Li, Wenjie Zhang, Tao Li, Weihua Zhang, Renjing Xu, Junjie Lai

entry.summary: Tacinf is a modular, low-cost infrastructure unifying tactile sensing for force-aware manipulation: simulation data synthesis and benchmarking (Tabero), vision-tactile-language-action policy learning, handheld data collection matching deployment hardware (Tacumi), and sim-to-real evaluation (Taco). It enables policies to predict actions and fingertip forces from language, vision, and touch, with optional force-level specification in instructions.

entry.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields

author.name: Hu Zhou and Jiazhou Zhou and Shuowen Zhang and Ying-Chang Liang and Liang Liu

entry.summary: RadioWorld adapts a world model to synthesize radio-frequency radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, requiring no reference RF measurements at inference. It addresses generalization to unseen scenes and extrapolation beyond measurement vicinities, relevant to 6G communication and sensing.

entry.title: SWIFT: A Handcrafted, Arithmetic-Minimal FPGA Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Chirantan Banerjee, Soumita Chatterjee, Bhargab B. Bhattacharya, and Hafizur Rahaman

entry.summary: SWIFT is a handcrafted streaming detector for audio deepfakes operating in the high-frequency noise domain where synthesis artifacts concentrate, using integer fixed-point descriptors and tree-based fusion suitable for FPGA deployment. With leakage-controlled nested cross-validation it reportedly reaches strong accuracy while being far cheaper than neural detectors on edge hardware. It matters for deployable, low-power defenses against voice-cloning attacks on authentication systems.

entry.title: Can Speech LLMs Recognize When Audio Evidence Is Insufficient? A Diagnostic Study and a Pre-Generation Probing Mitigation

author.name: Vladislav Nesterenko, Polina Doronicheva, Olga Golubeva, Polina Sheviakova

entry.summary: This diagnostic study shows speech LLMs like Qwen2-Audio fabricate answers on unanswerable audio questions, and critically demonstrates that synthesized-speech evaluations mislead: an ASR cascade that looked safe on synthetic data hallucinates at similar rates to end-to-end models on human-read recordings. The authors also propose a pre-generation probing mitigation.

entry.title: Fill in the Blanks: Non-Autoregressive Schema-Parallel Key Information Extraction with CTC Decoding

author.name: Shaked Perek, Avihu Dekel, Ben Wiesel, Sivan Harary, Eli Schwartz

entry.summary: The paper proposes a non-autoregressive vision-language extractor for key information extraction that exploits the known answer schema: it writes structure from the schema, sizes lists with a count pass, and predicts all values in parallel using CTC decoding within fixed slot blocks. Decoding passes do not grow with document length, offering substantial efficiency gains.

entry.title: Breaking the Cascade: Compact Nonlinear Optical Computing with Single-Layer Encoder-Decoder Co-Localization

author.name: Yuntian Wang, Alexander Chen, Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates nonlinear optical computing with a single phase-only diffractive surface via an encoder-decoder co-localization architecture, where coherent interference between input-dependent encoder and static decoder fields plus intensity detection yields programmable nonlinear mappings. The authors prove the design is a universal approximator for band-limited nonlinear functions without nonlinear optical materials or multiple layers.

entry.title: How Multi-Timescale Memory Cools Optimization: Theory and Evidence from AdEMAMix

author.name: Jacopo Graldi, Antonio Orvieto, Anastasia Koloskova

entry.summary: Explains why adding a slow momentum timescale to AdamW (as in AdEMAMix) improves LLM pretraining: under decoupled weight decay, independently weighted slow momentum raises parameter norms while contributing little instantaneous update power, acting as an endogenous annealing schedule. The paper derives exact norm dynamics and shows weight decay controls how long update correlations influence optimization.

entry.title: GravHMR: Coupling SLAM and Human Mesh Recovery in a Shared Gravity Frame

author.name: Hanglei Jin, Chenglu Sun, Junchen Ge, Yuchao Wang, Siqi Chen, Yuzhi Huang, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: GravHMR is a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples SLAM and human mesh recovery through a shared gravity-aligned reference frame to recover globally consistent 3D human motion from monocular video under dynamic cameras. Yaw-Aware Orientation Optimization corrects body and velocity orientation inconsistencies about the gravity axis, reducing drift.

entry.title: Why Units Die in the Layer After a Frozen Random Encoder, and What the Number of Live Units Measures

author.name: Scott M. Norton

entry.summary: This paper investigates why ReLU units die in networks trained on top of frozen random convolutional encoders for Atari RL, identifying an input offset ratio (mean magnitude relative to variance) as the driver of unit death. The author revises an earlier claim, showing that live-unit count reflects this offset statistic rather than game complexity, across agents, classifiers, reservoir computers, and sparse autoencoders.

entry.title: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios from Role-Typed Signal Temporal Logic Specifications Drafted by Large Language Models

author.name: Zifan Zeng, Qunli Zhang, Peng Wang, Shiming Liu, Feng Liu, and Zheng Hu

entry.summary: The authors generate rare safety-critical driving scenarios for testing automated vehicle planners by expressing scenario types as signal temporal logic specifications with role-typed clauses, drafted by an LLM and validated by a type checker. A compiler then derives an optimization that edits diffusion model samples to realize the adversarial scenarios, addressing the problem of the vehicle under test cancelling or absorbing attacks.

entry.title: Arcadian: Open-Source Humanoid Ecosystem for Accessible and Customizable Research and Education

author.name: Zelin Shen, Gabriel Ramos Salinas, Qiyu Zhang, Yue Qin, Chen Qian, Yanran Ding

entry.summary: Arcadian is an open-source meter-scale humanoid hardware and software ecosystem designed for research and education groups with limited fabrication resources. It uses metal-embedded 3D printing to avoid CNC machining while retaining durability, and is validated with simulation and hardware tests including reinforcement-learning locomotion.

entry.title: MoMa-NMP: Scene-Scale Neural Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators

author.name: Adam Kan, Jason Jingzhou Liu, Jiahui Yang, Kenneth Shaw, and Deepak Pathak

entry.summary: This work introduces MoMa-DemoSmith, a demonstration-generation pipeline that separates global path discovery from local motion refinement, enabling millions of whole-body training trajectories in procedurally generated scenes. These demonstrations train neural motion planners (MoMa-NMP) for fast closed-loop, room-scale planning for mobile manipulators coordinating base and arm.

entry.title: Fast 4-bit KV-Cache Decoding on Hopper GPUs: Why Existing Kernels Are Slow and How to Fix Them

author.name: Jian Zhang

entry.summary: This systems paper diagnoses why 4-bit KV-cache decode kernels on Hopper GPUs reach only 10-20% of memory bandwidth — 2-6x excess instruction issue per byte and serialized load-decode-multiply pipelines — and introduces a Hopper-native kernel using a TMA producer warp, register-fed tensor cores, and write-time cache layout. On H200 it substantially outperforms existing FP4 paths.

entry.title: Ultrasound Watermark: Real-time Acoustic Watermarking against Voice Scams on Smartphones

author.name: Renzhi Hao, Shirui Cao, Yizhu Wen, Rishav Gupta, Dharani Nadendla, Mehran Kafai, Hanqing Guo, Dong Li

entry.summary: This systems-security paper introduces a real-time smartphone defense against AI voice scams: the phone emits ultrasonic signals, captures reflections from the caller's facial articulatory motion via its own speaker and microphone, and fuses these motion features with outgoing speech as a watermark binding speech to physical articulation. This counters TTS and voice-conversion impersonation without offline analysis.

entry.title: OmniSenMo: A Unified Multisensory Language Model for Generalizable Human Motion Estimation, Understanding, and Prediction

author.name: Cheng Guo, Qiming Cao, Pu Perry Wang, Pu Wang, Hongfei Xue

entry.summary: OmniSenMo is a multisensory language model that uses the human skeleton as a common reference so that heterogeneous sensors such as depth, LiDAR, mmWave, and WiFi each produce one token per body joint, enabling arbitrary sensor subsets for motion estimation, understanding, and prediction. This skeleton-grounded tokenization addresses semantic inconsistency, spatial misalignment, and differing temporal granularities across sensors.

entry.title: AdvMTO: Multimodal and Temporal Adversarial Object Attacks via 2D Gaussian Splatting for BEV-Based 3D Object Detection

author.name: Zhiyang Cui, Hao Tan, Ruonan Li, Shibin Wu, Junjian Zhang, Hong'an Lin, Zhaoquan Gu

entry.summary: AdvMTO is an adversarial attack framework against BEV-based 3D object detectors that uses 2D Gaussian Splatting to render consistent adversarial objects across camera images, LiDAR returns, and historical timestamps, suppressing accumulated detector evidence over time. Prior attacks were single-modality or temporally limited to camera streams.

entry.title: Draft Forcing: Target-guided Speculative Drafting and Learned Verifier for Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Chenkai Xu, Yuji Ren, Zihui Liu, Yijie Jin, Yuhao Shen, Xin Wang, Yajing Chen, Keyang Luo, Shengju Qian, Litong Gong, Tiezheng Ge, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Draft Forcing accelerates autoregressive video diffusion by offloading chunk generation to a lightweight draft model guided at the feature level by target hidden states, coupled with an on-policy trained verifier that checks consistency against the target. This addresses draft divergence and the lack of principled verification in prior speculative video decoding schemes.

entry.title: Does coverage explain core-set active learning? Mean, max, and the choice of distance

author.name: Ferdinand Equilbey (XLIM, UFR SFA [Poitiers], XLIM-ASALI)

entry.summary: This theory paper critically examines the generalization bound underlying core-set active learning, showing that under the zero-conditional-risk assumption used in its proof the bound holds for any dissimilarity and any label-free selection rule, and decomposes behavior into mean pool-to-sample distance and cell purity. It clarifies what coverage arguments actually explain about active learning performance.

entry.title: GC-MoE K3: A Green-Context Role Graph for Latent Mixture-of-Experts Decode

author.name: Yong Li, Haoyu Wang, Kan Liu, Tao Lan

entry.summary: GC-MoE K3 presents a datacenter Blackwell GPU implementation that schedules the full latent mixture-of-experts feed-forward evaluation of Kimi K3 as a CUDA Graph across two Green Contexts. Five base roles split projection, routing, dispatch, expert computation, and finalization, enabling overlap of dispatch with shared-expert compute and of routed reduction with output loading. This targets high-throughput decode for MoE architectures.

entry.title: A Search Worth a Billion Pixels: Explaining Gigapixel Classifiers

author.name: Danilo Danese, Angela Lombardi, Tommaso Di Noia

entry.summary: Introduces WaFR, a model-agnostic perturbation-based attribution method for high-resolution images combining adaptive hierarchical search with sparse multiscale regression. It keeps fine-grained localization at 8,192-pixel resolution while keeping compute dependent on evidence distribution, achieving high Pointing Game scores.

entry.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce

author.name: Binhui Xie, Jinmin Li, Haomiao Tang, Guangting Wang, Song Jin, Jianwei Zhu, Fengyun Rao, Jing Lyu

entry.summary: Presents WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal LLMs from 0.8B dense to 35B MoE (3B active) trained with two-stage continued pre-training on e-commerce-heavy data mixtures and hybrid-thinking post-training combining on-policy distillation and RL. The team also builds a 28-benchmark e-commerce evaluation suite spanning eight business scenarios, claiming SOTA general-purpose performance at each scale.

entry.title: CocoonBench: Can Multilingual Search Agents Escape Language Information Cocoons?

author.name: Hongchuan Zeng, Bowen Liu, Changjiang Gao, Senyu Han, Zhipei Xu, Peisong Wang, Xinbing Liang, Yuhan Li, Nuo Chen, Blaze Chen

entry.summary: Introduces CocoonBench, a benchmark testing whether multilingual search agents can escape language information cocoons by mining answer-centered relational paths from a frozen Wikidata-derived graph where clues are individually necessary and span multiple languages. Tasks are rendered as multiple languages with direct identifiers removed, testing cross-lingual evidence gathering that single-language benchmarks miss.

entry.title: AvatarAnyone: Agentic Reconstruction of Mesh-Based Layered Avatars from YouTube Video

author.name: Aymen Mir, Peter Wonka, Stefanos Zafeiriou, R{\i}za Alp G\"uler

entry.summary: AvatarAnyone reconstructs layered mesh avatars (separate meshes per garment and footwear layered on a body mesh) from casual YouTube videos, using AI agents to plan a per-person reconstruction pipeline by predicting garment classes, clothing types, and layering order. The layered representation enables applications such as virtual try-on and cloth simulation.

entry.title: Precise Asymptotics of Non-Convex M-Estimators

author.name: Shirley Xiaoqi Liu, Tirthankar Adhikari, Parthe Pandit

entry.summary: The paper extends precise asymptotic theory for M-estimation in high-dimensional GLMs to cases where the loss or regularizer is non-convex, using VAMP and state evolution under rotationally invariant designs. The key technical hurdle is that non-convex losses can have discontinuous proximal operators, breaking standard Lipschitz-based proofs.

entry.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Zhuoying Yang, Yichen Guo, Kathy Jia, Zichang Su, Ayesha Kashif, Nange Hai, Jeffrey Ming Han Li, Zhewen He, Silvio Kempf, Ni Jiachen, Junjie Yang, Muhammad Hamza, Zakaria El Ouahidi, Gabriel Azpitarte, Manling Li, Yi Fang, Shuhong Liu, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: LatentParse is a training-free framework that lets a VLM probe latent features from pretrained encoders (CLIP, DINOv3, VGGT) via predefined tools to convert them into explicit spatial evidence, improving multi-view 3D spatial reasoning without fine-tuning. It addresses the fact that VLMs cannot directly use these features presented as feature images in context.

entry.title: SurgeCount: A Protocol-Guided Composition Harness for Bimanual Surgical Sponge Counting

author.name: Sung Eun Kim, Xiaoman Zhang, Xucheng Wang, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: SurgeCount is a robotic system for auditable surgical sponge counting that composes eleven learned short-horizon skills under a written procedural protocol, with a stateful vision-language model selecting the next skill at learned subtask boundaries. It handles deformable, occluded objects in a tangled pile while preserving step order and enabling failure recovery, addressing a real patient-safety task.

entry.title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing

author.name: Zhengyang Wang, Renfei Tan, Shuze Daniel Liu, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: The authors propose an automatic heuristic design framework in which an LLM autonomously refines heuristics for selecting promising subproblems in large-scale capacitated vehicle routing, which are then solved by conventional solvers. Unlike learned neural delegators, the discovered heuristics are generalizable and interpretable.

entry.title: Tokens as Locality-Preserving Anchors: Scalable Novel View Synthesis with Target-Adaptive Token Routing

author.name: Sagnik Ghosh, Aswin C. Sankaranarayanan

entry.summary: The paper observes that source tokens in transformer-based novel view synthesis act as spatial anchors whose attention concentrates for any given viewpoint, and introduces a lightweight router that predicts relevant tokens per viewpoint so the decoder attends to a fixed budget rather than all source tokens. This brings rasterization-style culling benefits to attention-based view synthesis, keeping render time from growing with each added source image. An efficiency contribution for scalable view synthesis.

entry.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Avinash Kumar Singh, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

entry.summary: This work formulates confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation under a latent correctness variable, using a critic LLM fused with generator confidence, token-level uncertainty, and SQL-structural features in a conformal framework. The result lets deployed systems know when to abstain even without gold queries at inference time.

entry.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: The Allen Institute for AI introduces RoboTrack, comprising a new benchmark, a synthetic training dataset, and two models that improve how robots track object points during real-world manipulation tasks. Better point tracking is a key perception primitive for dexterous, closed-loop manipulation in unstructured environments.

entry.title: BehaviorICL: Task-Conditioned Decoder States for Visual In-Context Learning

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Jiamo Hu, Chengrui Wu, Lingyue Chen, Jianguo Chen, Xun Xu, Xulei Yang

entry.summary: BehaviorICL selects in-context demonstrations for vision-language models using the VLM's own frozen decoder states read before answer generation, representing each image-task pair by a task-conditioned signature across decoder layers. A training-free variant averaging cosine similarities retrieves largely different demonstrations when the same image is queried about object versus context, outperforming task-aware image retrievers. The insight that internal states encode task conditioning is valuable for efficient visual ICL.

entry.title: STEGOGUARD-LM: Evaluating End-to-End Protection Against LLM Covert Channels

author.name: Martha Dimgba and George Williams

entry.summary: Presents StegoGuard-LM, a controlled framework for evaluating defenses against steganographic covert channels in LLM outputs, tracking messages through detection, intervention, and recovery across token-rank, synonym, and Unicode channels. A striking finding is that deterministic rewriting stops nearly all synonym-encoded messages unconditionally but almost none when intervention depends on a false-alarm-limited detector.

entry.title: FastD4RT: Training-Free Acceleration of Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking

author.name: Meng Bi, Yili Jin, Kaiyuan Hu, Xize Duan, Jiaxin Huang, Hong Huang, Xue Liu

entry.summary: FastD4RT accelerates query-based 4D reconstruction model D4RT without retraining by exploiting the finding that later decoder blocks attend to a small shared token set and that outputs are smooth over time and pixels. It reduces the dense per-pixel, per-frame query cost and redundant segment encoding of long videos while preserving output quality.

entry.title: Coupling-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Co-Evolving Graph Games

author.name: Mina Kim, Guanghui Lan, Benoit Montreuil

entry.summary: This work formalizes the Co-Evolving Graph Game, where two separately operated graphs (e.g., demand facilities and supply networks) co-evolve with interdependent payoffs, relevant to hydrogen stations, EV charging, and vaccine distribution. CGA-PMD combines cross-graph attention restricted to structurally coupled partner nodes with policy mirror descent for stable training. It fills a gap between facility location, interdependent-network analysis, and graph-based MARL.

entry.title: WorldWeave: Rethinking Embodied Navigation through Cross-Task World Modeling

author.name: Xuan Yao, Jiahao Zhang, Rongjunchen Zhang, Kaixuan Huang, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: WorldWeave is a cross-task world model coupling shared predictive dynamics with task-specific adaptation across Vision-and-Language Navigation and Embodied Visual Tracking. It learns latent actions from observed state changes via inverse dynamics rather than conditioning on heterogeneous physical actions, enabling transfer between navigation toward stationary goals and tracking moving targets. This explores an underexplored joint-learning direction in embodied AI.

entry.title: When Fog Becomes a Weapon: Atmospheric Attacks on Visible-Infrared Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chengyin Hu, Dehe Zhao, Dingyi Lu, Qike Zhang, Jiaju Han, Banglong Nong, Xu Kang, Jiujiang Guo, Kalibinuer Tiliwalidi, Jiahuan Long

entry.summary: Introduces the Fog Manipulation Attack (FMA), a zero-gradient attack that optimizes a natural shared 3D fog state to simultaneously disrupt visible and thermal infrared cues in cross-spectral VLMs, avoiding conspicuous adversarial artifacts. This reveals a physically realizable, stealthy threat to multisensor perception.

entry.title: OrthoLatentCAD: Orthographic Spatial Latents for Hand-Drawn CAD Program Generation

author.name: Xiaolei Zhou, Xinjie Zhu, Chuangjie Fang, Chenyu Wang, Jianwei Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces Hand2CAD, a large benchmark of 215K synthetic orthographic-drawing-to-CAD-program pairs plus 1,000 real three-view drawings, and OrthoLatentCAD, a method that fuses local geometry with global context on canonical planes and exchanges evidence across views to recover executable sketch-extrude CAD programs from raster drawings. This targets converting early design intent into structured CAD programs, a task relevant to engineering design automation.

entry.title: Wavelet-CFM for the extragalactic millimeter-wave sky

author.name: M. Mebratu, W. L. K. Wu, and S. Gasiorowski

entry.summary: The paper develops Wavelet-factorized Conditional Flow Matching to generate fast, accurate joint simulations of correlated astrophysical fields (lensing convergence, kSZ, tSZ, and CIB) at 1-arcminute resolution, including their cross couplings, with a tractable likelihood claimed as a first for this field set. This enables better forward models for cosmology analyses of the millimeter-wave sky. It is a strong domain application of modern generative modeling to scientific simulation.

entry.title: LIBERO-MOR: A Multimodal Robustness Benchmark Across the Vision-Language-Action Pipeline

author.name: Qihang Chen, Tengjie Li, Hongwei Lu, Jason Wu, Chyna Qu, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: LIBERO-MOR is a multimodal robustness benchmark for vision-language-action robot policies built on LIBERO, spanning five deployment-facing domains: vision, language, proprioception, action execution, and environment. It defines 22 perturbations at three severity levels across 40 tasks with a paired clean-perturbed protocol, and evaluates seven representative VLA models with different action-generation mechanisms. The benchmark enables controlled, reproducible assessment of deployment reliability of manipulation policies.

entry.title: CANDOR: A Multilingual Provenance-Documented Corpus for Dysarthric Speech Research

author.name: Bernard Muller, LaVonne Roberts, Leo Kaiya, Antonio Ortiz Barra\~n\'on

entry.summary: CANDOR assembles 61 corpora across 17 languages totaling 4,469.7 hours of audio, including 1,178.8 hours from 2,057 dysarthric speakers, with documented provenance, licensing, and consent distinctions. It notably covers 732 dysarthric speakers in 14 non-English languages, addressing severe gaps in accessible dysarthric speech data.

entry.title: When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners

author.name: Jiucheng Zang, Congkai Peng, Yankai Wei

entry.summary: Testing a small trained Hierarchical Reasoning Model on Sudoku-Extreme, the authors extend recurrence beyond the normal stopping budget and find solved answers persist (0.95) while many wrong answers are unsettled and revise with more compute. The solved-over-wrong persistence ordering replicates across five further settings, though specific thresholds and dynamics do not generalize.

entry.title: TesseraFlow: Scalable Video Diffusion for Dynamic Medical Imaging Inverse Problems

author.name: Atakan Topcu, Mohammadhossein Momeni, Alfredo De Goyeneche, Michael Lustig

entry.summary: TesseraFlow introduces a complex-valued pixel-space flow prior for video reconstruction in medical imaging, addressing the speed bottlenecks of pixel-space patch priors through a global encoder on low-resolution input and more efficient sampling. It targets making state-of-the-art video generative priors practical for dynamic imaging inverse problems.

entry.title: What Makes Recurrence Generalize Across Lengths?

author.name: Yoonsung Jung, Sunghun Jung, Louise Nayeong Koh, Yongjun Choi

entry.summary: This controlled study examines when recurrent Transformers generalize beyond the training range of state-tracking steps, varying operation representation, positional encoding, and recurrent capacity. It finds recurrence alone is insufficient: multi-token template representations and absolute positional encodings can severely limit length generalization. Offers concrete design guidance for length-generalizing recurrent computation.

entry.title: QASparse: Query-Adaptive Sparse Attention with Tailored Budgets and Tokens

author.name: Zhiyuan Chen, Zihao Yang, Quanjiang Li, Haijiang Li, Jiancheng Pan, Qichao Zhao, Zihan Dong, Qiushi Shi, Jinshi Liu

entry.summary: QASparse is a query-adaptive sparse attention mechanism for long-sequence LLM inference that preserves the efficiency of shared cross-head importance estimation while adapting computational budgets and token selection to varying query-region needs. It targets the quadratic prefill cost of dense attention with hardware-efficient execution.

entry.title: Probe Before You Learn: Allocating Prompts from Initial Gradients under Label Noise

author.name: Jiazhe Zhang, Zibin Geng, Qiang Ma, Xuefeng Jiang, Yijun Lin, Jingyi Wang, Yu Yan, Xingzhou Zhang, Min Liu, Yuwei Wang, Sheng Sun

entry.summary: GPrompt addresses an overlooked aspect of prompt learning for vision-language models: allocating the parameter budget between text and visual prompts, showing this choice substantially affects robustness to label noise. It derives allocations training-free from initial gradient statistics, avoiding costly candidate training. This is a practical, principled improvement to parameter-efficient adaptation.

entry.title: Optimal Labelling Designs for Sequential Decisions on Language Model Updates

author.name: Doudou Zhou, Jiahui Xie, Yue Liu

entry.summary: SOLD formulates the problem of deciding whether an LLM update improved accuracy as a sequential labeling design, using a cheap imperfect LLM judge plus selectively purchased human labels, with guaranteed error control at stopping. The paper shows Neyman allocation, the common variance-minimizing choice, can be highly suboptimal here and proposes a better design.

entry.title: Music Circuit: Trace and Control Style Dynamics in Large Music Generation Model

author.name: Ruiji Yu, Wenye Ma, Gus Xia

entry.summary: Applies mechanistic circuit analysis to musical style in large music generation models, building on YuE2 a dataset pairing the same lyrics with five styles and a three-step analysis framework. They localize style formation mainly in the score-planning stage and identify sparse attention-head and MLP-neuron circuits that can be traced and controlled. This extends interpretability techniques from language models to music generation.

entry.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato

author.name: Mingxiao Li, Xuantuo Huang, Encheng Su, Aoran Wang, Han Zhang, Jinouwen Zhang, Shixiang Tang

entry.summary: Studies which training path should receive the representation-alignment loss in one-step generators trained from scratch via the Priming recipe. Across 17 configurations, aligning the generative path collapses recall, while aligning the instance-paired corrupted-to-clean path avoids this, yielding a clear design rule for one-step diffusion-style generators.

entry.title: Reducing Authorship Attribution Risk in Student Texts Through Style-Conditioned Rewriting

author.name: Li Siyan, Zhen Xu, Jiayi Chen, Shopnil Shahriar, Alessandro Sayad, Xuanming Zhang, Renzhe Yu, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: The authors propose a style-aware rewriting method for student forum posts that retains analytical value while reducing identifiability, separating content, structure, and style into conditioning channels and extending Differentially Private In-context Learning with cluster-restricted retrieval over student-disjoint exemplars. Across three educational datasets it preserves task performance while reducing authorship attribution risk, including against a dedicated attribution model.

entry.title: ComplexIF: A Challenging Multi-Turn, Multi-Constraint Instruction-Following Benchmark

author.name: Zhichao Xu, Bingsen Chen, Yawei Wang, Tao Li, Haoyu Wang, Dan Roth, Vivek Srikumar

entry.summary: ComplexIF is a benchmark and generation pipeline for multi-turn, multi-constraint instruction following, expanding seed requests into conversations with constraints woven across turns while keeping tasks solvable. It includes a verifiable format-constraint split and a harder split, targeting the gap as frontier models saturate existing instruction-following tests.

entry.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control

author.name: Yue Huang, Tianshan Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Jayeon Kang, Akide Liu, Sungjoon Choi, Dacheng Tao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: Motion Mamba 2.0 is a Mamba-based diffusion architecture for long-horizon, real-time humanoid motion generation that combines local attention, resumable recurrent states, and a persistent content memory of dynamically updated content slots. The design addresses the limited-history problem of bounded attention caches and the inference overhead of repeated denoising in autoregressive diffusion.

entry.title: How Relations Impose Embedding-Space Structure

author.name: Lachlan Cowley, Jey Han Lau, Yulia Otmakhova, Eduard Hovy

entry.summary: This work presents a parameter-free method comparing internal structural arrangements of representations across domains to test whether language models encode complex relational patterns like analogy, not just simple relations such as synonymy. Across multiple models, representations are arranged consistently to encode complex relationship similarities, with distant representation clouds aligned for comparability under simple mappings. It extends mechanistic interpretability to the global relative geometry of representation spaces.

entry.title: One Latent World for Heterogeneous LiDARs: A Scan Pattern Agnostic 4D World Model via Direct Ray Decoding

author.name: Minwoo Jung, Dongjae Lee, DongGuw Lee, Yeong Sang Park, Maurice Fallon, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose a scan-pattern-agnostic 4D LiDAR world model that decouples scene representation from sensor observation, allowing one spatial latent to be rendered by heterogeneous LiDARs at the same mounting position. The decoder predicts per-ray hit probability and depth directly, avoiding the depth errors of intermediate-surface rendering and the transfer limits of fixed scan patterns.

entry.title: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Jinlin Liu, Yumeng He, Qihan Huang, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Han Peng

entry.summary: The paper identifies context misalignment (CoMi) in skill internalization for VLM agents: when models are fine-tuned on their own trajectories with an in-context skill removed, 12.2-46.0% of test trajectories still reference the removed skill across ALFWorld, WebShop, and ARC-AGI-1. The proposed CGSI method grounds fine-tuning to eliminate these stale references and improve internalized agent behavior.

entry.title: Character Information in Language Models: A Prompt-Independent Word Store and a Late, Question-Driven Signal That Grows With Scale

author.name: Pratyush Acharya, Nuraj Rimal, Apar Baral, Habish Dhakal, Piyush Mohan Bhattarai

entry.summary: Using a word-position baseline that separates stored information from question-driven computation, this study shows across 16 open-weight models (0.6B-14B) that word tokens already encode first/last/most-frequent-letter properties, with about 70 percent of that signal present in token embeddings. A second, question-driven character signal emerges at the answer position and grows with model scale.

entry.title: Revisiting Continual Learning in Language Models: A Three-Interface Diagnosis of Stability and Plasticity

author.name: Keuntae Kim, Beomseok Lee, Hyunwoo Kim, Yong Suk Choi

entry.summary: This paper argues that backward and forward transfer in continual learning of language models should be treated as interface-dependent rather than model-level properties. By evaluating through three interfaces, a sequentially trained head, a probe on frozen features, and a classifier-free diagnostic, the authors can distinguish representation degradation from readout mismatch as causes of forgetting.

entry.title: Confidently Lost: Silent Failure and Edge Deployment of Dense Visual SLAM under Photon Starvation

author.name: Shrikrishna Bhagirath Rajule, Srinath Neelamagam, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: This paper documents a silent failure mode of dense visual SLAM built on learned two-view geometry in low light: MASt3R-SLAM's network produces highly self-consistent geometry even for pure noise frames, causing the system to accept over 95 percent of correspondences that violate ground-truth geometry while reporting full frame rate and no rejections. The authors trace how one inflated statistic is read in opposite directions by keyframing and relocalization subsystems and propose a mitigation.

entry.title: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis

author.name: Xiaohao Sun, Angel X. Chang

entry.summary: RoomTokens proposes a sliced structured-token representation for 3D indoor scene generation where each token encodes semantic class, instance identity, and facing field, enabling generation on a discrete grid while preserving instance grouping and orientation cues. A masked diffusion model learns the resulting token distribution, addressing collisions and boundary violations that plague sequence-based scene generators.

entry.title: RepoClean: Evaluating Coding Agents on Repository-Level Obsolete Code Cleanup

author.name: Hongyixuan Yuan, Qixing Zhou, Pengcheng Huang, Qingshuo Ni, Runsong Zhao, Shaokai He, Xiangpeng Li, Deqiang Ouyang

entry.summary: RepoClean is a benchmark of 200 obsolete-code cleanup tasks from 34 popular open-source Python repositories, constructed by automatically reintroducing deleted code from real histories while preserving current implementations and previously passing tests that now fail. It isolates and evaluates the underexamined capability of safe, autonomous repository-level code removal.

entry.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers

author.name: Junrui Zhang, Zeyu Xu, Runchuan Zhu, Jie Peng, Long Zhang, Zixin Ding, Jiaxin Lin, Kai Wang, Jianmin Ji, Junyuan Hong

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies when and how large language models can automate context engineering, building a benchmark with datasets exhibiting different reasoning patterns and comparing LLM-context-engineering methods across multiple 8B model families. Results indicate no single winner, with effectiveness depending on the interplay between method, model, and reasoning pattern of the task.

entry.title: De Novo Generation of Odorant Molecules with Targeted Olfactory Receptor Activation Patterns

author.name: Kexin Zhang, Manhao Guan

entry.summary: The paper builds a binding matrix over 20 olfactory receptors, clusters it into representative activation patterns, and uses a structured selectivity loss with reinforcement learning to steer a molecular generator toward target multi-receptor activation profiles.
