Across nine target profiles the method achieves high predicted selectivity within 18,000 oracle calls. This connects generative molecular design to the combinatorial code underlying smell perception.

entry.title: Seeing Is Locating: Spatial Awareness and Geographic Bias in Decision Language Models

author.name: Wilson Wongso, Hada Melino Muhammad, Xiachong Lin, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: Presents GeoDecisions, a multimodal benchmark testing whether decision models that output label distributions over candidates can use spatial context and whether they exhibit geographic bias, via geo-aware image classification and location rating tasks. Findings show textual coordinates alone are insufficient for spatial awareness and that vision is required, alongside measurable geographic bias.

entry.title: Vasicek Diffusion Bridge for Graph Generation

author.name: Junyi Tang, Chang Liu, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes Vasicek Graph Diffusion, a graph generation process derived from Vasicek dynamics with data-anchored mean dynamics and a closed-form solution, giving a smoother noise-to-data bridge. This counters excessive uncertainty and delayed signal-to-noise growth seen in existing graph diffusion models, so structure emerges earlier in generation.

entry.title: ABI: Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations for Zero-Shot Test-Time Guidance

author.name: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Guanbo Jiao, Jianming Ma, Xing Gao, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: Observes that evaluating actions under the data-collecting behavior policy largely preserves their relative value ordering across target policies, enabling actor-free critic training. Combining this with reward-free successor prediction, ABI learns representations that provide zero-shot test-time guidance for behavior-cloning policies on unseen tasks without task-specific rewards or actor coupling.

entry.title: Coordinating Perception and Planning for Test-Time Adaptation in End-to-End Driving under Distribution Shifts

author.name: Shiyu Fang, Yiming Cui, Qihang Huang, Zhan Chen, Collister Chua, Wenhui Huang, Peng Hang, Chen Lv, Jian Sun

entry.summary: Proposes P2-TTA, a plug-and-play test-time adaptation framework for end-to-end driving that coordinates perception and planning updates, addressing multi-task adaptation dependency and continuous-adaptation instability under distribution shifts. It uses planning-aware signals rather than perception confidence alone to assess downstream effects of upstream updates.

entry.title: Predicting Rare-Mode Collapse in Recursive Generative Training from Single-Generation Calibration

author.name: Jingyao Zhang and Mingyu Du and Lu Han

entry.summary: The paper develops a decoupled framework that forecasts multi-generation rare-mode collapse in recursive generative training from independent single-generation conditional fits, pairing an exact three-source multinomial count law with single-generation response banks to propagate marginals in closed form. It provides calibration-error and boundary-resolution bounds and proves policy reversals for additive Gaussian perturbations.

entry.title: LimeTree: Linear-Memory Graph Neural Networks over Tree-Graphs for Resource-Efficient Language Modeling and Context Extrapolation

author.name: Elisabeth Fink

entry.summary: LimeTree is a linear-complexity sequence modeling architecture that integrates synthetic key-value retrieval tasks directly into language modeling training, achieving strong perplexity alongside reliable associative recall. Evaluated under strict compute constraints, it reaches perplexity 19 on WikiText-103 in 6 hours on four GPUs while maintaining 100% KV retrieval accuracy.

entry.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret

author.name: Tomas Ortega, Hamid Jafarkhani

entry.summary: This theory paper studies comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, proving via a two-node counterexample that gossip-based algorithms cannot achieve sublinear network regret with one gossip step per round, resolving an open question. It then introduces a black-box reduction turning any local learner with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret into one achieving sublinear network regret.

entry.title: Head Anything: Correspondence-Guided Joint Generation of 3D Heads from Few Images

author.name: Umut Kocasari, Bart{\l}omiej Baranowski, Richard Shaw, Eduardo P\'erez-Pellitero, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner

entry.summary: Head Anything turns a pretrained single-image 3D head generator into a joint multi-image generator via lightweight correspondence-attention adapters, letting each 3D token attend to corresponding points across images of the same person with varying expressions and viewpoints. Correspondences come from fitting a neural parametric head model, avoiding training a costly multi-image prior. This addresses independent hallucination across views in few-shot 3D head reconstruction.

entry.title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers present SLIC (Small LM Iterating on Circuits), a method for training a small language model to perform analog integrated circuit design as well as or better than frontier LLMs. Because the small model runs locally, it avoids exposing proprietary circuit designs and foundry data to cloud-hosted frontier models while enabling faster prototyping and broader design exploration.

entry.title: Neural solver for Wasserstein Geodesics and optimal transport dynamics

author.name: Hailiang Liu, Yan-Han Chen

entry.summary: The authors introduce a sample-based neural solver that computes Wasserstein geodesics and associated velocity fields by recasting the dynamical optimal transport problem as a minimax problem solved with neural networks. The method also recovers the OT map, enabling direct sampling from target distributions.

entry.title: Fairness Evaluation for Diffusion and Flow Models Should Account for the Generation Path: Implications for Clinical Imaging

author.name: Dharini Raghavan, Amritpal Singh, Anant Madabhushi

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that fairness evaluations of diffusion and flow models in medical imaging must treat the sampling procedure (step count, schedule, solver) as part of the evaluated system, since sampling choices can differentially affect clinical task errors across patient groups. It builds on prior work on generation dynamics and fairness to show fairness results under one sampling procedure may not generalize to another. The argument has direct implications for clinical deployment of generative models.

entry.title: ReSUL: Learning Regional Sensor Utility for Robust Multisensor Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Yiwen Wang, Jiahao Qin

entry.summary: ReSUL learns where corrupted multisensor observations should be retained, excluded, or re-registered by comparing full-sensor predictions, sensor-exclusion paths, and a re-registration path for displaced thermal inputs. A router predicts each path's signed reduction in category-balanced Brier risk and allocates spatial mixture weights accordingly, connecting spatial allocation to measurable task benefit without inference-time fault labels. The regional utility framing is a fresh angle on robust sensor fusion.

entry.title: Gradient-Free Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision Models via Agentic Coding

author.name: Khayrul Islam

entry.summary: The Agent edit method has a coding agent write a program that directly sets new-class weights in a frozen detector's classification head, using limited detector runs and COCO mAP feedback instead of gradient descent. The resulting program rebuilds weights without the agent, and at five shots outperforms full-decoder fine-tuning on 2 of 4 fine-grained sets by large F1 margins. This is a novel, surprising demonstration that agentic code generation can substitute for gradient-based few-shot adaptation.

entry.title: FinEvo: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Financial Modeling

author.name: Chengjun Pan, Shichun Liu, Zekai Zhou, Shihan Dou, Jiahang Lin, Chengsong Huang, Dingwei Zhu, Tao Gui

entry.summary: FinEvo is a self-evolution framework for financial modeling in which a model (demonstrated end-to-end with Qwen3.6-27B, an existing model) prepares financial models, iteratively generates challenges via self-play, and learns from interactions using executable rewards, all with the same underlying model. The work explores whether financial modeling provides a substrate for model self-evolution and whether self-evolution advances financial capability.

entry.title: Temporal Logic Tensor Networks: Foundations of Temporal Reasoning in Neural Networks

author.name: Edjard Mota, Artur d'Avila Garcez, Maria Azevedo, Odalisio Neto

entry.summary: This paper introduces Temporal Logic Tensor Networks (tLTN), a neurosymbolic framework combining point-wise and interval temporal semantics to enable neural reasoning across multiple time scales in dynamic scenes such as sports, traffic, and surgery. It provides principled foundations for temporal reasoning that pure visual models lack. The work is relevant to bridging logic-based reasoning and neural perception.

entry.title: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks on EEG Models

author.name: Mehrdad Khodapanahandeh, Selin Unal, Berkay Kemal Balioglu, Alireza Khodaie, Beren Semiz, M. Emre Gursoy

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic empirical study of membership inference attacks on EEG models, spanning three datasets, seven architectures, four attacks, and two metrics. It finds that poor generalization (large train-test gaps) is the strongest vulnerability indicator, with longer training and larger models also increasing risk. It provides the first comprehensive privacy-risk characterization for sensitive neural-signal models.

entry.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough

author.name: Zachary Morrow, Yucheng Fu, Pratanu Roy, Michael Penwarden

entry.summary: The paper argues that PINN difficulties with high-frequency and high-order PDEs stem from deep architectures rather than insufficient approximation capacity, and proposes PI-SUPNs, which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions in a shallow graph. Experiments on high-frequency PDEs show common remedies like curvature-aware optimizers and FP64 act as workarounds rather than fixes.

entry.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space

author.name: Xu Lin, Ruilin Yao, Haoran Xu, Zixiang Wang, Ming Ma, Yu Zhao, Pu Miao, Chonghan Liu

entry.summary: Presents Open Vision Banana (OVB), an open framework adapting Qwen-Image-2.1's 7B diffusion generator into one instruction-driven model for depth, semantic, instance, and referring segmentation via a single low-rank adapter and public data, testing whether closed-generator perception-as-generation results transfer to open models. It studies 42 checkpoints, weight merges, and controlled runs to characterize the remaining gap. Rigorous open replication and analysis of a notable generative-perception paradigm.

entry.title: Lifted Multiple Shooting for Parallel-in-Time Contact-Rich Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Wei-Chen Li and Glen Chou

entry.summary: The paper proposes lifted multiple shooting, an NLP transcription for trajectory optimization through contact that introduces contact impulses as optimization variables, satisfying state-transition constraints with friction-cone-feasible impulses while separately enforcing contact-model consistency. This makes gradient-based contact-rich planning tractable and parallelizable in time. It is relevant for dexterous manipulation and legged locomotion where non-smooth contact dynamics complicate optimization.

entry.title: CLOSE: A Calibrated Label-free Online Self-Evaluating Verifier for Object Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhaoxi Wang, Jiahao Lai

entry.summary: Observes that VLMs already reject 44-62% of their own hallucinations when asked separately, with high AUROC, but probabilities lack a cross-model scale and overlap for remaining cases. CLOSE enforces this self-judgment during generation using a quantile-of-memory threshold that is calibrated and label-free, reducing object hallucination online.

entry.title: Self-prediction residuals improve single-pass detection of wrong-object boxes in grounded vision-language models

author.name: Enhao Cui, Junzhi Yang, Yaoshun Lin, Yuhan Feng, Zijian Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a single-pass signal for detecting wrong-object bounding boxes in grounded VLMs: a linear probe fitted per model reads a box from hidden states before it is written, and the disagreement between the read-out and the written box (the self-prediction residual) flags errors. Averaged over six models on RefCOCOg items, the residual improves error detection AUC for fifteen different single-pass scores. This is a practical, label-free consistency check for model self-monitoring.

entry.title: Peel, Don't Whack: Partial Coverage, Imperfect Validators, and Intervention Based Shortcut Mitigation

author.name: Ali Alavi

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes shortcut mitigation via automatic label-preserving interventions accepted by validators, in a stylized linear model with partial edit coverage and validator errors. It derives an additive decision rule showing worst-group accuracy never decreases with coverage while individual groups can degrade, explaining the Whac-a-Mole effect, and gives a closed-form bound on the validator false-accept rate. It provides rare theoretical grounding for data-centric robustness interventions.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG

author.name: Syed Khaderi, Karima Makhlouf, Sami Zhioua

entry.summary: This paper introduces CRELT, a framework tracking turn-by-turn training-data PII leakage in conversational RAG, with a strict criterion counting leaks only when the item is absent from model input at the emitting turn. The strict criterion removes 29-53% of raw matches that were false positives, and experiments on GPT-J, Pythia, and other models show that RAG's single-turn protection degrades over multi-turn conversations.

entry.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Ungbae Yoon, Kwanyoung Kim

entry.summary: For sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting, the authors show that the direction of flatness-inducing perturbations determines whether they improve generalization to unseen viewpoints. They decompose per-view gradients and propose steering optimization toward flat minima along directions informed by the training-view geometry.

entry.title: ViTrust: Learning 3D Observation Trust for Deformable Physical World Models

author.name: Zhihao Guo, Zhihao Li, Xu Ge, Lijian Zhong, Yu Lu, Haitao Wu, Longqing Zhao, Yue Ma

entry.summary: ViTrust learns how strongly each tracked 3D point should influence physical identification in deformable world models, via a visual-contact trust adapter combining spatiotemporal evidence with interaction history on a persistent contact graph. A single-stage shared-forward objective jointly optimizes observation weights and physical parameters, motivated by the fact that accurate reconstruction does not guarantee accurate future prediction.

entry.title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View

author.name: Bo Liu, Yuan Xie, Junan Chen, Fujun Han

entry.summary: The authors formulate LLM pre-training as a non-autonomous dynamical system over weights and Adam optimizer states, introducing a normalized sensitivity score in optimizer-relative coordinates to locate fragile checkpoints. They show that at a sensitive checkpoint a perturbation of only 1e-5 causes 35.7% top-1 prediction disagreement and near-total divergence of greedy generations while loss stays nearly flat. The work reveals loss curves conceal substantial training instability.

entry.title: Learning from Another Angle: Rotation-Based Test-Time Training for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Changyu Liu, Fei Zhao, Yiyang Liu, Xi Xiao, Tianyang Wang, Cheng Han

entry.summary: RoTTT is an efficient test-time training method for multimodal LLMs that adapts each test instance via a few gradient updates on predicting the rotation angle of the input image, using the known angle as reliable self-supervision. This avoids the cost of multiple sampling and the error reinforcement from biased self-generated labels in prior TTT approaches.

entry.title: JEPA-Tuner: From Predictive Fine-Tuning to Asynchronous Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jingxiang Qu, Tian Xie, Youngjin Hong, Changhyun Choi, Yang Katie Zhao, Yi Liu

entry.summary: JEPA-Tuner is a predictive fine-tuning framework for vision-language-action models that regularizes policy guidance through action-conditioned future prediction, exploiting the natural predictive signal from embodied interaction. It aims to improve over standard action-supervised fine-tuning by capturing temporal dependencies in the policy's guidance.

entry.title: ContextFact: Remembering Facts in Context for Long-Term Conversational Agents

author.name: Jiayu Huang, Yichao Cai, Xinyu Li, Zhen Zhang, Javen Qinfeng Shi

entry.summary: ContextFact studies how memory construction and retrieval-unit boundaries affect answerability and evidence access in long-term conversational agents, showing that some context must be preserved during memory construction since retrieval alone cannot close gaps. Adjacent-turn grouping improves evidence access at matched turn budgets. It offers concrete empirical guidance for LLM agent memory design.

entry.title: Tenlai-TTS 2.0: Continuous-Representation LLM-Based TTS System with End-to-End Training

author.name: Changfeng Gao, Yong Ren, Jun Yuan, Zhengkun Tian, Ye Bai, Zhao You, Shidong Shang

entry.summary: Tenlai-TTS 2.0 is an autoregressive TTS system using continuous speech latents learned end-to-end rather than frozen from a separately trained codec, balancing acoustic fidelity with autoregressive predictability. It combines a speech encoder with a capacity-controlled Gaussian bottleneck, an LLM with an AR-DiT head, and a flow-matching style component.

entry.title: MetaSkill: Reusable Problem-Solving Methods for Adaptive Skill Orchestration in LLM Agents

author.name: Tianxing Wang, Mingming Zhao, Shuai Huang, Chaoyue Niu, Huiyang Xu, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: MetaSkill is a two-layer framework for LLM agents that reuses abstract problem-solving methods across tasks: a method layer selects from curated methods and binds roles to task objects, while an execution layer coordinates native skills and guides repair. It outperforms baselines on SkillsBench and ToolHop with accuracy gains of 3.51-13.48%.

entry.title: Hybrid state-space and attention neural operators for nonlinear structural dynamics under environmental loading

author.name: Anastasios Stamou and Rui Teixeira and Maria Nogal and Michalis Fragiadakis

entry.summary: DeepOJamba combines selective state-space recurrence with attention in a neural operator that predicts structural response histories to dynamic loads, using physical-parameter conditioning and predicted-state transfer to generalize across conditions and sequence lengths. Evaluated on a 15 MW offshore wind turbine monopile under wind and wave loading, it outperforms pure attention, pure SSM, Fourier, and DeepONet baselines. The work demonstrates hybrid sequence architectures for engineering surrogate modeling.

entry.title: MIMORPHEUS: Rethinking Cross-Modal Supervision for Human Pose Estimation from Radar Signals

author.name: Shizhao Zhang, Yanyan Zhang, Deshui Yu, Jun Pan, Guangyou Fang

entry.summary: MIMORPHEUS generates radar echoes from 3D human poses via conditional diffusion to bypass costly paired radar-pose data collection, using a MIMO-VAE to compress echoes and a SkeleCoder for contrastive pose-echo alignment. This enables through-wall MIMO radar human pose estimation with cheaper supervision. It addresses the core data-scarcity bottleneck in radar perception.

entry.title: GraphSeer: Multimodal Knowledge Graph Relational Image Retrieval with MLLMs

author.name: Linyu Li, Zhi Jin, Yuanpeng He, Haoran Duan, Dongming Jin, Wenchun Jing, Xuan Zhang, Gadeng Luosang, Nyima Tashi

entry.summary: Defines knowledge graph relational image retrieval (KRIR): given a photo and a natural-language relation, retrieve the related MMKG entity, which rarely resembles the photo and may be unseen in the graph. The authors build three benchmarks from YAGO, Wikidata, and OVEN photos, with tasks requiring two hops of reasoning: recognizing the depicted entity and traversing a relation. This carves out a new retrieval task distinct from link prediction and content-based image retrieval.

entry.title: From Learning Rates to Rotational Schedules: Finite-Horizon Theory on the Sphere

author.name: Jacopo Graldi, Antonio Orvieto, Anastasia Koloskova

entry.summary: Reframes learning-rate schedule design for scale-invariant (normalized) parameter groups as rotational motion on the sphere, deriving last-iterate convergence bounds for arbitrary rotational schedules in a geodesically convex setting. The bound-separating scale from temporal distribution yields a unique optimal schedule that approaches linear decay in the limit, offering theoretical grounding for cosine and WSD schedules.

entry.title: Diversity in Unity, Theory in Practice: Hierarchical Multitask Benchmarks for Chinese Minority Languages

author.name: Yijie Li, Xi Cao, Yuan Sun, Quulgan Minggad, Abdulla Ablikim, JiaQingCaiWang

entry.summary: CMiLBench is a hierarchical multitask benchmark for Tibetan, Mongolian, and Uyghur comprising 24,663 instances across 17 tasks and 5 difficulty levels, covering foundational ability, cultural specificity, and safety alignment. The authors evaluate 14 commercial and open-source LLMs with a hybrid framework, revealing gaps in minority-language capability.

entry.title: CrysLDM: Latent Diffusion Model for Crystal Material Generation

author.name: Subhojyoti Khastagir, Kishalay Das, Pawan Goyal, Seung-Cheol Lee, Satadeep Bhattacharjee, Niloy Ganguly

entry.summary: CrysLDM is a latent diffusion model for 3D crystal material generation that uses a VAE to map crystal structures (atom types, coordinates, lattices) into a latent space where diffusion operates, reducing diffusion steps and training/sampling cost relative to feature-space diffusion models. It targets generation under time- and resource-constrained settings where existing models are poorly suited.

entry.title: Selecting Stable Sampling Dynamics for Compositional Diffusion: A Feynman-Kac Weight Reduction

author.name: Sunjin Kim, Sungsoo Ahn, Michael Chertkov

entry.summary: The paper studies how to sample from weighted products of separately trained diffusion models without joint retraining, analyzing a family of Feynman-Kac weighted SDEs. It identifies a distinguished drift parameter lambda equal to 1/B that minimizes aggregate squared score error, giving a principled criterion for choosing stable compositional sampling dynamics.

entry.title: GlobalHRBench: Does Changing the Question Language Change the Legal Answer?

author.name: Yuding Wang, Yuhang Yao

entry.summary: GlobalHRBench pairs 240 employment-law problems across eight jurisdictions and eight languages while holding facts, law, and conclusions fixed, and evaluates nine models on 1,920 prompts for legal correctness, completeness, and answer-language compliance. GPT-6.1 Sol, an existing frontier model, leads at 76.2 percent strict passes with a 5.8 percent best-to-worst language decline, while some models like Kimi K3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 5.5 reverse rankings between English and Chinese.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Software Migration: from Module-Level Transformation to Repository-Level Integration

author.name: Yanan Zhang, Shengqi Liu, Tao Zhang, Yidi Liu, Alan Tang, Hailong Chen, Yantao Jia

entry.summary: This survey reviews LLM-assisted software migration across 96 sources, including 46 direct migration papers, analyzing supported engineering activities, model roles, orchestration workflows (agentless, single-agent, multi-agent), and enabling techniques. It traces the field's progression from module-level code transformation toward repository-level integration and deployable applications. It offers a structured map of an increasingly important agentic coding application area.

entry.title: Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent

author.name: Zhongyuan Lyu and Xiaocong Xu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes strategy selection when an opponent adapts to what it observes, as in red-teaming LLMs and game-playing AI, proposing the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR) for deciding when to stop testing and select or abstain. The goal is to select strategies meeting a target win probability while rarely selecting ones that have already degraded.

entry.title: Stable but Hidden: Identifiability and Experimental Design under Missing Compositional Support

author.name: Harry Sevi, Joonatan E. M. Laulainen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies a structural identifiability failure in AI-guided scientific discovery: when components are observed separately but never jointly, distinct response functions can agree on all observed data yet disagree on missing combinations, and model agreement does not reveal the ambiguity. It characterizes the invisible subspace, derives minimax risk, and shows optimally designed joint measurements recover the missing response at a rate tied to basis conditioning.

entry.title: MotionServe: Efficient Multi-Robot Serving by Exploiting Robot Execution Slack

author.name: Zikang Wen, Yuning Zhang, Dong Yuan

entry.summary: MotionServe is a shared-GPU serving system for multiple robots running LoRA-adapted VLA policies, which schedules inference using each robot's execution slack — the buffered action-chunk time available before the robot stalls. This addresses a real systems gap as deployments move from one GPU per robot toward multi-robot inference sharing.

entry.title: WASP: Continual Weight Adaptation for Streaming LLM Personalization

author.name: Linxi Xie, Chonghua Liao, Mengxuan Wu, Guandao Yang, Zhangyang Wang, Kai Wang

entry.summary: WASP is a hypernetwork-based framework for streaming LLM personalization that maintains a compact user representation from raw interactions and generates personalized LoRA adapters in a single forward pass, updating the representation incrementally without reprocessing full histories. This enables continual per-user adaptation with low update cost, avoiding expensive per-user optimization.

entry.title: UUBench: Understanding the Unspoken toward Full-Duplex Multimodal Interaction

author.name: Ye Pan, Chenfei Liao, Bin Ren, Hanqian Li, Haocong He, Jialei Chen, Jinlin He, Kunyu Peng, Mengyu Jin, Shijie Li, Wenqian Cui, Yuanqi Yao, Yuqian Fu, Kailong Ruan, Yuan Gao, Wei Wang, Xuming Hu, Irwin King, Nicu Sebe, Xu Zheng

entry.summary: UUBench is a benchmark evaluating whether multimodal interactive systems understand implicit communicative needs conveyed through prosody, facial expressions, gestures, and context, and respond appropriately in real-time full-duplex interaction. It introduces Process-Oriented Scoring to ground the inherently subjective assessment of intent fulfillment.

entry.title: Benchmarking Geospatial Foundation Models under Calibrated Label Errors

author.name: Mollah Md Saif, Showrin Rahman, Anindya Majumder, Sowad Rahman, Md. Golam Rabiul Alam

entry.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark protocol evaluating geospatial foundation models when training labels are imperfect, applying four spatially structured error types calibrated to equal label mIoU across nine encoders, six decoder heads, and ten datasets. Contrasts are read against explicit equivalence margins, offering practitioners guidance on encoder choice under realistic label noise.

entry.title: Operator-Valued Q-Learning: Compositional Bellman Recursions for Order-Sensitive Decision Making

author.name: Swagatam Das, Swagato Das

entry.summary: The paper generalizes Q-learning so each Q(s,a) is an operator, with Bellman backups applying the action's dual map, capturing non-commuting actions in domains like quantum pulse control and in-hand object reorientation where action order determines outcomes. It provides exactness results for blind policies, contraction guarantees for unitary/orthogonal dynamics, and an asynchronous operator TD scheme with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Changwei Lv, Yunfei Li, Zhongjing Du, Kehui Tan, Zijun Liao, Ruochong Zheng, Hao Chen, Can Deng, Zheni Zeng, Chang Liu, Jie Chen

entry.summary: MMMem is a task-aware multimodal memory framework that lets agents consolidate experience from completed tasks, using source-linked multi-view memory, generated scene images combining cross-record clues, and additional strategies for extracting and retaining task lessons. It aims to prevent repeated errors on related questions during long-term user interactions.

entry.title: One Policy, Many Bodies: Cooperative Human-Object Interaction with Heterogeneous Teams

author.name: Zhihao Cao, Tianxu An, Chenhao Li, Chenyangguang Zhang, Stelian Coros, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: MorphHOI presents a decentralized physics-based policy enabling cooperative human-object interaction across heterogeneous embodiments, team compositions, and skills. It introduces a canonical body interface unifying observation and action spaces plus an embodiment-conditioned transformer that adapts decisions to physical capability differences.

entry.title: SOAR: temporal Structure-guided One-step Action generation for Robotic manipulation

author.name: Di Xin, Mingfei Han, Genming Cui, Yuanxiang Chen, Xiaolong Wu, Siyu Ning, Xiaojun Chang, Zhihui Li

entry.summary: SOAR is a one-step generative policy for robotic manipulation that predicts an observation-conditioned DCT representation of future actions, using explicit temporal frequency-band structure to guide action generation without costly iterative refinement of diffusion or flow policies. It aims to combine the latency advantage of one-step policies with the action quality of multi-step methods.

entry.title: Field-Level Crop Classification via Similarity-Induced Supervision from Imperfect Labels

author.name: Raul Lomonte Figueiredo, Jo\~ao Rebou\c{c}as Dorea and D\'ario Augusto Borges Oliveira

entry.summary: The paper proposes a method for large-scale crop classification using imperfect public land cover products as labels, avoiding costly new field campaigns. It combines a mechanism to reduce label semantic inconsistency by shifting supervision with similarity structure, and targets tropical regions where cloud cover makes SAR imagery essential. The approach addresses systematic biases that underestimate less prevalent crops.

entry.title: JaxNaviSim: A GPU-Accelerated, Data-Driven Simulator and Learning Benchmark for Maritime Navigation

author.name: Quang Anh Pham, Janaka Chathuranga Brahmanage, Hue Tse Leong, Akshat Kumar, Tien Anh Mai, Siu Loon Hoe, Venky Shankararaman

entry.summary: Introduces JaxNaviSim, a GPU-accelerated, data-driven maritime navigation simulator coupling AIS data with fast, controllable closed-loop traffic simulation where learned models steer vessels through recorded traffic, plus a learning benchmark. It releases a large dataset of roughly 141 million data points, supporting port traffic management and safety research.

entry.title: How Systems Treat Intent: A Faceted Taxonomy of Intent for Human-AI Co-Creation

author.name: Ashwin Ram, Radha Kumaran, Alexander Koller, Kevin Baum, J\"urgen Steimle

entry.summary: The authors introduce a six-facet taxonomy of user intent grounded in philosophy of mind, action, and meaning, applying it to systems from 198 SIGCHI papers. The analysis shows different forms of incomplete intent map to distinct interaction and authorship strategies, exposing blind spots where superficially similar mechanisms address fundamentally different intent-related problems.

entry.title: MUNDO: a multiresolution generative framework for temporal downscaling

author.name: Aymeric Delefosse, Manon Tavernier, Julie Keisler, Anastase Charantonis, Dominique B\'er\'eziat

entry.summary: MUNDO is a generative framework for temporal downscaling of dynamical systems observed through sparse states or aggregates, using a null-space parameterization to enforce exact observation consistency in one network evaluation. Reverse Markov learning factorizes the observation operator into a hierarchy of successive coarsening steps to capture multiscale dynamics.

entry.title: A theory of inductive node-level generalization from a single large graph

author.name: Nicolas Keriven, Yann Viegas

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops a generalization framework for inductive node-level tasks in graph machine learning when learning from a single large graph with dependent nodes, moving beyond transductive settings or unrealistic assumptions of many independent graphs. It provides a principled account of generalization in a setting common in practice but poorly covered by existing theory.

entry.title: Token Pruning Needs a Protected Sink Token: Coherent Spatial Aggregation in Vision Transformers

author.name: Julian Wyatt, James Willoughby, Allison Clement, Irina Voiculescu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact by explicitly removing tokens during the forward pass, revealing that models like DINOv3 maintain coherent token-importance rankings across depth while SigLIP 2 does not. It shows prediction survival under pruning depends on keeping high-norm sink tokens, yielding practical guidance for ViT token reduction.

entry.title: HoloSplat: Real-Time Token Streaming for Feed-Forward Human Reconstruction

author.name: Chaofan Li, Qihan Ding, Shihan Wang, Zhehao Shen, Boyu Shen, Quanyu Chen, Haoyu Wu, Lan Xu, Xin Lou

entry.summary: HoloSplat is a real-time streaming framework for human-centric volumetric video that splits a feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstructor before its Gaussian head, applying server-side token compression and client-side restoration under strict bandwidth budgets. It addresses the gap between reconstruction quality and practical streaming constraints for telepresence and XR. A systems-level contribution combining 3DGS, feed-forward inference, and streaming codecs.

entry.title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates

author.name: Konstantinos Dovelos

entry.summary: The paper proposes that PDE solvers return a verifiable certificate — an admissible potential and exactly charge-conserving current — that a small independent checker turns into guaranteed error bounds, demonstrating the checker on FEniCSx and five plausible bugs. This addresses trust in simulation outputs from uninspected sources like LLM-written code and learned surrogates.

entry.title: SplatFlow3D: Learning Scene Flow via 3D Motion Feature Splatting

author.name: Bo Wang, Dekang Zhu, Jian Li, Zhipeng Meng, Bo Wang, Dewen Hu

entry.summary: The paper proposes SimpleFlow3D, a two-frame scene flow backbone that decouples and couples dense image-plane and sparse depth information, achieving SOTA results with minimal parameters, plus a weight-sharing multi-frame framework that splats prior 3D motion features to handle occlusion. The combined SplatFlow3D system unifies first and subsequent frame inference via pseudo inputs.

entry.title: FittedGenes: Domain-Aware Sewing Pattern Layout Optimization

author.name: Ay\c{s}eg\"ul Barlas, Maria Korosteleva

entry.summary: This paper reformulates 2D cutting/nesting optimization by making garment panel geometry itself a decision variable, constrained to preserve garment fit while allowing appearance changes within designer-specified bounds. It embeds these domain-aware modifications into an evolutionary framework with two novel mutation operators, including one that splits panels into stitchable sub-panels. This matters because it bridges garment design and manufacturing optimization, moving beyond fixed-geometry assumptions in traditional nesting research.

entry.title: Shallow may be better: Physics-Constrained Lightweight Networks for High-Throughput Particle Image Velocimetry

author.name: Claudio Mucignat and Kamila Zdybal and Ivan Lunati

entry.summary: This paper derives an explicit upper bound on spatial-support growth from the physically admissible tracer displacement in particle image velocimetry, showing that deep pyramidal optical-flow encoders exceed the required receptive field and harm training stability, resolution under particle loss, and inference speed. Based on this analysis it develops LIMA3, a lightweight physics-constrained pyramidal displacement network for high-throughput PIV. A nice demonstration that physics can dictate architecture depth.

entry.title: LightOnOCR for AMNLT: Reading Chant Notation and Lyrics in One Pass, from Single Staves to Whole Pages

author.name: Robert Klugseder (Austrian Centre for Digital Humanities (ACDH), Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna)

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a 1B-parameter page OCR model end to end to transcribe chant notation and aligned lyrics as GABC strings, addressing the AMNLT task where prior VLM approaches underperformed specialized recognizers. Trained only on the published split, it more than halves the best published aligned error rate on Solesmes and improves results on Einsiedeln and Salzinnes. This shows general-purpose OCR models can beat specialized systems on structured music transcription with sufficient end-to-end training.

entry.title: DINO-KNN: Training-Free Multiclass In-Context Segmentation via Nearest Neighbors

author.name: Hussain Alasmawi, Numan Saeed, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: DINO-KNN performs in-context segmentation by storing all labeled reference patches from a frozen DINOv3 encoder in a nearest-neighbor memory and labeling target patches via distance-weighted k-NN voting, predicting all classes in a single pass without training or a mask decoder. It achieves the best average mIoU across eight natural and medical datasets in multiclass, multi-reference settings.

entry.title: How Far Can LLMs Go in Generating Android Lint Checks from Natural Language?

author.name: Moshood A. Fakorede, A.B. Siddique, Manu Sridharan, Umar Farooq

entry.summary: Introduces LintBench, a human-validated benchmark of 113 real-world Android lint rules, to measure whether LLMs can generate working static-analysis checks from natural language descriptions alone, without patches, CVE records, or test suites. The study characterizes what external knowledge LLMs need for this demanding program-analysis task.

entry.title: SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets

author.name: Sudhakar Mishra

entry.summary: SAMA is a training-free remote photoplethysmography estimator that combines quality-weighted consensus of POS and CHROM spectra, discounts pulse-free reference frequencies from motion and background signals, and tracks heart rate over time with a Viterbi ridge under a random-walk prior. It evaluates on 218 recordings from 111 participants across five public datasets with no learned parameters or dataset-specific tuning.

entry.title: The Cross-Context Threshold Test: Detecting Discrimination Under Environmental Shifts

author.name: Jun Yuan and Xinyue Ye

entry.summary: This paper studies threshold-based tests for detecting discrimination in the Veil-of-Darkness setting, showing that standard tests violate assumptions when applied separately across daylight and darkness contexts due to risk distribution drift. The authors propose a cross-context threshold test enforcing distributional invariance and monotonic threshold decay, validated on NYC stop-and-frisk data and synthetic experiments. It matters because it improves the statistical rigor of fairness auditing in social contexts.

entry.title: SMAD: A Semantics-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Unsupervised Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Qinghua Liu, Junpeng Wang, Mingzhi Hu, Menghai Pan, Shubham Jain, Yuzhong Chen, Yan Zheng, Yiwei Cai, John Paparrizos

entry.summary: SMAD is an LLM-based multi-agent framework for time-series anomaly detection that first translates an anomaly intent into a natural-language semantic contract specifying target event patterns and validation questions, then builds and tests detection pipelines against that contract. This addresses the problem that automated TSAD selects how to detect without defining what to detect. LLM agents propose detectors governed by the measurable contract.

entry.title: Directional Bias in Quantile SGD and Score-Inversion Inference under Dependence

author.name: Xiaoli Li, Qianqian Lei, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: This statistics paper analyzes quantile stochastic gradient descent, showing that serially dependent inputs introduce a directional bias that existing independence-based guarantees miss and that score autocovariances cannot detect—reversing a stationary stream leaves autocovariances unchanged but can triple the leading bias. The authors decompose the bias into lag-specific threshold-observation interactions and a curvature term, and propose delaying the threshold to remove interactions one lag at a time.

entry.title: PFN-Syn: Generating Synthetic Tabular Data with Prior-Data Fitted Networks

author.name: Michael Zuo, Inwon Kang, Oshani Seneviratne, Stacy Patterson

entry.summary: Introduces PFN-Syn, a training-free synthetic tabular data generator built on prior-data fitted networks (tabular foundation models). On eight binary classification datasets it achieves the best average downstream utility versus training-based generators, with faster generation and competitive distributional similarity and privacy metrics. This matters because it removes dataset-specific training costs from a common privacy-preserving data sharing workflow.

entry.title: A generative framework for unified representations bridging electrophysiological and haemodynamic brain activity

author.name: Weiheng Yao, Changhong Jing, Xuhang Chen, Chi-Man Pun, Michael Kwok-Po Ng, Shuqiang Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a generative framework that aligns EEG recordings with hemodynamic signals (fMRI BOLD, fNIRS) in a unified representation space, enabling generation of hemodynamic responses from electrophysiological data. Generated signals reproduce cortical maps, functional connectivity, and task structure, supporting cross-task decoding. This matters because paired multimodal brain recordings are hard to scale, so cross-modality generation could broaden neuroimaging applications.

entry.title: DisSparse: Pipelined Top-$p$ Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving

author.name: Nurlan Nazaraliyev, Elaheh Sadredini, Nael Abu-Ghazaleh

entry.summary: This paper introduces DisSparse, a system for long-context LLM inference that replaces the dominant fixed-budget top-k sparse attention primitive with adaptive top-p (nucleus) token selection. The authors argue top-k wastes memory bandwidth on heads with peaky attention distributions and drops important context on diffuse ones, and they present a pipelined design that makes variable-budget top-p selection compatible with static-allocation serving systems like vLLM.

entry.title: MedCoast: Semantic Abstraction of Reasoning Trajectories for Test-Time Biomedical Question Answering

author.name: Yishan Zhong, Jieru Li, Xuanzhe Ding, Shaunna Wang, Yanxin Yang, Micky C. Nnamdi, J. Ben Tamo, Yifei Wang, Yining Yuan, Benoit L. Marteau, Shaun Q. Y. Tan, Carrie Moore, Luyu Xie, Yang Xie, Wenqi Shi, May D. Wang

entry.summary: MedCoast converts sampled chain-of-thought trajectories into a compact abstract reasoning tree by recursively clustering semantically similar steps under shared prefixes, then derives node-level supervision for efficient test-time biomedical QA under limited inference budgets. This avoids redundant search over free-form language.

entry.title: Reducing Permutation Sensitivity in Multimodal Large Language Models via Shared Positions and Attention-Only Distillation

author.name: Yifei Cheng, Xiaolin Zhang, Yu-Xuan Qiu

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies permutation bias in multimodal LLMs, categorizing it into four scenarios and analyzing root causes via multiple-choice QA with reordered text options. The authors propose shared positions with blocked cross-unit attention (SP-B) and a bidirectional variant (SP-V), then use attention-only distillation from frozen native models to recover accuracy lost to the structural changes. This matters because order-invariance failures are a persistent reliability problem for deployed multimodal models.

entry.title: Neural Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling

author.name: Yan-Han Chen, Abhishek Halder, Hailiang Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a neural solver for the Schrodinger bridge problem based on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. By learning the optimal velocity of an ordinary differential equation instead of the drift of a stochastic differential equation, the method only requires source and target samples rather than full distributions, making it well suited to high-dimensional generative modeling. Experiments on low- and high-dimensional real and synthetic datasets demonstrate its effectiveness.

entry.title: Dual-Stream Event-to-Video Reconstruction

author.name: Lei Sun, Zhendong Li, Chenxin Shao, Weilun Li, Ruibo Ming, Kaiwei Wang, Jinjin Gu, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: Proposes EvDualDiff, a dual-stream framework for event-camera video reconstruction inspired by parvocellular/magnocellular pathways in human vision, combining a brightness reference from temporal-mapping events with motion-event cues, conditioned into a video diffusion model that autoregressively reconstructs long sequences. This addresses the fundamental ill-posedness of event-to-video conversion via a biologically motivated brightness reference. Includes photometric constraints and self-generated data finetuning.

entry.title: Learning Continuous Scene Depth Representations via Cross-Modal Gaussian Rendering

author.name: Zhiwei Zhong, Lingyu Zhu, Baoliang Chen, Peilin Chen, Shiqi Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a cross-modal Gaussian rendering framework for arbitrary-scale depth super-resolution with color guidance, building hierarchical representations to avoid per-pixel neural decoding while recovering sharp depth boundaries. It addresses the practical problem that RGB-D systems have varying resolution gaps and existing methods assume fixed integer upsampling factors. It is a solid technical contribution to geometric scene understanding, though within an established research line.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Self-Supervised Learning for Cuneiform Sign Representation

author.name: Asim Niaz, Morris Alper, Shai Gordin, and Enrique Jim\'enez

entry.summary: The paper pretrains a masked autoencoder, CuneiMAE, on over 900K unlabeled cuneiform sign crops and shows it substantially outperforms ImageNet-pretrained MAE, CLIP, and DINOv2 on a 218-class sign recognition benchmark (43.7% vs 25.2% linear-probe accuracy), with gains on cross-period transfer. It demonstrates the value of domain-specific SSL for ancient scripts where expert annotation is scarce. This is a strong example of adapting foundation-model techniques to the digital humanities.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Planning: Spatiotemporal Planning and Plan Repair in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Siyuan Li, Ethan Lin, Xiang Li, Tianming Liu

entry.summary: The authors introduce Railbound-Bench, a benchmark of railway puzzle layouts with a simulator that tests multimodal LLMs on spatiotemporal planning and repair of failed plans across up to five attempts. Best-of-nine models solves only 59.5% on the main set, with most models at 10% or below, exposing large gaps between visual understanding and genuine planning.

entry.title: Joint Client Scheduling and Resource Allocation for Optimal Federated Learning over Wireless Networks

author.name: Ahmad Dabaja and Rachid El-Azouzi

entry.summary: The paper introduces RAOCS, a resource-aware optimal client sampling framework for federated learning over wireless networks that minimizes sampling variance under uplink resource-block constraints, round deadlines, and update-size limits. It unifies variance-minimizing sampling with communication-aware scheduling, which prior work treated separately.

entry.title: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qihang Chen, Tengjie Li, Hongwei Lu, Jason Wu, Chyna Qu, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: The authors introduce SG-LL, a vision-language-action model that predicts an actionable near-future latent representation grounded in the current spatial state, combining distilled geometric knowledge from a frozen spatial teacher with predictive lookahead. The method addresses the gap between semantic competence and precise manipulation by ensuring predicted future information is anchored in control-relevant spatial states. It targets improved manipulation performance in robot learning.

entry.title: Interaction Retention and Output-Likelihood Training in Parallel Sampling

author.name: Da Li, Bo Jin, Xiaopeng Wei, Hui Wang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper gives an exact account of distributional distortion in parallel samplers such as masked diffusion language models, which generate multiple coordinates per step from conditional marginals. The Gram operator's eigenvalues are interpreted as retention probabilities for interactions, determining the exact frontier between output accuracy and conditional calibration, its regularization path, and population responses of finite-mixture likelihood training, including a sharp dichotomy for pairwise interactions. This quantifies a fundamental limitation of parallel generation.

entry.title: SENSA: Visual-to-Brain Generation with Individualized Subject-State Transfer and Adaptation

author.name: Yihang Zou, Chunmei Qing, Ruixi Liang, Haichuan Wei, Junpeng Tan, Qifan Yang, Wanxiang Luo, Haodong Li, Xiangmin Xu, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: SENSA is a framework for predicting brain responses to visual stimuli that disentangles shared neural activity from image-specific responses and calibrates a compact per-subject state, improving cross-subject generalization with limited calibration data. This matters for neural decoding and visual cognition research where individual differences and scarce data have limited encoding accuracy.

entry.title: PIAE: Physics-Informed Continuous Autoencoding for Compact 3D Human Motion

author.name: Osama Alshammari, Omar Mohammed, Kerven Durdymyradov, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: PIAE is a physics-informed continuous autoencoder that allocates a fixed token budget between explicitly retained kinematic signals (root velocity, heading) and learned features, achieving 8x temporal compression with strong global trajectory fidelity. On HumanML3D it reports 8.936mm global MPJPE, an 82% reduction relative to baselines.

entry.title: EmoRouter: Adaptive Modality Cascading for Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Fangxu Yu, Lingzhi Yuan, Dehai Min, Tao Feng, Ge Liu, Furong Huang, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: EmoRouter is a training-free, model-agnostic cascading framework that adaptively selects which modality combinations (text, audio, vision) to run through an omni-modal LLM per utterance for emotion recognition, balancing accuracy against compute. It exploits the observation that extra modalities sometimes fix and sometimes break predictions.

entry.title: Do You Even Know What I Want? Improving LLMs Ability to Detect Hidden User Intent

author.name: Kelsey Sikes and Sarath Sreedharan

entry.summary: The paper adapts a formulation of the objective misspecification problem to LLMs, where users hold skewed beliefs about the system's model and LLMs tend to answer by default rather than ask clarifying questions. The authors test whether proactive questioning about objectives improves goal alignment. This addresses a documented behavioral gap with direct relevance to assistant alignment.

entry.title: When Can a Rewiring Control Test LLM Weight Readers? C2 and an Eligibility Protocol

author.name: Vaishak Girish Kumar, Sanika Vilas Najan

entry.summary: The paper proposes C2, a counterfactual control that permutes columns of a network's final readout while preserving weight-space statistics, to distinguish whether LLMs predicting small-network outputs rely on weight fingerprints or on actual computation. It states an eligibility protocol under which C2 validly separates the two hypotheses.

entry.title: Supply the Global, Supervise the Local: Combining Representation Conditioning and Alignment in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Chaojie Ji, Sergio Quiroga-Sandoval, Ruxin Wang, Zheju Zheng, Yankai Cao

entry.summary: This paper studies whether representation alignment (REPA) targets and representation conditioning inputs conflict when combined in diffusion transformer training. The authors decompose image patch representations into global (image-level) and local components, using the global part as a conditioning token while supervising on the local part, empirically testing where the two roles overlap and interfere. This clarifies design principles for faster, better-conditioned image generation training.

entry.title: On Adaptive Step Sizes for Eligibility Traces in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Esraa Elelimy, Martha White

entry.summary: The paper studies basic design questions for eligibility-trace algorithms in deep RL, where incremental streaming updates with multi-step credit assignment are enjoying renewed interest as alternatives to replay-buffer methods. The authors analyze how adaptive step sizes should interact with traces, addressing under-explored fundamentals from the linear era in the deep setting. Foundational empirical work for streaming deep RL.

entry.title: Force2Act: A Force-Aware Visuomotor Policy for Generalizable Compliant Robot Manipulation

author.name: Keerthi Vasan Murugan, Fangguo Zhao, Jiafei Duan

entry.summary: Force2Act is a hybrid force-position policy for contact-rich manipulation that scales planned force relative to measured interaction rather than reproducing demonstrated force levels. It combines a global force policy planning per action chunk with a reactive Mixture of Force Experts module that regulates force at each control step.

entry.title: Dually Constrained Parameter Projection for Continual Learning

author.name: Bowyn Tan, Zhilong Zheng, Yang Guan, Liming Xiao, Liye Tang, Xiao Li, Naizheng Wang, Keqiang Li, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes DUET, a bidirectional Jacobian null-space projection algorithm for continual learning that constrains parameters from both previous and new tasks during post-training adjustment. Unlike unidirectional projection that only minimizes distance to the new-task optimum, DUET formulates a dually constrained optimization that also respects the new-task loss landscape.

entry.title: Counting Symbols on Technical Drawings: A Benchmark and Verified Rewards for MLLMs

author.name: Junxian Li, Ruixuan Yang, Zhenhua Xu

entry.summary: This paper introduces CountDrawBench, a benchmark of 1,574 counting questions over technical drawings such as floor plans, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and molecular structures, where multimodal LLMs currently struggle due to small, dense, or convention-implied objects. It also proposes Code-Verified RL, a reinforcement learning framework that trains MLLMs to count using executable feedback, combining a count reward with two other complementary reward signals. The work addresses a real gap in applying vision-language models to engineering and scientific document understanding.

entry.title: Prompt-Consistent Cross-View Object Geo-Localization

author.name: Lingyun Xing, Wenning Hao, Kai Jiang, Dawei Jin, Xiaohan Zhang, Xiaoxiong Zhang

entry.summary: This work shows that existing cross-view object geo-localization methods overfit to spurious scene-object correlations: moving or removing the click prompt barely changes predictions. Tracing this to a small benchmark of only 4,343 prompt-object pairs, the authors propose two plug-in remedies to make models genuinely follow prompt semantics. The diagnostic is valuable for anyone building instruction-following localization systems.

entry.title: Specification-Aware Sparse Differentiation: Planning under Signal Temporal Logic with Sparsemax Robustness

author.name: Sai Sandeep Damera, Ryan Matheu, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: This work derives sparsity patterns for Jacobian and Hessian computation directly from Signal Temporal Logic task specifications, enabling efficient gradient-based optimal control that would otherwise be computationally intractable. It leverages this structure with the Sparsemax robustness formulation. The contribution improves scalability of formal-methods-guided trajectory optimization.

entry.title: BenchMint: From Real-World Tasks to Executable Benchmarks

author.name: Zining Huang, Zuo Wang, Mengyao Zhang, Yilan Piao, Zhe Wang, Shuohan Wang, Ruiying Wang, Huicong Yi, Qianyu Yang, Zilong Pan, Wenlong Wu, Jiajun Shi, Shen Yan, Xingyu Pan, Houxuan Chen, Yuan Xu, Jinzhao Li

entry.summary: BenchMint is an automated workflow for building LLM benchmarks of everyday reasoning and tool use, jointly constructing tasks and scoring criteria from source documents, with Daily-Life offering 100 tasks across 11 domains judged via tool traces and private evidence. The authors report descriptive results for 26 model/harness configurations including GPT, Claude, and Gemini families while explicitly avoiding controlled rankings. It contributes to more trustworthy, contamination-resistant evaluation of agentic everyday reasoning.

entry.title: SAE-Audit: Clinical-Trial Prediction via Inference-Time Optimization of Black-Box LLMs Audited by Sparse Autoencoder Evidence

author.name: Junbo Shen

entry.summary: SAE-Audit improves black-box LLM predictions of clinical-trial completion or early termination by extracting clinical-concept evidence from a sparse autoencoder on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and using it to optimize a frontier LLM at inference time. The work addresses the reliability and faithfulness gaps that keep LLM trial-outcome forecasts only modestly above chance.

entry.title: Phase-Conditioned Action Contracts for Auditable Microsurgical Control

author.name: Jiaxi You, Yiwei Shi, Yanlin Li, Rihui Song, Weibing Li, Kai Huang, Weiru Liu

entry.summary: This work introduces phase-conditioned action contracts for robotic microsurgery that separate learned action proposals from deterministic command formation, enforcing admissibility, bounds, and phase-dependent task-space decoding, plus a read-only provenance trace for exact replay and rule-level auditing. It reports 94.27% procedural completion on held-out retinal-injection evaluations.

entry.title: CAR: Reducing Decoder Output Shift in Visual Token Pruning via Coverage Selection and Attention Reallocation

author.name: Xixi Jiang, Pingcheng Dong, Chen Yang, Xin Yang, Kwang-Ting Cheng

entry.summary: Analyzes degradation in MLLMs under aggressive visual token pruning by decomposing the decoder output shift in closed form into an image summary error and an attention allocation error. The proposed CAR framework mitigates both via coverage-based token selection and attention reallocation that restores the visual attention share. It specifically targets visual grounding, where existing pruning methods fail badly.

entry.title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning

author.name: Jiarui Li, Runyu Zhang, and Gioele Zardini

entry.summary: Presents TAKT, a framework that accounts for robot dynamics before search, reducing kinodynamic multi-agent planning to a lattice search for double-integrator robots. Analytic bounds reserve clearance lost during smoothing, and a closed-form convolution converts valid plans into dynamically feasible trajectories with continuous-time collision avoidance at scale.

entry.title: Dr. Grasp-RL: Diverse and Robust Dexterous Grasping via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kunqi Xu, Xiaokang Sun, Xueyan Zou

entry.summary: This paper bridges two separate research directions in dexterous grasping: generative approaches that produce diverse grasp poses but execute open-loop, and RL approaches that learn closed-loop policies with limited behavioral diversity. The authors introduce a time-reversed curriculum with a cooperative mechanism to obtain both diversity and robustness in RL-based grasping.

entry.title: Explainable Emotion and Mental Health Reasoning in Large Language Models Using Theories of Emotion

author.name: Tadesse Destaw Bela, Iqra Ameer, Helena G\'omez Adorno, Alexander Gelbukh, Eusebio Ricardez V\'azquez, Olga Kolesnikova, Grigori Sidorov, Seid Muhie Yimam

entry.summary: This paper introduces Psychology-based Chain-of-Thought (PsyCoT), a prompting strategy that grounds LLM emotion reasoning in established psychological theories, specifically the Schachter-Singer and Cognitive Appraisal theories. Rather than directly classifying text into emotion labels, the approach elicits step-by-step reasoning about the appraisal processes that explain why a person feels a particular emotion, and is evaluated on subjective NLP tasks including emotion analysis, emotion intensity prediction, and stress detection.

entry.title: DeclareViT: Decoupling Early Classification from Feature Refinement with Exit Query for Efficient ViTs

author.name: Xinrui Gong, Yao Rong, Chuangtao Chen, Daniel Ochs, Ulf Schlichtmann, Bing Li, Kristian Kersting, Grace Li Zhang

entry.summary: DeclareViT decouples early classification from feature refinement in Vision Transformers, addressing the conflicting gradient directions that arise when shared backbone parameters must support both early exits and subsequent refinement. It introduces an exit query mechanism so easy samples terminate at intermediate layers with improved efficiency under latency and compute constraints.

entry.title: MERIT: Experience-Guided Memory for Long-Horizon Persona-Specific Persuasive Dialogue

author.name: Rohan Kirti, Akash Ghosh, Pratik Amrit, Aryan Vats, Niladri Ghosh, Sriparna Saha

entry.summary: MERIT introduces a graph-based memory of four persuasion-specific memory types plus a per-persona experience rationale library that records which persuasion strategies work for each user and why. The system enables adaptive, cross-session persuasion through prompt composition alone, without parameter updates, addressing the single-session and static limitations of prior persuasive dialogue systems.

entry.title: HandiVid: A High-Quality Dataset for Hand-Driven Interactive Video Generation

author.name: Chaoyang Zhang, Shaohao Rui, Xiaofeng Mao, Yuanxun Xu, Haoyuan Xia, Xiaohong Liu, Qinghe Du and Weijie Ma

entry.summary: This paper introduces HandiVid, a dataset of 200K curated and annotated egocentric video clips designed for hand-driven interactive video generation, where scenes respond realistically to hand movements and camera motion. The authors build a unified pipeline combining public datasets, online video, and synthetic data, using video quality assessment, hand detection filtering, and multi-stage VLM-based interaction validation. It addresses a key data bottleneck for egocentric and interactive video generation research.

entry.title: MISeg-Agent: A Human-in-the-Loop Agentic Framework for Error Diagnosis and Executable Prompt Review in 3D Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Delin An, Mingqi Xu, Jian-Xun Wang, Pengfei Gu

entry.summary: This paper introduces MISeg-Agent, a human-in-the-loop agentic framework that diagnoses localized errors in 3D medical image segmentation and offers evidence-based correction recommendations. The system adapts its diagnosis as corrections change the mask, addressing a reliability gap in deployed medical segmentation models.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Weighted Regression and Classification

author.name: Junwen Xia, Yan He, Dehan Kong, Zhenhua Lin

entry.summary: The authors extend tabular foundation models such as TabPFN-3.5 to weighted regression and classification via weighted attention, a normalized weighted loss, and pretraining on synthetic weighted tasks, enabling in-context prediction without per-dataset fitting. This serves applications from causal inference and missing-data analysis to insurance pricing.

entry.title: Can Vibe Coding Produce Accessible Websites: An Empirical Study on LLM Coding Agents and Skills

author.name: Syed Fatiul Huq, Md. Asif Haider, Abu Jafar Saifullah, Thomas Zimmermann, Sam Malek

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates the web accessibility of sites generated end-to-end by LLM coding agents across 90 websites, three agents, four language models, and multiple reasoning-effort levels, checked with axe-core, IBM Equal Access, and QualWeb tools. It examines whether agent-level accessibility interventions improve output, finding that natural-language-only development propagates accessibility defects at scale.

entry.title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions

author.name: Luizza Dalla Pria, Amelia l. Nelson, Renata Ivanek

entry.summary: An empirical study measuring how consistently GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash — both established commercial models — answer 15 H5N1 public-health questions, using 5,400 responses across repeated queries and chain-of-thought reformulations with a centroid-based evaluation framework. It establishes a consistency baseline that must precede any accuracy assessment of chatbot health advice during outbreaks.

entry.title: Training-Free Interventions for Hallucination in Large Language Models

author.name: Can Huang

entry.summary: This is a survey of 116 works on inference-time hallucination interventions in LLMs, tracing the evolution from retrieval and controllable generation to methods acting on input evidence, token scores, internal representations, claims, and answer decisions. It organizes methods by evidence source, model access, cost, and task, with a detailed decomposition of activation steering approaches.

entry.title: SpectralRoute: Adaptive Spectral Routing for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Hyperspectral Segmentation

author.name: Qingmei Li, Xiaoya Fan, Juepeng Zheng, Jianxi Huang, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: This paper proposes SpectralRoute, a training-free framework for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation of hyperspectral remote sensing imagery. It constructs complementary spectral views and adaptively routes category-specific spectral cues to vision-language models, avoiding the uniform fusion that weakens category-relevant signals. This matters because it extends open-vocabulary VLM capabilities to rich hyperspectral data without costly fine-tuning.

entry.title: Language models seek help despite guaranteed score losses in question answering

author.name: Jiahao You, Ziye Jia, Chao Dong, Fuhui Zhou, Qihui Wu

entry.summary: Across 2,291 questions and 54 expert-accuracy/cost combinations, all seven tested open-weight LLMs consult an expert even when doing so guarantees lower expected score, with help-seeking rates from 20.8% to 94.1%. Help-seeking varies across conditions with equal expected value, and fine-tuning reduces decision regret but increases inconsistency. The study reveals systematic deviations from expected-value rationality in LLM help-seeking decisions.

entry.title: SHAKTI: Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI for Nutrition and Health

author.name: Chaitanya Pallerla, Dongyi Wang

entry.summary: SHAKTI is a conversational health and nutrition assistant that answers exclusively from retrieved scholarly literature and exact food-composition data, aiming to eliminate unsupported claims and misleading citations. The system indexes hundreds of millions of OpenAlex works and is evaluated with retrieval, generation, grounding, and efficiency metrics across thousands of biomedical questions, comparing multiple RAG strategies against Claude Sonnet.

entry.title: Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing

author.name: Theshani Nuradha, Sujeet Bhalerao, Christoph Hirche, Mark M. Wilde, Mingze Xu

entry.summary: This quantum information theory paper proves that the noncommutative minimum of positive semidefinite operators is super-multiplicative on tensor products, yielding a sub-additivity property of the hockey-stick divergence on product states. This divergence characterizes quantum differential privacy and optimal binary quantum hypothesis testing, so the result has broad implications for composing privacy guarantees and analyzing multi-copy distinguishability.

entry.title: PushMimic: Learning Adaptive Humanoid Box Pushing via Dynamic Motion Augmentation and Reference Distillation

author.name: Yulun Zhuang, Hanyu Zhang, Jingyu Liu, Yanran Ding

entry.summary: This robotics paper introduces PushMimic, a framework enabling humanoid robots to push boxes adaptively when physical properties like mass and ramp inclination are unknown. The approach augments a single kinematic reference motion into a dynamically feasible dataset using sampling-based trajectory optimization, then distills it into one motion-tracking policy trained in a single stage. Simulation results show success rates improving from 57.8% to 88.8% across box masses of 5-15 kg and inclinations up to 15 degrees compared with a baseline.

entry.title: LMnOP: Pruning 3D Gaussian Splatting via Leave-Many-Out Importance

author.name: Sunjae Jeong, Jaeseung Kim, Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: LMnOP prunes 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes using leave-many-out importance — the average loss increase when a Gaussian is removed while others are also randomly removed — capturing groups of Gaussians that are redundant individually but essential jointly. Exact mean and variance computations for pixel colors support the estimate, targeting high pruning ratios where leave-one-out scores fail.

entry.title: Preserve to Compress: Beyond Low-Dimensional Latents in One-Step Diffusion Codec

author.name: Chuqin Zhou, Xiaoyue Ling, Yuhang Wei, Yunuo Chen, Guo Lu

entry.summary: PICS is a one-step generative image codec that addresses the reconstruction-generation tradeoff in pretrained latent diffusion latent spaces for ultra-low-bitrate compression. Rather than accepting lossy low-dimensional latents, it preserves source information for both coding and synthesis, improving fidelity within a fixed computational budget.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Agentic Era: Tradition, Present, and Prospect

author.name: Chenming Tang, Haolin Li, Yiran Li, Zixian Yang, Lizhu Zhai, Rui Sun, Qizhou Huang, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: A survey mapping retrieval-augmented generation onto a single lifecycle axis spanning offline indexing, pre-retrieval, retrieval, post-retrieval, and orchestration, with agentic workflows treated as a distinct paradigm. It also covers evaluation, applications, and open questions, positioning itself as the most current review of agentic RAG.

entry.title: ConsisX: Cross-View Consistency Thinking in 3D for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yunhe Zhang, Long Gao, Yuedong Fu, Gang He, Li Xu, Chang Wu, Pengyu Li

entry.summary: ConsisX tackles physically inconsistent cross-view reasoning in vision-language-action models for robotic manipulation, where 2D feature similarity causes incorrect entity associations and fragmented information across camera views. It introduces Cross-View Association Modeling and entity coherence mechanisms to enable 3D-consistent cross-view reasoning.

entry.title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation

author.name: Vasilii Liamin, Oleg Bakhteev, Vladimir Vanovskiy

entry.summary: FMSNO learns a shared map from irregular surface meshes to a regular spherical grid via flow matching with precomputed optimal transport targets, then applies Fourier or Spherical Fourier Neural Operators on the grid. The learned flow supports unseen geometries in a single forward pass, avoiding per-geometry mapping costs that dominate inference on large meshes.

entry.title: Boosting zero-shot learning through neuro-symbolic integration

author.name: Francesco Manigrasso, Fabrizio Lamberti, Lia Morra

entry.summary: This paper introduces Fuzzy Logic Prototypical Network (FLPN), which formulates zero-shot classification as prototype matching in a visual-semantic embedding space trained with a neuro-symbolic loss via the Logic Tensor Network framework. It demonstrates how symbolic background knowledge can be injected during training to improve recognition of unseen classes, an underexplored combination of neuro-symbolic AI and zero-shot learning.

entry.title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments

author.name: Yi-Fei Cao, Tianxin Huang, Hanbo Xie, Jian-Qiao Zhu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for evaluating LLM agents using interactive psychological environments rather than static, text-transcribed versions of classic psychology experiments. It argues that model behavior emerges jointly from the underlying model, its harness, and the test-time compute budget, and that psychology-style tasks offer a natural testbed for measuring how agentic workflows and deliberation levels change performance in settings where actions alter future observations.

entry.title: Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback

author.name: Hao Luan, Hao Qiu, Zhi Zheng, See-Kiong Ng, Zhiyong Huang

entry.summary: The paper tackles behavioral drift in multi-turn LLM coding agents by dynamically selecting among candidate activation-steering policies via optimistic online learning, using only aggregate feedback rather than per-step signals. This addresses the fact that a single static steering policy is rarely effective across heterogeneous tasks and execution turns.

entry.title: Automated Call for Action: RAG-Based Environmental Law Enforcement Screening System

author.name: Matas Jurkevicius, Yen-Chia Hsu

entry.summary: This paper builds a retrieval-augmented generation system that helps environmental law inspectors screen emission events by aligning air quality measurements, weather, and citizen complaints with permit conditions, using a case study of coke plants at a steel producer. It demonstrates how LLM pipelines can support evidence assembly and investigation recommendations in a real regulatory workflow.

entry.title: Policy Invariance Is Not Learning Invariance: Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Navigation with a Limited View

author.name: Nodirjon Khabibullaev, Rajat Dandekar

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how potential-based reward shaping changes the one-step reward while preserving discounted return, dissecting terms like the per-step (gamma-1)Phi contribution, terminal-state rules, and non-potential bonus cycles, then validates effects in pre-registered PPO experiments across two MiniGrid navigation tasks with 160 runs. A geodesic BFS potential substantially outperformed sparse and Euclidean potentials under limited egocentric view.

entry.title: A CPU-Only Framework for Mining Collectively-Behaving Bots in MMORPGs

author.name: Hyunsoo Kim, Jaeman Son, Sangdeok Seo, Ilhan Bang, and Man Jae Cho

entry.summary: The authors replace a GPU-trained Transformer pipeline for detecting collectively behaving bots in MMORPGs with a CPU-only approach combining zone embeddings from movement context, a training-free coordinate kernel, and density clustering. The CPU pipeline trains 3-5x faster than the GPU Transformer while matching mining quality on two commercial games, and has been deployed in production since late 2024. The paper includes practical deployment lessons on threshold setting.

entry.title: ReDiffDet: Rotation-equivariant Diffusion Model for Oriented Object Detection

author.name: Zeyu Ding, Yong Zhou, Jiaqi Zhao, Hancheng Zhu, Wen-Liang Du, Rui Yao

entry.summary: ReDiffDet formulates oriented object detection as a rotation-equivariant denoising diffusion process, representing oriented boxes as 2D Gaussian distributions so the reverse process is provably rotation-equivariant. This addresses encoding orientation, misalignment between boxes and image features, and inaccurate localization of dense objects with extreme aspect ratios. The framework targets aerial and similarly rotated-object domains.

entry.title: JONES-19: A Cultural Image Dataset Based on The Grammar of Ornament

author.name: Linh Pham, Stuart Shieber, David Alvarez-Melis, Alexandros Haridis

entry.summary: Introduces JONES-19, a curated image dataset of 1,901 ornament designs from nineteen cultures, digitized from the open-access 1856 Grammar of Ornament. It targets hard vision problems: small sample sizes, imbalanced classes, human-designed artifacts, and fine-grained distinctions in line, relief, and color, making it a benchmark for visual recognition and data-efficient learning at the ML-art intersection.

entry.title: What Environment Invariance Identifies: Minimal Invariant Sets in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces

author.name: Ridham Patel

entry.summary: Formalizes invariant causal prediction at the operator level in RKHS, calling a covariate set invariant when conditional mean embeddings of the target agree across environments, and exactly characterizes the invariant set family. It proves that invariance does not uniquely identify the direct cause set, since descendant-free supersets are also invariant, but the parent set is the unique minimal invariant set.

entry.title: Auxiliary Clues Aware's Geometry Problem Solving

author.name: Qigong Lei, Qingsong Wang, Wang Lin, Qianyi Yang, Chang Yao, Jingyuan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes AuxCA, a reinforcement learning framework (auxiliary-clues-aware GRPO) that teaches multimodal LLMs transferable auxiliary-construction strategies for geometry problem solving without generating diagrams at inference time. This avoids the instability of explicit diagram generation and the limits of attention methods that only focus on visible elements.

entry.title: Zhengrong: World Models with Pole-Based Action-Response Factorization for Direct Visual Planning

author.name: Yu Zhang, Jingrui Li, Congyu Wang, Yuhang Cheng, Wenbo Chen, Xiaobo Zhang, Jing Zou, Yuxi Dai

entry.summary: Introduces Zhengrong, a direct visual world model that decomposes latent trajectories into an initial-condition anchor, a free response, and delayed responses to action innovations, with evolution governed by a shared bank of stable conjugate poles.
