This factorization anchors predictions at the initial state, enforces causality (future actions cannot affect earlier predictions), and guarantees bounded responses to finite control plans.

entry.title: How Many Parameters Does Forecasting Need? A Survey and Code-Level Audit of Lightweight Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Issam Ait Yahia, Abdelkader El Mahdaouy, and Ismail Berrada

entry.summary: A survey and code-level audit of lightweight long-term time series forecasting, providing a taxonomy of roughly 35 models across six families and examining why models with only hundreds to tens of thousands of parameters remain competitive against large Transformer and foundation-model approaches. It also audits how parameter counts are reported in the literature, a commonly neglected methodological issue.

entry.title: SignalCount: Approximate Counts with Structured and Semantic Predicates in Seconds

author.name: Matteo Agius-D'Arrigo, Zachary Zelner, Harrison Ju, Rushab Munot

entry.summary: SignalCount is a production system that answers interactive COUNT queries combining structured filters with semantic predicates judged from text, avoiding expensive per-query LLM oracle calls through pre-computed signals. It targets the gap between fast structured queries and slow LLM-judged batch pipelines.

entry.title: Can Multimodal Fusion MakeSense for Embodied Vision in Degraded Sensing?

author.name: Cheng-Ru Chou, Shih-Yu Lai, Pei-Lin Chiang, Shou-Po Tsai, Jing-Zhe Huang, Fukuharu Tanaka, Hirozumi Yamaguchi, Bing-Yu Chen, Yu-Lun Liu, Hsun-Ping Hsieh

entry.summary: MakeSense is a multimodal fusion framework for embodied vision that addresses negative fusion, where adding a sensor increases error, by preserving sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combining it through shared bottleneck tokens. Training on full and subset views of degraded observations reduces negative fusion and clarifies when sensor additions help or hurt across five datasets.

entry.title: Certified Defense against Adversarial Patches on Traffic Signs via Mask-Aware Training

author.name: Rudra Saxena, Vishal Dev Verma, Rohan Sharma, and Palani Thanaraj K

entry.summary: This paper examines why PatchCleanser, a certified defense against adversarial patches, fails on traffic-sign recognition, certifying only 1.7-4.8% accuracy on GTSRB when paired with normally trained classifiers because masking can occlude the small central symbols that distinguish sign classes. The authors propose mask-aware training, which trains the classifier on images occluded by random mask pairs drawn from the defense's own mask set, biased toward masks covering the sign center, dramatically improving certified robustness for safety-critical road-sign classifiers.

entry.title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind

author.name: Anh Dao, Quan-Dung Pham, Danh Vinh Le, Tuyen Pham Le, Quan Nguyen, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: GlanceNav is a streaming vision-and-language navigator built on a hybrid MLLM that uses Gated DeltaNet layers to carry recurrent state across an episode at constant per-step cost, combined with a short attention window and keyframe bank. It also introduces counterfactual rewind for more efficient credit assignment than whole-episode outcome rewards.

entry.title: CoSel: Cooperation as Selection for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Yiping Li, Haohua Que, Zhipeng Bao, Wenjie Zhao, Qianwen Li

entry.summary: CoSel reframes cooperative autonomous driving by decoupling cooperation from planning: a separately trained predictor anticipates how surrounding agents will move given shared information, and the ego planner then selects among its own candidate trajectories. This avoids needing rare cooperative demonstrations to teach a planner when shared information should change decisions.

entry.title: LeCellModel: Interpretable Density Estimation over the Gene Expression Manifold

author.name: Gil Karin, Artemii Bakulin, Nir Yosef

entry.summary: LeCellModel argues that modeling the distribution of cell states on the gene expression manifold should be the primary objective for single-cell representation learning, building on LeJEPA's SIGReg objective that enforces an isotropic Gaussian latent. By reading the encoder's Jacobian log-volume under this Gaussian latent, it enables density estimation, rare-state detection, perturbation scoring, and gene-level attribution in one framework.

entry.title: Explanation Selection in Abductive Learning

author.name: En-Hao Gao, Yuan Jiang

entry.summary: This paper develops a dynamical analysis of abductive learning (ABL), showing how the bidirectional feedback between machine learning and logical reasoning can select among competing explanations of intermediate concepts. The authors prove that Gram matrices with identical spectra can select different explanations under identical supervision, objective, and initialization, clarifying when incorrect concept semantics become locked in and when labels remain correctable.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned

author.name: Mohit Tekriwal, Het Mankad, Naifeng Zhang, Keita Teranishi, Sahil Bhola, Daisuke Uchida, Jean-Baptiste Jeannin, Franz Franchetti, Karthik Duraisamy, Jeffrey Vetter, Yohann Dudouit

entry.summary: The paper presents a systematic study of using agentic AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex) and specialized mathematics agents to auto-formalize applied mathematics and scientific computing code, extending beyond pure-math theorem formalization. Through case studies, it documents challenges such as formalizing computational procedures and modeling transformations rather than declarative theorems, and distills lessons learned.

entry.title: D\'ej\`a VAE: When Do Autoencoder Traces Reveal Generated Images?

author.name: Saugat Pandey

entry.summary: This paper analyzes reconstruction-based detection of AI-generated images, showing that a second pass through a diffusion model's autoencoder changes its output little, leaving a detectable fingerprint. Using a frozen vision foundation model to read this trace in intermediate layers, the author finds the signal is specific to each generator's exact decoder, with the correct autoencoders catching 94-100% of generated images at a 5% false-alarm rate on Synthbuster while near-identical variants catch only 7-42%. The work clarifies both when such detectors succeed and their fundamental limitation in generalizing to unseen generators.

entry.title: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Jiaze Li, Jingyang Chen, Wenhao Zhao, Haoran Xu, Zhenlong Yuan, Dianmo Sheng, Yuanxing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why self-teacher distillation from vision-language critic revisions barely improves text-to-image alignment: prompt rewrites entangle the intended fix with unrelated scene additions. It proposes Hindsight Twins (HinT), which isolates the critic's correction so distillation learns only the fix rather than the full rewrite. This offers a cleaner mechanism for self-improving generative models without absorbing critic artifacts.

entry.title: Leakage-Safe Auditing of Attribution-Driven Data Curation in Medical Imaging

author.name: Malay Phadke, Akshay Gokhale

entry.summary: The paper formulates attribution-driven data curation as three testable claims (anomaly detection, harmfulness estimation, intervention utility) and audits a 3D CT angiography classifier with a patient-disjoint, identifier-preserving protocol. It uncovers hundreds of exactly zero-valued arrays among training positives and invalidates a historical attention-failure subgroup, finding GradCAM++ attribution patterns central across candidate classes on held-out data.

entry.title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zien Wang, Yuhao Pan, Yunfeng Fan, Nan Cheng, Xin Xia, Wenchao Xu

entry.summary: WeaveVLA improves vision-language-action models by explicitly encoding task-relevant relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and references via a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network, with recurrent edge states tracking evolving spatial context across observations. A learned-query readout summarizes the graph for action generation. The work targets the gap between implicit VLA representations and explicit 3D relational understanding.

entry.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis

author.name: Yiming Sun, Yifan Wang, Aosong Feng, Yijia Ma, Ben Cheng, Xurui Wang, Yufan He, Yucheng Tang, Qing Lyu, Daguang Xu, Pei-Fen Kuan, Mingzhou Ding, Wen Li, Chenyu You

entry.summary: The authors introduce Neurovascular Codes, shared EEG representations learned from target-specific frozen encoders, which condition a stochastic interpolant to synthesize fMRI signals from EEG windows. Evaluated on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets with over 61,000 volume-level pairs, the model improves correlation under within- and held-out-subject settings.

entry.title: Riemann is Good News For Alignment

author.name: Josh Snider

entry.summary: The author pushes back against the view that the recent solving of the Riemann Hypothesis by Levent Alpoge working with Claude, formalized in Lean, is bad news for AI safety. While agreeing that this demonstrates very short timelines and rapid AI research capability, the author argues that superhuman performance in formal mathematics arriving before broad real-world agency is actually favorable for alignment, since current methods may suffice in worlds where capability gains are domain-limited.

entry.title: Epigraph Form Reinforcement Learning-based Safe Trajectory Tracking Control for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Xiaoke Yang, Jin Chen, Yafei Wang, Qi Zhang, Ming Li, Haiwen Wu, Chengliang Yin, Yong Zhang

entry.summary: STTC-EFRL applies epigraph-form reinforcement learning to safe trajectory tracking for connected autonomous vehicles, avoiding the unstable training of Lagrangian constrained RL where growing multipliers amplify policy-gradient magnitudes. The framework improves tracking accuracy over non-learning baselines while maintaining collision avoidance in dynamic environments.

entry.title: WISP: Composable Representations for Wrist-Worn Activity Recognition

author.name: Zipeng Wu, Shiqiao Zhou, Fabian Spill, James Andrews

entry.summary: The paper introduces WristHARBench, a standardized participant-disjoint benchmark spanning nine wrist-acceleration datasets, and WISP, a composable representation space capturing complementary motion patterns (shape, rhythm, temporal order, cross-axis relations) for wrist-only activity recognition. This addresses a real benchmarking flaw where prior datasets mix body-worn sensor positions. It is a solid benchmark-plus-method contribution for wearable sensing.

entry.title: UbiEnlight: User-Perception-Aware Real-Time Low-Light Video Enhancement on Mobile Devices and Smartglasses

author.name: Minfan Wang, Sicong Liu, Teng Li, Zimu Zhou, Sixun He, Bin Guo, Junzhao Du, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: UbiEnlight is presented as the first diffusion-transformer-based on-device system for real-time, temporally stable low-light video enhancement on smartphones and smartglasses. It exploits the insight that illumination and structure separate more robustly in the frequency domain, using specialized processing to handle spatiotemporally coupled low-light and motion degradations that defeat per-frame post-hoc consistency. Targeting users with night blindness and near-eye displays adds an accessibility dimension.

entry.title: GC-GS: Optimizing 3D Gaussian Splatting with Gradient Conflict as a Geometry Signal

author.name: Chenhao Zhang, Fengze Zhang, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: GC-GS reformulates 3D Gaussian Splatting training with multiple reconstruction and perceptual losses as multi-objective optimization, deriving conflict-aware position updates that reduce interference between competing objectives. The paper observes that gradient conflicts persist throughout training and correlate with Gaussian positions, using them as a geometry signal. A solid methodological contribution to 3D scene reconstruction quality.

entry.title: ENGRAM: Reliability-Weighted Latent Fusion and Occlusion-Aware Layered Readout for Video World Models

author.name: Chenhao Wu, Zhaolong Su, Yang Liu, Tianrui Su, Yingguang Yang, Shang Luo, Yancheng Chen, Chongyang Zhang, Hao Zheng, Kefu Xu, Congjing Ran, Bin Chong

entry.summary: ENGRAM improves camera-conditioned video world models with a latent spatial memory that recursively fuses geometrically and visually compatible observations into a consolidated scene representation and provides occlusion-aware layered readout across depths. This replaces naive set-union updates and frontmost-only readout, improving 3D consistency in generated videos.

entry.title: BReD: BEV Residual Diffusion for Feed-Forward Road Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Baizhi Wang

entry.summary: BReD is a feed-forward framework reconstructing road elevation, appearance, and semantics from six-camera sequences, using LiDAR-supervised depth learning and BEV lifting for coarse elevation, then refining it with a lightweight BEV residual diffusion model conditioned on depth-elevation discrepancy. This targets the gap between optimization-based methods with high per-scene cost and feed-forward methods with poor elevation accuracy.

entry.title: What Do Differentiable Rule Learners Need? FLARE: Fuzzy Rules with Additive Evidence

author.name: Javier Fumanal-Idocin, Javier Andreu-Perez

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why differentiable rule learners underperform, finding that rule weighting drives most performance — random rules with learned weights beat all published differentiable rule learners tested. Based on this insight the authors propose FLARE, a fuzzy rule learner with additive evidence. The finding is a striking negative result for the neurosymbolic rule-learning literature.

entry.title: Learning a Food World Model That Predicts the Next State from Production Data

author.name: Inkyu Sa, Gaurav Kuppa, Steve Van der Hoeven, Konstantin Stulov, Rajat Bhageria, Luis Rayas

entry.summary: The authors learn a world model for food-assembly robots that predicts post-pick pan state and picked mass with uncertainty, trained self-supervised on 61,773 production picks labeled automatically by camera and scale. The model beats both commanded targets and the controller's internal mass estimate on 12,294 held-out picks across nine foods. It demonstrates industrial-scale world modeling from unlabeled production data.

entry.title: Occupancy Planar Patch: Incremental Probabilistic Bounded-Plane Reconstruction from LiDAR Data

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Chaehyeon Song, Dongjiao He, Jan Quenzel, Lintong Zhang, Ayoung Kim and Maurice Fallon

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Occupancy Planar Patch, an incremental bounded-plane representation for online LiDAR surface reconstruction that models anisotropic range noise and free-space constraints directly in range-space. A single ray-to-patch association weight jointly updates plane geometry, surface boundaries, and camera image blending, achieving state-of-the-art precision on Oxford Spires and Multi-Campus sequences.

entry.title: An equivariant classical density functional for ionic fluids at complex interfaces

author.name: Bingqing Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces a machine-learned classical density functional for ionic fluids combining a symmetry-adapted neural free energy for short-range correlations with explicit long-range electrostatics, trained on the full-Coulomb restricted primitive model. A single functional transfers to charge-patterned particles and structured electrodes, reproducing molecular dynamics structure and forces including electrostatic force reversals. Notable work from a recognized computational chemistry researcher (Bingqing Cheng).

entry.title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning

author.name: Kaili Zheng, Wei Ding, Yuchen Ding, Kaiwen Wang, Xun Zhu, Chenyi Guo, Yudong Zhang, Ji Wu

entry.summary: X-AQA is the first unified training and evaluation framework for general-purpose action quality assessment using multimodal LLMs, built on X-AQA-40K, a corpus of 40,163 samples from 22 sources across sports, fitness, rehabilitation, and general skills. Heterogeneous annotations are converted into a unified QA format, and a single fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B model handles cross-domain assessment. This moves AQA beyond dataset-specific silos.

entry.title: AsyncMixVLA: Runtime Asynchronous Robot Policy Switching for Adaptation to Dynamic Environments

author.name: Tamoghno Das, Keyon Jazayeri, Yerin Cho, Nazmul Takbir, Arshia Aravinthan, Nikil Dutt

entry.summary: Presents AsyncMixVLA, an adaptive inference framework for asynchronous switching between heterogeneous vision-language-action policies under mid-rollout environmental perturbations. A learned trigger balances recovery potential against intervention harm to escalate to higher-compute policies while avoiding stalls from synchronous inference or stale-observation errors.

entry.title: Action-Conditioned Transition Irreversibility for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Emil Mittag, Richard Dazeley, and Peter Vamplew

entry.summary: Proposes ACTI, an OOD detector for reinforcement learning that evaluates forward versus backward transition likelihoods, calibrates against the in-distribution profile per timestep, and smooths scores over a window without future information. Evaluated rigorously across six environments, fifteen detectors, and multiple anomaly mechanisms and policy replicates.

entry.title: Seeing 3D Occupancy Through Scene-Adaptive Projection

author.name: Yuan Wu, Zhiqiang Yan, Zhengxue Wang, Guangfa Wang, Jun Li, Jian Yang

entry.summary: Proposes SAP, a scene-adaptive projection framework for vision-based 3D occupancy prediction that uses depth-based geometric priors from a frozen depth model to guide 2D-to-3D view transformation, replacing scene-agnostic uniform sampling of reference points. This allocates sampling budget to actual scene geometry rather than empty space, improving efficiency. Relevant to autonomous driving perception where occupancy prediction is a key task.

entry.title: VTLA-RL: Learning Visuotactile Policies for Load-Adaptive Grasping

author.name: Qiwei Wu, Qixuan Li, Xin Xiang, Xiangyu Chen, Xiang Xiao, Daochen Shi, Ruihua Zhang, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: VTLA-RL trains visuotactile grasping policies that adjust to varying object loads and slip using a shared visual encoder over tactile histories and RGB, generating motion and bilateral force targets in a unified action space. Mixed real/simulated demonstrations establish priors, then two-stage multi-task RL in simulation optimizes success without requiring load-varied real demonstrations.

entry.title: NavDecision: Parallel Multi-Step Action Prediction with Persistent Self-Referential Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Kai Wu, Yufan Hu, Quan Fang, Boning Zhang, Junyu Gao

entry.summary: NavDecision is an efficient VLN decision model that predicts multiple action distributions in parallel from a shared vision-language state (PMAP) instead of token-by-token generation, paired with memory-augmented self-referential policy optimization that learns from unsuccessful trajectories using successful ones as references, plus a cross-iteration success memory.

entry.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics

author.name: Rulin Zhou, Yujie Ma, Rui Tang, Qiujie Song, Wanhao Liu, Guoheng Ma, Liangjing Shao, An Wang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: KineState-SWAM is a surgical world-action model that couples action prediction and video generation through a persistent interaction state, explicitly separating kinematically determined instrument motion from learned tissue/scene evolution. It uses a flow-matching policy for joint trajectories, kinematic geometry conditioning converting trajectories into surface-motion tokens via calibrated URDF kinematics, and causal interaction dynamics with geometry-guided attention. The work targets reliable surgical scene prediction and action generation.

entry.title: Div3DAfford: Diverse 3D affordance grounding

author.name: Haomeng Zhang, Raymond A. Yeh

entry.summary: The paper defines a new task, diverse 3D affordance grounding, requiring multiple plausible region predictions per object-affordance query, and proposes Div3DAffordNet, a transformer set-prediction model. An automated data pipeline using 2D generative models and 3D reconstruction with lightweight human verification (72X annotation speedup) yields the Div3DAfford benchmark.

entry.title: PruneNAS: Constraint Aware Neural Architecture Search based Pruning

author.name: Sudhakar Sah, Nikhil Chhabra, Honnesh Rohmetra, Andy Li

entry.summary: PruneNAS integrates structured pruning into neural architecture search, generating candidate architectures by pruning pretrained networks at multiple granularities and selecting via training-free importance metrics as a global optimization problem. This cuts search cost from hundreds of GPU hours to minutes while respecting resource constraints.

entry.title: Stochastic non-metric MDS for noisy high-dimensional data

author.name: Sebastian Damrich, Dmitry Kobak

entry.summary: The authors extend prior theory for metric MDS on uninformative data to finite high-dimensional datasets with concentrated distances, showing metric MDS embeddings stay close to the data-independent limit under the curse of dimensionality. They then show non-metric MDS is more robust to high-dimensional noise and can produce informative embeddings where metric MDS fails.

entry.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation

author.name: Mohamed Kamel, Tamer Nadeem

entry.summary: TrustFlow-ECG combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow ECG restoration model with a lightweight window-level risk predictor that estimates whether a restored waveform is trustworthy for downstream analysis. It achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, validated on MIT-BIH, PTB-XL, and mixed noise conditions.

entry.title: Unleashing the Value of Raw Point Clouds for 3D Understanding with LLMs

author.name: Tailai Chen, Jiawei Yu, Yiming Cheng, Ping Nie, Yongyong Chen, Tao Zhou, Zheng Zhu, Ming Li

entry.summary: PointTool is an encoder-free, tool-augmented framework for 3D reasoning with LLMs, using Alignment-Free Patch Tokenization to aggregate raw point clouds locally while preserving fine-grained structure, and enabling active inspection of task-relevant 3D regions and external knowledge retrieval. This removes the representation bottleneck of pretrained point encoders and moves beyond single-pass closed-book generation. A notable direction for 3D multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Curvature Mismatch and Local Errors in Galaxy Property Estimation

author.name: Austin Lutterbach, Angus Hoy, Jasper Chong, Aman Kumar, Michael J. Smith

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that linear probes on curved representation manifolds have systematic intrinsic errors characterized by the dot product of the probe normal with the manifold's second fundamental form, termed probe-facing curvature. Even a representation containing complete target information can yield biased probe estimates due to manifold geometry.

entry.title: MM-DataLoop: Closing the Data-Side Loop for Recursive Self-Improvement in MLLM Post-Training

author.name: Likang Peng, Chen Ju, Xu Chen, Xiangyang Wu, Jinsong Lan, Haihong Tang, Ying Chen

entry.summary: MM-DataLoop studies the data side of recursive self-improvement for multimodal LLM post-training, organizing data interventions into five operation families connected through an Observe-Diagnose-Plan-Execute-Verify-Reflect cycle with shared rule memory. Controlled experiments on Qwen3.5-0.8B across five benchmarks show a 5.32-point mean improvement over the zero-shot baseline across 34 candidate rounds.

entry.title: DeciForm: Incorporating Task Structure into Decision Models

author.name: Qiuyu Tian, Haojie Yin, Yingce Xia, Youyong Kong, Zequn Liu

entry.summary: Deciform is a unified decision model that respects differing answer-space structures: order-invariant classification via candidate-free queries and isolated branches, and numerical scoring via a log-spherical objective plus a decimal-prefix readout combining point and interval supervision. Shared adapters and task-private components support joint multi-task adaptation, and it shows gains on a shared 15,000-request test set. The design is relevant to LLMs serving mixed decision tasks in production.

entry.title: MSBench: Benchmarking Script-Controlled Multi-Shot Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Tao Huang, ZiHao Liang, Junhao Liu, Junzhe Li, Yuancheng Wei, Sifan Zuo, Beiming Yu, Taojin Liu, Zhuoyang Li, Bing Cao

entry.summary: MSBench is a benchmark for controllable multi-shot text-to-video generation built on structured Scene-Entity-Shot mini-scripts specifying shot timing, camera state, content, and transitions, with a four-dimensional hybrid evaluation protocol. It measures capabilities (cut timing, cross-shot continuity) that existing single-shot benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: RSWP: Robust SO(3)-Equivariant Watermarking for Panoramic Images

author.name: Pengzhen Chen, Yanwei Liu, Xiaoyan Gu, Jinxia Liu, Siwei Ma, Weiping Wang, Wu Liu

entry.summary: Proposes RSWP, a watermarking framework for panoramic images grounded in icosahedral group theory, decomposing spherical rotations into local planar rotations and facet permutations to survive SO(3) viewing rotations. It uses a decoupling architecture that embeds watermarks into discrete facets with theoretically grounded robustness. This addresses topological mismatch between spherical signals and planar watermarking representations, including viewport extraction.

entry.title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity

author.name: Qi Wu, Xiaoyu Liu, Ao Wang, Rongsheng Wang, Wenting Chen, Wenxuan Wang, Qingsong Yao

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode in closed-ended medical VQA called stable wrongness, where models give confident, repeatable incorrect yes/no answers even when patient-specific visual evidence is removed or mismatched. This undermines sampling-stability uncertainty methods including hallucination-aware calibration variants, and motivates counterfactual answer-sensitivity evaluation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations

author.name: Anurag Kadkol, Lawson L.S. Wong

entry.summary: The authors use an LLM to generate an advice policy producing demonstration data at no human cost, then warmstart a DQN agent and use the advice policy to guide exploration. Because LLM advice is often suboptimal, a value warmstart method initializes the agent to recognize promising states from the advice policy's behavior rather than imitating it blindly.

entry.title: When Does Fine-Tuning Beat Prompting for Qiskit-to-CUDA-Q Translation? An Execution-Verified Study

author.name: Ana Paula Appel

entry.summary: This study benchmarks small open models on translating quantum code from Qiskit to NVIDIA CUDA-Q, verifying correctness by executing both programs and comparing state-vector fidelity rather than text matching or LLM judging. It builds a 640-task benchmark with held-out circuit families and coding styles, showing that measurement counts miss all phase-only errors and that rule-based baselines solve several splits.

entry.title: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems

author.name: Jiarui Guo, Jinkai Zhang, Yuanhong Yu, Yongchen Zai, Futang Zhu, Ruizhen Hu, Sida Peng, Xiaowei Zhou

entry.summary: SuperNav-1.5 is an agentic navigation system with a structured spatial memory consisting of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This representation avoids the context overhead of dense scene graphs and the non-executability of image-text records, guiding agents toward unvisited areas and providing executable routes across sessions and goals.

entry.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes

author.name: Xiaoqian Hu, Ruihong Qiu, Yanran Tang, Sen Wang

entry.summary: CARE-3D is a reinforcement post-training framework for embodied agents in 3D scenes that learns adaptively what to ground, which tools to invoke, and how to assess evidence utility, rather than imitating prescribed evidence-acquisition traces. Supervised fine-tuning establishes basic grounding, followed by RL that rewards the support evidence provides for correct answers. This improves over imitation-based agents that underexplore tools.

entry.title: Antiphony: A Dual-Process Agent for Deepfake Video Detection with Real-Video Calibration

author.name: Xinyu Yan, Yurong Hao, Zherui Li, Yebo Wu, Tiantong Wu, Jiaming Zhang, Zihao Zeng, Zheng Lin, Zijie Wang, Pengpeng Qiao, Yang Cao, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: Antiphony combines calibrated fusion of four visual experts with selective investigation for video deepfake detection, using authentic videos as a shared reference so thresholds can be recalibrated without target deepfakes. The framework establishes finite-sample false-alarm control and targets generalization to unseen generators while limiting false positives on real footage.

entry.title: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding

author.name: Kieren Yu, Qian Zhang, Ziyang Liu, Chang Huang, Jintai Chen, Kaishun Wu

entry.summary: EVD-Bench standardizes EEG-to-image decoding evaluation on THINGS-EEG2, controlling gallery and training budgets and explicitly comparing three participant-access regimes: within-subject, joint-subject, and leave-one-subject-out. The paper shows that participant-data access alone shifts results by more than most architectural differences, confounding prior comparisons.

entry.title: The Growth Path Is the Missing Half of Neural Networks

author.name: Tingan Jin, Haosong Li

entry.summary: The authors propose a dual-pathway neuron with a Growth Path alongside the standard Task Path: a fixed nutrient budget is allocated across layers in proportion to usage, causing well-fed units to divide and starving units to die during training. This built-in, always-on structural adaptation replaces explicit pruning or architecture search as a separate phase.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Vocabulary Expansion via Cross-Lingual Embedding Alignment

author.name: Andrew Ivan Soegeng, Muhammad Reza Qorib, Weishi Wang, Daniel Dahlmeier, Hwee Tou Ng

entry.summary: MATE is a parameter-efficient vocabulary expansion method that transfers learned representations by exploiting semantic equivalence between words in a model's primary language and new-language tokens, reducing added parameters by around 8x compared to standard expansion while mitigating the under-training of new tokens. This targets multilingual extension of LLMs via continual pretraining.

entry.title: Audio-Visual Rearrangement

author.name: Ruohao Guo, Jiatong Ye, Chenwei Dong, Jinxing Zhou, Dantong Niu, Guangyao Li, Zhenbo Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces Audio-Visual Rearrangement (AVR), a task where an embodied agent hears a spoken request, retrieves the right object, and delivers it to the requesting user by acoustically localizing them. The authors contribute a dataset spanning explicit, speaker-relative, and implicit query types, and a framework integrating motion-aware spatial audio into an audio-visual LLM.

entry.title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization

author.name: Luong Tran, Lan-Cuong Nguyen, Huynh Dang Nguyen, Dat Nguyen Cong, Dung D. Le, Van Nguyen

entry.summary: CLIP-FMoE integrates mixture-of-experts into CLIP fine-tuning using Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning on cluster-based data partitions to accelerate expert specialization, plus a Fusion Gate to limit catastrophic forgetting of pretrained knowledge. Experiments report improved scaling and maintained zero-shot capability relative to existing MoE adaptations of CLIP.

entry.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI

author.name: Alina Ermilova, Valeria Yakupova, Nikita Sushko, Andrey Lovyagin, George Ovchinnikov, Maksim G. Sharaev, Evgeny M. Mirkes, Denis Turdakov, Ivan Y. Tyukin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a trustworthiness framework estimating per-token trust of a generative model as the statistical typicality of each token relative to an expert model's distribution, using the expert as a distributional reference rather than a fact-checking oracle. An AI ontology calibrator built on the student model's own ontology supports calibration against external expert references.

entry.title: Video Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Bardia Safaei, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: This work extends generalized category discovery to videos, where temporal dynamics and larger intra-class variation degrade existing image-based GCD methods. VideoGCD combines a partitioned Mixture-of-Experts for known versus novel category specialization, a novel-class balancing loss, and a temporal optimal transport loss for consistent routing across frames.

entry.title: AutoClip-DPZO: Practical Private Clipping Selection for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xinghe Chen, Haichao Sha, Zihao Wang, Xiaokui Xiao, XiaoFeng Wang, Wei Dong

entry.summary: AutoClip-DPZO provides a practical differentially private procedure for selecting the clipping threshold in zeroth-order DP fine-tuning of LLMs, avoiding the repeated evaluations that existing methods use to tune this sensitive hyperparameter. The design accounts for privacy cost, utility, and efficiency constraints that defeat straightforward search strategies.

entry.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport

author.name: Johann Cl{\'e}ment-Cottuz (UNIROUEN, LITIS, LITIS - App), Gilles Gasso (INSA Rouen Normandie, LITIS, LITIS - App), Maxime Berar (UNIROUEN, LITIS, LITIS - App)

entry.summary: This paper introduces LRMOT, restricting multimarginal optimal transport plans to tensors of bounded multilinear rank, which yields compact coupling representations and efficient algorithms with low memory footprint. The authors establish approximation bounds and show substantial runtime reductions with low transport cost empirically.

entry.title: Target-Part Preference Optimization for Part-Aware 3D Generation

author.name: Zishan Qin and Rui Li and Zeyu Zhang and Sevvandi Kandanaarachchi and Lina Yao and Dong Gong

entry.summary: The paper adapts a pretrained part-aware 3D generator using DPO-based preference fine-tuning with limited part-annotated data, constructing preference pairs from seed-paired flow trajectories sharing one clean compositional latent but differing only in noise, ranked against ground-truth geometric metrics. A reference-relative target-block preference objective focuses training on the target part.

entry.title: Assembly-JEPA: Using World Models for Fine-Grained Industrial Image Verification

author.name: Michael Hollmer, Andreas Fischer

entry.summary: This work adapts JEPA-based world models to industrial assembly verification, formulating the task as predictive world modelling to detect fine-grained assembly errors without labeled defect data. Starting from a JEPA world model, the authors study required architectural adaptations for verifying assembly correctness across changing products and configurations. The self-supervised approach avoids reliance on CAD models or supervised pipelines.

entry.title: Irreducible shallow tanh neural networks are a manifold

author.name: Ivan Bioli, Isabella Carla Gonnella, Carlo Marcati, Federico Pichi

entry.summary: This mathematical paper proves that the set of functions represented by shallow tanh networks with fixed dimensions and n hidden neurons, restricted to irreducible networks in the sense of Sussmann, forms a smooth embedded submanifold of Sobolev spaces. The key step shows that W-l,p convergence to an irreducible network forces parameter convergence. This contributes to understanding the geometry of neural function spaces.

entry.title: DARE: Dual-Level Adversarial Learning with Domain-Aware Regularization for Whole Slide Image Classification

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Haichuan Dong, Manning Wang

entry.summary: Proposes DARE, an unsupervised domain adaptation method for pathological whole slide images that combats domain shifts from scanners, staining, and tissue preparation using dual-level adversarial learning with domain-aware regularization. It targets instability and negative transfer caused by WSI ultra-high resolution and heterogeneity.

entry.title: GeoMerge-OPD: Balanced Skill Integration in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Le Yang, Haoyang Lyu, Honglei Jin, Wenshuo Chen, Jiawei Liang, Wenqiang Wang, Yutao Yue, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: Analyzes why joint fine-tuning and parameter merging degrade individual skills in vision-language-action models, attributing failures to expert response energy concentrated in dominant directions of a shared task-relevant subspace. GeoMerge-OPD combines response-subspace analysis with orthogonal projection decomposition to merge heterogeneous manipulation and locomotion skills without unintended action shifts.

entry.title: Skill-Composer: Requirement-Driven Skill Selection from Multiple Marketplaces

author.name: Zicheng Chen, Jia Li, Xiaohong Chen, and Zhi Jin

entry.summary: Reframes agent skill acquisition from ranking individual skills to selecting a non-redundant set, proposing Skill-Composer, which selects skill bundles covering a task's complete requirements across multiple marketplaces. This addresses the problem that top-ranked skills are often functionally redundant while genuinely needed capabilities remain uncovered.

entry.title: Semantic-aware Decoding for Diverse Text-to-SQL under Schema Ambiguity

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Anna Mitsopoulou, Apostolos Koukouvinis, Yannis Velegrakis, Georgia Koutrika

entry.summary: The paper proposes Semantic-aware Logit Adjustment (SLA), a training-free decoding method that promotes diverse SQL interpretations under schema ambiguity by adjusting token logits based on semantic similarity between schema elements. SLA improves interpretation coverage over standard decoding without reasoning-heavy prompting or fine-tuning.

entry.title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?

author.name: Liu Yang, Huiyu Duan, Yixuan Gao, Sirui Liu, Lu Liu, Zhaolin Cai, Ke Gu, Xiongkuo Min, Xiaoping Zhang, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: OmniV-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs on omnidirectional (360-degree) video understanding, containing 4,123 ODVs and 8,923 human-annotated QA pairs spanning spatial and temporal comprehension. It exposes a largely unexplored capability gap in MLLMs for immersive spatio-temporal reasoning relevant to VR/AR and embodied applications.

entry.title: Optimal Regret Lower Bounds in Matrix Games

author.name: Taira Tsuchiya

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that for every deterministic learning dynamic in two-player zero-sum matrix games, there exists a payoff matrix forcing worst-case individual regret of Omega(sqrt(log m log n)). Combined with known optimistic-Hedge upper bounds, this establishes minimax optimality of deterministic dynamics in matrix games. A clean, matching lower-bound result in online learning and game theory.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization

author.name: Mohammad Hossein Moslemi, Mahdi Beitollahi, Zhimin Mei, Jiale Cai, Bissan Ghaddar, Boyu Wang

entry.summary: MIPA extends dataset distillation to self-supervised learning by treating synthetic images as learnable prototypes assigned to real samples via a frozen encoder, optimizing them to preserve augmentation-invariant information through mutual information maximization. This targets the unique requirement that SSL-distilled data must support representation learning consistent across augmentations.

entry.title: SIGMAE: A Spectral-Index-Guided Foundation Model for Multispectral Remote Sensing

author.name: Xiaokang Zhang, Bo Li, Chufeng Zhou, Weikang Yu, Lefei Zhang

entry.summary: SIGMAE improves masked autoencoder pretraining for multispectral remote sensing by using domain-specific spectral indices as priors to guide dynamic token masking toward informative regions. This injects semantic guidance where standard MAE masking struggles with complex backgrounds and indistinct targets.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for English-Swedish Medical Question Answering

author.name: Seyed Alireza Molavi, Zhan Su, Stefan Byttner, Yan Hu, Peyman Sheikholharam Mashhadi, Prayag Tiwari

entry.summary: The authors build an item-aligned English-Swedish medical QA benchmark from ten multiple-choice datasets, with a conservative translation-refinement loop grounded in a Swedish medical term base and blind judge voting. They show small open models suffer much larger accuracy drops in Swedish than large models, then demonstrate that translated English training data and open teacher models can narrow the gap. This is a useful multilingual medical AI resource for a lower-resource language.

entry.title: Intervene or Trust CLIP? Competence-Gated Adaptation for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Chenhao Zhu, Yu Huo, Haoran Shou, Shuguang Cui, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: The paper shows that token-level interventions during CLIP fine-tuning help only where frozen CLIP is incompetent on the target domain, and can hurt where it already performs well; a bias-variance analysis explains both cases. It proposes competence gating that predicts from the support set alone whether to intervene. The finding is a useful, general lesson: adaptation methods should be conditioned on model competence rather than applied uniformly.

entry.title: Urban State Representation for Autonomous Mobility: A Survey of Multimodal Perception, Architectures, Datasets, and Benchmarks

author.name: Binay Kumar Singh, Niels Da Vitoria Lobo

entry.summary: A survey formalizing Urban State Representation (USR), a georeferenced, layered, time-varying, uncertainty-aware state that multiple sensing platforms can write to and downstream tasks can read from. It relates USR to BEV features, occupancy, neural fields, 3D Gaussians, scene graphs, and world-model latents, and organizes sensing platforms, datasets, and benchmarks.

entry.title: Choose What Returns: Object-Aware KV Memory for Selective Recall in Interactive Video Generation

author.name: Hyunwook Kang, Junoh Park, Hyunggyu Lim, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Introduces an object-aware key-value memory framework for frozen autoregressive diffusion video generators, enabling precise selective recall of characters and settings across interactive multi-prompt sessions. It stores original KV for tracked object regions, selects background KV by attention scores, and uses an LLM to choose requested memory records.

entry.title: Duplicate- and Patient-Overlap Leakage in Brain MRI Tumor Classification: A Multi-Model Evaluation

author.name: Xin Li, Samson Oluwadare

entry.summary: Audits the widely used Cheng/Figshare brain MRI dataset for duplicate images and patient overlap across train-test splits, training four CNN architectures under image-level and patient-disjoint protocols across many runs and seeds. The study quantifies how patient overlap inflates discrimination metrics and distorts model rankings, highlighting a common evaluation pitfall in medical imaging.

entry.title: A Closed-Form Temporal Readout for Surgical Triplet Recognition

author.name: Lemar Abdi, Amaan Valiuddin, Fida Mohammad Thoker, Karen Sanchez, Bernard Ghanem, Fons van der Sommen

entry.summary: STRIDE is a post-hoc temporal readout for surgical triplet recognition that averages a trained recognizer's features and logits over fixed temporal windows and combines them with the current frame via closed-form ridge regression on CPU. Applied to nine existing methods, it improves AP in 24 of 27 method-dataset pairs by up to 7.4 points with minimal overhead.

entry.title: FoGConcept: Identifying Interpretable Movement Concepts for Freezing-of-Gait Detection from Multi-Scale IMU Signals

author.name: Chuntian Chi, John Clapham, GinaMari Blackwell, Leslie Cloud, Ingrid Pretzer-Aboff, Yanfu Zhang, Huajie Shao, Gang Zhou

entry.summary: FoGConcept discovers nine human-understandable movement concepts (e.g., gait initiation, trembling in place, pivot turns) encoded by a multi-scale IMU model for detecting freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease. The concepts recur across subjects and are functionally linked to model decisions, with emergent temporal specialization. This advances interpretable clinical wearables, where explainability is essential for clinical trust.

entry.title: Task-Agnostic Incremental Vision-Language Object Detection via Prompt Augmentation and Distribution-Aware Fusion

author.name: Yonghan Jiang, Zhengyuan Xie, Wenchu Liu, Linlan Huang, Fei Yang, Xialei Liu

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Task-Agnostic Incremental Vision-Language Object Detection (TA-IVLOD), a realistic continual-learning setting where task identities are unavailable at inference, and proposes TADA with stochastic prompt augmentation and distribution-aware fusion to counter cross-task semantic interference. Removing oracle task assumptions exposes severe degradation in prior methods. It advances practical open-vocabulary continual learning.

entry.title: Knowing What You Carry: Scalable Physics-Anchored World Models for Robotic Planning with Liquid Payloads

author.name: Yicheng Zhu, Linfeng Tian, Yang Chen, Tao Li, Zilin Bian

entry.summary: This robotics paper addresses planning for vehicles carrying unmeasured liquid payloads, where rigid-payload assumptions break down near safety limits. The authors build PL, a physics-anchored framework studying the trade-off between costly coupled fluid simulation and cheap but resonance-limited slosh models, evaluated on a ground vehicle with a partly filled tank near its rollover limit.

entry.title: Center-Aware Ordinal Learning for Prostate Cancer Grading from Histopathology Images

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Parvin Mousavi, Purang Abolmaesumi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a center-aware ordinal learning framework for prostate cancer grading in whole-slide images, combining a pretrained pathology encoder with attention-based MIL, an Earth Mover's Distance loss for ordinal errors, ordinal supervised contrastive alignment across centers, and curriculum learning to handle class imbalance. The goal is representations that transfer reliably across institutions despite staining and scanning variation.

entry.title: Optimal User-Level Private Stochastic Convex Optimization and Mean Estimation with Heavy Tails

author.name: Andrew Lowy

entry.summary: Studies stochastic convex optimization under (epsilon, delta) user-level differential privacy with heavy-tailed gradients, replacing bounded-Lipschitz assumptions with moment bounds. The paper characterizes minimax optimal excess risk up to log factors and achieves the optimal rate with only O(1/epsilon) users, plus tight user-level private mean estimation bounds. A strong theoretical result advancing the theory of user-level privacy.

entry.title: Information Access and Gain-Loss Framing in Six Large Language Models and Human Decision Makers

author.name: Aadithya Chandramouli, Jeremy M. Gernand (The Pennsylvania State University)

entry.summary: This study tests gain-loss framing effects across six LLMs (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3 235B, Llama 4 Maverick) over 11,519 risky choices with varied wording and information cards. All six models showed large framing effects without information access, with gaps of 27 to 79 percentage points, shrinking as more information cards were opened. The work has implications for LLM reliability in decision-support contexts.

entry.title: CLASP: Deciding Structure and Claims Before Decoding for Whole-Slide Pathology Report Generation

author.name: Ziaullah Khan, Rashadul Islam Sumon, Md Ariful Islam Mozumder, Duc-Son Pham, Moon-Il Joo, Hee-Cheol

entry.summary: Finds that on PathText-BRCA, report-level structural choices dominate n-gram metrics, with exemplar reports approaching SOTA, motivating CLASP, a decide-then-decode generator that explicitly fixes sentence plan, length, and claims per slide before decoding. Includes an Exemplar Structure Prior to inherit organization from image-similar cases.

entry.title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation

author.name: Di Lu, Xinran Zhang, Qingwen Zhou, Yan Gao, Yuan Zhang, Xiaoqing Wang, Yuming Sun, Xiaobing Li, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: PopMelodyGen combines rule-based synthesis of labeled synthetic pop melodies with neural generation, pretraining on an auditable synthetic corpus and adapting with a small licensed real-pop corpus to support controllable, copyright-aware melody generation. It addresses the scarcity of redistributable symbolic pop-melody data caused by copyright restrictions. This is notable for tackling data provenance, an increasingly important issue in generative music.

entry.title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills

author.name: Shuo Yan, Rui Sheng, Xiaoyan Gu, Lian Lian, Chengran Xu, Yifang Wang

entry.summary: SkillLens is an interactive human-LLM system for diagnosing and refining reusable LLM agent skills, linking performance changes, case transitions, skill diffs, invocation sequences, and outputs in a recoverable workflow with model explanations under human review. It is grounded in a formative study with five developers and evaluated via a between-subjects user study with 20 participants. It addresses the practical maintenance burden as agent skills become central to LLM agent ecosystems.

entry.title: JevNavAgent: A Single-Forward Visual Navigation Agent with Trajectory-Level RL for Gigapixel Pathology

author.name: Yonghuang Wu, Zhenyang Liang, Pengfei Wang, Yize Ma, Guoqing Wu, and Jinhua Yu

entry.summary: JevNavAgent navigates gigapixel whole-slide pathology images by predicting distributions over predefined decision spaces in a single forward pass, avoiding autoregressive latency that throttles online multi-trajectory RL. It uses trajectory-level RL to fix stopping asymmetries and shortcut behaviors that let multi-step VLM agents pass metastases without stopping, targeting clinical cancer detection.

entry.title: AgriManager: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-RL Generalization in Agricultural Management

author.name: Chi Gui, Junwen Zheng, Ritwik Nigam, Qianlan Yang, Meagan Lang, Vardhan Dongre, Jeremiah Barr, Yu-Xiong Wang, Vikram S. Adve

entry.summary: AgriManager is a framework that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators (DSSAT, WOFOST, Cycles), formalizing schema shift as variation in the policy-facing schema of observations, actions, and objectives between training and deployment. It tests LLM-RL generalization along two axes: distributional shift within a fixed interface and structural schema shift across interfaces. It appears to be the first RL framework for LLM policies spanning multiple agricultural simulators.

entry.title: CivilCADBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Understanding, Reconstructing, and Designing Civil Engineering Drawing Sets

author.name: Zelin Zheng, Difei Wu, Xinyan Liu, Minghong Chen, Antoni B. Chan, Difan Zou

entry.summary: CivilCADBench is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLMs on understanding, reconstructing, and designing civil engineering drawing sets, built from real infrastructure drawings and source CAD files with over 250,000 CAD entities. It stresses dense, layered, multi-sheet documents where printed output is a lossy projection that hides layer structure, covering three task families. The benchmark targets a high-value, labor-intensive professional workflow.

entry.title: Topological Neural Collapse

author.name: Nicholas Enbar-Salo and Jeova Farias Sales Rocha Neto

entry.summary: This paper extends neural collapse theory by examining the functional connectome (correlation graphs of hidden units) per class, summarized via persistent graph homology, finding new topological phenomena (TNC1, TNC2) that co-occur with geometric neural collapse late in training. Notably, some results contradict NC1-style invariance expectations.

entry.title: Global Stability and Loss Convergence in Matrix Factorization

author.name: Eric Gan

entry.summary: The paper proves that gradient descent on the matrix factorization objective with convex smooth output losses such as cross-entropy, under compactness modulo invariances, yields bounded parameters, summable squared gradients, and loss convergence from any finite initialization above a learning-rate threshold. The proof builds on a monotone parameter-imbalance quantity.

entry.title: LITMUS - Literature Informed Testbed for Mapping Usecases and Synthesizing Risk-Cards

author.name: Seshu Tirupathi, Elizabeth M. Daly, Radu Marinescu, Javier Carnerero Cano, Yannis Belkhiter

entry.summary: LITMUS introduces a structured pipeline that, given a deployment use-case, automatically produces a tailored dataset and accompanying risk card, coupling identified risks to the specific use-case rather than the model architecture alone. This shifts safety assessment toward context-aware hazard analysis grounded in literature. It addresses the gap between generic model risk cards and practical deployment needs.

entry.title: Certified Comparative Statics for Conservation-Law Equilibrium Layers, with an Application to RNA Interference

author.name: Shadi Khodagholi and Sara Karimi and Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: For equilibrium/implicit neural layers with order-preserving conservation-law coupling, the paper proves that every input-output comparative static is sign-certified if and only if the residual Jacobian is a nonsingular M-matrix, with the certified sign determined by the occupancy derivative. This covers Langmuir, Hill, and saturating-exponential occupancies under one guarantee, with a sharp phase boundary where certification fails. It is demonstrated on RNA interference applications.

entry.title: Pain Reassessment from Pulse Waveforms with Language Model Explanations

author.name: Cheng Ding, Jiaming Liu, and Daoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: This work evaluates pain reassessment from longitudinal photoplethysmography paired with evidence-linked language model explanations across 52,082 assessments from 21,514 patients in MIMIC-III and MC-MED, comparing 27 methods. Full-history models achieved average precision around 0.82 across care settings, and ablations show historical pulse representations carry individualized physiological signal beyond care-process timing.

entry.title: MVAgent: Per-Video Agents under Global Coordination for Multi-Video Understanding

author.name: Kewei Wei, XueXiang Wen, Bocheng Hu, Weili Xu, Haiyang Yu, Kaiyue Zhou, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: MVAgent is a training-free multi-video understanding agent that separates observation decisions from cross-video judgments: one LocalAgent per video plans observations and keeps a private history, while a GlobalAgent coordinates reasoning and combines reports. This avoids the context blowup of single-controller agents over multiple videos. An architecture pattern likely relevant beyond video to any multi-source evidence aggregation.

entry.title: loopxDINO: Dense Visual Prediction via Iterative Latent Reasoning

author.name: Xiangjing An, Zhibin Jiao and Aiting Chen

entry.summary: loopxDINO replaces deep stacked feedforward decoders for dense visual prediction with a compact weight-tied looped cross-attention decoder (about 8M core parameters) iterating over cached frozen DINOv2 features. This cuts activation memory, bandwidth, and static compute allocation while adapting computation to spatial complexity. Demonstrates that iterative latent reasoning can substitute for physical decoder depth.

entry.title: EMIP: Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform

author.name: Koichiro Terao and Rikunari Sagara and Moe Nagao and Naoto Iwahashi

entry.summary: EMIP is a Minecraft-based virtual platform connecting multiple humans and multiple AI agents in a shared environment with full-duplex speech and simultaneous physical interaction, exposed via Model Context Protocol interfaces for observation, action, and audio. It enables controlled experiments on human-agent cooperation in embodied settings. It fills a genuine infrastructure gap for multi-party embodied AI research.

entry.title: MusicListenBench: Can Audio LLMs Hear the Difference Yet?

author.name: Abhinaba Roy, Ambuj Mehrish, Dorien Herremans

entry.summary: MusicListenBench tests audio LLMs on basic perceptual discrimination of melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo using paired FLIP/STAY variants where ignoring the audio guarantees 50% accuracy. Results on rendered and real-recording test sets show most models fail these basic listening tests.

entry.title: BQDNA: Multi-Head Binary Spherical Quantization for Genomic Sequence Modeling

author.name: Xudong Wang, Siwei Cheng and Haozhe Hu

entry.summary: BQDNA introduces a context-aware BQVAE for learned scalar quantization of DNA and an autoregressive genomic language model with multi-head codebooks, replacing suboptimal k-mer/BPE tokenizers. The work reports unique quantization dynamics in DNA space, gains over hand-crafted tokenizers, and strong cross-species generalization.

entry.title: Learning Global Probabilistic Explanations

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Koriche and Louenas Bounia

entry.summary: Studies global probabilistic explanations for black-box classifiers: small feature subsets whose relevance is the expected probability that a random input and a random input agreeing on those features receive the same label. The authors formalize the problem of finding maximally relevant subsets under cardinality constraints for product distributions on discrete feature spaces and develop algorithms with guarantees. This moves XAI beyond purely local explanations toward distribution-aware global summaries.

entry.title: Seeing vs. Knowing: Counterfactual Supervision and Correction for 3D-Aware Object Editing

author.name: Jian Zahng and Zhijun Zhang

entry.summary: Addresses 3D-aware photo editing by constructing counterfactual photo-state conflicts (repainted hidden surfaces, re-rendered shadows, replaced textures) that teach an editor when to trust a reconstructed 3D asset versus the photograph. This supervision lets the model reveal unseen content from the 3D state while preserving visible appearance from the source image.

entry.title: SuperFine3D: Efficient Global-Local Recursive Refinement for Extremely Detailed 3D Geometry Generation

author.name: Lihan Li, Junwei Zhou, Yu-wing Tai

entry.summary: SuperFine3D generates extremely detailed 3D geometry from images via global-local recursive refinement, learning a shared refinement operator from coarse-to-fine pairs and recursively reusing it to synthesize geometry beyond training resolutions without additional paired supervision. Efficiency techniques make recursive refinement computationally feasible against image-guided generation constraints.

entry.title: Lightweight Spectral Subspace Filtering for Trojan-Resilient AI Inference Engines

author.name: Soumita Chatterjee, Sudip Ghosh, Tamal Ghosh, Bhargab B. Bhattacharya, and Hafizur Rahaman

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free Spectral Subspace Filtering framework that detects and suppresses multi-trigger backdoor activations in DNNs by using SVD to exploit geometric separation between benign and malicious latent feature distributions. It targets deployment on inference engines and hardware accelerators where retraining is impractical.

entry.title: DREAM: Dual-Memory Reasoning for Anticipatory 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Sriram Mandalika and Athira Nambiar

entry.summary: DREAM reframes LiDAR semantic segmentation for autonomous driving as an anticipatory, experience-driven process using two online memory banks: a latent memory of semantic abstractions and an error memory of past failure patterns. This aims to improve robustness to occlusions and dynamic scene changes compared with frame-centric segmentation.

entry.title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States

author.name: Yuhao Cai, Zhenzhang Li

entry.summary: This quantum information theory paper proves query-complexity bounds for estimating zero-temperature first-order transition points of 3D lattice Hamiltonians from adaptively prepared Gibbs or ground states. It establishes an exponential separation between two system-size caps at the same temperature, quantifying how the number of state copies needed depends on observed system size.

entry.title: Beyond Language Optimization: Enhancing Visual Representations for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Rui Zuo, Qinyue Tong, Ziqian Lu, Zheming Lu

entry.summary: The paper observes that GRPO-based training improves clinical accuracy of chest X-ray report generation without meaningfully improving visual representations of abnormalities, and proposes selective regional visual distillation from a region-aware teacher. The method transfers only verified-useful teacher features for challenging anatomical regions while preserving existing capabilities.

entry.title: Notes on Generative AI for Mathematical Research

author.name: Shurui Liu

entry.summary: These notes survey how generative AI is currently used to solve and verify research-level mathematics, focusing on the proving agents Rethlas, Danus, and Pharos and the verification agent OSVerify, including design principles, base-model comparisons, and case studies. It also reviews the history of AI for mathematics and community reactions.

entry.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay

author.name: Josue Casco-Rodriguez, Nanda H. Krishna, Richard G. Baraniuk

entry.summary: This work reinterprets spontaneous replay in noisy recurrent neural networks as time-indexed Langevin sampling from a time-series distribution of lived experience rather than Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution. A normative second-order framework using spike-frequency adaptation accounts for both environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in biological replay.

entry.title: Benchmarking VLM Medical Hallucination across 5 Modalities

author.name: Zhixing Cao, Yusen Peng

entry.summary: The authors introduce Multi-Med, a 1,000-pair medical hallucination benchmark for vision-language models spanning five imaging modalities and four question categories. They evaluate 10 widely used VLMs and find performance varies substantially by modality and question type, with differences among top models not statistically significant. The benchmark helps localize where medical VLMs hallucinate.

entry.title: Tracing Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming

author.name: Chris Tava

entry.summary: This study examines where and why RL-based automated red teaming loses attack diversity, testing six mechanisms (defender adaptation, success edge, reward reinforcement, row cap, update size, measurement) across three experimental arms over 24 iterations. It finds frozen defenders cause earlier diversity collapse and that successful attacks are systematically narrower than the generated attack distribution. Findings inform how to sustain diverse adversarial testing of LLMs.

entry.title: STUN-Bench: Truly Unseen Tools for Evaluating Shared Tool Experience

author.name: Abhijit Chakraborty, Ni Trieu, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: STUN-Bench is a corrected split of StableToolBench whose shared-experience pool contains no items naming 172 held-out tools, exposing that prior unseen-tool evaluations leaked test queries and gold tools into retriever and experience data. On this clean split the authors find a crowding effect: pooled experience across simulated clients degrades rather than helps routing.

entry.title: SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments

author.name: Jenna Kang, Bingxuan Li, Colin Groth, Anatolii Evdokimov, Sai Zhang, Qi Sun

entry.summary: SWAM separates agent-state evolution from autoregressive visual generation in interactive 3D world models, using a lightweight state model to propagate character dynamics from actions without consuming generated frames. This addresses the key problem that NPCs outside the camera view have untracked states, avoiding reliance on external maps or predefined transitions used in prior multi-agent world models.

entry.title: Policy-intrinsic Demonstration Curation

author.name: Sunjae Jeong, Geunhyeok Yu, Dowoon Lee, and Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: For cross-task robot demonstration reuse, the authors propose a policy-intrinsic curation branch that estimates each candidate demonstration's effect on the policy using only forward passes of the pretrained policy, requiring no additional training. This sits between similarity-only retrieval (fast but policy-blind) and performance-aware curation (policy-aware but slow).

entry.title: iFeST: An Iterative Motion Correction Framework for Fetal Brain Diffusion MRI via Frequency-Spatial-Temporal Modeling

author.name: Haoan Xu, Ruike Chen, Jing Xia, Haotian Li, Huanyun Zhang, Cong Sun, Guangbin Wang, Shuhao Zhang, Zhigang Gao, Dan Wu

entry.summary: iFeST is an iterative motion-correction framework for fetal brain diffusion MRI that jointly models frequency (k-space), spatial, and temporal (inter-slice) information across diffusion directions, unlike prior methods that correct each volume independently and handle only inter-slice motion. This targets a clinically important bottleneck since fetal motion severely corrupts dMRI acquisitions.

entry.title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading

author.name: Tianle Zeng, Hanjing Ye, Bingyi Xia, Yuchen Zhou, Zibo Zhang, Yufei Huang, Yonggen Ling, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: LeadVLA is a multimodal vision-language-action policy for robot leading that keeps the route as an explicit path reference while separately learning pace control and residual follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation. The authors also build LeadInfra, an Unreal Engine-based closed-loop data generation pipeline producing roughly 4 million samples for training and evaluation.

entry.title: EditGRN: Inversion-Free Image Editing by Source-Target Generative Synchronization

author.name: Jiahuan Wang, Jianan Chen, Jian Han, Rui Li, Guangming Lu, Wenjie Pei

entry.summary: EditGRN is a training- and inversion-free text-guided image editing framework for discrete generative models, using a dual-branch design where a source branch constructs references and a target branch generates the edited image with trajectory-wide synchronization between them. This replaces post-hoc probability correction and better balances source preservation with coherent target semantics.

entry.title: Skill-Adaptive Noise Scheduling for Diffusion Policies

author.name: Woo Kyung Kim, Gwangpyo Yoo, Eunyoung Park, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: SaND makes the noise schedule in diffusion policies a learnable, skill-conditioned component rather than a fixed uniform schedule, modulating diffusion across skills with distinct action-dimension couplings. This targets contact-rich, dexterous manipulation where fixed schedules limit performance in hierarchical skill-based frameworks.

entry.title: Face Is Not All You Need: MIME Benchmark for Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Yuxin Jia, Xing Lan, Wensong Wang, Jian Xue, Feiliang Ren, Ke Lu

entry.summary: The paper formally defines Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition (IMER) and releases the MIME benchmark, which evaluates emotion recognition robustness under fine-grained, unpredictable modality degradation rather than coarse full-modality removal. It shows existing models that anchor inference on facial cues suffer catastrophic collapse and adds interpretable analysis of emotional reasoning.

entry.title: SceneCast: Learning Indoor Scene Synthesis from Curated Synthetic Videos with LLM Reward

author.name: Ziyang Zong, Canming Xia, Haoran Xu, Guang Tan

entry.summary: SceneCast trains 3D indoor scene synthesis annotation-free on large-scale unlabeled videos, using a Transformer model that predicts objects sequentially and is fine-tuned with RL where an LLM acts as a spatial common-sense reward evaluator. It addresses partial-view extrapolation and uncurated video quality challenges.

entry.title: IP-GNO: An Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator for Automated Distribution System State Estimation

author.name: Sakshi Kumar, Chhavi Jhari, Ajay Singh, Subho Paul

entry.summary: IP-GNO frames distribution system state estimation as an operator-learning problem inspired by Neumann series expansion of the inverse bus admittance matrix, enabling physics-informed graph neural operators that generalize zero-shot to unseen grid sizes and topologies. It targets scalable, transferable DSSE for modern distribution grids with volatile power injection.

entry.title: TAP: Policy Interfaces for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Preeti and Ankita Kushwaha and Kiran Ravish and Pawan Kumar

entry.summary: TAP-DiLM adds a typed policy variable to masked diffusion language models enabling selective generation decisions such as answering, clarifying, waiting, or refusing, and systematically compares how the policy attaches to the denoising process across BERT-base, MDLMOWT, LLaDA-8B, and Dream-7B. It finds dedicated heads are robust across scales while shared-vocabulary heads depend on LM-head geometry, and offers an LM-head sharpness probe as a diagnostic.

entry.title: Struct2Det: Grounding Category Structure in Visual Evidence for Few-Shot Object Detection

author.name: Kaixuan Chang, Huabing Zhou, Yanduo Zhang, Tao Lu, Liwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, and Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Struct2Det improves few-shot object detection for visually similar categories by encoding category graphs into component embeddings and using component queries to retrieve multi-scale image evidence that modulates category text embeddings, followed by verification-guided refinement matching candidate regions against expected components. This grounds category structure in concrete visual evidence.

entry.title: VeriOrigin: A Proactive Image Protection Framework for Provenance, Tamper Localization, and Lossless Recovery

author.name: Jiale Chen, Wei William Wang, Junnan Yin, Chongyang Shi, Li Dong, Yuanman Li, and Xiping Hu

entry.summary: VeriOrigin unifies image provenance verification, precise tamper localization under distortions, and lossless recovery of the original image in a single framework. Its XOnet component is a CNN-based invertible encoder achieving reversibility through cross residual prediction between two subnetworks, replacing conventional flow-based architectures. Training uses a two-stage strategy.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times

author.name: Dennis Bogatov Wilkman, Karl Henrik Johansson, Matthieu Barreau

entry.summary: Reconstructs vehicle trajectories and learns microscopic traffic dynamics from sparse entry/exit timestamps using Neural ODEs combined with local density approximation. A normalization over a monotone network with learned regime changes enforces physical realism, preventing artifacts like negative speeds or nonzero flow under full congestion.

entry.title: Motion on Demand: Adaptive Optical Excitation for Event Cameras

author.name: Yingtao Li, Chaoran Feng, Haoran Jiang, Zhenyu Tang, Wangbo Yu, Zhankuo Xu, Jianbin Zhao, Li Yuan, Yonghong Tian

entry.summary: Presents EvGaze, an event camera system with a rotating wedge prism whose speed is adaptively regulated by a learned multimodal controller, inspired by fly gaze-control haltere/visual feedback division of labor. This generates controlled image motion to reveal static or slow edges only when natural motion is insufficient, avoiding redundant events and alignment errors from fixed-speed excitation.

entry.title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs

author.name: Vijayasri Iyer, Cristiano De Nobili, Mubashir Hussain Shah, S\'ebastien Brati\`eres

entry.summary: Trallie is an open-source framework for LLM-based information extraction that converts unstructured documents (HTML, PDF, TXT, JSON) into structured data with zero- or few-shot prompting and no extensive labeled datasets. It can automatically induce extraction schemas from document collections, lowering the barrier for non-expert users.

entry.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots

author.name: Rui Dai, Shunpeng Yang, Zhen Fu, Maolin Lei, Jiaqi Song, Hua Chen, Nikos Tsagarakis

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework that adapts a learned dynamics model to deployed target conditions instead of relying on static domain randomization, using a concurrent teacher-student paradigm for both policy and dynamics model within an on-policy RL pipeline. Experiments on bipedal locomotion demonstrate improved robustness to unmodeled dynamics such as payload and friction changes.

entry.title: NeuroMotion: Aligning EEG to Discrete Motion Primitives for Continuous Motion Decoding

author.name: Yi Liu, Qi Zhang, HaoLin Li, Lai Zhong Yuan, Lei Zhu, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: NeuroMotion aligns noisy EEG representations to discrete motion primitives via a VQ-based motion prior, contrastive alignment objectives, and an E2M Transformer that predicts motion-code sequences, enabling continuous motion decoding. It works across heterogeneous paradigms including full-body free movement, treadmill locomotion, and upper-limb reaching and grasping.

entry.title: Fast and Consistent Structure Learning in Graphical Models via Approximate Cross-Validation

author.name: Zhao Lyu, Mladen Kolar, Bryon Aragam

entry.summary: The authors develop a scalable graph-recovery procedure based on approximate cross-validation, resolving the tension that CV is computationally infeasible and theoretically inconsistent for structure learning while BIC-type criteria require model-specific calibration. They provide consistency guarantees and demonstrate effectiveness on large graphical models.

entry.title: How Do Deep Networks Encode and Selectively Use Information? Shared Encoding and Conditional Signed Readout in Vision and Language Models

author.name: Kaixiang Shu

entry.summary: Through controlled edits in vision classifiers and frozen language models, the paper shows network representations preserve recognizable structure across disjoint blocks of hidden units while selectively reading them out for decisions. It decomposes local output changes into signed channel and pathway contributions, offering a mechanistic account of shared encoding and conditional readout across modalities.

entry.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware

author.name: William Fleshman

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that provably secure linguistic steganography schemes break in practice when the receiver's floating-point precision, quantization, GPU architecture, or even batching differs from the sender's, since they assume bit-exact recomputation of token probabilities. STEALTH introduces an exponential-race token sampling scheme that remains robust to these hardware-level discrepancies.

entry.title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning

author.name: Andreas Hermansen, Tobias Golling, Slava Voloshynovskiy

entry.summary: The paper unifies self-supervised learning and physical inductive biases for jet tagging by combining a Lorentz-equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformer with the LeJEPA framework, pre-training on 100 million jets from JetClass. It shows enforcing Lorentz symmetry in the latent space, whether architectural or learned via kinematic augmentations, is critical for representation quality, and a non-invariant backbone with LeJEPA outperforms established baselines.

entry.title: NoveltyGate: Novelty, Not Error, Decides Which VLA Prefix Tokens to Compute Exactly

author.name: Lemeng Qi

entry.summary: This paper studies compute-efficient flow-matching vision-language-action models and shows that selecting which prefix tokens need exact computation based on approximation error is the wrong criterion: an oracle error verifier performs worse than a simple novelty test checking whether a token input lies outside the calibration subspace. The novelty-based gate yields 1.3-1.7x lower action deviation.

entry.title: Data-Driven Identification of Uncertainty Sets with Conformance Guarantees

author.name: Laura L\"utzow, Mykel J. Kochenderfer, and Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: ConfID is a unified framework that establishes reachset, trace, and simulation conformance between a possibly nonlinear nominal model and measured traces by identifying uncertainty sets, treating unmodeled effects as nondeterminism. For all three conformance relations the identification reduces to a linear program minimizing set size. This enables formal verification and controller synthesis guarantees grounded in data.

entry.title: EEG Decoding in Context: A Framework for Tuning-Free EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Hao-Run Cai, Si-Yang Liu, Han-Jia Ye, Hairong Zheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes an in-context learning paradigm for EEG foundation models in which labeled recordings define the decoding task as context and new recordings are decoded without parameter updates, eliminating task-specific decoders and gradient adaptation. Direct pairing of raw EEG features with a pretrained general-purpose in-context predictor is a promising but limited starting point that the framework then improves. Relevant to brain-computer interfaces and cross-domain transfer of in-context learning.

entry.title: Matching Under Metric Privacy

author.name: Hongyi B. Hu, Dung Nguyen, M. Amin Rahimian

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies how to randomize private points in d-dimensional Euclidean space so accurate bipartite matchings can be computed, establishing the tight rate Theta(n min(d, log n)/eps) for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. It analyzes Gumbel matching under a trusted server and constructs compact representations preserving matching costs using the affine span of public points.

entry.title: Comparing AI R&D compute caps and deployment lags

author.name: elifland
