entry.summary: Written in response to Evan Hubinger's shortform on deployment blocking as a pacing mechanism, this post compares two classes of AI governance policies: caps on the fraction of compute used for capabilities R&D and deployment lags or freezes that restrict which model generations can be used for AI R&D. The author concludes compute caps are similarly good or slightly better than lags, and that combining both is likely optimal.

entry.title: Vision-Language Truck Driving Advisories Grounded in Provincial Rules and Forecast Risks

author.name: Xintong Jiang, Shucheng Huang, Qiaoxuan Zhang, Jincheng Xu, Yukun Lu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a data generation and distillation framework combining structured scene understanding, risk forecasting, and traffic-rule retrieval to produce truck driving advisories consistent with jurisdiction-specific regulations. An 8B teacher generates records with consistency checks, distilled into a 3B student model for onboard deployment, accompanied by a new dashcam dataset. It addresses the practically important problem of long-haul trucking across jurisdictions with varying traffic rules.

entry.title: SceneTether: Activity-Gated Value Anchoring for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Image Animation

author.name: Matiur Rahman Minar, Seunghun Oh, Ganghyeon Jeong, Unsang Park

entry.summary: SceneTether is a training-free attention-read policy for autoregressive video generation that anchors low-activity scene regions back to source-image values while leaving high-activity regions free to move, preventing accumulated appearance drift over long horizons. An activity map estimated from the first generated latents and frozen thereafter gates the blending.

entry.title: LoKiTO: Local Kinodynamic Trajectory Optimization for UAVs based on Memory-Efficient Neural Distance Fields

author.name: Guillermo Gil-Garcia, J. A. Cobano, L. Merino, F. Caballero

entry.summary: LoKiTO is a 3D local kinodynamic trajectory optimizer for aerial robots combining Chebyshev polynomial parameterization with an online neural Euclidean Signed Distance Field updated from LiDAR, reducing map memory to about 1.0 MB while embedding dynamic constraints in a modular cost function. It benchmarks favorably against state-of-the-art planners in highly cluttered simulated environments.

entry.title: Accelerating wave-scattering simulations with learned search directions

author.name: Haoran Sun, Tao Shan, Hongyu Zhou, Rui Guo, Shenheng Xu, Fan Yang and Maokun Li

entry.summary: Presents BEMFormer, a learned solver that generates Krylov search directions for boundary-element wave-scattering systems, with coarse-grid correction for geometry-specific directions. It generalizes to unseen geometries, meshes, and excitations, and solves a 1.04M-unknown quadcopter problem 30 times faster than a preconditioned Krylov solver at comparable radar cross-section accuracy. Strong scientific computing result combining learning with classical numerical methods.

entry.title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage

author.name: Qiuyu Ren and Sudipta Paria and Aritra Dasgupta and Swarup Bhunia

entry.summary: BitShare is a codebook-free weight format that varies precision within quantization groups by binning channels by sensitivity and letting less-sensitive weights share their lower bits, with a sharing-aware GPTQ variant choosing stored values without fine-tuning. This targets memory-bandwidth-bound small-batch LLM decoding.

entry.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication

author.name: Soumyabrata Chaudhuri and Joydeep Ghosh

entry.summary: The authors formalize decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning where N agents with partial visibility exchange budget-constrained natural language messages, and introduce a benchmark isolating queries requiring non-trivial multi-view integration. It extends language-mediated spatial coordination beyond prior two-agent settings.

entry.title: Denoised but Not Improved: What EEG Denoising Does to a Downstream Task

author.name: Xianglong Bao, Zhe Wang, Kewen Wang, Ming Jin

entry.summary: This audit paper shows that five standard EEG denoising methods, scored by fidelity to synthesized clean references, provide no downstream benefit when inserted into a fixed seizure-detection pipeline. It argues the standard denoising evaluation objective is unvalidatable since the clean reference is synthetic and even perfect separation returns volume-conduction-blurred cortical activity.

entry.title: RSLaA: Self-Reconfiguring Roadside LiDARs as Agents for 3D Traffic Perception

author.name: Yang Ma, Yichen Sun, Yubing Zheng, Zhongxiang Feng, Zeyang Cheng, Said M. Easa

entry.summary: RSLaA treats roadside LiDAR units as agents that adaptively adjust their poses to evolving traffic scenes over decision-time windows, replacing the standard fixed-placement paradigm. Since ground truth is unavailable at decision time, the framework centers on surrogate metrics computed from probabilistic occupancy representations.

entry.title: HKD-ACPA: Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks in Power Grids

author.name: Junhao Ren, Honglin Gao, Shuo Feng, Kun Cao, Qiyu Kang, Xiaofeng Zong, Shuping He, Gaoxi Xiao

entry.summary: HKD-ACPA studies zero-query adversarial attacks on power-grid attack-localization systems, coordinating physical, DoS, and false-data-injection attacks using only local measurements and historical detector outputs, via heterogeneous knowledge distillation into a graph surrogate ensemble with residual calibration. It highlights a practical threat model that avoids white-box access or online queries.

entry.title: MOVER: Planning Beyond Motion

author.name: Xiangyu Li, Yu Jiang, Tianyi Wang, Liang He, Qixing Huang, Zhaomiao Guo

entry.summary: MOVER addresses a blind spot of residual world models in autonomous driving — temporally static but safety-critical elements like waiting pedestrians that vanish from residual features — via a complementary event-routing mechanism. A training-time teacher measures each event query's sensitivity to removing past frames and the student learns to predict routing priorities without inference-time cost.

entry.title: What Do Co-Folding Models Learn? Insights from Enhanced Transition Path Sampling

author.name: Muhammad R. Hasyim

entry.summary: This paper applies Markov chain Monte Carlo transition path sampling over denoising trajectories of diffusion-based biomolecular co-folding models to examine whether their learned conformational ensembles are physically meaningful. Applied to Boltz-2, enhanced sampling recovers full conformational ensembles showing physically plausible conformational changes biased toward crystal-like states.

entry.title: Beyond Which: Where, How, and When in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yunhe Zhang, Long Gao, Yuedong Fu, Gang He, Li Xu, Chang Wu, Songyuheng Gao

entry.summary: W3H-VLA augments VLA models beyond identifying which entities matter, incorporating where entities are located, how geometry constrains interaction, and when spatial/geometric cues should dominate action prediction. It retains VLM-based semantics while adding structured spatial and geometric reasoning for manipulation.

entry.title: Toward a Theoretical Understanding of Transformer Attention: Bayesian Estimation and Predictive Sufficiency

author.name: Fouad B. Chedid

entry.summary: This paper organizes probabilistic and information-theoretic results to characterize when Transformer attention computes a posterior mean and what additional conditions yield accurate next-token prediction. An excess-log-loss decomposition separates representation information loss from prediction-head error, clarifying when predictive guarantees actually hold.

entry.title: DMC-5: Dual-Model Collaboration with Cache-aware Context Compression for Long-horizon Agents

author.name: Haochen Li, Xiaobing Tu, Yinggui Wang, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang

entry.summary: DMC-5 is an asymmetric dual-model framework for long-horizon agents that combines prefix caching with cache-aware context compression, assigning compression roles between a general-purpose model and a specialized agent model to avoid the pitfalls of selective-context loss, summary drift, and repeated full-history recompression. It targets the growing cost of ever-lengthening agent trajectories.

entry.title: Optimising VLM Harnesses to Localise Errors in Generated Videos

author.name: Ankit Yadav, Nikhil Cherian Kurian, Arpit Garg, Lingqiao Liu

entry.summary: Studies how the choice of harness (which frames to inspect, which tools and model calls to make) strongly affects vision-language models' ability to localize errors in generated videos. Proposes Harness Search and Merge, an algorithm in which an LLM orchestrator automatically constructs and merges harnesses by searching over executable evaluation programs refined on random training subsets.

entry.title: Ask Again: Answer-List Instability in Generative Engines

author.name: Bj\"orn Busch-Geertsema, David Antony Selby, Sebastian Vollmer

entry.summary: Analyzing 60,000 responses from generative search engines, the paper shows answer lists are highly unstable: the first named item changes 32% of the time for the same prompt, and close leaders are identified only 60% of the time even after 25 runs. Variability between engines exceeds within-engine variability, with implications for brand and source monitoring measurement budgets.

entry.title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling

author.name: Abhishek Sharma and Aleksej Zelezniak

entry.summary: BiPert is a simple linear framework decomposing transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components, handling both forward perturbation prediction in unseen cell types and inverse identification of perturbed genes from expression effects. It outperforms existing methods that use no external biological knowledge despite its simplicity.

entry.title: Convex Clustering Redefined: Robust Learning with the Median of Means Estimator

author.name: Sourav De, Koustav Chowdhury, Bibhabasu Mandal, Sagar Ghosh, Swagatam Das, Debolina Paul, and Saptarshi Chakraborty

entry.summary: This work improves convex clustering, which offers unique global optima but struggles with high-dimensional noisy data, by incorporating the median of means estimator for robustness to outliers. The approach addresses tuning-parameter sensitivity and improves cluster formation in challenging data regimes.

entry.title: Towards Objective Estimation of Physical Functioning Status in Breast-Cancer Patients using Real-World Data

author.name: Alexandros Papadopoulos, Ioannis Sarafis, Vasileios Papapanagiotou, Marius Stensland, Kristin Jonsdottir, Ingrid Holsvik Dahl, Marie Austdal, Tone Hoel Lende, Kjersti Tjensvoll, Anastasios Delopoulos

entry.summary: The paper introduces a method to objectively estimate physical functioning status of breast cancer patients from consumer smartwatch data, replacing difficult continuous clinical monitoring. Features derived from wearable data predict functioning levels, enabling targeted personalized interventions to improve quality of life.

entry.title: Measuring Human-AI and AI-AI Teams in Multi-turn Layout Creation

author.name: Rajvir Singh Naginder Singh Virdi and Yewen Pu

entry.summary: This exploratory study (n=6) compares human-AI and AI-AI teams on iterative multi-turn layout creation tasks, where a speaker issues natural-language instructions to a fixed listener LLM. Instead of LLM-as-judge, the authors fit a scoring function over geometric layout features from curated human judgments. It offers an early, human-grounded methodology for benchmarking multi-turn instruction following, though the sample size limits generalizability.

entry.title: Following the Error Through a Compressed Network:An Angular Measure for FFN Weight Compression in ViT-L/16

author.name: Paolo D'Alberto

entry.summary: This study compresses the 48 FFN matrices of ViT-L/16 to 2-8 bits using four quantization schemes, including a random-sign Hadamard rotation with a fixed Lloyd-Max table, and evaluates on 50,000 images. It proposes an angular error measure between compressed and float32 residual streams tracked across blocks as a portable diagnostic that predicts final accuracy rankings and localizes where compression error accumulates. The rotation-based scheme shows error growth near the square root of block count.

entry.title: Every IVUS Frame in Its Place: A Zero-Install Browser Tool for Registering Intravascular Ultrasound to the Coronary Angiogram, and a Path to Angiography-Only Plaque Imaging

author.name: Prahlad G. Menon, Srilakshmi Adhyapak

entry.summary: This paper presents a browser-based, zero-install tool for semi-automatic co-registration of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) pullback frames to coronary angiograms, using automatic contrast and cardiac-phase analysis plus Frangi vesselness and minimal-path centerline tracing. Because commercial registration requires vendor consoles at acquisition time, the tool enables registration of archived data, helping address the scarcity of paired training data for AI plaque imaging. A longer-term goal is angiography-only plaque imaging.

entry.title: Auditing two-stage MS/MS molecular retrieval on MassSpecGym v1.5: Reranking gains, candidate priors and spectrum dependence

author.name: Jiaqi Xue, Yutong Wu, Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper audits a two-stage molecular structure retrieval pipeline from tandem mass spectra on the official MassSpecGym v1.5 split, using a DreaMS encoder shortlist plus a support-gated reranker to reach 31.05% Recall@1. Critically, ablations show results are partly driven by candidate priors, precursor mass, and training coverage rather than genuine spectral understanding. Such critical audits are valuable for interpreting benchmark progress in computational chemistry.

entry.title: Cyclic Discrete Diffusion: A Novel Multi-Class Segmentation Refinement Technique

author.name: Libo Chen, Souvik Ghosh, Vinay P. Namboodiri

entry.summary: CDD casts segmentation mask refinement as a discrete diffusion process with a cyclic label topology, where pixels jump to the next label or stay put under a finite-state Markov process with analytically tractable reverse dynamics. It refines all classes jointly in one pass without per-class machinery. A technically clean discrete-diffusion formulation applied to a classic vision task.

entry.title: RALC: Risk-Controlled Local Adoption of Segmentation Updates with Few Calibration Images

author.name: Shize Yin

entry.summary: RALC provides distribution-free risk control for selectively adopting label changes from a fine-tuned road-scene segmentation model, so improvements in rain and night conditions do not degrade daytime performance. It forms nested candidate sets from confidence differences and uses a small calibration set with a per-replacement error bound to certify net error increase without test labels.

entry.title: Beyond Fidelity: Evaluating Synthetic Medical Imaging Data

author.name: Seyed Kahaki, Alexander R. Webber, Tahsin Rahman, Elim Thompson, Jana Delfino, Aldo Badano

entry.summary: Presents the ScoreCard Toolkit, a modular pipeline operationalizing six dimensions of the 7Cs framework (Congruence, Coverage, Completeness, Consistency, Constraint, Comprehension) for evaluating synthetic medical imaging datasets beyond fidelity metrics. It addresses clinically relevant properties like anatomical plausibility, subgroup consistency, and documentation quality.

entry.title: Selective Verification in Multi-Agent Orchestration with Large Language Models

author.name: Ramesh Krishnamaneni, Muralidhar Kurni

entry.summary: The authors model multi-agent LLM orchestration as nine binary votes to determine when a verifier should intervene, addressing the problem that agents can agree because they share the same flawed evidence. They show the optimal verification policy (checking close votes vs. random vs. error-reduction-ranked checks) depends on the failure regime, with orderings reversing between 80 and 90 percent worker error under shared failure.

entry.title: Learning a Rule Bank to Revise 3D CT Reports with Independent Evidence

author.name: Renjie Liang, Mengxian Lyu, Zijian Xu, Boxin Zhao, Yang Yang, Jinqian Pan, Zhengkang Fan, Mei Liu, Yonghui Wu, Jie Xu

entry.summary: This work proposes an agent system that learns an executable revision-policy rule bank for radiology report models, refining rules from revision outcomes across development cases. At inference, rules guide local edits using independent classifier predictions and quantitative image measurements without retraining the report model, preserving unedited sentences and linking each change to its triggering rule. This improves accountability in clinical report generation.

entry.title: MRI-Driven Dual-Energy CT Synthesis via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for MRI-only Radiotherapy and Protontherapy

author.name: Juan Manuel Molina-Maza Chih-Wei Chang, David Viar-Hernandez, Zach Eidex, Mojtaba Safari, Shaoyan Pan, Juan Maria Perez-Moreno, Norberto Malpica, Angel Torrado-Carvajal, Borja Rodriguez-Vila, Xiaofeng Yang

entry.summary: The authors develop a multi-decoder denoising diffusion model that synthesizes high- and low-energy CT images simultaneously from a single MRI scan for radiotherapy and proton therapy planning, avoiding extra radiation from DECT. Compared against Pix2PixGAN and CycleGAN on paired head-and-neck patient data, the DDPM improves HU accuracy and stopping-power-ratio estimation. This has direct clinical translation potential for MRI-only treatment planning.

entry.title: Selection Policies for Equal-Byte Mixed-Precision Quantization of Small Language Models

author.name: Smit Anand

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether non-uniform bit allocation (2, 4, or 8 bits per matrix) can improve small language models at a fixed byte budget compared to uniform 4-bit quantization. Using a genetic algorithm framework, the author compares two parent-selection rules (binary tournament versus an Alternis-inspired rule) plus a random-allocation baseline on Qwen-family small models, finding tournament selection consistently reduces held-out next-token negative log-likelihood across all seeds on AG News and IMDb.

entry.title: Which Loans, Not How Many: Exactly Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Monitoring of Deployed Risk Models

author.name: Xin Xu

entry.summary: This paper develops statistically exact, anytime-valid monitoring methods for deployed risk models, conditioning on counts to achieve level invariance in mortgage prepayment modeling. It introduces fixed-start slope product tests and restarted level sums with confidence sequences, validated on Freddie Mac data reproducing most maintained-model AUC variance. It addresses rigorous post-deployment monitoring of ML models in finance.

entry.title: Beyond Gaussian Calibration: Local Inference in Decentralized SGD

author.name: Xiaoli Li, Qianqian Lei, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that a client's constant-step endpoint in decentralized SGD can have near-nominal Gaussian coverage while both tails are badly miscalibrated, using an exact noise-filter representation to explain when local error deviates from Gaussianity. It identifies a computable graph-and-stepsize criterion and shows that on networks with summable return probabilities (e.g., high-dimensional tori, expanders), nearby clients' noise retains a fixed share of local variance.

entry.title: Belief-Driven Quantum Magnetometer Control for GPS-Denied Navigation

author.name: Murtuza Lemonwala, Laxima Niure Kandel

entry.summary: The paper closes the loop in magnetic anomaly navigation by using the navigator's position belief, projected through an anomaly map, to set the Ramsey phase and interrogation time of a quantum magnetometer each epoch via a closed-form rule balancing ambiguity and decoherence limits. This improves weak, low-SWaP sensors suitable for small drones navigating without satellite positioning.

entry.title: Guidance-Induced Activation of Score Estimation Errors in Diffusion Models

author.name: Pengyu Luo, Yisha Yao, Bolun Li

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of how classifier-free guidance activates score estimation errors in diffusion models: while the solenoidal component of each score error has no instantaneous effect on its own reference density, combining conditional and unconditional estimates can affect the guided marginals. Using a weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition, the authors identify and quantify this guidance-induced error field and characterize when it vanishes. Offers a rigorous explanation for why CFG amplifies certain generation artifacts.

entry.title: ESM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Whether AI Agents Understand Earth System Model Physics and Code

author.name: Koutian Wu, Yuxuan Cao, Gengchen Mai, Zeping Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ESM-Bench, a benchmark of 60 developer-commit tasks across six Earth System Model repositories (Noah-MP, CLM5, SUMMA, ParFlow, MOM6, VIC) testing whether AI coding agents preserve physics while modifying model code, with audited reference diffs and an eight-item patch-review rubric. Fills a gap in evaluating agents on scientifically consequential code edits. Valuable for scientific code-agent evaluation.

entry.title: Environment-Aware Probabilistic State Estimation of Continuum Robots from Planar Imaging

author.name: Aedan Mangan, Spencer Teetaert, Chengnan Shentu, Michael G. Brandel, Jeremy J. Heit, Alexander Norbash, Timothy D. Barfoot, Nikolay Atanasov, Tania K. Morimoto, Jessica Burgner-Kahrs

entry.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic state estimator for continuum robots that represents a known environment as a signed distance field to inform shape estimation under contact. The estimator is continuous in arclength and time, fuses asynchronous measurements along the robot, and targets applications like medical navigation with preoperative imaging. This addresses a real modeling challenge for compliant robots in confined spaces.

entry.title: Selective ROM Weight Storage for Responsive LLM Control on Edge Robots

author.name: Boxiang Song, Zhihong Chen, Xiaoyu Hao, Jinhong Huang, Chengkai Zhu, Jiaqi Yang, Hongyang Pan, Changhao Yan and Keren Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid memory architecture for edge robots running LLMs, storing selected fixed weights in banked ROM while keeping mutable weights and state in LPDDR, with coordinated scheduling to reduce bandwidth contention and control latency. This addresses the practical bottleneck of deploying LLM inference on memory-constrained robotic hardware.

entry.title: Fast World Planner: Advantage-Aware Action-Chunk Policy for Online Planning

author.name: Jiangtao Kong, Yuchen Wang, Yandong Luo, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang, Yanbing Mao, Lu Gan, Tianyi Zhou, Huajie Shao

entry.summary: Proposes SWAN, an advantage-aware MPPI-based model-based RL framework that represents and improves complete H-step planner proposals rather than aligning only at the action level, reducing planning latency in online control. By learning stronger policy guidance from the planner, it avoids the performance degradation that comes with fewer MPPI refinement iterations. This targets a practical bottleneck for real-time model-based RL in robotics.

entry.title: CoopOcc: Cooperative 3D Semantic Occupancy Perception via Multi-Agent and Cross-Modal Fusion

author.name: Zengle Zhu, Zhen Li, Tianyi Huai, Xinhu Zheng, Liuqing Yang, Rongqing Zhang

entry.summary: CoopOcc proposes cooperative 3D semantic occupancy perception that fuses multi-agent and cross-modal (semantic and geometric) information while establishing reliable 3D correspondence across agents and preserving modality-specific structures. It targets occlusion and sensor coverage gaps that a single agent's occupancy representation cannot compensate for. This is relevant to autonomous driving fleets and collaborative perception.

entry.title: Routing Collapse in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts: Cross-Modal Conditioning Restores Expert Diversity Without Improving Accuracy

author.name: Syed Hussamuddin, Mubashra Fayyaz

entry.summary: This paper studies routing health in a seven-expert MoE head for multimodal emotion recognition, showing that scalar fusion causes routing collapse onto under two experts while cross-modal attention fusion more than doubles expert utilization and entropy. Notably, the restored routing diversity yields no detectable accuracy improvement across six seeds.

entry.title: PSC-Gen: Physical Sequence Conditioning for Video Generation via Agentic Visual Planning

author.name: Wonsik Shin, Jinju Jang, Junhoo Lee, Yeonjin Chang, Jimyeong Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: PSC-Gen is a training-free framework that improves physical plausibility of video diffusion outputs by using an agentic loop to plan physical states iteratively and inject their core dynamics into generation via low-frequency filtering. It targets the persistent failure of video models to respect physical laws despite internet-scale training.

entry.title: The Humming Revachol: A Dialogue Network Analysis of Narrative Power in Disco Elysium

author.name: Xinran Liu, Miguel Arana-Catania, Jack Orchard

entry.summary: This computational humanities study applies social network analysis to Disco Elysium's dialogue, building a directed weighted character-mention network of 73 NPCs annotated across social attributes. It operationalizes narrative power through four dimensions and finds that narrative power is largely independent of social identity categories, correlating instead with narrative function and structural embeddedness.

entry.title: Omni-H3-Image: Constrained Foundation Priors Usher in a New Era of All-in-One Blind Image Restoration

author.name: Zihao He, Songhua Liu

entry.summary: The paper shows that powerful unified image generation/editing models (e.g., a 33B MiniMax image model, FLUX.1-Kontext, Qwen-Image-Edit) achieve very low PSNR on blind restoration due to spatial drift, chromatic hallucination, and semantic fabrication. Omni-H3 wraps unmodified foundation models in an approximate three-stage constrained posterior projection framework using a tiny 0.92M-parameter auxiliary pre-conditioner, combining physics-aware VLM sensing, lattice anchoring, and closed-loop text verification. It reports results across 925 blind tasks against 11 SOTA baselines.

entry.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions

author.name: Xu Wan, Wenyue Xu, Shenjie Zhao

entry.summary: EA-Bench evaluates personal agents' efficiency under imperfect user information, jointly measuring tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency with controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. It is presented as the first benchmark to combine these two efficiency dimensions under such perturbations, built from 63 work-related task instances with task requirements represented to guide perturbation design. The benchmark exposes inefficiencies hidden when agents assume complete instructions.

entry.title: FormaFin: Verifiable Financial Analysis with Solver-Guided Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bethel Hall, William Eiers

entry.summary: FormaFin trains small open LLMs to translate natural-language financial rules into reusable SMT formulas, combining teacher distillation with reinforcement learning where an SMT solver computes rewards from numerical thresholds in the rules. It targets privacy-sensitive settings like corporate loan monitoring where local small models are preferred.

entry.title: Gaze Graphs: A Scene-Level Representation of Visual Attention in the Operating Room

author.name: S\'eraphin Baributsa, Keqi Chen, Vinkle Srivastav, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: The authors introduce gaze graphs connecting clinicians to attended 3D scene entities from exocentric cameras, extending the EgoExOR dataset with gaze annotations to create EgoExOR-Gaze, the first multi-view gaze graph benchmark for operating rooms. They show utility for fine-grained surgical action recognition and semantic scene graph generation, without wearable eye trackers.

entry.title: MolReJev: Decision Models Are In-Context Molecular Predictors

author.name: Kaiyuan Lu, Jiatong Li, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: MolReJev combines retrieval of similar labeled examples with in-context learning and joint candidate scoring in a single forward pass, enabling cross-task molecular property prediction without token-by-token generation. It improves predictions over a released general-purpose checkpoint and over a separately trained variant across tasks.

entry.title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models

author.name: Saahil Islam, Adarsh Bhandary Panambur, Teodora Spasojevic, Eduardo Castaneda, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: CLASP is an ID-only framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution detection in medical imaging that ranks visual encoder layers by Gaussian conditional mutual information over layer-prompt responses, selects a compact layer subset via anchored spectral selection, and combines layer-prompt profiles with PCA-compressed visual features in a single discriminative model.

entry.title: A Finite-Rate Selection Law for Annealed Gibbs Sampling

author.name: Izhar Ali, Muhammad Haris Khan, Saeed Ahmad

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how finite cooling rates bias annealed Gibbs sampling in multimodal models, measuring retained log-odds between modes. In the Curie-Weiss model, runs select their mode near the mode-formation transition and rarely switch afterward, so unbiased Monte Carlo estimates can fail at finite rates. This provides an analytic selection law with implications for simulated annealing reliability.

entry.title: Do LLM Agents Compromise Like Humans? Risk and Responsibility in Dyadic Decision-Making

author.name: Noah S. Okada, Ketika Garg, Wenning Deng, Dean Mobbs

entry.summary: The authors test LLM agents in a repeated joint risk decision-making task previously run with humans, examining whether agents accommodate partners and how they attribute responsibility for shared outcomes. Agents converge toward partners' choices like humans, but do so through different dynamics with little reciprocal adjustment and different responsibility attribution patterns.

entry.title: ATLAS: Autoregressive Trajectories for Longitudinal Analysis of Survival

author.name: Morgan Nissen, Chunyang Li, Seth Glazier, Julia Bohman, Ahmad Halwani, Jeffrey Humpherys

entry.summary: ATLAS trains a sequence model on longitudinal patient data and autoregressively samples possible futures conditioned on observed history, forming patient-specific synthetic cohorts from which Kaplan-Meier and Aalen-Johansen curves are estimated. Evaluation uses stochastic finite-state automaton benchmarks with exact conditional reference curves, giving rigorous ground truth for comparison. A thoughtful bridge between deep sequence models and classical survival analysis.

entry.title: Training-Free 3D Editing via Feature-Divergence Localization and Trajectory Correction

author.name: Tri Ton, Siwoo Lim, Joshua Tian Jin Tee, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: FocusFlow is a training-free, segmentation-free 3D editing framework built on probability flow models that splits the integration trajectory into two phases: early structure formation with Feature-Divergence Localization to spatially gate velocity updates, and later trajectory correction to prevent stalled edits. It targets spatial bleed into preserved regions and under-committed edits that plague inversion-free methods. Addresses both precision and reliability in 3D editing.

entry.title: Direct Feedback Policy Optimization for AI Coding Agents

author.name: Fei Ding

entry.summary: DFPO is a single-trajectory reinforcement learning algorithm for multi-turn coding agents that trains directly from one trajectory, avoiding the sparse terminal rewards and repeated sampling of group-relative methods like GSPO. It achieves higher task resolution rates than GSPO under matched base models and execution harnesses. Targets the core RL problem of credit assignment for coding agents.

entry.title: THETA: Heat Diffusion as a Structural Prior for Cross-Domain Transfer in Graph Foundation Models

author.name: Haonan Liu, Shuo Wang, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: THETA is a graph foundation model that uses Heat Kernel Signatures as a topology-based structural prior, providing domain-agnostic node descriptors that transfer across graphs without aligned attribute semantics. This complements feature-based relations and helps particularly in low-label regimes.

entry.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds

author.name: Wenyi Wu, Siqi Liu, Yuru Feng, Zixuan Song, Aayush Salvi, Sibo Zhu, Kun Zhou, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: GameAnything is an open-source agentic platform that converts multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games via iterative development, combining coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and experience memory. It also introduces GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities and game creation objectives.

entry.title: ContinuLoc: Continuous Pose Inference over Neural Fields for UAV Geo-Localization

author.name: Weikun Zhou, Jinliang Lin, Yu Zang, Lin Xie, Haiqing Fu, Sheng Ao, Shangshu Yu, Zhiming Luo, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: ContinuLoc reformulates cross-view UAV geo-localization by replacing discretized 2DoF candidate map libraries with a continuously queryable semantic neural field, enabling pose estimation as optimization over a continuous 4DoF space (ground position, heading, and scale). This decoupling removes the ceiling that candidate sampling resolution places on localization precision. The work is relevant for drone navigation applications requiring accurate, fine-grained positioning without GPS.

entry.title: Dual-Side Uncertainty Estimation: Calibrating Data and Model Uncertainty into a Shared Probability Space

author.name: Jiaxuan Gao, Yang Hu, Feihong Lu, Yudi Huang, Qingyun Sun, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: DUE jointly estimates input-side aleatoric and sentence-level epistemic uncertainty for multimodal user intention analysis. It uses Dirichlet perturbations of cross-layer representations from a single generation to produce ordered token uncertainty sequences, which a sequence-aware Normal-Inverse-Gamma estimator converts into epistemic uncertainty and confidence estimates.

entry.title: Where Does Personalization Reside in Photo Editing? Evidence from One Photographer's Lightroom History

author.name: Dongwu Qian

entry.summary: This paper analyzes 3,193 Lightroom edits from a single professional photographer to disentangle recurring personal preferences from shoot-specific intent in personalized photo editing. Using batch-level holdouts and clustered bootstrap statistics, it finds that residual (prior-relative) prediction offers little significant advantage on unseen batches, and that a few same-batch anchor edits via closed-form shrinkage substantially improve prediction. The work matters because it provides careful, statistically grounded evidence that personalization signals in creative workflows are harder to exploit than commonly assumed.

entry.title: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Color Normalization Methods in Histopathology: Nuclei Preservation, Artifact Sensitivity, Background Fidelity, and Downstream Performanc

author.name: Falah Jabar, Aria Torkpour, Pasquale Lombardi, Masoud Tafavvoghi, Per Niklas Benzler Waaler, Sigve Andersen, Ilona Urbarova, David J. Pinato, Mehrdad Rakaee, Tom Donnem, Lill-Tove Rasmussen Busund, Elin Richardsen

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks 11 classical and deep-learning stain normalization methods across 7 nuclei datasets and 7 color spaces, evaluating nuclear structure preservation, background fidelity, artifact sensitivity, and downstream detection/classification performance. Notably, downstream performance varies more across datasets than across normalization methods. This sobering, systematic result informs best practices for cross-center histopathology model deployment.

entry.title: Self-Refining VLA Sampling

author.name: Jeff Duan, Arjun Sharma, Jennifer Cruden, Vansh Tibrewal

entry.summary: The authors adapt Predict-and-Perturb, a self-refinement technique for flow-based video generation, to Vision-Language-Action models, refining action samples at test time without large candidate ensembles or an external trained corrector. Required modifications to the refinement procedure are identified for the robotics domain.

entry.title: Who Plays What: Same-Instrument Music Separation from Video

author.name: Abhinaba Roy, Ambuj Mehrish, Sebastiano Vascon, Dorien Herremans

entry.summary: This paper tackles per-player music separation when multiple musicians play the same instrument, using body and hand keypoint velocities plus video features to disambiguate players, with a pretrained separator attending to these tokens via cross-attention. It provides the first real per-player evaluation rather than synthetic solo-video mixtures.

entry.title: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies

author.name: Xi Chen, Yuze Chen, Baichuan Mo, Jie Ying, Yuan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper builds an agentic system where LLMs revise symbolic inventory-policy structures while a numerical engine fits parameters and evaluates policies, guided by multicriteria parent selection, operational diagnostics, and reusable symbolic motifs. It is validated at scale on 15,600 instances across 50 demand distributions covering lead times and perishability.

entry.title: Label-Efficient LiDAR Semantic Segmentation with 2D-3D Vision Transformer Adapters

author.name: Julia Hindel, Rohit Mohan, Jelena Bratuli\`c, Daniele Cattaneo, Thomas Brox, and Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: BALViT leverages frozen vision foundation models as amodal feature encoders for LiDAR semantic segmentation, combining range-view and bird's-eye-view encoding through a novel 2D-3D adapter. The approach enables label-efficient training and transfers advances from image-based vision architectures to point cloud segmentation.

entry.title: LithoFormer: A Robust Framework for Stratigraphic Inference via Transformers

author.name: Shwetha Salimath, Francesca Bugiotti, Sylvain Wlodarczyk and Sohaib Ouzineb

entry.summary: Introduces LithoFormer, a Seq2Seq transformer with a channel-independent PatchTST backbone and rotary positional embeddings that ingests entire multivariate well logs in one pass for stratigraphic inference, replacing limited sliding-window classifiers. It targets subsurface reservoir characterization relevant to carbon capture, geothermal, and resource extraction. The whole-sequence approach captures long-range geological context and improves formation-layer alignment.

entry.title: Reset Dependence Is Embodied: Training Protocol Changes Which Morphologies Appear Optimal

author.name: Kevin Qiu, Zhao Yang, Marek Cygan

entry.summary: Shows that the episode-reset rule in robot co-design benchmarks changes which evolved morphologies appear optimal: training PPO controllers for 100 DERL-evolved UNIMAL bodies with torso-height reset thresholds at 20%, 50%, or none yields rankings whose correlation drops sharply between protocols. Two studies can thus select different bodies from the same corpus under the same task and evaluator. This warns that benchmark conclusions about morphology are confounded by training protocol details.

entry.title: Estimating Silenced Tokens in Quantized LLMs

author.name: Giuseppe Pappalardo

entry.summary: Investigates tokens that become impossible for a quantized LLM to ever produce (no hidden state can make them the top output-layer choice), a failure mode invisible to perplexity and task-accuracy metrics. The paper gives a scalable method yielding certified lower and upper bounds on how many tokens each quantized output head silences.

entry.title: Action Windows Are Inherently Temporal: A Benchmark for Time-Sensitive Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Haoxiang Zhan, Haoqin Hong, Congcong Zhu, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AWAIT, a simulation benchmark evaluating VLM agents on time-sensitive manipulation tasks where evolving physical processes create finite action windows, with decision and execution time counted against a shared budget. Evaluation shows agents struggle to recognize window onset, and existing benchmarks cover such temporal constraints only partially.

entry.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge

author.name: Panagiotis Kasnesis, Lazaros Toumanidis, Amalia Contiero Syropoulou, Christos Chatzigeorgiou

entry.summary: Wactorz is an open-source runtime where LLM-generated agents are long-lived supervised actors that compile chat requests into Python actors, restart individually after crashes with state intact, and coordinate over MQTT so they can be spawned on and live-migrated between edge nodes like Raspberry Pis. A recorded demo builds camera-to-lamp automation from a single chat request.

entry.title: How Seasonal Reference Choice Changes the Apparent Gains of Chronos Models in Electricity Load Forecasting

author.name: ChandraMohan K (Bannari Amman Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: A single-author methodological study showing that apparent advantages of zero-shot foundation forecasting models (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2) over baselines on hourly electricity load depend heavily on which seasonal baseline is chosen, using 60 fixed cases, bootstrap uncertainty, and validation-selected references. A week ahead, Chronos-Bolt beats weekly persistence in 21 of 30 cases but gains shrink against better-selected references.

entry.title: Loop-Count Schedules in Looped Transformers: An Empirical Study

author.name: Konstantin Kolokolov

entry.summary: This empirical study examines how the training schedule of loop iteration count R affects looped transformers, using 46M-110M parameter models trained on 2B tokens with learned residual gates. The key finding is that whether the sampling range includes R=1 is decisive: including single-pass training collapses gates to small corrections, while R>=2 makes each loop pass act as a full layer.

entry.title: UniDR: Learning To Generate Anatomical Deformations From Images via Unified Diffusion Modeling and Registration

author.name: Swakshar Deb, Tonmoy Hossain, Tom Fletcher, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: UniDR proposes a unified framework that generates anatomical deformations with preserved topology by jointly coupling a conditional diffusion model over deformation fields with a registration process. A registration-guided score-matching objective aligns the diffusion process with the deformation distribution, avoiding the error propagation that arises when generation and registration are treated as separate stages. This has direct relevance to medical imaging and image registration tasks.

entry.title: Seeing Beyond Names: Image-Grounded Concept Linking for Robust Vision-Language Recognition

author.name: Behraj Khan, Shabir Ahmad, Tahir Qasim Syed, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari

entry.summary: This paper quantifies vocabulary shift in zero-shot CLIP classifiers — alternative class names (synonyms, abbreviations, ontology terms) reduce top-1 accuracy by 14.8-17.6 points — and proposes a training-free image-grounded concept linking method with a reliability gate, yielding a pooled 1.8-point gain over template ensembles across four benchmark datasets.

entry.title: CarlHOI: Counterfactual Predictive Imagination for Generalizable Multi-Humanoid Object Interaction under Constrained Environments

author.name: Wenjie Lin, Jin Wei-Kocsis

entry.summary: CarlHOI proposes a counterfactual-anchored relational latent world model enabling multi-humanoid teams to adapt cooperative object-transport behaviors to unseen obstacles without retraining the underlying control policies. It explicitly models the shared object, individual humanoids, and obstacles as interacting entities for planning under environmental constraints.

entry.title: DictaRashi: A State-of-the-Art OCR Model For Rashi Script

author.name: Ometz Shmidman, Yonah Taurog, Aryeh Sanders, Shlomo Bluth, Moshe Koppel, Joshua Geudalia, Avi Shmidman

entry.summary: The authors release DictaRashi, a Tesseract OCR model for Hebrew books printed in Rashi script, trained on over one million manually corrected lines from more than 100 Rabbinic works. It achieves 0.86% character error rate and 3.38% word error rate, beating all 31 public Hebrew Tesseract models and outperforming frontier LLMs on this task.

entry.title: Revisiting RadioGalaxyNET: modern detectors for radio galaxy detection and host identification

author.name: Argo Saakyan

entry.summary: This paper re-evaluates the RadioGalaxyNET benchmark for detecting extended radio galaxies and identifying their infrared hosts by training three modern detectors (D-FINE-seg, YOLO26-pose, RF-DETR) and scoring them with the original benchmark code. All three exceed the 2023 published state of the art, with D-FINE-seg M reaching 67.1 box AP and 72.4 host AP, improvements of 12.6 and 24.3 points over prior best results.

entry.title: LexiDet-OVD: Benchmarking Lexical Sensitivity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Amit Thakur, Mukesh Singhal

entry.summary: LexiDet-OVD is a benchmark and metric suite probing how lexical choices in free-form prompts affect open-vocabulary object detection, organizing prompt sets into equivalent, conditional, and broad semantic scopes and evaluating four detector families on fixed COCO and LVIS samples. Beyond mean and worst-prompt AP50, it reports P10, CVaR, leave-one-prompt-out influence, detection agreement, box consistency, and confidence variance.

entry.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming

author.name: Sameera S Kashyap, Akshitha Nagaraj, Razvan Marinescu

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the best foundation for simulating centuries-long Mars terraforming interventions. It contrasts learned world models with data-driven climate emulators (which lack action-conditioning) and expensive physics-based general circulation models, highlighting advantages in uncertainty quantification and stability under sparse non-terrestrial data.

entry.title: Safe Quantum Stochastic Linear Bandits

author.name: Ruizhe Zhang, Junyi Wu, Guang Lin

entry.summary: This paper initiates the study of safe quantum stochastic linear bandits, where a learner maximizes unknown linear reward subject to unknown linear mean constraints, and proposes QRS-COLTS, a quantum resampled-scaling constrained Thompson sampling algorithm with feasibility guarantees and polylogarithmic regret. It also analyzes a superposition-query model with an unsafe-action flag measured per query.

entry.title: Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems

author.name: Andrei Vlad Nicula, Kalp Shah, Robert-Stefan Sofroni, Mihnea Andrei B\^arsan, Agneya Bhardwaj, Jan Jel\'inek, Chris Hoes, Remco Hogerwerf, Finn Govers, Storm Koper, Gerrit Janssen, Stef de Wildt, Alejandro Valverde Mahou

entry.summary: This work argues that physics-informed neural networks struggle with singular PDE solutions and proposes enforcing the 2D Laplace equation directly in the network architecture via holomorphic networks that are harmonic by construction. Adding singular functions tailored to boundary junctions yields the most accurate neural model on six singular benchmarks. It demonstrates a compelling alternative to residual-penalty PINN training.

entry.title: SAGE-Drive: Benefit-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Planning

author.name: Donglei Rong, Wenbin Yao, Congcong Bai, Xi Gao, Qiaoqiao Ren, Sheng Jin, Cheng Xu

entry.summary: SAGE-Drive learns when explicit reasoning actually improves autonomous driving planning, using paired planning outcomes with and without reasoning to label reasoning benefit, then training a gate to invoke reasoning only where beneficial. This reduces computational cost while preserving accuracy in scenarios where reasoning helps. The adaptive gating idea addresses a real efficiency concern for reasoning-augmented AV planners.

entry.title: When 1+1 $\neq$ 2: Benchmarking Civil-Time Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Melika Shirian, Kianoosh Vadaei, Arshia Hemmat, Mohammad Hossein Shaker Ardakani, Ali Mamanpoosh, Matin Moqadas, Amirmasoud Rismanchian, Afsaneh Fatemi

entry.summary: CivilTime-Bench is a 60,011-example training and 10,500-example evaluation benchmark for civil-time reasoning, covering daylight saving transitions, non-hour offsets, date-line crossings, and ISO week boundaries under strict output-contract evaluation. Testing seven LLMs shows highly variable zero-shot accuracy, inconsistent gains from contract-aware prompting and few-shot learning, and fine-tuned performance of 74.6-86.6% EM. It exposes a concrete class of arithmetic-adjacent reasoning failures in LLMs.

entry.title: Wavelet determinantal samplers: Optimal approximation rates adapting to regularity

author.name: Hoang-Son Tran, Pranav Gupta, Subhroshekhar Ghosh

entry.summary: The authors construct wavelet-based determinantal point process samplers on Riemannian manifolds and geometric graphs whose variance reduction adapts to the regularity of the observed function. They derive optimal unbiased quadrature rules matching classical randomized integration rates with modest function evaluations, extending to epsilon-graphs and k-nearest-neighbor graph settings.

entry.title: Spiking World-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Mingquan Liu, Peng Zhou, Shanming Yao, Shuai Wang, Simo Wu, Malu Zhang

entry.summary: SpikingWAM is presented as the first spiking neural network version of a world-action model for robotic manipulation, using a sparse task-skeleton state of keypoint positions rather than dense video to avoid wasting computation on background pixels. This design makes action-conditioned world models far more deployable on power-constrained robot hardware.

entry.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery

author.name: Harry Sevi, Joonatan E. M. Laulainen

entry.summary: The paper argues that standard reliability metrics for machine-learned interatomic potentials (evaluating MACE-MP, CHGNet, Orb V3) do not predict downstream screening value, and proposes a deployment objective measuring how much DFT computation can be avoided while maintaining decision quality. It evaluates novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits under this decision-aligned lens.

entry.title: Correlated by Construction: Endpoint Choice and the Validation of Protein Screening

author.name: Eric LoPrete, Galen Loving, George Sabin, Pavle Jeremi\'c

entry.summary: This work tests whether miniaturized solution-phase protein-metal affinity measurements transfer to a real deployment setting — immobilized rare-earth separation — using an automated production and screening platform across 82 protein-metal-pair measurements. It finds strong correlations (Spearman roughly 0.87-0.92) between assay endpoints, addressing an often-assumed but rarely demonstrated validity question in ML-driven protein engineering.

entry.title: Optimal Private Gaussian Multi-sampling

author.name: Raoof Zare Moayedi, Mohammad Hossein Yassaee, Javad B. Ebrahimi

entry.summary: This theory paper gives polynomial-time algorithms for generating m samples from a d-dimensional Gaussian with unknown mean and covariance under approximate differential privacy, with near-optimal sample complexity using roughly m plus d times sqrt(m) over epsilon input samples. Lower bounds show exact independence of outputs incurs essentially no extra sample cost.

entry.title: FiRE: Fine-grained Ranking Evaluation for Machine Translation

author.name: Wenyang Gao (1 and 2), Yinghao Yang (2), Xi Jin (1), Jing Li (3) and Yue Zhang (2) ((1) Zhejiang University, (2) School of Engineering, Westlake University, (3) Sichuan Lan-bridge Information Technology Co., Ltd.)

entry.summary: FiRE is a reference-free machine translation evaluation method that uses off-the-shelf LLMs for criterion-driven pairwise comparisons along faithfulness, fluency, and style consistency, rather than a single holistic score. The authors also build the first human-annotated reference-free benchmark for fine-grained MT ranking to enable rigorous meta-evaluation.

entry.title: ToWo-VTON: Take-Off Wear-On Virtual Try-On via Topology-aware Decoupling

author.name: Zhenchen Wan, Tianxi Chen, Runqi Lin, Tianyi Bo, Ce Chen, Jiaxin Huang, Yanwu Xu, Tongliang Liu, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: ToWo-VTON introduces a two-stage virtual try-on paradigm that first generates a tight-fitting body proxy (Take-Off) and then synthesizes the target garment conditioned on this structural prior (Wear-On). The decoupling reduces source-garment interference and improves lower-body and full-body try-on under large silhouette changes and occlusions.

entry.title: TriSegAgent: Context-Efficient 3D Annotation with MLLMs via Tri-Planes

author.name: Qingqiao Hu, Jialin Li, Meilong Xu, Kehan Qi, Yipeng Zhang, Lin Tian, Hongwei Bran Li, Klaus Mueller, Xiaoling Hu

entry.summary: TriSegAgent uses multimodal LLM agents to drive interactive 3D segmentation annotation loops, representing 3D volumes via tri-planes (three orthogonal views) to keep each MLLM call token-compact while preserving error-region visibility. This makes iterative click-based 3D annotation more affordable and reliable.

entry.title: RigidAnchor: Cross-View Geo-Localization for UAV via Iterative Planar Rigid Alignment

author.name: Bo Wang, Dekang Zhu, Jian Li, Zhipeng Meng, Bo Wang, Dewen Hu

entry.summary: RigidAnchor reformulates UAV-to-satellite geo-localization as iterative planar rigid alignment over the continuous satellite map rather than independent tile retrieval, removing grid-quantized outputs and adding absolute heading estimation for GNSS-denied navigation. It exploits the known fixed spacing, scale, and orientation of satellite tiles.

entry.title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift

author.name: Samy Haffoudhi (DIG, LTCI, GENCI), Fabian M Suchanek (IP Paris, LTCI), Nils Holzenberger

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether reasoning-capable small LLMs remain competitive at entity disambiguation, comparing pointwise, listwise, and reasoning-based candidate selection within a coarse-to-fine pipeline, both in-domain and under distribution shift. It clarifies when the cost of reasoning is justified at small model scale.

entry.title: AirVT-15k: A Query-Diverse UAV Video-Text Dataset and Query-Adaptive Evidence Alignment Network for Retrieval

author.name: Xi Chen, Xu Chen, Xiangyang Jia, Ting Gan, Xu Zhang, Shuquan Wei

entry.summary: The paper introduces AirVT-15k, a benchmark of 15,504 UAV videos with 155,040 bilingual captions covering scene context, object states, and temporal changes, plus AirFocus-CST, a retrieval network selecting query-relevant frames and patches with coarse-to-fine interaction and optimal-transport alignment. It emphasizes that different queries need different evidence within the same video.

entry.title: Cost-Sensitive Reversibility of Non-Deterministic Actions

author.name: Giuseppe Canonaco, Alberto Pozanco, Daniel Borrajo

entry.summary: The paper extends qualitative reversibility notions in FOND planning to cost-sensitive settings, defining weak and strong reversal budgets, k-bounded reversibility, and a reversibility lattice relating these concepts, with proven cost-aware policy results. This lets planners reason not just whether actions can be undone but at what cost.

entry.title: LiveMirror: Real-Time Diffusion Virtual Try-On on a Consumer GPU and Its Self-Supervised Adaptation to Indian Ethnic Wear

author.name: Jigyansha Jeevan Rout, Sukanta Kumar Sabut

entry.summary: LiveMirror achieves live-camera virtual try-on with diffusion models on a single 16 GB consumer GPU via asynchronous keyframe generation: displayed frames are optical-flow warps of the latest keyframe while new try-on images arrive every 370-490 ms at 25 FPS 720p display rate. It also adapts self-supervisedly to Indian ethnic wear, a domain underserved by existing datasets.

entry.title: AXE: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report

author.name: Joonhee Lim, Seonmyeong Lee, Sihwan Hwang, Hanbin Jang, Hiwon Shin, Dogun Kim, Hyelin Jo, Hyeonjun Jeong, Yongjae Lee, Junseong Kwak, Junhyeok Park, Satyam Mishra, Juyeb Shin, Uisung Kim, Hyeonseo Kim, Saparkhan Kassymbekov, Hailemichael Molla Gashaw, Abi Rahman Syamil, Mingyu Kim, Hyeongjun Kim, Yeina Lee, Moogeun Park, Dongsuk Kum

entry.summary: This technical report describes an end-to-end autonomous driving pipeline for the Physical AI AV Track, combining data curation, HD map auto-labelling, imitation learning, and simulator-based reinforcement learning. A selection-based planner scores a fixed vocabulary of trajectory candidates using collision, drivable-area, and progress models learned from simulated rollouts, filtered by object detection and BEV segmentation for safety. Training used NVIDIA NuRec and the PAI-AV dataset.

entry.title: GeoRead3D: Grounding Part Descriptions for 3D Pointing and Reorientation

author.name: Zhangcheng Hou, Kevin Tonkich, Tomoaki Ohtsuki

entry.summary: The paper identifies a gap between language-guided part segmentation, evaluated by mask overlap, and part geometry needed for 3D pointing and reorientation tasks, since overlapping masks poorly predict center-to-part directions. It learns point evidence, weights over observed points whose weighted centroid gives part location, closing this gap. This enables grounding part descriptions for pointing and object reorientation.

entry.title: Towards an Armenian Epigraphic Corpus

author.name: Chahan Vidal-Gor{\`e}ne (CJM, LIPN), Arpine Avetisyan, Edita Matevosyan, Seda Kirakosyan, Victoria Khurshudyan (Inalco, SeDyL), Pollet Samvelian (Lattice)

entry.summary: This paper presents the Corpus Inscriptionum Armenicarum Electronicum, an open digital corpus digitizing the ten printed volumes of the Divan hay vimagrut'yan (1960-2017), which document nearly 7,600 Armenian inscriptions, many of which are now damaged or destroyed. The pipeline combines layout detection, OCR, and a vision-language model to produce structured initial readings of each record, which specialists then verify on a proofreading platform. It fills a significant gap, as Armenian epigraphy has lacked a digital resource comparable to those available for Greek, Latin, or Georgian inscriptions.

entry.title: Tri-DNO: Trilateral Diffusion Noise Optimization for 3D Human Object Interaction

author.name: Paul Hinzer, Niklas Gard, Anna Hilsmann, Peter Eisert

entry.summary: Presents Tri-DNO, a diffusion noise optimization strategy for sampling from a pretrained multimodal human-object-interaction diffusion model to improve hand-object contact plausibility. It avoids retraining the generative model and targets AR/VR and character animation use cases where contact errors like interpenetration break realism.

entry.title: Does the Mixer Matter ? Paired-Seed Ablations of Tiny Bilingual Language Models

author.name: Ayoub Kirouane

entry.summary: Reports paired-seed architecture ablations on a Greek-English model family from 54M to 759M parameters, holding data, tokenizer, and recipe fixed. The key finding is that at tiny scale stored capacity dominates mixer design: adding routed experts lowers loss substantially more than architectural choices like hybrid recurrent-attention mixers or layer reuse.

entry.title: Testing Quantized KV-Cache Maintenance: Encoding Layout and Historical Restoration

author.name: Ziyang Huang and Songwei Wu

entry.summary: Tests whether quantized KV-cache maintenance operations actually preserve state, showing that repeating rows then selecting originals retains layout-dependent drift and that existing checks fail to establish preservation contracts in fixed implementations. On four-bit HQQ caches, paired relative-L2 drift grows substantially over sixteen cycles for Qwen3-1.7B and SmolLM3-3B, and a prefix-view extension changes history and next logits despite passing current-prefix checks.

entry.title: Object-Centric Differentiable Logic Networks for Abstract Visual Reasoning

author.name: Hanne Say Eren, Ana Ezquerro, Ozan \"Ozdenizci

entry.summary: Introduces Slot-Dwn, a neuro-symbolic architecture combining object-centric slot representations with differentiable logic networks for abstract visual reasoning, aiming for relational analogy and modular abstraction with bounded computation. It avoids both explicit rule supervision and parameter-heavy transformers that reintroduce the inefficiencies neuro-symbolic methods seek to solve.

entry.title: Reconstructing 3D+t Cardiovascular Flow From Sparse Planar Velocity Fields With Neural Fields

author.name: Viraj Patel, Deblina Bhattacharjee, Katharine Fraser

entry.summary: This work reconstructs time-resolved 3D cardiovascular velocity fields from sparse planar MRI-like measurements using a plane-aware neural-field framework with per-plane projections, optionally constrained by physics. Evaluated on computational aortic/aneurysm datasets and real 4D Flow MRI, a physics-constrained SIREN achieved the largest error reductions for the aorta.

entry.title: Quantum resources constrain function approximation

author.name: Oxana Shaya, Lirand\"e Pira

entry.summary: This theoretical work quantifies how quantum resources - coherence, imaginarity, entanglement, and magic - constrain function approximation in quantum learning models with fixed encoding and readout. It derives concrete bounds, e.g., coherence bounding oscillation and entanglement bounding distance from product functions, and shows Clifford gates suffice for uniform approximation on domains bounded away from zero.

entry.title: Go Far, Look Less: Active Multi-Room Reconstruction with Persistent Goals and Selective Views

author.name: Jiawei Jiang, Haonan Zhou, Wendi Hu, Jiabei Hu, Yina Xiang, Kaiyue Zhou, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: ROAM-GS is a training-free active reconstruction framework for multi-room scenes that couples persistent goals with selective views, capturing only at variable-horizon endpoints and crediting transit with remaining goal value. A Surface Reconstruction Memory scores candidate poses by projecting post-update defects, addressing the myopia of next-best-view methods in homes.

entry.title: Potential Games for Self-Neighborhood Channel Mixing in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Marco Lavorini, Davide Bacciu, Giancarlo Bigi

entry.summary: Frames the trade-off between neighborhood aggregation and node-specific information in graph neural networks as a game, showing that a distinctness payoff induces an exact potential game whose potential is degree-normalized strict Dirichlet energy. The proposed CG2 architecture amortizes mixing decisions via a shared six-parameter per-layer policy and improves mean performance on three of five heterophily benchmarks.

entry.title: XFreq: Geometry-Aligned Cross-View Residual Learning for Sparse 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction

author.name: Yuhuan Lu, P. Ellen Grant, Davood Karimi

entry.summary: XFreq reconstructs 3D ultrasound from sparse 2D slices by querying geometry-aligned 2D features at 3D locations using known slice poses, complementing splatted intensities. A low-frequency decoder predicts a smooth field and a high-frequency component recovers residual details, separating structural prediction from detail synthesis.

entry.title: Do Waste Classifiers Recognise Items They Have Never Seen? Object-Disjoint Evaluation on Household and Medical Waste

author.name: Nusrat Jahan, Mst. Eshrat Jahan Esha, Masuma Sadia, Saad Ahmed, Md Zahim Hassan, and S M Jahangir Alam

entry.summary: This paper introduces BanglaWaste-23, a dataset of 4,160 images covering 172 household and medical waste objects from Bangladesh, where each image is tagged to its physical item so models can be evaluated on truly unseen objects. Object-disjoint cross-validation of 13 models reveals that the near-perfect accuracies reported on random splits collapse on new items, exposing inflated evaluation practices in waste classification.

entry.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks

author.name: Milan Vojnovic

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies agents that each align a model to their own preference data via KL-regularized steps while observing one another, characterizing which aggregation rule the resulting collective policies implement. It shows the effective rule weights agents by their long-run attention share divided by temperature, concentrating on responses maximizing a weighted sum of rewards.

entry.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications

author.name: Marvin Kopka, Austen El-Osta, Christoph Kollwitz, Felix Balzer, Florian Bontrup

entry.summary: The study evaluates 16 LLM-based decision models (14 open-weight) for medical triage on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, totaling 163,728 assessments. Best models correctly triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real cases, but showed stronger performance for early emergency recognition with an AUROC of 0.87 from demographics and red-flag answers alone.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems

author.name: Hoang T. Nguyen, Deepjyoti Deka, Priya L. Donti, Varsha Pendyala, Nurali Virani, Wajid Muneer, and Reetam Sen Biswas

entry.summary: The paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for AC optimal power flow in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems, where a neural network predicts DER setpoints processed through differentiable AC power flow to enforce limits without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems achieve mean objective gaps of 0.32-0.92% while balancing cost, curtailment, and constraint penalties.

entry.title: RoFE: Rotated Frozen Embeddings for Low-Data Multimodal Tabular Learning

author.name: Yihao Qiao, Jiajian Ma, Wushuang Rui, Abhishek Jha, Aarti Darji, Yiqiu Shen

entry.summary: The paper shows that PCA-based compression of high-dimensional frozen image/text embeddings can underperform simple linear classifiers when combined with tabular prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) in low-label regimes. It identifies the per-column standardization mechanism behind the failure and proposes RoFE, a rotated frozen-embedding interface. This matters for practical multimodal tabular learning where labeled data are scarce.

entry.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression

author.name: Anindya Roy Chowdhury, Atanu Barai, Nandakishore Santhi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free weight quantization framework using randomized orthogonal mixing and progressive residual-sign quantization, motivated by a Gaussian central-limit-theorem argument, to compress Transformer weights at low bit rates without codebooks or trellis optimization. On GPT-2 Large and Llama-3-8B, five residual stages preserve near-baseline perplexity with flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs.

entry.title: CrownFusion: 3D Dental Crown Generation Using Geometry Images and Latent Diffusion

author.name: Johan Ziruo Ye, Xingguang Yan, S{\o}ren Hauberg, Angel X. Chang, Hao Zhang, Peter Lempel S{\o}ndergaard

entry.summary: CrownFusion generates 3D dental crown designs with a latent diffusion model operating on geometry images, a 2D grid encoding of surface coordinates, rather than point clouds, preserving fine detail at high spatial resolution. Conditioned on embeddings of surrounding dentition, it produces anatomically plausible crowns with patient-specific morphological variation and proposes an occlusal fit metric for multi-design evaluation. A strong application of modern generative modeling to dental CAD.

entry.title: SPROUT: Predicting Objective-Grounded Prompt Utility for Efficient Text-to-Image Preference Tuning

author.name: Kangping Hu, Akshay Mehra, Stephen Mussmann

entry.summary: SPROUT improves compute efficiency of preference tuning for text-to-image diffusion models by selecting the most useful training prompts rather than sampling uniformly. It factors prompt selection into utility score, estimator, and batch selection, using a text-only model refit each iteration to predict objective-grounded utility, with randomized acceptance for selection. This reduces wasted candidate-image generation compute.

entry.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions

author.name: Sungchul Kim, Weixiao Huang, Mekala Raja Sekhar Reddy, Amrutha Srinivasan

entry.summary: Needwise replaces LLM generation in conversational recommendation with typed decisions over fixed options, tracking user needs at the catalog-field level and ranking candidates must-first by need tiers. This yields faster turns than LLM re-ranking and interpretable orderings that show which needs each item satisfies.

entry.title: How long must an honest confidence interval be after causal discovery? Benign and malignant weak edges

author.name: Ruiqi Zhao

entry.summary: This theory paper quantifies the price of structural uncertainty in confidence intervals for total causal effects after causal discovery, in linear Gaussian models with known adjacency supersets and k-triangle faithfulness. The main result classifies weak edges by Meek closures: benign edges (where the effect remains identifiable) incur bounded local price, while malignant edges force intervals of order sqrt(n) longer. It gives a sharp characterization of when post-discovery inference is feasible.

entry.title: NSFL: A Post-Training Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic Framework for Boolean Operators in Neural Embeddings

author.name: Vladi Vexler, Ofer Idan, Gil Lederman, Dima Sivov

entry.summary: NSFL adapts formal t-norms and t-conorms to dense embedding spaces post-training, enabling retrieval under multi-atom logical constraints without retraining. It introduces Neuro-Symbolic Deltas and spherical query optimization via Riemannian techniques for scalable real-time retrieval.

entry.title: OSLA: Observation-Aware Local Alignment and Cross-Scene Relation Learning for Any-Scenario Person Re-Identification

author.name: Xinyang Zhang, Feiyu Han, Chenhao Wu, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Yingguang Yang, Feng Zhang, Chongyang Zhang, Hao Zheng, Kefu Xu, Congjing Ran, Bin Chong

entry.summary: OSLA extends supervised CLIP-ReID to any-scenario person re-identification across spectral modalities and aerial-ground viewpoints via Local Identity Alignment, which uses historical identity observations to select reliable cross-scene local correspondences, and Cross-Scene Relation Learning to capture positive relations conventional sampling misses, with local-to-global identity distillation. It targets a unified model for difficult cross-modality, cross-viewpoint retrieval.

entry.title: Robust Trajectory Prediction Under Sensing and V2X Noise: Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies

author.name: Shahab Salehi, Luca Lusvarghi, Miguel Sepulcre, and Javier Gozalvez

entry.summary: Evaluates the sensitivity of five state-of-the-art transformer-based trajectory prediction models to realistic sensing, localization, and V2X communication noise, departing from curated datasets with post-processed ground truth. The paper also proposes mitigation strategies to improve robustness for real-world autonomous vehicle deployment.

entry.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy

author.name: Ajith Nayanananda, Xuping Xie

entry.summary: This theoretical and empirical study examines how to schedule rollout length when training Neural ODEs on chaotic systems, showing that a single global Lyapunov time overlooks local instability variation. The authors characterize the optimal schedule under an instability budget, bound the resulting coverage gains and losses when instability estimates err, and validate numerically.

entry.title: HandXFM: Semantic-Structural Distillation for Hand Radiograph Foundation Models

author.name: Yuxi Long, Ganlin Feng, Lianghong Chen, Liam J. O'Neil, Carol A. Hitchon, Pingzhao Hu

entry.summary: HandXFM is a domain-specific foundation model for hand X-rays that distills semantic priors from BiomedCLIP and structural cues from a chest X-ray ViT within a unified alignment framework. It adapts to multiple musculoskeletal tasks including bone age estimation, abnormality detection, and joint localization, replacing task-specific models. It demonstrates efficient cross-modality distillation for medical foundation models.

entry.title: Targeted Learning for Externally Controlled Trials and Beyond

author.name: Yixin Fang and Weili He

entry.summary: This methodological paper develops targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) for externally controlled clinical trials, covering estimands defined through balancing weights over three external control data sources: historical trial control arms, concurrent cohorts, and real-world data. It derives efficient influence functions and provides practical implementation algorithms with favorable theoretical and finite-sample properties.

entry.title: When a Permitted Action Completes a Forbidden Workflow: Designing Consequence-Oriented Approval for LLM Agents

author.name: S M Asif Hossain, Ruksat Khan Shayoni, Md Kishor Morol, and M F Mridha

entry.summary: Identifies cumulative authorization failure in tool-using LLM agents, where individually permitted steps combine into a forbidden workflow, such as sending an approved recipient a file assembled from data the user forbade sharing. The paper proposes the Cumulative Consent Ledger, an approval interface that restates user intent, binds review to the exact action, and composes cumulative consequences. Frames agent safety as an interaction design problem as much as a security problem.

entry.title: LoopSight: Looped Vision Transformers with Gated Prediction Memory

author.name: Zhaozhi Wang, Mingrui Wu, Jiaming Zhao, An-Syu Li, Jun Luo

entry.summary: Proposes LoopSight, a looped vision transformer with a Gated Prediction Memory that maintains a persistent prediction state separate from the evolving computation state, with patch- and channel-level gated writes controlled by cross-attention. Uses asymptotic loop encoding to condition the shared core on the current iteration.

entry.title: SemGuard: Semantics-Decoupled Watermarking for Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yingying Shi, Zhong Zhou, Bin Zhou

entry.summary: SemGuard addresses semantic interference in CLIP-guided watermarking of Gaussian Splatting 3D assets by learning to suppress scene-dependent semantic signals during universal message decoder pretraining, combining message-related and semantic-related objectives. This improves copyright protection reliability for increasingly popular 3D Gaussian assets. The motivation is timely as 3D generative content proliferates.

entry.title: Legal Is Not Good: A Pre-Registered Benchmark of Low-Cost Language and Decision Models on a New Strategy Game

author.name: Federico Lucca

entry.summary: This paper introduces hexfolk, a minimal two-player 4X strategy game designed so no model has prior exposure, and evaluates low-cost open language and decision models under a fully pre-registered protocol with a deterministic engine, mirrored seats, held-out seeds, and Wilson intervals. It extends a measure-before-you-train methodology to a second domain, probing how well small agents play under fair, replayable conditions. Its emphasis on pre-registration is a methodological contribution to agent evaluation.

entry.title: Analytical Modeling and Optimal GPU Provisioning for Disaggregated LLM Inference

author.name: Akshat Pandey, Dominic Cheng, Sidharth Sharma and Ashwin Gumaste

entry.summary: OSplit provides an exact analytical capacity model for splitting GPUs in disaggregated LLM inference into prefill and decode workers, modeling H100 and GB300 GPUs, scale-up domains, FlashAttention kernels, and vLLM-style serving. It computes optimal partitioning and collective generation policies to maximize throughput.

entry.title: Contrastive Gradient Guidance for Test-Time Multi-Preference Alignment of Diffusion Models

author.name: Po-Yi Lu, Jui-Chao Lu, Paul Kuo-Ming Huang, Shih-Hsin Wang, Chun-Liang Li, Hsuan-Tien Lin

entry.summary: CGG reformulates multi-preference alignment of diffusion models as test-time composition of distributions, representing each preference as a contrastive pair of favored and disfavored existing generative experts rather than compressing preferences into a single scalar reward. This avoids offline fine-tuning and per-tradeoff retraining while reusing already-released expert models.

entry.title: PhyMind: Physics-Informed Masked Autoencoding for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: A Adith

entry.summary: PhyMind replaces the free-form decoder used in masked autoencoding for EEG foundation models with a generative forward model based on 68 cortical regions driven by damped stochastic oscillators and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, projected through a boundary-element lead field. Training combines masked reconstruction with Whittle spectral likelihood, oscillator-dynamics residuals, and source priors. In controlled comparisons, this physics-informed pretraining improves over standard masked reconstruction.

entry.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shixin Hong, Wanqing Cui, Yibo Hu, Naen Xu, Zhiwei Huang, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma

entry.summary: STRIDE restructures skill-augmented agentic RL by separating stable episode-level strategies from locally retrieved tactical know-how, progressively disclosing skills: a visible strategy, a compact tactic menu, and full tactic content loaded only after explicit retrieval. This aims to reduce context bloat and improve skill reuse in LLM agents.

entry.title: World Models for Ocean Engineering: A Critical Review of Maritime Autonomy, Adaptive Latent Prediction, Digital Twins, and Biodiversity Monitoring

author.name: Basma Dokkara, Esteban W. G. Cluab, Luiz M. G. Goncalves, Paolo Spagnolo and Cosimo Distante

entry.summary: This review provides a functional taxonomy of world models for ocean engineering, centering on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures and AdaJEPA-style test-time adaptation within MPC, mapped to navigation, adaptive sampling, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring. It separates demonstrated evidence from speculation, identifies gaps in benchmarks, uncertainty calibration, and safe adaptation, and proposes a research agenda.
