entry.title: Beyond Evidence Coverage: Encoding-Time Access in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Joshua Huang, Ajit Mallavarapu, Elliott Kalt

entry.summary: This study tests whether cache-sharing multi-agent systems that retain all evidence tokens during encoding recover joint-encoding quality, using attention masks over logical workers in frozen Qwen3 and Llama models. Blocking encoding-time access costs 5.6-6.8 F1 points, and exposing earlier supporting paragraphs recovers most of this, while equal-token non-support access provides no benefit.

entry.title: PartPO: Part-Level Policy Optimization for Shape-to-Program Generation

author.name: Hannuo Zhang, Zhixiang Chi, Xuanchen Li, Yiqun Zhou, Yang Wang, Xinxin Zuo

entry.summary: PartPO is a reinforcement learning method for generating structured shape programs from 3D point clouds that exploits the self-describing structure of shape programs. It applies part-level rewards to the corresponding code blocks, category rewards to object names, and shape-level rewards to whole programs, solving the credit assignment problem of scalar execution rewards.

entry.title: Beyond Omission: Measuring Critical-Information Fulfillment of Large Language Models in Bengali and English

author.name: Avijit Roy

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether multilingual trustworthiness metrics based on information omission are sufficient, scoring 1,413 responses across English, Bengali, and code-switched Bengali-English tasks against prespecified required information units. The primary estimand found no detectable omission-rate difference between Bengali and English, but Bengali responses showed other quality deficiencies beyond omission.

entry.title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3

author.name: Mugdha Raje Ashiya, Samarjeet Malik

entry.summary: This paper introduces a five-step audit comparing ML energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays against the learner-independent Bayes-risk floor of their input summaries, applied to KASCADE simulations and 13.8 million measured events plus GRAPES-3 simulations. It can determine whether resolution limits stem from the model or from information loss in the fitted shower parameters. The audit methodology is transferable to other scientific ML applications where feature summaries may cap performance.

entry.title: VistaTree: Question Answering over Long Multimodal Documents with Image-Derived Summary Trees

author.name: Yexiang Cheng, Xiaochen Zheng, David Tokar, Tatyana Y. Doktorova

entry.summary: VistaTree builds a hierarchical summary tree directly from rendered page images of long multimodal documents, enabling an agent to navigate topic-structured nodes and read only relevant pages when content exceeds the context window. It is evaluated on MMLongBench-Doc and LongDocURL for answer quality and retrieval cost.

entry.title: ADEPT: Adaptive Monocular Depth Estimation via Model-In-The-Loop Photometric Tuning with Capture Risk Prediction

author.name: GiHyun Kim, JinMo Yang, Hyung-Sin Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a framework that adapts camera exposure and gain for monocular depth estimation using learned feedback from a frozen depth model, balancing light collection against motion blur during robot motion. A compact predictor scores candidate capture settings via reference-relative disagreement, and a Gaussian-process controller selects settings at deployment without ground truth. It couples camera control with perception quality in a model-in-the-loop design.

entry.title: Grounded in Contact: Reducing Floating and Interpenetration Artifacts with Multimodal Skill-Effect Models

author.name: Siyeon Kim, Mohanraj Devendran Shanthi, Joseph C. Liechty, and Tucker Hermans

entry.summary: The paper studies probabilistic skill-effect models that learn multimodal distributions over object pose changes from partial point clouds and actions, capturing distinct outcome modes like sliding, toppling, and rotating that deterministic or Gaussian models average away. Three model classes (including mixture density networks) are compared, with the goal of reducing floating and interpenetration artifacts in contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Continuous-Time LQR from a Single Discrete-Time Off-Policy Batch

author.name: Chaorui Yao and Yuhua Zhu

entry.summary: This paper develops PhiBE-PI, a drift-only policy iteration algorithm that learns a continuous-time LQR controller with unknown dynamics from a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions, explicitly balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while maintaining stability. It exploits the quadratic LQR structure with one critic and greedy improvement, with theoretical analysis of batch reuse.

entry.title: Training Dynamics of Large State-Transition Models

author.name: Yee Man Choi, Fengchi Wang, Ruiquan Huang

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes whether jointly training input and output embeddings by gradient descent from random initialization yields accurate next-token prediction when embedding dimension is smaller than vocabulary size, in the minimal setting of one-token-context state-transition models. It covers tied and untied embeddings trained with perturbed gradient descent and weight decay on population loss.

entry.title: FlexWAM: Learning Flexible Visual Routing for World Action Models

author.name: Mingyu Mei, Haojie Xu, Zibo Dai, Hongjie Fang, Shirun Tang, Zhengrui Lv, Yang Liu, Chen Guang, Xingyue Zhao, Huiliang Shen, Zaixing He

entry.summary: FlexWAM improves world action models for manipulation by dynamically routing attention across camera views based on current observations, alternating within-view and cross-view attention and using an observation-conditioned router for action prediction. A critic trained with counterfactual view credit calibrates the routing, mimicking how humans shift sensory reliance across manipulation stages.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Correctness: A Surrogate for Confidence Learning in Large Language and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chen Li, Xiaoling Hu, Chao Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues that binary correctness labels are poor supervision for confidence estimation in LLMs and VLMs because occasional errors and consistent failures receive identical labels. It proposes estimating query-level predictive reliability via repeated stochastic generations and combining it with realized correctness in a confidence-learning framework.

entry.title: RadarOSV: Unified 3D Scene and Motion Perception from mmWave Radars

author.name: Yuan Fang, Long Zhuang, Xijia Wei, Jingqi Jiang, Fangzhan Shi, Simon Julier, Kevin Chetty

entry.summary: RadarOSV is claimed as the first radar-only framework jointly predicting 3D occupancy, dynamic object semantics, and ground-relative velocity from raw mmWave data, fusing complementary cascaded imaging radar (fine spatial detail) and single-chip radar (wide velocity range) in unified voxels. Its Polar-to-Cartesian Geometry backbone enables cross-radar fusion for weather-resilient perception.

entry.title: Small data machine learning: the trilemma of low-sample tabular regimes

author.name: Ilya Emelyanov, Dmitrii Dobrydin, Muhammad Hamza, Malak Abid Ali Khan

entry.summary: This empirical study examines the competing demands of model selection, tuning, and evaluation in small tabular datasets using controlled simulations and six public datasets with fixed-configuration SmallGBM and SmallMLP case studies. It quantifies pitfalls such as cross-validation overstating tuning gains on random labels and shows robustness differences under label noise, e.g., much lower ROC-AUC loss for SmallGBM versus a 200-tree XGBoost under flipped labels.

entry.title: GUI-Q: Task-Sensitive Granularity and Relation-Preserving Quantization for GUI Agents

author.name: Tianqi Li, Yang Wang, Xin He, Le Zhang, Yun Liu

entry.summary: GUI-Q is a post-training quantization framework for GUI agents using 4-bit weights that targets preservation of task-relevant response accuracy and instruction-vision spatial relations rather than generic local reconstruction error. The motivation is that small coordinate or relation distortions cause missed clicks and cascading task failures on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: DUET: Dual-MDL Unsupervised Entropy-Trie Segmentation for Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Xiaotian Wang, Youyuan Lin, Zhan Shen, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: DUET is a deterministic unsupervised algorithm for morphological segmentation in extreme low-resource settings, decoupling candidate generation (branching entropy plus recursive paradigm discovery) from ranking via a dual minimum description length criterion. It avoids reliance on annotated data, external resources, or large-corpus statistics.

entry.title: HEART: Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer for ECG Representation Learning

author.name: Junho Song, Jong-Hwan Jang, Joon-Myoung Kwon, Yong-Yeon Jo

entry.summary: HEART is an ECG foundation model using hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts refinement during self-supervised pre-training: a local-level MoE over patch tokens before temporal contextualization and a global-level MoE over context-integrated representations after attention, with token-level Top-1 routing. It targets the mix of repeated cardiac cycles and sparse diagnostic cues in ECGs.

entry.title: MH-RAG-DIVE: Dynamic and Cost-Efficient Multi-Hop RAG Evaluation via Tree-Cached Dialogue Simulation

author.name: Lorenz Brehme, Daniel Hillebrand, Thomas Str\"ohle, Ruth Breu

entry.summary: MH-RAG-DIVE extends dynamic user-simulation-based RAG evaluation to multi-hop, multi-turn conversations using a Context Discoverer that identifies document combinations for generating multi-hop questions. A Conversation Cacher reuses previously simulated turns via tree caching to cut the high computational cost of dynamic evaluation.

entry.title: Toward a Scalable and Adaptive Evaluation Measure for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Emmanouil Sylligardos, Mingyi Huang, John Paparrizos, Pierre Senellart, Paul Boniol

entry.summary: The paper addresses limitations of the VUS measure for time series anomaly detection, which is computationally expensive (hours to evaluate dozens of detectors on a benchmark), proposing a more scalable and adaptive alternative that still accounts for thresholds and range-based anomaly buffering. This enables faster, more practical TSAD evaluation.

entry.title: TamperCert: A Benchmark for Detecting Text Tampering in Degree Certificates

author.name: ChiFung Kwan, Kangzhong Wang, Youqian Zhang, Weijie Chen, Jiaqi Gao, Yongjian Wu, Eugene Yujun Fu, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: TamperCert is a benchmark of 400 real degree certificates from 38 universities, each tampered via 11 publicly available editing methods, to evaluate detection of forged academic credentials, a problem highlighted by real cases such as the 2024 University of Hong Kong forgery discovery. It provides a public resource where none previously existed for this document-forensics task.

entry.title: Autonomous UAV Navigation in an Unknown Environment via Multi-Trajectory Model Predictive Control

author.name: Danilo Saccani, Lorenzo Fagiano

entry.summary: The paper presents multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), a formulation for autonomous UAV navigation with LiDAR in unknown environments, maintaining multiple candidate trajectories that trade off collision safety with uncertain, time-varying obstacles against target exploitation. A hierarchical control layout separates low-level trajectory stabilization from the high-level mt-MPC planner.

entry.title: Empirical Margin Sensitivity: An Interventional Neuron-Level Probe of Post-Trained Medical LLMs

author.name: Aniruddh Shreyas, Aarnav Kembhavi, Minal Moharir

entry.summary: Applies ROME/MEMIT-style weight-space interventions at the granularity of a single MLP down-projection column to medical LLMs, introducing Empirical Margin Sensitivity, which measures logit-margin changes when column coordinate structure is perturbed. The analysis discovers high-EMS anchor columns on MedQA across ten public checkpoints and examines whether components supporting one benchmark also support others.

entry.title: Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control

author.name: Guangyi He, Damir Filipovic, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: This work analyzes random feature neural networks as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives, extending quantitative random-feature approximation theory to feedback control. It derives stability estimates converting policy error into objective error, accounting for both random-feature approximation and objective estimation from finite sample paths.

entry.title: AeroJEPA: A Two-Stage Framework for Aerosol Forecasting with Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning

author.name: Zitong Shuai, Zengliang Zang, Chunlei Shi, Lang Liu, Ning Liu, Yiwen Hu, Dan Niu, Chenyan Zhou, Shangjian Xie

entry.summary: AeroJEPA is a two-stage joint-embedding predictive framework for regional surface PM2.5 forecasting that fuses historical observations, model backgrounds, and meteorology to predict initial states and multi-scale structures. Morphology-guided encoding and joint-embedding supervision improve spatial structure prediction over pointwise regression.

entry.title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture

author.name: Xulong Wang, Yu Zhang, Gaoshan Bi, Menghui Zhou, Simon Jeffery, Max Davis, Sam Maycock, Paul Harris, Po Yang

entry.summary: The paper presents a grower-in-the-loop framework for precision nitrogen fertilization in English winter wheat, combining ML-derived nitrogen-response curves for baseline planning with in-season adaptation via an LLM that incorporates on-farm constraints like weather delays, machinery availability, and budget changes. Evaluation uses data from long-term field experiments.

entry.title: CAST: A Deployed Speech-to-Text Cascade for Closed Captioning of Entertainment Television

author.name: Aditya Mishra, Thanish Bolla, Bidisha Sharma, Balaji Pitchaikannu, Surbhi Sinha, Anup Kotalwar

entry.summary: CAST is a production speech-to-text cascade for closed captioning of entertainment TV, combining frozen Whisper large-v3 with hierarchical voice activity detection that re-examines rejected segments to reduce hallucination and repetition. It tackles content dense in music, effects, accents, and crosstalk, where segmentation quality matters as much as the acoustic model. The paper reports real deployment experience, which is valuable for applied ASR.

entry.title: When Does Overriding the Majority Vote Help?

author.name: Terry Ma, Aidan Zhang

entry.summary: This empirical study examines when additional reasoning, executed programs, or cross-model reasoning should override a majority-vote answer on 150 competition math questions with three open reasoning models. It finds that when the vote is wrong, the correct answer is often absent from the original responses, that same-model additional reasoning rarely overrides, and that executed programs correct more errors than they introduce at all thresholds. Practical guidance for test-time compute allocation.

entry.title: Flood forecasting using a physics-guided conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model

author.name: Omar Sallam, David Coe, Jeremy Feinstein, Hugo Torres, Sofia Sahagun Covarrubias, Eugene Yan

entry.summary: The authors train a conditional DDPM to forecast 30 m water-depth fields over four days for the Des Plaines River watershed, using SynxFlow shallow-water simulations of 113 historical storms and optional coarse hydrodynamic conditioning. Each forecast is a 20-member ensemble, and coarse conditioning reduces ensemble-mean RMSE at far lower cost than full 2D SWE solvers.

entry.title: Tensor Recovery with Heterogeneous Mode Structures

author.name: Zhixin Huang, Ziyuan Chen, Fang Yao, Ying Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified convex framework for tensor recovery that treats each tensor mode according to its own structure: smooth indexing domains get local kernel weighting while retained modes can receive low-rank, group-sparse, graph-Laplacian, or autoregressive regularizations in flexible combinations. An HM-ADMM algorithm separates penalties into tractable updates, and the authors derive deterministic oracle inequalities and high-probability error bounds. This removes the usual one-size-fits-all structural assumption across modes.

entry.title: Empirical Limits of Risk-Averse Reinforcement Learning versus Gas-Aware Routing in Deterministic DeFi Execution

author.name: Sri Sairam Gautam B

entry.summary: The paper builds an end-to-end DeFi execution environment calibrated to live Uniswap V2 reserves, EIP-1559 gas dynamics, and real swap events, then trains a PPO agent with a CVaR penalty across risk-aversion levels, benchmarked against a gas-aware oracle. It documents a reproducible specification-gaming path, offering a cautionary case study for risk-sensitive RL.

entry.title: PhoneQC: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Order-Level Smartphone Trade-in Inspection

author.name: Zihan Deng, Xinpei Lin, Du Tiantian, and Lequan Yu

entry.summary: PhoneQC is a benchmark of 335 iPhone trade-in orders with six camera views and diagnostic screenshots, scoring complete order-level staff appraisal forms rather than single defects. Findings show current multimodal LLMs perform poorly (appearance fill near 0.25) and closed models gain only on answered orders, so human appraisal remains necessary. It exposes a gap between impressive single-image capabilities and reliable end-to-end business workflow automation.

entry.title: ReMiC: Representation-Driven Token Pruning for 3D VLMs via Minimax Hierarchical Clustering

author.name: Bangfeng Yan, Chaoning Zhang, Yuanhao Liu, Pengcheng Zheng, Mengyuan Li, Wei Dong, Sheng Zheng, Yang Yang

entry.summary: ReMiC is a training-free token pruning framework for 3D vision-language models that formulates pruning as minimax hierarchical clustering, treating retained tokens as prototypes that minimize the representation gap from the full multi-view token set. This reduces the heavy inference cost of long visual token sequences in 3D scene understanding.

entry.title: VICA: Video Contextual Agreement for AIGC Video Detection and Localization

author.name: Runheng Lin, Jialiang Shen, Jiyang Zheng, Ruiqi Liu, Zonglin He, Yu Yao, Huajie Chen, Chris Russell, Runqi Lin

entry.summary: Proposes VICA, a unified framework for detecting and localizing AI-generated video content that masks individual video regions and uses a frozen video-language model to measure disagreement between regions and their spatiotemporal context. It addresses limitations of holistic temporal detectors and region-only localization approaches. Socially relevant work amid rapid growth of AIGC video generation.

entry.title: Simple Baselines for Fetal Brain Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

author.name: Hongjia Yang, Mingxuan Liu, Yingqi Hao, Xiaotian Hu, Siyao Li, Xuguang Bai, Fenglin Jia, Yijin Li, Yifei Chen, Zihan Li, Juncheng Zhu, Jing Liu, Yi Liao, Ziyu Li, Haibo Qu, Qiyuan Tian

entry.summary: Proposes FetalBUAD, an unsupervised anomaly detection framework for fetal brain MRI based on voxel-level brain age estimation, using a multi-task network predicting global brain age, voxel-level age maps, and segmentation to build an internal biological reference independent of noisy gestational age labels. Uncertainty-aware voxel-level age gap maps enable anomaly localization, validated on 1,317 internal volumes plus external data. Medically meaningful advance for pathology-scarce pediatric imaging.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Guided Dual-Branch Learning for LiDAR Anomalous Object Detection

author.name: Guanyu Jiang, Junjie Cao, Jinshan Pan, Zhixun Su

entry.summary: This work proposes Structured Residual Reasoning (SRR) for LiDAR anomaly detection, combining semantic discrimination with reconstruction-based consistency checks by extracting anomaly evidence from residual structure across feature channels, time, and geometry. The authors show the two perspectives capture fundamentally complementary signals. Detecting unexpected objects is directly relevant to autonomous driving safety.

entry.title: CAR3T: Generalizable Calibration-Guided Reference-View Attention Reuse for Multi-View 3D Transformers

author.name: Lan Wei, Haosong Peng, Sicheng Tian, Tianyu Qi, Wenchao Xu, Lei Xue, Yufeng Zhan, Yuanqing Xia

entry.summary: Reduces the quadratic attention cost of multi-view 3D reconstruction transformers by reusing attention outputs across views, guided by a calibration-aware mechanism that decides which layers are suitable for reuse given the input, accounting for downstream feature changes. This exploits redundancy in global cross-view aggregation.

entry.title: From Pairwise to Collective: Encoder Collections Make Unpaired Vision-Language Alignment Reliable

author.name: Xuanhua Yin, Shunqi Mao, Chuanzhi Xu, Boyu Wei, Wei Guo, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: ConsensusAlign performs vision-text alignment without paired image-text data by leveraging collections of encoders: since all encoders of one modality embed the same items, within-modality correspondences are known exactly and can supervise the hidden cross-modal map. Pooling each modality into a shared space makes unpaired retrieval and zero-shot classification more reliable than independent pairwise fitting.

entry.title: Definition-Guided In-Context Learning for Zero-Shot Spoken Language Understanding

author.name: Neeraj Agrawala, Sriram Ganapathy

entry.summary: DG-ICL fine-tunes speech-text models so that natural-language definitions of labels, rather than fixed label names or demonstration examples, drive zero-shot adaptation to new SLU taxonomies. Randomized dynamic definitions decouple semantic categories from lexical names, improving multi-modal generalization and scaling.

entry.title: AlignHand: Multi-View Hand Reconstruction from a Frozen Monocular Prior

author.name: Zhilu Yang, Kun Yang, Shiyan Wang, Anqi Xu, Xinran Huang, Yizheng Jiao, Huan Yang, Rolandos Alexandros Potamias

entry.summary: AlignHand aligns and fuses independently predicted monocular 3D hand meshes across multiple views by calibrating cross-view joint observations, estimating their reliability, and refining with pixel-aligned fusion, all on top of a frozen monocular reconstruction prior. It resolves scale, placement, and articulation disagreements between views.

entry.title: SpatialDuet: Bayesian task routing between a metric expert and a geometry expert for spatial intelligence

author.name: Duy Tran Thanh

entry.summary: SpatialDuet pairs a metric-trained spatial VLM with a geometry-encoder VLM, routing tasks via a Bayesian router so each frozen model handles the spatial tasks it excels at, augmented with training-free modules on the metric expert. This avoids training a single generalist small model for all 3D spatial reasoning on constrained hardware. A pragmatic composition approach for embodied and wearable devices.

entry.title: OAT3D: A Generative Model for 3D Shape- and Resolution-Free Structural Topology Optimization

author.name: Hongrui Chen, Kittipong Thiamchaiboonthawee, Zhen Wei, Amin Heyrani Nobari, Faez Ahmed

entry.summary: OAT3D is a generative model for high-resolution, shape- and resolution-free 3D structural topology optimization, addressing the scarcity of large-scale 3D training data caused by costly finite-element solvers. It targets diverse boundary conditions and problem scales beyond prior 2D-focused data-driven approaches.

entry.title: Inspect Before You Decide: Evidence-Guided Visual Search for Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Peng Chen, Chao Huang, Yangyang Liu, Maodong Wu, Jinyi Xu, Mingbo Yang, Yunkang Cao, Fangjun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes EVAD, an evidence-guided visual search framework where multimodal LLMs actively acquire and examine fine-grained visual evidence for industrial anomaly reasoning. It starts with a global assessment of candidate anomalous regions, then applies MCTS-guided exploration to gather and verify diagnostic evidence before deciding.

entry.title: Ref2Light: From One Image to Interactive Glasses-Free 3D Characters

author.name: Hanzhong Zhang, Haoyang Wang, Siyang Song

entry.summary: Ref2Light is a feed-forward framework that maps a single A-pose character illustration plus continuous pose and expression controls directly to light-field animation for glasses-free 3D displays, without per-character 3D reconstruction, rigging, or test-time optimization. It decomposes synthesis into cached static identity features, view-dependent parallax, and control-driven articulation for rapid character switching.

entry.title: ApexID: Hierarchical Learning for Multi-Species Animal Re-Identification

author.name: Seifeldin Elkerdany, Mohamed ElBassat, Gamal Abouelhamd, Assem Elkady, Jana Ghoneim, Matin Mahmood, Abigail Allen Martin, Gerard de Melo, Antonio Rueda-Toicen

entry.summary: ApexID introduces a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss combining global identity discrimination with balanced animal-category supervision for cross-species animal re-identification. Using 132,533 curated images from 19 datasets, it achieves 64.89% average Rank-1 accuracy with ConvNeXt-Small and shows strong generalization, including on elephants absent from training.

entry.title: How Should a Home Robot Update Its Memories When Human Routines Change?

author.name: Oliver Wang, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: The authors simulate households where a resident's routine changes and reverts (e.g., getting sick and recovering) to study how home robots should maintain object-location memories. They find that a simple rule keeping all observed locations outperforms summary-only LLM memories, and that letting the LLM read raw sighting history helps, highlighting limits of compressed language-model memory under nonstationarity.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap between Continual Learning and Test-Time Adaptation with Domain Preview

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Li Combeau, Nicolas Michel, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: The paper introduces continual learning with domain preview (CL-P), a new setting combining continual learning and continual test-time adaptation in which both training and test data suffer from distribution shift, with a preview phase for adapting to a future domain. It benchmarks mainstream CL and TTA methods under this unified setup, exposing gaps in current approaches.

entry.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets

author.name: Bohan Zeng, Kaixin Zhu, Yifan Yang, Dongge Yu, Zihao Wu, Yifan Dai, Zhou Liu, Junbo Niu, Xiaochen Ma, Shiran Ge, Zimo Meng, Junzhu Liang, Huanyao Zhang, Jinhang Liu, Tianqi Xiao, Jinhao Zhang, Tianyi Bai, Zhixiong Zeng, Penghao Zhao, Yuanbo Peng, Key Zhang, and Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: This work introduces DivDynBench, a benchmark for rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing and trajectory constraints. The authors compare three generation paradigms with LLMs and propose an Agentic Motion Framework for animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions.

entry.title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering

author.name: Xu Yuan, Pangjing Wu, Wenqi Fan, and Qing Li

entry.summary: RenderEmbed proposes unification before encoding: heterogeneous inputs (text, image, composed queries) are rendered into a common visual substrate and encoded by a VLM, after which progressive hierarchical anchor encoding produces compact retrieval embeddings. This enables end-to-end joint optimization and supervision transfer across input configurations.

entry.title: Thermal-Guided Low-Light UAV Image Enhancement: A Reliability-Aware Guidance Network and a Unified Benchmark

author.name: Zhicheng Zhao, Yu Wang, Jiangong Xu, Lixiang Xu, Chenglong Li, and Jin Tang

entry.summary: The paper proposes RMGNet, a thermal-guided low-light image enhancement network for nighttime UAV perception that models the reliability of thermal cues under weak optical-thermal alignment, applying region-specific restoration instead of uniform enhancement. It also contributes a unified benchmark for this task setting.

entry.title: A New Perspective on ANN-to-SNN Conversion: Hardware-Aligned Multi-Threshold Neuron Dynamics for Neuromorphic Inference

author.name: Shaohong Gu, Jiyuan Zhang, Yimeng Shan, Chenxiao Dou, Wei Hua, Malu Zhang, Honglin Cao, Choonghyun Lee, Jingwei Chen

entry.summary: PRIME is a hardware-aligned multi-threshold spiking neuron framework for ANN-to-SNN conversion that reduces the accuracy gap without the redundancy of more timesteps or overly complex dynamics. It redesigns neuron dynamics around potential-residual integration for efficient neuromorphic inference.

entry.title: NNS-GS: Non-Local Neural Scattering for Relightable Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Shiyu Liang, Yang Gao, Lili Wang, Aimin Hao, Beibei Wang

entry.summary: NNS-GS enables relightable 3D assets of translucent objects by learning non-local subsurface scattering together with geometry-guided local reflection within a Gaussian splatting framework. The scattering module models how illumination from light-visible surface regions in light space contributes to shading points in view space.

entry.title: GeLiFiSH: Recursive LiDAR Keypoint Estimation with Ground and Moving Object Segmentation

author.name: Nikolaos Stathoulopoulos and George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: GeLiFiSH is a learning-free filter that recursively estimates persistent LiDAR keypoints at scan rate on a rolling voxel map, addressing repeatability across sessions, ghost trails from dynamic objects, and ground-reference inconsistency via sequential hypothesis testing with ground and moving-object segmentation. It targets robust registration and loop closure for long-term LiDAR SLAM.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Compositional Continual Learning for Robot Manipulation with Gated Low-Rank Experts

author.name: Nilay Kushawaha, Abdalla Swikir, and Fares Abu-Dakka

entry.summary: Presents a continual learning framework for manipulation where each skill is a Progressive Neural Network expert, with LoRA modules and learnable per-parent gates on lateral connections to attenuate transfer paths while cutting parameter costs. A frozen local LLM decomposes natural-language instructions into sub-tasks, routes them to experts, and requests new experts when the skill library is insufficient.

entry.title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI

author.name: Gizem Karagoz, Tanir Ozcelebi, Nirvana Meratnia

entry.summary: The paper formalizes alignment-based XAI evaluation as a structured configuration space covering ground-truth representations, metric families, soft versus hard formulations, and thresholding strategies, then studies how these design choices bias conclusions. It reveals that popular attribution-alignment metrics are implicitly sensitive to evaluator configuration.

entry.title: Bridging Continuous-Time MAPF and Industrial AGV Fleet Coordination with Lazy Priority-Based Search

author.name: Federico Signorile, Raffaele Carli, Alessandro Bertogli, Roberto Olmi, Sven Koenig, Mariagrazia Dotoli

entry.summary: The work formalizes AGV-MAPF_R-CTC, a continuous-time configuration-space variant of multi-agent path finding on roadmaps with precomputed conflicts, enabling reuse of MAPF_R solvers for industrial AGV fleets. It revisits continuous-time priority-based search to identify boundary conditions needed by its SIPP low-level planner under priority-induced constraints.

entry.title: UMAMI: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Evidence-Grounded Dietary Decisions

author.name: Safal Thapaliya, Jiatan Huang, Debapriya Chatterjee, Yanfang Ye, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: UMAMI is a multimodal dataset and benchmark linking food images with nutrient profiles and individual intake histories to evaluate evidence-grounded dietary decisions. It targets two coupled challenges: visually similar foods with different nutrient profiles, and nutrient-rule satisfaction not implying relevance to a person's intake. This enables more realistic evaluation of multimodal assistants for health and nutrition.

entry.title: Deep Negative Binomial Autoregression for Sparse Spatio-Temporal Counts: Estimation and Predictive Distribution Bounds

author.name: Hsin-Hsiung Huang

entry.summary: DeepNB-STAR is a negative binomial autoregressive model whose log-mean and log-size are produced by a deep ReLU network over temporal and neighborhood summaries, fitted by maximum likelihood. The paper proves oracle inequalities for Hellinger risk without mixing assumptions, matching lower bounds for a Hoelder subclass, and h-step predictive distribution bounds, all under arbitrary dependence between sites. It provides statistical guarantees for deep models of overdispersed count data.

entry.title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs

author.name: Hai-Xiao Wang and Xiucai Ding

entry.summary: The paper develops a method for spectral embedding and clustering under strong high-dimensional noise by first denoising pairwise distances with cross-fitted projections, then selecting a neighborhood radius and building a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates recover the latent geometry. It targets settings where curved or concentric clusters cannot be separated by centers and accumulated coordinate noise makes raw distances unreliable. The approach comes with theoretical support.

entry.title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks; airborne drone detection; and a national lab's AI science benchmark

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter covers AscendGYM, a kernel-optimization benchmark for Huawei Ascend NPUs built by Chinese researchers to enable AI-driven kernel development under export controls, which Clark frames as enabling a form of recursive self-improvement for China's chip stack. The issue also surveys airborne drone detection systems and a national lab's AI-for-science benchmark.

entry.title: Bayesian Network Fusion of Large Language Models for Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Rasoul Amirzadeh, Dhananjay Thiruvady, Fatemeh Shiri

entry.summary: BNLF is a late-fusion framework that combines predictions from FinBERT, RoBERTa, and BERTweet via probabilistic nodes in a Bayesian network for sentiment analysis, improving transparency and consistency relative to single models. Evaluation across multiple domains shows gains while avoiding costly fine-tuning.

entry.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations

author.name: Wenrui Zhou, Jiashun Liu, Sujie Hu, Bang Liu, Ling Pan

entry.summary: SlidesWeaver is a hybrid multi-agent system combining programmatic (editable) and image-based (visually rich) presentation generation, coordinating language and vision agents via shared deck- and slide-level states with staged multimodal commitment and diffusion-based composition planning. It addresses the editability-versus-richness tradeoff in slide generation.

entry.title: REMORA: A Voice-First Memory Assistant for Grounded Personal Recall and Independent Living

author.name: Bilal Jawaid, Muhammad Maaz Uddin, Osama Farooqi, Saadia Karim

entry.summary: REMORA is a voice-first assistant that converts consented speech into structured memory records to help people with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's, or age-related memory decline maintain independent living. It targets the gap where consequential spoken information (dosage intervals, moved deadlines) is never written down and conventional aids add cognitive load. The work is a socially meaningful applied system addressing assistive healthcare needs.

entry.title: 5G NR Sensing of Robotic Arm Motion in Indoor Factory Environments

author.name: Neeraj Varshney, Anuraag Bodi, Steve Blandino, Jian Wang, Camillo Gentile, and Nada Golmie

entry.summary: This paper develops a framework for monostatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) tracking of robotic arm kinematics in factories, combining a quasi-deterministic channel model from high-resolution measurements with hierarchical kinematic transformations and the standardized 3GPP indoor-factory channel model. Using 5G NR positioning reference signals as sensing waveforms, it evaluates performance in sparse and dense clutter. It is a solid systems/communications engineering contribution toward industrial ISAC.

entry.title: Scale-Aware Reference Attention for Mannequin-to-Model Gown Generation

author.name: Guang Yang, Fengchen Liu

entry.summary: SARA makes diffusion-transformer image editing aware of the zoom level of reference photos, biasing output attention toward references at similar magnification and leveraging macro fabric photos to preserve fine details like sequins and lace. It is trained and evaluated on Kiss3000, a new dataset of high-resolution gown images. This addresses a concrete failure of reference-based editing: loss of close-up detail.

entry.title: ROSE-SAM3: Response-Oriented Prompt Selection for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation

author.name: Yanghui Song, Chengfu Yang, Yongpeng Wen, Zhanxuan Hu, Wei Lu, Qi Ming, Nanqing Liu, Heng-Chao Li

entry.summary: ROSE-SAM3 is a training-free framework that selects class descriptions for open-vocabulary segmentation of remote-sensing imagery by examining frozen SAM 3 responses on unlabeled target images, screening candidates for coverage while protecting reliable native prompts, then using a DAG search to build a compact PromptBank per class. It addresses prompt sensitivity in a domain where class-name prompts miss varied object appearances. Practical, well-motivated, and requires no retraining.

entry.title: Seeing Beyond Pixels: Radar Feature Generation from Images and Sparse Returns

author.name: Hongyu Zhou, Yubo Peng, Luping Xiang, and Kun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes VRTG, a method that generates task-relevant radar features from camera images plus sparse radar returns, reducing the need for dense radar representations in camera-radar fusion. It selects informative radar points using visual object cues and builds calibrated one-to-one visual-radar associations to refine object ranges.

entry.title: The Value of Labels in Data Selection for Least Squares

author.name: Evan Borodow

entry.summary: A theoretical analysis of core-set style data selection for ordinary least squares, determining optimal worst-case excess-loss ratios for selectors that may or may not see labels before choosing rows. With normalized leverage bounded by kappa, a label-blind selector achieves d*kappa/n while a label-aware selector achieves between d*kappa/(2n) and d*kappa*Lambda_d/n, characterizing the value of label access.

entry.title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch

author.name: Vajira Thambawita, P{\aa}l Halvorsen, Ole-Christoffer Granmo

entry.summary: torchtsetlin reimplements the Tsetlin machine family (vanilla, weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional, segmentation) as native PyTorch modules, making automata a tensor buffer compatible with standard device movement, state saving, and mini-batch updates. Its core technique is a batched formulation of Type I and Type II feedback, integrating gradient-free rule-learning machines into the deep learning ecosystem.

entry.title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows

author.name: Maedeh Saberi, Hugo Franca, Maziyar Jalaal, Safa Jamali

entry.summary: This paper systematically investigates the RheOFormer neural operator on steady Bingham channel flow, a challenging viscoplastic setting with yield surfaces and discontinuous gradients. The authors isolate how dataset structure, value range, and input representation govern interpolation and extrapolation, and propose data-efficient remedies. It matters for understanding when neural-operator surrogates fail on nonsmooth physics.

entry.title: An LLM-Assisted Multi-Objective AutoML Framework for Efficient Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Ailin Barzegar, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: This work combines a locally hosted Llama 3.1 8B model with multi-objective optimization to automate design of intrusion detection models that balance accuracy, latency, and model size for IoT and EV charging deployments. The LLM analyzes dataset profiles to generate a bounded, validated policy guiding data balancing and search initialization. It targets the practical constraints of security ML on resource-limited edge devices.

entry.title: Decision models for UAVBench and the viability of edge deployment

author.name: Matthew Michelson, Goran Muric, Adrien Bibal, Steven Minton

entry.summary: This study examines whether small language models benchmarked on UAVBench, a drone decision-making benchmark, can actually run usefully on edge hardware. It evaluates 24 configurations on a Mac to screen candidates before physical-device testing, covering generative models and structured decision models. The work connects benchmark performance to realistic deployment constraints for onboard drone reasoning.

entry.title: A Hybrid Multi-Goal Path Planning Framework for Powered Wheelchairs in Dynamic Environments: From Simulation to Real-World Validation

author.name: Damla Leblebicio\u{g}lu, Ege \"Ozg\"ul, Ta\c{s}k{\i}n Pad{\i}r

entry.summary: A hybrid planner for autonomous powered wheelchairs combining TSP-based global task ordering, potential-field guidance, and local RRT or A* planners with direction-aware, extended-neighborhood search. The TSP-PF-RRT and TSP-PF-A* methods are validated across normal, crowded, and dynamic simulated environments with real-world validation.

entry.title: When AI Should Not Decide: Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability in Automated Job Interviews

author.name: Khalid Adnan Alsayed

entry.summary: The paper introduces ESDSA, an assessment combining criterion-level evidence classification, deterministic quotation traceability, and stability checks across linguistically equivalent variants, to determine whether automated interview recommendations are supported by sufficient evidence. Tested on 540 synthetic responses across software engineering, customer support, and operations, the integrated version achieved 85.19% actionable coverage in held-out testing.

entry.title: Decoding Frozen Vision Representations for Training-Free Few-Shot Pineapple Detection

author.name: Manfred Gonzalez-Hernandez, Danny Xie-Li, Fabian Fallas-Moya, Camile Lendering, Joaqu\'in Figueira, Erkut Akdag, Giacomo D'Amicantonio and Egor Bondarev

entry.summary: Presents a training-free few-shot object detector that decodes dense features from frozen vision foundation models using a whitened foreground-background direction from support images, without fine-tuning or learned heads. On aerial pineapple imagery it outperforms PET-DINO and GeCo2 at all support sizes, and shows predicted relative depth reaches 92% of RGB performance with DINOv2 at K=40. Demonstrates how far training-free decoding of frozen representations can go in hard agricultural domains.

entry.title: CAMA: Calibrated Anti-Collapse Marginal Alignment for Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jinho Kang, Yunhui Guo

entry.summary: Analyzes why entropy minimization fails in test-time adaptation of vision-language models under feature compression caused by image corruption, then proposes CAMA, an objective maximizing batch mutual information to prevent class collapse. The work connects the failure mode to a concrete remedy for TTA of VLMs under distribution shift. Useful for robust deployment of CLIP-style models.

entry.title: Walks2Maps: Learning Indoor Geometry from Crowdsourced Wi-Fi RTT and Motion Trajectories

author.name: Enguang Fan, Binh Minh Tran, Fulin Wang, Jiaxi Li, Klara Nahrstedt

entry.summary: Walks2Maps reconstructs shared metric indoor maps from crowdsourced smartphone Wi-Fi round-trip-time and motion data without floor plans, surveyed access-point coordinates, or position labels. It jointly estimates pedestrian trajectories, AP locations, and stride scales, using an asymmetric range loss to handle multipath-induced delay excess. Validation covered 22 phone trajectories, demonstrating a scalable approach to indoor mapping.

entry.title: When and Where to Transfer: Learning Transferable Historical Contexts for Short-History Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Huiling Yuan, Yize Wang, Guodong Li

entry.summary: Proposes HiCT, a hierarchical context-transfer framework that adaptively weights source groups and historical periods to decide where and when to transfer knowledge for short-history multivariate time series forecasting. Provides a target excess-risk bound and shows competitive empirical results.

entry.title: Beyond Full-Context Accuracy: Context-Marginalized Evaluation of Test-Time Structure-Aware Inference in EEG-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Ke Xiao, Banghua Yang, Yingjie Li, Hang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Context-Marginalized Retrieval Evaluation (CMRE), which repeatedly evaluates each query in sampled contexts to separate structural exploitability from context robustness in EEG-to-image retrieval, addressing the dependence of test-time structure-aware inference on query-set composition. Applied to THINGS-EEG2 with leave-one-subject-out evaluation across methods. This is a methodological contribution to more honest evaluation of test-time inference techniques.

entry.title: DeCo: Decoupled Traffic State Modeling with Cross-Variable Coordination

author.name: Du Yin, Lindong Xie, Xiachong Lin, Ruiyi Yang, Yifan Duan, Hao Xue, Flora Salim

entry.summary: DeCo is a traffic forecasting framework that trains dedicated forecasters for flow, occupancy, and speed, then estimates residual corrections by jointly leveraging their coupled dynamics, capturing congestion onset and dissipation. It addresses the limitation that unified models struggle to handle each variable's distinct spatiotemporal patterns. The work is relevant to smart-city and transportation applications.

entry.title: When Local Semantics Disagree: Learning to Detect Fake News through Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Zeheng Wang, Hao Zhang, Yige Wang, Xi Xiao, Hao Xu

entry.summary: DMIL is a dual-branch multiple instance learning framework that formulates multimodal fake news detection as weakly supervised learning, capturing fine-grained local cross-modal inconsistencies (sentiment-scene mismatches, object-level manipulations) rather than coarse global similarity, while modeling domain-specific variation in how conflicts manifest. This improves generalization and interpretability for vision-language misinformation detection. The topic is socially important though methodologically familiar.

entry.title: ReCoRain: Reliability-Coupled Content and Noise Conditioning for Event-Guided Video Deraining

author.name: Runzhe Li, Zhaocheng Yu, Binbin Song, Kui Jiang, Junjun Jiang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: ReCoRain is an event-guided residual video diffusion framework for video deraining that couples temporal content transfer and noise correlation through a common assessment of correspondence reliability, combining RGB appearance, interval-event evidence, and forward-backward motion consistency. It prevents incorrect matches from transferring unrelated content in diffusion restoration. A technically focused contribution to video restoration.

entry.title: Data-Driven Trajectory Prediction via Probabilistic Modes and Constrained Optimization

author.name: Danyang Li, Ana Theodora Balaci, Matthew Cleaveland, Roberto Tron

entry.summary: ProMo-CoOp is a two-stage multimodal trajectory prediction framework for autonomous driving that clusters trajectories into behavioral modes with a Gaussian Mixture Model and then generates one candidate trajectory per mode via convex optimization constrained to match observations. This combines probabilistic intent modeling with physically feasible, optimization-based prediction.

entry.title: Dynamic Spectrum Re-parameterized Convolution for Cost-free Image Enhancement

author.name: Zhiyan Zhou, Hailong Yan, Hanlin Liu, Yongrui Zhang, Xiangtao Zhang, Le Zhang

entry.summary: DSRC is a plug-and-play convolution module that learns task-adaptive frequency-band responses during training via high/low-pass modulation and residual branches, then analytically fuses all training-time components into a single standard kernel for inference. It delivers consistent gains on low-light enhancement, underwater enhancement, and super-resolution at no extra inference cost.

entry.title: Frozen by the Mean: Early Temporal Guidance Unfreezes Motion in Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Xuanhua Yin, Boyu Wei, Chengkun Yue, Shunqi Mao, Chuanzhi Xu, Wei Guo, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: THAW is a training-free method that strengthens motion in video diffusion by adding a separately weighted temporal residual during an early denoising window, avoiding the color shifts and saturation of raising scalar classifier-free guidance. It reuses CFG's two predictions with no extra network evaluations and improves motion at matched cost.

entry.title: ArrythML-II: An Optimized TinyML Framework for ECG Arrhythmia Detection and Multi-Class Beat Classification on Wearable Devices

author.name: Nagarajan S, Kurian Polachan

entry.summary: ArrythML-II is an optimized TinyML framework for on-device ECG arrhythmia detection and six-class beat classification, using systematic hyperparameter optimization and a custom joint scoring of detection performance, thresholds, and model size. Models are INT8-quantized and deployed on a custom battery-operated single-lead ECG device based on a PSoC 6 microcontroller.

entry.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification

author.name: Omm Swarup and Shrishail M. Hiremath

entry.summary: The paper investigates learned semantic representations as compact alternatives to high-dimensional IQ representations for automatic modulation classification, evaluating dimensions from 4 to 64. It finds a 16-dimensional representation offers the best trade-off between classification performance, noise robustness, and representation size for semantic communication.

entry.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes

author.name: Na Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a PointNeXt-based adapter model for associating construction-site defects with the correct BIM components by aligning site image crops, point cloud patches, and BIM attributes (identity, geometry, material, installation stage) into component-level inspection windows. PointNeXt learns local geometry deviations while the adapter fuses design-model attributes for defect-to-component linkage.

entry.title: Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation for Synthetic Segmentation Data

author.name: Chunming He, Dingming Zhang, Jifan Zhang, Yuhan Dong, Longxiang Tang, Youwei Pang, Xiaoqi Zhao, Fengyang Xiao, Sina Farsiu

entry.summary: This paper proposes TCDA, a method that scores synthetic segmentation images by how much class-specific visual detail they carry in labeled regions, using response changes of a small task reference model before and after blurring. The score ranks synthetic candidates and guides local edits or repairs, improving the training value of synthetic data for segmentation. It focuses on selective allocation of detail rather than uniform generation quality.

entry.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models

author.name: Ning Ning

entry.summary: The paper introduces a twisted block particle filter that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact blockwise change of measure at resampling, tilting one offspring per block while keeping the transition kernel unchanged. The authors prove the correction exactly preserves the finite-particle normalizer expectation, separating guided-sampling effects from blocking-induced approximation, and derive exact conditional local moments with a one-step central limit result. The method targets weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models.

entry.title: OmniDecisionBench: Evaluating and Benchmarking the Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models

author.name: Tianxiang Gao and Jinzhe Li and Yue Zhou and Dandan Guo and Qi Wang and Diana Inkpen and Yuan Wu and Yi Chang

entry.summary: OmniDecisionBench is a large-scale benchmark (45 datasets, ~193k records) comparing fast-typed multimodal decision models against general VLMs across five capability families and twelve angles, scoring accuracy and probability calibration, plus single-factor diagnostics. Findings show System One models lead discrete tasks but strengths depend on angle and metric.

entry.title: Micro Operational Robustness of LLMs on Code Generation

author.name: Debalina Ghosh Paul, Hong Zhu, Ian Bayley

entry.summary: The paper proposes scenario domain analysis, a method for measuring how sensitive LLM code generation is to small natural-language variations in task descriptions, formalizing the minimal perturbation that flips outputs to incorrect. The authors prove theoretical properties and apply the method to evaluate LLM robustness for coding.

entry.title: 3D-EMCAD: Efficient Multi-scale Convolutional Attention Decoding for Volumetric Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Iftakhar Hossain, Israt Jahan Sinthia and Md. Hadiur Rahman Khan

entry.summary: The paper extends the lightweight 2D EMCAD decoder to 3D volumetric brain tumor segmentation by converting operations to 3D and using group normalization for small batch sizes. It provides a controlled comparison of five decoders under an identical encoder to isolate decoder impact. The work targets strong segmentation accuracy at low computational cost.

entry.title: DiRGeo: Learning Directional Geometry of Visual Representations

author.name: Muhammad Ahtesham, Xin Zhong

entry.summary: DiRGeo learns directional (asymmetric) geometry over frozen visual representations using Randers geometry, trained via self-supervised contrast on ordered image trajectories without labels. Techniques like sphere-tangent correction separate learned directional structure from normalization artifacts. Experiments across 17 visual processes and three encoder families show consistent directional discrimination beyond attractor-based explanations.

entry.title: Sub-Gaussian HDLSS Principal Component Analysis: High-Probability Theory and Numerical Evidence for NRM, CDM, and Block Noise Reduction

author.name: Yugo Nakayama

entry.summary: The paper develops high-probability theory for PCA when dimension far exceeds sample size under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model, decomposing the dual sample covariance into a finite-rank score matrix, isotropic bulk shift, and bounded remainder. It clarifies when sequential noise reduction targets a later-spike-subtracted oracle versus when an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction, and analyzes cross-data-matrix sample splitting. Reproducible simulations support the theory.

entry.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation

author.name: Jannik Graebner and Ryne Beeson

entry.summary: The paper trains neural networks to predict accurate initial costates for indirect optimal control, enabling onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation in the challenging cislunar region of the Earth-Moon system. Recovery trajectories are built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm suitable for constrained flight computers.

entry.title: The Retry Tax: Why Static Same-Task Retries Can Cost More per Completion

author.name: Wei-Jung Huang

entry.summary: This theoretical analysis shows that a static retry policy for AI agents, which stops at verified success or an attempt cap without passing feedback, shifts the serving mix toward harder tasks so that cost per completion is at least as high as one-shot serving. It distinguishes average cost per completion from marginal cost per additional completion using survivor-selection arguments.

entry.title: Towards Edge Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Antimicrobial Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis

author.name: Nishat Tasnim, Faisal Ahmed, Rokan Uddin Faruqui

entry.summary: The authors present a lightweight machine learning pipeline for predicting antimicrobial resistance in tuberculosis from genomic data, targeting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in low- and middle-income countries. This addresses the gap between computationally heavy AMR prediction pipelines and the infrastructure realities of the clinics that need them most. High practical relevance for global health.

entry.title: Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation via Topology-Aware Distillation and Progressive Kinematic Reasoning

author.name: Kanglei Zhou, Zikai Hao, Liyuan Wang, Xiaohui Liang

entry.summary: The paper addresses hand pose estimation under structural incompleteness (missing fingers or parts), where standard fully-articulated methods fail. The authors construct IncNYU, a physiologically constrained benchmark simulating structural incompleteness, and propose topology-aware distillation with progressive kinematic reasoning for robust prediction from partial observations. Relevant to inclusive interfaces and prosthetics.

entry.title: DriveTTO: Understanding Search and Selection in Test-Time Trajectory Optimization for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Xinyao Rao, Zecheng Tang, Zheyuan Lai, Liuxuan Sun, Minjun Yu, Xun Cao, Wei Li

entry.summary: DriveTTO is a training-free test-time method that improves end-to-end autonomous driving by searching around a planner's native trajectory proposals and validating refinements with a frozen scorer. It branches over planner proposals and vehicle control perturbations, blending poses at matching times to find better maneuvers in difficult scenes.

entry.title: Ego-HMB: Human Motion Bridging from Egocentric Images via A Motion Bridge Diffusion Model

author.name: Gaoge Han, Yongkang Cheng, Shaoli Huang, Jing Zhang, Mingming Gong, Fakhri Karray, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: Ego-HMB introduces a new task of generating coherent 3D human motion from two endpoint egocentric images, relevant for VR/AR and robotics where only first-person views are available. It uses a unified diffusion framework with staged training that jointly handles egocentric-to-canonical pose estimation and temporally consistent motion infilling.

entry.title: Complementary Geometry in Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Mingle Jiang, Jikui Zhou, Chenghan Lyu, Rui Xu, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: The paper observes that depth predictions from different views of a frozen Gaussian Splatting representation exhibit complementary errors, and proposes REVEAL, a framework that refines novel-view depth by reprojecting and combining geometric information from source views without modifying the original representation.

entry.title: One-shot is Enough: Boosting SAM for Medical Image Segmentation through Structured Information Modeling

author.name: Guilin Guan

entry.summary: This paper proposes OB-SAM, a one-shot enhancement framework that adapts the Segment Anything Model for medical image segmentation by maximizing information extracted from a single labeled sample. It targets SAM's known weakness on medical images caused by pre-training on natural images.

entry.title: SKIA: Spatial-Knowledge Informed Attention for Robust Remote Photoplethysmography under Lower-Face Motion Artifacts

author.name: Van-Truong Le, Viet-Tham Huynh, Minh-Triet Tran

entry.summary: SKIA is a lightweight mask-guided framework for remote heart-rate monitoring that suppresses motion-prone lower-face regions while preserving forehead and cheek signals, improving waveform correlation and reducing heart-rate error on UBFC-rPPG. The authors first show static masking helps the classical CHROM pipeline, then build SKIA-Net, a compact spatiotemporal network building on that finding. It is a solid incremental contribution to contactless physiological monitoring robustness.

entry.title: Scenario Compliant Indoor Pedestrian Trajectory Reconstruction from Partial Observation

author.name: Qi Dang, Luis Quintero, Shibo Zhu, Oskar Juhlin, Xiaodan Shi

entry.summary: The authors propose a map-conditioned conditional diffusion framework that reconstructs indoor pedestrian trajectories from partial observations, encoding dense scenario geometry via a CNN so generated paths respect walls and corridors unlike unconstrained coordinate-sequence models. This reduces physically infeasible paths and collisions for surveillance and indoor navigation applications. It addresses a concrete gap between outdoor trajectory imputation and constraint-heavy indoor settings.

entry.title: Gaussian Belief Propagation and Periodic Jacobi Matrices on Trees: Spectral Curve, Antibound Poles, and Fixed Points

author.name: Yusuke Watanabe

entry.summary: This pure-mathematics paper proves a conjecture of Christiansen, Simon and Zinchenko about diagonal Green functions of periodic Jacobi operators on covering trees, connecting them to Gaussian belief propagation covariance equations and characterizing antibound poles and walk-summability thresholds. It also establishes fixed-point structure for positive-definite local beliefs.

entry.title: HGDNA: Overlapping k-mer Tokenization for Efficient Autoregressive Genomic Language Models

author.name: Xudong Wang, Siwei Cheng and Haozhe Hu

entry.summary: HGDNA revisits overlapping k-mer tokenization in causal pretraining for genomic language models, presenting a hybrid linear-attention gLM with a shared token-prediction interface, a species-classification auxiliary task, and competitive performance across classification and frozen-embedding evaluations. From the same group as BQDNA, it offers a complementary tokenizer-centric perspective.

entry.title: Seeing Through Preferences: Recovering Hidden Local Preference Neighborhoods for Text-to-Image Alignment

author.name: Pulkit Bansal, Vivek Srivastava, Shirish Karande

entry.summary: PrefLens argues that informative supervision for text-to-image alignment comes from local preference neighborhoods around preferred images rather than distant pairwise comparisons, and proposes recovering these neighborhoods from sparse human feedback by generating controlled perturbations. This aims to reduce annotation cost while exposing fine-grained perceptual differences.

entry.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition

author.name: Hao Jia, Chunyu Yang, Fan Feng, Cesar F. Caiafa, Feng Duan, Jordi Sol\'e-Casals

entry.summary: Building on the equivalence between hard-partition Variational Mode Decomposition and weighted K-means, this paper develops a soft extraction theory showing that hard and soft extraction optimize different functionals over the same simplex. It proves that the regularized soft VMD problem admits a closed-form, unique global optimum, addressing boundary artifacts of hard Voronoi masks.

entry.title: PAWP-TTS: Phoneme-Aware Weight Programming for Compact Bilingual English-Nepali Speech Synthesis

author.name: Firoj Paudel

entry.summary: PAWP-TTS is a compact non-autoregressive text-to-speech system for English, Nepali, and code-mixed speech at 24 kHz with no language model at inference, using a rule- and lexicon-based bilingual frontend. The 1.5M-parameter model achieves low character and phoneme error rates, and even 281K-parameter variants remain intelligible.

entry.title: Information Bottleneck-Based Hebbian Learning Rule Naturally Ties Working Memory and Synaptic Updates

author.name: Kyle Daruwalla and Mikko Lipasti

entry.summary: The paper develops a layer-wise information bottleneck learning rule for neural networks that avoids backpropagation's biological implausibilities (weight transport, separate phases), framing updates in a Hebbian form. It shows this rule naturally connects working memory maintenance with synaptic updates, relevant to both spiking networks and neuroscience.

entry.title: Safeguarding Federated Learning-based Road Condition Classification

author.name: Sheng Liu and Panos Papadimitratos

entry.summary: This paper studies targeted label-flipping attacks against federated learning for camera-based road condition classification in autonomous driving, where malicious vehicles poison labels to hide dangerous road conditions. It provides the first systematic treatment of TLFAs in FL-RCC and develops countermeasures to preserve safety-critical inference performance.

entry.title: DEFEND: Poisoned Model Detection and Malicious Client Exclusion Mechanism for Secure Federated Learning-based Road Condition Classification

author.name: Sheng Liu and Panos Papadimitratos

entry.summary: DEFEND complements prior TLFA analysis for federated road condition classification by detecting poisoned models and excluding malicious clients during training. It aims to maintain model performance under targeted label-flipping attacks close to attack-free levels, where existing countermeasures fall short.

entry.title: Separating Action Allocation from Image Matching in Visual Token Routing

author.name: Chenxi Wang, Bin Wang

entry.summary: Disentangles whether adaptive visual token routers gain from per-image action matching versus from task-level frequency of high-resolution choices, by fixing action counts per task and comparing assignments against random pairings. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and -7B over ChartQA and TextVQA show matching gains are smaller than losses from suboptimal action frequencies (e.g., 1.71-point gain vs 3.95-point loss on 7B). The findings suggest simple task-conditioned tables can outperform learned routers.

entry.title: SCRA-CLIP: Spherical-Contextual Representation Adaptation for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Peng Chen, Chao Huang, Wenqiang Wang, Mingbo Yang, Yannan Chen, Yunkang Cao, Wei Wang, Li Shen, Fangjun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes SCRA-CLIP, a framework adapting CLIP-style vision-language representations for zero-shot anomaly detection by jointly refining anomaly-aware textual semantics and context-sensitive visual features. It models normal and abnormal patch feature distributions with von Mises-Fisher mixtures and conditions prompts on spherical prototypes.

entry.title: Learning Acceptable Lotteries via Queries: Minimizing Aggregated Violation Distances

author.name: Nicholas Teh and Paul W. Goldberg

entry.summary: Studies preference aggregation for AI deployment where stakeholders reveal only binary acceptability of randomized policies (lotteries) over candidate model versions, with acceptability regions defined by unknown hyperplanes. Since universally accepted lotteries may not exist when requirements conflict, the authors minimize a power mean of normalized stakeholder violations, providing query-complexity algorithms.

entry.title: TASC: Time-to-Collision Anticipation and Selective Crowd Attention for Non-Holonomic Service Robots

author.name: Mohammadhossein Malmir, Mohammadali Rahmati, Mohammad Reza Kolani, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: TASC is a navigation system for non-holonomic service robots combining an attention-based crowd encoder, a time-to-collision anticipatory feature, and a continuous-control PPO policy, addressing the freezing-robot problem and the holonomic-motion assumptions of standard crowd-navigation benchmarks. It adapts a dual-selection attention module from discrete-action learning to continuous velocity control.

entry.title: How Reliable is AI-Generated Audio Description? A Multilingual Expert Evaluation

author.name: Annette Rios, Lukas Fischer, Sarah Ebling

entry.summary: This paper presents an expert evaluation of AI-generated audio description scripts for movies in Italian and German, comparing a GPT-4o-based pipeline and a Qwen-based pipeline against human-authored descriptions. Professional audio describers rated the outputs using a detailed error taxonomy covering content, character, fluency, and coherence errors, finding that while GPT-4o outperforms the Qwen models, both AI systems still fall short of professional human describers.

entry.title: Learning-Augmented QUBO for Time-Expanded Multi-Commodity Flow

author.name: Aikaterini Nikolidaki

entry.summary: This work formulates energy-aware multi-commodity flow on time-expanded graphs as a QUBO problem with a provably feasible penalty coefficient smaller than standard bounds, and derives structural results including a treewidth-based FPT exact algorithm and a proof that the annealing gap of the associated Ising Hamiltonian is strictly positive for instances with unique optima.

entry.title: LAF-ECG: Multi-Resolution Lead-Aware Fusion of Time-Series and Language Foundation Models for ECG Classification

author.name: Kiana Taktehrani, Maryam Hosseini, Amir Keynia, Aram Montazami, Arash Mohammadi

entry.summary: LAF-ECG fuses frozen time-series foundation model representations with language-aligned ECG features through a lead-aware interface, multi-resolution temporal context, and adaptive residual integration, extending MedTsLLM for automated ECG classification. The design targets the lead- and scale-dependent structure of ECG signals that complicates dual-foundation integration.

entry.title: Refine, Don't Reinvent: RASA-Bench for Source-Grounded Hindi Prose Refinement

author.name: Abdur Rahman, Pratham Singla, Mohammad Saifullah, Vasu Sharma

entry.summary: RASA-Bench is a benchmark for refining under-written AI-generated Hindi prose across three creative forms, evaluating 16,400 rewrites from eight models with a faithfulness filter followed by Bradley-Terry preference ranking. Results show faithfulness is a decisive gating test that changes model rankings relative to generation tasks.

entry.title: probly: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning

author.name: Paul Hofman, Clemens Damke, Timo L\"ohr, Santo M. A. R. Thies, Alireza Javanmardi, Valentin Margraf, Jakub Paplham, Yusuf Sale, Eyke H\"ullermeier, Maximilian Muschalik

entry.summary: probly is a Python package providing a modular framework for uncertainty-aware machine learning, including lightweight transformations that convert existing PyTorch and scikit-learn models into uncertainty-aware ones. It consolidates scattered uncertainty quantification tools with guidance on representation, quantification, and evaluation choices.

entry.title: Inferring Experimental Objectives in Microscopy Experiments from Decision Traces

author.name: Kamyar Barakati, Boris N. Slautin, Aditya Raghavan, Babita Babita, Surya Prakash Reddy, Jordan Marshall, Munireach Nannory, Stephen Puplampu, Alla Slautina, Faith M. Hines, Newsha Javanmardi, and Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: This paper explores learning reward functions that capture a microscope operator's scientific logic from recorded choices among alternative measurement locations. The authors compare several reconstruction algorithms, including interpretable linear models on physically meaningful image descriptors and nonlinear alternatives, enabling automated microscopes to follow human experimental objectives.

entry.title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks

author.name: Jonghyun Lee and Soojung Kang

entry.summary: A pre-specified study examining whether pretraining ConvNeXt on formula-labeled synthetic microstructures helps low-label material property regression, finding that weight averaging across seeds confounds results and formula-label pretraining can underperform ImageNet initialization due to generator artifacts and prediction compression.

entry.title: World Models and the Law

author.name: Claudio Novelli

entry.summary: This legal analysis examines how AI regulation in the EU, California, and China handles the distinctive risks of world models, proposing a taxonomy based on who acts on their predictions and identifying risks of misplaced reliance. It argues existing rules nominally cover world models but leave open questions of action provenance, trajectory validity, and more.

entry.title: UnderGrasp: Envelopment-Oriented Grasp Refinement for an Underactuated Gripper

author.name: Zhiwen Song, Ruidi Liu, Guanglu Jia, Zuowei Chen, Hao Wen and Qing Shi

entry.summary: UnderGrasp is a post-hoc grasp refinement and evaluation framework for underactuated grippers that reuses candidates from a frozen generator and jointly encodes target, environment, support surface, and approach-path geometry to propose insertion depth, pre-grasp width, and closing width combinations. It ranks actions by predicted envelopment and interaction quality, addressing limits of conventional collision filtering.

entry.title: Dynamic Gaussian Scene Reconstruction by Integrating Events and Structural Priors

author.name: Zihao Yu, Guozhen Liu, Jie Yan, Jialiang Liu, Panlong Tan, Qinglin Sun, Hao Sun

entry.summary: ESC-DGR improves event-based dynamic Gaussian scene reconstruction by removing reliance on two assumptions that fail under fast motion: that existing Gaussians can absorb errors and that photometric optimization has converged. It uses event observations to independently identify regions needing additional Gaussian support. This improves reconstruction robustness in challenging dynamic scenes.

entry.title: When Should We Trust Medical Image Models? Evaluating Confidence Reliability under Cross-Dataset Shift

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Sarah Lam, Yuting Lin, Nuo Chen, Mingyang Li

entry.summary: This controlled empirical study evaluates chest X-ray model confidence under cross-dataset transfer, training ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 on CheXpert and testing on MIMIC-CXR across five settings. Using AUC, ECE, Brier score, and confidence-on-errors metrics, it quantifies how distributional and labeling shifts degrade both accuracy and calibration. It highlights reliability risks of deploying benchmark-tuned medical models across hospital systems.

entry.title: Differential Proteomics to XAI Rules: A SHAP-FOL-ILP Modeling for Lung Adenocarcinoma

author.name: Surajit Das

entry.summary: This work builds an interpretable pipeline connecting differential proteomics on 213 CPTAC lung adenocarcinoma samples to first-order logic rules via sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and inductive logic programming. The nested cross-validation design and patient-grouped evaluation yield human-readable rules linking protein signatures to cancer status.

entry.title: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models

author.name: Xuanya Zhu, Da Li, Xiatian Zhu

entry.summary: The paper studies how the geometry of latent transitions in world models affects multi-step planning, using action-conditioned curvature regularization as a controlled intervention across four continuous-control tasks. It finds moderately tuned regularization improves planning while excess hurts, and decomposes the effect into affine and non-affine transition-field components.

entry.title: SF-Flow: Spectral Flow Matching with High Structural Fidelity for Hallucination-Suppressed Scientific Image Generation

author.name: Zehua Wang, Patxi Fernandez-Zelaia, Mohamed Wahib, Xiao Wang, Isaac Lyngaas, Amir Koushyar Ziabari, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: SF-Flow is a flow-matching model trained only on real material images that imposes spectral constraints during generation, producing high-fidelity scientific images consistent with prescribed layouts from unpaired data. The design suppresses hallucination and preserves intended phase boundaries, a chronic weakness of unpaired generative translation in scientific imaging.

entry.title: FToken: Factors as Tokens for Dual-Axis Cross-Sectional Return Prediction

author.name: Juntang Wang, Yihan Wang, Sheng'en Li, Dongmian Zou, Shixin Xu

entry.summary: FToken extends stock Transformer architectures by adding a factor branch that treats each factor's cross-section of stock values as a token with self-attention across factors, alongside a stock-axis attention branch, with a gate combining the two forecasts using trailing factor covariance and market volatility. It evaluates on NASDAQ, NYSE, and S&P 500 panels with up to 158 factors.

entry.title: Separating Protocol Effects from Spatio-Temporal Evidence in Person Re-Identification Re-Ranking

author.name: Mochamad Rizal Fauzan, Doan Pham Thao Nhu, Jeslin Konthoujam, Purit Hongjirakul, Lakshay Chawla

entry.summary: This paper shows that reported gains from spatio-temporal priors in person re-identification re-ranking on Market-1501 largely reflect evaluation protocol artifacts rather than genuine evidence: a simple same-camera penalty alone recovers most of the improvement. The authors use identity-disjoint validation and control priors to disentangle protocol effects from learned signal.

entry.title: ReVAgent: Multi-Agent Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation

author.name: Yehui Yang (1 and 2), Jing Fan (3), Jun Hu (2), Shangyao Chen (2), Jinhua Bian (2), Song Wang (2), Ruize Han (2) ((1) Shenzhen University, (2) Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology, (3) Yunnan Minzu University)

entry.summary: ReVAgent is a multi-agent framework for generating instructional videos on reasoning-intensive topics, in which agents share a solution program execution record, reuse scene constructions, and check rendered keyframes against the explanation to guide revisions. It also introduces a multidimensional rubric assessing whether generated videos present reasoning clearly and coherently.

entry.title: Adopting AI Technologies without Traps: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework

author.name: Jitong Yang, Avinash Reddy Mudireddy, Ziqing Lu, Huan Cai, Weiyu Xu

entry.summary: The authors build a general multi-agent MDP reinforcement learning framework for analyzing optimal societal adoption of AI technologies, capturing long-term dynamics such as productivity gains versus losses of jobs, training opportunities, and cognitive capabilities. The framework can be used to derive adoption policies that avoid negative 'traps'.

entry.title: StutterStigma-TR: A Novel Turkish Dataset and Target-Aware BERT Framework for Stuttering-Related Stigma Detection

author.name: Muhsin D\"{o}lek and Arezoo Sadeghzadeh

entry.summary: The authors release StutterStigma-TR, a Turkish dataset of 6,019 annotated tweets for stuttering-related stigma, built with a speech-therapy-informed protocol and lived-experience evaluation. They propose a target-aware BERTurk framework combining target marking, character-level features, and gated discourse cues, evaluated with multi-seed ablations.

entry.title: SGPC: Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint for Stable Off-Policy Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yifan Liu, Nan Zhang, Yang Cong
