entry.summary: SGPC reformulates safe RL as an augmented constrained optimization problem introducing a Safety-Guiding Policy that stabilizes oscillatory primal-dual updates near the safety boundary and mitigates unreliable reward estimates outside the safe set. The actor is evaluated by a cost critic and conditionally steered during updates.

entry.title: The Stigmergic Index: A Biomimetic Edge Centrality for Spatial Network Analysis

author.name: Sofiane Madmar (ESPACE, AU), Didier Josselin (ESPACE, AU), Vincent Labatut (LIA), Muhammad Zaly Shah (UTM, AU), Olivier Blight (IMBE, AU)

entry.summary: This paper repurposes Ant Colony Optimization pheromone dynamics from a tool for optimization into a diagnostic instrument for network structure, introducing the Stigmergic Index as a new topological and behavioral edge centrality metric. It shares baseline properties with betweenness centrality on simple grids but captures path polarization effects that shortest-path measures miss.

entry.title: TAED: Trajectory-Aligned Encoder--Decoder Distillation for Detection Transformers

author.name: Zilong He, Zhangchi Hu, Hebei Li, Yijun Pan, Yifan Zhao, Xiangyu Yu, Yansong Peng, Xinghao Wang, Dongsheng Jiang, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: TAED improves knowledge distillation between DETRs of different capacities by solving the unreliable rank-based query correspondence that arises when teacher and student independently select top-K proposals. It aligns multi-scale encoder features and uses source-informed trajectory alignment for consistent query supervision across decoder layers.

entry.title: Trustworthy Speech-Based Autism Screening under Class Imbalance with Uncertainty-Aware HuBERT Ensembles

author.name: Nihel Loubna Ghennani (IRIT, GBM), Mourtada Benazzouz (GBM), Julie Mauclair (IRIT-SAMoVA, IRIT)

entry.summary: This work proposes an uncertainty-aware autism screening framework built on self-supervised HuBERT representations, combining leave-one-subject-out validation, balanced k-bagging, and Monte Carlo Dropout ensembling, evaluated on the Child Pathological Speech Database. It reports 86.30% balanced accuracy and 93.74% ROC-AUC at the subject level.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representation for 3D Radio Map Compression in Low-Altitude Environments

author.name: Jiaming Cheng, Wei Chen, Yuchen Li, Bo Ai and Jun Zhang

entry.summary: NeRM3D compresses 3D radio maps for low-altitude wireless networks by encoding the entire volumetric map as a lightweight implicit neural representation that maps height values to map slices, combining horizontal embeddings with height-aware modulation. This reduces prohibitive storage and transmission overhead for environment-aware communication supporting drones and low-altitude economy.

entry.title: Part-wise Certified State Estimation of Articulated Objects from Passive Stereo

author.name: Orion Desbonnet, Kei Higuchi, Alex Sykes, Ayush Deshmukh, Victor Leve, Joao Moura, Sethu Vijayakumar

entry.summary: Presents part-wise certification of articulated object state (pose plus semi-deformable part shape) estimated from passive stereo by detecting CAD-defined corners in both images and fitting the articulated model. The estimator rivals the precision of the best model-based fitting without requiring depth sensors, close initial estimates, or object masks, targeting manufacturing tasks like folding cartons.

entry.title: Synthetic Twins: Closing the Gap Between TTS Test Sets and Real Recordings in Turkish ASR Evaluation

author.name: Nur Ya\u{g}mur Tuncer, Mustafa Serta\c{c} T\"urkel, Fatma Nur Korkmaz, Ahmet Tu\u{g}rul Bayrak

entry.summary: Builds synthetic twins of 507 Turkish Common Voice recordings by progressively adding speaker pitch, voice cloning, real recording channel, and speaking rate to measure how much of the gap between synthetic test sets and real recordings can be closed for ASR evaluation. The factor-by-factor ladder design identifies which recording properties matter most for agreement with real-recording error rates.

entry.title: Learning Dense Head-Object Contact Estimation with Synthetic Data

author.name: Daniel Sungho Jung and Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: Tackles dense head-object contact estimation, previously unexplored due to missing data, by learning from synthetic data that captures diverse head-object interactions and contact patterns. The work addresses two core challenges: diversity of contact regions across objects and interactions, and sparsity or observability limits of real contact regions.

entry.title: GRAIN: Shared-Budget Complementary Re-observation for Object Detection

author.name: Chengxuan Zhou, Shaoyang Zhang, Rui Qian, Juntao Cheng, Feng Liu, Wanru Song

entry.summary: GRAIN formulates the problem of allocating a shared budget of extra detector calls across an image collection, planning crops over enlarged regions to recover small and crowded objects without retraining. It uses resolution-deficit hypotheses, a monotone submodular surrogate with multiplicative residuals, and efficient data structures (prefix sums and a global max-heap) for collection-wide planning.

entry.title: BridgeMVS: Bridging Multi-View Stereo and Monodepth via Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion

author.name: Jianfei Jiang, Haochen Yu, Qiankun Liu, Rui Yang, Hongyuan Liu, Xianglong Meng, Jiansheng Chen, Huimin Ma

entry.summary: BridgeMVS is a cascaded multi-stage multi-view stereo framework that fuses monocular depth features with multi-view cost volumes through Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion, performing dynamic mono-to-cost and cost-to-mono updates at each stage. This exploits complementary cues: MVS provides metric depth but struggles in textureless regions, while MDE offers robust but scale-ambiguous structure.

entry.title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports

author.name: Lars Hillebrand, Thiago B. F. de Oliveira, Tim Dilmaghani, Mohamed Khaled, Writwick Das, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: SARA is a human-in-the-loop LLM system delivered as a Word add-in that helps assurance professionals map around 1,700 regulatory requirements to passages in corporate sustainability reports and predict compliance verdicts. It casts auditing as content-based recommendation over a fixed taxonomy and uses topic-prediction filtering to make per-requirement LLM matching cheaper, faster, and more accurate.

entry.title: FGSCalib: Targetless Camera-LiDAR Extrinsic Calibration from Foreground Segmentation

author.name: Marcell K\'egl, Csaba Benedek

entry.summary: FGSCalib calibrates stationary camera-LiDAR pairs without targets by exploiting arbitrary moving objects: each sensor separates moving foreground from static background, and the correct extrinsic makes LiDAR foreground points project onto camera foreground masks. It uses a boundary-proximity field and two-stage simulated annealing, requiring no measured initial extrinsic and supporting both rotating and non-rotating LiDARs.

entry.title: The AMPEL Platform: An Open-Source Project for Developing Hospital-Wide Clinical Decision Support Systems under EU-Regulation

author.name: Alexander Twrdik, Daniel Steinbach, Martin Federbusch, Clemens Malkawi, Maria Schmidt, Toralf Kirsten

entry.summary: AMPEL is an open-source platform for building hospital-wide clinical decision support systems that satisfy the EU Medical Device Regulation, handling large-scale medical data without disrupting clinical workflows. It addresses documentation and risk-management obligations required for deploying ML-based tools in European patient care.

entry.title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Mathijs A. Langezaal, Egon L. van den Broek, Lukas P.A. Arts, Marcel Goldberg, Gr\'egoire Rey, Melissa C. Friesen, Sarah J. Locke, Nathaniel Rothman, Qing Lan, Roel C.H. Vermeulen, Susan Peters

entry.summary: This work applies retrieval-augmented generation to automate standardization of free-text job descriptions into occupational classifications for exposure assessment in large health cohorts. Manual coding is slow, costly, and only 44-89% reliable between coders, while prior automatic tools reach 46-79% accuracy. An RAG pipeline could substantially improve epidemiological occupational health research at scale.

entry.title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech

author.name: Tianyi Huang, Lucas Su, Fred Zhang, Andy Liang, Gordon Li

entry.summary: SayWhen is a test-time controller deciding when a voice AI should commit to early speech, using typed continuation plans, a persistent veto blocking playback when new transcripts invalidate a candidate, and a new metric called regret-free early speech (RFES). On a branching diagnostic it attains 6.0% RFES with zero observed mean regret, and results carry to a tau-Voice retail simulation.

entry.title: Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure for Subsurface Seepage Forecasting and Relief Placement

author.name: Edward Holmberg, Elias Ioup, Mahdi Abdelguerfi

entry.summary: SCBC is a reduced-order modeling technique for truncated diffusion domains that maps local physical descriptors to boundary exchange coefficients, preserving exterior feedback when cutting a large heterogeneous model around a localized outlet. It is validated against full MODFLOW 6 simulations for flood-driven seepage under levees across held-out foundation panels. Useful for engineering forecasting and relief-well placement.

entry.title: Robust Forest-based Estimation of Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Under High-dimensional Confounding

author.name: Zhixin Qiu, Xuanxuan Wang, Xinyuan Song, Yinfeng Wang, Yanlin Tang

entry.summary: The authors develop an Orthogonal Huber Random Forest (OHRF) framework for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects, combining Huber robust loss, Neyman orthogonality, and forest-based adaptive weighting. They apply it to ADNI observational data to study how donepezil dosage effects on 12-month cognition vary with diagnostic stage and hippocampal volume. The method targets nonlinear effect heterogeneity, high-dimensional confounding, and heavy-tailed outcomes.

entry.title: Human empowerment in a few fake graphs

author.name: Boaz Barak

entry.summary: Boaz Barak challenges the view that increasing AI capability necessarily forces a control handover to AI (benevolent or otherwise), arguing that humanity's collective intelligence has grown without biological change through inventions like writing, markets, and democracy, and that ceding control is neither necessary nor desirable. He advocates preserving human autonomy and sovereignty regardless of alignment quality, illustrated with deliberately simplified conceptual graphs. It is a strategic vision piece from a highly credible researcher.

entry.title: Social-Qwen: From Individual Nonverbal Cues and Emotion to Multiparty Social Dynamics Understanding with Instruction Tuning

author.name: The Tung Nguyen, Jouh Yeong Chew

entry.summary: Social-Qwen uses instruction tuning to teach a comparatively small model to understand group-level social dynamics in multiparty settings from individual nonverbal cues and emotions, addressing data scarcity through hypothesis-driven annotation strategies. It targets real-time robotics applications where large VLMs are too costly.

entry.title: Close the Loop on the Retrievability Gap

author.name: Guangyuan Dong, Wenhao Li, Zhen Tian, Jiaqi Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Junhao Xu, Mingzhe Liu, Pan Wang, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Identifies a retrievability gap in pansharpening: fidelity metrics disagree about which systems produce outputs most retrievable by a frozen vision-language encoder used downstream, with LEDGER proposed to close the loop by re-encoding generated outputs and minimizing set-level concept mismatch against indexed input concepts. The work traces the gap to area weighting of position-averaged losses across eighteen pansharpening systems.

entry.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents

author.name: Suleman Khan, Rasa Rahnema, Tara Khani, Majid Fekri, Fattane Zarrinkalam

entry.summary: The authors evaluate Memanto, a memory agent ranking memories by an information-theoretic relevance score, on DolphinBench's 600 simulated workplace tasks requiring implicit memory use. Running with GPT-6-Luna and at most 6 iterations, Memanto completes 83.83 percent of tasks versus 70.67 percent for the benchmark authors' strongest configuration, at the lowest reported total cost.

entry.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction

author.name: Yiyu Qian (Cornell University), Xing Wu (Shanghai University)

entry.summary: GERF is a graph-based evidence retrieval framework for schema-guided multimodal scientific information extraction, targeting token efficiency by avoiding full-document context and coarse page-level retrieval that introduce irrelevant text and visual tokens. It structures evidence across text, tables, figures, and captions for traceable extraction. It matters for making AI-for-Science pipelines cost-effective.

entry.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code

author.name: Justin Asher, Pietro Pellegrino

entry.summary: The authors compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean proof libraries against Mathlib using distributions of simple code statistics such as inline claims, proof length, declaration usage, and design choices. AI-generated libraries show more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than human-written ones, with the analysis package released as lean-census.

entry.title: PAMS: Preconditioned Activation-Metric Subspace for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-tuning

author.name: Pradeep Kumar Ragu Chanthar, Saksham Sahai Srivastava, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: Introduces PAMS, a zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning framework that uses forward-pass activation statistics to build structured, layer-wise perturbation geometries without gradients or dense curvature matrices. It tracks a low-rank activation subspace online and reweights perturbation variance using its spectrum, addressing the anisotropy ignored by isotropic ZO methods. Advances gradient-free fine-tuning efficiency for large models.

entry.title: OKB-CFM: Observation-Keyed Barycentric Conditional Flow Matching for Unpaired Sparse-to-Dense Cardiac Shape Completion

author.name: Kangneng Zhou, Shuang Song, Yitian Zhao, Dian Song, Yujia Wang, Xinghua Zhang, Li Wang, Xi Li, Hao Dai, Feng Cao

entry.summary: Proposes observation-keyed barycentric conditional flow matching to complete dense cardiac segmentations from sparse cine MRI labels across clinically unpaired cohorts, using a fixed memory of sparse keys and dense encodings to retrieve candidate values aggregated into query-dependent barycentric flow endpoints.

entry.title: UACR: Uncertainty-Aware Collaborative Routing for Explainable Industrial Anomaly Inspection

author.name: Yiwei Li, Qiyang Chen, Zheming Yang

entry.summary: UACR is an uncertainty-aware routing framework for industrial anomaly inspection that adaptively allocates computation so ambiguous cases receive deeper scrutiny, delivering anomaly decisions with operator-facing explanations under strict online latency budgets. It addresses the tension between detection accuracy, inference efficiency, and interpretability that fixed computational paths cannot resolve. Applied to a safety-critical industrial setting.

entry.title: DynFlux: Learning to Dynamically Balance Consensus and Conflict in Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Zeheng Wang, Hao Zhang, Yige Wang, Xi Xiao, Hao Xu

entry.summary: DynFlux is a multimodal emotion recognition model guided by a temporal heterogeneous graph that explicitly encodes both cross-modal consensus and conflict relationships, dynamically modeling their interplay to reduce semantic ambiguity. It addresses the limitation of traditional methods that treat modal inconsistencies uniformly. The contribution is solid but within a well-trodden multimodal fusion niche.

entry.title: InfoField3D: Differentiable Information Field for Embodied Task-Oriented View Planning

author.name: Huan Lyu, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: InfoField3D casts task-driven camera placement as gradient-based optimization over a differentiable 3D information field, using spherical harmonics for directional information responses and analytic line integrals of Gaussian occupancy for occlusion. This enables efficient viewpoint selection for embodied agents incorporating constraints like reachability.

entry.title: Think Before You Forecast: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Daojun Liang, Xiao Hong, Pei Zhang, Yinglong Wang, Shuo Li, Jing Chen, Ying Guo, Hu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TTC4TS, an architecture-agnostic framework that applies test-time compute to frozen time-series forecasting models: a generator produces multiple candidate forecast trajectories via augmentation, retrieval, and adapters, and a synthesizer selects or refines the most reliable prediction. The approach targets robustness to distribution shift and non-stationarity.

entry.title: Learning Gaussian Process Priors with Linear Semigroups and Kinetic Regularisation

author.name: Angela Lavinia Varazi and Felipe Tobar

entry.summary: The paper introduces a semigroup-based construction of Gaussian process priors, where a learned linear operator transforms a source GP into a prior at a later time, with a generator trained via marginal likelihood and a kinetic-energy regularizer. Linearity preserves Gaussianity, connecting the approach to optimal transport and convolution models.

entry.title: FlexGaze: Weakly Supervised Gaze Estimation at Scale

author.name: Zongjian Li, Mohammad Soleymani

entry.summary: FlexGaze is a family of 3D gaze estimators pretrained with weak supervision from roughly 3.24 million pseudo-labeled head instances generated by combining off-the-shelf 2D gaze and depth predictions on in-the-wild images. At inference it predicts gaze from a head crop alone, handling profile and rear views without face detection or head pose estimation.

entry.title: Regularizing Hard Examples Improves Adversarial Robustness

author.name: Hyungyu Lee, Saehyung Lee, Ho Bae, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: The paper theoretically and empirically shows that hard examples have disproportionate negative effects in adversarial training, being fitted only through label memorization, and that pruning or regularizing them improves robustness. It extends the known hard-example generalization phenomenon into the adversarial setting with a theory of the asymmetry between hard and easy examples.

entry.title: Evaluating Persona Consistency in LLM User Simulators Without External Reference Annotations

author.name: Anping Zhang, Yang Tan, Yipeng Liu, Clive Bai, Blaze Chen, Yang Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a self-anchored diagnostic for evaluating persona consistency of LLM user simulators when no external ground truth exists: a persona self-reports via Likert scale and acts in two constrained behavioral profiles, with consistency measured as correlation in a shared BFI-2 facet space. This enables comparing persona-construction strategies reference-free.

entry.title: Shift by Analogy for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning

author.name: Zanwu Liu, Bo Li and Guanglin Niu

entry.summary: SBA recognizes unseen attribute-object compositions via a shift-then-match procedure where an add-subtract-add rule transfers an attribute change between seen image-text residuals on a source object to the target object. An analogy library and same-object attention extend the construction across candidates during training with each target excluded from its supports.

entry.title: LiquidGazeNet: Towards Event-Based Near-Eye Gaze Estimation under Low-Light Conditions

author.name: Himanshu Kumar, and Sanjay Singh

entry.summary: LiquidGazeNet is an event-only gaze estimation framework for low-light near-eye settings, combining polarity-aware spike-latency encoding with a custom LTC-inspired recurrent module that integrates features causally over event windows, trained with a hybrid objective. It targets wearable AR/VR gaze tracking where conventional intensity frames degrade at night.

entry.title: Doc-to-LoRA Analysis: Query Conditioning, Wrong Facts, and Distractor Interference

author.name: Jesper Derehag

entry.summary: This analysis examines Doc-to-LoRA, which compiles documents into low-rank adapters for knowledge internalization, finding across Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B that D2L underperforms in-context learning and suffers substantial interference as document banks grow. Controlled interventions show single-document errors often match answers to other questions and that interference accumulates across model depth.

entry.title: CableMoE: Harm-Regularized Mean-Residual Expert Fusion for Transmission-Corridor Segmentation

author.name: Shima Salehi

entry.summary: CableMoE is a post-hoc mixture of four frozen segmentation experts for transmission-corridor mapping that predicts a calibrated residual around availability-aware probability averaging, with a harm penalty preventing degradation on points the ensemble already classifies correctly. The component study quantifies how harm regularization recovers performance lost by unconstrained learned mixtures.

entry.title: Diffutoon-2: Toon Shading with Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuze Sun, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: Diffutoon-2 is a video diffusion framework for converting photorealistic videos to anime-style toon shading, trained via animation reconstruction with two complementary modules that reconstruct clips from outlines and blurred colors while keeping the video backbone frozen. It removes the need for curated source-style pairs or visual references required by prior approaches.

entry.title: Serialization and the Character-System: Measuring Narrative Concentration in French Fiction (1800--1940)

author.name: Jean Barr\'e, Antoine Bourgois, Thierry Poibeau

entry.summary: This computational-literary study operationalizes Woloch's character-system concept as the Gini coefficient of PageRank over character networks and traces narrative attention concentration across 12,011 French novels from 1800-1940. It tests whether the balance between a central protagonist and an ensemble cast has a measurable history over the long nineteenth century. A rigorous blend of NLP, network analysis, and literary theory.

entry.title: Pay people to create high quality alignment training data

author.name: testingthewaters

entry.summary: The post proposes that AI labs should pay diverse scholars and moral thinkers to author rich, high-quality reasoning chains on hard ethical questions, rather than relying on LLM-generated synthetic data or elaborate post-training filters. It suggests capturing genuine diversity of human moral reasoning through essays and recorded multi-perspective chat conversations formatted as training data.

entry.title: Misalignment Between Educators' Testing and End Users' Behavior: What 17,000+ Chatbot Messages Reveal About AI Literacy Training for Teachers

author.name: Ruiwei Xiao, Jiayi Wang, Miina Koyama, Yue Wang, Qing Xiao, Xinying Hou, Norman Bier, John Stamper

entry.summary: The study trains 87 higher-education educators in an online AI literacy course, has them build and deploy educational chatbots, and analyzes 17,000+ messages of builder, peer, and end-user conversations using validated LLM-assisted coding. It reveals misalignment between how educators test their bots and how end users actually behave, informing AI literacy training design.

entry.title: VUOD: A Versatile Unsupervised Outlier Detection Framework for Natural, Industrial, Medical Images and Beyond

author.name: Zhonghang Liu, Siyuan Chen, Jingwen Yu, Changshuo Wang, Kunyang Li, Jiangbo Lu

entry.summary: Introduces a versatile unsupervised outlier detection framework that improves feature discriminativeness by exploiting intrinsic distribution priors, moving beyond frozen pre-trained extractors that underperform on industrial and medical imagery. Achieves state-of-the-art results across 3 domains and 14 benchmark datasets.

entry.title: Dynamic Model Merging with Multi-Layer Aggregated Routing Evidence

author.name: Yuxi Li, Jiacong Hu, Jie Song, Mingli Song and Yuanyu Wan

entry.summary: The paper improves dynamic model merging by introducing MATE, a unified mechanism aggregating routing evidence across multiple layers for both task-level and head-level routing. The authors propose a metric for task routing separability across layers, showing different layers give complementary evidence, and replace simple max-logit head routing with aggregated evidence. The goal is to preserve task-specific expertise in a merged model while retaining unified-model efficiency.

entry.title: STEdgeFormer: MCU and NPU Deployable Transformer Architecture

author.name: Sudhakar Sah

entry.summary: STEdgeFormer replaces pairwise self-attention with a compact accelerator-aware causal memory block combined with polynomial mixture layers and DyT normalization, targeting microcontroller/NPU deployment. On TinyStories, a fully NPU-supported 4.12M-parameter variant reaches perplexity 7.39 in 6.51MB RAM with 40ms latency.

entry.title: FolioWeaver: A LayerGraph-Grounded Agent for Layered Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Wentao Lu, Shengzhe Cui, Xihao Wu, Dingxin Yan, Yixuan Qin, Pengfei Fang

entry.summary: FolioWeaver unifies layered image generation and iterative editing through a persistent Executable Scene State and LayerGraph representation, generating independent visual assets conditioned on a shared scene reference. An editing agent performs feedback-driven scoped actions with selective layer execution and visual verification, enabling targeted edits while preserving unaffected content.

entry.title: Event-Driven Parameter Dynamics for Spatiotemporal Parameter-Update Application in Deep Learning

author.name: Ruixue Li and Chaofei Hong

entry.summary: EPD separates candidate optimizer updates from their application via an intermediate state with accumulation, event-triggered release, and reset, introducing a spatiotemporal view of parameter updating in which dense updating is a boundary case. Experiments on CIFAR-100 across four model-optimizer configurations show near-conventional final performance while applying only a fraction of coordinate-wise updates.

entry.title: Active Observation for Robust Visual Servoing in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhilun Hu, Yuqi Cheng, Yuxiang Tan, Wenpan Li, Weiming Shen

entry.summary: Presents an active observation framework for dual-arm robotic grasping in which one arm carries an RGB-D camera as an active observer that repositions to maintain or recover a shared target-gripper view during occlusion-prone approach phases. A two-phase viewpoint strategy aligns camera axes with task-relevant error directions to sustain closed-loop visual servoing where fixed eye-to-hand and eye-in-hand setups fail.

entry.title: Graph2Scene: Relation-Aware Text-to-Image Generation with Graph-Guided Diffusion Model

author.name: Peizheng Li, Xin Ai, Guanghui Cheng, Zikang Dong, Qiange Wang, Yanfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Graph2Scene is a training-free framework that uses scene graphs as control signals for text-to-image diffusion, translating element-relation dependencies into selective attention guidance so that relation tokens attend to the correct regions and object interactions are rendered faithfully. It targets the failure of existing attention-control methods to handle interactions in complex multi-element prompts.

entry.title: Typing Behavior in Human-LLM Interaction: Keystroke Dynamics Reveal Cognitive Effort During Prompting

author.name: Laura Sch\"utz, Yousri Cherif, Clara Sayffaerth, Thomas Weber, Francesco Chiossi

entry.summary: A user study (N=36) shows keystroke dynamics during human-LLM interaction reflect task difficulty and workload: hard tasks produce more keystrokes, slower typing, more pauses, and higher NASA-TLX workload, while device type has weaker effects. This establishes typing behavior as a passive behavioral measure of cognitive effort in prompting.

entry.title: Distributed Multimodal Monitoring and Prediction for PV Asset and Site Conditions

author.name: Jan Stiefel, Brendan Do, Reza Arablouei, Ross Dungavell, Brano Kusy, Kenrick Anderson, Benjamin Duck, Noel W Duffy, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: This work presents a distributed monitoring framework for utility-scale photovoltaic plants that fuses mechanical, optical, electrical, and microclimate measurements from wireless nodes attached at string level to derive higher-level asset and site condition indicators. A four-node field deployment demonstrates the system. It is a well-motivated applied systems paper for renewable energy asset management.

entry.title: Teacher-Guided Multimodal Dual Representation Reconstruction for Egocentric Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Yuzhe Hao, Ikuro Sato, Rei Kawakami, Koichi Shinoda

entry.summary: MDR2 is a teacher-guided pre-training framework for egocentric activity recognition in which frozen, label-informed video and inertial teachers each supervise a modality-specific representation, rather than a single joint objective on the fused representation. This better preserves complementarity between first-person video and inertial sensor signals. The approach improves multimodal fusion for activity recognition.

entry.title: Tangent incompleteness under coupled image transformations: margin reconstruction and decision consequences

author.name: Karim Bounja, Abdeljalil Sakat

entry.summary: This theoretical paper asks whether per-axis responses to geometric image transformations can be composed to predict their combined effect on classifier decisions, deriving conditions (signed ridge cancellation, an exact even-odd identity) under which coordinatewise assembly fails at first order. The coupled correction achieves O(s^2) projected error versus a possible Theta(s) axiswise defect, with large RMS error reductions on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. It provides rigorous insight into transformation compositionality in learned classifiers.

entry.title: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Bone Scaffold Pore Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Few-Shot Performance

author.name: Tri Tin Vo, Vu Thien An Ngo, Nhi Kieu, Cuong Hung Luu, Giang V. H. Phan, Kien Nguyen, Clinton Fookes

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first expert-annotated pixel-dense dataset of biopolymer bone-scaffold SEM images and benchmarks SAM3 and YOLOv26 under 12-shot fine-tuning, feeding predicted pore geometry to heads that estimate Young's modulus and compressive yield strength. A key finding is that both models fail by pore density rather than magnification, with YOLOv26's pore counts saturating. A useful domain-specific benchmark exposing limits of general foundation models in materials science imaging.

entry.title: Separating Module Gain From Transport Plan Contribution in Audio-Visual Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition

author.name: Vu Nhat Minh Pham, Cong Khanh Nguyen, Minh Tuan Le, Van Thong Huynh

entry.summary: A rigorous ablation study showing that gains attributed to a Sinkhorn cross-modal routing module in dynamic facial expression recognition may not come from its transport plan: parameter-matched pooled variants narrow or eliminate the apparent improvement. The paper proposes stronger evaluation protocols including parameter-matched comparisons and plan-replacement interventions.

entry.title: Which Vertebral Landmark Errors Change a Cobb Angle? Geometry-Weighted Supervision for Radiographic Landmark Regression

author.name: Zizhao Peng

entry.summary: Derives a geometry-aware training loss for vertebral corner localization that upweights the single displacement direction most responsible for rotating spinal curvature measurement lines, using a Hadamard basis to retain supervision on other degrees of freedom. Experiments on 372 radiographs show the approach reduces pooled symmetric percentage error versus standard objectives.

entry.title: EID-Net: Endoscopic Illumination-aware Degradation Correction Network

author.name: Junzhi Liu, Yinghao Zeng, Yang Liu, Huafeng Li, Xiaosong Li

entry.summary: EID-Net corrects spatially non-uniform illumination degradation in endoscopic images, including local under- and over-exposure and color shifts, by explicitly extracting an endoscopy-oriented degradation prior rather than applying global intensity adjustment. The goal is visibility improvement while preserving tissue structure and chromatic cues for downstream analysis.

entry.title: Preserving Prosody in Speaker Anonymization

author.name: Kevin Everson and Mari Ostendorf

entry.summary: This work integrates a pretrained privacy-preserving prosody encoder into a speech synthesis model so that speaker anonymization preserves intended prosodic meaning. Human-subject evaluations show improved perception of intended prosody while anonymization performance remains competitive with prior work. It resolves a known trade-off in privacy-preserving speech technology.

entry.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series

author.name: Zhaodong Guo (Imperial College London), Haoyun Feng (Imperial College London)

entry.summary: Introduces HiPPO Functional Memory, an attention operator that writes an irregular time series history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates via kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features and a regularized Gram solve, enabling queries at arbitrary times. Bridges continuous-time latent dynamics and time-aware attention for irregularly sampled series. A novel architectural operator at the intersection of SSM-style memory and attention.

entry.title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change

author.name: Truc Nguyen Thi Le, Phuoc Nguyen T. H

entry.summary: PAV-Twin is a framework for digital twins of agent networks that combines Jacobian-based propagation features, recent errors, and ensemble disagreement to estimate forecast risk, and simulates candidate network edits ranked by predicted collective outcome. It addresses when error propagation information improves failure detection and whether imperfect twins can still select effective interventions. This is a useful step toward trustworthy simulation of networked multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Complex band-limited maximum likelihood: estimating the wave behind detected quanta

author.name: Rahul Agarwal, Ankit Agarwal

entry.summary: Introduces complex BLML, a maximum-likelihood estimator that recovers the complex quantum wavefunction (phase included) from detected particle positions by restricting to physically allowed band-limited complex functions, with a single-eigenvalue certificate for global optimality. Demonstrated on simulated two-slit experiments.

entry.title: Unlearning Model Identity: Ablating LoRA Weights from Question-Based Identity Tuning

author.name: Ming Cheung

entry.summary: Proposes a method to localize self-identity representations in LoRA modules and ablate them, using probing questions to elicit self-naming outputs and fine-tuning to modify identity traits in open-weight models. This addresses a practical deployment need where service providers must remove inherited proprietary-model identity without exposing provider affiliations. Touches on both model customization and the emerging issue of identity leakage from distillation on teacher outputs.

entry.title: CLAIR: Consistent LLM Adaptation via Index-free Reprogramming

author.name: Dongkuk Kim, Jungkyu Shin, Yoonhyuk Choi, Jong Wook Kim, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: CLAIR improves time-series forecasting with pretrained LLMs by addressing inconsistent patch-to-embedding alignment. It combines patch-level transport alignment and forecast-level consistency under a teacher-guided framework, allowing correspondences across temporal positions while keeping forecasts stable. This targets a known brittleness in LLM-based forecasters.

entry.title: The Complexity of Oracle-Efficient Realizable Transductive Learning

author.name: Changlong Wu

entry.summary: This theory paper shows a negative answer to whether the halving algorithm's log N mistake bound in realizable transductive learning can be matched with polynomially many ERM oracle queries. Even with a powerful weighted-ERM oracle, any polynomial-query randomized learner suffers Omega(sqrt(T log N)) style mistakes on instances with N=2^Theta(T^beta) hypotheses.

entry.title: Statistical mechanics of linear classification on hierarchical tree data

author.name: Jerome Garnier-Brun, Federica Kulka, Carlo Lucibello

entry.summary: The authors analyze linear classification on data generated by the classical broadcast process on a tree, a setting where the Gaussian equivalence assumption common in statistical mechanics approaches fails because a few latent variables influence all coordinates. They retain the exact non-Gaussian law along the label-carrying direction and approximate transverse fluctuations as Gaussian, deriving tractable results despite strong finite-size effects. The work clarifies how structured, non-Gaussian data affect learnability.

entry.title: Thakaa at AlexandriaX-2026: Who Gets the Final Say? Assigning Output Authority in Dialectal Arabic Machine Translation and Error Detection

author.name: Meshal Alamr, Maryam Altuwaijri, Hassan Alqaeri, Abdullah Aldahlawi

entry.summary: A systems report on first-place solutions across all four AlexandriaX-2026 shared-task settings for dialectal Arabic machine translation and error detection. Key techniques include candidate-constrained minimum Bayes risk selection that restricts output authority among a pool of systems, and country-routed LoRA adapters over a shared NileChat-3B-Base backbone for the constrained track. The approach outperforms even a retrospective oracle picking the best whole-candidate system per dialect.

entry.title: Can Open LLMs Clear Sanctions-Screening Alerts? A Pre-registered Test on Public Sanctions Lists with Turkish Name Variants

author.name: Mehmet Murat Huyut

entry.summary: A pre-registered study tests whether open-weight LLMs run on-premises can perform level-1 disposition of sanctions-screening alerts, using 12,200 synthetic customers built from UK/EU sanctions lists with Turkish and Cyrillic name variants. Three open models and rule baselines are compared on 7,383 fuzzy/embedding-screened alerts.

entry.title: HME-PFD: Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Privileged Feature Distillation

author.name: Wen Xu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yucheng Yang, Danny Liu, Xunlong Gui, Fei Huang, Sha Meng

entry.summary: This paper proposes HME-PFD, which incorporates limited-coverage privileged features into the routing module of a Mixture-of-Experts architecture for privileged feature distillation in ads recommendation. It addresses real-world heterogeneity in privileged feature distributions and varying example importance during distillation.

entry.title: ArborNet: Volume- and skeleton-aware completion of tree quantitative structure models from incomplete point clouds using anchor-conditioned graph learning

author.name: Ge Jiang, Tiangang Yin, Wei Yao, Wai Yeung Yan, Qi Chen, Jinhong Wang, Qihao Weng

entry.summary: ArborNet completes tree quantitative structure models from occluded terrestrial laser scans using a multi-relation graph encoder over TreeQSM cylinder graphs, with anchor-conditioned generation preserving branch topology, radii, and woody volume. Unlike generic point-cloud completion, it explicitly maintains the structural quantities needed for biomass estimation. Relevant to forestry, carbon accounting, and ecological monitoring.

entry.title: NANO: Unifying Missingness and Input Uncertainty in Tabular Learning

author.name: Kuangdai Leng, Maria Tsekhmistrenko, Matteo Bagagli, Simon Jeffery, Tarje Nissen-Meyer

entry.summary: NANO is a plug-in input encoding scheme for token-based tabular architectures that represents a continuous spectrum from no evidence to fully trusted observation, unifying missing values and input uncertainty. Guided by Bayesian evidence weighting, it maps zero-confidence estimates to a shared Not-Observed representation and explicitly handles Not-Applicable semantics.

entry.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?

author.name: Pinaki Prasad Guha Neogi, Spyros Mastorakis, Ankur Mallick, Saravan Rajmohan, Victor R\"uhle

entry.summary: NoeVera is an agentic Second Brain for LLM serving system optimization that turns papers, code, benchmarks, and experimental results into a persistent, provenance-preserving knowledge base with source-evidence, synthesis, and agent-memory planes. Decision-aware retrieval assembles evidence packs that role-specific agents use with a simulator to decide which configurations and mechanisms to investigate.

entry.title: Automatic Construction of Persian E-Commerce Dialogue Datasets for Conversational Product Search

author.name: Fariba Nafar, Hassan Naderi

entry.summary: The authors present a framework that automatically builds a Persian conversational product search dataset from the Digikala catalog, crawling 12,926 products in seven categories, clustering them into 170 coherent groups, and selecting clarifying questions via a Regularized Partition Balance score. They release the resulting dataset, addressing a resource gap for low-resource conversational IR. This expands multilingual coverage for an underrepresented language.

entry.title: SpectralGS: Spectral Gaussian Splatting for Unsupervised Spectral Super-Resolution

author.name: Qiaoying Qu, Bin Pan, Chen Jia, Haiyang Xu, Xia Xu and Zhenwei Shi

entry.summary: SpectralGS performs unsupervised spectral super-resolution from RGB images using a Gaussian splatting framework with shared spectral-spatial Gaussian primitives and a rendering module that models the sensor's spectral response function. It exploits the low-rank structure of hyperspectral imagery without paired training data.

entry.title: Towards the Roof of the World: NLP Progress in Tibetan Languages

author.name: Xi Cao, Yijie Li, Yuan Sun, Shiwei Dong, Zeguang Huang, Nuo Qun

entry.summary: A systematic bibliometric survey of Tibetan NLP covering 140 publications from 2004 to 2026, annotated across venue type, research area, affiliation country, and resource release. Output has grown rapidly with 84% of work since 2018, expanding from corpora and segmentation up to LLMs, though 87% of first authors are China-based. It highlights persistent underrepresentation and uneven geographic participation for a language of seven million speakers.

entry.title: STAGE: Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling for Cross-Subject Brain-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Yihang Zou, Ruixi Liang, Chunmei Qing, Junpeng Tan, Haichuan Wei, Wanxiang Luo, Gao Wu, Haodong Li, Xiangmin Xu, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes STAGE, a structured test-time adaptation framework for cross-subject brain-to-image retrieval that aligns brain and image representations from uncertain correspondences without target labels. It combines moment calibration, coupling-weighted initialization, and soft-coupling ranking to handle inter-subject variability and prediction concentration.

entry.title: Aggregation Dispersion: An Information-Geometric Diagnostic of Oversmoothing in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Abdessalam Ed-dib, Amine Mohamed Aboussalah

entry.summary: Offers a geometric perspective on oversmoothing in message-passing GNNs: at each depth, propagation assigns each node a walk distribution over source nodes, and contraction of this point cloud on the probability simplex characterizes complete mixing. The authors propose Fisher-Rao-based aggregation dispersion as a diagnostic measure of this contraction.

entry.title: ReqSeek: Transformer-Based Automatic Requirements Identification for Building Large Requirements Datasets

author.name: Mohammad Kasra Habib, Umm-e-Habiba, Daniel Graziotin, Stefan Wagner

entry.summary: ReqSeek is a domain-agnostic transformer model for identifying ISO 29148-style requirements in software requirement specification documents, accompanied by the ARID dataset of 2,396 training instances from 23 heterogeneous SRSs. Fine-tuned RoBERTa achieved roughly 95% precision, recall, and F1, supporting large-scale requirements dataset construction.

entry.title: S\'anchez, Feij\'oo, or Abascal? Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X of the Leaders of the Three Main Parties of the 29N General Election in Spain

author.name: V\'ictor Yeste, Candida Maria Greco, Paolo Rosso, Andrea Tagarelli

entry.summary: Using 1,075 anonymized posts by Spanish party leaders and 791 value-grounded LLM personas across four author-attribution conditions, this study tests whether synthetic audiences respond to who speaks rather than only what is said, spanning 322,470 persona-post quartets. It grounds personas in Inglehart-Welzel and Moral Foundations frameworks ahead of the November 2026 Spanish election.

entry.title: A Cascaded Framework with a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN Model for Pre- and Post-Treatment Glioma Segmentation

author.name: Siavash Taremi, Mahmoud Heidari, Seyed Mohammad Hossein Hashemi, Mohsen Hooshmand

entry.summary: CMC-Seg combines a Mamba-CNN hybrid with cross-attention guidance in a cascaded framework for both pre- and post-treatment diffuse glioma segmentation, addressing underexplored post-treatment cases with resection cavities. It aims to balance the accuracy of transformer-style global context with lower computational cost.

entry.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel

author.name: Ameer Qaqish, Sudipto Banerjee, Didong Li

entry.summary: This mathematical statistics paper develops sharp asymptotic theory for the joint maximum likelihood estimators of Matern kernel parameters in Gaussian processes under fixed-domain asymptotics, going beyond known identifiability results to establish consistency and asymptotic behavior. The results depend critically on the smoothness parameter regime.

entry.title: Active sensing as control over sensory acquisition

author.name: Neeli Tummala and Mitra J. Hartmann

entry.summary: This position/conceptual paper argues that the diverse behaviors labeled active sensing in neuroscience and engineering are better framed as control over sensory acquisition, distinguishing mechanistic, strategic, and agentic forms of control. The framework clarifies how these control types differ in their consequences for perception, behavior, and performance.

entry.title: KGLP-Net: Kalman-Reliable Global--Local Learning With Group Fisher Pruning for Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Wenshuai Deng, Wen Xie, Abdel Hamid Soliman, and Qianzheng Zhao

entry.summary: KGLP-Net unifies uncertainty-aware feature fusion with structured pruning for hyperspectral image classification. It combines a Global Mamba Encoder for long-range spatial context with a Local CNN Encoder, using Kalman-based reliability estimates to guide fusion and Fisher-based group pruning for compression. The coupling of uncertainty estimation with compression guidance is the key novelty.

entry.title: When Learned IDS Model Selection Collapses to a Static Choice: A Measurement Study at the Edge

author.name: Nuonan Ouyang, Bonan Zhang, Adrian Shatte, Zhigang Lu, Chao Chen and Wei Xiang

entry.summary: This measurement study evaluates whether learned runtime model selection for intrusion detection at the edge actually beats static choices, using matched static controls and a factorial design on a Raspberry Pi 4B with four frozen TON-IoT detectors. Both Q-learning and DQN collapse to selecting one model almost always, and a retrospective audit mostly rules out preference reversals. It demonstrates that learned selectors can degenerate to static policies and provides a framework to detect this.

entry.title: QSRadar: Query-Conditioned Sparse Radar-Camera Fusion for Efficient 3D Object Detection

author.name: Chenhao Yan, Hongyu Liu, Xiang Cai, Yifei Sun and Zhe Zhang

entry.summary: QSRadar is a query-conditioned sparse fusion framework that retrieves compact sets of raw radar points around each evolving object hypothesis on a Sparse4Dv3-style detector, preserving point-level radar geometry and motion cues while avoiding costly global BEV construction. It targets efficient long-range 3D detection for autonomous trucks.

entry.title: PsyDrift: Healthy-Reference Latent Diffusion for Anomaly Scoring in Autism Spectrum Disorder

author.name: Yasaman Mohammadpour, Pouya Shaeri, Ariane Middel

entry.summary: PsyDrift combines supervised functional-connectivity representations with a diffusion model trained only on healthy-control latents, scoring ASD deviation as distance from a diffusion-denoised reconstruction. Evaluated on 1,102 subjects across all 20 ABIDE-I sites with leave-one-site-out validation, the classifier reaches a mean-site AUROC of about 0.798.

entry.title: HERO: Hierarchical Region-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Exploration

author.name: Xulin Xiao, Shengyi Liang, Mingjie Zhang, Chengkai Wu, Chen Chen, Zhigang Li, Jinni Zhou, Jun Ma, Boyu Zhou

entry.summary: HERO combines classical hierarchical global planning with learned region-aware local decision-making for autonomous exploration of unknown environments, assigning each level the function it handles best. It reduces the inference cost growth of graph-based RL while preserving path efficiency and low online computation at scale.

entry.title: Value function based Reward shaping for safety in quadrupeds

author.name: Janani S K, Manan Tayal, Shishir N.Y Kolathaya

entry.summary: The paper presents a barrier-function-inspired safety reward-shaping framework for reinforcement learning in quadruped locomotion, evaluated in simulation on a Unitree Go1 in Isaac Gym. The approach reduces safety violations from 27 percent to 0.1 percent with almost no performance cost compared to existing baselines.

entry.title: OpenViVE: New Benchmark and Dual-Stream Co-Attention Framework for Vietnamese Visual Entailment

author.name: Bao Quoc Trinh, Tin Van Huynh, Kiet Van Nguyen, and Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen

entry.summary: OpenViVE is the first large-scale native Vietnamese visual entailment benchmark with 62,268 balanced image-hypothesis pairs from 10,378 culturally grounded images, built via a hybrid LLM-human pipeline with artifact-aware refinement that substantially reduces shortcut hypotheses. The authors also propose a dual-stream co-attention model evaluated on the benchmark.

entry.title: OmniSLAM: Evidence-Authorized Revision of Persistent Object Maps

author.name: Haoxiang Jie, Yaoyuan Yan, Zhiyou Heng, Liang Li, Zhaosong Li, Lifeng Liu

entry.summary: This work presents a map-revision module for persistent object maps that separates historical identity changes from new-surface admission, authorizing merges only when evidence margins stay positive after frame removal. On two KITTI-360 windows, the method improves building/car instance AP50:90 from 17.259 to 18.762 under a local evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Voyag: Joint Multi-Intent Detection and Execution-Relation Classification for In-Vehicle Voice Assistants

author.name: Sen Luo

entry.summary: Voyag is a single-forward model that jointly predicts vehicle intents and a three-way execution relation (parallel, sequential, mutually exclusive) between co-active intents, using a multilingual ModernBERT-style encoder plus a small calibration relation head. This targets the underexplored question of how multiple intents should be executed in cars, not just which intents occur.

entry.title: SafeRank-ReID: Candidate-Conditioned Re-Ranking under Identity Conflicts for Multimodal Person Re-Identification

author.name: Yizhi Wang, Zixuan Li, Zhuwen Chen, Feiwei Qin

entry.summary: SafeRank-ReID tackles conflicting inputs in multimodal person re-identification that retain visual quality but carry incorrect identity signals, which query-level modality reliability estimation misses. It introduces candidate-conditioned evidence arbitration to capture how each modality supports different gallery candidates and applies safe re-ranking.

entry.title: Mind the Gaps: State-Guided Supervision Allocation for Object Detection Dataset Distillation

author.name: Jiehui Xie, Zhengxun Jin, Jiahao Zhang, Yuxuan Luan, Dongshen Han, Caiyan Qin, Sung-Ho Bae, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: SGSA reformulates object detection dataset distillation as a dataset-level progressive supervision allocation problem, establishing class-scale supervision quotas to avoid redundant supervision and uneven coverage under tight image budgets. It explicitly accounts for accumulated supervision across the distilled set rather than per-image informativeness alone.

entry.title: Splitting Belief Bases Conditionally based on Constraints for c-Representations and their Solutions

author.name: Lars-Phillip Spiegel, Christoph Beierle, Gabriele Kern-Isberner, Alexander Hahn

entry.summary: The paper introduces conditional constraint splittings for belief bases in symbolic AI, extending constraint splittings to allow subbases to share conditionals, and identifies safe and fully localized subclasses. These enable local and independent solving of the constraint satisfaction problem specifying c-representations, a high-quality ranking-based inference mechanism. This localizes reasoning and computation to relevant subbases.

entry.title: Do Candlestick Charts Suffice? The Incremental Economic Value of Technical Indicators in Stock Return Prediction

author.name: Peng Liu and Yanyan Zheng

entry.summary: Tests whether trading volume and manually constructed technical indicators add incremental economic value beyond raw OHLC candlestick data for stock return prediction, using 3.36 million samples from 1,707 Chinese A-share stocks encoded as multi-channel images. The main analysis uses a 2D CNN with complementary logistic and other checks.

entry.title: Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood

author.name: Huiming Zhang, Longkun Hao

entry.summary: Proposes a log-truncated likelihood for finite mixture regression that yields a smooth residual-robust estimator stable under Laplace, Pareto, or infinite-variance heavy-tailed errors. The construction uses a Catoni-type score integrated and exponentiated into a proper location-scale density with EM-compatible responsibilities and provable tail envelopes.

entry.title: Place-Revisit Consistency Evaluation of Reference Poses

author.name: Jianzhu Huai, Yujia Zhang, Grzegorz Jozkow

entry.summary: Presents a method for auditing reference trajectories in odometry/SLAM benchmark datasets by checking whether relative poses at revisited places agree with sensor-derived relative poses from lidar registration and stereo pose estimation. Applied to KITTI Odometry and SNAIL Radar, it identifies regions where public reference poses are inconsistent with sensor data, which can bias system evaluations.

entry.title: Age and Gender Estimation from Face and Ocular Smartphone Images via Identity Transfer and Ordinal Learning

author.name: Fernando Alonso-Fernandez, Kevin Hernandez-Diaz, Jose Maria Buades, Josef Bigun

entry.summary: The study evaluates how identity-recognition representations transfer to age and gender estimation from smartphone face and ocular images, showing domain-matched identity pre-training outperforms ImageNet or scratch initialization. It also introduces an ordinal loss exploiting age-group ordering that consistently improves 1-off accuracy across architectures.

entry.title: SIAMBA: A Pseudo-Siamese Mamba-based Deep Learning Network for Multimodal Flood Change Detection

author.name: Muhammad Fasih Ishfaq, Giulio Weikmann, and Lorenzo Bruzzone

entry.summary: SIAMBA is a pseudo-siamese Mamba-based network for bi-temporal flood change detection that fuses Sentinel-2 multispectral and Sentinel-1 SAR imagery with modality-specific encoders to handle cross-modal heterogeneity, clouds, speckle, and illumination variability. It targets rapid disaster response where weather-independent structural information is crucial.

entry.title: CART: Clustering-based Analysis of Recurring narratives for Taxonomy construction

author.name: Aggelos Semoglou, Thomas Tselentis, John Pavlopoulos

entry.summary: CART is a computational pipeline that extracts political narratives from parliamentary discourse and builds a data-driven taxonomy using semantic encoding, unsupervised confidence filtering, LLM-based narrative extraction, and clustering. Applied to Greek Parliament proceedings on the 2023 Tempi train crash, it identifies ten recurring narrative families around responsibility and accountability.

entry.title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization

author.name: Adeep Hande, Shaghayegh Agah, Neeraj Sharma, Karina Halevy, Sardar Hamidian

entry.summary: The authors address popularity bias in sequential recommenders by using LLMs to generate synthetic interactions for under-served long-tail and cold-start item groups. They formulate group-specific augmentation as a constrained optimization problem balancing NDCG@20 and coverage, and show that per-group optimal strategies are not additive when combined. The work also ablates LLM scale and augmentation choices.

entry.title: Genome-to-Image Translation: Reconstructing Escherichia coli Morphology from Genomic Sequences

author.name: Son T. Huynh, Thuy T. Le, Thu H. A. Huynh, Binh T. Nguyen

entry.summary: The authors formulate predicting E. coli colony appearance from genome sequences as conditional image generation, encoding assembled contigs into a 768-dimensional vector via a frozen genomic language model and synthesizing colony images with a conditional WGAN-GP. The motivation is faster antimicrobial-resistance triage, since morphology traces resistance and sequencing is increasingly available. A creative cross-modal genomics-to-vision pipeline.

entry.title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks

author.name: Burak Demirel and Yu Wang and Pablo Soldati

entry.summary: This position-style article proposes a triadic agentic AI framework for mobile networks, co-designing intent management and fulfillment through an LLM-powered interpreter, an optimizer, and a fast controller. It maps the design space of each agent and how the workflow translates high-level network intents into concrete optimization and control actions.

entry.title: Why flattening the P-value histogram works: a theory of the standard-deviation optimization in tensor-decomposition-based unsupervised feature extraction

author.name: Y-h. Taguchi, Turki Turki

entry.summary: This paper provides the first theoretical justification for a widely used heuristic in tensor-decomposition-based unsupervised feature extraction, where the null standard deviation is tuned so the P-value histogram of unselected genes is flat. The authors prove that HOSVD yields a component reproducing the experimental design and that background gene singular vector components are approximately normal with an explicit standard deviation. This closes a longstanding gap between practice and theory in genomics feature selection.

entry.title: Multimodal Violence Understanding and Temporal Retrieval in Movies with Adaptive Audio-Visual Fusion

author.name: Jiaqian Li and Rohitash Chandra

entry.summary: The authors develop a multimodal framework that classifies violence severity, predicts multiple violence types, and temporally localizes violent events in long untrimmed movies, fusing temporally aligned audio and visual features via attention-based adaptive fusion with Transformer temporal modeling. This supports content moderation and audience protection at scale. It is a competent applied video-understanding contribution addressing localization in full-length films rather than short clips.

entry.title: Benchmarking EEG feature families for ADHD research in children and adolescents: performance and explainability across attention tasks

author.name: Javier Sanchis, Jorge Garc\'ia-Carrasco, \'Alvaro Navarro, Tahar Kechadi, Juan Trujillo

entry.summary: This benchmarking study compares seven EEG feature families and four combinations for discriminating ADHD recruitment groups across attention tasks, using repeated nested participant-held-out evaluation and bootstrap-corrected tests across four cohorts of 123-140 participants. It also assesses the stability of held-out explanations. The rigorous evaluation protocol is a methodological contribution to reproducible EEG biomarker research.

entry.title: AERIN: Aerial Instance Navigation with a Visual World Model

author.name: Zhenzhen Jiao, Rui Tian, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: AERIN is a visual world model for UAV navigation to image-referenced targets, using action-conditioned prediction to guide search from high altitude while adjusting viewpoint for better instance verification. It uses compact fixed-size representations to avoid the cost of repeatedly predicting dense visual details.

entry.title: MemVanta: Memory-Efficient CPU Inference for Quantized GGUF Language Models

author.name: Saurav Singla, Aarav Singla, Advik Gupta, Parnika Gupta

entry.summary: MemVanta is an experimental C++20 runtime for quantized GGUF language models that treats memory residency as a first-class objective, using memory-mapped access, bounded caching, quantized execution paths, and paged KV state. Against a pinned llama.cpp baseline on OpenLLaMA 7B Q4_0, it roughly halves peak resident memory (~3.8GB vs ~7.2GB) on CPU-only execution.

entry.title: Do as I Say, Not as You Do: Assessing Public Versus Practitioner Perspectives on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Language Technologies

author.name: Tyler Loakman and Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: This survey compares practitioner (academics and industry) and general-public views on AI benefit and risk, machine consciousness, AI art, and use of copyrighted material in training. It highlights systematic gaps between those building AI and those most affected by it.

entry.title: DRU-Mixer: An Explainable Dilated Recurrent Unit-Based Mixer Model with Focal Loss for EEG-Based Interictal Epileptiform Discharges Detection

author.name: Aditya P Kamath, Xiaohui Tao, Taotao Cai, Prabal Datta Barua, Sreeni Chadalavada, Abdulkadir Sengur

entry.summary: DRU-Mixer is a deep learning architecture combining a convolutional front end, dilated recurrent units, and mixer modules to automatically detect and classify interictal epileptiform discharges in EEG, with focal loss handling class imbalance. It aims to reduce expert labeling burden and inter-rater variability in epilepsy diagnosis. The work is a competent applied medical signal-processing contribution with an explainability angle.

entry.title: Dynamics-Guided Conditional MeanFlow from Regional Interaction to Internal Revision and Its Application to CT Imaging

author.name: Md Shifatul Ahsan Apurba, Md Selim, Jin Chen

entry.summary: IRCMF is a conditional MeanFlow framework for medical image enhancement in which the decoder predicts signed interval velocity and a velocity-change cue to guide recurrent internal feature revision via dynamics-conditioned graphs. This allows spatially varying computational effort where fixed-depth one-step flow models spend uniformly.

entry.title: SONATI: Spatio-temporal ocean neighbourhood asymmetric transformer for imputation of sparse, tabular data with uncertainty

author.name: Yvonne Jenniges and Boris Peter Koch and Maike Sonnewald and Sebastian Maneth

entry.summary: SONATI is a masked, factorized time-space transformer for imputing sparse tabular oceanographic data, operating on local time-space neighborhoods to reduce complexity versus global attention. It provides aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty estimates and works in principle on both gridded and unstructured data, though evaluated only on gridded North Atlantic data. It offers a practical domain tool for geoscience data pipelines.

entry.title: AV-FLARE: Feature-Level Reliability Estimation for Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Ines Jemmali, Alaa Nfissi, Wassim Bouachir and Nizar Bouguila

entry.summary: AV-FLARE explicitly estimates fine-grained reliability scores across temporal and feature dimensions of audio-visual inputs before temporal modeling, using a supervised reliability network plus an unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model. These scores modulate feature representations to handle noisy audio, occluded video, and sparse affective cues. The framework makes input reliability an explicit first-class signal in multimodal emotion recognition.

entry.title: Digital Knockoffs

author.name: Niuniu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes calibrating LLM-based social simulation agents to multidimensional trait profiles via activation steering: extracting per-trait steering directions, learning a mapping from steering strengths to measured trait scores, and searching interventions with Bayesian optimization. Evaluated on Big Five personality scores of 500 respondents, outperforming prompting and steering baselines on mean absolute error. Improves fidelity of synthetic personas for social science simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Unit Tests: Path-Aware Rubric-Guided LLM Autograding of Notebooks

author.name: Salman Hajizada, Mohammed Yusuf Ansari, Gianni Di Caro

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-based autograder for flow-structured Jupyter notebook assessments that generates rubrics from reference solutions and applies a softening pass so legitimate alternative solution paths are not penalized. Grades question groups in single calls so later answers are judged against the student's earlier choices.

entry.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization

author.name: Xingyu Zhou and Roberto Armellin and Jack Yarndley and Xiangyu Li

entry.summary: The paper develops two neural approximators for low-thrust multi-asteroid mission design: one predicting maximum admissible initial mass for transfer capacity, and one predicting mass-dependent propellant consumption across mission legs. These reduce errors substantially and enable fast coupled sequencing-and-trajectory search for spacecraft mission planning.

entry.title: Learning Optical Flow with Task-Oriented Feature Adaptation

author.name: Mengtan Zhang, Dazhong Wang, Haoran Zhang, Hongbo Zhao, Yuhang Ming, Weihao Yuan, Wei Ye, Hanli Wang, Rui Fan

entry.summary: TO-Flow adapts general-purpose encoder features for optical flow by separately aligning matching and context features with their task requirements, using channel modulation and affinity-based spatial reorganization that distinguishes motion-region interiors from boundaries. This corrects systematic mismatches when off-the-shelf visual features are reused for correspondence and context.

entry.title: AdapToC: A Unified Framework for Multi-Task Visual Token Communication

author.name: Zhicheng Liu, Chenliang Wu, Zhouxiang Zhao, Zhaohui Yang, and Zhaoyang Zhang

entry.summary: AdapToC makes wireless streaming of discrete visual tokens robust to fading and noisy channels by replacing hard CRC erasures with soft bit posteriors, aligning codebook geometry to the channel via Pseudo-Gray relabeling and Halton dispersion, all in a single-pass transceiver without altering tokenizer weights. This restores multi-tier rate-distortion tradeoffs for token-based synthesis, recognition, and embodied perception over wireless links.

entry.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters

author.name: Amarnath R

entry.summary: The paper addresses visual world models' inability to distinguish visually identical characters with different dynamics by proposing an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation via contrastive learning. It introduces ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters organized in look-alike groups differing only in dynamics, to test few-shot body inference. The work targets action prediction for animated characters from minimal context.

entry.title: Controlled One-Click Benchmarking and Post-Fusion Recalibration for Support-Conditioned Medical Segmentation

author.name: Wang-Chi-Shiun, Wei-Huan Hu, Liu-En-Chi, Liu Zhi Shun, ChengYi Peng, Shin-Jye Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces a controlled one-click benchmarking protocol for sparse-prompt medical segmentation with matched sample budgets, shared splits, and threshold-free Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC metrics, plus a Support-Aware Recalibration (SAR) block appended to MultiverSeg. SAR improves over protocol-matched baselines on BUSI, NerveUS, and Kvasir-SEG.

entry.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer

author.name: Bo Zhang and Amy Zhaomei Zhang

entry.summary: JAX-Nano is a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable solver for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation, covering steady-state and transient regimes with flexible meshes, boundary conditions, and scattering, and enabling gradients with respect to transport properties and boundary conditions. It addresses nanoscale heat transfer where Fourier's law fails.

entry.title: GAG-Net: Graph-Based Anatomical Guidance Network for Pharyngeal Area Segmentation in VFSS Images

author.name: JunYeong Park, Myung Woo Park, Byung Chan Lee, Hyung Jin Chang, Sang-Il Choi

entry.summary: GAG-Net automates segmentation of the pharyngeal area at rest in videofluoroscopic swallowing images, a biomarker that could replace costly CT/MRI assessment of sarcopenic dysphagia in elderly patients. The method translates an implicit clinical measurement into explicit landmark specifications through a clinically informed annotation protocol.

entry.title: Tissot indicatrix for location encoders: Characterizing local distortion in learned geographic embeddings

author.name: Guofeng Cao and Gengchen Mai

entry.summary: The authors adapt Tissot's indicatrix, a classic cartographic distortion tool, to characterize how location encoders distort geographic space by fitting local ellipses from encoder outputs at equal distances in 32 directions. Anisotropy and orientation of these ellipses reveal local distortion that can propagate into downstream geospatial applications.

entry.title: AgroVG+: Generalized Visual Grounding in Agriculture with Region-Supervised Action Generation

author.name: Haocheng Li, Juepeng Zheng, Guilong Xiao, Kaiqi Du, Gengmeng Pu, Haohuan Fu, Jianxi Huang

entry.summary: AgroVG+ contributes an expert-annotated visual grounding dataset for agriculture (7,404 images, 10,081 queries across six scene families, including multi-target and target-absent cases) and ReSAG, a framework coupling regional evidence supervision with explicit box generation and termination decisions.

entry.title: Ride on Anything: Contact-Coupled Monocular 4D Reconstruction of a Rider and Horse in Camera and World Frames

author.name: Zehang Weng, Ci Li

entry.summary: Ride on Anything is a training-free method for reconstructing a horse and rider from a single video, coupling frozen rider and mount estimators (SAM 3D Body and 4DEquine) through a shared camera and joint optimization to fix along-axis interpenetration and jitter artifacts. It generalizes to reconstructing a person riding an animal.

entry.title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Tiwari Ankit Satyaprakash, Adamya Shyam, Vikas Kumar, Bharti Rana, Venkateswara Rao Kagita

entry.summary: MoR4Rec applies a mixture-of-recursion approach to sequential recommendation, adaptively allocating computation depth per interaction item instead of applying uniform transformer depth. This addresses the mismatch between heterogeneous user behavior complexity and fixed-depth architectures, improving efficiency and capacity utilization.

entry.title: RISC-V R-Extension: Advancing Efficiency with Rented-Pipeline for Edge DNN Processing

author.name: Won Hyeok Kim, Hyeong Jin Kim and Tae Hee Han

entry.summary: The paper introduces a RISC-V instruction set extension for efficient DNN inference on edge devices, featuring rented-pipeline stages and architectural pipeline registers that reduce latency and memory access frequency. New custom instructions support these mechanisms, offering an alternative to full NPUs in lightweight edge devices.

entry.title: CogEvo-Edu: Cognitive Evolution Educational Multi-Agent Collaborative System

author.name: Yefeng Wu, Yuchen Song, Yecheng Zhao, Ling Wu, Shan Wan

entry.summary: CogEvo-Edu is a hierarchical multi-agent tutoring system for complex STEM domains like digital signal processing, comprising cognitive perception, knowledge evolution, and meta-control layers that couple retrieval, memory, and control. It aims to maintain coherent long-term student models and adapt teaching strategies over extended interactions.

entry.title: Scalar Tuned Lens Summaries Offer Limited Incremental Value for Mid-Generation Abstention

author.name: Khurram Khalil, Khaza Anuarul Hoque

entry.summary: Evaluates whether scalar summaries (entropy, divergence) of intermediate transformer states help predict eventual response correctness for mid-generation abstention, comparing against final-state and raw intermediate-state probes under matched causal evaluation. Across eight instruction-tuned models on MATH-500, raw intermediate states help while scalar-only probes generally underperform, suggesting caution about cheap tuned-lens features.

entry.title: Fin-RSI: A Unified Library of Financial Skills, Checks, and Self-Improvement for LLM Agents

author.name: Wanghao Ye, Shwai He, Sihan Chen, Yiting Wang, Bowei Tian, Guoheng Sun, Ziyi Wang, Ziyao Wang, Yexiao He, Zheyu Shen, Meng Liu, Yuning Zhang, Meng Feng, Yifei Dong, Yanhong Qian, Yang Wang, Siyuan Peng, Yilong Dai, Zhenle Duan, Joshua Liu, Lang Xiong, Aarosh Das, Zhaoyi Liu, Daeun Jung, Aditya Sarkar, Parastoo Pilevar, Xiaochuan Gong, Yancheng Zhu, Yingying Fan, Qiong Wang, Ang Li

entry.summary: Fin-RSI is a unified Python library giving LLM agents discoverable financial tools spanning market analysis, forecasting, portfolio construction, and trading research, with shared interfaces, natural-language tool discovery, built-in checks, and feedback-based program improvement. It aims to reduce the fragmentation of financial software for reliable agent workflows.

entry.title: When Source-Domain Validation Fails to Transfer: A Staged Study of Hyperparameter Selection

author.name: Veet Zaveri

entry.summary: This paper asks whether withholding entire source domains during hyperparameter validation yields better selections on unseen target domains, running a factorial experiment and a staged study with complete target-performance landscapes on four image benchmarks. The domain-aware fitness measure provides no consistent advantage, and the study clarifies when source-domain validation transfers.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Prompt Configuration: Alternating Policy Learning for Adaptive Topology-Based Prompting in Few-Shot Graph Learning

author.name: Yizhuo Ma, Yihong Huang, Rongzheng Wang, Jiakai Li, Ke Qin, Shuang Liang, Jie Shao

entry.summary: This paper identifies two challenges in topology-based graph prompting: asymmetric performance effects and coupled configuration selection between prompt content and propagation structure. It proposes TTPR, a two-stage RL framework alternating between two policies to generate adaptive prompt configurations for few-shot graph tasks. The work improves flexibility of graph prompt learning beyond fixed prompt setups.

entry.title: TeleMultiStream: An Integrated Robot Teleoperation System with Low-Latency Multi-Stream Video Feedback

author.name: Chenchen Lv, Lingchen Hu, Yaosai Zhang, Chunlan Li, Gengkui Wei, Wei Xin, Li Li

entry.summary: TeleMultiStream is a robot teleoperation system combining multi-stream WebRTC video feedback with UDP pose downlink, supporting heterogeneous video sources with buffer reuse, bounded queues, and native XR rendering. It achieves 60-66 ms median glass-to-glass latency in wired-LAN tests, supporting high-quality demonstration data collection for embodied intelligence and DAgger-based corrective learning. Low-latency teleoperation infrastructure is a key enabler for scalable robot learning data.

entry.title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning

author.name: Byunggu Yu and Justin Kim

entry.summary: DAWIN is a continuous-time neuron primitive replacing standard layers in MLPs, Transformers, and GNNs, coupling spatial projection with elapsed-time-dependent wave excitation integrated via closed-form damped evolution without numerical ODE solvers. The authors derive closed-form gradients and establish bounded-input bounded-output stability under positive damping.

entry.title: STMemoLLM: A Spatial-Temporal Memory-Augmented LLM for Robust Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Jian Zhou, Binqing Wu, Zongjiang Shang, Wanghui Qiu, Dongliang Cui, Chenxi Jin, Yue Yu, Xinyi Fu, Ling Chen

entry.summary: STMemoLLM augments an LLM with spatial-temporal memory prototypes that compress inputs into summary tokens and extract reliable dynamics from residual signals, aiming for robust traffic forecasting under input perturbations. A memory-enhanced tokenizer encodes prototypes and sensor characteristics into attention biases to guide adaptive compression of corrupted inputs.

entry.title: WaDiS: Boundary-Preserving Diffusion Segmentation via Multi-Scale Wavelet Conditioning and Frequency-Aware Gating

author.name: Qiang Gao, Yi Wang, Yong Zhang, Bin Fang, Yong Li, Lan Du, Cunjian Chen

entry.summary: WaDiS is a wavelet-conditioned latent diffusion framework for medical image segmentation that uses multi-scale wavelet conditioning and frequency-aware gating to preserve fine anatomical boundaries and multi-scale structural information. The lossless nature of wavelet features helps retain semantic priors under difficult clinical imaging conditions.

entry.title: Robust Lateral String Stability and Error Attenuation for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons

author.name: Sixu Li, Swaroop Darbha, Yang Zhou

entry.summary: The paper develops a robust lateral string stability framework for heterogeneous vehicle platoons, using arc-length-based feedback linearization to give all vehicles identical nominal lateral error dynamics. It defines robust L2 lateral string stability with platoon-length-uniform error bounds and derives sufficient conditions for downstream error attenuation.

entry.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks

author.name: Gwangui Hong, Seonho An, Seonkyu Lim, KyungTae Lim, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: PseuDRAGON supports financial-data pseudonymization in closed networks by keeping confirmed judgments and learned rules outside a fixed local LLM and reusing them via exact-name lookup and learned rules, with an expert-review workflow grounded in institutional policy and privacy law. Rules improved label reuse from 75 to 83 without reuse errors in evaluation on 92 columns.
