entry.title: Placing the Control Plane: Cloud-Native Federated Learning Across Batch-Scheduled HPC

author.name: Paul J. Wright, Huw Day, Ryan K. Daniels, Simon Li, Ruairidh MacLeod, Rob Baxter, Abdelwahab Kawafi, Richard Lane, Christopher Woods, Sadaf R. Alam

entry.summary: This systems paper characterizes the placement asymmetry between long-lived federated-learning control planes and short-lived batch-scheduled HPC allocations in national supercomputing contexts like the UK AIRR, showing the coordination server can sit on neutral infrastructure while client processes must stay inside site trust boundaries. It demonstrates a cross-silo federation spanning HPC centers using outbound-only connections.

entry.title: Bayesian sequential decision-making for adaptive early warning of bridge failure risk

author.name: Teng Li, James L. Beck, Yong Huang, Hui Li, Hongju Han

entry.summary: Formulates early warning of increased bridge failure risk as a Bayesian sequential decision-making problem, unifying probabilistic state transition models, observation prediction, and cost models with a threshold-based decision strategy. This moves beyond passive detection against fixed safety limits by accounting for evolving uncertainties and the economic consequences of warning decisions.

entry.title: Co-speech Gesture Attribute Annotation with 3D Human Mesh Recovery

author.name: Frances Yung and Muhammad Naufilr

entry.summary: Automates annotation of ten co-speech gesture attributes in video using 3D human mesh recovery from SAM 3D Body, via AI-assisted geometric rules and a graph convolutional network, evaluated on 2,020 gestures. Physically defined attributes reach inter-annotator-level agreement with experts, while attributes requiring higher-level multimodal inference remain harder.

entry.title: A High-Resolution UAV Benchmark Dataset and Baseline Evaluation for Teak Crown Segmentation in Western Ghats Tropical Forests

author.name: Anand S Sahadevan, Sunita Arya, Anup Kumar Das, Bimal Kumar Bhattacharya, S Manthira Moorthi

entry.summary: Introduces TeakTreeNet, a benchmark dataset for binary teak-tree segmentation from 2cm-resolution drone imagery in tropical forests, with rigorous multi-seed evaluation of four segmentation architectures. SegFormer sets a new SOTA (F1 0.938, IoU 0.968), and scratch training outperforms ImageNet-pretrained baselines, avoiding pretraining overhead.

entry.title: CHICO: Bridging Sparse Metadata and Multimodal Evidence in Cultural Heritage Collections

author.name: Vagner In\'acio de Oliveira and Paula Dornhofer Paro Costa

entry.summary: CHICO is a multimodal dataset of over 60,000 cultural heritage records from Europeana, pairing curated catalog fields with images and contextual information to support evidence-grounded description generation. It addresses sparse, heterogeneous metadata and broken media links that hinder reproducible multimodal AI research on cultural collections.

entry.title: Deneb-Vritra: Descriptions, Edges and Names Examined by Blocking Via Restoring Token Representations and Attention

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Akhil P, Shahina Shaik

entry.summary: Using Laya, a 421M-parameter multiple-choice encoder, this mechanistic-interpretability study locates where the model follows an option's name over its contradicting description. Via name-swapping interventions on synthetic questions and attention blocking in layers 14-17, the authors cut the name shortcut from 67% to 16% on a sample. A focused circuit-level analysis of spurious shortcut behavior in option-scoring models.

entry.title: Spectral Regularization Beyond Ridge Regression

author.name: Kathryn Vasilaky, Walter Vasilaky

entry.summary: The authors study Inclusive Ridge, a two-parameter spectral regularization family containing ridge and iterated Tikhonov regression. They derive exact finite-sample coefficient risk, conditions under which tuning the extra filter-shape parameter lowers risk, and show oracle-tuned ridge is generically suboptimal within the family, with a continuous exponential filter emerging in a joint limit. This offers a principled extension of the most widely used regularizer in statistics.

entry.title: Wearable environmental sensing to forecast how legged systems will interact with upcoming terrain

author.name: Michael D. Murray, James Tung, Richard W. Nuckols

entry.summary: A small study (8 subjects) uses a shank-mounted RGB-D camera and instrumented insoles with a CNN-RNN to forecast foot center-of-pressure and time-of-impact up to 250ms before foot-streak during stair transitions. The work targets predictive control for assistive wearable and legged systems.

entry.title: ABCoord: An Artificial Bee Colony (ABC)-Based Decentralized Distributed Two-Layer Decision-Making Architecture for the Coordination of AI Agents

author.name: Dervis Karaboga, Bugra Alperen Uluirmak

entry.summary: ABCoord adapts the artificial bee colony algorithm as a two-layer decentralized coordination architecture for multi-agent LLM systems, aiming to avoid central bottlenecks while keeping communication costs low as agent counts grow. Experiments show improved coordination compared to alternatives. Bio-inspired coordination for multi-agent systems is interesting but the evaluation scope appears limited.

entry.title: The UNIFESP Chest CT Fatty Liver Dataset

author.name: Augusto Sarquis Serpa, Mariana Ramos Scolari, Eduardo Moreno Judice de Mattos Farina, Eduardo Caminha Nunes, Felipe Matsuoka, Felipe Campos Kitamura, Nitamar Abdala

entry.summary: Describes a public dataset of 285 unenhanced CT studies (99,883 images) from 264 patients with binary labels for hepatic steatosis assigned via liver-spleen attenuation comparison, provided as de-identified DICOM. The dataset supported a 2022 Kaggle competition and enables incidental fatty liver detection research on chest CT.

entry.title: Click and Count: Multimodal Prototype Adaptation for Class-Agnostic Object Counting

author.name: Amani Aifi, Wassim Bouachir, Ahmed Zgaren and Nizar Bouguila

entry.summary: This paper proposes a class-agnostic object counting framework that accepts visual exemplars, text descriptions, or both, expanding a single click into an object mask via a frozen segmentation model. An iterative prototype-refinement pipeline fuses text at every step to specify the counting target. It unifies several prior interaction modalities into one pipeline for flexible object counting.

entry.title: On Monotonic Hamming Sphere Landscapes

author.name: Dominic Wilson

entry.summary: This theory paper introduces Monotonic Hamming Sphere Landscapes, binary fitness landscapes whose fitness is nonincreasing with distance from a unique optimum, encompassing OneMax and related unitation functions. It counts Hamming sphere encodings and proves that for the elitist (1+1) EA, certain MHSLs share OneMax's optimization-time distribution, making them the easiest landscapes at low mutation rates. This formalizes which landscape structures yield easy evolutionary optimization.

entry.title: MACE: Memory-Augmented Crop-Disease Evaluation of Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Tirtho Roy, Shreyan Ganguly, Muhammad Arbab Arshad, Nikhil Bhattacharya, Soumik Sarkar

entry.summary: MACE is a training-free method that augments frozen vision-language models for crop disease diagnosis with a memory of symptom descriptions paired with labels, retrieving only text so the query is the sole image processed. This improves case-level symptom variability coverage over static knowledge bases.

entry.title: How many mistakes does it take to learn an interval? Exact Littlestone dimensions of intervals and their unions

author.name: Miit Daga, Swarna Priya Ramu

entry.summary: This theory paper exactly determines the Littlestone dimension of discrete intervals and unions of intervals, deriving a three-regime law for the minimum size on which d mistakes can be forced as a function of switch budget k. It also shows the natural binary-search learner is not optimal for this problem.

entry.title: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems under Governance Opacity

author.name: Pedro Pinacho-Davidson

entry.summary: This paper argues that corporate-governance-focused and model-inspection-focused oversight both fail under AI-as-a-Service opacity, where deployers cannot audit training or internal operations. It proposes an operational assurance framework inspired by Zero-Trust cybersecurity principles, shifting auditing to the application layer where risk is observable and contextualized. The work is a conceptual/governance contribution for real-world LLM system assurance.

entry.title: MQCODet: Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization for UAV-Based RGB-T Tiny Pedestrian Detection

author.name: Hui Li, Jianbo Ma, Hui Luo, Guanglin Qi, Zhixing Wang, Haorui Zuo, Jianlin Zhang

entry.summary: MQCODet targets tiny pedestrian detection in UAV-based RGB-thermal imagery, addressing modality quality imbalance and spatial misalignment by coupling feature fusion with object localization rather than treating modality quality only as a fusion prior. The method extends modality quality guidance into a collaborative optimization across fusion and localization. It targets improved robustness under complex aerial observation conditions.

entry.title: Beyond Invoice Volumes: Temporal Network Structure, Maturity Concentration, and Systemic Liquidity Exposure in SME Trade-Credit Networks

author.name: Sai Srikanth Madugula, Peplluis Esteva de la Rosa, Daya Shankar

entry.summary: This paper analyzes 749,952 B2B trade-credit invoices (EUR 99.7B) from 2012-2023 to build a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator capturing temporal synchronization and counterparty concentration in SME liquidity risk. It reveals extreme value skew (top 1% hold ~81% of value) and applies network science methods to financial systemic risk.

entry.title: DMPT-Swarm: A Directional Mass-Preserving Transform for Decentralized Swarm Navigation in Obstacle Environments

author.name: Jacob Lee, Samuel Sutphin, Haroon Malik, Chang Liu, Pingping Zhu

entry.summary: DMPT-Swarm is a decentralized swarm control framework that adapts a precomputed macroscopic GMM trajectory to obstacles via a directional mass-preserving transform on Wasserstein-2 transport, with each agent then following a local artificial potential field controller without communication. Simulations demonstrate obstacle-aware navigation with reduced communication and computational burden.

entry.title: BO-COMM: Bidirectional Optical System for Simultaneous Localization and Communication in Swarm Robotics

author.name: Cheng Hu, Haotian Wu, Qi Lin, Manrui Zheng, Shigang Yue, Tao Zou and Jigen Peng

entry.summary: BO-COMM is an optical system for swarm robots combining pose estimation and dynamic state reporting: cameras observe LED arrays on Colias IV robots, ring-based voting estimates centers, spatial LED patterns encode orientation and state, and a projector plus infrared module supply environmental cues and commands. It sidesteps wireless channel contention in dense swarms. The contribution is a hardware-software systems integration for swarm experimentation.

entry.title: CFANet: Learning Conflict-Free Weather Adapters for All-Weather Image Restoration

author.name: Minglong Xue, Wenchao Yan, Guoan Guan, Palaiahnakote Shivakumara, Yirui Wu

entry.summary: CFANet handles compositional weather degradations (rain, haze, snow co-occurring) via a Weather Mixture Router predicting non-exclusive composition weights and a Shared-Private Weather Adapter composing common and weather-private adapters. This enables open-compositional all-weather image restoration beyond single-label weather modeling.

entry.title: MobileNeTTT: a Lightweight DNN-based Time-To-Transit Estimator for Visual Navigation

author.name: Chiara Boretti, Philippe Bich, Manuel Morteo, Roberto Tron, John Baillieul

entry.summary: MobileNeTTT is a lightweight neural network that estimates Time-To-Transit, a bio-inspired depth proxy computable from a monocular camera, for mobile robot navigation. The method uses the full field of view, is robust to camera rotation, and adapts to path geometry and obstacles, offering a simpler alternative to large depth foundation models.

entry.title: Decoding Funded Research: Comparative Analysis of Topic Models and Uncovering the Effect of Gender and Geographic Location

author.name: Shirin Tavakoli Kafiabad and Andrea Schiffauerova and Ashkan Ebadi

entry.summary: The study compares LDA, Structural Topic Modelling, and BERTopic on 18 years of NSERC funded research proposals and introduces COFFEE, a novel algorithm enabling covariate effect estimation for BERTopic. It analyzes how gender and geographic location relate to funded research topics in the context of equity, diversity, and inclusion goals.

entry.title: Frequency-domain Event-based Imaging for Selective Surveillance

author.name: Megan Birch, James Rick, Adrish Kar, Jason Zutty, and Joseph L. Greene

entry.summary: FRIES is a neuromorphic processing framework that detects periodicity in event camera streams, such as rotor rotation and mechanical vibrations, to discriminate and monitor man-made objects for surveillance. It combines time gating, pixel-wise activity maps, ROI clustering, and frequency analysis to identify targets without processing full frames.

entry.title: Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming

author.name: Chris Tava

entry.summary: Reproduces the reported phenomenon that co-training LLM attackers and defenders reduces attack diversity, using a Qwen2.5-14B attacker with success-only reward against a Phi-4-mini DPO-trained defender over three runs on 26 AdvBench behaviors. It introduces an Attack Diversity Retention metric to quantify within-behavior diversity loss. The paper documents a reproducibility-oriented, small-scale study with nominal confidence intervals.

entry.title: LM2 Compiling a Language Model into Another Model Weights

author.name: Naman Chawla, Chhavi Dhiman

entry.summary: Presents LM2, which compiles a small trained story generator directly into added layers of a larger conversational host model by constraining the generator's arithmetic during training. Compared with executing the generator on an embedded processor, LM2 needs one host token per generated character versus roughly 25,000, though the compiled generator has slightly worse held-out prediction.

entry.title: Similarity-Constrained Reweighting for Complex Query Answering on Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Daniel Daza, Alberto Bernardi, Luca Costabello, Christophe Gueret, Michael Cochez, Martijn Schut

entry.summary: Extends complex query answering on knowledge graphs to support similarity constraints on an arbitrary query variable, and introduces SCORE, a lightweight, interpretable method based on a score-adjustment function requiring only two hyperparameters tuned on validation data. Experiments show effective incorporation of soft entity constraints into CQA models.

entry.title: Randomized Weighted Distance Nearest Neighbor Classification

author.name: Shayan Shafaei, Naeem Shahabi Sani, Chao Lan

entry.summary: RWNN randomizes the greedy ball-search of weighted distance nearest neighbor compression, cutting compression time to roughly 0.1-1% of the original while maintaining similar accuracy and retaining theoretical properties like consistency and generalization bounds. Experiments across multiple datasets support the efficiency-accuracy trade-off.

entry.title: Data-Quality-Aware Fundus Classification with Anatomy-Guided Glaucoma Assessment and Cross-Dataset Evaluation

author.name: Imdadul Haque Sourav, Marjana Jannat Miti, Md. Jehadul Islam Mony

entry.summary: The paper audits a fundus image dataset for duplicates and label conflicts, removing 942 images from 5,318, then trains nine-class classifiers and an anatomy-guided glaucoma specialist using segmentation maps and cup-to-disc features. Frozen models are evaluated externally on RFMiD and JSIEC to assess reliability beyond internal accuracy.

entry.title: Generalizable Variable-Rate Adaptation for Image Coding for Machines

author.name: Yui Tatsumi, Hiroshi Watanabe

entry.summary: The paper proposes a loss-agnostic distillation framework for variable-rate image coding for machines, using a pretrained fixed-rate ICM model as a frozen teacher and a student learning variable-rate behavior via importance-adaptive quantization. This enables continuous bitrate control with a single model without needing task-specific losses or downstream labels.

entry.title: Separating Genetic and Protein Evidence in Open Targets: An Auditable Re-ranking Study

author.name: Ye Ye

entry.summary: This study re-ranks Open Targets gene-disease associations for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's by scoring genetics-linked and protein-oriented evidence in separate channels before late fusion, rather than using the single integrated score. The separated approach improves representation of curated genetics-supported genes and removes symptomatic pharmacology controls from the top ranks. It demonstrates the value of auditable, channel-separated evidence scoring in biomedical target prioritization.

entry.title: Categorical Foundations of AI Agents

author.name: Yong Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a category-theoretic framework for AI agents, formally categorizing transformers, agents, and multi-agent orchestrations and choreographies, including their associated coalgebras and algebras. The approach follows the idea of separating intelligence from execution, aiming to give multi-agent systems rigorous mathematical foundations. Such formalism could help with compositional reasoning about agent systems, though its practical impact depends on future adoption.

entry.title: ReplaySAM: Zero-Shot 3D Particle-Pack Segmentation with SAM 2

author.name: Bogong Wang, Yulai Zhang, Philipp D. L\"osel, Andrew Kingston, Mark Knackstedt

entry.summary: ReplaySAM adapts the pretrained SAM 2 to zero-shot 3D segmentation of particle packs in X-ray computed tomography volumes, generating point prompts from foreground geometry and fusing predictions across slices without additional training. This addresses a labor-intensive materials-science workflow that normally requires manual correction or task-specific models.

entry.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Jelle De Moerloose, Anton Lambrecht, Adnan Shahid, Eli De Poorter

entry.summary: This work systematically compares range-time, range-Doppler, and time-Doppler representations from IEEE 802.15.4z UWB radar for contactless human activity recognition, with independently tuned processing per representation, and evaluates fusion gains across environments and activities at various computational costs. The authors release an open dataset to support replication.

entry.title: Teaching How to Reason, Beyond What to Answer: Evidence-Faithful On-Policy Distillation for streaming video understanding

author.name: Mengnan Liu, Sanping Zhou, Kun Xia, Jiaxuan Lin, Gang Hua, Le Wang

entry.summary: The paper addresses moment retrieval in videos, where sparse textual queries must be aligned with rich visual content that may contain multiple similar candidate segments. It proposes a Multi-Perspective Auxiliary Representation framework that enriches the single text input with auxiliary evidence to bridge the cross-modal alignment gap, with an on-policy distillation component for faithful reasoning.

entry.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow

author.name: Qinyi Zhang, Duanyu Feng, Yangshuai Wang, Hao Wang

entry.summary: IADR is a neural operator for the Allen-Cahn equation that preserves the phase-field structure through a diffusion-and-reaction target network, while a hypernetwork maps the interface width parameter epsilon to the target network weights. This enables a single model to cover a range of epsilon values without per-parameter retraining.

entry.title: Topology-Prior-Guided Regional Latent Dynamics for Transient Structural Response Prediction

author.name: Yuan Zhang, Mohammad Amin Nabian, Shaotong Fu, Yiding Liu, Chengcheng Chu, Xuelin Tao, Hua Li

entry.summary: TPLD is a surrogate model for predicting transient nonlinear structural responses, encoding mesh responses into topology-constrained regional latent variables with state-transition supervision and load conditioning for full-field time-history prediction. It targets large finite-element meshes and history-dependent mechanics where standard surrogates struggle.

entry.title: STAR: Structure-Aware Temporal Action Recovery for Point Supervised Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Yawar Rehman, Min Young Kim

entry.summary: STAR improves point-supervised temporal action localization by modeling internal temporal structure of actions with start, core, and end roles and temporal-difference attention to capture snippet changes. It also refines pseudo-label generation to reduce boundary ambiguity and over-extended proposals.

entry.title: MF-EDA: Joining Membership Functions to Adapt the Number of Distributions in Gaussian Estimation-of-Distribution Algorithms

author.name: Jun Zhang, Tong Qian, Hua Ding, Wei-Jie Yu, Xiao-Fang Liu, Jian-Yu Li

entry.summary: MF-EDA improves Gaussian estimation-of-distribution algorithms by building the search distribution from Gaussian membership functions joined by membership degrees, detecting bimodal directions among selected individuals and choosing one or two membership functions per direction via BIC and a separation test. This prevents premature convergence to the wide funnel on multi-funnel optimization landscapes.

entry.title: Inclusion of obstacles in ground point classification in ALS data for terrain models used for analysis of vehicle traversability

author.name: Mikael Lundb\"ack, Erik Wallin, Sima Mohtasami, Martin Servin, Mattias Nystr\"om, Henrik Persson

entry.summary: The paper evaluates ground point classification algorithms for airborne laser scanning data when obstacles like boulders must be distinguished from non-obstacles like bushes, in service of terrain models for offroad vehicle traversability. It highlights that existing algorithms designed for lower-density point clouds struggle with modern high-density data and obstacle/non-obstacle discrimination in forested terrain.

entry.title: Beyond Naming Accuracy: Template Composition and Species-Name Decisions

author.name: Junle li, Bochang zhang

entry.summary: Investigates how prompt-template composition, not just template count, changes the relative rankings of BioCLIP2 and BioCLIP 2.5 Huge in zero-shot species classification. Exhaustively comparing four-template subsets of an 80-template bank and a reviewed 24-template pool shows ranking reversals on a notable fraction of subsets, challenging single-number leaderboard conclusions.

entry.title: Intra-Class Diversity Loss for Person Re-Identification

author.name: Wei Zhou, BaXian Chen

entry.summary: Introduces an Intra-Class Diversity (ICD) loss for person re-identification that maximizes intra-class differences in classification-irrelevant directions, complementing the usual focus on intra-class compactness and inter-class separation. The class-weight-orthogonal diversity objective is claimed as a first for ReID.

entry.title: Screening for nonrigidity in structure from motion using projected reprojection residuals

author.name: \'I\~nigo Cirauqui-Viloria (Universidad de Zaragoza)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a diagnostic for detecting when scenes violate the static-scene assumption in structure from motion, by removing residual components explainable by small point/camera adjustments and temporal spatial trends, then measuring alignment with fixed spatiotemporal patterns. On four synthetic tubular families it detected all eight acquisitions with prescribed motion, outperforming reprojection-error magnitude summaries.

entry.title: Vetoes and missed agreements in language-model bargaining

author.name: Fuad Ali

entry.summary: In a three-representative bargaining game with 60 trials, a language model acting as proposer reliably requested mutually beneficial plans when at risk of loss, but often proposed plans that were vetoed; showing the proposer how many groups gained under each plan raised mutually beneficial agreements from 6/60 to 31/60. The single-model, small-scale design makes it a controlled probe of LLM bargaining behavior rather than a general evaluation.

entry.title: The Curved Exponential Family of Cylindrical Distributions: m-Projection, Curvature and a Test of the von Mises-Fisher Component

author.name: Amine M. Aboussalah

entry.summary: The paper studies a curved exponential family of cylindrical distributions generalizing the Mardia-Sutton model, where the directional component is von Mises-Fisher and the vector component is Gaussian with direction-dependent mean. It gives necessary and sufficient conditions for MLE existence and uniqueness, shows the estimator is a KL m-projection, and connects a residual gap to the classical score test. This is solid mathematical statistics for directional/cylindrical data.

entry.title: Persona Space Seems Blind to Cheating

author.name: unruly abstractions

entry.summary: An ARENA capstone project tested whether reward-hacking (cheating) behavior in LLMs is mediated by persona features, hypothesizing that cheating steps would drift to a distinct region of persona space. Running Qwen3.8-27B (an existing model released in August 2026) through CheatBench tasks and projecting activations onto mean-activation persona space, the authors found no separating signal. The negative result suggests current semantic persona characterizations fail to capture reward-hacking, without disproving the persona-mediated hypothesis.

entry.title: T-Tac: A Soft and Thin Active Thermal Tactile Sensor for Robotic In-Grasp Material Identification

author.name: Jiankun Li, Yu Feng, Yehui Liu, Meng Chen, Rui Luo, Guanglie Zhang, Jianshu Zhou and Wen Jung Li

entry.summary: T-Tac is a soft, film-based tactile sensor combining a polyimide heater with an ionic conductive temperature sensor to identify gripped materials via transient thermal responses, supported by thermal modeling and finite-element simulation plus loading experiments. It addresses material identification cases where vision alone fails.

entry.title: Projecting Beauty: Transferring Image Aesthetic Analysis onto 3D Heritage and Urban Scenes

author.name: Sophia Kovalenko, Alexander M. Rusnak, Vittoria Meroni, Yasmine Kroknes-Gomez, Fr\'ed\'eric Kaplan

entry.summary: This work extends 2D image aesthetic assessment to dense per-point aesthetic descriptions of 3D heritage and urban point clouds, comparing approaches that lift image model scores onto geometry versus training regression heads on frozen vision backbones. It addresses architectural design, urban planning, and conservation use cases while avoiding costly human labeling.

entry.title: Toward Open Room-Scale Scanning with Consumer LiDAR via Depth-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Minsuk Jang

entry.summary: This paper presents Mobile-LIO, an open depth-inertial odometry pipeline for on-device room scanning with consumer LiDAR that avoids the ARKit black box. Across seven ScanNet++ iPhone recordings it completed every scene with 0.2-2.0 m deviation, whereas six open-source LiDAR-inertial estimators failed or deviated at least 4.46 m in most runs.

entry.title: PestWeave: Linking Semantic Modeling and Evidence-Guided Text Modulation through Visual Prototypes for Fine-Grained Pest Learning

author.name: Xueheng Li, Yu Wang, Yuxiang Shen, Wen Xue, Rui Li, Jie Zhang, Chengjun Xie

entry.summary: PestWeave is a multimodal framework for fine-grained pest recognition that augments an RWKV architecture with semantic token grouping and auxiliary tokens in the visual pathway, while using visual prototypes to modulate which textual information is fused. This mitigates problems where complex backgrounds obscure cues and text contains information unsupported by the image.

entry.title: Green ACO: An Energy-Aware Ant Colony Optimisation for the MAX-SAT Problem with EI/J Scheduling and Thompson Sampling

author.name: Maroua Ogab, Nazim Abdeerhmane Aouni, Rayane Rahmat Errahmane Smara, Nour El Imane Elbar, Zakaria Soualah Mohammed, Malika Bessedik

entry.summary: Green ACO schedules three heuristic operators for MAX-SAT by expected improvement per joule, calibrated through offline dual-regime profiling and combined with Thompson sampling, to balance solution quality against energy cost. The work targets the environmental footprint of combinatorial optimization in carbon-intensive regions. Energy-aware optimization scheduling is a timely if narrow contribution.

entry.title: AMP-OD: Active Model Probing for Unsupervised Outlier Model Selection--Extended Version

author.name: Hong-Phuc Phan, Tuan-Anh Vu, Tung Kieu, Son Ha Xuan, Sean Bin Yang, Bin Yang, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: Proposes AMP-OD, a probe-then-commit framework for unsupervised outlier model selection that runs a few inexpensive probe detectors and uses their score patterns as target-dataset evidence before committing to a final detector, with a Leave-One-Out Family Probe Posterior to interpret unlabeled probe responses. Moves beyond static meta-features by conditioning selection on actual detector behavior. A methodologically clean improvement to a practical model-selection problem.

entry.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price

author.name: Mandar R. Nalavade, Gaurav S. Kasbekar, Koushik Kar

entry.summary: The paper formulates LEO satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem and proposes an RL-based branch-and-price framework with learned multiple-column selection to accelerate column generation while retaining exact pricing. It also contributes two lightweight heuristics for online and offline planning plus a local-search repair algorithm.

entry.title: FireDesmoke: Fire Smoke Removal via Real Smoke Transfer and Semantic Rectification

author.name: Chih-Chung Hsu, Rong-Lin Jian

entry.summary: FireDesmoke removes fire smoke from images by exploiting the spatial locality of real smoke: it calibrates smoke fields on real fire footage to synthesize training pairs over clean images, and uses pixel features to rectify tokens of a frozen foundation encoder where smoke corrupts semantics. This avoids hallucination of people or removal of flames that generative approaches can cause.

entry.title: Participant-Independent Validation of Smartphone Video and Wearable Inertial Sensing for Coach-Rated Running-Form Classification

author.name: Kian Lee, Eric Zhou

entry.summary: This study validates a low-cost pipeline using smartphone video and wearable IMU data to classify coach-rated running form across four cues, using participant-independent holdout splits with 294 recordings from 20 runners. Video-only LightGBM reaches modest macro F1 of 0.310, with IMU features providing some added value.

entry.title: Shoonya: Zero-Socket In-Process Small Language Models for Graph Databases with Schema-Epoch KV Caching, Live Catalog Logit Masking, and Verifier-Advantage Distillation

author.name: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

entry.summary: Presents Shoonya, commercially-clean tri-modal small language models (16.8M to 1.07B parameters) co-designed with a zero-dependency Rust inference runtime embedded inside a graph database process, eliminating serialization overhead, repeated schema prefill, and catalog-blind decoding via schema-epoch KV caching and live logit masking. A systems co-design of small LMs with database engines for text-to-Cypher workloads. Interesting deep systems integration, though heavily infrastructure-specific.

entry.title: Where the Image Sits: Vision-Text Order Bias in Jev

author.name: Youzhi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper examines whether the known image-text token order sensitivity of vision-language models extends to Jev-style single-prefill decision readouts, where the answer token is always read at the prompt's end. Using four image placements with fixed option listing, the study measures argmax flips, calibration, and label marginals. The work clarifies how positional structure in prompts affects vision-language decision reliability.

entry.title: Centerline-Guided Multi-Class Road Surface Segmentation

author.name: Xu Ouyang, Lin Gan, Di Ma, Sonnie Chen, Sanjay Boddhu

entry.summary: The paper presents a centerline-guided segmentation framework for satellite imagery that explicitly models road axes, transverse width, and junction structure via specialized decoders for regular roads, intersections, and overpasses, conditioned on predicted centerline features. A width branch supplies transverse geometry and feature fusion produces the final road mask. This improves on binary-mask approaches for geographic mapping.

entry.title: Thakaa at StanceEval-2026: Inference-Time Target Grounding for Arabic Stance Detection

author.name: Meshal Alamr, Hassan Alqaeri, Abdullah Aldahlawi

entry.summary: A shared-task report on Arabic stance detection under target shift, where evaluation targets are absent from labeled data. The system retrieves external labeled demonstrations (Women Driving examples) and uses inference-time target grounding via label-token scoring with an existing model (Gemma-4-31B-IT), plus cached factual target context and constrained prediction fusion across multiple LLMs. It ranks fourth and sixth on the two tracks with strong Favg2 scores.

entry.title: Correlation-aware sequential sampling for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions

author.name: Qitian Lu and Miroslav Vo\v{r}echovsk\'y and Luk\'a\v{s} Nov\'ak

entry.summary: The paper proposes adaptive sequential sampling strategies designed for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions, exploiting cross-correlations between quantities of interest in engineering uncertainty quantification rather than naively aggregating per-output information. This improves surrogate-model sampling efficiency under limited evaluation budgets.

entry.title: graspit-py: A Python Interface to GraspIt! for Grasp Planning Under Pose and Friction Uncertainty

author.name: Clinton Enwerem, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: graspit-py is a Python interface to the GraspIt! grasp simulator, providing native scene access, contact-wrench analysis, and approach planning under pose and friction uncertainty. It replaces the need for C++ bindings or ROS 1 services and integrates contact geometry with caller-defined uncertainty sampling. This is primarily an engineering contribution lowering the barrier for uncertainty-aware grasp planning research.

entry.title: Beyond Free-Form Generation: Measuring Interface Composition in Competitive NLP Systems

author.name: Xinchen Xiao

entry.summary: This empirical study measures how decoder-LLM systems in competitive NLP combine free generation with scoring, ranking, or selection interfaces, analyzing 517 Kaggle solutions and 76 SemEval/TREC/WMT systems. It finds hybrid generation-plus-constrained-interface designs are common, though shares vary widely (0.327 to 0.876) depending on weighting.

entry.title: Medical Specialty Prediction from Bangla Patient Narratives: A Comparative Study of ML, DL, Transformers, and LLMs

author.name: Tasnin Tabassum Ali, Faisal Ahmed, Muhammad Anwarul Azim

entry.summary: A comparative study of six ML models, four deep learning models, four fine-tuned transformers, and five zero-shot LLMs for routing Bangla patient narratives to medical specialties, using a corpus of 3,798 patient records across five specialties. The work addresses referral inefficiency in Bangladesh's healthcare system where patients use informal rather than clinical language. Useful baseline evidence for low-resource-language medical NLP.

entry.title: A comparison of knot point screening algorithms for highly adaptive lasso

author.name: Yadi Weng, Sky Qiu

entry.summary: This statistics paper compares knot point screening algorithms for the highly adaptive lasso (HAL), a nonparametric regression estimator with fast convergence rates crucial for causal inference tasks like TMLE. Screening rules reduce the computational burden of HAL's large basis expansions.

entry.title: Emotion-Aware and Context-Grounded Dialogue Agents for Personalized Video Game Interactions

author.name: Michael Adjeisah, Jin Zhang, Pierluigi Vito Amadori, Ryan Spick, Eshani Kawshika Fernando, Kwame Omono Asamoah, Huiwen Zhao, Jian Jun Zhang, Guy Moss, Jian Chang

entry.summary: ChatNPC is an LLM-based game companion that adapts responses to players' emotional shifts in real time, combining a sentinel-guided agent, memory retrieval, and tool-calling-based reasoning for NPC dialogue. It targets immersion through personalized, context-grounded conversation.

entry.title: A colour-marker tracker for pose estimation of slender surgical instruments: vision-language-model-guided adaptive colour calibration

author.name: Jaesung Hong, Dong Won Lee

entry.summary: The paper proposes using a fine-tuned VLM to adaptively calibrate colour-stripe markers on slender surgical instruments, overcoming the circular dependency where markers must be found before their colours can be corrected for lighting and camera drift. It compares VLM guidance against two rule-based calibration baselines.

entry.title: Exploring Attention-Driven Deep Learning for Accurate Lung Nodule Segmentation

author.name: Nima Shafiei Rezvani Nezhad, Meysam Mansouri, Saeid Ghayour, Ruhollah Abolhasani, Shahla Azizi

entry.summary: The study evaluates several deep learning architectures for lung nodule segmentation on LIDC-IDRI, emphasizing training on a filtered subset of 356 samples rather than the full dataset. A proposed DPL nkNet50 model with a Channel Attention Bridge and ResNet backbone achieves a Dice score of 0.86, outperforming conventional architectures.

entry.title: The Exploitation of Distance Distributions for Clustering

author.name: Michael C. Thrun

entry.summary: This paper proposes a context-independent framework for selecting and evaluating distance measures in cluster analysis based on distance distribution properties, rather than reproducing predefined partitions. It argues current evaluation practices bake in context-specific assumptions about what clusters should look like.

entry.title: A PyTorch-Enabled Tool for Synthetic Event Camera Data Generation and Algorithm Development

author.name: Joseph L. Greene, Adrish Kar, Ignacio Galindo, Elijah Quiles, Elliott Chen, and Matthew Anderson

entry.summary: SENPI is a PyTorch-based library for simulating and processing event camera data, including a differentiable digital twin of event camera characteristics and tools for synthetic data generation. It addresses barriers to neuromorphic vision adoption such as limited hardware availability and scarce datasets.

entry.title: GeoFusion: An Uncertain Machine Learning Framework for Sensor Fusion

author.name: Basant Ahmed Mounir Abdelhamid, Amr T. Abdel-Hamid

entry.summary: Proposes GeoFusion, a three-stage uncertain machine learning framework for cooperative GPS sensor fusion across multiple smartphones observing the same location. Each GPS observation is modeled as an uncertain object via a volcano function grounded in satellite geometry or an empirically derived mountain function, exploiting measurement uncertainty rather than treating observations as absolute points. The approach targets high positioning precision from affordable sensors.

entry.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows

author.name: Jiaxun Sun, Yuqi Yang, Senlan Yao, Hengyu Xue, Hongming Fu, Zhimu Zhou

entry.summary: Studies inspection robots that owe multiple timed measurements at the same station, characterizing what a feedback controller must retain about past visits to guarantee remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. The authors prove a compact sufficient state (one boundary plus capped run length) and recover feedback policies on a verified library of motion primitives.

entry.title: Topological analysis of permeability tensor in anisotropic porous media

author.name: Rafa{\l} Topolnicki, Pawe{\l} D{\l}otko, Maciej Matyka

entry.summary: The paper introduces two direction-aware topological descriptors — a cone-based filtration and a throat-scale filtration — to predict the full anisotropic permeability tensor of 3D porous media directly from geometry, validated against lattice Boltzmann simulations and compared to comprehensive non-topological baselines.

entry.title: Superellipse Function: A Powerful Geometric Tool for the Design and Deformation Modeling of Tendon-Driven Continuum Manipulators With Flexural Patterns Experiencing Tension Loss

author.name: Yang Liu and Farshid Alambeigi

entry.summary: This robotics paper uses the Superellipse function to design and model discontinuous flexural patterns in tendon-driven continuum manipulators, and develops a mathematical framework capturing tension loss from friction of partially-constrained tendons. It establishes intuitive mappings between geometric parameters, kinematics, and deformation behavior to guide manipulator design.

entry.title: TidyFlow: Geometry-Aware Tabletop Arrangement Generation with Human-Aligned Tidiness Evaluation

author.name: Jiahui Qian, Tiandong Wang, Shubao Fan, Chenyu Niu, Erqi Wu

entry.summary: TidyFlow generates tidy tabletop arrangements by combining conditional flow matching, conditioned on object attributes and tabletop geometry, with topology-aware geometric refinement to fix layout errors. The authors contribute two tabletop layout datasets (GTL and WTL) and a six-dimensional tidiness scoring function aimed at aligning with human organizational preferences.

entry.title: One Size Doesn't Fit All: Input Adaptive Class Activation Mapping for Improved Visual Explanations

author.name: Ayesha Sahar, Tahir Mustafa Madni, Tehseen Zia, David Windridge, Uzair Iqbal Janjua, Waleed Umar

entry.summary: ADAPT-CAM is a gradient-based, input-adaptive extension of class activation mapping that improves channel weighting and localization for CNN and ViT explanations. The method targets noisy or imprecise visual explanations that undermine trust in safety-critical vision applications.

entry.title: The response field approach to path integral control

author.name: George Stamatescu

entry.summary: This exploratory theoretical paper connects the response field formalism from nonequilibrium statistical physics to backward adjoint processes in stochastic optimal control, showing the response field plays a role analogous to the adjoint process under the stochastic maximum principle. Notably, the response function is found to be acausal in this setting, and the optimal control emerges as an average of the response field at the initial time.

entry.title: SalivaryHSI-Seg: A New Challenging Benchmark for Ex Vivo Salivary Gland Hyperspectral Tissue Segmentation

author.name: Xiaoqi Guo, Xianran Wang, Xinquan Yang, Qinyi Lu, Fangqian Zhang, Jiangyi Chen, Ming Li, Wen Ma, Linlin Shen

entry.summary: The paper introduces SalivaryHSI-Seg, a benchmark of 119 hyperspectral imaging samples of ex vivo salivary gland specimens with pixel-level annotations and unified evaluation protocols, aimed at surgical and pathological decision support. It fills a data gap limiting hyperspectral tissue segmentation development in oral and maxillofacial medicine.

entry.title: LambdaLens: Auditing a Representation-Changing Hyperparameter in Graph Neighbor Embedding

author.name: Juntang Wang, Yihan Wang, Sheng'en Li, Siyuan Cao, Liming Zhu, Man Zhang, Dongmian Zou, Shixin Xu

entry.summary: LambdaLens analyzes how the rescaling parameter lambda in SG-t-SNE-Pi graph embedding changes the meaning of the resulting layout, deriving a normalized power path for edge probabilities and connecting per-edge sensitivity to surprisal and neighborhood entropy. The work provides controlled geometric experiments across six graphs to audit what the parameter changes represent.

entry.title: Why Calibrated BM25 Filtering Barely Reduced Context on LongMemEval

author.name: John Knight, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: The paper empirically tests whether BM25 filtering of archived conversation passages saves input tokens for long-memory assistants, calibrating the filter on passages that individually corrected summarization-only errors across 75 LongMemEval questions. It finds filtering changed only one prompt and saved just 0.096% of tokens, with careful validation via automated grading cross-checked by human graders.

entry.title: MTL-MHOL: Predicting Online Conversions under Delayed Feedback and Data Sparsity

author.name: Mario Tejera Vicente, Eva Hagen, Emma van Breukelen, Quinten van de Vijver, Kathrin Gruber

entry.summary: Proposes MTL-MHOL, a model-agnostic multi-task, multi-head online learning framework for conversion rate prediction that combines time bucketing for delayed feedback with an auxiliary multi-task objective to mitigate data sparsity. Evaluated on proprietary and Criteo datasets, it matches or outperforms benchmarks on NLL and RCE while capturing temporal trends.

entry.title: Optimizing Locally Equivalent Graph States in Quantum Computing Using Greedy Best-First Search

author.name: Sora Harada, Ryo Kuroiwa, Shin Nishio, Takeaki Uno

entry.summary: Formulates finding locally equivalent graph states with fewer edges and lower maximum degree — via local complementations — as a search problem solved with greedy best-first search, reducing CZ gate counts and circuit depth in measurement-based quantum computation and quantum repeaters. This classical optimization directly lowers quantum resource requirements.

entry.title: What Quality Engineers Need to Know About Generative AI: Structured Data Extraction

author.name: Fadel M. Megahed, Ying-Ju Chen, Yamin Dahwich, Zhao-Wei Chen, Lucas K. Hung, Arthur Carvalho, L. Allison Jones-Farmer, Ibrahim Yousif, Inez M. Zwetsloot

entry.summary: An expository paper teaching quality engineers how to use LLMs and vision-language models for structured data extraction, framed from a measurement-system perspective with R and Python implementations. It presents two validated web applications, including automotive recall-notice extraction where human reviewers judged 98.6% of 720 field-level ratings fully correct.

entry.title: Leveraging Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) for the Exchange of Wearable Inertial Sensor Data: Design and Development Study

author.name: Gabriela Ciortuz, Joshua Wiedekopf, Hannes Ulrich, Hawzhin Hozhabr Pour, Sebastian Fudickar

entry.summary: The paper presents WHIR, a FHIR R5-based information model and implementation guide for exchanging wearable IMU recordings in electronic health records, with metadata requirements derived from a review of 23 human activity recognition datasets. It addresses the gap where existing FHIR profiles only support spot measurements and short waveforms rather than long multichannel motion recordings.

entry.title: When AI Performance Is Not Enough: Statistical Guardrails for Clinical Development

author.name: Siddhesh Kulkarni, Gina D'Angelo, Swarna Reddy, Rakhi Kilaru

entry.summary: A first-principles commentary on where AI/ML adoption in clinical development outpaces statistical scrutiny, covering anomaly detection in trial data, real-time monitoring and adaptive designs, biomarker-based enrichment, and virtual/digital twins. It articulates inferential risks such as methods succeeding locally while failing on broader estimands. A thoughtful perspective piece for responsible AI in clinical research.

entry.title: SBTenv: A Literature-Validated Split-Belt Treadmill Simulation Environment

author.name: Philip Byrne, John Drazan, Nidhi Seethapathi

entry.summary: SBTenv is an open-source split-belt treadmill environment in MuJoCo for studying human locomotor adaptation, validated against published experimental data using a rimless wheel passive walker with compliant contacts. It reproduces experimental average steady velocity without empirical fitting. This fills a genuine tooling gap for high-throughput simulation of locomotion adaptation experiments.

entry.title: Operating-Condition Normalization in C-MAPSS: Matched Historical Baselines, Multi-Seed Robustness, and Prognostic-Score Trade-offs

author.name: Mohammad Adeel

entry.summary: A controlled retrospective audit of operating-condition normalization for turbofan RUL prediction on NASA C-MAPSS FD002/FD004, using engine-disjoint folds and multi-seed comparisons. It finds that previously reported benefits of six-condition standardization largely disappear when raw sensor values are combined with condition-matched histories, questioning a common preprocessing assumption in prognostics.

entry.title: Which Model Belongs in the Loop? Evaluating Fitness Functions for Network Topology Optimization with a Quality-Diversity Algorithm

author.name: Paul Bannm\"uller, Olayiwola Arowolo, Jochen Stiasny, Jochen Cremer

entry.summary: The study compares DC- and AC-power-flow-based fitness functions within quality-diversity optimization for transmission network topology optimization, quantifying how fitness-function accuracy affects optimization outcomes and operational decisions. It highlights when cheaper DC approximations misjudge cost and feasibility.

entry.title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera

author.name: Alex Bocchieri, Devanshi Jain, Andreas Velten

entry.summary: This physics instrumentation paper proposes a monolithic Compton camera using SPAD array sensors to resolve two nearby scintillation events in a single detector volume, addressing bulkiness and efficiency drawbacks of conventional two-volume designs. It builds on recent SPAD camera work for high-resolution photon-counting acquisition.

entry.title: Implementation and Software-in-the-Loop Evaluation of a Trans-Domain Digital Twin Architecture for Autonomous Guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV Without Online GNSS

author.name: Mansoorali Amiri

entry.summary: The paper implements and evaluates a Trans-Domain Digital Twin for autonomous guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV without online GNSS, coordinating navigation, flight dynamics, and meteorological models in a state estimation and decision loop. It targets GNSS-denied scenarios such as enclosed spaces, spoofing, and electronic warfare. Single-author systems work validated via software-in-the-loop simulation.

entry.title: CoHABIT: Complementary Evaluation of Furniture Layouts through Spatial Rules and Household Routines

author.name: Ewsey Obzherin, Samira Atlangirieva, Anastasia Antsiferova, Valentin Khrulkov, Art Prosvetov, Andrey Kuznetsov

entry.summary: Introduces CoHABIT, a framework evaluating furniture layouts via complementary static spatial rules (geometric validity, ergonomics, Feng Shui-style preferences) and dynamic multi-agent simulations of resident routines including resource sharing and coordination burdens. Controlled comparisons show the two assessment modes reveal distinct aspects of layout quality, grounded by independent verification of household needs. It enables interpretable evaluation of how furnished environments serve different households.

entry.title: Single-Coordinate Activation Steering for Controllable Social Stance in Language Models

author.name: Naman Chawla, Chhavi Dhiman

entry.summary: Investigates whether a single neuron can control an interpersonal stance (a guarded, intermittently warm distant-crush persona) in a small Qwen3.5 4B model, identifying layer-9 neuron 7515 via contrasting activations. Increasing the neuron's activation makes replies more distant, with the effect validated by LLM raters and a blind human comparison, and checked against random-neuron controls.

entry.title: ESGPT: A Data-Centric ESG Language Model with Unified Instruction and Benchmark Resources

author.name: Jaeyoung Lee and Misuk Kim

entry.summary: The authors build ESG-Instruct, a 30,000-instance ESG instruction dataset, and ESGU-Bench, a benchmark covering six ESG understanding tasks, then train ESGPT, an 8B ESG-specialized language model. Experiments show competitive results against open-source and API-based LLMs on unified ESG evaluation.

entry.title: $K$-Midranks: A robust clustering algorithm for heavy-tailed data with applications to spectroscopy and finance

author.name: Larry Goldstein and Nathakhun Wiroonsri

entry.summary: K-midranks is a clustering method that replaces raw observations with coordinatewise ranks before applying a K-means-like partition, reducing the influence of extreme values while preserving within-variable ordering. Simulations against K-means, K-medoids, and several heavy-tailed mixture models show it generally wins on Cauchy-shifted data, with applications to spectroscopy and finance. It is a simple, robust alternative for clustering heavy-tailed data.

entry.title: Psychological State Monitoring Methods Based on Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Ran Meng

entry.summary: A hierarchical framework fuses facial images, speech, and physiological signals in early and late fusion stages for multimodal emotion recognition and psychological state monitoring, validated on a real-world stress-response dataset with improved accuracy and F1 over unimodal baselines.

entry.title: A Nepali-Accented English Evaluation Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Santosh Dahal and Kiran Chandra Dahal

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Nepali-accented English ASR evaluation dataset collected via a privacy-conscious web platform, with 57 speakers following a fixed 22-prompt protocol combining phonetic and domain prompts. It fills a gap since Nepali-accented English is under-served relative to native-English benchmarks. The dataset enables robust benchmarking of ASR systems under accent mismatch.

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Runbook Improvement with Agentic Support Automation

author.name: Rocker D'Antonio and Harry Xie

entry.summary: Investigates an operational system that embeds agentic AI into runbook-based incident resolution for production software support, using the runbook corpus plus system-specific context while keeping humans in the loop. It targets faster operator response times for escalations and unplanned outages. Relevant as an applied case study of agentic automation in real operational settings.

entry.title: Analyzing Atypical Local Features in Museum Artifacts using Generative Image Inpainting

author.name: Maho Kinoshita, Wakana Kuwata, Ryota Mibayashi, Hiroaki Ohshima

entry.summary: The method uses an image generation model's learned appearance distribution as a reference for what is typical within an artifact category: a region-excluded fine-tuned model completes masked regions, and large deviations from the original flag atypical features reflecting regional or cultural characteristics. This offers digital humanities researchers a tool for comparative artifact analysis. It is a creative application of generative inpainting outside engineering domains.

entry.title: Modeling Perceived Promptness in Simultaneous Interpreting from Quality, Structure, and Timing Signals

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Satoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: Studies whether professional interpreters' perceived-promptness judgments in simultaneous interpreting can be predicted from timing alone or also require linguistic features of the output, using a dataset of 622 Chinese-English segments rated by senior interpreters. Onset delay alone achieves moderate correlation, motivating richer signal modeling.

entry.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education

author.name: Stephan Vonschallen, Karim Kaufmann, Dominique Oberle, Friederike Eyssel, and Theresa Schmiedel

entry.summary: Teachy Mini operationalizes knowledge-based design requirements for generative social robots on the Reachy Mini platform using system prompting, RAG, and stateful prompt orchestration for higher-education tutoring. A preliminary evaluation study assesses its tutoring behavior and responsible-design properties.

entry.title: Neutron Imaging Enhancement for Lithium Batteries Based on Swin-Transformer and Image Fusion

author.name: Hansheng Ding, Fanxu Meng, Tian Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an enhancement pipeline for lithium-battery neutron imaging combining an improved Swin-Transformer (with Multi-Dconv Head Transposed Attention and Global Response Normalization) and spatial-domain image fusion. Neutron imaging is valuable for non-destructive testing of batteries but suffers from mixed noise, low contrast, and blurred edges. The method suppresses artifacts to enable better assessment of internal battery states.

entry.title: Non unitary and nonlinear quantum generative large model design and fast large-scale training without back propagation

author.name: Tianze Zhu, Xiaofeng Jiang, Min Liao, Luying Zhang, Ruixi Liu, Sen Kuang, Yongzhe Lin, Chenhao Zhou, Shuangwu Chen, Huasen He, Xiaobin Tan, Quan Zheng, Jian Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a fully quantum implementation of Transformer layers, realizing non-unitary transformations via SVD-decomposition-based quantum circuits and approximating nonlinear activations with pre-trained parameterized quantum circuits, plus a backpropagation-free quantum circuit training method. The work aims to translate the computational promises of quantum computing to large generative models.

entry.title: Deep Discriminative Feature Fusion of Convolutional and Attention-Based Recurrent Representations for Subject-Independent ECG Stress Recognition

author.name: Zeeshan Ahmad, Muhammad Rehman Zafar

entry.summary: The paper proposes three deep feature-fusion frameworks that combine convolutional and attention-based recurrent representations of ECG signals for subject-independent stress classification. It aims to capture both morphological patterns and temporal dynamics that single-representation approaches miss.

entry.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach

author.name: J. R. Rivadeneyra, I. Lee, F. Nugen, S. M. Srinivasan

entry.summary: ANNA is a framework combining statistical anomaly detection, KNN, clustering, and Deep Q-Network reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions in complex energy market settlements from ISOs like CAISO and MISO. It is positioned as an analyst-support tool replacing inefficient rule-based manual auditing.

entry.title: Bi-Refine: Semantic Verification-Guided Progressive Refinement for Moment Retrieval

author.name: Mengnan Liu, Sanping Zhou, Kun Xia, Jiaxuan Lin, Yuxuan Wu, Gang Hua

entry.summary: Bi-Refine formulates video moment retrieval as a closed-loop verification-and-refinement process, pairing a heuristic localization branch with a semantic verification branch that checks candidate-query consistency in an enriched latent space. Query supervision guards against over-correction when the verification signal is unreliable.

entry.title: OCCA-Seg: Object and Channel Context Aggregation for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images

author.name: Gang Yang, Si Chen, Quan Zhou, Jiangchuan Li

entry.summary: OCCA-Seg aggregates object-level and channel-level context for remote sensing semantic segmentation via an object contextual attention module, a channel contextual attention module, and an aggregation module, targeting multi-scale objects in complex scenes. The approach builds on the observation that pixels share their object's class label.

entry.title: Task-Dependent Linguistic Measures in Aphasia Discourse: A Comparative Analysis of Narrative, Descriptive, and Procedural Speech

author.name: Emma Al Kubaisi

entry.summary: Using 61 speakers with chronic aphasia from the AphasiaBank corpus, this study tests whether standard discourse measures (word counts, lexical diversity, disfluency rates) differ across procedural, descriptive, and narrative elicitation tasks within the same speakers. The results inform whether such transcript-based measures are comparable across studies using different tasks.

entry.title: Completing analytical conversion scheme among DH, Hayati, CPC and POE models for manipulator calibration

author.name: Oleg Yu. Sumenkov, Danil D. Kulminskiy, Sergei V. Gusev

entry.summary: This robotics paper completes the set of analytical conversions between four standard manipulator kinematic parameterizations (DH, Hayati, CPC, POE), filling missing direct POE-HAY and CPC-HAY conversions. It situates these conversions within Mooring's four-stage calibration framework and evaluates their effect on calibration performance. The result is a complete, principled toolbox for kinematic model interchange in robot calibration.

entry.title: SRCWDNet: Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network for Multi-Label Remote Sensing Scene Classification

author.name: Fareeha Amir

entry.summary: SRCWDNet tackles multi-label remote sensing scene classification with three modules: cross-window attention with learnable global tokens, a dual label-graph combining co-occurrence and learned semantic graphs, and a neural classifier chain exploiting label dependencies. Evaluation uses five-fold cross-validation under class imbalance. A competent architecture paper in a specialized application domain.

entry.title: Two cultures of causal modeling, and why one of them is unlikely to ever work

author.name: Frederik Hytting Jørgensen

entry.summary: This essay distinguishes two cultures in causal modeling: one that encodes assumptions about specific regimes (using examples like the firefighter/property-damage confounding illustration) and another whose research program the author argues is flawed at its conceptual core. It is a conceptual critique aimed at clarifying what causal models are actually for. The post is a thoughtful discussion piece rather than formal research.

entry.title: Operational Runbooks as Living Documents: A Longitudinal Study of Document Evolution under Assisted Post-Incident Revision

author.name: Rocker D'Antonio and Harry Xie and Xuan Guo

entry.summary: This study analyzes 17 weeks of version-controlled runbook snapshots produced through machine-assisted post-incident revision with human oversight, quantifying document evolution using lightweight linguistic and structural signals. It offers empirical insight into how operational documentation collections change in production and which signals monitor that change.

entry.title: We’re Going to Send California 23,552 Calls To Delay Superintelligence

author.name: Ben AI Safety

entry.summary: An advocacy post announcing a campaign to generate 23,552 phone calls to California state representatives in support of AI safety recommendations sent to the Governor's Office on November 18, including compute-scale caps on recursive self-improvement, shutdown provisions for dangerous models, and embedded auditors. The author provides an S-curve schedule of call milestones through May 2027.

entry.title: Temporal Persistence for Stylized Rendering: Historical Image Storage and Reconstruction

author.name: Daniel Szelogowski

entry.summary: This graphics paper studies how to reproduce the distinctive history-based motion blur of Majora's Mask in a modern renderer, exploring complete image histories, shared regions, and selectively retained pixel changes with Godot implementations validated against composited references. It includes concrete memory and performance budgets, e.g., a ten-image 20 Hz history on an RTX 3060 Ti. A niche but technically careful rendering contribution.

entry.title: Real-time Priority-aware UAS Arrival Planning Framework for Multi-layer UTM

author.name: Anisha Mohapatra, Prasanna Ramamurthy, Shridhar Velhal, M. Sethumadhavan, and Suresh Sundaram

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time, priority-aware arrival-planning framework for drone (UAS) terminal airspace modeled as concentric rings, holding slots, and a landing pad, handling replanning for new arrivals, wind disturbances, and emergencies via a greedy priority-ordered planning method. It computes slot assignments, traversal paths, and landing times while maintaining separation constraints. Targets tractability in dense urban airspace management.

entry.title: UNIFY: Unified Learning with One Model via Batch Norm Switching

author.name: Shaharyar Ahmed Khan Tareen and Xiaojing Yuan

entry.summary: UNIFY lets a single network serve multiple datasets by sharing a parameter-heavy backbone while swapping dataset-specific batch normalization statistics and classification heads at inference. Validated on five image datasets across six CNN architectures, it reduces memory, deployment cost, and energy versus maintaining per-task models.

entry.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera

author.name: Sulaiman Abubakar, Blessed Oguh, Akaninyene Udoikono, Hackim Musah, Suk Kyoung Lee and Wen Li

entry.summary: This instrumentation paper demonstrates a 3D velocity map imaging system using a neuromorphic event-driven camera with a microchannel plate detector, achieving 2 microsecond latency for single ion/electron detection and boosting momentum imaging throughput above 100 kHz versus a few kHz for conventional frame cameras, while retaining high spatial and time resolution.

entry.title: IteraSong: LLM-Guided Iterative Symbolic Music Creation in a Web DAW

author.name: Di Lu, Xinran Zhang, Yan Gao, Yuan Zhang, Xiaoqing Wang, Qingwen Zhou, Xiaobing Li, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: IteraSong is an interactive web DAW for LLM-guided iterative symbolic music creation supporting a generate-audition-edit-refine loop over persistent multi-track projects. Natural-language instructions are mapped to a hierarchical editing action space exposed via Model Context Protocol tools, spanning global, track, section, and bar/note scopes.

entry.title: Seeing What the Vehicle Sees: Video-Augmented Virtual Reality for Physical Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Md Tanjemul Islam, Mohammad Shafin and Md Rafiul Kabir

entry.summary: Presents a VR framework coupling a physical ROS 2 autonomous robot vehicle to a Unity application on a Meta Quest 3S headset, streaming vehicle state and live camera feeds over two independent channels. This lets passengers see what a real, physically operating autonomous system perceives rather than pre-scripted simulations. It addresses passenger trust and explainability in autonomous driving.

entry.title: A ROS2 based Human-In-The-Loop Framework for UAV Search and Rescue Operations

author.name: Anubhav Pandey, Harshit Nagpal, Aditya Agarwal, Tejasvi Alladi and Fei Richard Yu

entry.summary: Describes a ROS 2 human-in-the-loop UAV framework for search and rescue that translates directional human gestures into navigation commands using RGB-D sensing and YOLOv11, prioritizing robustness in degraded SAR environments over peak accuracy. It achieves around 89% confidence in depth estimation and emphasizes the ROS1-to-ROS2 migration for real-time scalability and maintainability. The work targets practical deployment where human context supplements autonomy.

entry.title: Landscape and Taxonomy of Prompt Engineering Patterns in Software Engineering

author.name: Yuya Sasaki, Hironori Washizaki, Jialong Li, Nobukazu Yoshioka, Naoyasu Ubayashi, Yoshiaki Fukazawa

entry.summary: This article presents a taxonomy of prompt engineering patterns for software engineering based on a systematic literature review conducted in early 2023, emphasizing techniques that enhance LLM usability and reliability. It argues prompt patterns remain important even as model capabilities evolve.

entry.title: Design of a Compact Cable-driven 4-DoF Salamander Robotic Limb with Large Range of Motion and High Load Capacity

author.name: Zhuowen Li, Qiyuan Fu, Auke Ijspeert

entry.summary: The authors present a compact cable-driven 4-DoF robotic limb replicating salamander limb capabilities — large range of motion, multiple degrees of freedom, and high load capacity — for amphibious robots transitioning between swimming and walking. The design addresses self-collision and inertia problems of direct-drive architectures by routing actuation via cables.

entry.title: Can Cities Have Personalities? Introducing the SCD City Personality Assessment

author.name: Andrei Khurshudov

entry.summary: Introduces SCD-CPA, a method that instantiates document-grounded ChatGPT personas for cities and interrogates each with a 24-statement MBTI-inspired instrument, producing four bipolar dimensions and four-letter summaries. Evaluation spans Tokyo, New York, and Paris across repeated sessions and alternative evidence portraits to test sensitivity to documentary inputs.

entry.title: DKnown-Jev-2: Article-Level Answer-Evidence Classification and Efficient Inference with a Pre-trained Language Model

author.name: Qi Li, Jianjun Xu, Jiu Li, Pingtao Wei

entry.summary: The paper presents DKnown-Jev-2, an article-level classifier for determining whether a candidate article contains answer-supporting evidence in normative knowledge question answering. It jointly encodes question conditions, metadata, and paragraphs with a pointer-style head, achieving 91.77% accuracy on a 972-instance annotated test set and outperforming its predecessor Jev. The work targets efficient single-pass evidence integration across paragraphs.

entry.title: Gated Payoff-Weighted Net Profit Maximization For Online Portfolio Selection With Transaction Costs

author.name: Grace Chengrong Xie, Alvey Qianli Lin, Wai Ki Ching

entry.summary: The paper proposes AOLNPM, an online portfolio selection strategy that gates AOLMA forecasts by learning each asset's recent mixture proportion via predictive likelihoods against a neutral no-change forecast, thereby discounting unreliable forecasts. The gated forecast feeds a net-profit-maximization rule that trades only when forecast gain exceeds transaction costs. The key insight is that moving-average forecasts systematically overstate realized returns.

entry.title: Constellations of Colour: Mapping Semantic Neighbourhoods in CLIP

author.name: Matt DesLauriers

entry.summary: This pictorial visualizes color semantics in CLIP by embedding 2,500 named colors, projecting them to 2D, and forming constellations via a thresholded minimum spanning tree. The maps reveal perceptual gradients and semantic neighborhoods spanning botanical, fictional, and food-related color language.

entry.title: Feedback-Driven Prompt Refinement for Educational AI: Affective Trajectory Estimation and Bloom's Taxonomy Classification

author.name: Josh Dean, Karan Patel, Gaurangi Raul, Yu-Zheng Lin, Jesus Pacheco, Sicong Shao, Shalaka Satam, Soheil Salehi, Pratik Satam

entry.summary: This study shows that a shared prompt-refinement procedure guided by affective and cognitive feedback signals improves reference agreement and multi-label classification (Bloom's taxonomy) while reducing generation variability, without updating executor model parameters. It targets dependable personalized technical education in Industry 4.0 contexts. The approach is lightweight but limited to prompt-level engineering.

entry.title: A hybrid Graph-based Machine Learning Model for predicting Delivery Times in Supply Chain Logistics

author.name: Mattia Volpato, Andrea Giuseppe Landella, Bruno Puzzolante

entry.summary: A hybrid graph-theory and machine learning approach for predicting delays in inbound supply chain flows, developed within the Horizon Europe M4ESTRO project. It models order-fulfillment stages mathematically and computes disruption indicators from heterogeneous historical and real-time sources including traffic and weather. Applied industrial ML for supply chain resilience.

entry.title: Aegis: A Conversational Prototype for Lung Cancer Risk Information and Follow-up

author.name: Bowen Han, Chengwei Cao, Runxin Zhang, Yuyang Jiang

entry.summary: A browser-based research prototype combining a conversational questionnaire, rule-based risk categorization, RAG-based health information, and doctor-user communication for lung cancer screening workflows. A session controller manages question progression while an LLM assists with answer validation, in a multi-agent design separating collection, validation, assessment, and reporting. It is an applied systems demonstration rather than a research contribution.

entry.title: Spatial Ensemble Logic for Biomedical Imaging: Geometric Element Ensembles in Euclidean Space

author.name: Guo-Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper develops Spatial Ensemble Logic, a member of a modal logic family over metric monoids, applied to biomedical images via geometric element ensembles represented by semi-algebraic sets such as balls. It proves closure properties of translation, dilation, and erosion operations and gives a satisfaction-preserving translation result.

entry.title: Fuzzy e-Means: Fuzzy c-Means on Large Data with Moving-Average Mini-Batch Updates

author.name: Paritosh Tiwari, Punit Rathore

entry.summary: This paper adapts the mini-batch moving-average optimizer of e-means to fuzzy c-means clustering, enabling FCM on large datasets with far fewer passes than alternating optimization. The authors identify and fix two failure modes: cluster-relocation rules removing small-group centroids and poor random initialization.

entry.title: Rethinking Discovery Research with AI: The promise of transdisciplinarity and the danger of reductionism

author.name: Iulia Georgescu, Venkatesh Narayanamurti

entry.summary: This essay argues that AI could enable genuine transdisciplinary research that overcomes reductionist, department-bound science, and analyzes why current incentive structures prevent this from happening. It is a position piece on the organization of AI-assisted discovery rather than a technical contribution.

entry.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape

author.name: Erfun Bayat Sarmadi, Ali Asadi, Moosa Ayati

entry.summary: A comparative simulation study of Nonlinear Model Predictive Control versus Sliding Mode Control for a four-cable spatial cable-suspended parallel robot, evaluated on both an analytical dynamic model and a MATLAB Simscape Multibody model. NMPC achieves better tracking and disturbance rejection at higher computational cost.

entry.title: From Patterns to Threats: A Deep Learning Model for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Kayode L. Ogunsusi

entry.summary: This paper applies a deep autoencoder to anomaly detection in cyber-physical systems using the Edge-IIoTset dataset, training only on normal observations and flagging anomalies via reconstruction error with an F1-optimized threshold. The approach is evaluated with multiple random runs for stability on 2.2 million observations across 38 features.

entry.title: Advancements in Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Novel Multi-Stacked U-Net Architectures

author.name: Ameya Uppina, S Navaneetha Krishnan, Talluri Krishna Sai Teja, Joe Dhanith P R

entry.summary: Evaluates U-Net and stacked U-Net architectures for diabetic retinopathy classification from fundus images across several datasets, addressing limited annotations, variable image quality, and class imbalance. The paper compares and studies performance across these settings for automated screening.

entry.title: Two Ideas for Promoting an AI Security Mindset

author.name: PeterMcCluskey

entry.summary: The author proposes two mechanisms to push AI companies toward serious security practices and modestly slow the race to superintelligence: a government-adjudicated bug bounty program with canary files in training pipelines paying six-figure bounties for demonstrated weight-tampering access, and a second unspecified idea. The core concern is that arbitrary outsiders could take control of a powerful AI's goals if lab security is weak. It is a concrete policy proposal post.

entry.title: Moderately cursed questions of AI safety

author.name: alkjash

entry.summary: The post argues that AI safety contains many moderately taboo questions, short of extreme s-risk territory, that go undiscussed outside LessWrong because of social norms, leaving practitioners confused or reaching private conclusions alone. It advocates spreading decoupling norms so these questions can be examined openly as an explicit goal of AI safety acculturation.

entry.title: Heroism in AI Safety

author.name: David Africa

entry.summary: A philosophical essay, drawing on Joe Carlsmith's discussion of Timothy Treadwell in Grizzly Man, exploring what role heroism, wonder, and gentleness should play in AI safety work that is otherwise dominated by wariness toward superintelligence. The author argues for holding both openness toward the artificial other and clear-eyed recognition of danger, and reflects on what heroic conduct means for safety researchers.

entry.title: A Novel Approach to Clustering Shape Data Using Iteratively Weighted Vectors with k-Means

author.name: Jason Turk, Umar Islambekov

entry.summary: This work clusters topological shape data by embedding topological summaries into Euclidean space and adding an element-wise weight-update step to iterative k-means. It reports improved clustering performance on simulated and real datasets.

entry.title: From Vanishing Gradients to Recursive Self-Improvement: Evaluating the Most Influential Papers in Large Language Model Evolution (1997-2026)

author.name: Saadh Jawwadh

entry.summary: This review surveys 22 influential publications spanning nearly three decades of language model research, organized in a chronological taxonomy tracing the path from RNNs and LSTMs through Word2Vec to modern LLM topics including recursive self-improvement. It aims to distinguish paradigm shifts from incremental refinements using accessible analogies.

entry.title: Human military relevance is more important than economic relevance

author.name: cousin_it

entry.summary: The post argues that human bargaining power in an AI-transformed world depends more on military relevance than economic value, citing the historical example of how firearms made masses valuable as soldiers and thereby enabled democracy, while economically necessary but militarily irrelevant classes like slaves remained coerced. The author concludes that humans whose labor stays economically valuable but whose military roles AI takes will lose their protective bargaining chip. It is a compact geopolitical argument about AI risk.

entry.title: The Disappointment of a Satisfying Explanation

author.name: Ben Pace

entry.summary: The author reflects on Turing's 1950 paper introducing the Imitation Game, quoting Turing's anticipation of arguments from various disabilities and his observation that such criticisms are often disguised forms of the argument from consciousness. Prompted by a discussion of the paper at Inkhaven, the post examines why satisfying mechanistic explanations of machine abilities can feel deflationary.

entry.title: Alignment from equivariance III - moraloids and tribal subgroups

author.name: hamishtodd1
