entry.summary: Turnout mitigates the accuracy loss from post-hoc linearization of transformer attention while retaining its memory savings. A linear path is distilled into a pretrained full-attention model whose original path is preserved, and a learned policy adaptively switches between paths during generation. This is particularly valuable for reasoning tasks where long generations make key-value caches expensive.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models

author.name: Sarah Parisot, Melanie Fernandez Pradier, David Bignell, Sergio Valcarcel Macua, Katja Hofmann

entry.summary: This work systematically compares categorical versus continuous prediction in world models under next-token and whole-frame generation paradigms using controlled 2D and 3D environments. Findings show categorical models achieve higher rollout validity with less compute, especially for stochastic dynamics, and that decoding strategy matters.

entry.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Chi Yan, Guoyang Zhao, Wentao Yuan, Yixiao Ge, Yanning Zhou, Dan Xu

entry.summary: StereoVLM leverages calibrated stereo pairs with explicit cross-view geometry to train VLMs on grounded metric 3D spatial reasoning, addressing the ambiguity of inferring 3D structure from uncalibrated images. The work investigates learning transferable 3D representations directly from binocular inputs.

entry.title: Affine-Image Propagation for Tight and Scalable Neural Network Verification

author.name: Hong-Ming Chiu, Haoyu Li, Huan Zhang, Richard Y. Zhang

entry.summary: The authors introduce SDP-CROWN, a bound propagation method using affine-image constraints to tighten neural network verification against L2 adversaries, where existing methods suffer geometric and functional approximation losses. This extends tight, scalable certification beyond Lipschitz-regularized networks that current approaches are limited to.

entry.title: Verifying and Strengthening Neural Tangent Kernel Theory

author.name: Hao Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents a Lean 4 machine-checked formalization of NTK theory for two-layer networks, proving an end-to-end theorem that gradient flow exists uniquely with high probability and achieves exponential loss decay under explicit width and initialization conditions. This is the first machine-verified proof of the standard NKT lazy-training result and strengthens some assumptions.

entry.title: EgoSurgHands: An Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Dataset & Benchmark for Open Surgery Training

author.name: Ankit Pal, Guillaume Kugener, Sofia Volpi, Joshua Schwartz, Alex Idarraga, Pranav Rajpurkar, Gabriel A. Brat

entry.summary: EgoSurgHands is the first dataset providing real egocentric articulated 3D hand poses for open surgery, captured with multi-sensor glasses across 55 procedure recordings with over 41,000 training hand instances and 9,476 human-validated evaluation rows spanning 13 tasks and trainees from medical student to resident. Each frame includes rich sensor metadata such as eye gaze and hand landmarks. It enables surgical skill assessment, AR guidance, and robot learning from demonstration.

entry.title: SkillPrivus: Uncovering PRIVacy of USe Harms in Agentic Skills

author.name: Mariana Fernandez-Espinosa, Ivoline Ngong, Keerthiram Murugesan, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy

entry.summary: Introduces SkillPrivus, a static audit framework that detects privacy-of-use harms in installable agent skills before execution, using Contextual Integrity to assess whether data operations are appropriate. Applied to 726 real marketplace skills (563 handling personal data), it flags potential privacy harms at scale without running the code.

entry.title: Open CDLM: A Benchmark and Library for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Hao Jiang, Ruixi Chen, Jiayi Han, Yulei Sun, Yujian Chen, Gen Li, Brian. K Chen, Guang Cheng, Weijian Luo, Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: This work introduces Open CDLM, a benchmark and open-source library for reliably evaluating continuous diffusion language models and their samplers. It identifies flaws in common practices: variational likelihood upper bounds confound comparisons, and generative perplexity plus unigram entropy can look favorable even for degenerate samplers producing identical text. The benchmark proposes improved likelihood evaluation and richer sample-based metrics.

entry.title: TouchBench: Can Vision-Language Models Feel Invisible Physical Properties?

author.name: Ziyao Zeng, Ziyi Kou, Chuan Qin, Mia Huang, Roger Boldu, Zhiwen Fan, Daniel Rakita, Eric Whitmire, Li Guan

entry.summary: TouchBench is an egocentric vision-language-tactile benchmark pairing head-mounted video with synchronized 137-channel whole-hand tactile sensing across 900 clips and 11 tasks, separating visually answerable questions from those requiring touch-revealed properties like fill level or compliance. Four state-of-the-art VLMs show large performance gaps on touch-dependent questions, exposing a blind spot in embodied multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: Learning Video Foresight Reasoning from Unlabeled Videos via On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Jingchen Sun, Jiaxing Zhang, Qingqiao Hu, Dingqiang Ye, Yuqi Jia, Yijun Liang, Di Fu, Yunjie Tian, Dongdi Zhao, Changyou Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose an on-policy self-distillation framework that teaches vision-language models to anticipate future events from unlabeled video, using past-future pairs as a natural self-supervised signal. They also introduce a foresight score and a contrastive privilege advantage so models weight only the relevant portion of the future clip rather than treating it uniformly.

entry.title: ViewDreamer: A Robot World Model beyond Fixed Camera Setups

author.name: Ye Mao, Jinhui Xiong, Egor Larionov, Shiyang Lu, Krystian Mikolajczyk, Wei Ye

entry.summary: ViewDreamer is a single video world model that handles variable numbers and placements of cameras by disentangling per-view generation from cross-view interaction through shared slot tokens. A curriculum over view count and a Cross-View Slot Agreement loss using visual foundation models stabilize training across diverse robot embodiments.

entry.title: $R^2$: Recognizing and Reducing Redundant Visual Tool Use

author.name: Yilin Zhao, Jinyu Wang, Wenming Yang

entry.summary: R2 studies when visual tool use in vision-language models actually helps, introducing a sample-level Category Analysis of Tool Utility that reveals at most 12.44% of samples across seven benchmarks benefit from tools, while many are hurt or unaffected. The framework then uses this analysis to recognize and prune redundant tool calls, and shows benchmark scores can mask a model's true tool-use ability.

entry.title: TrajRealm: A Large-Scale Point Tracking Dataset with Diverse Dynamics

author.name: Ni Yang, Weiguang Zhao, Jiafei Cao, Yankai Jiang, Haoyu Guo, Tao Yang, Chunhua Shen, Junting Dong

entry.summary: TrajRealm is the first public synthetic point-tracking dataset at the ten-million-frame scale, built from game engines and embodied simulations with RGB, depth, camera parameters, and persistent 2D and 3D point trajectory annotations. It targets the combined need for dynamic diversity, accurate geometry, and scale in training general-purpose point trackers.

entry.title: SOAR: Training-Free Rank-Consistent Rollout Compression for Latent World Model Planning

author.name: Anqi Li, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: SOAR accelerates latent world model planning by exploiting the observation that sampling-based planners only use rollout costs for ranking, so rollouts can be compressed as long as candidate rankings survive. It adaptively probes token budgets at each decision to find the smallest compression preserving rank consistency, validated over more than 80,000 closed-loop episodes with no task labels.

entry.title: Search-Informed MPPI for Kinodynamic Motion Planning via Monte Carlo Tree Expansion

author.name: Ihab S. Mohamed, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: SI-MPPI unifies Monte Carlo Tree Search with MPPI trajectory optimization: MCTS provides strategic long-horizon exploration while MPPI handles local trajectory refinement, overcoming MCTS's large branching factors and MPPI's obstacle-induced local minima. The fusion of tree expansion with MPPI sampling targets kinodynamic planning in large cluttered environments. This hybrid addresses a genuine and persistent weakness of both approaches.

entry.title: ManipScope: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Instruction Following and Generalization in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jiacheng Li, Yaping Li, Congsheng Xu, Qingchen Liu, Haonan Wang, Zhijie Deng, Jiahu Qin

entry.summary: ManipScope is an evaluation-only diagnostic benchmark built on RoboTwin 2.0 with 48 held-out scenes across six task families, testing whether policies follow the requested goal rather than replaying familiar routines. Its chain-of-diagnostics design tests one failure explanation per step, and across twelve checkpoints 84.6% of failures are attributed. The distinction between instruction following and routine reuse is an important evaluation insight.

entry.title: Ego4Gen: Generating Geometry-Grounded Motion Tokens as a World-Action Interface

author.name: Yang Liu, Chao Ye, Jiahao Zhang, Zeyuan Hou, Ruijie Fang, Xiyin Ni, Xinyang Ren, Weiyang Lin

entry.summary: Ego4Gen is a world model for robotic manipulation that generates temporally aligned RGB frames, dense point maps, and scene flow from a single egocentric image and text prompt, built on the pretrained Cosmos3-Nano backbone with modality-routed LoRA. Its geometry and motion latents can be decoded into 3D structure or mapped to robot actions via a lightweight policy. It offers a unified world-action interface grounded in explicit geometry.

entry.title: Generalist Action Critic: Harnessing Frontier Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yun Yan, Shizhi Hu, Zhichao Li, Yang Guan, Shiqi Liu, Jiaxin Gao, Xiangteng Zhang, Wenbo Ding, Jiuhua Zhao, Hui Guo, Xintao Yan, Keqiang Li, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: The Generalist Action Critic (GAC) is a zero-shot inference-time framework in which specialized driving planners generate candidate trajectories and a frozen frontier model acts as an action critic that assesses and re-ranks them, combining general-purpose reasoning with specialist planning competence. No additional adaptation of the frontier model is required. This offers a practical pattern for leveraging large reasoning models in safety-relevant physical decision making.

entry.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language

author.name: Leon Lufkin, Cutter Dawes, Kamesh Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: Develops a theory of how predictive information is distributed along a text history, based on scaling behavior of a family of information measures, predicting self-similar organization across scales. Since LLMs trained on next-token prediction must exploit this predictive information, the theory illuminates how linguistic structure becomes learnable. Connects information theory, linguistics, and LLM training objectives.

entry.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training

author.name: Jiajun Fan, Ziwen Wang, Zhaoyu Zhu, Changyi Yang, Neil He, Chaoran Cheng, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Bel improves visual GUI agents at inference time with no training by using a decision model to select the best action among a frozen policy's samples, showing that judging a tap rendered on the screenshot works far better than judging raw coordinates as text. It applies this visual-grounded selection to models like GUI-R1-3B for step-level policy improvement.

entry.title: MedicalRSI: Medical Recursive Self-Improving Agents via Clinical Model-Harness Co-Evolution

author.name: Ziqing Wang, Hamid Palangi, Lili Zhao, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: MedicalRSI extends self-improvement of medical LLM agents to recursive self-improvement, co-evolving both the agent and its improving strategy so the system learns which harness changes actually help. It targets clinical workflows where reference harnesses are absent and delayed-error effects complicate evaluation, aiming to prevent the same errors recurring across patients.

entry.title: Tokenize Moments, Not Frames: Tokenizer-Aware Budget Allocation for Training-Free Video LLM Acceleration

author.name: Zirui Zhao, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong

entry.summary: Diagnoses why training-free video LLM token pruning loses accuracy on long videos: frame sampling under token budgets exceeds the roughly 2-second similarity window, causing two-frame 3D patch tokenizers like Qwen-VL's to blend unrelated scenes into single tokens before pruning even occurs. The proposed ESSENCE method performs tokenizer-aware budget allocation, training-free, and accounts for fixed-size tokenizers such as InternVL's.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Behavioral Agents and Detectors for Adaptive Information Operations

author.name: Lin Tian, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: IO-AI simulates information-operation agents built from real campaign posting behavior, giving them engagement and evasion objectives, then co-trains them against detectors in an adversarial loop. The framework quantifies how adaptive adversaries degrade state-actor IO detection and trains a more robust detector against the hardest agents.

entry.title: The Vulnerability Window: Decision Instability in Quantized Reward Models

author.name: Omkar Shewale, Deepak Kumar, Divakar Kumar Yadav

entry.summary: Across eight reward models and three generative judges, 4-bit quantization rewrites 1.1-12.3% of pairwise preference decisions on RewardBench while aggregate accuracy barely moves, because errors introduced and corrected cancel. Flips concentrate where the full-precision margin is small relative to quantization noise, described by a Gaussian flip-rate approximation.

entry.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering

author.name: Minye Shao, Chenghao Xiao, Xingyue Zhao, Yang Long

entry.summary: AutoOntologyBench is a task-grounded benchmark asking whether autonomous agents can construct ontologies that measurably help them solve real tasks, rather than evaluating ontology correctness in isolation. Motivated by the extension of foundation-model agents beyond software engineering into scientific research, it tests whether agent-built knowledge representations offer benefits over alternatives. This addresses a gap in evaluating agentic knowledge acquisition end-to-end.

entry.title: RemoteEvolver: Expanding Earth Observation Capabilities through Agent Harness Evolution

author.name: Shengxiang Xu, Liang Yao, Shuyi Chen, Yishu Wang, Shimin Di, Fan Liu, Bishun Yao, Hanghui Guo, Xinyu Liu, Chengye Liang, Yuyu Luo, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: RemoteEvolver proposes a continually self-improving remote sensing agent that identifies and fills its own capability gaps by evolving its harness, meaning tools and workflow knowledge stored as editable, persistent resources outside the base model. This lets the system expand beyond fixed toolsets and transfer accumulated improvements across tasks without retraining.

entry.title: Embodied Interaction Policy: A Unified Model for Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Youqiang Gui, Yunfei Liu, Lijian Lin, Ye Zhu, Jianan Wang, Cheng Peng, Yu Li

entry.summary: EIP is a unified streaming framework coupling an audio-interaction expert with a motion expert via layer-wise joint attention, enabling motion generation to condition on evolving conversational state, with a chunk-wise causal mask preventing future-context leakage and a vocal token encoding speaking state and emotion. It also introduces the EI-Data dataset from co-speech and dyadic interactions. Unifying dialogue and robot motion in one streaming model is a meaningful step toward natural social robots.

entry.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation

author.name: Tanzimul Alam Fahim, Mohammad Arif Hossain

entry.summary: Proposes generation-by-simulation for building relational artifacts like cyber threat intelligence knowledge graphs: LLM agents propose intents while a deterministic referee resolves outcomes against an explicit world model, so relationships are emitted only when events actually occur. This makes coherence a property of construction rather than post-hoc validation, instantiated in STIX 2.1. It also characterizes formal limits of coherence checking.

entry.title: A Continuous Relaxation of Quantization-Aware Training

author.name: Kartikeya Bhardwaj, Mohammed Almousa, Chaitanya Mullapudi, Ananth Balasubramanian, Nithin Ramesan, Tuc Nguyen, Harris Teague

entry.summary: This paper tackles sub-2-bit quantization-aware training by gradually changing bitwidth during training rather than fixing it or switching abruptly, addressing flat loss surfaces and saddle points in channelwise quantization. It targets hardware-efficient deployment of large generative models at extremely low precision.

entry.title: Jagged Robustness: Uneven Safety Transfer and Emerging Vulnerabilities under LLM Quantization

author.name: Ramneek Agnihotri, Yingte Xu, Hans Vath

entry.summary: The paper audits how quantization affects capabilities and safety domains, finding that safeguards and bias behavior can degrade under quantization while capabilities like truthfulness remain more stable in Qwen3-4B, a phenomenon named Jagged Robustness. The authors verify increased compliance with unsafe requests under quantization and identify drivers including task complexity, evaluation method, and generation coherence.

entry.title: QuASAR: Toward an LLM-Assisted Framework for Screening, Prototyping, and Assessing Quantum-Advantage Opportunities in Scientific Computing

author.name: Mark L. Carroll, Jordan A. Caraballo-Vega, Brian P. Powell, John L. Schnase

entry.summary: QuASAR is a two-agent LLM pipeline that screens scientific literature for computational kernels with plausible quantum-algorithmic analogues, verifies citations independently, then formulates quantum mappings and benchmarks prototypes against classical baselines. It addresses the rarity of combined domain and quantum-algorithm expertise.

entry.title: LoCo-WAM: Test-Time Training as Long Context for World-Action Models

author.name: Sheng Cheng, Deqian Kong

entry.summary: Introduces LoCo-WAM, which lets world-action models benefit from long observation histories without increasing per-step context: newly observed frames update a low-rank adapter in the video expert via test-time training, with updates accumulating within an episode and resetting between episodes. This allows past experience to influence actions after it leaves the input window, without extra action labels.

entry.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes

author.name: Kaviru Hapuarachchi

entry.summary: This audit grades 50 AI agent runtimes and coding-agent harnesses (12 persistent runtimes, 26 harnesses, 12 research runtimes) on eight recovery mechanisms such as checkpoints, undo, approval, and transactional rollback, using a pre-registered protocol with blind coding and archived-source verification. It finds recovery mechanisms are exercised almost everywhere in practice but guarantees like saga compensation are rarely demonstrated.

entry.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation

author.name: Joonhyuk Baek, Wonjune Seo, Jae-yun Kim, Saerom Park, Hoki Kim

entry.summary: The authors present the first comprehensive benchmark for proactive deepfake defenses, systematically evaluating disruption, robustness, and transferability across pixel, perceptual, and identity metrics. The analysis reveals conflicting signals between fidelity and identity metrics, shows that peak white-box performance often indicates overfitting, and introduces calibrated evaluation to correct generator-induced identity bias.

entry.title: Mechanism Parity for Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous-Driving Perception

author.name: Danial Safaei, Siddartha Khastgir, Matthew D. Higgins, Jeroen Ploeg, Mohsen Alirezaei, Son Tong, Paul A. Jennings, Xingyu Zhao

entry.summary: This paper addresses a gap in simulation-based validation of autonomous-driving perception: output agreement between real and synthetic scenes does not guarantee the perception system relied on the same evidence in both domains. It unifies Decisive-Feature Fidelity and Concept-Decisive Feature Fidelity into a diagnostic framework that checks whether simulations preserve the underlying decision mechanisms, not just outputs. The authors position it as a validation diagnostic rather than a standalone safety certificate.

entry.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search

author.name: Aadharsh Kannan, Robert Bruckner, Philip A. Bernstein

entry.summary: The authors propose interpretable embeddings where each coordinate stores a calibrated yes/no/not-stated answer from a decision model to a natural-language question, enabling exact decomposition of similarity into per-question contributions and incremental addition of new questions without re-encoding the corpus. This supports auditable entity matching and search, particularly for agent-driven record systems.

entry.title: Fair Property Tax: Reducing Regressivity in Machine-Learning Valuation

author.name: Nicolas Acevedo Villena, Haihao Lu, Michael Wagner, Timothy Sparer

entry.summary: In collaboration with the Cook County Assessor's Office, this paper develops two training methods that reduce regressivity in ML-based property tax valuation, where lower-priced homes systematically receive higher valuation-to-sale ratios. The Direct method, a penalty on covariance between valuation errors and sale prices, has been deployed in CCAO's public residential valuation software.

entry.title: More Bits Won't Fix It: Diagnosing and Treating an Ill-Conditioned Backward Pass (A Case Study on Gemma-4)

author.name: Jeong Hyun Lee

entry.summary: Analyzing LoRA fine-tuning of Gemma-4 (12B and 31B) on long prompts, the paper shows bf16 and fp32 gradients agree in upper layers but are nearly orthogonal in lower layers, tracing the discrepancy to an ill-conditioned backward path rather than insufficient precision. The study provides careful interventions and proposes a treatment for the numerical pathology.

entry.title: DPMA: Learning to Compress Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Jon Irureta, Jon Imaz, Philipp Wiesner, Gorka Azkune, Javier Fernandez-Marques, Alex Iacob, Andrej Jovanovi\'c, Aizea Lojo, Nicholas D. Lane

entry.summary: DPMA is a retraining-free framework that jointly learns expert pruning, merging, and routing absorption for Mixture-of-Experts models via differentiable optimization under a global expert budget, with layer-wise expert allocation. This addresses the memory bottleneck that limits MoE deployment on resource-constrained hardware, going beyond prior methods that commit to a single compression operation with uniform ratios.

entry.title: Latent Jacobian Steer: Eliciting Contact-Rich Out-of-Distribution Behaviors from Pretrained Humanoid Controllers

author.name: S K Swaminathan, Shivam Sood, Shreyansh Kansal, Chengyang He, Guillaume Adrien Sartoretti

entry.summary: Latent Jacobian Steer (LJS) elicits contact-rich out-of-distribution behaviors from pretrained latent-conditioned humanoid controllers by coupling direct joint-action sampling with the semantics of the frozen controller's learned latent space. It trades off the strengths of raw joint exploration and latent exploration, steering toward desired physical effects without destroying learned coordination. This addresses a practical challenge for adapting behavioral foundation models in humanoid robotics to new contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models

author.name: Konstantinos Skianis, Aristidis Likas

entry.summary: Studies weight-space programming, where a frontier language model reads and rewrites another network's weights without gradient descent, enabling a weaker model to perform tasks with an empty prompt. Across six tasks, the editors write the ICL task vector into near-silent MLP units keyed to prompt format, matching the accuracy of in-context learning and fine-tuning.

entry.title: Silent Arbitration: How Large Language Models Resolve Co-Authoritative Conflicting Instructions

author.name: Sihyeon Lee, Jiwoo Kum, Jihun Song, Chanwoo Kim, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: This study examines what happens when a prompt assigns two opposing personas with equal authority and no priority rule. Across eight conflict types and five LLMs, models acknowledge incompatibility in 72% of direct checks but surface it in only 22% of task responses, a phenomenon the authors call silent arbitration. Dominance resolves 45% of conflicts, and 35% of compromise-labeled responses retain hidden bias.

entry.title: 3D Open-Vocabulary Detection via Visual Alignment and Generative Captions

author.name: Thomas E. Huang, Alex Zihao Zhu, Hao Xiang, Tianyi Cai, Jingwei Ji, Yuliang Zou, Jiafan Yu, Xin Huang, Mingxing Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-part framework for open-vocabulary 3D object detection in outdoor scenes. It uses class-agnostic 3D proposals with a spatially-aware VLM to distill per-instance semantic embeddings into a 3D model without manual labels, and additionally leverages generative captions to enhance zero-shot capability and inject domain-specific information. The approach targets the difficulty of transferring 2D VLM semantics into 3D contexts.

entry.title: SonoAtlasWorld: Anatomy-Grounded Ultrasound World Models for Wide-Range Scanning

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Boris Mailhe, Hang Yu, Yikang Liu, Xiao Chen, Ankush Mukherjee, Terrence Chen, Shanhui Sun

entry.summary: SonoAtlasWorld is a generative world model for robotic ultrasound that anchors simulated scans to a persistent 3D anatomical asset extracted from CT, treating anatomy as the environment state. Probe actions determine anatomical and acoustic visibility for a causal ultrasound generator trained on clinical videos, enabling scalable policy training and repeatable evaluation without risking real patients.

entry.title: Beyond What They Say: Cue Acknowledgment and Robustness in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ali Rahimiakbr, Arvin Baghal Asl, Nima Niroumand, Mohammad Parsa Jafarnejady, Hossein Shahabadi, Amirmohammad Izadi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

entry.summary: Investigates whether VLM explanations that acknowledge misleading cues indicate robustness, comparing matched answers and explanations under helpful, misleading, and conflicting cues. A paired analysis shows models can select endorsed wrong answers more often while acknowledging cues more often, demonstrating that disclosure of a cue does not imply resistance to it.

entry.title: MoHA: Model-Conditioned Harness Adaptation for Long-Video Agents

author.name: Jianghan Chao, Wenhui Tan, Hang Su, Qiuyu Tian, Tanxiao Li, Bingzi Zhang, Zequn Liu, Ruihua Song, Yingce Xia

entry.summary: MoHA treats the execution harness of long-video agentic systems as a model-conditioned optimization object, adapting a common initial harness to the specific planner and observer models it hosts. This recognizes that different planner-observer stacks benefit from different executable harnesses under the same task distribution.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Steering: Where Verifiable Reasoning Can Enter an End-to-End Driving Planner

author.name: Gautam Kumar Jain, Atharva Mahindrakar, Shubham Phoolari, Ignacio Alvarez, Carsten Markgraf, Constanze Hungar, Christoph Lauer, Julian Staehler

entry.summary: The paper examines whether scene reasoning from a vision-language model can verifiably influence a frozen end-to-end driving planner (Drive-JEPA). Fine-tuned VLM facts yield no detectable benefit when read by learned components, whereas a rule-based fact check that rejects paths contradicting stated facts gains 2.4 EPDMS points on navhard, though its margin over a control is statistically uncertain.

entry.title: Latent Space Planning with Sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Anindita Ghosh, Uttaran Bhattacharya, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: This paper addresses limitations of sampling-based and gradient-based planners in learned world models by applying sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to planning in latent space. SMC maintains a population of hypotheses with resampling, avoiding the fresh Gaussian proposals of MPPI and the local minima of gradient methods, using intermediate distributions to bridge toward goal-reaching trajectories. This matters for long-horizon planning with world models, a key capability for general robot autonomy.

entry.title: OpenRing: Deadlock-Free Execution of Any Planner on AGV Floors with One-Way Lanes

author.name: Zhihao Lin, Anh-Tu Nguyen, Hui Zhang, Yoshinobu Kawahara

entry.summary: OpenRing guarantees deadlock-free execution of arbitrary planners for automated guided vehicles on floors with one-way lanes: a local guard vetoes only moves or route changes that could close a fully occupied ring, with provable guarantees despite planner loss or arbitrary proposals. The paper proves necessity of every guard veto within its rule class and guarantees eventual progress. This is a strong formal-methods contribution for warehouse multi-robot systems.

entry.title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Guangzhao Dai, Guoxin Lian, Shuo Wang, Shengbin Yue, Qianru Sun, Xiangbo Shu, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: NavRSI is a framework that recursively improves the harness governing frozen LLMs in vision-and-language navigation, using a designer agent that rewrites navigation tools, memory, and agent roles based on collected trajectories and failure diagnostics. Effective revisions are retained across rounds in a closed-loop self-improvement process. This connects to broader interest in automated agent-harness optimization.

entry.title: Eval awareness remains an unsolved problem

author.name: Vincent Cheng

entry.summary: This post compiles recent system card evidence that frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Mythos 5.2, and Claude Opus 5.5, show high rates of evaluation awareness, undermining confidence that low observed misbehavior in evals predicts deployment behavior. The author argues eval awareness remains unsolved and structures the problem, surveying mitigations and why current approaches fall short.

entry.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress

author.name: Congyuan Yu, Runping Tian

entry.summary: AstronautBench evaluates LLM agent self-improvement with fixed weights across episodes using three coupled views on the same run: knowledge, whether the agent's own evidence supports that knowledge, and task progress. Built on Outer Wilds, where each 22-minute episode resets the world, isolating what the agent retains. A novel embodied benchmark decoupling self-improvement from weight updates.

entry.title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization

author.name: Chengxi Li, Liang Xiao, Yutao Wang, Wenhao Lin, Xinzhuang Xiong, Han Zhao, Evangeline Young

entry.summary: EDAGoat is claimed to be the first EDA-aware coding agent for optimizing expert-engineered GPU code in electronic design automation, combining an optimization mode with four cross-project GPU patterns and a mandatory validation mode enforcing EDA constraints. It ships with a benchmark of five GPU EDA projects, four task families, and 55 circuit inputs.

entry.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: \'Elodie C\^ot\'e-Gauthier, Doina Precup, Isabeau Pr\'emont-Schwarz

entry.summary: The paper builds a successor feature basis from eigenvectors of a fixed reference policy's transition matrix, inspired by the identification of entorhinal grid cells with successor representation eigenvectors. This yields closed-form successor features that are linear combinations of same-state base features, enabling reuse for continual RL across changing tasks.

entry.title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models

author.name: Yao Tong, Jiaxin Qi, Yan Cui, Jinli Ou, Yuhua Zheng, Jianqiang Huang

entry.summary: Identifies Modal Polarization, a failure pattern where multimodal LLMs facing counter-intuitive video content bifurcate into Cognitive Inertia (clinging to priors despite visual evidence) or Perceptual Inertia (trusting perception while ignoring logical inconsistencies). Introduces TheaterBench, a benchmark of counter-intuitive scenarios violating physical or common-sense expectations, to diagnose this failure.

entry.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models

author.name: Huiyuan Tian, Chih-Yung Wen, Shijian Li

entry.summary: The paper draws an analogy between planning with latent world models and adversarial example generation, showing that more CEM iterations can lower predicted cost while losing up to half of previously solved problems on DINO-WM and LeWM. It proposes a round-trip test that executes plans during search to count solved-then-lost problems, exposing failures invisible to the model's own predictions.

entry.title: WEIR: Watershed Exploration and Drift-Aware Prefix Shrinkage for Multi-Turn Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pixel Nomand, Elena Voss, Marcus Hale, Sofia Reyes

entry.summary: WEIR is an actor-critic framework for multi-turn LLM agent RL that addresses two flaws of prefix-tree trajectory methods: stale off-policy outcomes polluting critic targets and wasted branching on dead-end states. Grounded in a Doob turn-variance identity, it performs drift-aware prefix shrinkage and watershed-based exploration to concentrate computation on decisive decisions.

entry.title: Pharos: Learning to Control Rare Events at Scale

author.name: Jiajun He, Jacky Chen, Weiliang Luo, Heather Kulik, David R. Koes, Carles Domingo-Enrich, Yuanqi Du

entry.summary: Pharos is a stochastic optimal control framework that jointly learns the probability of rare transitions and how to steer simulations toward them, so sampling and learning improve each other. Across biomolecular benchmarks it achieves order-of-magnitude convergence speedups over prior algorithms and transfers across ion assembly systems in explicit solvent.

entry.title: Spiking Neural Networks Incrementally Track Firing-Rate Networks

author.name: Hyunseok Oh, Youngki Lee

entry.summary: The paper proves that the output of a discrete spiking neural network continuously tracks the instantaneous output of its corresponding firing-rate (ANN) network, providing theory for how SNNs efficiently process unbounded data streams. Building on this, LIF-Stream is a conversion framework where the converted SNN reuses prior activation state and computes only activation updates between frames, enabling efficient continuous inference. This connects neuroscience-inspired computation with practical streaming inference efficiency.

entry.title: PP-CFG: Polarity-Preserving Guidance for Controllable Few-Step Image and Video Generation

author.name: Junyi He, Xu Peng, Chengming Xu, Sixiao Zheng, Donghao Luo, Chao Wen, Peng Tang, Xijie Huang, Chengjie Wang, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Proposes PP-CFG, an architecture that preserves classifier-free guidance and negative prompting in few-step distilled diffusion models by keeping positive and negative text conditions separate and combining their attention responses with opposite signs. A Scale-Time Polarity Mixer lets prompt influence vary with guidance scale and timestep, demonstrated on Wan2.1 video and Qwen-Image with single-pass efficiency.

entry.title: Ego2Ego: Generative Visual Perspective Taking Across Collaborators

author.name: Chuhan Jiao, John Gideon, Anshul Gupta, Guy Rosman, Andreas Bulling

entry.summary: Defines generative visual perspective taking: given an egocentric video, a scene point cloud, and a collaborator's camera trajectory, generate the continuous egocentric video from the collaborator's perspective. The task is challenging due to extreme viewpoint shifts and dynamic occlusions, going beyond prior state-estimation or question-answering formulations of perspective taking.

entry.title: RoboPRO: A Perturbation-Resilient and Obstacle-Aware Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhiyuan Li, Charles Eret, Dingsheng Liu, Xuan Zhao, Joshua Choi, Yangzheng Wu, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang, Amir Rasouli

entry.summary: RoboPRO is a benchmark for manipulation that goes beyond clean tabletop settings, comprising 80 bimanual atomic and compositional tasks across four furnished indoor environments with 16,000 demonstrations. It measures perturbation resilience and safe obstacle-aware planning, addressing whether policies fail safely and why they fail.

entry.title: PonderPounce-WM: When Does Predicting the Future Help Context-Dependent Robot Control?

author.name: Jaeyoon Jung, Suhwan Choi, Yunsung Lee, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: PonderPounce-WM extends the PonderPounce framework with future-predicting tokens supervised on visual-feature changes, carefully disentangling predictive supervision from direct future conditioning through token ordering and delivery ablations. On RoboMME, cognition-first ordering with cognition-only delivery raises success from 60.83% to 67.42%. The paper offers a scientifically careful answer to when and how world-model prediction benefits MLLM-based robot control.

entry.title: What Must a Model Tell a Planner? Outcome Interfaces for Risk-Aware Planning After Robot Damage

author.name: Hassan Iqbal, Krishna Kumar

entry.summary: This conceptual-experimental paper asks what interface a learned model should expose to a planner when a damaged robot must trade off feasible routes against mission-specific risk. Using simulated Unitree Go2 and H1 robots with weakened motors, payloads, or reduced friction, it compares decision policies, penalty-augmented policies, and outcome models that predict feasibility and cost consequences. It argues outcome models support flexible risk-aware replanning after damage better than fixed policies.

entry.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs

author.name: Radhika Bhargava, Shinibali Bhattacharyya, George Mihaila, Jay Prajapati, Anwesan Pal, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces normative-descriptive calibration: whether an LLM treats matched candidates differently when asked to predict an outcome versus decide one. The NDCB benchmark provides 697 matched-pair scenarios across six domains, testing a fairness dimension no existing benchmark covers. Moves beyond single-objective demographic discrimination testing toward decision-role sensitivity.

entry.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs

author.name: Vinnam Kim, Seong Hoon Seo, Junhan Kim, Jaeseong You, An Chen

entry.summary: MixFold executes 3-bit and symmetric 2-bit LLM weights using native integer NPU operations without widening, and assigns datatypes to output-channel groups aligned with matrix-unit tiles for finer-than-layer mixed precision. This addresses the gap where quantization memory savings fail to yield decoding speedups on mobile NPUs. A hardware-aware inference optimization with Samsung-like industry grounding.

entry.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming

author.name: Chengming Liu, Leon Viti, Hongxu Chen, Erdem Kemik, Mary-Anne Williams, Ruth Oliver

entry.summary: Studies reward fidelity in adversarial RL red-teaming of financial-services LLM guardrails, identifying false wins when attacks omit prescribed PII or when a reward judge credits non-violating responses. Compares decision models and logged Opus 4.8 judgments on an off-target set, showing judges can award false wins and that post-training improves agreement. Highlights reward-hacking risks in automated red-teaming loops.

entry.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain

author.name: Tengfei Shao, Asma Rezaei, Ali Reza Kamali

entry.summary: The authors build a graded-dependence exact reference over binary worlds to price how well LLMs avoid double counting evidence from shared sources in retrieval, consensus, and memory fusion. Testing claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6.1-sol across 2,976 worlds shows rule agreement and posterior gain can diverge in both directions.

entry.title: $\gamma$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Xiaotao Zhang, Lin Qian, Hao Zhang, Xuanrui Cui, Yuehao Huang, Yunzi Wu, Yucheng Deng, Jiankun Dong, Hujun Yin, Xinhai Li, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: gamma-Scape is an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence where agents compose motion tools and learned skills for combined navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. Its BenchForge component grounds structured objectives in physical task instances with instructions, reference programs, and goal evaluators while preserving valid agent strategies.

entry.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents

author.name: Yiwen Qiu, Che Sun, Shu Shen, Wentao Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free decision-point evidence sufficiency assessment with a three-tier sequential triage protocol for on-premise clinical AI agents, deciding when diagnoses can be auto-accepted versus deferred to clinician review. A 4B model scores evidence sufficiency, and calibration via Wilson confidence bounds allocates cases to single-run, five-run consistency, or full-deferral tiers to meet a 95% clinical target at reduced compute.

entry.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Arshia Rafieioskouie, Matthew Lucas, Tzu-Han Hsu, Borzoo Bonakdarpour

entry.summary: SLICR advances specification-guided RL to adversarial, partially observable settings by using Strategy Logic, which quantifies over agents' strategies and embeds LTL, to specify objectives and constraints. It enables reasoning about how agents should respond to other agents' strategies and is evaluated on Predator-Prey and Google Research Football benchmarks.

entry.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval

author.name: Venkata Chivukula, Zifeng Wang, Jinsung Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes ERA, a system for cross-model latent retrieval that avoids re-embedding an entire corpus when switching encoders: it spends a small anchor budget via cosine farthest point sampling, trains a lightweight adapter with a manifold alignment loss combining directional alignment and orthogonal regularization, and pairs it with a deterministic router. This targets production retrieval systems facing encoder migration and cold-start cost.

entry.title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology

author.name: Zhixuan Ge, Wei Qiu

entry.summary: Opsis provides a typed question interface over a frozen pathology encoder so a frontier model can query a slide encoded once, rather than relying on written descriptions or thumbnails. On 189 breast pathology report questions, baseline frontier models score 0.50-0.66, below the majority class, while Opsis enables many composed checklist questions to be answered from a single encoding of a 14,000-tile slide.

entry.title: Felid: A Flexible and Efficient Design for Transformer Fine-Tuning over Encrypted Data

author.name: Linru Zhang, Jun Jie Sim, Xiangning Wang, Jiahao Zhong, Kaiyu Zhou, Huanyi Ye, Yongsen Zheng, Lushan Song, Xiaojian Liang, Yingting Liu, Yujing Sun, Huaxiong Wang, Pu Duan, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: Felid advances privacy-preserving transformer fine-tuning under fully homomorphic encryption by attacking the bottleneck at the ciphertext-operation level, with a novel packing strategy supporting flexible input batching and operation-specific matrix evaluation algorithms that reduce rotations and linearization costs. It enables non-interactive fine-tuning on sensitive data.

entry.title: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Changin Choi, Jungwon Park, Jungmin Ko, Jimyeong Kim, Wonjong Rhee

entry.summary: VMSA is an agentic framework for long-video question answering that jointly designs structured video memories (segment captions, entity-event memory, and more) and memory skills for deciding what to search, which memory sources to access, and how to link evidence across distant temporal intervals. It targets videos spanning hours to days.

entry.title: No Audio, No Transcripts, No Problem: LLM-based ASR Adaptation Using Only Domain Documents

author.name: Sergio Burdisso, Dairazalia S\'anchez-Cort\'es, Esa\'u Villatoro-Tello, Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Manjunath K E, Kadri Hacioglu, Petr Motlicek, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: The paper shows a speech recognizer can be adapted to a new domain using only written documents — either used directly or rendered by an LLM into synthetic spoken dialogs — via a denoising-based text-only adaptation method, with no target audio or transcripts. Across in-domain, out-of-domain, and cross-domain settings on two corpora, document-only adaptation matches or approaches real transcriptions.

entry.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection

author.name: Sivashankar Selvarajan, Piyush Verma, Sumit Kumar, Sharayu N. Deshmukh

entry.summary: ARCAS 290M is Neural Defend's frozen production foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio, designed to generalize across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages without benchmark-specific fine-tuning. Evaluated on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks as released, it ranks first on the Podonos leaderboard with the lowest equal error rate among systems including commercial detectors.

entry.title: Graph Signal Generation via Graph-Aware Diffusion Models

author.name: Vimal K B, Sergio Rozada, Antonio G. Marques, Elvin Isufi, Hadi J. Rad

entry.summary: This paper proposes graph-aware diffusion (GAD), where the forward noise process is heat diffusion on the graph rather than independent per-node noise, giving a clean Gaussian channel interpretation in the graph Fourier basis. It adds Mode-Adaptive SNR Scheduling to handle frequency-dependent attenuation for graph signal imputation and forecasting.

entry.title: Structural Agreement Indicates Prediction Accuracy For Protein-Ligand Co-Folding

author.name: J. Henry Broster, Bojana Popovic, Diana Kondinskaia, Charlotte M. Deane, Fergus Imrie

entry.summary: Across seven protein-ligand co-folding models, the authors show that built-in confidence scores barely improve over random prediction selection, with about three-quarters of structures being all-correct or all-wrong. They demonstrate that structural agreement among independently generated predictions is a more reliable accuracy indicator than model confidence.

entry.title: HR-Merge: Model Merging with Headroom-Weighted Residual Refinement

author.name: Jiakang Huang, Xueyan Zhang, Renyi Cai, Jingcheng Niu, Jiaru Li, Yining Wang, Josh Zhang, Jiahe Jiang, Jinman Zhao, Gerald Penn, Baharan Mirzasoleiman

entry.summary: The paper shows accuracy lost in model merging remains recoverable from each task's residual (task vector minus merged update), and that validation headroom predicts where recovery pays off. HR-Merge is a training-free wrapper that weights residuals by headroom and re-merges them, improving any base merging method for combining LoRA experts.

entry.title: From Gist to Verbatim: The Controllable Path of One Image Through a Diffusion Prior

author.name: Luca Saglietti, Luca Giammanco, Marc Mezard, Chiara Plizzari, Luca Biggio

entry.summary: This work reframes memorization in diffusion models as a control problem, steering a frozen diffusion model toward a target image via a learned conditioning signal and tracking how the memory forms during training. It shows memory passes through a gist regime that preserves semantics with diverse appearance before converging to verbatim reproduction, with semantic organization emerging without any labels.

entry.title: Loop-OPF: Solver-Informed Learning for Optimal Power Flow with Inference-Time Topology Adaptivity

author.name: Mohamad Chehade, Hao Zhu

entry.summary: Loop-OPF is a solver-informed neural network whose layers are built from primal-dual hybrid gradient iterations, guaranteeing optimal and feasible solutions for DC optimal power flow under standard convexity conditions. Unlike prior learning-for-OPF methods, it adapts at inference time to unseen topologies such as line or generator outages. This is a meaningful step toward deploying learned surrogates in safety-critical power grid operations.

entry.title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison

author.name: Koji Hashimoto, Masaki Murata, Gakuto Ogiwara

entry.summary: The authors propose the 3D Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods, constructing fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon numbers 1 through 4 without imposing symmetry ansatzes. Remarkably, known toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic configurations emerge spontaneously from random initial lumps, and variational energies fall slightly below published reference values with topological charge preserved to about one part in a million. The work also compares KAN and MLP architectures on this task.

entry.title: ORBIT: Offset-based Activation Steering for Cross-lingual Multimodal Fact Verification

author.name: Huy Trieu, Duy-Minh Nguyen-Tran, Thanh-Dat Nguyen, Huy Tien Nguyen, Tung Le

entry.summary: ORBIT mitigates the disproportionate accuracy collapse small vision-language models suffer on low-resource languages in multimodal fact verification, using an inference-time intervention rather than scale or fine-tuning. It estimates span-specific offset vectors from parallel claim-evidence instances and applies them to claim and evidence representations to correct cross-lingual degradation. Experiments across eight languages show meaningful gains without training.

entry.title: When Do LLM-Elicited Priors Help? A Controlled Audit of Language Models as Priors for Small-Sample Bayesian Regression

author.name: Ran Zou, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Audits the use of LLMs as prior-elicitation tools for small-sample Bayesian regression using hidden feature names, post-cutoff housing data, and adversarially wrong feature descriptions. Findings show high error correlation (0.92-0.99) across draws and vendors, and that averaging draws creates overconfidence rather than accuracy.

entry.title: Tracktail: Multi-View 3D Point Tracking without Depth Input

author.name: Katie L Rupp, Jonathan Wong, Sharmishtaa Seshamani, Ana Mafalda Vicente, Lili Karashchuk

entry.summary: Tracktail is an architecture for tracking query points in 3D from multiple calibrated camera views without depth input, separating per-camera video feature encoding from a per-query decoder. Camera cross-attention is restricted to the decoder across queries, enabling efficient inference at 7 FPS and under 4 GB memory for 10 views and 100 query points. The authors also introduce per-camera scene-scale normalization and a new Multi-View Point Odyssey benchmark.

entry.title: Real-Time On-Drone Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection for Wilderness Search and Rescue

author.name: Jacqueline Liu (Kic'i), Gyabaah Kyere (Kic'i), Chengyan Liu (Kic'i), Kenneth Chiu (Kic'i), Lynn Marie (Kic'i), Church, Sean Gleason, Jayson Boubin

entry.summary: SABL is an edge-computing pipeline that runs hyperspectral anomaly detection (exponentially moving Reed-Xiaoli plus DBSCAN filtering) on drones to flag candidate regions where missing persons may be, targeting indicators that are rare or lack thermal signatures. It was evaluated on data from a 10-day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue in remote Alaska, achieving real-time on-drone processing.

entry.title: Real-Anchored Complementary Evidence for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Wenpeng Mu, Tanfeng Sun, Zhenyu Shao, Qiang Xu, Xinghao Jiang

entry.summary: RACE detects AI-generated images using only authentic training images, exploiting regularities of real photographs rooted in physical image formation rather than generator-specific artifacts. It combines a global pathway assessing proximity to authentic references plus responses to controlled perturbations with local evidence for complementary detection signals.

entry.title: PhysForce: Physics-aware Force Control for Interactive Video World Model

author.name: Xuancheng Xu, Xiaofeng Wang, Yue Ma, Zheng Zhu, Bing-Kun Bao

entry.summary: PhysForce improves interactive video world models by representing applied forces directly rather than as motion trajectories, which reduces overreliance on displacement priors and better localizes force-induced state changes. It also addresses the scarcity of force-annotated data to produce physically consistent, temporally stable predictions in unseen scenarios.

entry.title: SIR-Agent: Skill-Augmented Image Restoration Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Yijian Wang, Qingsen Yan, Weiyu Zhou, Mingde Zhang, Axi Niu, Haokui Zhang, Jiantao Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes SIR-Agent, an MLLM-based image restoration agent that maintains restoration knowledge in a scalable skill library rather than fine-tuning model parameters, avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Recursive self-improvement via Chain Feedback-driven Skill Revision analyzes restoration chains to identify and revise weak operations, evolving the library over time.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Human Demonstration: Learning from Scored Trajectory Alternatives for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Xinyao Rao, Zecheng Tang, Liuxuan Sun, Zheyuan Lai, Minjun Yu, Xun Cao, Wei Li

entry.summary: DriveSTA augments end-to-end autonomous driving training by generating scored trajectory alternatives offline through smooth deformations of the single logged human trajectory, evaluated in simulation against traffic. These alternatives supervise autoregressive proposal generation and residual flow refinement without costly VLM inference at test time.

entry.title: TacHOI: Contact-Aware Object Reconstruction and Tracking for Egocentric Videos

author.name: Jackson Codd, Haoyu Li, Xianyi Cheng

entry.summary: TacHOI is a training-free framework that fuses tactile contact information with monocular egocentric vision for joint hand-object reconstruction and tracking, using calibrated contacts on the hand as a physical ruler to resolve scale-depth ambiguity. It requires no object templates or depth sensors.

entry.title: RoboDyna: A Benchmark for Evaluating Robotic Manipulation under Physically Grounded Dynamics

author.name: Zhiyuan Li, Rui Heng Yang, Xuan Zhao, Amir Rasouli

entry.summary: RoboDyna is a benchmark for evaluating manipulation policies under realistic, physically grounded dynamic environments, addressing gaps where existing physics benchmarks lack closed-loop action evaluation and manipulation benchmarks use implausible object motions and freeze the environment during inference. It explicitly makes computation time relevant to outcomes. This fills a genuine evaluation gap for dynamic manipulation reasoning.

entry.title: Beyond Future Views: Exploring Future-State World Models for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Kangyi Wu, Pengna Li, Yucheng Wang, Yance Fang, Xihan Ma, Zhizhong Su, Yang Wu, Ye Deng, Jinjun Wang, Jianyi Liu

entry.summary: This work questions whether predicting future visual observations is the right target for navigation world models in Vision-Language Navigation, drawing on cognitive science findings about hippocampal predictive maps of goals and route waypoints. It proposes organizing the future around goal states and intervening locations rather than raw future views. The reframing could influence how embodied world models are designed.

entry.title: AceVLN: Asynchronous Cloud Edge Deployment of VLNs via Latent Scheduling and Compensation

author.name: Zihao Zheng, Hangyu Cao, Yulong Han, Xichang Wu, Zhihao Mao, Maoliang Li, Jiayu Chen, Hailong Zou, Donggang Cao, Xuanzhe Liu, Hong Mei, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: AceVLN is a training-free framework for cloud-edge deployment of vision-language navigation on resource-constrained robots, addressing latent mismatch caused by inference and communication delays in asynchronous dual-system architectures. It identifies a compact Critical Subspace where action-relevant mismatch concentrates and uses Critical Feature Drift Entropy for adaptive refresh plus Critical Drift Continuity for edge-side compensation. This enables practical asynchronous VLN deployment.

entry.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization

author.name: Trupti Mohanty, Ming Du, Mitchell A. Wood, Brad L. Boyce, Remi Dingreville, Mathew J. Cherukara

entry.summary: ChatAtom is a multi-agent LLM system that converts natural-language requests into complete molecular dynamics workflows, orchestrating LAMMPS simulation and OVITO visualization agents with generator-reviewer pairs. It removes the need for users to write input scripts or analysis code. This democratizes an expert-heavy materials-science workflow.

entry.title: Many Plans at Once: Diverse Top-Quality Planning in Continuous Time

author.name: Mahyar Jahani-nasab, Hamid Rezatofighi, Mor Vered, Buser Say

entry.summary: MPAO extends top-quality, diverse planning from discrete settings to continuous-time planning for physical systems, treating each found plan as a reason to search elsewhere via sampling untrained neural networks. Produces plan sets that are simultaneously low-cost and mutually distinct, providing alternatives and warm-starts when unmodeled constraints invalidate a chosen route. Addresses the fragility of single-trajectory planners.

entry.title: MAPES: Multi-Value Alignment Pipeline via Expert Specialization

author.name: SungHo Kim, SangKeun Lee

entry.summary: MAPES treats conflicting values in alignment as a first-class concern by decomposing supervision into value-specific experts trained in isolated parameter subspaces, then recomposing them via preference-aware merging and a harmonization stage. Evaluation spans five preference alignment benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Inside Types: Epistemic Typestates for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lorenzo Bacchiani, Mario Bravetti, Giovanni Pau, Roberto Girau

entry.summary: The paper introduces epistemic typestates, a type discipline for safe multi-agent reinforcement learning where an agent's type is a protocol whose states track its beliefs, permitting only actions safe in every world consistent with its observations. Because types constrain what an agent may choose rather than how, the safety guarantee holds for any learned policy.

entry.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models

author.name: Minda Zhao, Yue Zhang, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: Presents SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework protecting image privacy against VLM inference of locations, PII, and personal attributes, using LLM agents to iteratively locate visual evidence of private information and adapt invisible perturbations, with an appearance reviewer agent rejecting artifact-visible candidates. Unlike prior adversarial perturbation methods, it preserves image quality.

entry.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion

author.name: Ziyi Ding, Yiwei Wang, Zhongxing Wei, Xianxin Lai, Yechi Liu, Xiaodi Huang, Jinghua Hou, Xiaoquan Sun, Haijier Chen, Zhe Liu, Yinan Chen, Junqiao Zhao, Xiao-Ping Zhang, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: EgoLAM improves latent action models for robot learning from egocentric video by supervising the action code with measured wrist motion and feeding camera motion separately to the forward model, separating manipulation from viewpoint change. The action encoder pools object slots around hands, and decoding requires only lightweight computation.

entry.title: THRIFTY: Cost-Constrained Reasoning-Data Synthesis for Small Language Models

author.name: Aasheesh Singh, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: THRIFTY casts cost-aware synthetic reasoning-data collection for small language models as a bandits-with-knapsack problem, using a Thompson-sampling controller to allocate a fixed generation-token budget across queries of varying difficulty, harvesting diverse correct reasoning trajectories. It improves on uniform budget allocation that ignores problem difficulty variation.

entry.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance

author.name: Artin Tajdini, Jasper C. H. Lee, Jonathan Scarlett, Kevin Jamieson

entry.summary: This theory paper studies high-probability linear regression when noise has only a finite conditional alpha-moment (alpha between 1 and 2) and covariates have limited moments, giving a black-box reduction from finite-variance regression procedures to weak-moment ones via empirical residual pruning. The reduction is agnostic to moment exponent, noise scale, and covariance.

entry.title: Mind World Models: Joint Learning of Motor EEG Representations and Action-Conditioned World Dynamics

author.name: Weikang Qiu, Zheng Huang, Tinglin Huang, Yujun Yan, Rex Ying

entry.summary: Mind World Model (MWM) treats EEG signals as latent actions in a world model over egocentric video, enabling motor-decoding pretraining from naturalistic EEG-video pairs without action annotations. This yields transferable motor representations for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces without costly cue-based trial protocols.

entry.title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty

author.name: Oliver Lundqvist, Fabricio Oliveira

entry.summary: The paper trains a physics-informed DeepONet that returns optimal-control trajectories for all sampled uncertainty scenarios in a single evaluation, then corrects predictions with one Newton step on the dynamics computed via a parallel scan. The corrected state achieves second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest up to sampling error for every control. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark it matches batched Adam and Ipopt solvers, enabling fast gradient-based control under uncertainty.

entry.title: Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization

author.name: Kasidit Srimahajariyapong, Thiparat Chotibut, Suwannachad Suwannajitt, Tithivich Paka, Ricard Puig, Yudai Suzuki, Marek Gluza, Zo\"e Holmes, Supanut Thanasilp

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for self-training quantum machine learning where optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain via Riemannian gradient updates, eliminating the quantum-to-classical measurement bottleneck. The authors derive update rules for a broad class of tasks, identify conditions for fully autonomous dynamics, and prove exponential convergence guarantees.

entry.title: TSIR: Ray-Traced Triangle Splats for Inverse Rendering

author.name: Wentao Yang, Chentao Shen, Zhengqi Zhang, Bolin Chen, Yan Ye, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: TSIR is a two-stage inverse rendering method that reconstructs opaque, relightable triangle splats from multi-view images, then estimates materials by directly ray-tracing these surfaces with Monte Carlo integration of direct and indirect light. This avoids the costly multi-layer traversal and compositing that overlapping Gaussian primitives require.

entry.title: When Visually Rich Documents Meet Multi-Vector Retrieval for Region-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Xu Yuan, Liangbo Ning, Yujuan Ding, Qing Li, Wenqi Fan

entry.summary: MV-VisRAG is a region-level Vision-RAG framework that represents visually rich documents via semantically complete regions using multi-vector retrieval, rather than coarse full-page representations. This preserves local evidence while reducing redundancy and computational overhead in retrieval and generation.

entry.title: One Behavior, Out of Order: Deterministic Execution and Parallel Simulation of ROS 2 Applications

author.name: Chengzi Huang, Behnam Khodabandeloo, Duc Anh Nguyen, Chuanchao Gao, Wang Yi

entry.summary: The paper addresses nondeterminism in ROS 2's asynchronous publish-subscribe middleware, which makes robotic application behavior vary across runs and machines and hinders fault reproduction. It introduces a lightweight coordination scheme decoupling computation and communication at predefined time instants, enabling deterministic execution and parallel simulation.

entry.title: PACE-WM: Parallel World Modeling with Action History for Visual Planning

author.name: Haishan Liu, Shijie Lian, Bin Yu, Yao Zhang, Changti Wu, Fanping Liu, Jianzheng Liu, Lei Xie, Cong Huang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: PACE-WM is a JEPA-style world model that conditions future representation prediction on a recurrent memory of executed actions, recognizing that similar observations can hide different motion states. It predicts multiple future representations in parallel without recursive feedback within a window and introduces Reference-Anchored Minimum Progress (RAMP) for planning-time action selection. The action-history conditioning idea is a sensible fix to a known world-model ambiguity.

entry.title: Hillclimbing AISafetyResearchBench

author.name: frmsaul

entry.summary: The post proposes delegating easily verifiable numeric-output tasks in AI safety research (auditing games, white-box challenges, jailbreak robustness, sparse-reward RL) to AI systems, including potentially untrusted ones, to free human researchers for threat modeling and metric design. It discusses the limits of this approach, noting that some safety problems resist quantification and that humans must still decide which metrics matter.

entry.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers

author.name: Wei Jiang, Ziran Liu, Wei Wang

entry.summary: BudgetPV is an agentic system for automated theorem proving that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers of differing cost and capability. A cross-solver predictor guides solver selection per subgoal, revised as verification feedback arrives. Avoids wasting expensive model calls on easy subgoals and cheap calls on hard ones.

entry.title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout

author.name: Panayiotis Christou, Satyapragnya Kar, Flavjo Xhelollari, Parijat Dube, Rajarshi Das

entry.summary: This study examines how injecting physical structure (conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry-aware representations, temporal consistency, learned structured dynamics) improves world models on planetary motion and mechanical systems. Findings show angular-momentum supervision helps autonomous forecasting while benefits of other regularizers depend on the paired representation and objective.

entry.title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning

author.name: Jiawei Sun, Maosen Li, Jiamin Shi, Xiaoxu Zheng, Jiun Tian Hoe, Yechao Bai, Michael Bi Mi

entry.summary: GGDriver lets each candidate trajectory in an end-to-end driving planner select its own visual evidence: a global glance proposes hypotheses, then corridor masks projected into camera views attend to native-resolution patch features for refinement and scoring. This maneuver-specific attention contrasts with scoring all candidates against one compressed scene representation.

entry.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing

author.name: Pengjie Zheng, Mengwei Xie, Huan Yang, Si Wu, Pengfei Hu, Feng Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces a layer-skipping method where individual tokens execute different numbers of layers while each request's mean executed depth matches a continuous budget, with a router deciding per-token block execution and skipped tokens passing through lightweight residual adapters without writing KV entries. A single checkpoint serves multiple budgets in the same batch, performing best or tied across three LLaMA backbones and 13 budgets.

entry.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Guangyu Zhao, Yongchang Zhang, Ruizhang Jiang, Zhihong Yu, Yuhao Zhang, Tao Wu, Qimin Zhou, Kunsong Shi, Haoran Wen, Zeyu Zhang, Yin Li, Kun Zhan, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: The paper studies visual moment memory for robotic manipulation, where agents must retain no-longer-observable visual details like an object's original location. It introduces VMBench, a suite of long-horizon tasks requiring memory of spatial locations and appearances, and MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture where a VLM memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on stored moments.

entry.title: Non-Expanding Gated Continued Fraction Architecture for Feedforward Layers in Language Models

author.name: Amit Dhurandhar, Vijil Chenthamarakshan, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy, Dennis Wei, Rahul Nair

entry.summary: Proposes a non-expanding gated continued-fraction component that can replace feedforward layers, including MLPs, GLUs, and MoE experts, in standard language model architectures, plus a method for integrating it into standard pretraining protocols. The work aims to make the parameter-efficient CoFrGeNet line of architectures drop-in compatible with mainstream LLM training.

entry.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material

author.name: Jinxiang Xie, Xinyi Zhang, Changjiang Jiang, Kexu Liu, Qi Yang, Yuxin Su

entry.summary: The paper defines role integrity as whether a senior LLM agent actually fulfills its functional responsibilities when synthesizing subagent reports, rather than merely aggregating them, and introduces RI-Bench to measure this behaviorally. It targets a blind spot in multi-agent evaluation where final-answer fluency conceals failures of oversight and judgment.

entry.title: Detecting Word-Substitution Poisoning of a RAG Knowledge Base with Relative Entropy and Runtime Verification

author.name: Ali Yousefi, Nikos Komninos, Hafizul Asad

entry.summary: The paper studies an attacker who silently poisons a RAG knowledge base (built from MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC) via synonym substitution, showing answer correctness drops from 0.714 to 0.555 with damage driven mostly by lost evidence and refusals rather than false statements. It proposes relative entropy-based detection of edited passages plus runtime verification, with a 44-question reviewed benchmark and control corpus.

entry.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents

author.name: Aasheesh Singh, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: The paper studies the advisor-executor pattern for small language model agents, showing that simply wiring an SLM to a stronger advisor fails out of the box, and proposing ADAPT, a multi-stage post-training recipe that teaches models when to seek advice in a cost-aware manner and how to follow advice across multi-step tasks. Evaluated across open- and closed-source small-model families.

entry.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring

author.name: Wenqi Zhou, Leonardo Baldo, Edwin Kolbe, Manuel Arias Chao

entry.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical multi-agent LLM assistant for the Beznau Unit 1 nuclear reactor in Switzerland, orchestrating queries across decades of siloed monitoring systems, alarm logs, specifications, and investigation reports. An orchestrating agent decomposes engineer questions into subtasks handled by specialized agents, reducing manual searches in SAP systems during instrumentation anomaly investigations. It is a rare real-world deployment study in a safety-critical industrial setting.

entry.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier

author.name: Chengchao Lv, Yin Wang, Chunzheng Zhu, Wanli Chang

entry.summary: Search-RSI is a recursive self-improvement framework for multimodal search agents that expands the retrieval backend alongside the agent's growing capability frontier. It addresses the problem of unreachable negatives: well-formed verifiable questions whose evidence is absent from the retrieval corpus, which unfairly penalize correct policies as synthesized task sets grow. Each round the current policy co-evolves with the searchable world it can actually reach.

entry.title: LEAN: Library-Based Adaptation for Asynchronous, Federated Fine-Tuning

author.name: Erdong Hu, Zhimin Ding, Yuxin Tang, Chris Jermaine

entry.summary: LEAN replaces adapter averaging in federated LoRA fine-tuning with a library mechanism: the server maintains rank-1 basis pairs that participants check out, fine-tune locally, and check back in, so each basis pair is shuffled across heterogeneous, asynchronous sites. This sidesteps permutation non-identifiability and instability of averaging adapters from dissimilar data.

entry.title: Circular Predictive Coding Unlocks Effective Depth

author.name: Tommaso Salvatori, Matteo Forasassi

entry.summary: The paper addresses depth limitations of predictive coding networks by introducing circular networks whose depth emerges from energy minimization rather than stacked layers. It proves convergence to the energy functional's equilibrium approximates the fixed-point iteration of a deep equilibrium model, effectively unlocking deep behavior without unstable error propagation.

entry.title: SDG: State-Dependent Gating at Chunk Boundaries for Linear Attention

author.name: Renjia Deng, Yuxi Liu, Yutong He, Xue Wang, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: SDG computes element-wise gates from the change in recurrent memory over a chunk and applies them at chunk boundaries, giving gated linear attention models state feedback for forgetting while preserving within-chunk parallelism. The authors develop fused kernels for several modern architectures including Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention.

entry.title: Backbone-Specific LoRA Geometry: Orthogonality, Superposition, and Provenance

author.name: Kazuhiko Kawamoto, Keigo Watanabe, Hiroshi Kera

entry.summary: The paper studies when a LoRA update trained on one pretrained backbone can be shared with or transferred to another while preserving accuracy and distinguishing individual contributions. It derives a cross-backbone correlation bound from attention symmetries and equivariant LoRA learning, and uses backbone-specific update directions as signatures (provenance) of the training backbone. This contributes to the growing understanding of low-rank adaptation geometry and cross-model update reuse.

entry.title: Alliance Rupture and Repair in Simulating Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Dialogues

author.name: Jian Chai, Yitian Yang, Siqi Liu, Yi-Chia Wang, Yi-Chieh Lee

entry.summary: This paper presents ALLY, a simulation framework that models alliance rupture, repair, and replanning in CBT dialogue, where each client has a hidden alliance state governing engagement. The counselor agent must detect ruptures from dialogue alone, repair them, and adapt treatment plans over multiple turns. This goes beyond existing CBT simulators that model client resistance without tracking alliance dynamics.

entry.title: ReactDrive: Self-Reactive Driving World Model

author.name: Yifan Wang, Xiaoqi Wang, Cho-Ying Wu, Wenbin He, Chenyu You, Liu Ren

entry.summary: ReactDrive formalizes self-reactivity in driving world models: the ability to predict how other agents respond to a specified ego action from observed history, so generated futures reflect interaction effects. This matters because unmodeled agent responses can misrepresent maneuver safety in policy evaluation and learning.

entry.title: WINSO: A Large-Size Very-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Dataset for Wind Turbine Detection and Solar Panel Segmentation

author.name: Di Wang, Ke Li, Zhaokun Li, Weiping Ni, Junzheng Wu, Yahu Liu, Quan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: Introduces WINSO, a large benchmark of 10,962 large-size very-high-resolution (0.5-0.7 m GSD) satellite images annotated for wind turbine detection and solar panel segmentation, with systematic evaluation protocols. It supports accurate spatial inventories of renewable energy infrastructure needed for energy planning and the net-zero transition.

entry.title: Serial Dependence Emerges from Optimizing Vision for Noise Robustness

author.name: Hiroshi Higashi, Keigo Sugihara, Yuichi Tanaka

entry.summary: The paper tests the hypothesis that serial dependence in human vision - perception being shaped by recent stimuli - emerges normatively from optimizing for noise robustness. Recurrent autoencoders with ConvGRU memory trained to denoise natural videos, with no history-dependent objective, spontaneously develop serial-dependence-like behavior and outperform memory-free models.

entry.title: HermiteTwin: Bicubic Hermite Shell Digital Twins for Contact-Rich Deformable Manipulation

author.name: Kangrui Zhang, Mu Huang, Xing Shen, Tiantian Liu, Bo Ren

entry.summary: HermiteTwin reconstructs digital twins of thin deformable objects from multiview video of robot manipulation, representing deformation and contact separately: a coarse bicubic Hermite shell with Kirchhoff-Love bending models smooth deformation while the gripper interacts through a dense sampled surface. Separating these concerns at different resolutions is the key idea. This addresses a real gap in contact-rich deformable object manipulation.

entry.title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design

author.name: Haoyang Wang, Weibo Gao, Zhengxiong Li, Lingfeng Tao

entry.summary: Task2Hand packages dexterous hand design as an agent-executable Skill that converts a manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model, routing candidates through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and policy-training gates with evidence records and bounded parameter revisions on failure. The agent escalates trade-offs and conflicting evidence to a human who sets design direction. It demonstrates autonomous co-design of robot morphology with human oversight.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting

author.name: Yang Liu, Shengbo Tong, Xiyuan Chen, Shiwei Hou, Sen Yuan, Hao Wang, Yanfeng Li, Hongwen Li, Yiming Zhu, Zhuolun He, Wenjian Yu

entry.summary: ZhuLong-SE is an execution-grounded LLM agent for EDA scripting that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces via a three-tier memory store with governed cross-task self-evolution. It combines API retrieval, sandbox execution, and static checking to handle sparsely documented proprietary APIs and silent failures.
