Reduces dependence on hand-crafted, hard-to-maintain EDA knowledge.

entry.title: From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents

author.name: Yaoyuan Yan, Haoxiang Jie, Zhiyou Heng, Kailin Wang, Yumiao Li, Lifeng Liu, Anwan Yan

entry.summary: The paper studies which successful agent interaction records a student should learn from, comparing nine experience selectors for a 4B language agent across 288 trained students. Optimizer-aware gradient selection beats global random and high-NLL selection by meaningful margins under controlled selection budgets.

entry.title: LiDAR Signals for Robot Locomotion: Spherical Range Images Enable Robust Sim-to-Real Transfer

author.name: Nian Liu, Xinyi Tong, Ming Ren, Long Ye, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: The paper proposes a LiDAR perception pipeline for legged locomotion that aligns simulation and reality at both the sensor level (replaying real angular sampling patterns via GPU ray casting) and the representation level (spherical range images), avoiding depth-sensor sim-to-real gaps and elevation-map drift. This enables robust sim-to-real transfer of locomotion policies.

entry.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI

author.name: Oliver Sch\"on, Adrien Banse, John Lygeros, Lars Lindemann

entry.summary: The paper challenges the assumption that LLM text generation is needed to translate natural language instructions into linear temporal logic for robot control, showing the translation can be done efficiently under on-robot compute and energy constraints. This enables formally guaranteed task correctness without cloud offloading.

entry.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search

author.name: Yi Ding, Gaurav Kumar, Rui Min, Isabella Ye, Bhavika Goyal, Emilio Antunez, Huihui Chen, Ke Xu, Xiaowei Sun, Xin Xu, Huijie Feng, Pradyumna Narayana, Golnaz Farhadi

entry.summary: An industrial framework from a large web search team for automated UX attribution: Tier 1 uses a fine-tuned Gemini XS-based encoder-decoder on telemetry for scalable sentiment regression detection (plus 9.8% PR-AUC gain on over 500,000 held-out records), while Tier 2 provides fine-grained visual-spatial diagnosis of UX anomalies. It replaces slow survey-based UX evaluation in A/B testing.

entry.title: Modeling Attributional Style at Scale: A Dataset and Analysis for Psychological Attribution Assessment and Reframing

author.name: Qiang Zhou, Hanzhen Zhu, Pan Wang, Rui Tu, Huaizhi Qu, Zhuoran Wang, Xin Hu, Lei Li, Tianlong Chen, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: Introduces the Attributional Style Transfer Dataset (ASTD), a 42,000-example benchmark with dedicated metrics for modeling, assessing, and reframing depressogenic attributional explanations, built via a prevent-filter-validate pipeline combining LLM generation with specialist validation. It grounds computational mental-health work in the reformulated Learned Helplessness theory and cognitive therapy practice.

entry.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents

author.name: Sean Maxwell

entry.summary: Epistemic-guard is an open-source Python library that proxies MCP tool calls out-of-process, binds post-tool model prose to actual execution receipts, gates durable memory writes by provenance, and defends against syndicated echo amplification, all without GPU VRAM. It targets three runtime verification gaps in tool-using agents: action fabrication, provenance collapse, and echo-based corroboration spoofing.

entry.title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning

author.name: Mingxuan Wang, Siyuan Du, Yanfeng Wang, Ya Zhang, Chencheng Zhang, Jiangchao Yao

entry.summary: KnowSR aligns multimodal patient representations with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes, signed evidence directions, and pairwise diagnostic relations to improve differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders. Patient-specific knowledge alignment and target-aware pooling inject structured disease evidence into the model.

entry.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhenxuan Fan, Zhuoya Wang, Yuqian Yuan, Wenqiao Zhang, Juncheng Li, Jun Xiao, Siliang Tang, Yueting Zhuang

entry.summary: Embodied-Harness is a dual-agent framework for robotic manipulation that improves performance by refining the execution harness without updating model weights. An Actor interacts with the environment while a Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance, supported by a hierarchical memory architecture separating short-term execution context from long-term experiential knowledge. Evidence-based reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed outcomes.

entry.title: Auditing and Adapting kNNGuard for Long-Context Prompts

author.name: Niccol\`o Ronchetti

entry.summary: This audit shows that kNNGuard, a training-free activation guardrail for LLM safety, degrades substantially on long prompts, with AUROC dropping from near 0.74-0.99 on short inputs to around 0.55 on inputs over 1000 tokens for content-harm and RAG hallucination detection. The authors trace the degradation and propose adaptations for the long-context regime.

entry.title: Hierarchical Hybrid-Coordinate Flow Matching for Accurate and Physically Plausible Apo-to-Holo Protein Generation

author.name: Minjong Kim, Jaemin Sim, Dongwoo Kim, Myunghyun Jang, Eun-Sol Kim, Juyong Lee

entry.summary: CrypticFlow is a hierarchical flow-matching model for apo-to-holo protein conformation prediction that combines Cartesian and internal-coordinate representations: an ESM-3-conditioned equivariant graph network generates sparse C-alpha anchors, and a conditional midpoint transformer fills gaps in local internal coordinates. This balances global accuracy with physically valid local backbone geometry while avoiding the lever-arm effect.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimal Small-Loss Regret in Online Convex Optimization and Applications to Contextual Search and Online Inverse Optimization

author.name: Shinsaku Sakaue

entry.summary: The paper gives small-loss regret bounds for online convex optimization using one subgradient per round, achieving O(1 + sqrt(Delta_T*)) regret without knowing the best-in-hindsight loss, with minimax optimality on l_p balls including domain dependence. It extends the metric-update revocation technique to applications in contextual search and online inverse optimization.

entry.title: Skill-JEPA: Learning Planner-Aligned Action Spaces for World Models

author.name: Tom\'as Couso Coddou, Christ Devia, Rex G. Liu, Rodrigo Toro Icarte

entry.summary: Skill-JEPA fixes a failure mode of JEPA world-model planners, whose Gaussian action proposals fall outside the distribution of training actions, by learning a state-conditioned latent skill space via a VAE and planning within it. This aligns the planner's candidate actions with the model's training distribution, improving goal-reaching as goals get farther away.

entry.title: FM4SAR-Bench 1.0: Towards A Fair Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models for SAR Image Interpretation

author.name: Mingyao Chen, Yongxiang Liu, Tianpeng Liu, Yuchen Yong, Jie Zhou, Zhenhao Yang, Pinyi Huang, Weijie Li, Jiehua Zhang, Bowen Peng, Zhimao Peng, Zhiyuan Zhang, Li Liu

entry.summary: FM4SAR-Bench 1.0 provides a unified taxonomy and fair comparative framework for foundation models in synthetic aperture radar image interpretation, addressing a fragmented ecosystem where models differ in inputs, training data, architectures, and release policies. It goes beyond task-specific benchmarks to consider data transparency, reproducibility, interpretability, and deployment readiness. This is a needed standardization effort for a specialized but operationally important remote-sensing domain.

entry.title: From Novel Combinations to Informative Absence: Structural permission, communicative opportunity, and form choice in language learning

author.name: Yanzhe Zhao

entry.summary: This single-author paper proposes a generative theory of language learning that unites inferring grammatically licensed novel expressions and treating continued absence as evidence against them, via counterfactual expression opportunities. It decomposes utterance generation into structural permission, communicative opportunity, and form choice, validating structural permission recovery across 30 artificial grammars (mean AUC 0.945) and deriving a joint evidence law linking omissions to context diversity. The theory connects formal learning theory with language acquisition.

entry.title: Beyond Prompt Imitation: Capability-Aware Video Generation with Smaller Models

author.name: Ziqi Ding, Yuxin Cao, Kai Ye, Yaobo Yang, Wei Song

entry.summary: Introduces the oracle control ladder, a methodology that measures how much of the gap to a target video small open video generators can close when given progressively richer information from the target, such as dense captions, first frames, or depth videos. On 954 clips it quantifies that captions reproduce little motion while depth videos close most of the motion gap but leave appearance untouched.

entry.title: Refrain: Learning Multi-Shot Consistency from Inconsistent References for A$^2$O Video Generation

author.name: Hongru Yan, Yue Wu, Jian-Wei Zhang, Liangbin Xie, Mingzhe Zheng, Shenghua Gao

entry.summary: Refrain is a unified model for multi-shot video generation that learns cross-shot consistency via self-supervised reconstruction, deliberately perturbing reference clips to handle disparate per-shot styles and reference-target duration mismatches. It aims to unify subject identity, scene content, and style across shots without extra attention control or memory modules.

entry.title: A High-Compression Transformer VAE for Efficient and Controllable 3D Medical Image Generation with Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Bo Liu, Bingliang Zhang, Yubo Wang, Yunxiang Li, Yang Yang, Janine M. Lupo, Hui Lin

entry.summary: The paper trains a 249M-parameter Transformer VAE on BrainTumor-256K that encodes and decodes 256-cubed volumetric medical images 7.6x faster than a comparably sized CNN VAE with near-identical PSNR, enabling diffusion transformers to generate controllable 3D medical volumes. This supports tasks like inpainting and artifact correction conditioned on the same patient.

entry.title: NormFlowSDE: Normalizing Flows for Amortized Bayesian State Estimation

author.name: Yi Zhang, Lars Mikelsons

entry.summary: NormFlowSDE learns an amortized Bayesian state estimator that outputs a distribution over state trajectories conditioned on observations and controls, avoiding explicit physical models that struggle with friction, impacts, and contact-rich deformation. Normalizing flows provide the expressive posterior needed where Kalman-style filters degrade under model mismatch. This offers a principled learned alternative to model-based state estimation.

entry.title: Synthesizing Expressive Human-Object Interactions via Test-time Latent Adaptation

author.name: Zijing Wu, Yiping Li, ZhiPeng Yu, Yuzhou Zheng, Ziyazhuo Wang, Binghui Zuo, Yangang Wang

entry.summary: ExpHOI targets an overlooked aspect of human-object interaction synthesis: the imperfect, adaptive behaviors (probing, over-exerting, staggering) humans exhibit with objects of unknown physical properties. It proposes a test-time latent adaptation framework on top of an RL-trained physics-based controller, arguing that existing kinematic and RL methods produce unrealistically flawless motions. This broadens motion synthesis beyond idealized execution.

entry.title: Analysis of Multi-Client Inference Techniques for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Stefan de Lasa, Mohammadreza Mofayezi, Gennady Pekhimenko, Nandita Vijaykumar

entry.summary: This paper characterizes how classic multi-client serving techniques, batching and co-execution, affect latency, throughput, power, and hardware utilization for Vision-Language-Action models, which currently leave robot hardware idle between inference passes and underutilized during them. The empirical analysis informs the design of future multi-VLA serving systems. It is an early systems contribution to an emerging model class.

entry.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams

author.name: Rong-Ching Chang, Hao-Chuan Wang

entry.summary: A 168-participant brainstorming experiment crossing AI partner count (one vs. two) with behavioral formation (average-calibrated vs. user-customized). Adding a second AI increased board posts but reduced human-authored ideas, while a single average-calibrated AI outperformed all other conditions. The findings offer practical guidance on human-AI team composition and reveal how AI agents can crowd out human contribution.

entry.title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Yalin Yang, Xiao Huang, Yanan Wu, Hao Yang, Ryan Zhenqi Zhou

entry.summary: This work compares weight-space programming (a model directly editing another model's weights) against LoRA fine-tuning for spatial reasoning tasks on a small Qwen3.5 model. Closed-form weight edits help but plateau, while a rank-1 LoRA trained on worked solutions reaches near-perfect accuracy with 0.09% trainable parameters, with ablations confirming gains depend on the correct weight changes.

entry.title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection

author.name: Bohan Cui, Jingyi Cui, Hongwei Wen, Feng Wang, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: H-MSAE organizes multi-resolution concepts from a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder into a coarse-to-fine hierarchy for instruction data selection, using quality-weighted, diminishing-return coverage with ancestor propagation. It avoids the annotation and graph-construction overhead of existing diversity-aware selectors while choosing compact, non-redundant subsets.

entry.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG

author.name: Minh Pham, Quang Nguyen, Phong Kieu, Cong Tran

entry.summary: GRACE is a diagnostic benchmark for GraphRAG built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata, applying four controlled interventions to evidence subgraphs such as severing support paths, adding distractors, and counterfactual answer replacement. It contains 4,028 questions and 20,140 question-graph pairs, enabling fine-grained analysis of whether failures come from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with parametric knowledge.

entry.title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification

author.name: Targol Bakhtiarvand, Terrance E. Boult, Jugal Kalita, Adham Atyabi

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the TUSZ v2.0.3 corpus, defining known and unknown classes via the clinical taxonomy based on subject representation. It emphasizes that forcing wrong labels on rare seizure types is worse than abstaining, and includes fairness analysis.

entry.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech

author.name: C\^ome Hosxe, Rachid Riad, Quentin Spinat

entry.summary: This paper introduces SLP-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates whether reasoning audio language models make factually accurate claims about a speaker's voice during their chain of thought, checking each acoustic statement against clinicians' perceptual ratings. Spanning five clinician-rated datasets and 25 perceptual dimensions of clinical speech, it goes beyond prior evaluations that only scored final answers. This matters because audio models are increasingly used in clinical settings, and unverified acoustic reasoning could lead to misleading or unsafe conclusions.

entry.title: Your Judge Inherits Your Prompt: In-Context Label Bias in an LLM-as-Judge Is Directional, Not Symmetric

author.name: Abdullah Ahmad, Ahmed J. O. Ahmed, Luca Citi

entry.summary: Shows that an LLM judge in a frozen multimodal video-QA evaluation pipeline absorbs the Yes/No label balance of its few-shot demonstrations, and characterizes this bias as directional rather than symmetric, validated against two-annotator human consensus on 200 examples per dataset. The finding warns that judge prompts systematically steer verdicts even when generated answers are held fixed.

entry.title: FoRe: A Force-Guided Framework for Autonomous Grasp Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shuai Peng, Yongkai Liao, Yuxin Cheng, Haoyuan Wang, Jian Huang

entry.summary: Introduces FoRe, a framework for autonomous recovery from local grasping failures in VLA-based manipulation, using force feedback to partition demonstrations into approach-grasp and transport-placement stages and train separate policies. This addresses the tendency of policies to continue transport after a failed grasp due to overreliance on proprioceptive cues and limited retry supervision.

entry.title: PACE: Policy Augmentation and Compensation With Explicit Disturbance Estimation for Robust Locomotion

author.name: Shixuan Han, Yuyang Wang, Jingting Jia, Zeshuai Chen, Jindou Jia, Kexin Guo, Xiang Yu

entry.summary: PACE improves quadruped locomotion robustness by explicitly estimating a joint-space disturbance that lumps payload changes, center-of-mass shifts, actuator degradation, and external forces, then feeding this estimate back into both the RL policy and the controller. This relaxes the reliance on broad domain randomization and improves tracking and generalization.

entry.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

author.name: Yongkang He, Xiaofen Xing, Xiangmin Xu

entry.summary: MoReWorld is an action-conditioned video world model framework that focuses dynamics learning on the motion region — the part of the environment responding to robot actions — instead of global reconstruction error. This reduces physically implausible artifacts like hallucinated contact effects in robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation.

entry.title: Taking Apart and Putting Together: Tracking Objects Through Physical Transformations

author.name: Davide Gardenal, Mingxuan Liu, Flavio Vella, Quentin Guimard, Elisa Ricci

entry.summary: This paper introduces Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), a new video tracking task where objects must be tracked through physical assemblies and disassemblies, requiring maintenance of a state graph of entity relationships and semantic labeling of transformations. The authors observe that foundation models like SAM 2/3 preserve tracklets through appearance changes but fail to update semantic identities as objects physically evolve, and prior work handles only disassemblies via expensive failure-triggered searches. They propose TIPO, a training-free framework that continuously infers transformations via proposals and overlaps.

entry.title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act

author.name: Clara Punzi, Stefano Tramacere, Andrea Fedele, Sezer Kutluk, Roberto Pellungrini, Gizem Gezici, Paolo Baracco, Laura Castello, Eleonora Cusin, Eduardo Costa, Amedeo Giacovelli, Mario D'Almo, Fosca Giannotti, Dino Pedreschi, Marzio Di Vece

entry.summary: The paper translates the EU AI Act's obligations for high-risk AI systems, specifically Articles 9-15 and Annex IV, into techno-normative requirements and guiding questions for AI-assisted recruitment. It focuses on the hardest case: pipelines integrating third-party general-purpose AI models. The toolkit aims to support legal-by-design development of recruitment systems.

entry.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs

author.name: Junying Wang, Yijin Guo, Yalun Wu, Ziheng Jiao, Farong Wen, Qihang Yan, Wenzhe Li, Ye Shen, Qi Jia, Chunyi Li, Zicheng Zhang, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: The paper defines Scientific Model Robustness as a VLM's ability to detect anomalies, assess solvability, and self-calibrate when facing erroneous or missing information, introducing RoSci-Bench with 1,220 samples built via a seed-variant strategy across six degradation types. The authors also propose RoSci-Agent, a framework to mitigate VLM fragility under information error and loss. It targets the gap between idealized benchmark inputs and messy real-world scientific data.

entry.title: Who Should Verify? Reviewer Selection with Partial Information and Outcome Audits

author.name: The Viet Bui, Tien Mai

entry.summary: This theory paper formalizes how to cheaply certify that a chosen AI reviewer procedure is within a specified number of correct answers of the best available procedure, given unobserved review evidence and priced verification keys. It provides an exact stopping rule, an integer program, and a polynomial-time approximation within a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Improving the Optimisation Landscape for Particle Mixtures

author.name: Yan Lin, David T. Frazier, Paula Cordero Encinar, Chris J. Oates

entry.summary: This paper proves that the mixture predictive likelihood, commonly used to train equally weighted particle mixtures, is poorly suited to gradient-based optimization because training signal can be starved from poorly matched particles. The authors propose a regularized risk combining individual and mixture risks, imposing a reverse-KL barrier on particle responsibilities to guarantee every particle receives training signal.

entry.title: COMPASS: Cross-modal Observation with Multi-Path Adaptive Stopping and Selection for Early Time Series Classification

author.name: Cheng-En Chung, Yujia Wu, Oscar Tai-Yuan Chen, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: This paper introduces COMPASS, a two-stage framework for early time-series classification in multimodal settings, where the system must jointly decide when to stop observing data and which prediction branch (two modality-specific or one fusion branch) should produce the final output. The first stage trains cross-modal feature exchange and gated fusion with branch-wise supervision at every observed prefix, while the second stage learns a shared four-action controller for stopping and selection decisions. Experiments on six physiological and wearable datasets demonstrate the approach, which matters for time-sensitive applications like health monitoring where waiting for more data carries real costs.

entry.title: PLoQ: A Prompt-Specific Low-Rank Basis for 4-bit Quantization of LLM Activations

author.name: Faraz Tahmasebi, Michael Pellauer, Hyoukjun Kwon, Sitao Huang

entry.summary: PLoQ introduces prompt-adaptive low-rank decomposition for 4-bit activation quantization of LLMs, extracting dominant activation components per prompt before quantization and restoring them within the layer GEMM without modifying weights. This addresses the limitation of offline-calibrated transformations that fix a single protected subspace for all prompts.

entry.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction

author.name: Haowei He, Ziwen Zhao, Chenshuo Pan, Gang Lin, Zhihao Yang, Chao Wang, Xinzhang Liu, Kaidong Yu, Han Gao, Dongfang Li, Menglin Yang, Shuangyong Song, Yongxiang Li

entry.summary: This paper studies how to mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope for manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections, identifying a trade-off between under-mixing (streams degenerate into near-independent paths) and over-mixing (streams become indistinguishable). The authors propose cmHC, which controls mixing via geometric contraction, and theoretically validate it by bounding cumulative mixing behavior.

entry.title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning

author.name: Umberto Biccari, Junqing Huang, Kang Liu, Enrique Zuazua

entry.summary: The paper theoretically analyzes flow matching with linear interpolation between Gaussian and empirical samples, showing the squared distance to the training set generates paths that contract exponentially toward the nearest sample. It proves restarted trajectories approximate these paths uniformly away from Voronoi interfaces, illuminating how training-set geometry shapes which samples get probability mass.

entry.title: Renormalized Entropy from Symmetries: Simplicity Bias and Neural Heat Death

author.name: Vasco Portilheiro, Samuel Liebana, Andrew Saxe, Peter Orbanz

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how parameter symmetries of neural networks shape implicit bias by deriving equilibrium distributions over represented functions under Langevin dynamics with vanishing Gaussian regularization. Using renormalization techniques, it recovers known effective regularizations in the low-temperature limit and characterizes symmetry-induced simplicity bias at positive temperature.

entry.title: Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs

author.name: Prapti Roy, Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin

entry.summary: This paper probes whether large language models genuinely reason over brain connectivity graphs or merely exploit surface-level cues, using a controlled ADHD diagnosis task on resting-state fMRI data. By isolating one factor at a time across six models, the study reveals that LLM predictions are often driven by learned priors triggered by superficial features rather than true structural reasoning. This matters for anyone applying LLMs to graph-structured scientific data, as it exposes a validity risk in emerging LLM-plus-graph workflows.

entry.title: Do DeepONet Trunk-Basis Preconditioners Need Training?

author.name: Jaemin Oh, Jerome Darbon, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: The paper questions whether DeepONet trunk-basis preconditioners for two-level Schwarz methods actually require training, noting spectral bias is a training property while a randomly initialized trunk with smooth activations is already smooth. In one dimension the authors prove that, under nondegeneracy assumptions, the span of untrained trunk functions is close to the space of low-degree polynomials, with numerical corroboration. The result reframes why these preconditioners work, from Karniadakis and collaborators.

entry.title: Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures

author.name: Zayd Muhammad Kawakibi Zuhri, Munachiso Samuel Nwadike, Kentaro Inui, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: Introduces Tasklets, a benchmark of small synthetic tasks (recall, sequence manipulation, state tracking) for evaluating the computational capabilities of sequence-mixing layers in language model architectures. It standardizes task selection, formulation, and evaluation across studies, enabling controlled comparisons of architectural layer types with small models.

entry.title: LongCat Recall Sparse Attention: Co-Designing Key Organization and Retrieval for Long-Context Inference

author.name: Hao Zhang, Bin Xiao, Kefeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LongCat Recall Sparse Attention, which addresses retrieval bottlenecks in retrieval-based sparse attention by combining fine-grained representatives with paged retrieval in an incrementally maintained index. Time-bucketed, independently indexable storage with capacity-balanced structures avoids regrouping history as new keys arrive.

entry.title: Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR

author.name: Surapon Nonesung, Natapong Nitarach, Sittipong Sripaisarnmongkol, Kunat Pipatanakul, Warit Sirichotedumrong

entry.summary: Typhoon OCR 2 extends the earlier Thai-focused OCR model to multilingual, multi-task operation, supporting prompt-driven information extraction and structured full-page parsing for Thai, English, and Chinese. The authors release compact 2B and 0.8B models fine-tuned on curated data and refined with GRPO, achieving the best Thai MDPBench score among evaluated open models (80.7 versus 68.9 for the predecessor).

entry.title: S2D-Splat: Static-First Gaussian Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes with Layer-Wise Feature Guidance

author.name: Jinheng Li, Tianchen Deng, Bufan Zhang, Qu Chen, Jianwu Fang

entry.summary: S2D-Splat is a feed-forward Gaussian-splatting framework for driving scenes that separates static and dynamic features before estimating cameras and geometry, so the static branch is less corrupted by moving objects. Layer-wise feature guidance further supports recovery of static 3D Gaussians and camera parameters.

entry.title: Mem-X: A Memory-Dependent Cross-Episode Benchmark for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Zhikang Shi, Yuk Tung Samuel Fang, Hongyu Ding, Zixuan Chen, Yujin Wang, Junhui Guo, You Wu, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces Mem-X, a benchmark for evaluating whether vision-and-language navigation agents genuinely use long-term memory across episodes rather than relying on current exploration. It organizes episodes into sessions where later instructions reference objects and routes from earlier episodes, with three difficulty levels covering historical-object recall, in-memory localization, and off-memory relocalization.

entry.title: AppCon-Bench: Perception and Misperception of Material Appearance in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Santiago Jimenez-Navarro, Ana Serrano, Belen Masia

entry.summary: Introduces AppCon-Bench, a benchmark of five tasks assessing material appearance constancy in vision-language models under controlled variations in geometry and illumination, mirroring a human perceptual ability. Evaluations reveal how VLMs misperceive intrinsic surface material properties when confounding factors change.

entry.title: VeilGS: Solving Darkness as a Veil of 2D Basis Maps over Retinex 3DGS

author.name: Mohab Kishawy, Chengzhou Tang, Shahram Shirani, Jun Chen

entry.summary: VeilGS is a 3D Gaussian Splatting method for low-light novel view synthesis that models degradation as a spatially varying veil over a clear scene, giving each Gaussian an albedo and shading latent instead of spherical harmonics. This separates surface color from non-uniform illumination and tone-curve compression better than global per-view curves.

entry.title: ESSI: Computationally Efficient Semantic Search for Sparse Autoencoder Concepts

author.name: James Baker

entry.summary: ESSI accelerates the concept-to-feature search needed for steering diffusion models with sparse autoencoders, replacing costly grid searches and repeated UNet passes with segmentation-mask labeling and binary search over feature subsets. A linear classifier identifies the minimal feature set and is reused to calibrate steering strength, evaluated on SDXL.

entry.title: Inject, Encode, Navigate: Feature-Wise Time Injection for Rectified Flow with Bidirectional Feature Encoding

author.name: Xiaogang Wang, Debasish Mishra, Jia Hao Toh, Wangsheng Liu, Yash Shah

entry.summary: The paper improves vision-based robotic navigation by using a rectified flow policy that reduces inference to a single step with comparable or better performance than diffusion policies, plus a bidirectional Mamba-based visual encoder for temporal dependencies. It also identifies and fixes a failure mode when naively combining the flow framework with feature encoding.

entry.title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models

author.name: Fabio Guglietta, Tianyi Li, Francesco Viola, Luca Biferale

entry.summary: Using a controlled digital twin of a healthy human left heart, the paper shows that generative diffusion models can both unconditionally reproduce cycle-varying cardiac flow statistics and conditionally reconstruct missing or noisy flow fields from incomplete cardiovascular imaging measurements. This addresses the inherent ambiguity of flow reconstruction by sampling plausible fields.

entry.title: GeoSDF-Diff: Geometry-Aware Diffusion Planning for Collision-Free Trajectories

author.name: Yueming Li, Zhanjiang Yang, Yang Shen, Meng Li, Lijun Sun

entry.summary: GeoSDF-Diff incorporates multi-scale signed distance function conditioning into diffusion-based trajectory denoising, giving the denoiser both route-level geometric context and fine local clearance evidence to satisfy feasibility in unseen cluttered environments. It targets the known weakness of diffusion planners in respecting geometric constraints. The conditioning design directly addresses a recognized limitation.

entry.title: AnyBodyCodec: A Shared Native Interface for Body-Model Conversion, Extension, and Humanoid Control

author.name: Qianxing Li

entry.summary: AnyBodyCodec learns a shared latent representation that converts pose and shape controls between incompatible parametric body models such as SMPL-X, MHR, and SOMA, enabling humanoid policies trained on one format to work with others. The small converter (~1-3M parameters) covers nine conversion routes with millimeter-level accuracy and fast inference. This addresses a real interoperability pain point in humanoid robotics research.

entry.title: OpenAI proposes "common limits" for training, but...

author.name: Davidmanheim

entry.summary: This post summarizes and comments on a proposal attributed to Jakub Pachocki for frontier developers to adopt common training limits based on log-perplexity thresholds, with shared norms for evaluating and red-teaming models expected to be transformative in the roughly 0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window. The author voices skepticism, signaled by the trailing ellipsis in the title, and engages with the measurement and enforceability questions.

entry.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Story: When LLMs Narrate Financial Changes Beyond Their Inputs

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Junhyeok Kang, Jaehoon Lee, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: Identifies unsupported framing in LLM-drafted financial reports: factually correct numbers embellished with judgments and causal claims absent from input data, occurring far more often than in professional writing, and worsened by naive prompting fixes. Proposes FrameCheck, a plug-in that filters unsupported framing before output. A targeted, practical contribution to factual generation fidelity in finance.

entry.title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility

author.name: Md Abu Sayed, Asif Rahman, Ahmed Ryen, Ahmed Hemida, Charles Kamhoua, Christopher Kiekintveld

entry.summary: This work tests whether LoRA fine-tuned LLMs can act as solver-free surrogates for online equilibrium computation in honeypot allocation games where network mobility continuously reshapes the attack graph. It uses a dataset of 270 solver-grounded security games and evaluates open-weight models zero-shot versus fine-tuned across 1,524 held-out mobility events.

entry.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes

author.name: Shengze Huang, Yanyu Mao, Xiaofei Yu, Baoshen Guo, Xiaorui Wang, Zhiwen Wu, Sheng Wu, Fukang Wen, Chengxu Wu, Linhao Li, Kailai Sun, Baotong Mi

entry.summary: HookEvo uses an agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to iteratively evolve task-specific harnesses, with a separate improver diagnosing failures from execution traces and proposing candidates that jointly edit executable plugin handlers and shared state, evaluated against the current harness on matched tasks. It is instantiated on a DeepSeek-based harness with a frozen Qwen3 model.

entry.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries

author.name: Yifeng Xie, Chenke Li, Yangshuo Miao, Jingyuan Zheng, Mingxuan Liu, Feiwei Qin, YaQi Wang, Huiyu Zhou, Yifei Chen

entry.summary: MetaRigor is an LLM workflow framework for verifiable end-to-end evidence synthesis in meta-analysis, organizing results as Study x Target units with Task Contracts, programmatic rules, and source binding. Semantic interpretation is left to the model while formalizable computation, validation, and source verification are executed by programs, evaluated across five stages.

entry.title: INCISE: Training-Free In-Context Segmentation of Surgical Videos

author.name: Yifan Xu, Bofang Zheng, Guangyu Meng, Nishchal Sapkota, Xianshi Ma, Xu Cao, Tianjiao Yu, Danny Z Chen

entry.summary: INCISE is a training-free in-context segmentation framework for surgical videos that selects unlabeled reference frames from multiple views instead of random selection, avoiding costly expert-label fine-tuning while capturing transient instruments and small structures. It uses a few annotated references as the sole surgical knowledge source for a frozen model.

entry.title: Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework

author.name: Zijia Cao, Hanqing Dou

entry.summary: Studies how unsupported claims mutate as they pass through homogeneous and heterogeneous multi-agent LLM pipelines, and whether a provenance-aware framework that attaches support status, source, evidence, and transmission history to each claim limits semantic drift and unsupported detail accretion. Metrics quantify claim meaning change and provenance preservation across transmission.

entry.title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer

author.name: Allan Kazakov, Abdurrahman Javat, Duygu Cakir

entry.summary: The study compares five parameter-efficient adaptation families (LoRA, HiRA, KRAdapter, QuanTA, full fine-tuning) for adapting SAM-3 promptable segmentation to medical imaging, remote sensing, and dense material segmentation. It finds compact adapters often match full fine-tuning on DSC and IoU, and that performance cannot be explained by adapter rank or parameter count alone, pointing to update geometry.

entry.title: Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dennis Gross, J{\o}rn Eirik Betten, Helge Spieker

entry.summary: The paper proposes DisQ, a test-case selection method for finding failure-revealing states in value-based cooperative multi-agent RL, exploiting the Q-value gap — the difference between agents' estimates of achievable reward — as an explainable signal of coordination failure. It extends safety testing methodology, previously focused on single-agent RL, to CMARL settings.

entry.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Jee Eun Kim, Donghyeon Choi, Sangjune An, Hae Beom Lee, Kyong Hwan Jin

entry.summary: RoHa-SGG extends agentic harness optimization to scene graph generation by optimizing inference-time code around a frozen model instead of retraining. Two LLM agents collaborate: a root-cause analysis agent diagnoses where and why the model fails, and a proposer agent searches for harness modifications addressing those causes. The approach targets failure localization beyond standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet metrics.

entry.title: Redesigning Neural Networks to Not be Confidently Wrong even to Strong Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Michael W. Spratling, Heiko H. Sch\"utt

entry.summary: The authors revive the classic alternating simple/complex cell neural hierarchy using novel components that learn more selective and tolerant representations, yielding shallow networks with robust and accurate image classification. The architecture also shows improved alignment with human perception.

entry.title: ORION: Exact Canonical-State Supervision for Systematic Generalization in Transformers

author.name: Sibi Gokul, Jyoti Prakash Meher

entry.summary: ORION supervises exact canonical execution states via auxiliary heads to anchor transformer latent trajectories during algorithmic reasoning, addressing structural state drift. A pre-registered factorial experiment shows RoPE and ORION address orthogonal failure axes: RoPE recovers length extrapolation (59.8%) while ORION recovers depth extrapolation (66.7%), with additive gains when combined.

entry.title: Cannot Wait to Verify: Parallel Drafting to Eliminate Verifier Idle Time in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Divya Jyoti Bajpai, Arun Verma, Manjesh Kumar Hanawal

entry.summary: The paper proposes a plug-and-play drafting method for speculative decoding that parallelizes draft generation across transformer layers from a shared hidden state, accepting layer-wise draft states when hidden-state divergence is small and applying corrections otherwise. This keeps the verifier busy and improves GPU utilization for autoregressive inference.

entry.title: Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network

author.name: Marta Niedostatek, Ferran Hernandez Caralt, Runyue Wang, Federica Baccini, Lorenzo Giambagli, Pietro Li\'o, Ginestra Bianconi

entry.summary: The CCNN introduces cup and cap products into topological deep learning, enabling features to be lifted and lowered across more than one simplex dimension per layer, overcoming limitations of boundary-operator and Hodge-Laplacian approaches. The architecture learns node-level variables while accounting for many-body interactions such as triangles, with validation across multiple tasks.

entry.title: How Language Models Compress and Compare: Understanding Selection with Token Covariance Maps

author.name: Moshe Eliasof

entry.summary: The paper introduces token covariance maps, a prompt-level geometric view tracking how token positions co-vary in hidden-state space across layers, revealing a robust compress-then-compare organization in decoder-only transformers. Across 14 models from 4 families and 12 structured-selection benchmarks, early layers represent prompts diffusely, middle layers compress them into a shared structure, and later layers compare candidates.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Landslide Runout Reconstruction from Sparse Observations with LAPIS-SHRED

author.name: Xingyue Zhang, Yuxuan Bao, Jeffrey Keck, Erkan Istanbulluoglu, J. Nathan Kutz

entry.summary: The paper applies LAPIS-SHRED, a shallow recurrent decoder framework trained on physics-based simulation ensembles, to reconstruct landslide runout evolution near Mount St. Helens from very sparse data. It supports both backward reconstruction from a single frame and forward prediction from a short initial window, recovering full trajectories from as few as 32 sensor observations at one timepoint. This demonstrates how hybrid physics-ML models can bridge the gap between sparse geophysical observations and full spatiotemporal dynamics.

entry.title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking

author.name: Mikhail Trapeznikov, Sofia Gulevskaia, Maksim Utushkin, Aleksandr Poslavsky, Alexander D'yakonov

entry.summary: DCDN augments a DCNv2-style cross layer with a division branch, enabling industrial recommender ranking models to jointly learn product, ratio, and mixed product-ratio feature interactions, which cross layers limited to non-negative integer powers cannot represent without manual feature engineering. The paper characterizes representable interactions as multivariate Laurent polynomials. Deployed by an industrial team (Avito-linked authors), it addresses a concrete expressivity gap in production ranking systems.

entry.title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation

author.name: Akshata A Bhat, Sharath Naganna, Saiful Haq, Prashant Khatri, Krishna Chaitanya Reddy Tamataam, Neha Arun, Niyati Chhaya, Pushpak Bhattacharyya

entry.summary: SAVIOR is a sample-efficient data curation methodology for adapting vision-language models to high-impact financial OCR failure scenarios such as rotated text, logo-embedded vendor names, fine print, degraded scans, and multi-column layouts. It also proposes PaIRS, a structure-aware evaluation scheme. The work targets real-world operational failures underrepresented in public datasets.

entry.title: What Stays in the Picture? From Redundant Instructions to Dependency-Aware Image Editing

author.name: Zi-Jun Wang, Yu Lin, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces complex redundant-instruction image editing, where a single request specifies multiple objects, attributes, and spatial relations while revising or canceling earlier requirements. CRIE-Agent consolidates the revision history into an object-level final intent, executes retained objects in dependency-aware reference-first blocks, and verifies results so obsolete requests do not become visual edits.

entry.title: Solar-Conditioned Flow Matching for Multitemporal Aerial Visible-to-Infrared Image Translation

author.name: Wenwen Fang, Bingwei Hui, Xin Chen, Zhongzhen Sun, Zhenfeng Shao

entry.summary: Proposes Solar-Flow, a solar-conditioned latent flow matching model that translates aerial visible images to infrared across the diurnal cycle by conditioning on solar elevation, a thermal phase clock, and flight altitude. This converts V2IR translation from a static mapping into a multitemporal generative task.

entry.title: HumanoidPose: Monocular 3D Pose Estimation for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Jinlin Gan, Mingzhe Li, Junsheng Zhang, Zhibo Zhou, Jiahan Geng, Yuhua Luo, Changwang Zhang, Chenglu Wen, Lan Xu, Siqi Shen, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: HumanoidPose tackles monocular 3D whole-body pose estimation for humanoid robots, a problem sitting between robot pose estimation and human pose estimation that neither paradigm fully addresses. The paper identifies the gap in humanoid-native 3D recovery and contributes methods and presumably data to fill it, motivated by humanoids entering real environments.

entry.title: Re-JEPA: Coupling Representation Prediction and Signal Reconstruction for State-Conditioned EMG Tracking

author.name: Yijian Yang, Tao Chen, Xiaodong Yang, Zongheng Guo, Heng Liu, Lun Shu, Chen Luo, Junhao Tu, Lei Shu, Mingzhou Wu, Yifan Liu, Zhuanghui Zhang, Zhenqiang Liu, Shilei Wen

entry.summary: Re-JEPA is a tracking framework for continuous hand tracking from surface EMG that couples JEPA-style latent representation prediction with signal reconstruction and state-conditioned motion decoding, pretrained without kinematic labels. It targets generalization across users and motion types while remaining sensitive to subtle movements. Applying JEPA principles to biosignal decoding is a fresh cross-domain transfer.

entry.title: Instant-LIVO: Efficient LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry with Compact Geometry and a Bounded Single-Reference-Frame Map

author.name: Xinrui Wang, Ziwei Lan, Wenbin He, Mingjing Yang, Yihan Zhang, Yilin Liu, Peiji Chen, Wenxin Li, Shuyi Jiang, Yubin Lan, Weiguang Yang

entry.summary: Instant-LIVO is a tightly coupled, real-time LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry system designed for resource-constrained platforms. It introduces a spatial-hashed compact geometric map with cache-assisted KNN searches and a bounded single-reference-frame visual map with Schmidt-type uncertainty-aware photometric fusion. The systems contribution targets practical deployment of multi-sensor odometry on embedded hardware.

entry.title: Portable Active Recovery under Timed and Position-Dependent Visual Outages

author.name: Jinyuan Zhang, Shengshuo Jiao

entry.summary: For stereo visual-inertial quadrotors, the paper shows that timed blackouts and position-dependent dark zones look identical at onset yet demand opposite recovery behaviors, and formulates visual-outage recovery as a worst-condition active-observability problem. A portable recovery module at the reference interface of an unchanged host controller handles both cases with zero retraining.

entry.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance

author.name: Hwee Young Kang, Irwin De Tao Chin, Wen-Haw Chong, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: AMARIS is a covariance-driven, training-free model merging framework that transfers specialist fine-tuning updates only along selected activation directions, formulated as budgeted subspace inheritance. It builds a low-rank projection gate from ranked generalized eigendirections to control task-specific interference when combining generalist and specialist LLMs.

entry.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification

author.name: Chrisantus Eze

entry.summary: The paper identifies structural self-critique bias when debating LLM agents share the same base model and proposes a framework with asymmetric Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator roles with opposing epistemic directives, lowering role-embedding similarity. It also introduces convergence-based stopping instead of fixed iteration counts to avoid premature halting or wasted compute.

entry.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation

author.name: Jiangfan Zhang, Wentao Bao, Xian Wu, Xiangjun Fan, Jianpeng Cheng, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: DepThink introduces K learnable residual tokens whose hidden states are linked across depth within a single prefill pass, combining the sequential refinement of looped language models with the single-pass efficiency of register-token architectures. It targets multimodal retrieval and generation, addressing both latency of iterative backbones and redundancy of parallel special tokens.

entry.title: JevRisk: Zero-Shot Financial Risk Assessment with a Language Decision Model

author.name: Yaodong Yang, Li Huang, Junpeng Liang, Yi Ma, Hongyao Tang, Xingyu Fan, Jinpeng Li, Furui Liu

entry.summary: Presents JevRisk, a zero-shot language-based decision system for financial risk monitoring (money laundering, credit default) that interprets activity in customer context without relying on expert-designed threshold indicators or expensive labeled data. It aims to generalize across customers and risk types where supervised models are slow and costly to deploy.

entry.title: Separating Automation Gains from Agent Contributions in AI-Assisted Model Validation

author.name: M. Ahmadi Achachlouei

entry.summary: The paper proposes a staged architecture for bank model validation in which an LLM-free controlled workflow serves as both fallback and control arm, plus an attribution protocol that credits an LLM agent only for faults the deterministic workflow does not already catch. It accounts for decoy false alarms, unnecessary actions, and cost break-even gates to isolate genuine agent value from generic automation gains.

entry.title: NavTTT: Adaptive Parametric Memory via Hierarchical Test-Time Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Xiaoyu Luo, Chengxing Lin, Jiaxin Huang, Jiale Liu, Jingyu Guo, Sirui Chen, Aolin Li, Shaoli Huang, Cheng-zhong Xu, Hui Kong

entry.summary: NavTTT applies fast-weight test-time training to vision-and-language navigation, introducing navigation-conditioned adaptive memory formation that distinguishes informative observations from repetitive visual content within a hierarchical structure. This lets agents accumulate long-term history in an evolving parameter state despite transformer context limits.

entry.title: EAGLE: Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding

author.name: Zhongjian Zou, Quan Qian

entry.summary: EAGLE is a plug-in framework for multimodal LLMs that improves fine-grained understanding of high-resolution images by screening visually-grounded attention heads, performing entity-aware region extraction, and organizing hierarchical visual evidence with question-guided routing. It addresses the common disconnect between localized image details and broader scene context.

entry.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild

author.name: Bingyu Li, Lichang Yang, Zhiyuan Zhao, Junyu Gao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: The authors capture roughly 40 hours of real-world 8K panoramic UAV video to build PanoUAV-Track, a benchmark of 1,895 sequences and over 500,000 frames for full-spherical visual tracking from moving UAVs, including geometric challenges from equirectangular projection across azimuth and elevation. The dataset combines real captures with simulated sequences.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Continuous-Time Depth Learning and Ego-Motion Estimation from Asynchronous Events

author.name: Sadiq O. Macaulay, Dipon Kumar Ghosh, Hadfield Simon

entry.summary: The paper proposes self-supervised per-event depth and camera-motion estimation from asynchronous event-camera streams, avoiding frame condensation that discards the microsecond timing advantages of event sensing. Supervision arises geometrically: events lifted into 3D and displaced by predicted motion should coincide with events from the same edge, so misalignment exposes depth or motion errors via differentiable rendering. This preserves continuous-time fidelity throughout learning.

entry.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement

author.name: Huaze Tang, Runqing Miao, Tianren Peng, Lam Nguyen, Chao Wang, Jairong Li, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: The paper proposes canonical dependence analysis to build action-centered canonical dependence matrices whose SVD yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features, reward-independent representations capturing the predictive contribution of actions beyond states. These features enable zero-shot policy improvement across tasks in reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Accelerating Muon with Spectral Residual Correction

author.name: Zhixin Ren, Yao Lyu, Shengbo Eben Li, Liping Zhang

entry.summary: AIMuon refines Muon optimizer parameter steps using a gradient-momentum residual with its own matrix-sign transformation, derived from an ADMM-inspired momentum framework, while preserving Muon's momentum recursion. Spectral-nuclear duality determines relative weighting of momentum and residual directions, with both approximated via Newton-Schulz iterations.

entry.title: A preference for local interaction between layers emerges during training

author.name: Jiheon Lee

entry.summary: Through layer-pushforward interventions on network copies at many training stages, the paper shows that early in training layers respond weakly and non-locally to perturbations, but as training proceeds neighboring layers come to influence each other more strongly than distant ones. This locality emerges spontaneously despite training a single shared loss that couples all layers.

entry.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning II: Agnostic Proper Learning of Lipschitz Functions

author.name: Jane Lange, Cassandra Marcussen, Arsen Vasilyan

entry.summary: The paper gives a proper learner for Lipschitz functions over the Gaussian distribution, returning a globally Lipschitz hypothesis with loss at most epsilon and complexity (d+1)^(poly(lambda/epsilon)), extendable to the agnostic setting given a bound on label-marginal variance. It shows some scale control on labels is information-theoretically necessary.

entry.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes

author.name: Liang-Yu Zou

entry.summary: This paper constructs a deterministic agnostic PAC learner for partial concept classes that achieves the optimal sample complexity of O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon^2), matching the lower bound of Alon et al. (FOCS 2021). It resolves an open problem in the learning theory of partial labels, where examples may be labeled with the uncertainty marker star.

entry.title: FedQCal: Quadratic Programming with Dual-Space Calibration for One-Shot Federated Learning

author.name: Shunsei Koshibuchi, Hiroshi Kera, Kazuhiko Kawamoto

entry.summary: FedQCal addresses one-shot federated learning by using a reference model trained on a small labeled server set to define alignment requirements, then solving a minimum-norm quadratic program to merge heterogeneous client models after a single upload. Two dual variables of the QP select the merge via classification loss, so alignment thresholds are learned rather than prescribed, with proven exactness guarantees. This offers a principled solution to class-distribution heterogeneity in single-round aggregation.

entry.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models

author.name: Gert Aarts, Diaa E. Habibi, Andreas Ipp, David I. M\"uller, Thomas R. Ranner, Lingxiao Wang, Wei Wang, Qianteng Zhu

entry.summary: Presents gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories, combining lattice gauge-equivariant CNNs with a Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm. The models accurately sample 2D U(2) configurations, show promising results on 4D SU(3), and extrapolate well to larger inverse couplings, validated against analytic and hybrid Monte Carlo results.

entry.title: Isolating the Language Shell: A Content-Controlled Study of Multilingual Reasoning

author.name: Hoejoon Kwon, Jinhee Jang, Byeonggeuk Lim, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: Constructs content-controlled distillation supervision by rendering identical verified English reasoning trajectories into English, translated, and language-mixed shells, then fine-tunes students in three target languages. Shell choice alone changes downstream multilingual reasoning accuracy, with effects varying by student, language, and difficulty.

entry.title: Cross-Platform Production Signatures of State-Linked Information Operations

author.name: Lin Tian, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: Proposes identifying state-linked information operations across platforms via production signatures, regularities in posting, replying, and reposting timing, using no content, metadata, or network ties. Models trained on Twitter archives of four operations transfer to Internet Research Agency accounts on Reddit without Reddit training data.

entry.title: ConRef: Auditing Reference Reliability in 2D/3D Registration Benchmarks

author.name: Jianfeng Yue, Feng Li, Tianyu Song, Julius Watrinet, Ulrich Eck, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: ConRef is a multi-view framework for auditing reference poses in X-ray/CT registration benchmarks used in image-guided orthopedic surgery. By jointly exploiting multiple X-ray observations, it estimates additive reference errors, addressing the problem that reported performance may be capped by benchmark label uncertainty rather than algorithmic error. This matters as registration errors approach the uncertainty of the reference poses themselves.

entry.title: Towards Text-Mask Consistency in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Jie Gui, Hang Tu, Wen Sha, Xiuquan Du

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why vision-language medical segmentation masks conflict with their text descriptions, attributing failures to templated clinical language causing false negatives in contrastive learning and to one-way vision-dominant cross-attention. The proposed C2Seg uses cluster-aware contrastive pretraining and a consistency-enhanced two-stage design to strengthen text-mask alignment, particularly for multi-site and multi-lesion cases.

entry.title: Prune to Expand: Training Prompt Enhancers with Less to Imitate

author.name: Tianhe Wu, Qilin Sun, Kede Ma

entry.summary: Finds counterintuitively that prompt-enhancement models trained on caption pairs with substantial generation gains perform no better than those trained on marginal-gain pairs, arguing dense captions impose redundant supervision unrelated to user intent. The paper proposes pruning-based supervision to train better prompt enhancers with less data to imitate.

entry.title: BladeR: Scalable, Shape-Guided 3D Reconstruction of Wind Turbine Blades from UAV Imagery

author.name: Jonathan Sterckx, Michiel Vlaminck, Hiep Luong

entry.summary: Presents BladeR, a pipeline for high-quality 3D reconstruction of wind turbine blades from drone inspection imagery, using hierarchical sparse reconstruction guided by GPS/IMU data and blade shape priors. Dense reconstruction uses a tiled Gaussian Splatting framework handling 45 MP images at native resolution, isolating the blade and enabling wear localization and damage detection.

entry.title: GeoScaffold: From Latent to Realized Geometry in Collaborative Detection

author.name: Kang Yang, Yance Fang, Gaochen Cui, Xiaoqiang Jin, Deying Li, Yongcai Wang

entry.summary: Quantifies a gap in collaborative 3D detection: although fusion improves localization for about two-thirds of positive anchors, NMS keeps the better-localized box less than half the time on UrbanIng-V2X. GeoScaffold exploits latent geometric cues in fused BEV features to improve the readout pipeline beyond standard anchor scoring and NMS.

entry.title: MambaSplit: Severity-Robust and Inference-Efficient Semantic Unmixing of Fluorescence Microscopy Image Data

author.name: Aman Kukde (Fondazione Human Technopole, Milan, Italy), Ruggiero Santeramo (Fondazione Human Technopole, Milan, Italy), Federico Carrara (Fondazione Human Technopole, Milan, Italy), Ashesh Ashesh (Fondazione Human Technopole, Milan, Italy, IIT Hyderabad, Hyderabad, India), Igor Zubarev (Fondazione Human Technopole, Milan, Italy), Florian Jug (Fondazione Human Technopole, Milan, Italy)

entry.summary: MambaSplit uses a state-space (Mamba) architecture to computationally separate superimposed fluorescence microscopy channels, handling unknown and uneven mixing severities while capturing both local and long-range context efficiently. It improves on patch-based or auxiliary-context approaches for semantic unmixing in microscopy.

entry.title: Geo-Force: A Theory of Force Sensing from Object Geometry

author.name: Abdullah Ayad

entry.summary: Geo-Force formalizes virtual touch sensors that predict tactile signals from object geometry measured by depth cameras, defining the Geometric Force computed via surface rendering, learned touch maps, and analysis of when outputs are trustworthy. This offers a formal foundation for replacing fragile tactile electronics with geometry-based prediction.

entry.title: Opto-Electronic Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Based on MZI for Robotic Manipulator Control

author.name: Mengting Yu, Shuiying Xiang, Changjian Xie, Yonghang Chen, Haowen Zhao, Xingxing Guo, Zhijian Hao, Yahui Zhang, Yanan Han, Yue Hao

entry.summary: This work implements reinforcement learning control for robotic manipulators on an opto-electronic hybrid architecture using Mach-Zehnder interferometers, targeting the latency and energy bottlenecks of electronic computing for edge-deployed embodied intelligence. The photonic hardware accelerates RL inference for point-to-point reaching and grasping. It is an interesting intersection of photonic computing and robot control.

entry.title: Where Delay Compensation Belongs in a Decentralized Mean-Field-Game Swarm with a Control-Barrier Safety Filter

author.name: Jan Miko{\l}ajczyk, Igor Rostkowski, Bartosz Og\'orkiewicz, Szymon Skierski, Sylwia Opat, Wojciech Rybak, Miko{\l}aj Sczogiel, Rados{\l}aw Pa{\l}ys, Jan Gogulski, Bartosz Ko\'scio{\l}ek, Andrzej Pijanowski, Szymon Kowalski, Marcin Misiewicz

entry.summary: This study analyzes a decentralized drone-swarm stack combining mean-field-game routing with per-agent control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters under TDMA communication delays that grow with swarm size. A key finding is that estimation delay breaks only the safety layer, causing collisions beyond frame periods of roughly 125-175 ms for swarms of 75-100 agents. The paper identifies precisely where delay compensation must be placed in such architectures.

entry.title: Efficient inference for fairness-constrained sequential decision policies

author.name: Yi-Hui Zhou

entry.summary: The paper studies fairness-constrained optimal sequential decision-making in domains like education and health, where policies must not leave protected groups behind. Under sequential ignorability with multi-stage non-Markov data, it proves the constrained optimal value is pathwise differentiable with an efficient influence function given by a Lagrangian combination of group-value influence functions, enabling efficient estimation and inference.

entry.title: VerifiQuant: Governance-by-Execution for Financial LLM Workflows

author.name: Yu-Chi Ko, Mi-Yen Yeh, Shou-De Lin

entry.summary: VerifiQuant frames the key deployment risk of financial LLMs as emitting confidently wrong numbers, and proposes governance-by-execution: inference contracts package financial logic, and an executable diagnostic funnel decides whether to compute, clarify, or refuse before deterministic arithmetic happens outside the LLM. The separation makes computation and refusal structured and auditable.

entry.title: Privacy Protection in Self-Evolving Personal Agents: Persistent Memory and Cross-Carrier Transfer

author.name: Zibin Lin, Taotao Wang, Shengli Zhang

entry.summary: A thematic survey of privacy in personal agents with persistent memory, organizing findings around memory admission, maintenance, release, and withdrawal across protected change, observer, and validation settings, with worked scenarios tracing a private fact through booking, learning, and withdrawal. It highlights that reader non-use does not establish cleanup of learned state and measures utility costs of broad deletion.

entry.title: ADEPT: Adaptive Monocular Depth Estimation via Model-In-The-Loop Photometric Tuning with Capture Risk Prediction

author.name: GiHyun Kim, JinMo Yang, Hyung-Sin Kim

entry.summary: ADEPT adapts camera exposure and gain for monocular depth estimation using learned feedback from a frozen depth model, training a compact predictor to score candidate capture settings relative to a ground-truth-identified reference without needing ground truth at deployment. This balances light collection against motion blur during robot motion.

entry.title: PRISM: Validation-Free Online Batch Selection for LLM Fine-Tuning via Preconditioned Conic Ghost Matching

author.name: Lin Tang, Wei Zhang, Jing Li, Hongyu Chen, Ming Zhao, Yuxuan Wang

entry.summary: PRISM is a validation-free online batch selector for LLM fine-tuning that aligns candidate gradients in a factored second-moment metric and casts subset construction as conic facility location, avoiding distorted similarities from heavy-tailed gradient norms. It removes the need for held-out validation or proxy sets during data selection.

entry.title: Semiparametric Efficiency for Entropic Optimal Transport under Structured Distribution Shift

author.name: Yiming Ma, Weiwei Zhuang, Hang Liu

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes when structural information improves estimation of entropic optimal transport under a fixed-dimensional exponential density ratio model with a nonparametric baseline. It derives an exact projection identity quantifying the variance gain from the structural restriction, shows the pooled empirical-likelihood estimator attains the restricted bound, and characterizes when the gain can be zero even under correct specification. It also handles first-order bias under local misspecification.

entry.title: FACET: A Data-Efficient Regional Parametric Head Model

author.name: Mathieu Lamarre, Elly Akhoundi, Thibault Goyallon, Patrick Anderson, \'Etienne Danvoye

entry.summary: FACET is a parametric head model designed for production face pipelines that maximizes expressiveness from a small fixed pool of registered identities through architectural locality. Its regional identity decomposition into 16 anatomical regions bypasses the N-1 rank ceiling of global PCA, improving held-out neutral-fit performance. The work isolates each contribution against matched global-PCA ablations on identical topology, training data, and normalization.

entry.title: Crafting the Difference, Grounding the Evidence: Discriminative Concept Learning for Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition

author.name: Siyu Zhu, Feng Ding, Zixiao Jin, Kaizhi Li, Xin Dong, Haisheng Fu, Yuchen Zou, Guohe Zhang, Jie Liang

entry.summary: CRAFT improves zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition by refining LLM-generated descriptions with hard-negative-conditioned generation and contrastive scoring so concepts distinguish confusable actions, plus Unique-QDPP selection to avoid reusing descriptions across semantic slots. The curated concept bank supervises learnable concept tokens that read motion and context cues, improving five baselines across four paradigms on NTU-60 and NTU-120.

entry.title: EvoTER: Evolving Embodied Agents via Tool-Use Experience and Reflection

author.name: Yingting Zhou, Yuyin Zhou, Yongliang Wang, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: EvoTER is a parameter-free framework that lets embodied LLM agents self-evolve tool-use skills through a three-role loop: an Explorer records trajectories, a Diagnoser distills successes and failures into skills for tool selection and parameter computation, and the framework tracks whether local repairs translate into complete-task gains over the shared procedure library. It emphasizes whole-task improvement rather than local fixes alone.

entry.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory

author.name: Bao Pham

entry.summary: A thesis arguing that diffusion models behave as associative memories whose attractor basins around training samples explain the memorization-generalization tension, and that spurious states long viewed as memory failures are the locus of creative generation. It develops a unified retrieval-process account in which memorization and generalization coexist. Offers theoretical framing for open questions in generative model behavior.

entry.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents

author.name: Deepak Waghmare, Shaad Sufi

entry.summary: Proposes the Open Process Control Plane (OPCP), an execution boundary separating agent proposals from business-controlled authorization, context disclosure, and supplier selection, recording uncertain outcomes when suppliers act without acceptable replies. Evaluated extensively with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers across 2,400 fault episodes and 19,000 timed calls, without any language model in the loop. A systems-and-governance contribution for safe tool-using agents.

entry.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks

author.name: Kaicheng Liang, Jingyi Cui, Hongwei Wen, Feng Wang, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: EcomWriteBench provides 3,861 queries spanning 69 e-commerce writing tasks across 13 categories and five languages, with a shared pool of 37 abilities mapped to tasks and ability-wise scoring. It captures user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that general writing benchmarks miss.

entry.title: WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs

author.name: Zhiqiang Yuan, Qiwei Yan, Liwei Yang, Jinzhe Liu, Yang Liu, Zhongyan Hou, Liyan Xu, Peixiang Luo, Jiapei Zhang, Ying Deng, Jie Zhou, Jinchao Zhang

entry.summary: WePM targets on-device multimodal LLMs by formalizing heterogeneous capability density (HCD), a measure of how many task families a model serves per unit of resident memory. It proposes hierarchical conflict reconciliation to handle conflicting updates from separately collected task corpora under fixed token budgets, aiming at unified vision-language-capable edge models.

entry.title: Recoverable Symbols, Unstable Execution: Auditing Internal Pathways and Decision Identity in Visual State Tracking

author.name: Ruiqi Liu, Jinming Li, Mo Wang, Yang Lu, Yanlan Kang

entry.summary: The paper studies a gap in visual state tracking where features retain all needed symbols yet the model's answer changes when irrelevant image parts change. Using donor views, symbol-supervised decoders, and channel swaps, it shows on 3,526 pairs that fully recovered symbol chains still exhibit context-induced decision instability.

entry.title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation

author.name: Samarth Sarin, Lovepreet Singh, Dhagash Mehta

entry.summary: The paper presents a schema-driven methodology for building temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents, using phased LLM extraction of entities, quantitative observations, and relationships with schema validation and multi-stage deduplication. It targets auditable structures beyond chunk-based RAG for financial documents.

entry.title: Model the Annotation, Not the Noise: Semantic Annotation-Channel Prompt Learning against Noisy Labels

author.name: Zibin Geng, Yitong Bao, Jia Li, Xuefeng Jiang, Sheng Sun, Yuwei Wang, Min Liu

entry.summary: SACP reformulates noisy-label prompt learning for vision-language models through a data-generation lens, decoupling latent clean-label prediction from instance-dependent annotation generation. Rather than heuristic noise suppression or hard sample selection, it models the annotation channel to preserve semantic ambiguity, improving parameter-efficient adaptation under label noise.

entry.title: Realistic Robustness Evaluation of Tabular Data Driven Models

author.name: Miguel Silva, Eva Maia, Jo\~ao Vitorino, Isabel Pra\c{c}a

entry.summary: Introduces AURORA, an open-source modular tool for evaluating the robustness of ML classifiers on tabular data against adversarial perturbations, integrating multiple attack methods and evaluation metrics in one framework with a standardized evaluation report. It addresses the underexplored adversarial robustness of tabular models used in high-stakes systems.

entry.title: Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced Hierarchy-Aware Semi-Supervised Graph Classification

author.name: Guangjie Zeng, Hao Peng, Angsheng Li, Li Sun, Chunyang Liu, Yicheng Pan, Shengze Li, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces HypSEE, a framework for semi-supervised graph classification that builds walk-induced and embedding-derived hypergraphs to capture hierarchical, higher-order relationships beyond pairwise edges, using structural entropy to enhance representation learning. It addresses the underexplored problem of hierarchy-aware learning when labels are scarce.

entry.title: LingSante-Pulse: Unified Physiological Pretraining through Random-Feature Prediction and Cross-Modal Alignment

author.name: Linxiao Yang, Wenwei Wang, Tian Zhou, Bingqing Peng, Zihao Zhang, Zuyi Zhu, Jinjie Gu, Liang Sun

entry.summary: LingSante-Pulse is a unified physiological representation framework using a shared signal-conditioned encoder that processes each physical channel independently, supporting variable signal combinations for multimodal assessment and single-sensor inference. It combines pairwise cross-modal alignment, structured random-feature prediction, and masked waveform reconstruction to learn from heterogeneous clinical and wearable signals.

entry.title: PAVE: A Harness for Geometrically Consistent Road Network Modeling with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yajun Liu, Jinxi Wu, Juan Pablo Mill\'an Raya, Xuesong Zhou

entry.summary: PAVE uses vision-language models to extract lane-level road network data (junctions, movements) from satellite and street-level imagery, where OpenStreetMap tags prove correct for only 13 of 44 tested approaches. A harness maintains geometric consistency across views of the same location, addressing VLMs' tendency to lose geometric coherence under direct questioning.

entry.title: PhiJEPA: Denoising Latent Predictions for Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Makoto Yamada, Yao-Hung Hubert Tsai

entry.summary: PhiJEPA adapts PhiNet's two-stage prediction to masked Transformers within a joint-embedding predictive architecture: from sparse, photometrically corrupted context, a Transformer predicts hidden tokens of a corrupted teacher view, and a token-wise MLP maps predictions to clean teacher tokens. Trained on ImageNet-1K with 5.6e19 FLOPs, it reaches 69.3 mIoU on linear PASCAL VOC segmentation, outperforming tested one-stage alternatives in ablations.

entry.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions

author.name: Sulong Yang, Zhi Zeng, Xiupeng Wu, Juewen Hu, Pring Wong, Shuwu Zhang, Shuo Chen

entry.summary: PromptTTSD enables fine-grained, open-ended style control for multi-turn spoken dialogue synthesis using free-text descriptions instead of predefined tags. The authors build a scalable data pipeline extracting conversational speech from multi-narrator audiobooks with a two-stage alignment algorithm preserving dialogue continuity. The system targets speaker consistency and context-appropriate style shifts across turns.

entry.title: Shared Understanding in Human-AI Teams: Coordination Continuity in Evolving Work

author.name: Si\^an Lindley, Britta Burlin, Christian Poelitz, Lev Tankelevitch, Richard Banks

entry.summary: This qualitative HCI paper introduces coordination continuity, the extent to which human-AI collaborators sustain a workable basis for interdependent action as work evolves, noting that shared information access does not imply shared basis for action. Drawing on two team studies and a reflexive case from the authors' own repository-based environment, it proposes a framework of durable representations, relative coordination properties, and interactional elements. It comes from a Microsoft Research-affiliated team.

entry.title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?

author.name: Marcio Andre de Souza Estevam

entry.summary: This paper introduces TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark for coding agents based on Brazilian early-autism (TEA) screening specifications, with 144 parameterized tasks and 6,798 hidden test cases that kill all 1,955 non-equivalent mutants of the reference solution. Results show Gemma 4 12B solves 38 percent of single-instrument tasks and none at the FHIR level, while the 31B model degrades substantially at deeper levels.

entry.title: Multi-Tier Edge Triage: Optimizing Latency for Safe Clinical Agents

author.name: Joshua Broyde, Sarita A. Joshi

entry.summary: This paper presents a safety screening architecture for clinical AI agents that co-locates a compact Tier-1 sequence classifier on the host server to resolve clear queries in-process and escalate uncertain or sensitive cases to cloud LLM judges, enforcing HIPAA, scope-of-practice, and comprehension policies under interactive latency constraints.

entry.title: Action-Conditioned Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Yutong Xia, Yangyou Liu, Yuxuan Liang, Yuankai Wu, See-Kiong Ng, Roger Zimmermann

entry.summary: The paper introduces PairST, a benchmark of six datasets across traffic, power, and water systems with paired futures under intervention versus no intervention, enabling separate evaluation of affected-region accuracy and quiet-region spurious-change error. The accompanying ActionST model forecasts intervened futures while avoiding spurious changes in unaffected regions.

entry.title: Federated and Balanced $k$-means: Communication Efficiency, Privacy, and Heterogeneity

author.name: Feiteng Nie, Shengkun Zhu, Sheng Wang, Yuan Sun, Feiping Nie, Wei Song, Zhiyong Peng
