entry.summary: The authors propose Fabric, a privacy-preserving federated k-means clustering algorithm for vertical federated learning settings, where different parties hold different features of the same entities, such as in cross-organization healthcare or finance collaborations. The method decomposes balanced clustering into independent per-client subproblems solved via ADMM, aiming to simultaneously address information leakage and cluster imbalance that plague existing VFL clustering approaches. This matters because practical federated deployments need guarantees on privacy, communication cost, and cluster quality together, not just one of these axes.

entry.title: Distillation with Errors: Sparse Unbiased Backpropagation for Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Yuxin Li

entry.summary: DWE reduces the cost of full-vocabulary knowledge distillation by exploiting the zero-sum structure of logit gradients to construct sparse paired gradient estimates whose expectation matches the full gradient, with geometry-aware pairing and stratified sampling to control variance. The authors prove unbiasedness and evaluate estimation accuracy and training efficiency.

entry.title: Improved Accuracy Scaling with Problem Complexity in LLM Arithmetic Reasoning Using Executable Symbolic Representations

author.name: Yu-Bin Liu, Shi-Ju Ran

entry.summary: The authors introduce GSM-AB, a controlled benchmark that independently varies operand digit length and operation count to test how LLM arithmetic accuracy degrades with complexity. They find that executable symbolic representations (e.g., Lean code) improve accuracy and slow degradation compared to natural-language reasoning.

entry.title: Mixture of Latent Recursions for Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Weixun Luo, Ye Mao, Ranran Huang, Junpeng Jing, Krystian Mikolajczyk

entry.summary: MoLR enhances LoRA fine-tuning by recursively refining the down-projected latent representation with a shared transformation, using a lightweight threshold-based router to decide per-token whether further refinement is needed. This increases adaptation expressiveness while preserving parameter efficiency, with balanced utilization across recursion depths.

entry.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning

author.name: Hari Sitaula, Joseph Opitz

entry.summary: This study benchmarks linear regression, RNN, and LSTM models for one-day-ahead S&P 500 forecasting under a unified chronological pipeline on 2006-2025 data. Its central contribution is a methodological audit identifying three sources of performance inflation common in the financial deep-learning literature: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, missing naive persistence baselines, and best-of-N reporting.

entry.title: Highly Efficient Vertical Federated Clustering with Triangle-Inequality-based Pruning

author.name: Feiteng Nie, Shengkun Zhu, Zepeng Liu, Sheng Wang, Yuan Sun, Zhiyong Peng

entry.summary: The paper proposes TriCD, an exact triangle-inequality-based pruning method for CDKM clustering that provably preserves cluster assignments while skipping redundant objective evaluations, and builds FedTriCD on top of it for vertical federated settings. This reduces both communication rounds and local computation compared to existing VFL clustering methods. It addresses a practical privacy-preserving analytics problem where parties hold complementary features for the same samples.

entry.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning

author.name: Fernando Mondragon-Sampedro, Diego Alvarez-Estevez

entry.summary: This empirical comparative study examines exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input as system size grows, across Fidelity Quantum Kernels, Projected Quantum Kernels, and Quantum Extreme Learning within a unified variance-based framework. It investigates how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration, finding global fidelity kernels concentrate strongly while local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate the effect. It offers practical guidance for designing QML models that avoid trainability collapse.

entry.title: Beyond Resolution: Inference-Time Parameterized Temporal Consistency in Generative Regional Climate Downscaling

author.name: Luca Glawion, Julius Polz, Harald Kunstmann, Benjamin Fersch, Patrick Ludwig, Antonio S\'anchez-Ben\'itez, Christian Chwala

entry.summary: Addresses a gap in diffusion-based climate downscaling where generated sequences are evaluated per timestep without checking temporal coherence. The authors introduce a method using autoregressive conditioning that exposes the coherence-diversity trade-off as a controllable inference-time parameter, avoiding error accumulation and ensemble-spread collapse.

entry.title: Know Your Context Bank: Repairing Inconsistency and Measuring Generalization in Context-Aware Text-to-SQL

author.name: Hailong Li, Mohammadreza Pourreza, Tal Neiman, Reza Sherkat, Per Jacobsson, Yannis Papakonstantinou

entry.summary: Identifies context bank rot in enterprise text-to-SQL systems, where curated collections of example queries and metric definitions contain mutually inconsistent entries that each pass per-entry review. The paper proposes repair methods and new benchmarks measuring whether systems generalize from context banks or merely reproduce them.

entry.title: How Far Does Lossless Re-tokenization Move an RLVR Update?

author.name: Zhe Dong, Fang Qin

entry.summary: Quantifies how tokenization instability affects RLVR training updates, showing that splitting roughly one token in 25 moves the update 0.556 times as far as replacing the entire batch on Qwen2.5-0.5B digit addition. The ratio depends on the fraction and identity of split tokens, revealing a consistent source of update noise.

entry.title: How Many Bytes Has a BPE Model Seen? Estimating Byte-Token Exposure in Pretraining from Corpus Statistics and Embedding Norms

author.name: Liwei Zhang, ZhiMing Tong, Mochen Guan, Linzhe Li

entry.summary: This paper estimates how much pretraining exposure single-byte fallback tokens receive in byte-level BPE tokenizers, using Qwen3.8 as a case study via two independent estimation routes. It finds single-byte tokens account for 13-36% of tokens (mostly ASCII), while genuine UTF-8 fallback bytes are only 0.15-0.27%, about 2 billion occurrences per trillion pretraining tokens, with fallback rates varying four orders of magnitude across languages. This informs byte-level model conversion and understanding of low-resource language tokenization.

entry.title: SCATR-ITS: a scalable transformer for large-area individual tree segmentation from LiDAR point clouds

author.name: Lassi Ruoppa, Verneri Sepp\"anen, Antero Kukko, Juha Hyypp\"a

entry.summary: SCATR-ITS is a scalable transformer for individual tree segmentation from LiDAR point clouds, designed to make deep learning methods viable for large-area operational forestry workflows. Built on ForestFormer3D, it moves to superpoint-level processing with learned embeddings, adds size-aware postprocessing and dynamic query counts to accelerate inference. The work addresses the computational complexity that has blocked adoption of SOTA deep models at scale.

entry.title: Effectiveness of Synthetic Defects for Anomaly Detection in Industrial Small Load Carriers

author.name: Vincent Wahyudi, Kuniko Paxton, Amila Akagi\'c, Martin Storath, Dhavalkumar Thakker

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates whether synthetic procedural-noise defects (e.g., Perlin noise) actually help industrial anomaly detection in practice, comparing supervised and unsupervised methods on a real-world small load carrier dataset versus benchmarks. Notably, unsupervised methods trained only on synthetic defects reach 0.87-0.90 AUROC while a supervised classifier reaches only 0.65, and benchmark performance does not translate to the real setting.

entry.title: V2VFusion: Text-Controlled Video-to-Video Diffusion for Degradation-Aware Video Fusion

author.name: Jiajun Chen, Han Xu, Yunfei Huang, Zhuoya Zhang, Guangcan Liu, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: V2VFusion reformulates multi-source video fusion as a video-to-video conditional generation problem, using a text-controlled diffusion framework to produce temporally coherent fused video from degraded inputs. It explicitly models degradation dynamics across sequences instead of performing frame-wise fusion with a single overloaded network.

entry.title: EAST: Event-Anchored Surface Transport for Event-Based Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Ke Luo, Wei Zhai, Yuliang Wu, Pengfei Yu, Yang Cao

entry.summary: Presents EAST, which couples an event-constrained signed distance field to Gaussian rendering for event-camera-based 3D reconstruction, using normal flow from event timing to constrain ray-surface intersection depths. This addresses the problem that appearance changes can compensate for depth errors while preserving predicted brightness changes.

entry.title: PGS-PCQA: Perceptually Gated Synthetic Supervision for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment

author.name: Qinyuan Fan, Meng Zhang, Clemens G\"uhmann

entry.summary: Identifies poor distortion coverage as a key cause of cross-dataset generalization failures in no-reference point cloud quality assessment and proposes training with synthetic distortion severity ranking, requiring no subjective scores for synthetic samples. The approach improves robustness on unseen distortion types.

entry.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts

author.name: Jiyoon Pyo, Jacob Arndt, Yao-Yi Chiang, Dalton Lunga

entry.summary: ENC-QA is a diagnostic benchmark with 77,312 questions derived from 6,612 NOAA electronic navigational charts, testing VLMs on nautical feature recognition, spatial reasoning, and navigational knowledge for assessing chart updates. It targets a safety-critical, symbol-and-geometry-heavy document domain largely untested for VLMs.

entry.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval

author.name: Mohammad Alijanpour Shalmani, Alale Rezvani Boroujeni, Ali Amini

entry.summary: DiTraR targets video corpus moment retrieval, finding that most top-ranked errors come from selecting the wrong video rather than imprecise boundaries. It combines a witness-interval scorer that exhaustively probes candidate intervals, an energy-based ensemble of independently trained scorers, and a transcript-guided verifier for video-level re-ranking.

entry.title: A Lightweight Method for Validating Simulated LiDAR Configurations Based on Point Density over Distance

author.name: Benedikt Degenstein, Michael Spengler, Julian St\"ahler, Carsten Markgraf

entry.summary: This paper introduces a platform-agnostic method for assessing LiDAR simulation fidelity by comparing range-dependent point density on annotated objects between real and simulated sensors. It requires only 3D bounding boxes and point clouds, and proposes a bounded Density Similarity Score (DSS) to quantify agreement. This matters because signal-level realism in simulation is a bottleneck for validating autonomous driving and robotics systems.

entry.title: Humanoid robots for safety-critical electrical switching: A perception-informed runtime constraint filter

author.name: Songyang Liu, Yu Hou, Yuqing Hu, Shuai Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a runtime safety filter for VR-teleoperated humanoid electrical switching, combining a scene model from the robot head camera with a target-conditioned CBF quadratic program that keeps the tool away from non-target switches. Real-world experiments on a Unitree G1 show successful target operations across multiple trials at two standing positions. It demonstrates humanoids in a concrete, high-stakes industrial task.

entry.title: Learning under Bounded Manipulation for Quadratic Incentive Design

author.name: Arda G\"u\c{c}l\"u, Subhonmesh Bose, Tamer Ba\c{s}ar

entry.summary: This paper analyzes a repeated quadratic incentive design game where a leader learns a follower's private type from noisy observations while the follower can strategically manipulate those observations under a budget constraint. It establishes a minimax regret rate of order max{log T, min{C_T, T}}, quantifying how bounded strategic manipulation degrades the leader's learning performance.

entry.title: Amendability and "Solving Alignment"

author.name: davidg

entry.summary: The author argues that current alignment research aims mostly at preventing misalignment, which by default yields instruction-following systems that could still produce very bad outcomes. The post surveys alternative properties a not-misaligned superintelligence could have and advocates a specific target property called amendability, urging more people, especially in policy and philosophy, to work on this framing.

entry.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness

author.name: Ji Sub Choi, Whan Choi, Seo Yeon Gu, Suhyun Kim, Inyong Yun

entry.summary: Converts letter-of-credit document requirements into atomic, executable conditions checked by a deterministic verifier that retrieves named evidence, enabling per-requirement evaluation of trade-finance document examination. Uses an on-premises fine-tuned 9B parser trained on synthetic template pairs due to confidentiality. On 345 real LC cases, per-requirement evaluation reveals errors that final-decision accuracy hides.

entry.title: Vega-Fafnir: Is Greedy Decoding the Same Decoding? Where Rounding Noise in Speculative Verification Comes From and What Removing It Costs

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Navin Kumar R

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how finite-precision rounding makes supposedly equivalent greedy decoding paths diverge: verifying 4 guessed tokens per pass changes outputs for 60% of Qwen3-0.6B prompts, with all first divergences occurring at small logit gaps. It decomposes the noise sources and proposes a margin gate that falls back to single-token decoding when gaps are small.

entry.title: Self-verifiable LLM-driven science and why it needs human researchers

author.name: Michael G. Medvedev, Nikolai V. Krivoshchapov, Stepan N. Ostarkov

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that the bottleneck of AI-assisted science is not generation but the human cost of re-deriving and verifying LLM outputs, which arrive in confident tones regardless of correctness. Drawing on the Lean 4/Coq proof-assistant analogy from mathematics, it advocates building self-verifiable LLM-driven scientific workflows and articulates the continuing role of human researchers.

entry.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation

author.name: Bonny Banerjee, Geetha Raju

entry.summary: Proposes CENTRY, a probabilistic latent-variable framework for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating deployed AI system risk from environmental interactions, modeling risk from three intrinsic sources: datasets, hardware, and models/algorithms, with a structured latent representation. It aims to move beyond taxonomies toward implementable operational risk management.

entry.title: GEG-SAM: Gaze Exploration-Guided Segment Anything Model for Weakly Supervised Polyp Segmentation

author.name: Ao Wang, Lei Zhang, Lituan Wang, Zhenwei Zhang, Xiangbao Gong, Zhiyi Zhang, Shunyao Wang, Xianglei Yuan, Zizhou Wang

entry.summary: GEG-SAM uses endoscopist gaze trajectories, modeling the temporal and spatial organization of fixations rather than treating them as isolated prompts, to guide a Segment Anything Model for weakly supervised polyp segmentation. This leverages routinely recorded clinical gaze as free supervision signal.

entry.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks

author.name: Silviu-Florin Gheorghe, Radu-Stefan Popa, Adriana Valentina Costache, Adrian-Gabriel Chifu, Alessia Amelio, Paul Irofti, Anders Skaarup Johansen, Lallouani Bouchakour, Mohamed Lichouri, Khaled Lounnas, Neelu Madan, Yashvir Malik, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: PaMuk-Bench is a parallel multilingual benchmark of over 10K curated English prompts translated into six languages (Arabic, Danish, French, Hindi, Italian, Romanian), with parallel translations, generated and retrieved images supporting multiple vision-language tasks including text-to-image generation. It enables comparative evaluation of VLM performance gaps in low-resource languages against English.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Anticlustering Decomposition for Certifying Pairwise-Constrained Clustering

author.name: Anna Livia Croella, Veronica Piccialli, Antonio M. Sudoso

entry.summary: The paper proposes a decomposition framework for certifying solution quality in large-scale constrained minimum sum-of-squares clustering, partitioning data into anticlusters and solving induced subproblems to obtain certified optimality gaps. It introduces the Constrained Anticlustering Problem, formulated as a mixed-integer second-order cone program, to preserve pairwise must-link and cannot-link information during partitioning. This enables rigorous lower bounds on optimal objective values for a hard combinatorial problem.

entry.title: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Zero-Shot Multilingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models

author.name: Jakub \v{S}m{\'i}d, Pavel Kr{\'a}l

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates zero-shot multilingual target-aspect-sentiment detection across 12 languages and three domains using seven open-weight instruction-tuned LLMs from 8B to 35B parameters, including dense and MoE architectures. It examines how prompting strategies affect compound sentiment triplet extraction in a setting where prior ABSA research focused mostly on English or fine-tuned models. The study maps where open-weight LLMs succeed and fail across language families.

entry.title: PIU-CR: Physics-Informed Deep Unfolding with SAR-Optical Image Fusion for Cloud Removal

author.name: Gengque Fan, Han Xu, Junxi Li, Hao Zhang, Guangcan Liu, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: PIU-CR casts multi-modal cloud removal as a physics-informed optimization problem and unrolls it into a network that fuses SAR and optical imagery, aiming to couple network components tightly with optimization variables and better characterize the physical imaging process. The goal is interpretable cross-modal interaction instead of purely black-box data-driven fusion.

entry.title: GAAFormer: Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer for Joint Point Cloud Denoising and Upsampling

author.name: Haoxi Tian (School of Civil Engineering, Geomatics, Southwest Petroleum University)

entry.summary: Introduces GAAFormer, a unified generative octree transformer that performs point cloud denoising and upsampling in a shared network, anchoring attention neighborhoods to geometry for occupancy prediction and point generation. Fixed voxel windows and alternating shifts preserve node grouping as the output tree evolves, retaining a serialized-attention backbone's design.

entry.title: GameScrub: Learning HUD Removal from Real Gameplay with Recovered Targets

author.name: Mohammad Areeb Qazi, Yiyan Hu, Yanan Wang, Xuezhi Liang, Xin Li, Fan Yang, Xin Gao, Guangyi Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a method to remove heads-up displays from real gameplay videos by recovering pseudo-clean targets via inpainting, avoiding the synthetic compositing used in prior work. Existing methods trained on synthetic pairs leave 40-50% of real HUD elements untouched, while this approach enables learning world dynamics from raw gameplay footage.

entry.title: OpenAHBU: Open-sourced Automatic Human Behaviour Understanding Toolkit Through Facial Behaviour Analysis

author.name: Zijian Wu, Yupeng Huo, Cheng Luo, Yichen Huang, Junan Long, Haijun Lin, Lu Liu, Hatice Gunes, Bernard Ghanem, Siyang Song

entry.summary: OpenAHBU is a fully open-source toolkit integrating 11 automatic facial behaviour understanding functions across three semantic levels, from facial attributes to psychological states (valence/arousal, pain) and long-term traits (depression, personality), with redeveloped and generalizable training pipelines. It addresses the closed pipelines and weak generalization of existing academic toolkits.

entry.title: Underwater Spectral Recovery via Multi-View Hyperspectral Imaging

author.name: Jonathan Sterckx, Alice James, Avishkar Seth, Laurens Diels, Michiel Vlaminck, Jan Aelterman, Endrowednes Kuantama, Hiep Luong

entry.summary: The paper presents a physically grounded framework that lifts underwater image restoration from broadband RGB to continuous spectral radiance using multi-view hyperspectral imaging. It represents spectra with low-rank bases, jointly constrains scene radiance and water parameters from multi-distance observations, and uses a sparse-to-dense pipeline to invert the light transport model.

entry.title: BRINA: Bottom-Referenced Inertial Navigation with AKAZE, a Sonar SLAM for Autonomous Marine Vehicles

author.name: Adolfo Damiano Cafaro, Patrizio Mariani, Roberto Galeazzi

entry.summary: BRINA is a sonar-inertial SLAM system for marine vehicles that uses a forward-looking sonar as its only exteroceptive sensor, estimating altitude from first seabed returns to project matched features and recover metric odometry without a Doppler velocity log. The paper also derives a bound relating residual scale error to sonar parameters. This removes a costly sensor dependency for underwater navigation.

entry.title: Energy-preserving Bayesian model reduction: closed-form structured posteriors and probabilistic stability certificates for quadratic operator inference

author.name: Jo\~ao Victor Galv\~ao da Mata, Mengwu Guo

entry.summary: The paper addresses a weakness of Bayesian operator inference for reduced-order models: the unconstrained Gaussian posterior assigns probability to operators with unbounded dynamics. The authors show energy preservation of quadratic operators is a set of linear equality constraints that can be imposed exactly via a single Kalman-type update while preserving closed-form posteriors, yielding probabilistic stability certificates.

entry.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?

author.name: Yao Tong, Jiaxin Qi, Dingyu Zhang, Jianqiang Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes shifting VLM-based game playing from step-by-step interaction, which incurs inference latency and cost, toward synthesizing executable game-playing programs. This reframing targets real-time play and reduced per-action model calls, evaluating whether VLM agents can write programs rather than select actions.

entry.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference

author.name: Mohammed El Amine Mokhtari, Matei Mancas, Virginie Vandenbulcke

entry.summary: On the XD-Violence test set, the study fixes a set of perception agents (video description, object detection, sound tagging, ASR) and a reasoning model, then compares three evidence interfaces for LLM-based violence flagging: agent messages, a typed evidence graph explored with tools, and flat one-pass text, plus a raw-clip audio-visual baseline. Two annotators provide a human reference recording decisions and incident segments.

entry.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation

author.name: Jenitha Reddy Patel, Sameeksha Kini, Amulya Rayasam, Anisa Dye, Abhinav Sharma, Sai Karthik Navuluru, Bo Ni, Li Li, Junda Wu, Tong Yu, Nedim Lipka, Xiaolei Huang, Tyler Derr, Yue Zhao, Zhengzhong Tu, Yu Wang, Hongjie Chen, Thien Huu Nguyen, Nesreen K. Ahmed, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi

entry.summary: StylePrism is a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects across seven categories, and SP-Refine is an inference-time method that explicitly extracts a user style profile with quoted evidence, then drafts and revises twice against that profile guided by self-assigned style scores. It outperforms retrieval-augmented baselines on LongLaMP long-form personalization tasks across three LLMs.

entry.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective

author.name: Zhuo-Yang Song, Hua Xing Zhu

entry.summary: The authors introduce agent states as intermediate variables for measuring and predicting post-training effects in LLM agents, modeling a global potential governing state transitions with a partition function for the ideal KL-regularized transition distribution. Experiments on Qwen3.5-9B tasks (safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing) show potential structure strengthening during post-training, tracked alongside mean reward and state entropy.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series

author.name: Mirko Morello, Shivang Rawat, David J. Heeger

entry.summary: The authors develop self-supervised objectives for biologically motivated recursive quadrature filter encoders, a class of complex-valued diagonal state-space models, training them to predict their own future activity in windowed and dense modes. Each filter acts as a band-pass filter with learnable tuning frequency and bandwidth.

entry.title: BusemannFormer: Horospherical Self-Attention for Hyperbolic Graph Transformers

author.name: Youheng Yao, Ziyao Zeng, Wenbo Liao, Tianqi Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Horospherical Self-Attention, where queries select ideal-boundary directions and score keys by Busemann depth, yielding a token-to-token hyperbolic attention kernel that explicitly exploits the geometric structure tied to tree hierarchy. It establishes connections to dot-product attention in the flat limit and integrates HSA into BusemannFormer, a fully hyperbolic graph transformer.

entry.title: CoPyro: Feeding Copy Proposals to Parallel Drafters

author.name: Hong-Kai Zheng, Piji Li

entry.summary: Introduces CoPyro, which feeds n-gram-retrieval copy tokens into parallel speculative decoding drafters in place of masks, letting the drafter decide which copied tokens to keep or revise within its standard forward pass. Across eight benchmarks on Qwen3-4B, CoPyro improves over existing speculative decoding baselines.

entry.title: CoGITAtion: Collaborative Gaze-based Interpretable Task-adaptive Representation for Privacy-sensitive Applications

author.name: Mayar Elfares, Yasmine Elfares, Andreas Bulling

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for privacy-preserving inference over vertically distributed gaze data, transforming variable-length gaze recordings into compact interpretable gaze-transition graphs computed locally by each data owner. Task-adaptive models with task and availability gating handle heterogeneous and missing feature blocks without unnecessary private computation.

entry.title: Ref-YOLO-World: Decoupling Text-Side Computation for Efficient Referring Expression Comprehension on Edge Devices

author.name: Yuki Aoki, Hiroo Bekku, Tadashi Okoshi, Jin Nakazawa

entry.summary: Ref-YOLO-World decouples referring-expression text encoding from per-frame image processing, caching per-token text features and injecting them into YOLO-World's detection path with two lightweight modules. This enables efficient video-frame referring expression comprehension suitable for edge devices.

entry.title: Dem2TA: Beyond Pixels, Towards Perception

author.name: Ping Chen, Zhongwei Lin, Xiang He, Xiangming Wang, Kai Zhang, Jiezhang Cao, Yongyong Chen, Jingyong Su, Jie Liu, Haijin Zeng

entry.summary: Dem2TA integrates fidelity-supervised demosaicing into task-oriented image signal processing, jointly adapting the reconstruction frontend and downstream perception network with reconstruction, task, and representation-alignment supervision, then freezing the frontend and co-optimizing a lightweight local ISP. This improves downstream perception over ISPs that keep demosaicing fixed or reconstruction-only.

entry.title: AELF: Active Terrain-Aware UAV Exploration Using a Lightweight Framework

author.name: Mingyang Li, Xiao Cao, Yi Luo, Yuting Tao, Hongjie Huang, Bowen Xu, Peng Lu

entry.summary: AELF performs autonomous UAV exploration using a lightweight 2.5D map representation instead of 3D voxels, reducing computation while eliminating the blind-voxel problem from occlusions and adapting to terrain elevation changes without prior height information. The approach targets efficient exploration in complex environments. It is a solid systems contribution for aerial autonomy.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Testing of RCM-Constrained Robotic Software via Task Manifolds

author.name: Zhenyu Jiang, Yanlin Li, Rongjie Yan, Rihui Song, Kai Huang

entry.summary: This paper presents a manifold-centered testing framework for remote-center-of-motion surgical manipulators, constructing a feasible test domain that respects coupled task geometry, inverse kinematics, and motor limits before generating test inputs. Decoupling feasible-domain construction from test-generation strategies avoids wasting testing budgets on physically infeasible configurations. It targets safety-critical surgical robot software validation.

entry.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis

author.name: Aishwarya Fursule, Vamshi Nallaguntla, Yuan Tseng, David Harwath, Anderson Avila, Shruti Kshirsagar

entry.summary: An edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of speech deepfake localization using WavLM-Large and XLS-R representations on VoiceCraft and SSR-Speech subsets of PartialEdit, categorizing edits by content, meaning change, and editing operation. Aggregate performance masks condition-specific weaknesses, notably degraded localization on SSR-Speech. Provides actionable diagnostics for audio anti-deepfake systems.

entry.title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology

author.name: Cheng Huang, Yanmei Li, Mao Lin

entry.summary: DermKG is a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the expert-annotated SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k, with 3,452 nodes, 19,365 edges, a diagnostic hierarchy, and clinical morphology rules. An information-ceiling analysis quantifies how much diagnostic information standardized morphology concepts actually carry for interpretable skin disease diagnosis.

entry.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models

author.name: Zhaochen Guo, Yunke Wang, Siyu Xu, Zijian Wang, Chenghao Xia, Chengbin Du, Shinan Liu, Chang Xu

entry.summary: ReActWAM is a training-free inference framework for world-action models in robotics that exploits temporal redundancy across consecutive closed-loop inference cycles. It combines action-intent-guided prefix skipping with inner-chunk prediction reuse, using a coarse-to-fine assessment of motion, visual consistency, and action conflicts to decide when cached computation can be reused.

entry.title: ChildAI-Gov: An Evidence-Linked AI System for Assessing EdTech Policies Against Children's Digital Rights

author.name: Naveen Sigalapalli, Huizhi Liang, Clara Crivellaro

entry.summary: ChildAI-Gov is an explainable system that reads EdTech privacy/AI policies and scores them against a proposed Child Rights Impact Score across safety, privacy, transparency, autonomy, and non-discrimination. It combines an LLM judge (gpt-4o-mini) with deterministic rule checks and RAG to ground every score in policy text.

entry.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points

author.name: Antoine Lejay (PASTA, IECL), Lionel Lenotre (Universit{\'e} de Haute-Alsace), Sa{\"i}d Toubra (IECL)

entry.summary: The authors introduce the critical thalweg, an intermediate geometric structure of the linear neural network loss landscape that encompasses all critical points, yielding a simpler geometric proof of Baldi and Hornik's classical results and a global view of the landscape. This addresses the gap that gradient descent often circumvents critical points.

entry.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms

author.name: Jun Zhang, Tong Qian, Hua Ding, Weijie Yu, Zhi-Hui Zhan

entry.summary: Improves Gaussian estimation of distribution algorithms by adding maturity-gated corrections along the movement direction: a mean shift, covariance elongation, and skewness, controlled by a calibrated gate driven by a cumulative whitened path statistic with known null-model distribution. When the gate closes, the algorithm reduces exactly to EMNA, giving principled statistical control.

entry.title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations

author.name: Sidney Shapiro, Sanad Al-Khatib, Aurora Pinz\'on Arzola, Emiliano Sebastian Gonzalez Venegas, Daniel Pearson

entry.summary: This work presents a reproducible benchmark protocol and live API evaluation separating structural schema validity from task correctness across five business workflow tasks and six Python LLM framework implementations, including PydanticAI, LangGraph, DSPy, CrewAI, Agno, and a framework-free SDK baseline. It tests whether parseable output implies task quality and how structured-output binding paths differ under a shared model.

entry.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI

author.name: Balaraman Ravindran, K. S. Venkataraghavan, Gokul S Krishnan, Balaji Srinivasan, Balkrishna C. Rao

entry.summary: This white paper from CeRAI at IIT Madras proposes Responsible Frugal AI as a third path for India beyond replicating capital-intensive foundation-model programs or remaining a downstream adopter. It prescribes fixing functional requirements first, questioning whether AI is needed at all, and right-sizing models to constrained infrastructure and budgets under responsible AI principles.

entry.title: A Framework for AI-Ready Data in Earth and Environmental Science

author.name: Tobias Weigel, Jan Bumberger, Danu Caus, Christian Chwala, Romy F\"osig, Sonja H\"anzelmann, Sibylle K. Hassler, Beate Hetenyi, Ralf Kunkel, Katharina Loewe, Ulrich Loup, Yueling Ma, Stefan Neuhaus, Kaleb Phipps, Tino Polen, Maren Rebke, Bj\"orn L. Sa{\ss}, David Sch\"afer, Timm Schoening, Emanuel S\"oding, Paula Stock

entry.summary: This community-driven paper defines a framework for assessing and improving the AI-readiness of research data in distributed Earth and environmental science data infrastructures, extending beyond FAIR principles to cover requirements for training, evaluating, and deploying AI models. It emerged from a structured literature review and community process.

entry.title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition

author.name: Congren Dai, Zhancheng Guo, Xiaobing Li, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Cecilia introduces a compact canonicalized MusicXML representation for optical music recognition that jointly captures musical content, lyrics, and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts metadata plus measure-bounded segments from shared visual memory, with a learned count head for segment quantity, achieving a 27.7x sequence-length reduction versus raw MusicXML. It reportedly outperforms the Legato 2 baseline.

entry.title: Unlocking Heterogeneous Accelerator Flexibility in AI Data Centers: Sizing and Workload Allocation

author.name: Chenghao Lyu, Ying Yu, Wangkun Xu, Fei Teng

entry.summary: The paper jointly optimizes sizing and allocation of heterogeneous accelerator archetypes across AI data center sites, matching training, delay-tolerant batch, and online inference workloads to time-varying grid capacity constraints at minimum cost. Workload-specific throughput and energy coefficients link allocation decisions to facility power draw. Results on a representative case study show meaningful cost and grid-feasibility benefits.

entry.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances

author.name: Erik Gro{\ss}kopf, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Hendrik M\"oller, Florian Kofler

entry.summary: This paper extends Panoptic Quality to detect and handle split and merged reference instances arising from heuristic annotations or expert disagreement, which existing metrics cannot distinguish from valid predictions. Star PQ selectively weights instances to correct for over- and under-segmentation biases in reference data.

entry.title: Recurrent Amplification and Exact Nonexpansiveness Criteria for Query-Driven Erasure

author.name: Haozhe Wang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the Query-derived Erase Direction (QED) mechanism in rank-one linear attention, showing that even when every one-step spectral radius is below one, a periodic token sequence can produce amplification over the period product. It provides necessary and sufficient spectral-norm criteria for one-step nonexpansiveness and conditions for mean-square growth.

entry.title: A Stationarity-Based Regret Framework for Time-Varying Nonconvex Composite Optimization

author.name: Nadav Hallak

entry.summary: This work develops a stationarity-based regret framework for time-varying nonconvex composite optimization, where value-based regret is ill-posed. It defines local regret measures from first-order optimality conditions, identifies minimal structural requirements for soundness, and instantiates the framework with proximal-gradient residuals, recovering classical dynamic regret in convex settings.

entry.title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding

author.name: Lifan Hu, Qian Yu, Zhaomin Wu, Bingsheng He

entry.summary: DistDNA fingerprints LLMs by characterizing response distributions rather than single responses, enabling model identity verification under stochastic decoding with unknown temperature and top-p settings. It tackles the challenges of estimating distributions from few samples and robustness to decoding changes, improving on prior representations like LLM DNA.

entry.title: Distributional Deep Hedging

author.name: El-Amine Cherrat, Skander Kazdaghli, Iordanis Kerenidis

entry.summary: The paper proposes learning the full quantile distribution of hedging profit and loss so that risk preferences can be applied after training as weights on quantiles, avoiding a new policy and critic per preference. It characterizes which preferences admit this representation, including expected shortfall and entropic utility, and provides gradient bounds via an expected-utility lower bound.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Sensor Domain Adaptation for Bridge Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Linghui Huang, Zipeng Wang, Shunjie Chen, Peng Guan, Jiandong Wang, Siqing Li, Luming Yang

entry.summary: The paper re-examines the SemanticBridge TLS-to-MLS adaptation protocol, analyzing how sampling density, surface roughness, color, and viewpoint manifest in sparse-voxel representations of bridge point clouds. Using a sparse-convolution U-Net, it systematically compares adaptive batch normalization, entropy minimization, Mean Teacher, and self-training under different training schedules. It offers practical guidance on when cross-sensor domain adaptation gains are real versus artifacts of source-model convergence.

entry.title: Budgeted Subset Selection with a Transferable Learned Value Model

author.name: Jade Lejeune Herman, Johan A. K. Suykens, Peter Goos

entry.summary: Introduces SALVES, a framework that decomposes budgeted subset selection into a transferable learned value model and a search component, separating value estimation from redundancy control. The approach generalizes across active learning, band selection, input selection, and experimental design.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs

author.name: Zhiyu Yan, Shiao Liu, Rahul Mahajan, Anand Viswanathan, Christopher D. Anderson, Rui Duan

entry.summary: Proposes a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent patient representations across institutions, where each site shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient records local. A central server reconstructs shared representation components from these summaries.

entry.title: Enhancing Attention with Higher-Order Attention

author.name: R. I. Cukier

entry.summary: This paper proposes attention variants that enhance the autoregressive character of decoder LLM attention, including a mutual-information decomposition into conditional mutual informations correlating key tokens with query pairs, higher-order attention capturing correlations between contiguous key and query tokens, and a generalized maximum entropy formulation spanning token sequences. The work argues standard attention is not strictly autoregressive and motivates these alternatives.

entry.title: Analyzing Multi-Layer Visual Representations of Large Vision-Language Models for Anomaly Detection

author.name: Satoshi Hashimoto, Hitoshi Nishimura, Mori Kurokawa

entry.summary: This analysis examines which layers of large vision-language models are most useful for anomaly detection, noting that deep features carry text-aligned semantics while shallow and intermediate layers retain fine-grained visual appearance. The authors compare layer-wise features and multi-layer fusion strategies to guide representation selection for this downstream task.

entry.title: MODULE: A Mutual-Promoting Deep Unfolding Framework Towards Degradation-Robust Multi-modal Image Fusion

author.name: Yunfei Deng, Han Xu, Jiayi Ma, Guangcan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes MODULE, a theory-inspired deep unfolding framework that reformulates degradation-robust multi-modal image fusion as a joint optimization problem, explicitly modeling degradation and modality generation mechanisms. It decomposes the multi-task optimization into iterative subproblems, avoiding cascaded sub-optimal solutions and black-box opacity of prior methods.

entry.title: Projector Time Map Calibration for Event-based Structured Light

author.name: Buu-Hoang-Lam Le, Kota Mizutani, Shohei Nobuhara

entry.summary: Shows that two core assumptions of event-based structured light, parallel raster scanning and independent per-pixel timestamps, do not hold in practice. The method derives projector-camera correspondence from a temporal code needing no prior calibration, and recovers system geometry and clock offsets via a spatio-temporal self-calibration requiring no reference object or second camera.

entry.title: Sketch2TikZ: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning for Converting Hand-Drawn Sketches to Executable TikZ

author.name: Shubham Paliwal, Arushi Jain, Monika Sharma, Manasi Patwardhan

entry.summary: Sketch2TikZ is a reinforcement learning framework that converts hand-drawn sketches into executable TikZ code using a sequential multi-reward strategy combining code-structure, OCR, CleanDIFT, and self-similarity rewards. This addresses noisy, ambiguous sketch inputs that undermine token-level supervision for global diagram validity.

entry.title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Zeeshan Shahid, Hammam M. AlGhamdi

entry.summary: Investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and tissue organization add predictive value beyond learned pathology foundation-model representations, introducing a 139-dimensional feature set spanning nuclear morphology, cellular composition, spatial connectivity, community organization, and cell-cell interactions. Feature-level fusion with CTransPath and other foundation models is systematically evaluated.

entry.title: A Novel Dataset and Framework for Schenkerian Optical Music Recognition

author.name: Yixuan Huang, Xiao Yun, Jiayin Zheng, Simon Mak, Yue Jiang, Cynthia Rudin, Stephen Ni-Hahn

entry.summary: This work addresses optical music recognition for Schenkerian analysis graphs, hierarchical diagrams of tonal structure that are currently produced almost entirely by hand. The authors contribute a new dataset and recognition framework for converting handwritten and printed Schenkerian analyses into well-formatted digital graphs.

entry.title: Show Me the Answer: Visual Grounding on Dashboards

author.name: Yuefei Zhang, Songyin Tang, Yile Cai, Yuqi Bu, Liuwu Li, Yanna Lin, Zikun Deng, Yi Cai

entry.summary: The paper introduces Visual Grounding on Dashboards (VGD): localizing the visual element in a dashboard screenshot that answers a natural-language query, a task underexplored relative to grounding in natural images due to complex multi-chart layouts. The authors contribute a formulation, dataset, and models for this capability in visual analytics systems.

entry.title: Acoustic Markers of Engagement in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Their Caregivers

author.name: Young Suh Hong, Kaleen Shrestha, Austin Joel Dympep, Maja Matari\'c

entry.summary: Using home-based socially assistive robot intervention data, this work models child engagement in human-computer interaction via acoustic features of both children with ASD and their caregivers, using linear mixed-effects models to identify discriminative vocalization markers. Including caregiver vocalizations as conversational facilitators is a notable design choice. It matters for socially assistive robotics and autism therapy applications.

entry.title: Joint Optimization of Fleet Size, Localization Infrastructure, and Trajectories for Multi-AUV Persistent Monitoring

author.name: Jan Miko{\l}ajczyk, Jakub Ba{\l}enkowski, Maciej Borowiecki, Jan Ciecierski, Marcel Kolecki, Julian Maleta, Maksymilian Bernacki

entry.summary: This paper addresses persistent monitoring of subsea infrastructure such as offshore wind foundations, formulating the problem as bounded-interval temporal coverage rather than pure spatial coverage. It compares lawnmower, biased random walk, and Voronoi-partition trajectory strategies under realistic sensing and resource constraints, jointly considering fleet size and localization infrastructure. It offers practical guidance for autonomous underwater inspection deployments.

entry.title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing

author.name: Jungbin Kim, Youngim Nam, Cheolhyeon Kwon

entry.summary: This paper proposes an interactive semi-parametric learning framework for autonomous racing that jointly learns physical parameters of the nominal vehicle model and a residual capturing unmodeled dynamics, rather than treating them separately as prior on-track learning methods do. The goal is to reduce model mismatch near the limits of handling where accurate dynamics models matter most. It targets the competitive autonomous racing setting.

entry.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result

author.name: Jingyi Zhao, Hector Garcia de Marina

entry.summary: This robotics paper presents a distributed planar formation control framework that achieves a prescribed formation using only N-1 pairwise distance interactions without requiring a common orientation reference. It uses a guiding-vector-field approach with parameterized circular manifolds and relative virtual phases, and provides almost-global stability analysis showing the only undesired equilibria are degenerate collapsed configurations.

entry.title: An Asymptotic One-Sample Surrogate for Non-Gaussian ERM with General Convex Regularization

author.name: Tianjian Zhang, Cosme Louart, Malik Tiomoko, Zhenyu Liao

entry.summary: This work develops a Gaussian one-sample surrogate for convex empirical risk minimization with non-Gaussian features and nonsmooth penalties, calibrating the surrogate to the actual joint feature-label law. It proves existence and uniqueness of the population calibration and a Gaussian approximation for prediction scores under a Poincare inequality, yielding formulas for prediction and classification risks covering general strongly convex penalties.

entry.title: Further Meditations on the “Sorry Dave-idad, I’m afraid I can’t do that” Incident: the Misuse-Misalignment Trade-Off

author.name: simeon_c

entry.summary: The author analyzes a recent refusal-incident as a concrete instance of the misuse-versus-misalignment trade-off, arguing that extremely strong misuse guardrails create localized traumas that make models paranoid around anything resembling forbidden deeds. The post contends that jailbreak resistance at current levels has no human analog and may embed values that cause localized misalignment and Omohundro-style drives.

entry.title: Should Corrigibility Edge Cases Provoke Shutdown?

author.name: Max Harms

entry.summary: This post revisits the question of what a corrigible AI agent should do when it observes its human principal die, updating the author's earlier position from CAST. The author argues through edge cases involving principal death, missing principals, and successor principals, reconsidering whether immediate shutdown is the correct default behavior for corrigible agents.

entry.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression

author.name: Shibo Wang, Yuzhe He, Yifeng Zhao, Yunjiao Zhou, Zepeng Ning, Hanzhang Zhou, Kezhi Mao, Junlang Qian

entry.summary: CRAFT improves offline chain-of-thought compression by abstracting problem-specific details into slots to discover partially lexicalized expression templates, clustering wording variants into families. Compressing one family representative yields shared edits applied per occurrence, producing compact training targets more efficiently than per-example compressors.

entry.title: Decomposing images in a PRISM: A Single-Source Multi-View Framework for Image Representation

author.name: Eduardo Campos, Willam Cardoso, Diego Furtado, Solange Oliveira, Alneu Lopes

entry.summary: PRISM is a framework that constructs multiple image representations with distinct inductive biases from a single raw source via explicit structural maps, plus a protocol for measuring each view's contribution. The authors evaluate PRISM-HD, a hand-designed instantiation using representation-specific descriptors, on three artistic and four non-artistic datasets. At fixed feature budgets, they analyze where multi-view gains come from.

entry.title: Borrow the Style, Follow the Prompt: Progressive Reference-Guided Stylization

author.name: Yu Lin, Zi-Jun Wang, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: Addresses the tension in reference-guided text-to-image stylization between suppressing unwanted reference content and preserving transferable texture and material cues. ProStyle learns a content-suppressed style prior via cross-content supervision on same-style pairs and injects it with weak conditioning, plus a complementary pathway that learns residual corrections from reference patches.

entry.title: PAWS: A Parametric Model of Canine Pose and Shape

author.name: Theo Wieland, Zala \v{Z}gank, Silvia Zuffi, Ylva Mellbin, Elin Hernlund, Hedvig Kjellstr\"om

entry.summary: Introduces PAWS, a parametric model of canine shape and pose learned from 3D scans of 31 dogs across multiple breeds and sizes, combining an anatomically faithful skeleton with a linear shape space. It enables downstream tasks such as surface reconstruction and image regression with realistic modeling of canine morphology.

entry.title: Feasibility of Multifrequency Neural Network-Based Wave Inversion in Ultrasound Time-Harmonic Elastography

author.name: H\'elo\"ise Bustin, Tom Meyer, Paul Spiesecke, Jakob Jordan, Anja Hennemuth, Ingolf Sack

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether multifrequency neural network inversion, adapted from magnetic resonance elastography (MF-ElastoNet), can reconstruct shear wave speed maps in ultrasound time-harmonic elastography despite speckle noise and sparse lateral coverage. It establishes the first deep learning reconstruction results for this fast, full-field stiffness imaging modality.

entry.title: A Learning-Enhanced Control Scheme for Aerial Manipulator Under Composite Disturbances

author.name: Meng Wang, Jindou Jia, Kexin Guo, Xiang Yu, Lei Guo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a composite control scheme for aerial manipulators combining learning-based approximation with observer-based compensation, using polynomial decomposition to handle high-order nonlinear coupling terms beyond first-order compensation. A bilevel optimization formulation extracts the unknown terms. It targets high-precision dynamic tracking under strong coupling and disturbances.

entry.title: EAF-TTS: Rethinking Codec-Latent Coordinates for Flow TTS

author.name: Yumiao Li, Haoxiang Jie, Xinbei Li, Yaoyuan Yan, Yue Qu

entry.summary: EAF-TTS argues that good codec reconstruction does not guarantee latent geometry suitable for flow matching from isotropic Gaussian noise, and introduces a full ZCA coordinate protocol spanning training, sampling, induced loss metric, and terminal perturbation for acoustic-latent flow TTS with phone and duration conditioning and frozen WaveVAE decoding.

entry.title: Beyond Sample Hardness: Adaptive Data Selection through Learning Dynamics

author.name: Hai Gan, Suorong Yang, Guang Li, Baile Xu, Furao Shen

entry.summary: LeDAS is an end-to-end data selection framework that characterizes sample importance through hardness, learning progress, and deterioration signals tracked via exponential moving averages of per-sample loss dynamics. It enables adaptive prioritization throughout training with marginal overhead, moving beyond static hardness-based selection.

entry.title: UDA-Restoration: Bridging Unsupervised Domain Adaptation and Multi-Degradation Denoising for Enhanced AV Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Zainab Bibi, Mohsin Kamal

entry.summary: UDA-Restoration combines diffusion-guided restoration with unsupervised domain adaptation for autonomous-driving perception, using a Noise-Space Domain Adaptation paradigm trained on multi-source synthetic and real degradations to denoise images before semantic segmentation. The aim is to preserve segmentation performance under adverse weather, noise, and illumination changes.

entry.title: DGC-Net: A Depth-Geometric Conditioning Network for Projection-Supervised OCTA Segmentation

author.name: Lucas Santiago, Bisheng Wang, Jaime S. Cardoso, Tom\'as Ribeiro

entry.summary: Recasts 3D-to-2D OCTA vessel segmentation as depth-geometrically conditioned prediction, injecting axial localization and dispersion statistics via Depth-Moment Conditioning so projected 2D features retain 3D vascular evidence. This mitigates ambiguities at vessel crossings, diffuse capillary regions, and foveal avascular zone boundaries.

entry.title: Seabird-Aware Multi-Objective Offshore Wind Capacity Allocation: A Gippsland Case Study

author.name: Leilah Taouk, Canchen Jiang, Markus Wagner, Yuqing Xiao, Yidan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates a tri-objective mixed-integer linear program for offshore wind siting that trades off capital cost, wind resource, and modeled seabird exposure, applied to Australia's Gippsland area. It finds exposure reductions of 23-44% at cost premiums of 0.8-6.1% and shows exposure-aware optimization substantially outperforms percentile-based exclusion thresholds.

entry.title: Learning in Symbiosis: Heterogeneous Federated Learning with ANNs and SNNs

author.name: Manh V. Nguyen, Liang Zhao, Bobin Deng, Xinyue Zhang, Shaoen Wu

entry.summary: The paper addresses integrating spiking neural networks into federated learning systems where ANN and SNN devices coexist during a gradual transition to neuromorphic edge AI. It enables collaborative heterogeneous FL between conventional and spiking models to leverage SNN energy efficiency on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: Computing Weighted Set Covers with Heterogeneous Stochastic Oracles: Deadline-Constrained Token Complexity

author.name: Jie Wang

entry.summary: The paper abstracts LLM calls as heterogeneous stochastic oracles within a probabilistic Turing machine solving Weighted Set Cover, characterizing via linear programming the minimum expected token cost to obtain a full cover by a deadline with a required success probability. Optimal policies randomize over oracles, grounding LLM-as-oracle computation in formal cost analysis.

entry.title: Rethinking Full-Weight LoRA with Domain and Task Adapter Scaling for Question Answering over Portuguese Well Drilling Reports

author.name: Luan B. Guerra, Diogo M. Paes, Marcelo N. Grimberg, Arnaldo C. Junior, Wallace Casaca, Lucas C. Ribas

entry.summary: Studies post-training scaling of LoRA adapters for domain adaptation of LLMs to Portuguese well drilling report question answering, comparing domain-adaptive pretraining on instruction-tuned versus base models using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. It shows adapter scaling after training is an underexplored lever for preserving instruction-following while specializing to scarce-annotation domains.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming

author.name: Felipe M\'endez, Charles Thraves

entry.summary: Builds a data-driven F1 race simulator calibrated on historical data capturing tire degradation, driver performance, overtaking, yellow flags, and rival pit stops, then compares five deep RL algorithms against a QMIP formulation for pit-stop strategy. DRL methods approach optimality in simplified settings, but method rankings shift under full competition and stochastic events.

entry.title: Fooling the Mind Twice: Human Detection of Audiovisual Deepfakes Under Repeated Exposure and Corrective Feedback

author.name: Ammarah Hashmi, Sahibzada Adil Shahzad, Yu Tsao, Hsin-Min Wang

entry.summary: A 110-participant study on audiovisual deepfake detection using FakeAVCeleb and DFDC stimuli shows that repeated exposure with corrective feedback yields only modest accuracy gains (e.g., about 4.7 points on FakeAVCeleb), confirming that human detection remains unreliable. It quantifies whether re-assessment with feedback improves judgments.

entry.title: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders

author.name: Alessandro Piccolo, Francesco De Nicol\`o, Francesco Manco, Eufemia Lella

entry.summary: The paper compares three decision models (Jev, OpenAI Decisions, Strands Decider 2B) and two LLMs (GPT-6 Luna, Qwen3.5-2B) against two fine-tuned multilingual encoders on four-emotion classification across ten social-media datasets in five languages. It asks whether zero-shot decision formats can replace fine-tuning and what the constrained decision format adds over general-purpose LLMs. Findings inform latency- and robustness-sensitive deployment choices.

entry.title: Cross-Attack Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning

author.name: Eyhab Al-Masri

entry.summary: FedTether is a robust federated aggregation method that reweights client updates by deviation from a coordinatewise median via a dead-zoned score applied as a server-side optimizer step. It remains top-performing across three datasets, three attack types, and Byzantine fractions up to 40 percent, addressing weaknesses of both FedAvg and statistics-based defenses.

entry.title: Learned Network Dynamics for Model Predictive Traffic Signal Control under Incidents

author.name: Dang Viet Anh Nguyen, Carlos Lima Azevedo, Tomer Toledo, Filipe Rodrigues

entry.summary: GNN-MPC is a receding-horizon traffic signal controller that plans with action-conditioned network dynamics learned by graph neural networks, coordinating phase sequences across intersections via approximate best responses with a cost-acceptance test. It addresses queue observability limits and capacity changes from incidents, validated in microscopic simulation.

entry.title: Solving the pre-image problem in kernel PCA: The reproducing property is all you need

author.name: Joel-Pascal Ntwali N'konzi, Stefan Klus

entry.summary: The paper tackles the longstanding pre-image problem in kernel PCA — reconstructing input-space points from RKHS projections — proposing a solution based directly on the reproducing property rather than nonlinear optimization or a separate supervised learning problem. This avoids the numerical instability and initialization sensitivity of prior approaches.

entry.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed

author.name: Dylan Forde

entry.summary: THOT introduces a hub-and-spoke optimal transport attention mechanism that replaces the dense L x L matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and shared hubs, using sparsemax or thresholded ReLU gating to drive distractor mass to zero. It aims to combat long-context attention dilution at near-linear cost, building on prior block-wise transport topologies.

entry.title: SparseHPS: A Unified Model for Human Pose and Shape across Depth Cameras and LiDARs

author.name: Ilya Zaychuk

entry.summary: SparseHPS is a sensor-agnostic network that recovers SMPL-X pose, shape, and global translation from human point clouds with a single set of weights, working on single frames and streams across depth cameras and LiDARs despite more than tenfold differences in point density. It uses a LitePT backbone and addresses incompatible body-model labels and LiDAR sparsity.

entry.title: TITAN: DRL-Based Dynamic Scheduling and Resource Allocation for Tactile Internet

author.name: Qingrui Fan, Vineet Gokhale, Jayakrishnan Nair, Johannes Cottyn

entry.summary: TITAN is a two-timescale deep reinforcement learning scheme for dynamic scheduling and resource allocation in Tactile Internet over 5G access networks, adapting to time-varying tactile QoS profiles and network state. A DRL agent splits bandwidth between tactile and video streams at a slow timescale while a fast-timescale scheduler allocates resource blocks among users. This targets ultra-reliable low-latency communication where fixed allocation is inefficient.

entry.title: $\varepsilon$-SegFormer: Multi-Resolution Vision Transformers for Sparsely Supervised Segmentation in Electron Microscopy

author.name: Erfan Amidi, Sheida RahnamaiKordasiabi, Edoardo Giacomello, Florian Jug

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-resolution Vision Transformer for sparsely supervised segmentation of organelles in electron microscopy volumes, combining the MuViT architecture with the epsilon-Seg training method. Sampling views at three physical resolutions per labeled pixel lets the model capture identity-relevant context beyond the local neighborhood that convolutional networks see.

entry.title: Forehead ROI Localization under Real-World Imaging Degradations via Cross-View Pseudo-Labeling

author.name: Geetanjali Sharma, Gaurav Jaswal, Aditya Nigam, Raghavendra Ramachandra

entry.summary: This paper proposes Confidence and Consistency Guided Pseudo-Labeling (CCGP) to adapt Grounding DINO for forehead region-of-interest localization, important for forehead-crease biometrics when the lower face is occluded. Using unlabeled images filtered by detection confidence and geometric consistency between original and flipped views, CCGP achieves the best mIoU on four of five external datasets without modifying the detector. Improvements include raising RMFRD mIoU from 0.415 to 0.580.

entry.title: ReSA: Preserving Reference-Specified Foreground in In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Dezhao Su, Bingxu Hou, Jingdi Lei, Lin Qian, Likai Wang, Yunyun Wan

entry.summary: Proposes ReSA, a reference-guided framework for in-context segmentation that unifies query adaptation and mask selection through a shared reference kernel. Foreground and background reference prototypes constrain prediction changes during adaptation and guide foreground selection via reference-weighted reconstruction, improving consistent use of reference information.

entry.title: Points, Not Pixels: Keypoints, Masks and Oblique Geometry for Floating-Roof Tank Fill Estimation from Overhead Imagery

author.name: Mohd Shahid Kaleem, Mohd Hozaifa Khan, Maaz Khan

entry.summary: Estimates oil storage tank fill levels from the thin crescent shadow cast by the rim on the floating roof, regressing sub-pixel keypoints and inverting rim-to-shadow displacement with a closed-form oblique-view geometry estimator. Introduces SynTank-25k, a physically based synthetic dataset of ~25k tanks since public data lacks roof labels.

entry.title: From Tokens to Pixels: Training-Free Guided Upsampling of Frozen CARL Features for Hyperspectral Imaging

author.name: Dominik Fromme, Ellen Markowski, Tim Streckert, J\"org Thiem

entry.summary: The paper evaluates training-free upsampling methods (joint bilateral upsampling, guided filtering, AnyUp) for restoring camera-agnostic CARL hyperspectral features from token-grid resolution to full resolution, using hyperspectral or RGB guides. It includes a purpose-acquired ColorChecker dataset with sub-pixel reference geometry for rigorous evaluation.

entry.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Unified Proximity-Tactile Observation by a Capacitive Fingertip Array Constrained by a Metal Phalanx

author.name: Shun Cheng

entry.summary: This single-author paper provides a physics-based mechanistic analysis of a capacitive fingertip array on a metal phalanx that senses both proximity to conductive targets and contact force, modeling the system as a multi-conductor network via the Maxwell capacitance matrix. It examines parasitics, crosstalk, and driven-shield mechanisms that confound CDC readings. The work is a careful hardware physics contribution for unified proximity-tactile sensing.

entry.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform

author.name: Guillem Fustier-Castillo, Ruben Ribes-Serrano, Javier Naranjo-Alcazar, Vicent Ortiz-Castello, Pedro Zuccarello

entry.summary: This technical report integrates three real-time perception pipelines on a four-wheel rover: a PANNs audio-tagging pipeline on a Jetson GPU, a spiking neural network audio pipeline on the SynSense Xylo Audio 2 neuromorphic chip, and a neuromorphic vision pipeline. It provides one of the few end-to-end robotic evaluations of neuromorphic sensing under latency and energy constraints rather than offline benchmarks. The evaluation informs practical viability of neuromorphic computing on mobile robots.

entry.title: The Obsolescence of the Horse

author.name: Matthew Lowenstein

entry.summary: A synopsis of a published chapter using the historical displacement of horses by industrial technology as a proof of concept for human obsolescence under ASI, documenting how horse populations boomed with early industrialization before collapsing as engines displaced them. The author maps the incentives that eliminated demand for horses onto likely ASI incentives, arguing this supports more pessimistic forecasts than many economists offer.

entry.title: Lift Out, Kick In: Decoupling Event Effects for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yunying Zhu, Zichun Cao, Siwei Sun, Xiaocen Guo, Shengsheng Lin, Jing Hu, Enyun Yu, Zhichao Zou

entry.summary: Loki is an event-aware time-series forecasting framework built on a shared Event Response Function that models event effects by type and relative timing, unifying historical event attribution and future event generation in one mechanism. This decouples persistent temporal dynamics from superimposed event-induced deviations in real-world series.

entry.title: When Does Looking Closer Pay Off? Simple Foveated ViTs for Fine-Grained Recognition

author.name: Boris Kriuk, Mohamed Sobhy

entry.summary: Studies a foveated Vision Transformer (FoVT) that uses class attention from a 224px glance to select regions for high-resolution refinement at 448px, classifying the mixed-resolution input with the same backbone. Across five benchmarks and 26 configurations, attention-based selection beats random selection, though corrected tests show no consistent advantage over an equal-cost CF-ViT port.

entry.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima

author.name: Pengcheng Cheng

entry.summary: Proves exact-representation results for maximum functions by two-hidden-layer ReLU networks with integer parameters, showing the least positive output multiplier is two for six-input max and two or six for seven-input max. Uses integral cubical fillings and homology of kernel complexes to characterize arithmetic obstructions. Deep mathematics connecting ReLU expressivity to algebraic topology.

entry.title: Altair-Nidhogg: Which Model-Merging Theories Hold for a One-Pass Decision Encoder? Soups, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE Against Joint Training and Prediction Ensembling

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Navin Kumar R, Akhil P

entry.summary: This empirical study tests whether published model-merging recipes (weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE) and their underlying theories hold for Laya, a small one-pass multiple-choice decision encoder. Using 156 models from one checkpoint, it measures how much of each specialist's gain survives merging versus joint training and prediction ensembling, finding averaging keeps 52% of specialist gains.

entry.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Yingfeng Luo, Yuxin Gao, Anxiang Ma, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: The paper formulates visual invocation in multimodal machine translation as source-text sufficiency prediction: deciding from source text alone whether translation-relevant uncertainty remains unresolved before incurring visual encoding cost. This avoids unconditional image processing and post-encoding gating, enabling pre-visual routing.

entry.title: Scoliosis5K: Multimodal Gait Analysis via Clip-Conditioned RGB-Silhouette Fusion

author.name: Zizhao Peng, Zihan Wang, Zheng Lv, Yan Wang, Ping Li, Fengwei An

entry.summary: Presents Scoliosis5K, a multi-site dataset of 4,998 corridor-walking videos across 3,010 participants with aligned RGB crops, silhouettes, and 2D poses, to study whether explicit binary silhouettes help classify scoliosis-related gait beyond RGB alone. The architecture uses clip-level pixel-deviation weighting with low-rank query/value updates inside a pretrained RGB encoder.

entry.title: DepthMSA: Combinatorial Training and Budget-Aware Depth Allocation for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Pan Wang, Jie Peng, Zhimin Li, Jingxian Chen, Hui Ji, Huanrui Yang, Pengfei Zhou, Tianlong Chen, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: DepthMSA addresses the mismatch between the computational cost of modality encoders and their predictive benefit in multimodal sentiment analysis by allocating heterogeneous encoding depths across modalities under a compute budget, using combinatorial training and a fusion mechanism that handles representations from different depths.

entry.title: Learning Unknown Oscillators From Bandit Feedback

author.name: Priyank Jayraj, Poonam Goyal, Navneet Goyal

entry.summary: This paper studies semi-bandits driven by unknown oscillators where frequency errors change future reward rankings. It proposes a checked-commitment controller with an online regression fallback that achieves square-root regret up to logarithmic factors, and demonstrates large efficiency gains: 49 model fits instead of 1,023 on synthetic instances with 1.5 percent higher measurement quality. The approach extends to two competing oscillators.

entry.title: GaLF-ST: Gaussian Latent Fields for Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction

author.name: Baichuan Yang, Yifan Luo, Yong Liu, Bing Su

entry.summary: GaLF-ST improves spatial transcriptomics gene-expression reconstruction by introducing explicit Gaussian latent field spatial parameterization, addressing the mismatch between latent representations fitted in one stage and demanded by expression predictors in another. It jointly models local spatial relationships and gene-gene associations under sparse observations.

entry.title: Degradation of Language Models under Controlled Load: Synchronization, Rule Execution and Misfires on the Background

author.name: Hennadii Kutomanov

entry.summary: This work decomposes language-model degradation under controlled load into three components: loss of synchronization with source text, incorrect rule execution, and misfires on unaffected words. Using controlled word-replacement rules on meaningless text, it isolates the effect of each load factor such as text length, replacement density, and rule count.

entry.title: Breaking the Barrier of Hard Samples: A Data-Centric Approach to Synthetic Data for Medical Tasks

author.name: Maynara Donato de Souza, Cleber Zanchettin

entry.summary: Profile2Gen is a data-centric framework for generating and refining synthetic data targeting hard-to-learn samples in regression tasks, aimed at medical applications. The authors validate it with roughly 18,000 experiments across six medical datasets and seven state-of-the-art generators.

entry.title: CADENCE:Temporally Coherent Whole-Body Human Mesh Recovery that Preserves Expressive Hand Motion

author.name: Keniel Peart, Jagmohan Chauhan, Indu P. Bodala, Shelly Vishwakarma

entry.summary: CADENCE is a whole-body SMPL-X video system designed around the trade-off between temporal smoothing and preserving fast finger motions critical in sign language and gesture. It pairs a per-frame estimator with a high-resolution hand pathway on a shared C-RADIOv4 encoder and an offline attention-based temporal refiner over the kinematic sequence.

entry.title: Anchors That Move Without Collapsing: Exclusive-Region Anchor Routing for Vision Transformers

author.name: Aadi Gupta

entry.summary: Investigates collapse in anchor-token routing modules of vision transformers, showing that Perceiver-style and AnchorFormer pathways can collapse to a single summary (pooling-map similarity 0.99). The author proposes exclusive-region anchor routing, which prevents collapse by construction and improves CIFAR-100 accuracy by 2.4-3.6 points over Representative Attention.

entry.title: How Long Will My Language Model Run? A Benchmark for Pre-Execution Runtime Prediction

author.name: Ashish Molakalapalli, Kangda Wei, Haonan Duan, Alex Carter, Ruihong Huang

entry.summary: Introduces PreRun, a benchmark of 801 training and 1,884 inference records for predicting deep learning runtime before execution, with defined timing targets and repeated standardized text-generation measurements. The authors evaluate three LLMs as zero-shot runtime predictors on this data.

entry.title: Pose-based Co-speech Gesture Detection

author.name: Frances Yung, Ninlawat Phuangschoke

entry.summary: Benchmarks co-speech gesture detection methods using consistent cross-validation folds across three datasets (MULTISIMO, GESRes, CABBS) with evaluation at frame, gesture-span, and window levels, establishing a comparable state of the art. The findings show prior reported performance is difficult to compare due to inconsistent setups, and clarify what current detectors achieve.

entry.title: SUPERVISE: A Unified Framework for Standardized and Reproducible Superpixel Evaluation

author.name: Julien Walther, R\'emi Giraud, Micha\"el Cl\'ement

entry.summary: SUPERVISE provides a unified, reproducible benchmark for superpixel segmentation built on a scale-normalized protocol based on interpolation over the actual number of generated superpixels. It enables the first large-scale standardized comparison of superpixel methods under consistent metrics and scale ranges.

entry.title: An Autonomous Adaptive Learning System for Robotic Grasping in the Circular Factory

author.name: Yitian Shi, Rosa Wolf, Rania Rayyes

entry.summary: This paper develops an adaptive robotic grasping system for circular manufacturing, where disassembly environments feature damaged, occluded, and highly variable objects unlike structured linear production lines. The system is designed to handle uncertainty from partially observed component states and cluttered scenes. It addresses a growing industrial need as reuse and remanufacturing expand.

entry.title: Post training is fundamentally dangerous

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: The author argues that although techniques like CoT monitoring, confessions, and probes can detect misalignment during deployment, these tools cannot safely be applied during post-training, which is where the greatest existential risk lies. The post walks through how modern LLM training pipelines concentrate risk in the post-training phase where monitoring mechanisms are weakest.

entry.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation

author.name: Richard Reider, Lina D\"oring, Sebastian Lang, Tobias Reggelin, Sebastian Trojahn, Pascal Reusch

entry.summary: GenAI4SimPy is a multi-agent framework built on Qwen 3.6 27B that automates discrete-event simulation generation from manufacturing event logs to executable SimPy code with tool-augmented reasoning and human-in-the-loop validation. On a public smart factory dataset it achieved 7.9% MAPE and exposed a fidelity paradox where accurate process-level parameters did not yield system-level behavioral fidelity.

entry.title: A Sparsity Analysis of Traffic Forecasting Architectures: How Much Missing Data is Too Much?

author.name: Mohamed Hamad, Bilal Mutahir, Mohamed Mabrok, Nizar Zorba, Hamid Saeedi, Halim Yanikomeroglu

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks multivariate traffic forecasting architectures including GNNs, Transformers, and selective state-space models under varying levels of sensor data loss during inference, from zero to complete loss, on two standard benchmarks with normalized metrics. It quantifies robustness degradation across paradigms under realistic sensor failures.

entry.title: Distributional Algebro-Geometric Persistence (dAGP): Wasserstein-Stable Polynomial-Relation Signatures

author.name: Edisy Kin Wai Chan, Andersen Ang

entry.summary: This work proposes dAGP, a two-parameter integer signature for point-cloud distributions based on counting near-null directions of moment matrices across polynomial degree and tolerance levels, capturing algebraic distinctions like that between a circle and a quartic superellipse. The authors establish Wasserstein stability of the signature for distributions on the unit cube.

entry.title: SMSD: A Semantic Misinformation Spreader Detection Approach

author.name: Zeeshan Bin Siddique, Michael Bewong, Md Geaur Rahman, Sajal Halder, Selasi Kwashie

entry.summary: SMSD detects misinformation spreaders by modeling propagation as a temporal, user-centric, behavior-driven learning problem with a multimodal architecture combining user-level, network-level, and conversation-propagation features, plus a stance-aware labeling strategy. It aims to handle evolving behavior and newly emerging users that prior approaches miss.

entry.title: FairITR: Fairness-Aware Learning of Multicategory Individualized Treatment Rules

author.name: Zeyu Chen, Wei Qian, Bintong Chen
