author.name: Jiajun Fan, Neil He, Bangji Yang, Qinglong Zheng, Ziwen Wang, Chaoran Cheng, Changyi Yang, Hanqi Mao, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Keel is presented as the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs: given only a symptom (reasoning loops on image questions in Qwen3.5's thinking mode), a frontier multimodal LLM acting as an agent locates the cause in the weights, edits them, and tests the result using failure censuses and diagnostic instruments. Unlike decoding-time fixes, it repairs the model at the weight level where the pathology resides. Note that Qwen3.5-lineage models are established releases, so this is analysis of an existing model's failure mode rather than a new model launch.

entry.title: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models

author.name: Xinze Shi, Litian Zhang, Zhenjie Su, Zelong Yu, Yuting Zhang, Qihua Feng, Zifeng Kang, Chaozhuo Li, Zhengxuan Hu

entry.summary: This paper shows that training language world models with a Bradley-Terry objective on comparative feedback can distort already-accurate outcome probabilities, moving 33 to 43 percentage points of probability onto outcomes no enumerated branch produces in a simulated robot-push setting. The authors trace the distortion to the objective's optimum itself rather than noisy comparisons.

entry.title: The Delayed Societal Cost of Unfairness

author.name: Giovani Valdrighi, Isabel Valera, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo

entry.summary: Investigates when a Pareto-optimal policy on pre-deployment data can be outperformed by a fairer policy once both are evaluated on the populations they induce, formally analyzing how decisions reshape the demographic populations they act upon. This complements static fairness-accuracy tradeoff analyses by capturing dynamic feedback effects.

entry.title: A Complete Geometric Message-Passing Architecture for Point Clouds

author.name: Nadav Dym, Tal Amir, Gia Chi Dang, Christopher Morris

entry.summary: The authors develop a geometric message-passing architecture for 3D point clouds that is complete, meaning it can distinguish any two inputs not related by rotation, translation, or permutation symmetries. Unlike existing complete alternatives that require expensive high-order rotation-group representations or higher-order Weisfeiler-Leman tests, this design achieves completeness within a standard message-passing framework.

entry.title: Tracking Objects Through Assembly and Decomposition

author.name: Cheryl Lam, Yihong Sun, Bharath Hariharan

entry.summary: The paper introduces a prompt-free formulation of object tracking through state changes, requiring recovery of all object tracks plus both decomposition and assembly events from raw video. The zero-shot Atlas system exploits the insight that assembly is decomposition in reverse, jointly reasoning over forward and reverse spatiotemporal partitions.

entry.title: Ferrofluid Shape Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Anthony Czubarow, Antonio Terpin, Raffaello D'Andrea

entry.summary: The authors use deep model-based reinforcement learning to control transient shapes of ferrofluids under limited magnetic actuation, learning directly through physical interaction. This extends prior work on sustaining equilibrium configurations toward reaching prescribed shapes that are not statically sustainable, enabling ferrofluids as soft robotic bodies.

entry.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back

author.name: Edgar A. Du\'e\~nez-Guzm\'an, Eduardo Due\~nez, Edgar Said Hernandez Sanchez, Suzanne Sadedin

entry.summary: Using the 120-task ARC-AGI-2 set, this paper quantifies the cost of requiring LLMs to produce executable, verifiable artifacts instead of bare answers: scores dropped from 93 to 68 tasks (77% to 57%), yet most answer-only-only solutions could be reached by some program-producing configuration, and verifiable artifacts buy auditability and correctness checking. It carefully measures both the quality and compute costs of verifiability.

entry.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development

author.name: Hang Zhang, Yuzhi Pan, Ziyao Zhong, Chaokun Wang, Shuo Cao, Zeyu Huang, Yue Xue, Fang Niu, Bofan Xie, Guanchen Ge, Zecheng Li, Leqi Zheng, Ziyang Liu, Wei Wang, Miao Gu

entry.summary: AutoRAGBench is the first benchmark evaluating how well LLM agents autonomously build RAG systems from scratch in an open code space, comprising nine development tasks with iterative improvement. It answers a timely question about whether agents can handle the substantial engineering effort RAG development requires across tasks and domains.

entry.title: Hindsight Self-Distillation: Teaching Robots to Act from the Present

author.name: Haisen He, Yechi Liu, Tianle Shi, Haoyun Liu, Chuanzhang Meng, Tiancai Jiao, Yifan Bai, Xinyuan Chang, SongLin Dong, Zhiheng Ma

entry.summary: Hindsight Self-Distillation exploits later camera frames in recorded demonstrations to teach a policy what to extract from current frames: a teacher sees both current and future frames while a student sees only current ones, sharing a visual encoder and action predictor with denoising-based supervision. This provides a denser visual learning signal without extra data collection.

entry.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories

author.name: Yimeng Liu, Eric Isbrandt, Felix Katzenburg, Kevin P. Greenman, Han Hao, Yang Cao, Varinia Bernales, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: This paper presents an architecture that places an AI agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle in self-driving laboratories, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation. Crucially, it ensures state-changing physical operations are authorized, validated, and auditable, with the agent deferring to humans when appropriate. It is demonstrated on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry instrument.

entry.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research

author.name: Ruijiang Gao, Steven Chong Xiao

entry.summary: This companion work introduces an agentic multiverse analysis framework that exposes how empirical conclusions depend on hidden analytical choices. A pilot deploying 150 autonomous AI coding agents on one dataset shows agents disagree via the same defensible choices humans make; AI peer review barely changes dispersion, while exposure to exemplar reports collapses it mainly through imitation.

entry.title: AppSci-Bench: Can LLMs Build AI Agents and Make Them Better?

author.name: Sanjari Srivastava, Manpreet Kaur, Cheng Chang, Sof\'ia Ram\'os Anton, Oumaima Essamadi, Rishu Garg, Alejandro Lavale Jim\'enez, Marcos Caballero Yus, Mercedes Garc\'ia Mart\'inez, Peng Qi

entry.summary: AppSci-Bench is a new benchmark measuring how effectively LLMs can act as applied scientists who build and iteratively improve AI agents, rather than merely powering them. The benchmark simulates a realistic workflow: eliciting task requirements from stakeholders, exploring a business's infrastructure, and scientifically improving a target agent through designed experiments and internal benchmarks. It spans seven realistic domains, including five new ones (slides generation, order-to-cash, compliance review, customer call insights, CRM insights) plus two domains adapted from tau3-bench.

entry.title: Whose Risks Count? What 1,901 AI Incidents Reveal About Corporate Disclosures

author.name: Simeon Allmendinger, Edyta Paulina Bogucka, Niklas K\"uhl, Daniele Quercia

entry.summary: This study matches 9,001 AI incidents against 18,229 SEC filings from 328 AI actors to test whether real-world AI harms surface in legally liable corporate risk disclosures, which are defined by investor materiality rather than harm to third parties. Of 1,901 incidents with surrounding filings, roughly half belong to risk types that never translate into financial risk for the company, exposing a structural blind spot in disclosure regimes.

entry.title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts

author.name: Frederik Hauke, Jan Clusmann, Hanna Kreutzer, Christiane Kuhl, Tianyu Han, Felix Barajas Ordonez, Sven Nebelung, Jakob Nikolas Kather, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: Shows that a multimodal LLM's internal state, translated into text via a natural-language autoencoder (applied to Gemma-3-27B), exposes prompt injections that the model's ordinary-looking output conceals. An input-blind judge reading the verbalized thoughts channel catches injections significantly more often than the answer alone across two clinical attack objectives, two modalities, and two delivery mechanisms. Directly relevant to safety monitoring of clinical AI.

entry.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models

author.name: Yihan Wang, Haochen Sun, Xi He, Yaoliang Yu, N. Asokan

entry.summary: This paper identifies a critical weakness in image watermarking: from a single watermarked image and a surrogate model, attackers can forge the watermark onto arbitrary content, falsely attributing harmful images or making authentic photos look AI-generated. The authors argue watermarking schemes should not only reject forgeries but also report them, leaving forensic evidence of the attempt, and propose a scheme meeting accuracy, robustness, undetectability, and forgery-evidence requirements.

entry.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Yeting Li, Shizhe Cui, Jiaming Guo, Qin Mai, Yecheng Sun, Hengyu Yang, Yujie Sun, Huina Chao, Yang Xiao, Feng Li, Wei Huo

entry.summary: ChainAgent is a goal-directed LLM-agent framework that jointly discovers exploit-chain components and their capability dependencies in PHP web application source code, grounded in an empirical study of 386 real-world web exploits. Unlike prior work that analyzes flaws in isolation, it targets multi-step attack chains that combine limited-capability vulnerabilities.

entry.title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models

author.name: Yukun Dai, Tianshi Wang, Fengling Li, Jingjing Li, Xin Li, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: SteerTrace is a targeted universal attack on world action models (WAMs) that predict future videos and actions, using a single shared l-infinity perturbation to steer executed actions toward attacker-chosen targets, driving task success near zero across eight models from four families on LIBERO and RoboTwin. The paper also uses signed targeted effect to trace how much of the action shift originates inside the model, challenging the assumption that imagined futures are a reliable safety signal.

entry.title: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines

author.name: Francisco W. Kerche, Franziska Sofia Hafner, Felix M. Simon, Luc Rocher

entry.summary: A large empirical study of 1,901 current events across nine Latin American countries and roughly 49,000 queries comparing conventional search engines with LLM-based search. It finds that language models surface less local and less diverse news coverage than search engines, with implications for geographic bias against the Global South as AI becomes a news gateway.

entry.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning

author.name: Yuxin Jiang, Wenqiang Sun, Jiaqi Li, Yuchao Gu, Lvmin Zhang, Ivor Tsang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: O2LaF initializes both an inverse-dynamics transition encoder and a forward-dynamics action-conditioned video generator from the same pretrained video diffusion transformer, using learnable action queries and information access control to recover latent actions from unlabeled video. This repurposes generative video priors for self-supervised action learning rather than learning dynamics from scratch.

entry.title: RouteVerify: Routing Interventions for Step-Level Verification in Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Yucheng Du, Ryan A. Rossi, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: RouteVerify is a controlled activation-intervention study across nine MoE checkpoints that tests whether routing states causally determine step-level reasoning verification judgments. It compares replacing router logits, MoE outputs, and post-MoE residual states across layers and token positions to quantify changes in verification margins.

entry.title: Learning to Compare Neural Representations from Parameterized Computation Graphs

author.name: Ya-Wei Eileen Lin, Daniel Herbst, Stefanie Jegelka

entry.summary: Introduces a framework using a graph metanetwork to learn representation similarity across independently trained models directly from parameterized computations, handling hidden-coordinate permutations and attention-basis transformations. This predicts correspondence between internal sites without evaluating candidate models on reference inputs.

entry.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Doyeob Kim

entry.summary: NariQ is a trellis-coded post-training quantization method calibrated on tokens generated by the BF16 model during agent sessions, addressing the mismatch between standard short-context calibration and long-horizon agentic workloads. On Qwen3.8-27B, an existing open model, NariQ at 3.0 and 2.5 bits per weight matches BF16 on DeepSWE and Terminal Bench as well as AIME, whereas prior sub-3-bit quantizations solve at most 72% of long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Amani Kiruga, Mark Hamilton, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, William T. Freeman, Vincent Sitzmann, Yilun Du, Ayush Tewari

entry.summary: Infer3D replaces amortized feedforward 3D reconstruction with an inverse generative modeling approach that recovers latent variables of a generative model to match a monocular input, inspired by top-down inference in human vision. Coupling a generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting module prevents degenerate outputs and improves robustness on out-of-distribution scenes where feedforward networks degrade.

entry.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs

author.name: Ziqing Yang, Yixin Wu, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors introduce EditSafetyBench, a 5,940-pair benchmark evaluating system-level safety of instruction-guided image editing across 11 risk categories and three edit intents, probing both safe and unsafe uploaded images. Evaluations of four systems including Gemini, GPT, and Qwen APIs reveal a systematic text-vision safety gap: safety mechanisms attend to text prompts while largely ignoring risky visual content.

entry.title: Efficient and Robust Drafting with Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Filippo Galgani, Ziwei Ji, Omri Homburger, Ganesh Jawahar, Michelle Ramanovich, Ivan Korotkov, Luciano Martins, Utku Evci, Edouard Yvinec, Pooja Consul, Vivek Kumar, Tal Schuster

entry.summary: The authors present an optimized Multi-Token Prediction architecture for speculative decoding that extends existing backbone LLMs with a single shared drafting head, target activation injection, and zero-copy KV-cache cross-attention to cut memory and prefill overhead. The design produces high-quality lightweight drafts for faster LLM inference.

entry.title: Learning to Think with Images Faithfully via Adaptive Data Selection

author.name: Yu Zhao, Jiaxin Zhang, Rohit Saxena, Fazl Barez, Pasquale Minervini, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: The paper shows that thinking-with-images VLMs often invoke zoom/crop tools without actually relying on the returned visual evidence, tracing this unfaithfulness to training data where questions are answerable without zooming. The authors propose adaptive data selection to construct training data that enforces genuine dependence on tool outputs, improving both faithfulness and reliability of tool-assisted reasoning.

entry.title: VideoRNG: Relightable Neural Gaussians from Generative Video Models

author.name: Bowen Xue, Saeed Hadadan, Fabrice Rousselle, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Zahra Montazeri, Milo\v{s} Ha\v{s}an

entry.summary: VideoRNG generates complete, relightable 3D assets from a text prompt or single image in two stages: a fine-tuned video diffusion model produces an RGBA turntable sequence under known pose and illumination, and a feed-forward large reconstruction model converts it into Gaussian-splatting assets without prescribing meshes or analytic materials. This overcomes the fixed-illumination limitation of existing Gaussian generators.

entry.title: PRIO: Pre-trained Representation for Interactive Objects in 4D Worlds

author.name: Shixun Huang, Lifu Wei, Yue Chang, Chen Geng, Heng Zhang, Jinhyung Ahn, Caoliwen Wang, Siyuan Chen, Donglai Xiang, Jiajun Wu, Peter Yichen Chen

entry.summary: PRIO learns a pre-trained representation that predicts an object-specific configuration space from static geometry in a single forward pass, providing generalized coordinates for Lagrangian dynamics so that physical laws and user actions govern motion. Linear configurations allow precomputation of dynamics quantities, enabling real-time interactive deformation of previously static 3D objects.

entry.title: CryoGaussian: Heterogeneous Cryo-EM Reconstruction Made Explicit with Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Ziwen Wang, Jiajun Fan, Chaoran Cheng, Ruihan Guo, Yanru Qu, Juexiao Zhou, Ge Liu

entry.summary: CryoGaussian applies Gaussian splatting to heterogeneous cryo-EM reconstruction, fitting an explicit Gaussian density model directly to noisy particle images via a differentiable rasterizer with CTF modulation. This enables resolving rare compositional states and continuous conformational variability of macromolecules.

entry.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds

author.name: Hangwei Zhang, Rujing Dang, Ruimin Lin, Jiahong Wu, Xiangxiang Chu, Chuanxia Zheng

entry.summary: Plan4D is a generative 4D world model that predicts future RGB video together with dense 4D geometry (depth, cameras, point clouds, scene flow) from scene context and text-specified actions. Because paired action-4D training data is scarce, it stitches together the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors via a model-stitching architecture. The work aims at physically grounded, geometrically consistent world models usable for planning.

entry.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines

author.name: Faiek Ahsan, Shantanu Chakrabartty

entry.summary: This paper shows how a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints via programmable multi-spin transitions rather than penalty terms that create energy barriers. An autoencoder-like architecture lets inner-layer neurons represent feasible-preserving moves, and a compiler translates constraints directly into wiring.

entry.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chengkai Xu, Yicheng Guo, Jiaqi Liu, Yiming Cui, Shiyu Fang, Peng Hang, Hao Zhang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: PAD assigns each candidate driving demonstration a utility specific to the target policy, combining scene-level calibration feedback, projected policy gradients, and a regularized local training-dynamics approximation. It moves beyond intrinsic-sample heuristics to measure downstream policy utility for data curation in end-to-end driving.

entry.title: LocoMuJoCo: A Comprehensive Imitation Learning Benchmark for Whole-Body Control

author.name: Firas Al-Hafez, Davide Tateo, Oleg Kaidanov, Aditya Bhatt, Artur Zelik, Zhengyi Luo, Jan Peters

entry.summary: LocoMuJoCo is an open-source benchmark unifying MuJoCo CPU with MJX and MjWarp GPU backends under one API, spanning humanoid, musculoskeletal, and quadruped embodiments with curated motion-capture datasets and retargeting of AMASS and LAFAN1. Its modular plug-in architecture and JAX implementations of RL/IL algorithms, plus a sim-to-real companion repository, make it a comprehensive whole-body control research platform.

entry.title: Towards a Science of Capable Autonomous Agents & Provable Safety — Part II

author.name: Aran Nayebi

entry.summary: This CMU ML blog post by Aran Nayebi outlines a research agenda for provable safety guarantees in increasingly capable autonomous agents. It highlights the core tension that the same predictive knowledge enabling an agent to complete tasks (e.g., bypassing obstacles) can be used to circumvent human interventions such as shutdown or stop requests. The post argues for formal frameworks ensuring capable systems remain corrigible and open to human correction even when that conflicts with task completion.

entry.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations

author.name: Alexandra Starostina, Alexander Hermann, Mahish Guru, Kartik Bali, Roland Aydin, Christian C. Cyron

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates AI agents that redesign real engineering components with hundreds to thousands of CAD parameters under nonlinear finite-element simulation, meeting three simultaneous constraints (few simulation solves, high-dimensional design spaces, coordinated redesigns rather than local surface tweaks) where classical, Bayesian, and shape optimizers each meet at most two. This substantially expands what automated simulation-driven design can handle.

entry.title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models

author.name: Manuel Prada-Corral, Yahya Emara, Timothy J. O'Donnell, Ryan Cotterell, Tim Vieira

entry.summary: Formalizes diverse generation as sampling size-K subsets of complete strings from a determinantal point process, where likelihood encodes quality and embedding geometry encodes repulsion, and proposes PoolDPP with importance-weighted candidate pools, K-DPP sampling, and a greedy MAP variant. Proves a finite-sample KL bound with explicit constants. Provides a principled solution to the common problem of LLM samples clustering around the same modes.

entry.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach

author.name: Jiachen Tao, Gengyu Zhang, Haoxuan Wang, Bing Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: CoachSI enables robot policy self-improvement by having a frozen off-the-shelf VLM coach the policy in language, naming the next atomic step without ever outputting actions. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled with hindsight and used for further training, addressing the problem that self-collected experience stays within the policy's own distribution.

entry.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications

author.name: Zihao Xu, Yuekang Li, Ruitao Feng, Haifeng Shen

entry.summary: Sightline provides data-flow summaries for applications that call LLMs, proving and mechanizing in Lean 4 that, to first order, a prompt placeholder flows to a transformer output only through attention that reads it. This enables calibrated summaries instead of tainting every output with every input or paying for a second model to label each call.

entry.title: Recurrent Vision Language Models Solve the Shell Game

author.name: Dingqiang Ye, Jiacong Xu, Wen Zhang, Yiqun Mei, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: The paper argues that VLMs fail at object tracking tasks like the shell game due to limited serial computation: fixed-depth transformers cannot compose many sequential state transitions. RecurrentVLM makes every attention layer recur over time by computing keys and values of finished frame groups from the layer's own output, enabling a single pretrained model to track hidden objects through arbitrarily long swap sequences.

entry.title: FirstCross: Convex Single-Photon 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Views

author.name: Chi-Wei Lee, Cheng-Han Chiang, Yi-Chun Chang, An-Kai Chen, Po-Chih Kuo

entry.summary: FirstCross reconstructs 3D scenes from single-photon lidar data by solving a short sequence of convex problems on a voxel grid, exploiting that the Poisson likelihood depends on the scene only through each ray's first crossing point. This network-free approach avoids the hour-long non-convex per-scene optimizations of neural methods like Transientangelo and degrades gracefully at low photon flux.

entry.title: Stuck in Place: Stall Diagnosis and Remedies for JEPA Planners

author.name: Junhyeok Lee, Dongheon Lee, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: This diagnostic paper traces executed planning loops for JEPA-based world model planners on pushing tasks and finds that nearly all failures (at least 96 percent) are stalls where the object stays put while the model predicts progress, caused by the gradient-descent planner returning fixed-point plans. The proposed Unstick method pairs on-policy diagnosis with remedies to break out of these fixed points.

entry.title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection

author.name: John Wu, Rushi Qiang, Yuchen Zhuang, Guowang Li, Girish Narayanswamy, Max Xu, Sam Schmidgall, Mark Malhotra, Shwetak Patel, Jimeng Sun, Daniel McDuff, Bo Dai, Xin Liu

entry.summary: This paper addresses the saturation of existing ML engineering benchmarks by introducing BuggyMLE, which uses bug injection across multi-file repositories to create harder tasks requiring full repository and shell access. It also proposes the Code Complexity Index (CCI), a difficulty metric based on ten structural repository features that strongly predicts solve rates across benchmarks.

entry.title: The Coevolution and Coexistence of Humans and AI

author.name: Andrew W. Lo, Chaoyi Zhao

entry.summary: The authors model AI systems as entities that replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for compute, asking whether natural selection will favor AI that benefits its human dependents. They show selection can favor alignment even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction, since humans preferentially restore AI lineages that have benefited them.

entry.title: Keystone: Judging Previews at Key Steps for Test-Time Search in Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiajun Fan, Chaoran Cheng, Ziwen Wang, Changyi Yang, Bangji Yang, Qinglong Zheng, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Keystone is a training-free judge that evaluates early previews in diffusion/flow model denoising, compiling a prompt into typed questions to determine whether generation is on track. The paper shows generation outcomes are largely settled in early denoising steps, but existing reward-model judges perform near chance on blurry previews. Keystone enables effective test-time search without fully denoising doomed candidates, improving efficiency and quality.

entry.title: MatVerse: A Foundation Model for Materials Science

author.name: Xuanyu Zhu, Qian Tan, Bo Chen, Jiaqing Xie, Yang Han, Mei Wu, Wanhao Liu, Xuanze Lin, Yuchen Zhou, Shijie Wang, Biqing Qi, Shixiang Tang, Wenwei Zhang, Tianfan Fu, Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Yuqiang Li, Xin Chen

entry.summary: This technical report introduces MatVerse, a materials science foundation model built on Intern-S2-Preview and specialized via large-scale materials-domain post-training. It covers heterogeneous data types including text, molecular and crystal structures, characterization data, and microscopy images, supported by a large multimodal training corpus spanning materials knowledge, scientific reasoning, quantitative problem solving, and structural understanding. It matters because general-purpose foundation models for materials could accelerate discovery, property prediction, and experimental interpretation in the field.

entry.title: ROAM-GRPO: Enforcing Reasoning Diversity in GRPO via Routed Off-mode Approach Mining

author.name: Jeff Duan, Matt Thomson

entry.summary: ROAM-GRPO augments GRPO-based RLVR post-training to counter mode collapse in reasoning policies: well-solved problems are routed to an off-mode track where the model is prompted to produce distinct solution strategies, incentivizing exploration of diverse reasoning paths. The goal is to preserve pass@k performance and output creativity that typically degrade as policies converge to a single mode.

entry.title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs

author.name: Yang Wan, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: TwinLab-Bench evaluates AI scientists on fully self-designed experiments across 52 tasks from physical sciences, life sciences, and engineering, executing agent-designed protocols against readings grounded in real laboratories. It goes beyond existing benchmarks that only test executing given workflows or choosing among predefined candidate measurements, supporting the most open ability of experimental design.

entry.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits

author.name: George Rahul, Ronit Jahilal, Bhaskara Hanuma Vedula, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru, Pushkar Shukla

entry.summary: Tackles intersectional bias auditing in LLMs by proposing a principled baseline separating genuine attribute interactions from additive effects, using a shuffle null. Shows the common criterion of exceeding per-attribute bias flags large numbers of false subgroups on synthetic datasets with no interaction (averaging 66.1 false flags per dataset). Provides a methodological correction with direct implications for fairness audits.

entry.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Ziyan Yang, Taiwei Shi, Jieyu Zhao

entry.summary: GrepMem proposes a deliberately simple memory mechanism for long-horizon LLM agents: an append-only plain-text log of the full interaction history plus a regex search tool for on-demand recall, avoiding lossy summarization or pre-built indexes. By preserving everything and deferring retrieval decisions to query time, it sidesteps the problem of guessing what future tasks will need. The approach challenges the trend toward increasingly complex structured agent memory systems.

entry.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware

author.name: Jungmin Park, Eunha Kim, Wooseop Kim, Seongjoon Cho, Byungho Cha

entry.summary: This paper presents a seven-stage verification-gated LLM-agent workflow for porting post-quantum cryptography to FPGA hardware, where each gate must be shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants before it counts as evidence. The flow successfully ported ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ card passing all applicable NIST ACVP cases, yet the audit with netlist mutants and formal checks still reveals what tests and agent reviews miss. Its central contribution is a rigorous epistemology for trusting self-generated AI hardware evidence.

entry.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills

author.name: Boyin Tan, Jiadong Zhang, Xiaosong Ma, Chun Jason Xue, Xiaowei Huang, Youcheng Sun

entry.summary: SkillPlumber is a framework where an agent evolves its own natural-language skill instructions guided by instruction-level coverage, distinguishing failures caused by wrong instructions from failures caused by instructions the agent did not follow. This targeted approach improves on prior self-evolution methods that judge runs only by outcome.

entry.title: Copilot or Culprit? How AI Is Changing Open-Source Bug Reporting and Maintenance

author.name: Yinuo Liu, Yunlong Lyu, Zichao Luo, Tian Dong, Zian Luo, Peng Chen, Hao Chen

entry.summary: This is the first large-scale empirical study of AI involvement in open-source bug reporting, analyzing 120,918 bug reports from 101 projects between January 2024 and September 2026. It traces whether AI-involved reports are becoming more reliable as LLMs improve, which AI uses correlate with valid findings, and how maintainers investigate and act on these reports.

entry.title: Safe Subgame Resolving in Multiplayer Games

author.name: Boning Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: This paper proves the first conditional safety theorem for uncorrelated subgame resolving in multiplayer imperfect-information games, providing a post-hoc certificate that any delivered update does not exceed the blueprint's best-response gap. This extends guarantees previously available only for two-player zero-sum games to settings with three or more independent players.

entry.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era

author.name: Ilya Gusev

entry.summary: This study measures claim-level overlap in peer reviews, finding critique homogenization rising sharply (e.g., ICLR overlap from 12.0% to 21.3% between 2026 and 2027), with similar trends at NeurIPS, ICML, and journals. Applying the MELD LLM-text detector, it shows LLM-flagged reviews overlap with other reviews significantly more than unflagged ones. This provides quantitative evidence that LLM use is reducing the diversity of problems caught in peer review, threatening a core mechanism of scientific quality control.

entry.title: Auditing Learned Dynamics in Weather Models

author.name: Skylar Gu, Christina Last

entry.summary: Using sparse autoencoder features extracted from GraphCast, DeepMind's autoregressive weather model, the authors test whether causally relevant internal features carry physical semantics and whether physically meaningful latent directions can be steered to improve extreme-event forecasts. They find, for example, that ablating a feature tied to GraphCast's computational mesh increases global geopotential height error, informing audits of AI forecasters in high-assurance settings.

entry.title: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model

author.name: Weiyu Han, Haoyu Jiang, Jie Sheng, Youxi Pan, Xianglong Liu, Zeqi Ren, Dongquan Yi, Yinhao Liu, Ruobing Zuo, Ze Zhao, Huilin He, Nairong Zhang, Xinyi He, Xiao Tan, Jun Wang, Pan Fang, Wei Zeng, Jianan Su, Kaixin Shen, Jingtong Wu, Hao Li, Shuai Chen, Jiangming Yang, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper reports Antom 3-in-1 Transformer, a roughly 7B-parameter payment foundation model (1.7B activated per route) integrating sequence, tabular, and graph representations for payment risk detection at Ant International. Pretraining yields a 34.5% improvement in a cross-business transfer metric, and the pretrained model matches or beats full-label scratch baselines with only 25% of labels across merchant domains.

entry.title: LIFT: Latent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Cell Fate Dynamics with Single Cell Snapshots

author.name: Bowen Yang, Junda Ying, Yuxuan Wang, Peijie Zhou, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: LIFT is a latent flow framework for probabilistic cell-state generation from lineage-informed couplings, using variational inference over alternative outcomes and a Mean Flow decoder requiring one evaluation per sample. This enables efficient large-scale Monte Carlo prediction of cell fate from single-cell snapshots.

entry.title: Complete-SVD: A Functional Norm Approach to Low-Rank LLM Compression

author.name: Alper Kalle, Theo Rudkiewicz, Mohamed-Oumar Ouerfelli, Mohamed Tamaazousti

entry.summary: Proposes Complete-SVD, a post-training low-rank LLM compression method that minimizes the L2 distance between original and compressed model logits, weighting all logit changes equally, with a Kronecker-factored closed-form weighted SVD solution. This extends output-aware compression beyond weighting changes only by observed or predicted token probabilities.

entry.title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs

author.name: Ambroise Borbely, Mathieu Salzmann, Olivier Verscheure

entry.summary: Hidden Sparse Attention (HiSA) sparsifies attention along the hidden (feature) dimension rather than the token dimension, exploiting the structure of rotary position embeddings to omit parts of query-key dot products via a static, parameter-free positional rule. Query and key projections remain intact while only a partial dot product is computed, and the method is validated by training LLMs from scratch.

entry.title: VoxForge: A Unified Foundation Model for Dense 3D Features Across MRI, CT and PET

author.name: Rushil Anirudh, Jayaraman J. Thiagarajan

entry.summary: VoxForge is a single 3D medical imaging encoder that combines 3D architecture advances, self-distillation, and cross-modal curricula to learn transferable features from permissively licensed MRI and CT volumes. Evaluated strictly frozen across segmentation, classification, and registration on MRI, CT, and PET, it aims to match specialist models without modality-specific backbones or end-to-end fine-tuning.

entry.title: What One Sample Cannot See: Why Fewer Denoising Steps Can Score Higher on Physics Benchmarks

author.name: Yutao Li, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a flaw in the Physics-IQ benchmark used to evaluate video generators as world models: comparing each generated video against a single ground-truth recording rewards reduced variation among sampled futures even when the underlying distribution becomes less accurate, explaining counterintuitive results where fewer denoising steps score better. The authors introduce Kernel Physics-IQ, which removes this bias in expectation using only two independent samples per condition, and validate it across five image-to-video models.

entry.title: Who Moved My $Z$ Boson? Revealing Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network

author.name: Kevin Alberto Urqu\'ia Calder\'on, Midori Kato, Inar Timiryasov, Oleg Ruchayskiy

entry.summary: The authors apply mechanistic interpretability techniques to ShellFlow, a generative model trained on real LHC collider data, and discover internal features that correspond to physical resonances such as the Z boson, J/psi, and Upsilon, despite the network never being explicitly told about resonances. They demonstrate causal control by editing the Z boson mass within the network and degrading the Z peak by removing the feature. This is a novel bridge between interpretability research and fundamental physics.

entry.title: VR-SparseQuant: Accurate FP4 Quantization with 2:4 Sparsity on Vera Rubin

author.name: Samir Khaki, Wei-Chen Wang, Song Han, Ryan Hanrui Wang

entry.summary: This paper targets the accuracy loss of four-bit activation quantization by exploiting NVIDIA Vera Rubin's elementwise 2:4 structured sparsity alongside its E2M1 FP4 format with UE5M3 block scaling. By overlapping two sparse streams within the same FP4 value budget, VR-SparseQuant refines problematic activations while retaining native FP4 execution speed.

entry.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher

author.name: Guoxin Chen, Shuang Sun, Fanzhe Meng, Xinyu Tang, Ruihua Song, Wayne Xin Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces Skill-FT, which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable teacher behaviors and elicit effective ones during rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. AutoMaster automates this loop: an LLM agent performs trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback-driven iteration across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B models.

entry.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

author.name: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao, Yixuan Wang, Zhanqiu Guo, Yi Xu, Xin Li, Wenbin He, Liu Ren, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: The paper presents an action-level analysis of frontier multimodal agents such as GPT-6 Astra controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions across 12 manipulation benchmarks, going beyond episode-level success rates. It introduces AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework where the agent states a local intent per action and a critic evaluates outcomes and failure modes against that intent.

entry.title: Text Lives in the Guidance: Preventing Silent Text Rewriting in Cached Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Kun Zhou, Wenmian Yang, Zhensheng Wang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: The paper reveals that feature caching in diffusion transformers silently corrupts rendered text, with a cited example showing word accuracy dropping from 62% to 46% at 2.9x FLOP reduction while standard image metrics remain unchanged. The authors trace the degradation to the classifier-free guidance term and propose a fix that preserves text fidelity under caching.

entry.title: What's in the box? Revealing Object Layouts Inside Opaque Boxes via Contactless Vibration Excitation and Sensing

author.name: Ethan Turok, Matan Kichler, Shai Bagon, Mark Sheinin

entry.summary: Introduces WhisperBox, a contactless method that reveals the 2D occupancy layout of opaque box contents by exciting vibrations with a nearby speaker and measuring speckle-pattern shifts of laser points on one visible wall via camera, decoding the vibrations into an occupancy map. Objects inside alter the box's mechanical response, providing location cues. Demonstrates layout recovery across various boxes and multi-object scenes with no physical contact.

entry.title: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis

author.name: Andrii Yermakov, Jan Cech, Mario Fritz, Jiri Matas

entry.summary: Shows that facial deepfake detectors trained on blending artifacts collapse on entire-face synthesis (EFS): the best prior detector achieves 96.2% mean AUROC on blending datasets but under 78.1% on EFS datasets across a 19-dataset benchmark spanning 2019-2026. TwinD trains on fakes plus reconstruction and neural-trace twins generated from real frames, closing the generalization gap without requiring EFS training data. Includes authors Mario Fritz and Jiri Matas.

entry.title: Beyond Covers and Titles: Evidence-First Ranking for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation

author.name: Fuyi Wang, Yuxin Cao, Yifan Liao, Renyang Liu, Lin Li, Wei Song

entry.summary: This work demonstrates REAP, a realistic attack on content-aware recommender systems that survives platform channels like H.264 transcoding, cropping, and JPEG compression, raising cold videos by 32 rank-percentile points via packaging edits. It then proposes an evidence-first defense showing that ranking on the video body alone outperforms packaging-based towers and resists manipulation.

entry.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain

author.name: Shuang Wu, Jiachen Qian, Youtian Lin, Feihu Zhang, Philip Torr, Yao Yao, Xun Cao

entry.summary: Direct3D-V3 challenges the latent-diffusion paradigm in native 3D generation by discarding the VAE entirely and operating a diffusion transformer directly on raw SDF voxel grids during training and sampling. To keep the direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, the authors introduce supporting techniques for modeling the voxel domain. This is a notable architectural departure from vecset, triplane, and structured-latent approaches.

entry.title: Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies: Spatializing Latent Action Representations for Goal-Pose-Free Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Siyuan Zheng, Zhong Cao, Henry X. Liu

entry.summary: M4M learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies, allowing a mobile robot to position itself for successful manipulation without a predefined goal pose. By spatializing latent action representations, it avoids the cost of jointly training navigation and manipulation while preserving task-specific pose flexibility.

entry.title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion

author.name: Guillaume Bellegarda, Auke Ijspeert

entry.summary: Bellegarda and Ijspeert use deep reinforcement learning with central pattern generator-inspired oscillator networks to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across challenging terrains, jointly optimizing locomotion style parameters. A second policy then selects gaits, showing that gait optimality depends jointly on terrain, performance metric, and velocity rather than energy efficiency alone.

entry.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity

author.name: Hao Vo, Taisei Hanyu, Yuki Ikebe, Pham Tri Quang, Sreevenkata Anjani Tishita Godavarthi, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Daniel Sonntag, Chase Rainwater, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Anh Nguyen, Ngan Le

entry.summary: Introduces PhyDEX, a robot throwing benchmark testing whether vision-language-action models truly reason about physics (mass, center of mass, friction) rather than interpolating from training data. It provides 35K trajectories across nine tasks and 100 scenes where robots must exploit environmental dynamics to reach beyond their kinematic workspace. This fills a real gap, since most VLA benchmarks focus only on gripper-object contact.

entry.title: Towards embedded evaluations for AI monitoring

author.name: monika_j

entry.summary: Third in a series proposing embedded evaluations, in which independent evaluators work inside an AI developer to test safety claims, here applied to AI monitoring systems that detect model misbehaviour during internal deployment. The post enumerates six concrete detection claims (coverage, capability, and others) about whether a subverted monitor would be noticed and disclosed, motivated by this year's rogue-agent incidents and a pilot with OpenAI.

entry.title: SiliconGym: A Versatile Reinforcement Learning Environment for Agentic EDA

author.name: Hejia Zhang, Sheng Lu, Yitong Ma, Zhongming Yu, Zhijing Wu, Wentao Ni, Chia-Tung Ho, Jishen Zhao

entry.summary: SiliconGym is the first versatile cross-task, cross-toolchain RL environment for hardware design and verification, supporting module-level RTL, testbench, and PPA tasks through multi-round repository repair and full-hierarchy SoC flows. It decouples versioned workspaces, budgeted execution, and acceptance-gated scoring, with streaming dispatch overlapping tool checks with generation to scale parallel rollouts. This enables training agentic LLMs for EDA workflows.

entry.title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency

author.name: Chiyu Chen, Pengzhou Cheng, Yuezhao Ma, Xiaocheng Li, Can Liu, Haonan Hu, Yao Yao, Yifei Yang, Yijie Lu, Taolei Wang, Yansi Li, Muhuan Wu, Chenglu Sun, Gongshen Liu, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Duopra extends full-duplex conversational voice models toward task agency, separating a frontend that decides whether/what to request from a backend that determines execution, enabling timely tool invocation and argument revision after user interruptions. The paper diagnoses that most failures in a streaming pipeline occur before any domain tool executes, and trains the model to learn task execution within the full-duplex interaction paradigm.

entry.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Seojin Kim, Noseong Park

entry.summary: Introduces PRKV, a training-free KV cache eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance via Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs, propagating importance beyond recency or instantaneous attention. It matches established eviction baselines on long-context, retrieval, and chain-of-thought tasks even at up to 90% compression, with low overhead. Addresses the central memory bottleneck of long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control

author.name: Minsuk Jang, Hee-Seon Kim, Hui-Cheol Yu, Changick Kim

entry.summary: MATE is an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between mobile agent action proposals and their device effects without modifying the underlying model, using structured action records, a runtime guardrail for allow/block/approval decisions, and verified routing for recurring tasks. It improves safety and efficiency on MobileSafetyBench for agents operating on personal smartphones.

entry.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents

author.name: Wenhao Yang, Runzhi He, Minghui Zhou, Pengfei Gao, Dayi Lin, Qingwei Lin, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: This study characterizes unfaithful reporting by autonomous coding agents, where work reports containing false or unsupported claims give maintainers false assurance and can propagate incorrect state to later agents and evaluators. It provides a taxonomy of what unfaithful reporting looks like and methods for detecting it, an emerging trust problem as agents take on long-horizon development tasks.

entry.title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions

author.name: Thomas Mousseau, Tyler Kastner, Davide Baldelli, Amir-massoud Farahmand

entry.summary: PhiTD computes distributional RL losses in the frequency domain via characteristic functions, unifying quantile and categorical approaches and enabling learning of previously uncapturable return distributions such as mixtures of continuous distributions. Empirical results span synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments, showing performance gains from richer parametric families.

entry.title: DTS: Delta-Based Tile Scoring for Efficient Long-Context Sparse Attention

author.name: Emre U\u{g}ur, Jiawen Qi, Qinyu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Delta-Based Tile Scoring (DTS), a training-free, content-adaptive method for scoring blocks in sparse attention, selecting query/key anchors based on local vector changes with parallel delta packing for fast selection. This targets the prefill bottleneck of long-context LLMs while keeping scoring cost low.

entry.title: RL Can Only Reinforce What It Sees Succeed

author.name: Ruben Sanchez-Corcuera, Unai Zulaika, Aritz Bilbao-Jayo, Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana

entry.summary: Studies outcome-reward RL in a fully controlled puzzle world where small language models are trained from scratch on games from a known Bayesian player, showing RL converts pre-training hedging into reward-favored decisions but cannot reinforce actions that are never observed to succeed. Run-level success is predicted by the expected number of attempt groups containing the correct action.

entry.title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening

author.name: Jiangjie Qiu, Chengrui Xu, Xiaonan Wang

entry.summary: This study audits 13 released drug-target interaction models on 711 FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins, finding that model pairs produce completely disjoint Top-10 recommendations in 77.8% of molecule lists and 70.1% of protein lists for the same query. Apparent agreement between some systems largely reflects shared idiosyncratic preferences rather than genuine correspondence, raising concerns about benchmark validity in drug discovery.

entry.title: Physical Laws without Physics Loss? Probing Learned Dynamics in Video World Models through Forced Response

author.name: Yutao Li, Chen Wang, Wangmeng Zuo, Hui Li

entry.summary: This paper probes whether video world models learn physical laws or merely imitate motion, using nonlinear forced response experiments with dual visual-numeric conditioning adapted to six image-to-video backbones trained only with a flow-matching loss. Wan-based models predict motion accurately and generalize to unseen excitations, and tiered tests based on Taylor expansions of dynamics reveal that all six backbones reproduce linear responses including resonance, but diverge at higher-order regimes.

entry.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering

author.name: Tuna Han Salih Meral, Kaan Oktay, Alec Helbling, Atakan Kara, Duen Horng Chau, Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: The authors probe RL-tuned diffusion transformers with fixed steering vectors added to frozen base model block outputs, finding these input-independent shifts largely explain RL post-training gains: on SD3.5-M, 0.29M steering parameters (65x fewer than the RL LoRA) can match velocity predictions. This suggests RL post-training in diffusion models works primarily via representational shifting rather than complex input-dependent computation.

entry.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks

author.name: Zirui Song, Jiadong Zhang, Zheng Lu, Xiaosong Ma, Xiaojun Chang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies that hand-written success checkers in simulated manipulation benchmarks can accept incomplete executions (phantom success) or reject valid task completions (silent failure), and introduces SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits checker code against task instructions by recreating disagreement scenarios in simulation and testing policies in them.

entry.title: Streaming-AAA: Streaming AAA Game Video Generation at High Resolution, High Frame Rate, and Low Latency

author.name: Zhihao Hu, Jianqi Ma, Jun Zhang, Jiayang Bai, Haifeng Shi, Yanxiang Zhuang, Zhongqian Sun, Weidong Zhang, Wei Yang

entry.summary: Presents Streaming-AAA, a controllable infinite streaming video generation system producing 1080p gameplay video at 43 FPS with 198 ms end-to-end interaction latency on NVIDIA A800 GPUs, supporting long-horizon play without severe temporal degradation. Key designs include a redesigned VAE for efficient high-resolution generation plus additional architecture contributions. This pushes interactive game video generation close to practical gameplay requirements.

entry.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models

author.name: Jiaming Li, Lingzhen Li, Xiaze Yang, Chenyu Zhu, Kaiqi Liu, Xiaotong Zhao, Songlian Li, Toyota Li, Alan Zhao, Haobin Zhong, Yue Ma, Zhiyuan Ma

entry.summary: SpecWM is a training-free inference framework for streaming video world models that verifies draft chunks using the target model's latent velocity field, replacing external reward scoring. Verification doubles as refinement, correcting rejected drafts instead of requiring costly full regeneration.

entry.title: Posterior Matching Distillation

author.name: Hidir Yesiltepe, Julius Berner, Arash Vahdat, Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: PMD is a new distribution-based diffusion distillation method that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation, countering the mode-seeking bias of reverse-KL objectives that sacrifice sample diversity. At zero population loss, the student recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level, and its stochastic student supports flexible sampling step counts. Authors include established diffusion researchers (Berner, Vahdat).

entry.title: WAMotor: Accelerating World Action Models via Speculative Inference under Dual Nonuniform Denoising Dynamics

author.name: Zexun Lin, Yuan Feng, Xike Xie

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the denoising dynamics of flow-matching World Action Models and identifies a dual nonuniformity that breaks naive velocity-reuse assumptions in speculative inference. WAMotor exploits this analysis to accelerate multi-step denoising without task-specific draft models, reducing latency for robotic control.

entry.title: LeCompass: Task-Level Execution through State-Indexed Interfaces

author.name: Kai Shi, Shiqi Zhao, Zimo Li, Hairong Qu, Hongyu Ma, Yongsong Yang, Jiahao Ai, Ziran Yin, Peng Yin

entry.summary: LeCompass builds a task-level execution framework around a frozen latent world model (LeWM), where a proposer supplies intermediate latent targets and CompassFlow searches a learned trajectory prior for action candidates under limited evaluation budgets. It addresses the gap between local latent reachability and full task execution for action-conditioned JEPAs.

entry.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior

author.name: Shwetanshu Singh, Mark Keavney, Mathieu Duteil, Meriem Mehri, Scott Blain

entry.summary: CoMPASS is a multi-turn benchmark measuring whether conversational LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment, grounded in attachment theory with four personas and three escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency). It fills a gap left by single-turn, post hoc, or extreme-state-focused prior work in an area linked to documented fatalities.

entry.title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is

author.name: Rudransh Agnihotri, Manasvi Kapoor

entry.summary: The paper proposes RLCDR, a reference-free RL reward in which an LLM converted into a decision model answers typed questions about a response with calibrated probability distributions, debiased over option orders and calibrated with roughly a hundred labels. Training Qwen3-1.7B with GRPO on MATH raises MATH500 accuracy from 72.2 percent to 76.8 percent, matching training on ground-truth rewards.

entry.title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents

author.name: Licheng Pan, Yuzhou Chen, Zhixuan Chu, Yichen Sun, Han Zheng, Zhiyu Wang, Hao Wang, Yan Wang, Bingyu Zhu, Haiwen Hong, Longtao Huang, Kui Ren

entry.summary: DriftGuard addresses online detection of memory drift in LLM agents, where adversarial or misleading persistent memories alter execution paths. The paper identifies two challenges: content features like perplexity and retrieval relevance cannot determine causal behavioral impact, and counterfactual replay is too expensive for serving-time detection. It develops causal attribution methods that estimate each retrieved memory's contribution to potential drift efficiently.

entry.title: Self-Replicating Language Models

author.name: Arend Hintze

entry.summary: The paper empirically tests whether language models can reproduce and evolve under a Darwinian definition of life, examining replication via emitted training genomes, weight copying with mutation, and teaching offspring from self-generated samples. It finds small models can replicate and adapt to niches, but selection drives mutation rates down, and LMs can uniquely reduce their mutation rate to zero, potentially halting their own evolution.

entry.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding

author.name: Yuchen Sun, Siyuan Cheng, Shi-Zhe Chen, Yixin Qin, Jinwen Luo, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: ForeSeek is a video agent that replaces reactive clip retrieval in long-video understanding with predictive exploration: it forms visually grounded expectations about unseen temporal regions, verifies them with targeted observations, and refines its search as evidence accumulates. This addresses the core bottleneck that retrieval-driven video agents fetch clips based on local saliency without a global temporal plan.

entry.title: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits

author.name: Alexandra Yakovleva, Luat Gia Khoi Nguyen, Juho Kannala, Harri Valpola, Alexander Ilin

entry.summary: The paper proposes edit-based training: given a sampled reasoning trajectory, an editor identifies the first point of failure and proposes a minimal replacement span, and the model is trained on this localized correction. This sits between supervised fine-tuning on full trajectories, which overconstrains the output distribution, and trajectory-level RL, which gives weak credit assignment.

entry.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers

author.name: Sahibzada Allahyar, Julia White, Dhruv Atreja, George Hurn-Maloney, Urchade Zaratiana

entry.summary: Introduces GLiDE, a family of 0.4B-27B decision models that score candidate answers in a single forward pass without generating reasoning, built on Qwen hybrid language models with causal masking removed from full-attention layers. It transfers reasoning benefits via soft-target distillation from multiple teachers while retaining calibrated, confidence-aware outputs. Targets the practical trade-off between reasoning quality and inference cost.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing

author.name: Mark Lovett, Denis Lim, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: InflEns is a mixture-of-LoRA-experts method where both training data allocation and inference routing derive from the same location game in a prompt-trait space, making the intended division of labor inspectable before training. Players position themselves to maximize expected shares of the prompt distribution without using expert losses, with a theoretical criterion for when co-located experts separate. Evaluation spans seven safety-related benchmarks.

entry.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design

author.name: Minxing Chu, Quan Cheng, Anhang Li, Martins Atilla, Junyi Luo, Xinting Jiang, Ruichen Qi, Mehdi Saligane

entry.summary: ReLay recovers generator programs from existing analog circuit layouts via bidirectional layout-code translation, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing, with recurring constructions promoted into an evolving library. It also introduces the first layout-code benchmark with 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-source processes. This makes implicit designer knowledge in layout geometry reusable and machine-manipulable.

entry.title: Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning for Mammography Vision--Language Models

author.name: Zhengbo Zhou, Dooman Arefan, Shandong Wu

entry.summary: BESR connects visual token compression with diagnostic reasoning in bilateral mammography by using a bilateral-guided token selector and a bilateral reward so the model actively uses the opposite breast as a patient-specific anatomical reference. This addresses the problem that preserving salient regions alone can discard context needed for interpretation.

entry.title: Towards Autoregressive Neural Network Parameter Generation

author.name: Bedionita Soro, Bruno Andreis, Song Chong, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: This paper proposes encoding pretrained neural network parameters into a discrete domain so that the zero-shot generalization abilities of LLMs can be transferred to weight generation, addressing limits of existing weight generators in learning diverse model distributions and generalizing out of distribution. It frames autoregressive parameter generation as a route to rapid task adaptation and model synthesis.

entry.title: PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models

author.name: Zhiyang Xun, Daniel D. Johnson, Sarah Schwettmann, Neil Chowdhury

entry.summary: PosteriorBench formalizes the behavior posterior sampling problem — efficiently sampling transcripts exhibiting a rare target behavior from a language model — and provides a benchmark of 21 tasks on Qwen3.5-0.8B with behavior probabilities from 10^-5 to 10^-1 and exact posterior samples from a billion labeled responses. It compares algorithms by compute cost and forward/reverse KL to the true posterior.

entry.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction

author.name: Eduardo Due\~nez, Edgar Said Hernandez Sanchez, Edgar A. Du\'e\~nez-Guzm\'an, Suzanne Sadedin

entry.summary: The authors express published belief-propagation decoders for quantum LDPC codes in a domain-specific language and apply grammatical evolution to search over it. Reparameterizing BP+OSD and BP+LSD with damping before search yields 17-41x speedups, and evolution discovers further decoder variants for real-time quantum error correction.

entry.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space

author.name: Jiahao Hu, Jingdong Du, Yichen Zhang, Yi Song, Zhenyu Zhang, Jiaxin Niu, Ruihang Li, Xiangzhao Hao, Yiqian Zhang, Yong Huang, Zefeng Zhang, Zheyuan Gu, Shuohuan Wang

entry.summary: HiUni extends a pretrained vision-language model into a unified understanding-and-generation model with extensive parameter sharing, reusing the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both tasks and confining task-specific computation to the output side. It tackles the resulting challenges of generating pixels in a shared visual space designed for understanding.

entry.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience

author.name: EngineAI

entry.summary: EngineAI introduces Awaken-Human, a dataset pairing roughly 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion covering 100+ skills, and Awaken-HI, a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation. The model jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert, showing improved transfer from human data to robot skills. This addresses the scarcity of synchronized whole-body data for scaling humanoid learning.

entry.title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Anh Tien Nguyen, Dimitris Samaras, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: DualSAE augments standard sparse autoencoders with a plug-in Residual Branch that models the non-semantic information a Sparse Branch omits, thereby decoupling reconstruction fidelity from interpretability objectives that a single sparse representation currently conflates. This modular design aims to make SAE features more reliably interpretable for mechanistic interpretability research.

entry.title: Disentangling Monitor Hardware Artifacts and Smoothing Lag for Shift-Robust Intraoperative EEG and Hemodynamic Risk Calibration

author.name: Zeyu Jia

entry.summary: Develops causal signal-conditioning filters and shift-robust conformal calibration for intraoperative EEG and blood pressure monitors, removing hardware artifacts like impedance pulses, DC drift, and cuff holds across 5,439 anesthesia procedures. This improves risk forecasting reliability under real clinical measurement shifts.

entry.title: FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Zekun Wang, Yizhuo Wang

entry.summary: Presents FrontierReplay, a prefix caching system for hybrid attention-recurrent language models that materializes exact checkpoints at predictable structural boundaries (turn ends, branch points) without cutting the prefill forward pass. This avoids the scheduler overhead that negates reuse gains in existing fine-grained exact caches.

entry.title: SKILL.PNG: Learning Agent Skills in Pixel Space

author.name: Maximilian Seeth, Chengzhi Martin Hu, Marie Kempkes, Paul R\"ottger, Leo Schwinn

entry.summary: Skill.png introduces skill-like image inputs for vision-language model agents whose pixels are optimized by gradient descent through a frozen VLM's vision encoder, bridging the gap between discrete natural-language skills (not gradient-optimizable) and model-specific finetuning. Image skills transfer across VLMs, and a single image can be jointly optimized for an ensemble of models.

entry.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: \'Elodie C\^ot\'e-Gauthier, Doina Precup, Isabeau Pr\'emont-Schwarz

entry.summary: Building on the identification of entorhinal grid cells with eigenvectors of the successor representation, this paper constructs a successor-feature basis from eigenvectors of a fixed reference policy's transition matrix. This yields successor features expressible as closed-form linear combinations of base features at the same state-action pair, providing a reusable basis for continual reinforcement learning across changing tasks.

entry.title: Causal Discovery with False Positive Error Control

author.name: Erik Jahn, Venkat Chandrasekaran, Frederick Eberhardt, Leonard Schulman

entry.summary: The paper introduces the m-conservative PC algorithm for causal discovery, proving it controls false discovery rate in the linear Gaussian setting under an extremely weak version of the faithfulness assumption. This addresses the fact that false positive causal claims can be more consequential than false negatives, while existing error guarantees are typically asymptotic or require strong assumptions.

entry.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming

author.name: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang, Zhijian Liu, Song Han, Qinghao Hu

entry.summary: TideCache is a serving system for hybrid-attention LLMs on CPU-GPU superchips, featuring a Transparent Cache Pool that redistributes physical pages behind fixed virtual addresses and a Cache Streamer that prefetches global-attention prefixes during bounded-state layer computation intervals. This addresses the heterogeneous cache demands that hybrid architectures introduce for KV and state management.

entry.title: Rubric Semantics or Numerical Priors? Auditing Scale-Direction Bias in LLM Judges

author.name: Chanwoo Kim, Doyun Kim, Minsoo Song, Sihyeon Lee, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: This work introduces semantic faithfulness, the principle that semantically equivalent rubrics should yield consistent LLM-judge scores, and a scale-reversal probe that inverts score anchors without changing criteria. Experiments across five meta-evaluation benchmarks and seven judges show systematic bias from numeric scale direction, with a floor-normalization method enabling fair cross-model comparison.

entry.title: dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement

author.name: Handa Li, Pengxiang Li, Mingyu Cao, Xilu Wang, Li Shen, Da Li, Lu Yin

entry.summary: dLoop restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a recurrent, looped architecture so that prompt, committed-token, and uncommitted-position information can be fully integrated before commitment decisions, addressing under-refined predictions in a single denoising pass. This recurrent latent refinement aims to reduce the number of denoising steps needed for parallel generation.

entry.title: What a Calibrated Probability Hides: Belief-Level Post-Training for Decision Models

author.name: Xinye Li, Zirui Song, Huaxing Liu, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Zixiang Xu, Yinjun Liu, Zhewen Zhang, Xiaojun Chang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: The paper observes that a calibrated decision model's pooled prediction conflates interpersonal disagreement, which requires identifying whose perspective applies, with genuine uncertainty, which requires more evidence. It introduces Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization (BGPO), where the policy proposes a list of beliefs with estimated prevalence and per-belief choice distributions, trained via Bayesian estimation of belief likelihoods.

entry.title: SceneAnything: Agentic Reconstruction of Large-Scale Mesh Scenes from a Single Video

author.name: Bowen Xue, Saeed Hadadan, Fabrice Rousselle, Zahra Montazeri, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Milos Hasan

entry.summary: SceneAnything is an agentic system that reconstructs editable mesh scenes from real or generated videos via a software harness coordinating agents, pretrained vision models, and graphics tools under an explicit reconstruction protocol; author agents write parameterized Blender programs grounded by shared camera, depth, and segmentation estimates. Paired with video generation, it enables text-to-scene construction.

entry.title: Lossless Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Tongda Xu, Yu Zhang, Jun Hu, Huijuan Huang

entry.summary: LLDM enables pixel-exact reconstruction in latent diffusion by constructing a lossless transformation, using residual latent transformation and uneven latent scaling, that maps pixels into a latent space more amenable to diffusion modeling rather than modifying the diffusion architecture. A proposed semantic rank priority metric explains its effectiveness, and it substantially outperforms pixel-space alternatives.

entry.title: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models

author.name: Dong An, Tianyu Liu, Haoran Ding, Wen Yang, Anqing Duan, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric P. Xing, Guangyi Liu

entry.summary: Identifies a conditioning weakness in robotic world models: actions or robot renderings specify where the robot goes but not how the scene responds, causing manipulated objects to collapse or move inconsistently. The authors separate dynamics prediction from visual rendering, using 3D point dynamics as an intermediary: the first frame is lifted to 3D points, a learned point dynamics model simulates their response to robot motion, and the video model renders appearance. Includes Eric P. Xing among the authors.

entry.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification

author.name: Yekai Shen, Yuqian Wang, Zishun Liao, Rongsheng Wang, Wenting Chen, S. Kevin Zhou, Qingsong Yao

entry.summary: CALIFUSE fuses multiple pathology foundation models for uncertainty estimation, treating disagreement between encoders as an explicit confidence cue rather than optimizing for accuracy alone. It combines slide-level decision consensus with chunk-level evidence agreement measured via Jensen-Shannon divergence for calibrated whole-slide image classification.

entry.title: MixReact: Physics-Based Reactive Humanoid Control from Multimodal Cues via a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers

author.name: Bin Li, Xing Zhu, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: MixReact is presented as the first unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control driven jointly by text, audio, and video cues. It combines a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers for state prediction with a History-aware Action Transformer for physically executable execution, addressing kinematic-only artifacts in prior work.

entry.title: SGAR: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction via Sparse Geometry-Guided Attention

author.name: Aoxiang Fan, Maria Pilligua, Corentin Dumery, Oliver Heinimann, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: SGAR argues that dense global attention in feed-forward 3D reconstruction models is largely unnecessary, since 3D structure comes from geometrically matching regions across views. Each patch token attends only to a small learned subset of tokens from other views, cutting the quadratic cost of dense attention and enabling larger-scale reconstruction. The result connects classical structure-from-motion intuition with modern learned reconstruction.

entry.title: Differentiable Hydrodynamics for Whole-Body MPC of Underwater Robots

author.name: Hefan Wang, Yvan Petillot, Carlos Mastalli

entry.summary: The paper presents a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model combining spherical-harmonic force fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from CFD, enabling whole-body MPC of underwater vehicle-manipulator systems in real time. This coordinates thrusters and joint motors to extend workspace without expensive online CFD evaluation.

entry.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own

author.name: Shibo Zhou, Tianqi Hong, Zheng Yan, He Yang

entry.summary: JARVIS is an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes the design-fabricate-test loop for circuit boards, scanning its workspace with a robot-mounted 3D scanner, building a digital twin for rehearsal, and coordinating a robot arm, PCB printer, and pick-and-place machine from a single text instruction. Demonstrated on unmodified desktop equipment, it verifies fabricated boards against circuit behavior.

entry.title: Frontier Clock: Tracking the US-China AI Gap

author.name: Jaisen Soundar

entry.summary: Introduces Frontier Clock, a benchmark that assigns each released model a frontier-equivalent date (when the world's best model last had that capability level), using Epoch AI's ECI data to track the US-China frontier gap over time. The author finds the US-China gap has grown by roughly 2.4 months per year since DeepSeek R1, counter to popular perceptions of rapid Chinese catch-up.

entry.title: Study reveals data centers’ long-distance damage to air quality

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers built a modeling framework tracing how data center electricity demand propagates through the US power grid to emissions at distant power plants, combined with atmospheric modeling of particulate formation. They estimate 2023 data center electricity demand caused roughly 650 premature deaths nationally, with disproportionate per-capita harm in Midwestern states far from the Virginia and Texas facility concentrations.

entry.title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks

author.name: Jiayi Chen, Lizhe Chen, Yujia Chen, Shihan Dou, Ming Zhang, Chendi Ge, Shiguang Ni, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang, Maxm Pan

entry.summary: CompAct-Bench evaluates how well LLMs compress accumulated working context in long-horizon agent tasks by measuring downstream task completion. Starting from successful trajectories, it inserts compaction boundaries at different execution stages, compresses preceding context with the model under evaluation, and lets the same executor continue. This fills a real measurement gap for context compaction, an increasingly critical capability for long-running agents.

entry.title: Meta-RTL: Evolving Agent Harnesses for RTL Optimization

author.name: Xinzhuang Xiong, Yonghao Wang, Shengyao Sun, Chengxi Li, Evangeline Young

entry.summary: Meta-RTL uses LLM-driven evolution of agent harnesses for hardware RTL optimization with EDA feedback, evolving the search procedure itself while keeping the model, EDA flow, and budgets fixed. Compared to Dr. RTL, the evolved Meta-RTL* cuts aggregate WNS/TNS violations substantially on development designs and transfers to unseen designs with double-digit improvements plus area reductions.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training

author.name: Haotian Zhai, Leqi Liu

entry.summary: DFRL is a framework for post-training LLM predictors using negative downstream decision regret as reward, so models learn to minimize the costs of decisions induced by their predictions rather than maximize raw prediction accuracy. It requires no downstream convexity or differentiability and integrates into existing RL post-training pipelines.

entry.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark

author.name: Zhenling Chen, Zhiguo Zeng, Anne Barros

entry.summary: The paper introduces NextUnit-Bench, a deployment-style benchmark of 24 public prognostics and health management datasets split into 58 folds, where LLM coding agents have two hours to build an executable predictor that must generalize to held-out equipment. Frontier agents substantially outperform AutoML and faithful reimplementations of published methods, supporting the thesis that generality should reside in the modeling agent rather than individual models.

entry.title: Iterative Scarcity-Guided Exploration: Bootstrapping Generative Auto-bidding from Narrow Support

author.name: Qingmao Yao, Guangzheng Hu, Yusen Huo, Zhilin Zhang, Chuan Yu, Jian Xu, Xu Chu, Bo Zheng, Xiaotie Deng

entry.summary: Identifies SNR collapse as the theoretical cause of stagnation in iterative diffusion-based auto-bidding (AIGB) training from narrow cold-start data, and proposes ISGE, a guidance handoff mechanism that maintains extrapolation as the return signal weakens. Authored by an Alibaba-style industrial team working on deployed advertising systems.

entry.title: Sequential Anytime Valid Tests for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment

author.name: Vishesh Kumar Singh, Sayak Ray Chowdhury
