entry.summary: ScaleDiag is a controlled diagnostic framework that independently isolates the effects of visual scaling, instruction scaling, and sampling scaling on GUI grounding by varying target scale, context, instruction information, and candidate coverage. Evaluated across five benchmarks and up to eight model variants, it clarifies where each test-time scaling strategy saturates.

entry.title: Multi-View Relighting with Mergeable Radiance Fields

author.name: Yinan Wang, Rohan Kadkol, Hyunjin Yoo, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lalonde, James J. Clark

entry.summary: MergeableRF enables radiance-field relighting by directly merging parameters of radiance fields trained under known basis lights, exploiting the linearity of light transport. It uses shared geometry with per-light appearance networks from a shared initialization plus merge-aware regularization so that parameter combinations produce the corresponding image combinations.

entry.title: TRACE: Attribute Execution for Sequential Image Editing

author.name: Xiyang Zhang, Yuanhe Tian, Hongzhi Wang, Yan Song

entry.summary: Addresses sequential image editing where each new instruction must be satisfied while preserving still-active earlier requirements, separating continuing attributes from their visual carriers and prioritizing local appearance operations under complete-request checks. Active-goal binding resolves conflicts when a retrieved image contains a valid attribute on an obsolete surface. This targets state-tracking failures that plague iterative editing with current generative models.

entry.title: Less Than Meets the Eye: Action-Set Identifiability and Principled Abstention for 3D Physical Geometry

author.name: Reshad Ul Karim, Abrar Samin, Sammam Mahdi, Syeda Maliha Tabassum, Md Rashad Al Hasan Rony

entry.summary: Investigates whether bounded camera motions can distinguish physically distinct 3D geometry explanations that look identical from a viewpoint, such as a corridor versus its mirror reflection or a display image. Intervene3D predicts views under each hypothesis and candidate motion, selects maximin-separating motions, and abstains when available motions cannot separate remaining hypotheses. On matched synthetic benchmarks, disabling abstention yields confident answers on 76.4% of unresolvable scenes while abstention eliminates such overconfidence.

entry.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish

author.name: Ahmet Tu\u{g}rul Bayrak, Fatma Nur Korkmaz, Mustafa Serta\c{c} T\"urkel, Nur Ya\u{g}mur Tuncer

entry.summary: The study examines end-of-turn detection for voice agents using turn ends and turn-internal pauses from the Real-TurnTurk corpus of Turkish dyadic video calls, comparing a fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT, a zero-shot Turkish LM, and a deployed multilingual detector alongside voice-activity timing and facial features. The fine-tuned model best separates turn ends from pauses and is best calibrated under recording- and speaker-disjoint evaluation.

entry.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing

author.name: Tianren Li, Dongbo Li, Hongkai Chen, Jie Liu, Guoliang Xing

entry.summary: AeroBelief treats the next executable action as the unit of verification in aerial sensing, grouping candidate views by first action and selectively querying a structured world model under calibrated group bounds. Across 40 worlds and 960 closed-loop executions, it completes 75.42% of tasks, outperforming exhaustive world-model scoring (73.33%) and line-of-sight baselines (65.83%). This demonstrates selective verification can beat brute-force approaches under budget constraints.

entry.title: Efficient Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language Model via Dynamics-Aware Quantization and Distillation

author.name: Yanjing Li, Sheng Xu, Baochang Zhang, Xianbin Cao, Yawei Li

entry.summary: This paper tackles efficient latent chain-of-thought reasoning in vision-language models by lowering numerical precision of full-precision latent-CoT models, which otherwise incur large storage and compute costs. The authors analyze sensitivity and direction-dependent effects of continuous-thought errors and propose a dynamics-aware quantization and distillation approach preserving information retrieval and downstream reasoning rather than mere reconstruction. It targets severe accuracy degradation seen with direct 4-bit quantization.

entry.title: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing

author.name: Nina Goncharova, Alexandra Ivanova, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: The paper improves prompt-driven image editing in rectified-flow models like FLUX by spatially gating source-feature injection with adaptive masks and using REINFORCE to select which transformer blocks perform injection under different preservation-versus-editability objectives. On PIE-Bench with FLUX.1-dev, the approach better controls the alignment-preservation trade-off and requires no online search at inference.

entry.title: Studying AI Act Mentions: A first look at the impact of the European Union's AI regulation on Hugging Face

author.name: Anamaria Mojica-Hanke, Tessi Aigbovbiosa-Igbinovia, Steffen Herbold

entry.summary: An empirical study of how AI practitioners respond to the EU AI Act, analyzing over five million Hugging Face records (model cards, discussions, commits) for explicit references to the regulation. It provides a first large-scale look at whether and how regulatory obligations surface in public AI artifact sharing since the Act's staged obligations took effect.

entry.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: K. R. Jayaram, Vatche Isahagian, Aswath Vaithinathan Aravindan, Vinod Muthusamy, Punleuk Oum, Gaodan Fang, Michal Ulewicz, Gegi Thomas, Evelyn Duesterwald

entry.summary: Drawing on an IBM-deployed pipeline, the authors describe an agent that mines short lessons from its own trajectories and consolidates them into a smaller set of guidelines injected at inference, shipped in the open-source altk-evolve library and used in IBM's CUGA agent and watsonx Orchestrate. The paper reports deployment lessons about what agents should remember and how memory size affects performance.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces

author.name: Andrew Kang

entry.summary: Introduces Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS), which models corner kicks and lofted free kicks as distributions over plausible executions and futures rather than single realized events, using a world model with 3D ball physics, generative player models, and a value model to score counterfactual deliveries and setups. Evaluated on 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches. This brings decision-making and search techniques from games into sports analytics with counterfactual evaluation.

entry.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences

author.name: Ivan Kuznetsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin, Sonja H\"anzelmann, Fabian Wachsmann, Jonas S{\o}lvsteen, Daniel Wiesmann, Thomas Jung, Nikolay Koldunov

entry.summary: This position paper argues that FAIR data principles are insufficient for autonomous AI agents in Earth sciences, since data curated for expert researchers can mislead a machine acting alone. It proposes AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled) as an agent-specific requirements layer extending FAIR, within an agenda of bounded tools and layered validation. The paper outlines a staged, measurable adoption path to reduce silent errors.

entry.title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation

author.name: Oankar R. Patil, May D. Wang

entry.summary: SEANA addresses a representational shortcut in self-supervised learning on noisy scientific imaging (e.g., microscopy): since both augmented views come from the same noisy image, encoders can agree by encoding noise instead of semantics. The module learns an invertible variance-stabilizing transform from noisy data, estimates the clean signal, and regenerates noise-aligned views without requiring knowledge of the noise model. It is a drop-in improvement for SSL in signal-dependent noise regimes.

entry.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation

author.name: Bochen Han, Anshu Xiong, Mingyang Ma

entry.summary: This paper abstracts a four-stage workflow shared by argumentation-augmented LLM decision-making methods and systematically studies design choices for argument construction, evaluation, and incorporation across debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact-verification tasks. Notably, it finds existing argumentation methods do not consistently improve performance with recent LLMs, motivating two task-specific methods. It provides a useful sobering assessment of a popular reasoning-augmentation direction.

entry.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins

author.name: Younghwan Joo, Jeonghoon Han, Sanghyun Oh, Soosik Bang, Sung-il Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes a four-level protocol for validating LLM-written declarative specifications for HVAC digital twins, testing static validity, model build, simulation convergence, and physical correctness rather than stopping at parse success or textual similarity. It matters because physically wrong but executable specifications currently pass existing evaluation standards.

entry.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair

author.name: Jingyi Zhou, Yi Liu, Bin Sun, Hongji Zhang, Dongsheng Zuo, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: GRODE-RTL tackles LLM-based repair of Register-Transfer Level hardware code by extracting the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, mapping it back to editable source lines, and organizing it into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. This anchor-centric representation helps standard LLMs localize non-local faults that flat token sequences obscure.

entry.title: Many Solutions, One Answer: Search Order Shapes the Default Solutions of Language Models

author.name: Qinhan Hou, Jing Tang

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that when constraint puzzles have multiple valid answers, language models concentrate on one shared default solution far beyond uniform chance. Comparing name-order versus fewest-candidates-first search strategies, the authors find that search-order dynamics best explain which default solution models output across four open-weight models.

entry.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)

author.name: Natasha E Blycha, James Myint, Chen Feng, Dr Amani Soysa, Koshin Jama, Schellie-Jayne Price, Matthew Blycha

entry.summary: This position paper argues that protocol maturity in agent communication standards such as MCP and Agent2Agent does not produce legal legibility, since runtime enforcement constrains resources rather than legal authority. It proposes AULA, an architecture aiming to map autonomous agent activity onto legal personhood, rights and liabilities.

entry.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology

author.name: Esha Sadia Nasir, Jiaqi Lv, Gozde N. Gunesli, Shan E Ahmed Raza

entry.summary: C-LiTE is a lightweight cell-level foundation model for computational pathology that learns cellular features directly, avoiding the costly upsampling of small cellular crops that ViTs require. It addresses the gap between tissue-level pathology foundation models, which capture cell morphology only implicitly, and expensive cell-level models with hundreds of millions of parameters. This enables efficient tumour grading, mitotic assessment, and immune profiling.

entry.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yuzhi Huang, Jie Wu, Fanding Huang, Junchao Lin, Weichen Zhang, Ziyi Xiong, Yang Li, Zhengwei Xie, Zhimin Wang, Zhen Liu, Jiazhen Huang, Yuzheng Zhang, Yuche Liu, Hongyi Yang, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang, Hakan Aktas, Adam Wu, Duo Wu, Kangye Ji, Shuzhao Xie, Huanan Liu, Weijue Bu, Chenxin Li, Xinyuan Wang, Tianyi Bai, Yinan Mao, Jiawei Wang, Minglei Li, Heng Yu, Ehsan Adeli, Minchen Li, Yong-Lu Li, Cengiz \"Oztireli, Huazhe Xu, Chao Yu, Jing Zhang, Shanghang Zhang, Weitao Zhou, Wenwu Zhu, Cheng Chi, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks across five real-world domains, each with three difficulty levels and two scene settings, designed to separately assess history-based cognitive reasoning, precise physical execution, and their composition through environmental feedback. Existing benchmarks conflate these capabilities, obscuring the source of failures. The large multi-institution author list spans many robotics groups.

entry.title: Long-Range Video Presentation Attack Detection: A Three-Class Benchmark Across 1-100 m and Two Sensor Types

author.name: Lambert Igene, Mohammad Zahir Uddin Chowdhury, Afzal Hossain, Sandip Purnapatra, Peter Johnson, Stephanie Schuckers

entry.summary: The authors release a large video face presentation-attack-detection benchmark with 374,000+ frames from 261 identities captured at standoff distances from 1 to 100 meters, indoors and outdoors, on DSLR and mobile sensors, with live/spoof/props labels. It addresses the unrealistic close-range assumption of deployed face PAD systems used in border control and surveillance.

entry.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Huixin Zhan, Jason H. Moore

entry.summary: The authors propose an uncertainty-conditioned path-energy framework that converts genomic foundation model variant predictions and calibrated uncertainty into explicit probability distributions over gene-disease-phenotype hypotheses on a knowledge graph. Query uncertainty controls the temperature of the target distribution, making evidence quality an explicit determinant of hypothesis breadth while retaining interpretable multi-patient reasoning without phenotype supervision.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing

author.name: Ishita Asnani, Shaghayegh Fazliani, Zachary Ryan, Kriyoshig Prasai, Chirag Kumar, Indra Gonzalez Ojeda, Marc Lipsitch, Madeleine Udell

entry.summary: Epira is a protocol-controlled LLM interviewer for multi-disease case investigation and contact tracing, pairing LLM dialogue with a rule-based controller that enforces required questions, safety handoffs, and structured case records, adaptable to new diseases via questionnaire upload. It was evaluated with simulated cases using local (Qwen2.5) and cloud backends, and the cloud backend comparison uses GPT-5.4, an established OpenAI model rather than a new release.

entry.title: NIMIS: A Structure-Agnostic, Chemically Informed Slot-Attention Framework for Demixing 1D $^1$H-NMR Mixture Spectra

author.name: Anna Marija Sumrova, Jonathan M. Goodman

entry.summary: NIMIS is a deep learning framework that unmixes 1D proton NMR mixture spectra by grouping peaks according to their source molecule without requiring knowledge of component structures. It injects J-coupling information into a multi-head Transformer attention mechanism and uses slot attention to separate contextualized peak embeddings, trained on over 158,000 synthetic mixtures. This enables direct analysis of crude reaction mixtures, accelerating chemical reaction analysis.

entry.title: X Hedging: towards an eXplainable artificial intelligence option Hedging framework

author.name: Bj{\o}rn Andr\'e Aaslund, Johannes Berge, Ayoub Haida, Ying Ni, Rita Pimentel

entry.summary: Proposes X Hedging, replacing neural networks in the Deep Hedging framework with LightGBM tree ensembles for option hedging, reducing data requirements and improving interpretability while retaining strong hedging performance. Integrates explanation tooling into the hedging pipeline for more user-centered transparency.

entry.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for a Universal Fluid Gibbs Free Energy Equation of State

author.name: Xurui Li, Zhiguo Gan, Jiaming Zhang, Hongxi Zeng, Diannan Lu

entry.summary: The authors construct GEoS, a thermodynamically consistent neural network framework built on Gibbs free energy that provides a unified machine learning representation of fluid states. It achieves average absolute relative deviations of 5.25% and 3.96% on vapor and liquid phase density test sets, outperforming conventional volume-translated cubic equations of state.

entry.title: Variance-Adaptive Upper Confidence Bounds for Multi-Armed Bandits with Kaplan--Meier Survival Estimation

author.name: Yangfan Cui, Andrew Papanicolaou

entry.summary: The paper proposes KM-UCB, a multi-armed bandit policy for settings where rewards are survival probabilities at a time horizon and observations are right-censored time-to-event data. Using martingale theory and continuous influence functions, it derives a variance-adaptive empirical Bernstein bound that improves on prior Hoeffding-type Kaplan-Meier bounds.

entry.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?

author.name: Myeong-Su Lee

entry.summary: The paper provides a mathematical explanation for when and why integral constraints improve physics-informed neural networks, deriving stability estimates for losses with and without such constraints across several PDEs. It shows that in certain parameter regimes the standard loss weakly controls specific error components and integral constraints restore uniform control, with numerical experiments supporting the analysis.

entry.title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction

author.name: Changzhi Ai, Frank Abild-Pedersen, Johannes Voss

entry.summary: AdsNet is an equivariant graph neural network that predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass using a local graph restricted to the adsorbate and immediate surface neighbors. The local formulation decouples cost from total system size while retaining geometric sensitivity, targeting high-throughput computational catalyst screening.

entry.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries

author.name: Niklas Houba, Giovanni Giarda, Davide Piras

entry.summary: SlotFlow-GB is a neural framework for LISA gravitational-wave data analysis that learns an approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior over the number and parameters of overlapping Galactic binaries, producing source multiplicity probabilities and per-source parameter densities in a single evaluation. This addresses a computationally demanding inference problem expected to involve millions of long-lived signals.

entry.title: Conformal Selection for Hierarchical Streaming Data

author.name: Zhenyuan Sun, Chengyao Yu, Ruixing Ming, Bingyi Jing

entry.summary: The paper extends online conformal selection to hierarchical data streams where candidates arrive sequentially from distinct populations, relaxing the standard i.i.d./exchangeability assumption. The proposed Online Hierarchical Selection method provides distribution-free, statistically valid candidate selection with sequentially constructed test statistics.

entry.title: ChronoDossier: Long-Form Personas as Temporal Memory Representations

author.name: Noah Sturgill, Jinho D. Choi

entry.summary: ChronoDossier is a benchmark of 311 synthetic long-form persona dossiers (1k-10k words) that treat personas as temporal memory representations, comprising an invariant identity plus a timeline of facts, routines, and decision rules. Intrinsic metrics score records against intended states and extrinsic metrics test fact recovery by five readers on a seeded GPT-5.1 panel with 520 rated turns per condition.

entry.title: TableRoute: Capability-Aware Routing for Scalable Table Question Answering

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi

entry.summary: TableRoute is a capability-aware routing framework for table question answering that selects among full-table reading, table reduction, and program execution based on table scale and model capability, using evidence-conditioned inference. This addresses brittleness of fixed strategies across compact to million-token tables.

entry.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management

author.name: Xuyang Liu, Chenwen Lu, Junxi Wang, Siyu Ren, Xinying Lin, Siteng Huang, Hongli Sun, Linfeng Zhang, Honggang Chen

entry.summary: MemFolder is a structure-guided memory folding framework for long-running agents that sequentially reduces both record count and retrieved context length by using cross-record structure to guide evidence selection and consolidation. It avoids the failure modes of pure pruning (losing evidence) and pure consolidation (longer retrieval units).

entry.title: CoRelate: Coordinated Human-Object Motion Synthesis through Interaction Relations

author.name: Zhiwen Qiu, Daisy Lin, Diyu Zhou, Jialin Wu, Rosita Ji, Saleh Kalantari

entry.summary: CoRelate is a diffusion framework for coordinated human-object motion synthesis that represents intended participation through hand-part relations specifying the participating hand, its reference position, and participation interval. These relations serve both as generation conditions and as references for measuring interaction realization, with task feedback ensuring contact is maintained while object goals are reached.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Image Manipulation Localization Under Multi-Type Weak Supervision

author.name: Songlin Li, Hui Ma, Zhiqing Guo, Dan Ma, Gaobo Yang, Xin Liao

entry.summary: UniIML is a teacher-student framework that unifies diverse weak annotations for image manipulation localization by mapping them into a common representation that guides SAM to generate candidate masks, with an Ordinal Safe Consensus mechanism to select the best candidate. This enables joint training on heterogeneous annotation types and larger datasets.

entry.title: SegAnyFruit: Learning Generalizable and Edge Deployable Fruit Instance Segmentation at Scale

author.name: Yanan Wang, Yuzheng wang, Yibin Ying, Zhenghao Fei

entry.summary: SegAnyFruit distills foundation-model priors into lightweight, prompt-free fruit segmentation models via a progressive training regime over a curated 733K-image, 9.66M-mask dataset spanning 165 fruit types. Zero-shot results improve substantially over prior work across seven benchmarks while remaining edge-deployable.

entry.title: Characterizing Age-Conditioned Affective Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shahriyar Zaman Ridoy, Azmine Toushik Wasi, Lin Gu, Ruogu Fang

entry.summary: Evaluates 17 vision-language models on 900 OASIS images with young, middle, and older-adult persona prompts, comparing model emotion ratings against data from 822 human participants. While unprompted models track average human valence well (median r=0.891), the age-conditioned shifts do not correlate with actual human age differences, revealing that VLMs perform age perspective-taking superficially. Findings are clearest on sensitive images, with fairness implications.

entry.title: Calibrate in Context: Efficient Data-Free Quantization from Small Synthetic Pools

author.name: Haowen Hua, Sen Lin, Yaokun Huang, Zeyi Shao, Hao Zhang, Wei Sui, John See, Zeyd Boukhers, Cong Yang

entry.summary: Improves data-free low-bit quantization by calibrating activation scales and integer offsets against full-precision responses in the student's block context, evaluating candidates only at consuming operators at near-local scoring cost. Progressive inversion updates the same synthetic images through increasingly deep teacher prefixes for ViT-family models. With only 1,000 images the pipeline exceeds MimiQ's accuracy across 18 W4A4/W5A5 settings, addressing data-scarce quantization for transformers.

entry.title: GeoPillars: A Large-Kernel Pillar Detector for Single-Sweep LiDAR Under Point Sparsity, and a Decomposition of Its Gain

author.name: Chaitanya Dumbre, Shubham Sarkar, Akash Mohapatra, Ghanasham Patil, Sheetal Girase

entry.summary: GeoPillars is a pillar-based 3D detector designed for single-sweep LiDAR under extreme sparsity (eight points per pillar), combining geometric pillar features, grouped vector attention, a large-kernel backbone, and surface-normal supervision. It outperforms CenterPoint by over 13 BEV AP points at the same input budget, and notably the paper includes an honest ablation decomposition showing its gains are in-distribution, since validation is per-frame rather than scene-disjoint.

entry.title: TrajCal: Trajectory-Calibrated Time Schedules for Few-Step Flow Sampling

author.name: Junchi Zhang, Zihan Gu, Jiangcan Jia, Lulu Zhao, Wenbo Su, Hua Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TrajCal, a training-free calibration framework for few-step flow matching sampling that uses scatter search, a metaheuristic optimization method, to find a fixed time schedule achieving higher output fidelity. Starting from diverse seed schedules, it deforms and combines candidates and selects one fixed schedule by final output fidelity for reuse on new inputs. It improves reference agreement over baselines at low evaluation budgets for both image and video generation.

entry.title: Fast Self-Supervised Generative CT Denoising via Few-Step Sampling

author.name: Xingyi Yao, Zhengtao Ma, Zhennong Chen

entry.summary: N2N-iMF combines Noise2Noise self-supervised training with improved mean flow for few-step CT denoising, generating one noisy image conditioned on its pair and averaging independent samples to suppress noise without oversmoothing. This avoids costly multi-step diffusion sampling where clean references are unavailable.

entry.title: FFGaussType: Feed-Forward Conversion of Glyph and SVG Geometry into Compact Gaussian Assets

author.name: Haoan Feng, Tianfu Wang, Peimeng Guan, Dae Yeol Lee, Guan-ming Su

entry.summary: FFGaussType converts extruded glyph and SVG outlines into Gaussian-splatting assets in a single forward pass, enabling text and icons to be embedded as 3D elements inside Gaussian scenes with correct occlusion, perspective, and lighting. A shared decoder predicts neural Gaussians with surface normals from a feature plane, removing the need for per-glyph iterative optimization. This addresses a scalability bottleneck for adding graphic elements to immersive 3D content.

entry.title: A Synthetic Multi-Modal Testbed for Security Stress Testing of Agentic Counter-UAS Systems

author.name: Ivan A. Fernandez, Jingdao Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System testbed built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking pipelines under degraded or manipulated sensor data. It generates synchronized RGB, LiDAR, and IR-like observations with controllable range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability.

entry.title: Design and Validation of a Telescopic Chassis-Assisted Stair-Climbing Mechanism for Powered Wheelchairs

author.name: Yasuhiro Fukuoka, Haruya Shirado, Yuto Nakamura, Haruto Okabe, Ahmad Najmuddin Ibrahim, Takahiro Fukui

entry.summary: The authors design and validate a stair-climbing mechanism for powered wheelchairs using an auxiliary telescopic chassis actuator that keeps front or rear wheels stationary during ascent, reduces required force and slip risk, and improves level-ground mobility via adjustable wheelbase. The mechanism prioritizes safety and simplicity.

entry.title: Close&Safe: Maximal Task Preservation for Redundant Manipulators via C-Space Boundary Detour

author.name: Abhigyan Singh, Manthan Goyal, Fares Abu-Dakka, Ravi Prakash

entry.summary: Close&Safe decouples trajectory tracking from obstacle avoidance for contact-rich manipulation: the nominal end-effector trajectory is followed exactly wherever feasible, and avoidance is applied only on obstructed intervals via configuration-space boundary detour sampling. This maximally preserves unobstructed portions of tasks like wiping or polishing that conventional planners would unnecessarily perturb.

entry.title: Could Model Councils Reduce Misalignment Risk from RSI?

author.name: Skye

entry.summary: Explores whether having multiple AI models review each other during recursive self-improvement could reduce the risk of a misaligned AI designing successors aligned to itself rather than to humans, using the AI 2027 scenario as a motivating example. It engages with evidence that frontier labs increasingly automate AI R&D experiments.

entry.title: Does most AI x-risk come from mostly-aligned models?

author.name: RohanS

entry.summary: The author proposes three cruxy claims for threat modeling: current AIs are mostly well-behaved, this will persist through early superintelligence, and yet misalignment x-risk remains >10% likely because catastrophic behavior on a tiny minority of inputs suffices. Commentary from Constellation researchers is included, making it a structured discussion of an important threat-model question.

entry.title: LATER: Learning Action-Conditioned Temporal Evidence Retrieval for Predictive World Models

author.name: Zihan Zhou, Wenxi Xu, Qilin Wang, Hao Tang

entry.summary: LATER is an action-conditioned world model built on CF-JEPA that stores completed real transitions in fixed partitioned memories, queried via a response bridge using current state and candidate actions, with multi-cut auxiliary supervision. Inspired by working-memory retention and selective readout, it captures physical properties visible only in early interactions. On distracted Two-Stage PushT, it raises terminal success from 15.5% to 25.0% over reconstructed CF-JEPA.

entry.title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets

author.name: Anxo Perez, Jorge Gab\'in, Javier Parapar

entry.summary: Studies in-context learning under fixed token budgets, asking whether the budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or many short ones in question answering, using length-binned demonstration pools. It reframes prompt construction as a resource-allocation problem with direct cost and latency implications. Provides practical guidance for prompt engineering in cost-sensitive deployments.

entry.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics

author.name: Ahmad Hussein, Ali Anaissi, Mukesh Prasad, Ali Braytee

entry.summary: HIT-Fuse integrates six modalities of molecular and pathology data across four TCGA cancer cohorts using modality-specific autoencoders and two-stage CP tensor decomposition, with missing latent modalities reconstructed from clinical covariates. It targets precision oncology with an emphasis on biologically grounded interpretability and robustness to missing modalities.

entry.title: DARSY: A Tool for Data-Driven Abstraction and Policy Synthesis for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Dynamics

author.name: Thom Badings, Ibon Gracia, Mahdi Nazeri, Morteza Lahijanian, Alessandro Abate

entry.summary: DARSY is an automated software tool that builds finite interval Markov decision process abstractions from simulator samples of stochastic systems with unknown dynamics, requiring only a simulator and a Lipschitz bound. Robust dynamic programming then yields policies with certified lower bounds on the probability of satisfying specifications.

entry.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration

author.name: Weiyu Zhou, Jiacong Tang, Tao Hu, Axi Niu, Jinqiu Sun, Peng Wu, Wei Dong, Qingsen Yan

entry.summary: RegionAgent trains a vision-language model via two-stage preference learning to select region-specific restoration actions iteratively, addressing non-uniform coupled degradations that global methods handle poorly. The agentic framework accounts for how earlier restoration actions alter residual degradation for subsequent steps.

entry.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Kai Lu, Chenyang Ma, Ioannis Havoutis

entry.summary: PGX is a framework that decomposes long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation into three layers, offloading temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components (including a predicate-based state machine with physical gating) so the VLA model can focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstrations with online execution, recovery, and coordination of navigation and waiting. This targets VLA weakness on temporally extended, precision-critical tasks.

entry.title: Bayesian $\kappa$-Explorer for Minimax Model Estimation in MDPs

author.name: Xihe Gu, Urbashi Mitra, Tara Javidi

entry.summary: This paper extends the frequentist kappa-Explorer for active exploration in minimax transition estimation of unknown MDPs to a Bayesian formulation using Dirichlet priors. Under the posterior mean estimator, the posterior expected squared error equals total posterior variance, yielding a closed-form exploration signal that removes the computational burden of confidence-bound constructions and joint optimization.

entry.title: Full Rank and Stable Sampling of $\tanh$ Networks

author.name: Philipp Grohs, Mat\v{e}j Tr\"odler

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes the parameter sets where the realization map of feedforward tanh networks has full rank, showing these coincide with regular parameters in the sense of Vlasic and Bolcskei. It proves that almost every tuple of 2P+1 sampling points yields Lipschitz-stable network recovery on compact subsets, and that projected gradient descent and Gauss-Newton converge locally for exact observations.

entry.title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space

author.name: Tristan Fauvel, Federico Pavone, Titouan Guillou, Pau Redon Mu\~noz, Chlo\'e Geoffroy

entry.summary: The paper shows that an amortized inverse map of a mechanistic simulator can restrict the Bayesian optimization search space while a geometry-aware Gaussian process kernel exploits the problem's low intrinsic dimensionality. The authors characterize approximation bias and information gain and derive an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret bound, demonstrated on a drug dosing application.

entry.title: Multimodal Error Detection in Chest X-ray Reports: A Large Language Model Reading Image Evidence

author.name: Yanda Cheng, Bo Wen, Yuhao Lu

entry.summary: Rad-Linter flags potential errors in chest X-ray reports by checking them against image-derived pathology scores from a pretrained classifier, using a 1.5B language model fine-tuned with LoRA on 1,816 examples. Evaluation uses carefully controlled counterfactual report-score pairings so that either input alone is insufficient, isolating true cross-modal consistency checking.

entry.title: Decision Boundaries Matter: Graph-Regularized Residual Adaptation for Cross-Domain Fake Image Detection

author.name: Shichuang Xie, Qishuai Ding, Tong Qiao, Liquan Shen, Guorui Feng

entry.summary: GraRA addresses cross-domain generalization of fake image detectors by showing that frozen forensic encoder features remain discriminative while the source-trained decision boundary does not exploit them fully. The method refines the boundary using only unlabeled target data via a graph-regularized residual subspace, without requiring source data or target labels.

entry.title: Support-Guided Triadic Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Dialogue with LVLMs

author.name: Yiheng Li, Wenhao Wang, Xingyi Li, Zhilin Tang, Zichang Tan, Zhen Lei, Yang Yang

entry.summary: SGTD targets hallucination propagation in multi-turn multimodal dialogue by estimating the visual support of historical responses against type-matched alternatives, then selectively down-weighting unreliable history while fusing complementary predictions during decoding. This preserves useful context without globally weakening dialogue history influence.

entry.title: Minimal Memory for Correctable Visual Continuation

author.name: Xiyang Zhang, Yuanhe Tian, Hongzhi Wang, Yan Song

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical matching sparse and dense bounds on the memory needed to support later corrections in visual continuation from one evolving scene state, showing logarithmic overhead in one dimension and polynomial overhead in higher dimensions under stated assumptions. Proposes Coherent Archive Memory (CAM), storing geometric summaries with exact updates under clipping. Combines formal memory bounds with a practical memory mechanism for revisable scene state.

entry.title: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback

author.name: Yao Zhang, Zhuchenyang Liu, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: Inhabitant is a training-free agent framework for long-horizon human-scene interaction in 3D environments, in which a language-model agent specifies motions through positions, paths, and poses, then measures deviations between executed interaction and intent and revises control specifications accordingly. This adds spatial control and quantitative feedback that prior HSI agents lack, enabling challenging everyday sequences like throwing a toy into a basket.

entry.title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study

author.name: Seungho Song, Donggyu Lee, Jaehan Kim, Jiyoung Choi, Jinwoo Kim

entry.summary: HalluVision is a reproducible framework measuring hallucinations in LLM outputs for cyber threat intelligence tasks like summarization and question answering. It generates outputs from commercial and open LLMs, extracts domain-specific entities with a fine-tuned NER model, and evaluates factual consistency using multiple similarity metrics over 4,940 real cybersecurity articles. The study quantifies hallucination risks that could mislead security analysts.

entry.title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors

author.name: Morgan Colin-Mourre, Felipe Garrido-Lucero, Patrick Loiseau

entry.summary: The paper models data-sharing among competing firms whose profits depend on predictive precision and market share, characterizing Pareto-optimal contracts as those where at least one firm receives all others' data. It proposes a parametric contract family under which relative market shares stay constant, eliminating competitive harm from sharing, and identifies a strategyproof contract within the family.

entry.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models

author.name: Yuhao Zhou, Yang Zhou, Yuanxi Li, Jindi Lv, Dan Si, Qing Ye, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: Seer is an inference-time guidance framework for small, locally deployed deep-research agents that separates action proposal from learned consequence prediction and value estimation, drawing on a shared corpus of real research trajectories. It avoids the costs of exploratory execution, prompted self-evaluation limits, and model-specific adaptation, suiting privacy-preserving on-device agents.

entry.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience

author.name: Weihao Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes PlayCraft, an automated framework where a vision-based player agent repeatedly plays generated games and reports progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections, which a crafter agent uses to revise games for mastery-based engagement. It targets the problem that AI-generated games are playable but not necessarily fun. A closed-loop play-and-design system for game generation.

entry.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards

author.name: Ana E. Sanchez Villalobos, Michael D. Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, Minh D. Luu, David Kebo Houngninou

entry.summary: This paper introduces an LLM-based anomaly cross-checker that examines passing hardware verification regressions against the specification to catch scoreboard escapes, i.e., bugs that pass all checks because the scoreboard does not cover the violated property. On 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 were candidate escapes and 41 were confirmed. This applies LLM reasoning to a genuine gap in hardware verification workflows.

entry.title: DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware

author.name: Marco Roschkowski, Hannes Gernandt

entry.summary: DS3M proposes deep structured state space models combining compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and series, with custom Triton GPU kernels reducing launch and memory overhead of sequential evaluation, addressing the slow training of continuous-time neural state-space identification like SUBNET. A port-Hamiltonian variant and benchmark comparisons are included.

entry.title: Seeing Beyond the Obvious: Complementary Semantic Guidance for Salient Single-Positive Multi-Label Learning

author.name: Tong Jin, Meng-Long Wang, Xingyu Zhao, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes CoST, a coverage-guided soft-target refinement framework for salient single-positive multi-label learning that supplements salient prototypes with complementary class-semantic information from unknown classes. This mitigates bias toward visually prominent instances when supervising hidden positive labels.

entry.title: When Should Deployed BCI Decoders Adapt? A Resource-Priced Ladder for Frozen EEG Trunks

author.name: Sergey Musienko

entry.summary: This paper asks when a deployed motor-imagery EEG decoder should spend adaptation resources, proposing a resource ladder from a factory head to a closed-form Bayesian Normal-Inverse-Wishart head to affine maps, with full fine-tuning as an escape hatch, governed by regime-aware gating under a utility that prices accuracy, fit time, and label cost. The thesis is that adaptation should be gated and capped rather than always-on.

entry.title: TETHER: Training-Free, Elastic, ToC-Anchored Hierarchy Extraction and Recovery in Design-Driven Long Documents

author.name: Yu Zou, Yan Chen, Jialei Zeng, Xiaorui Zhou, Aixi Zhong, Qi Zhou, Haoran You, Ke Jiang, Changyu Hu

entry.summary: TETHER is a training-free framework for extracting document hierarchies that uses the table of contents as a structural prior instead of relying solely on localized visual cues or ungrounded LLM extraction, addressing fragility in high-entropy layouts and hallucination in long contexts. It operates via a two-stage scheme to recover document structure in design-driven long documents, supporting downstream LLM deployment.

entry.title: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi

entry.summary: SheetAlign is a spreadsheet manipulation framework for locally deployed open-weight LLMs that organizes policy learning into stages covering where to operate, what to change, and how to implement transformations. Task-guided inspection and API grounding anchor code generation in workbook observations while stage isolation simplifies learning.

entry.title: HOPD: Historical On-Policy Distillation for SAR MLLM Continual Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Li, Derrick Goh Xin Deik, Zheng-Peng Duan, Qianru Sun, Weijie Li

entry.summary: HOPD tackles continual learning for SAR image interpretation with multimodal LLMs by archiving LoRA states from past tasks as persistent teachers that supervise the student model's own generated outputs. Combined with augmented replay of scarce historical imagery, it retains old capabilities while absorbing new acquisition conditions.

entry.title: LIFT: Lifting Language-Controlled Image Fusion to Free-Viewpoint 3D Scenes

author.name: Jingning Tian, Hao Zhang, Yumin Huang, Zizhuo Li, Xingyu Jiang, Erdun Zhao, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Extends multimodal image fusion from 2D pairs to free-viewpoint 3D scenes via a language-controlled 3D fusion paradigm built on Gaussian scene representations. Semantic Modality Binding interprets instructions to identify semantic targets and modality preferences grounded in the shared scene, enabling task-tailored fused views from arbitrary viewpoints. A new paradigm at the intersection of image fusion, 3D reconstruction, and language grounding.

entry.title: EvoMem: Self-Evolving Skills for Time-Aware Long Video Memory Agents

author.name: Yutong Guan, Meixing Shi, Haoran Sun, Bing Sun, Yuxiang Cai, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes EvoMem, a time-aware long-video memory agent for large vision-language models that builds a hierarchical time-indexed memory aligned to a unified video timeline. During retrieval, temporal cues from acquired evidence are converted into explicit signals constraining subsequent memory access, and self-evolving retrieval skills address the fragmentation of global semantic matching. This targets coherent evidence chains in long-video understanding.

entry.title: DfD-GS: Defocus Image Prior for Metric-Scale Single-View Depth Estimation and View Synthesis

author.name: Shiori Ueda, Rinto Yagawa, Hideo Saito, Shohei Mori

entry.summary: Proposes DfD-GS, a feed-forward framework predicting metric-scale 3D Gaussian scene representations from an all-in-focus/defocused image pair, exploiting defocus blur as a physical metric depth cue. A defocus-based disparity estimate aligns and refines monocular depth predictions, addressing scale ambiguity and dataset-dependent biases of learned priors. This grounds single-view geometry in physical optics rather than learned scale priors alone.

entry.title: Prism: Hierarchical Text Detection with Minimalist Design

author.name: Yuchen Su, Xuesheng Wang, Zhilong Ji, Jinfeng Bai, Shijian Lu, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: Prism is a minimalist framework for hierarchical text detection that localizes words, lines, and paragraphs while parsing their structural relationships. It argues that a well-pretrained backbone can replace complex multi-scale fusion necks and heavy heads, using simple geometric inclusion rules for hierarchy parsing with parallel lightweight heads.

entry.title: GEMS: Generation and Experience Memory for Subgoal-Guided Long-Horizon World Model Planning

author.name: Yangchen Zhao, Ali Payani, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: GEMS extends visual world model planning to long-horizon tasks by combining generated subgoals with an experience memory, addressing error accumulation in long rollouts and weak guidance from distant goal representations. The system mitigates hallucinations in generated subgoals by drawing on selected real experience. It targets goal-conditioned manipulation planning beyond short-horizon reaching and pushing.

entry.title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction

author.name: Una Suman Kumar Patro, Sibangi Subhadarsani, Narendra Badam

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neurosymbolic framework for predicting 30-day diabetic readmissions that fuses structured EHR features, Bio_ClinicalBERT note embeddings, and symbolic entities extracted to handle code-mixed Hinglish phrasing and negation. It is evaluated on the public Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset with a patient-level grouped split.

entry.title: MS-Point: Multi-Modal Hierarchical Spectral Learning for Point Cloud Understanding

author.name: Hai-tao Yu, Jun Xia

entry.summary: MS-Point is a cross-modal pretraining framework for point cloud understanding that supervises intermediate point features and neighborhood responses before pooling, aligning branch descriptors with image features at selected encoder stages. Branch-level objectives, cross-level consistency, and adaptive fusion coordinate information across encoder stages and support both graph encoders and point Transformers.

entry.title: Stop Going in Circles:Loop-Triggered Routing for System 1 Decision Agents

author.name: Zeming Yu, Huamin Ma, Yingyu Chen, Yuan Sun, Peng Hu, Yang Qin

entry.summary: LoopRoute is a routing mechanism that preserves fast low-cost System 1 action selection (exemplified by a model called Jev) and invokes LLM reasoning only when recurring state-action pairs signal stalled execution. It aims to combine cheap local decisions with strong LLM planning exactly when agents get stuck in loops.

entry.title: Diagnosis is not a policy: a state-transition audit of caoability-conditioned test-time inference

author.name: Yuchong Hu, Zhao Zhang, Kainan Liu, Haoyu Wang, Siyan Zhang, Jing Xiao

entry.summary: TERRA is an evaluation and auditing protocol (not an inference algorithm) that decomposes test-time intervention outcomes into applicability, state realization, endpoint translation, harm, and cost. Paired financial reasoning experiments show the same context expansion can help one model configuration and harm another, and that sufficient evidence does not guarantee correctness. The work underscores that diagnosing model capability is distinct from choosing an intervention policy.

entry.title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version

author.name: Hiro Kataoka (MOEX), J{\'e}r{\^o}me Euzenat (MOEX), Koji Hasebe

entry.summary: This opinion dynamics study extends classical models by propagating beliefs (supporting propositions) alongside opinions, using belief merge operations to test effects on echo chamber formation. The corrected result is that coherent belief and opinion propagation actually increases echo chamber formation across homogeneity, segregation, and reinforcement properties.

entry.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network

author.name: Fatima Atwi (LAAS-GEPETTO, Nantes Univ - ECN), Constant Roux (LAAS-GEPETTO), Christian Bergaud (LAAS-MEMS), Olivier Stasse (LAAS-GEPETTO)

entry.summary: This work trains biologically inspired spiking neural networks for humanoid locomotion on the Unitree H1-2, comparing learning schemes that differ in how recurrent weights are trained, from a frozen in-vitro-like reservoir to fully learned recurrence. It addresses whether biological plausibility and robust locomotion performance can be achieved simultaneously.

entry.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models

author.name: Md. Abdullah Al Zami, Suraiya Shanaz, Mahdi Hasan, Shoaib Ahmed Dipu, Farig Yousuf Sadeque, Md. Sabbir Ahmed

entry.summary: Studies label-free linear-probe deception detection using persona directions from honest versus deceptive role-play, tested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge where a lie and honest denial are textually identical. Results are mixed: persona directions rank lies well on most models but fail on Qwen, and gains over a published persona bank are within the noise of random widenings. An honest negative-and-positive result paper on probe transferability.

entry.title: Beyond Restoration: Content-Degradation Factor Unfolding for Real-World Concealed Object Segmentation

author.name: Rihan Zhang, Fengyang Xiao, Yuhan Chen, Sina Farsiu

entry.summary: This work tackles concealed object segmentation under real-world degradations by explicitly factorizing content evidence from degradation effects using a Retinex-based spatially aligned decomposition, rather than simply restoring images first. The goal is to assess the reliability of content cues amid degradation-induced variation. It reframes the problem from visibility improvement to evidence identification.

entry.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots

author.name: Gustavo Rezende Silva, Tobias John, Francisco Mart\'in, EinarR Broch Johnsen

entry.summary: PLANTA is an ontology-mediated planning approach for autonomous robots that co-adapts task plans and architectural configurations, capturing the interdependency between what actions a mission requires and which software architecture enables them. It combines a Web Ontology Language representation of architectural alternatives with PDDL task planning, automatically translating and integrating the two models. This brings formal methods rigor to runtime self-adaptation in robotics.

entry.title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation

author.name: Madeleine Nouri, Gelareh Mohammadi, Francisco Cruz

entry.summary: This paper evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical reinforcement learning pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation, comparing them against flat RL baselines on unseen layouts and task instances. It examines complete pipelines with task-specific observation, reward, and control structures, including skills initialized from predecessor rollout states.

entry.title: Persona Lenses: What Makes a Vision-Language Model See Through Its Persona's Eyes?

author.name: Yoonho Shin

entry.summary: This single-author study quantifies how much a persona in a prompt influences VLM-simulated gaze on web pages and introduces persona lenses - text, pixel, and weight-lens interventions that place the persona between the model and the page. Experiments with Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5 models compare the lenses with each other and with model scale.

entry.title: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation

author.name: Ye Lin Tun, Chu Myaet Thwal, Eui-Nam Huh, Choong Seon Hong

entry.summary: The paper identifies the plateau problem in federated reinforcement learning for robot fleets: uniform averaging over-weights clients whose easy environments are already mastered, whose updates carry little new information despite high reported returns. The authors propose difficulty- and improvement-aware aggregation rules that weight client updates by ongoing learning signal rather than return.

entry.title: From Geographic Memory to Spatial Generalization in Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Chu, Zhaonan Wang, Cyrus Shahabi, Hengcai Zhang, Feng Lu

entry.summary: The paper distinguishes geospatial memory (recalling location-description associations seen in training) from spatial generalization (predicting descriptions for unobserved regions) in LLMs. It models geographic knowledge as a latent spatial field via a continuous spatial encoder, encouraging spatially organized representations that improve generalization to new locations.

entry.title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?

author.name: Marc Jansen

entry.summary: The paper proposes replacing Chain-of-Thought prompting with Question-Option-Criteria (QOC), a structured decision framework that decomposes tasks into explicit questions, competing options, and evaluation criteria. It presents a three-generation training pipeline evolving from a basic QOC decision core to statistically enriched reasoning, evaluating models on internal consistency and output quality. This explores whether internalized reasoning behavior can be deliberately reshaped.

entry.title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware

author.name: V\'ictor Rodrigo Gonz\'alez, Pablo M. Olmos, Ignacio Peis, Alejandro Lancho

entry.summary: Asuka-FM is an end-to-end system and architecture co-design framework enabling competitive dual-stream text-to-image DiT pretraining on a single consumer GPU such as an RTX 4090. It tackles three bottlenecks: quadratic attention costs, JIT compilation graph breaks from variable aspect-ratio bucketing, and VAE throughput walls. The work demonstrates that academic labs can train competitive T2I models without massive compute clusters.

entry.title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents

author.name: Yicheng Cai, Taegyu Kim, Peng Liu

entry.summary: This paper addresses post-incident forensics for LLM agent applications, where trajectory logs record agent functionality while compromise entry points live at the application code layer, creating a semantic gap for analysts. The authors build tooling to bridge trajectory logs and source code, helping identify compromise entry points, remediate damage, and prevent recurrence of agent-specific attacks. This fills a real operational security need as agent deployments grow.

entry.title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Dongsu Song, Jay Hoon Jung

entry.summary: The paper proposes Density Feedback Control (DFC), a controller that adjusts the sparsity coefficient of generator-based sparse adversarial attacks each epoch based on the gap between observed perturbation density and a target. DFC reaches target densities reliably and improves transferability at low densities without changing the generator architecture or loss.

entry.title: Scone: Symmetry-aware Neural Combinatorial Optimization for Graph Coloring

author.name: Paolo Pellizzoni, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Scone exploits the permutation symmetry of valid graph colorings to shrink the effective state space for learning-based graph coloring, while deliberately breaking symmetries where required, such as assigning distinct colors to particular nodes. This symmetry-aware approach improves learning-based solutions to the NP-hard graph coloring problem.

entry.title: Dimension-Free Buffer Bounds for Compressed-Momentum Error Feedback

author.name: Alireza Moayedikia

entry.summary: The paper shows that error-feedback analyses of compressed distributed optimization need not include the compressor contraction constant in the memory buffer bound or resulting rates. When compressed momentum is re-injected into the pre-compression accumulator, the buffer obeys a bound free of dimensions and rank, covering top-k selection and truncated SVD under a metric-projection assumption.

entry.title: A Lightweight Hybrid Approach for Milling Force Reconstruction from Internal Machine Signals

author.name: Eric Hirsch, Christian Friedrich

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid method that reconstructs milling forces from low-sampling-rate machine-internal signals and metadata, enabling force-based condition monitoring on legacy machines without intrusive sensors. Rather than modeling the full force signal, it targets lower-frequency reconstruction to limit model complexity and data requirements.

entry.title: Loss-Guided Tsetlin Machines: Making the Learning Objective Explicit

author.name: Mayur Shende, Runar Helin, Ole-Christoffer Granmo, Vladimir I. Zadorozhny

entry.summary: Tsetlin Machines traditionally lack an explicit loss function, relying on a fixed margin-based update rule. This work introduces Loss-Guided TM, which swaps in explicit losses (cross entropy, symmetric cross entropy, asymmetric loss) while keeping the Tsetlin Automaton and clause logic unchanged, matching or improving accuracy across six classification datasets.

entry.title: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions

author.name: Christian Wald

entry.summary: This single-author theoretical work studies jump diffusion models that reset coordinates to embeddings of categorical values, proposing leave-one-out prediction where each coordinate is predicted only from the corrupted states of other coordinates. Under stated assumptions, such diffusions with complete coordinate resets and state-independent clocks preserve prescribed marginals when reset destinations use exact LOO probabilities and the drift uses the full endpoint posterior.

entry.title: Risk-optimal active learning with informative abstention

author.name: Fariborz Setoudehtazangi, Geoffrey J. McLachlan

entry.summary: This paper studies active learning when an oracle may abstain from answering, showing that a query provides information both through the returned label and through the abstention outcome itself. The authors derive an acquisition criterion combining adjusted classifier information with the curvature of multiclass zero-one risk, and characterize optimal query allocation under a fixed budget.

entry.title: CAIMS: Scalable Cross-Array In-Memory Search

author.name: Yi-Chun Liao, Liu Liu, Ruiyang Qin, Yiran Chen, X. Sharon Hu

entry.summary: CAIMS tackles the problem of computing accurate global top-k similarity search results across multiple content-addressable memory (CAM) arrays, where each array only produces local binary match results. The design enables scalable in-memory search with the low latency and energy efficiency of CAM hardware for modern workloads exceeding single-array capacity.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Secure Inference for Drug--Target Interaction Prediction

author.name: Sikha Pentyala, Steven Golob, Daniil Filienko, Ming-Chun Kao, Martine De Cock

entry.summary: The authors present a two-party secure multiparty computation (MPC) solution for deep-model drug-target interaction prediction, developed for Track III of the iDASH 2026 privacy competition. The work co-designs MPC-friendly neural models and GPU-compatible MPC protocols to overcome the slow communication-heavy nature of non-linear operations in secure inference.

entry.title: Hellinger Decision Trees for Density Ratio Estimation: Finite-Sample Guarantees

author.name: Ren-Rui Liu, Zheng-Chu Guo

entry.summary: The paper develops a direct method for log density ratio estimation by minimizing a balanced Hellinger risk over additive ensembles of axis-aligned decision trees trained via Newton boosting. It establishes finite-sample convergence guarantees with explicit rates that, under smoothness and tail conditions, match minimax-optimal rates up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Statistical Inference with Ill-Conditioned Random Weight Neural Network Sieves

author.name: Giovanni Ballarin, Lyudmila Grigoryeva, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: The authors prove that random-weight neural network sieves cannot remain uniformly well-conditioned as dimension grows, deriving polynomial eigenvalue bounds for the population covariance matrix that imply a vanishing smallest eigenvalue. They develop approximation, estimation, and inference theory that accounts for this ill-conditioning.

entry.title: DRVEXO-4B-Unified: Design and Evaluation of a Modular Speech-Vision System

author.name: Zeyuan Li

entry.summary: The authors present a modular multimodal assistant built on a 4B language backbone that handles text, image, and speech input plus reference-conditioned speech output, using a temporal residual connector and task-conditioned scoring heads. It reports 74.22% on all 900 MMMU validation questions, exceeding published scores of Gemma 3 4B IT and InternVL3.5-4B.

entry.title: FoodReact-AR: Learning Audience Reactions that Zero-Shot LLMs Miss in Arabic Food-Insecurity Discourse

author.name: Wajdi Zaghouani, Mabrouka Bessghaier, Salma Azouzi, Shimaa Amer Ibrahim

entry.summary: The authors analyze 74,241 Arabic food-insecurity Facebook posts from 2020-2024, modeling the six reaction types as compositions and clustering them into four audience profiles such as Solidarity and Dismissal. They find dismissal peaked in 2022 during the wheat price shock and grief peaked in 2024 during the Gaza food emergency, with statistical confirmation via clustered GEE and robustness checks.

entry.title: SEAF: Selective Semantic Enrichment and Visual Evidence Fusion for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection

author.name: Faxian Wan, Xiaocui Yang, Yifan Cao, Shi Feng, Daling Wang, Yifei Zhang

entry.summary: SEAF is a dual-branch framework for multimodal sarcasm detection that assigns distinct roles to outputs generated by a frozen multimodal LLM: entity background enriches the semantic branch while image descriptions provide alignment statistics for the visual branch. The framework fuses original post text, OCR text, and MLLM-generated background to separate useful knowledge from redundant visual description.

entry.title: TAP: Tapping the Discriminative Potential of Frozen Representations for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Zihao Wang (Shandong University), Yu-Wei Zhan (Zhejiang University of Technology), Xiao-Qian Liu (Shandong University), Zhen-Duo Chen (Shandong University), Weitong Liu (Shandong University), Xin Luo (Shandong University), Xin-Shun Xu (Shandong University)

entry.summary: TAP explores class-incremental learning with fully frozen encoders, accumulating visual and semantic class information in the frozen CLIP embedding space through lightweight modules for class-conditional visual distinction and semantic structuring. This avoids optimization costs and feature-structure disruption from sequential adaptation.

entry.title: LG-FiLM: Local-Global Mixture-of-Experts Modulation for RAW-to-RGB Reconstruction

author.name: Fei Li, Xilei Cao, Shichang Zhai, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes an image signal processor architecture that makes scene-dependent adaptation explicit by placing a small mixture-of-affine-experts at the bottleneck of a shared encoder-decoder, with expert parameters predicted from local neighborhood evidence plus a global scene descriptor. This lets the network choose denoising strength, color balance, and tone mapping per scene rather than applying one fixed transformation. Targeted at RAW-to-RGB reconstruction, likely for automotive imaging given the author list.

entry.title: DACA: Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Jiaming Liu, Linghe Kong, Guixu Zhang, Huaxi Huang

entry.summary: DACA reframes zero-shot 3D visual grounding as a collaborative reasoning process between semantic and geometric anchors, replacing the typical unidirectional pipeline-style agent architecture with two complementary specialized tools. This design aims to reduce error accumulation and enable autonomous recovery from failures, which is important for embodied intelligence and human-computer interaction applications.

entry.title: SCCV-6D: Sparse Canonical Coordinate Voting for Holistic Multi-View RGB-D 6D Pose Estimation in Robotic Bin Picking

author.name: Nico Leuze, Samed Dogan, Maximilian Hoh, Henry Schaub, Alfred Sch\"ottl

entry.summary: Presents SCCV-6D, a fully sparse multi-view RGB-D 6D pose estimator for industrial bin picking that handles clutter, occlusion, and texture-less reflective parts in a single pass. It reconstructs 3D space at millimeter precision, prunes background with staged heatmaps, and keeps memory and runtime within operational constraints that defeat heavier multi-stage pipelines. The focus on practical industrial deployment constraints distinguishes it from accuracy-first academic methods.

entry.title: SpatialMem: Building Quantitative Spatial Reasoning Agents with Hierarchical Memory

author.name: Zinan Zheng, Nuo Chen, Jia Li

entry.summary: Addresses quantitative spatial reasoning in VLM agents by proposing SpatialMem, which uses hierarchical memory to handle the combinatorial space of pipeline orchestration and vision specialist selection. Existing tool-using agents bind each functional requirement to one predefined specialist, making pipelines rigid; SpatialMem enables more flexible orchestration for diverse spatial scenarios. This moves beyond purely qualitative spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Attention Drift Regularization with Adaptive Initialization for Domain-Robust Visual Recognition

author.name: Shivangi Rai, Vinod K Kurmi

entry.summary: The paper identifies two failure modes in source-free domain adaptation: attention drift toward spurious features under distribution shift, and domain-gap-agnostic initialization. The proposed DGA-CAFC uses counterfactual attention-based feature consistency plus adaptive initialization to stabilize representations across target domains.

entry.title: GateTrace: Where Do Crowd Crossings Go Missing Under Occlusion?

author.name: Ao He, Qianchen Yu, Vivian W. H. Wong

entry.summary: GateTrace is a diagnostic framework that locates missed pedestrian crossings in event crowd-counting systems, motivated by a stadium study where only one in three mostly-obscured crossings was recorded. It derives reference crossings from MOT20 annotations, matches reports, and traces misses through tracking decisions, showing that ByteTrack, OC-SORT and BoT-SORT recover only 38.9-46.7% of losses.

entry.title: SHUSH: Emission-Aware Reward Design for Proactive Video Assistants

author.name: Shawn Liang, Soamar Homsi, Gourav Datta

entry.summary: SHUSH identifies a reward-design flaw in proactive video assistants: the PAUC reward used by MMDuet2 makes extra responses effectively free, encouraging over-emission. The authors prove this analytically and propose an emission-aware F1 reward with exclusive span-emission matching that prices both false emissions and missed spans. This teaches reinforcement-learned assistants when to stay silent as well as when to speak.

entry.title: On the Hamel Coefficients and the Boltzmann-Hamel Equations for the Rigid Body

author.name: Andreas M\"uller

entry.summary: This theoretical paper provides an explicit coordinate-free derivation of the Boltzmann-Hamel equations for the rigid body, identifying Hamel coefficients as the structure constants of SE(3) and clarifying their connections to Newton-Euler, Euler-Poincare, and reduced Euler-Lagrange equations.

entry.title: Reference-Twist-Based Velocity-Domain Spatiotemporal Calibration for mmWave Radar, Event Camera, and IMU

author.name: Zhenghao Zou, Yang Lyu, Xiaohu Guo, Chunhui Zhao, Quan Pan

entry.summary: This paper formulates target-free spatiotemporal calibration for a multi-sensor suite of two mmWave radars, an event camera, and two IMUs by regressing radar Doppler, event normal flow, and inertial measurements against a reference body twist. It jointly estimates extrinsics, time offsets, and sensor biases without artificial targets or point cloud associations.

entry.title: PUPPET: Physical-Unified Platform for Presence, Embodiment, and Teleoperation

author.name: Mahika Vats, Milan Groshev, Carlos Gomez Cubero, Eduardo Castell\'o Ferrer

entry.summary: PUPPET is a cyber-physical framework providing remote access to a physical robotics lab through a continuously synchronized VR replica of the robot, workspace, and task objects, with an integrated trial-validation pipeline to ensure usable experimental data. A 30-participant within-subject study showed VR teleoperation reduced completion time by 27.7% versus 2D teleoperation for a table-to-shelf transfer task.

entry.title: "Prosaic AI alignment": 10 years later

author.name: Morgan S

entry.summary: A retrospective on the tenth anniversary of Paul Christiano's foundational post on prosaic AI alignment, examining its original arguments and tracing how the paradigm became the standard frame for empirical alignment research. The author is explicit that it is a time-capsule analysis rather than a claim about Christiano's current views.

entry.title: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Interface Framework for Multi-Layer Refractive Transport

author.name: Zixuan Zhao, Tao Wang

entry.summary: GaussTrans is a compact framework for light transport in scenes with many transparent layers, combining Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces, Transport-Coupled Refinement, and Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection to handle the interplay of geometric, light-path, and observation errors. It avoids the simplifications (fewer layers, simpler light paths) that limit existing transparent-scene reconstruction techniques.

entry.title: SenseAlign: Learning Decision-Aligned Predictive Representations for Active Urban Sensing with UAVs

author.name: Weijiang Xiong, Nikolas Geroliminis

entry.summary: SenseAlign is a reinforcement learning framework that coordinates drone fleets for active sensing of dynamic urban road networks by learning decision-aligned predictive representations. It uses a privileged teacher agent trained with future ground-truth traffic states and aligns student representations to downstream decision value rather than pure state prediction.

entry.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots

author.name: Wai Ka Sun, Waiyiu Pong, Bowen Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes passage-conditioned navigation for wheeled-legged robots, which stores each taught crossing of a stair or ledge as an event encoding how the transition was entered, then enforces those entry conditions at runtime without training or a robot model. A single 27-minute teaching session suffices, addressing the failure of fixed locomotion skills at geometry-mismatched passages.

entry.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher

author.name: Yang Meng, Zixin Ding, Robert L. Grossman, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: The paper constructs an explicit oracle teacher for active feature acquisition that, given labels and unobserved feature values at training time, ranks candidate features in closed form by their effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy via soft-target imitation, replacing prior methods that optimized self-constructed utility targets. This provides a cleaner, theoretically grounded training signal for budget-constrained feature acquisition.

entry.title: PDE-State Conditioning for Learned Optimization Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Farzana Yasmin, Ricardo Vilalta

entry.summary: The authors design a learned optimizer for PINN training that conditions on an 11-dimensional PDE state capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, going beyond fixed statistics like Adam or purely local learned features. They study both what PDE-level information the optimizer should observe and how it should influence updates.

entry.title: From Data Alignment to Parameter Generation: Few-Shot Cross-City Traffic Prediction with Conditional Diffusion

author.name: Shengchun Wang, Yuhang Lin, Tong Li, Pengyuan Zhou, Andy Chi Lok Tai, Wenjie Chen, Zhu Xiao, Zhu Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes conditional diffusion-based parameter generation for few-shot cross-city mobile traffic prediction, generating model parameters for data-scarce cities instead of aligning traffic distributions in data space. This avoids brittleness of data-space alignment under distribution shifts, noise, and city-specific bias, supporting capacity provisioning and congestion management.

entry.title: Extending Rademacher Complexity-Based Generalization Theory to Domain Generalization

author.name: Xi Wang, Liang Bai, Xian Yang, Richard Yi Da Xu

entry.summary: This paper extends Rademacher complexity-based generalization bounds to domain generalization by endowing the domain space with geometric structure, departing from prior frameworks that treat domain space as geometry-free. It elevates generalization analysis from the sample level to the distribution level over an infinite-dimensional space of probability distributions.

entry.title: The Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Outweigh the Observed Effects of Data, Capacity, and Architecture in Customer Behavior Forecasting

author.name: Tara Sowrirajan, Yanqiao Wang

entry.summary: Through experiments on long-horizon customer behavior forecasting, the authors find that increasing the observation window (from 8 to 16 weeks of history) improves log-space R-squared by 0.070 to 0.107 across every model family, outweighing effects of more data, capacity, and newer architectures. The finding holds across five public datasets plus internal data, with matched test cohorts confirming the effect, and longer windows also admit more cold-start customers.

entry.title: Statistical, Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Missing Covariates: An Empirical Evaluation with Applications to Alzheimer's Disease Research

author.name: Yiqing Pan, Sharon X. Xie, Shujie Ma, Angela L. Jefferson, Panpan Zhang

entry.summary: This study empirically compares eight methods for handling missing covariates, spanning complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, ML techniques, and deep learning frameworks like VAEs and GANs, under different missingness mechanisms. It applies the evaluation to Alzheimer's disease research where costly biomarkers such as cerebrospinal fluid measures create pervasive missingness.

entry.title: RE-CAM: Readout-Enhanced Content-Addressable Memory for Quantitative Similarity Search

author.name: Yi-Chun Liao, Dongyoung Lee, Jiazheng Chen, Tergel Molom-Ochir, Tomohisa Kawakami, Tania Roy, Ik-Joon Chang, X. Sharon Hu, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: RE-CAM extracts quantitative similarity information from content-addressable memory searches, which traditionally output only binary match results, by interpreting the array's output voltage evolution during the search. It treats the sensing timestamp as a key design variable alongside reference voltage and decoding parameters to enable richer similarity search directly in hardware.

entry.title: Watertight Mesh Optimization of Textured Objects

author.name: Nathaniel Burgdorfer, Philippos Mordohai

entry.summary: MODL jointly optimizes geometry and view-dependent appearance directly on a watertight triangle mesh using Laplacian-preconditioned updates and curvature-adaptive remeshing, constrained by multi-view normalized cross-correlation. It avoids segmentation, geometric supervision, and alpha-blending while producing high-quality 3D assets from images.

entry.title: Slide2PPT: Native PowerPoint Reconstruction with Localization-Guided Refinement

author.name: Baoliang Chen, Xinlong Bu, Lingyu Zhu, Xiangjie Sui

entry.summary: A model-agnostic, training-free framework that gives open and closed vision-language models the ability to reconstruct slides as native, editable PowerPoint objects, using a typed record interface with a fixed renderer and localization-guided refinement driven by visual discrepancies. This avoids the common failure where visually faithful charts and tables lack editable series and cells. Practically useful for document-to-editable-content conversion pipelines.

entry.title: AGSR: Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution for Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Ayman Alkhateeb, Hadi Amirpour, Christian Timmerer

entry.summary: Proposes AGSR, a lightweight inference-time super-resolution framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting based on the insight that contracting projected covariances can mitigate the bandwidth limitation of finite Gaussian footprints. It progressively fuses multi-aperture renderings using uncertainty-guided feature aggregation and geometric conditioning from transmittance and depth cues. The method works as a plug-in enhancement for pre-trained 3DGS models.

entry.title: Planning to Stop: Factored Certification and Terminal Repair for Noncircular Robots

author.name: Runtian Zheng, Congpeng Zhang, Ying Liu

entry.summary: GeoDiff is a motion-program planner for tight-space navigation that certifies reach-and-stop behavior for noncircular robots, coupling stopped-set inclusion with witness-guided terminal repair and factored proof compilation. Evaluated on 11,440 floorplan-derived jobs, it certifies more tasks at 5-cm tolerance within 15 seconds than a stop-set baseline.
