entry.title: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination

author.name: Xiaoqian Shen, Yunyang Xiong, Changsheng Zhao, Saksham Suri, Chong Zhou, Zechun Liu, Zhipeng Cai, Zhuang Liu, Qi Qian, Wei Wen, Hongyu Xu, Hanxian Huang, Ernie Chang, Yanbei Chen, Vikas Chandra, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Lemeng Wu

entry.summary: AVTR introduces visual imagination as a complementary reasoning modality to textual thinking in vision-language models, adaptively selecting reasoning modality and depth per question. This addresses verbose textual traces on vision-centric questions and reduces unnecessary computation.

entry.title: Comparing Each Generation with Independent Siblings Gives Video World Model Post-Training a Proper Objective for Outcome Frequencies

author.name: Xin Li, Yiwen Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that physics post-training of video world models against the single recorded future biases models toward always producing the most likely outcome, since the expected score is linear in the model distribution. The authors derive an objective based on log-likelihood of recorded outcomes whose gradient can be estimated by comparing each generation with independent-sibling generations of the same history. This yields correct outcome frequencies in simulation-like world models.

entry.title: Gaussian Splatoms: Direct Atomic Structure Identification in Electron Tomography

author.name: Nalini Singh, Tiffany Chien, Cedric Lim, Arthur R. C. McCray, Colin Ophus, Laura Waller

entry.summary: Applies Gaussian splatting ideas to atomic electron tomography by representing material samples as lists of 3D Gaussian atoms with learned location, scale, and amplitude, incorporating physics priors like atomic isotropy and minimum interatomic distances. Enables direct atomic structure identification instead of voxel-grid reconstruction.

entry.title: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability

author.name: Chenxi Han, Ruby, Epoch, Orion, Luke, Bin, Dusk, Lyra, Cal, Alvin, Hubert, Alex, Jiahe Han, Tao Zhang, Hang Liu, Shoujie Li, Yizhe Li, Bokui Chen, Houde Liu, Guoping Pan, Yi Cheng

entry.summary: ZERITH V2.5 is a video-action model where the action policy reads intermediate features of a video generation model, used to study under fixed demonstrations and update budgets which kinds of predictive training supervision best improve subsequent action learning. The central finding is that prediction quality does not automatically translate into policy learnability.

entry.title: Old Experience, New Lessons: Relabeling Autonomous Robot Rollouts in Interactive Imitation Learning

author.name: Zhaoting Li, Cosimo Della Santina, Jens Kober

entry.summary: The paper proposes SeRA, a framework that exploits abundant unlabeled autonomous robot experience in interactive imitation learning by relabeling it with later policy checkpoints and filtering via cross-checkpoint agreement, combined with human-in-the-loop correction signals. It avoids reinforcing suboptimal behavior that comes from imitating historical robot actions. This improves sample efficiency of human intervention data in robot learning.

entry.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL

author.name: Jiin Woo, Gauri Joshi, Yuejie Chi

entry.summary: This theory paper reframes reward heterogeneity in federated reinforcement learning as a structural asset for exploration rather than a hindrance, proposing PF-UCBVI which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. It further introduces PF-EFVI, a purely greedy exploration-free algorithm that leverages reward diversity to guarantee state-action coverage.

entry.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents

author.name: Lipeng He, Yihan Wang, Jiawen Zhang, N. Asokan

entry.summary: Shows that high attack success rates during RL-based red-teaming of LLM agents do not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training, and proposes PIPETTE, a purple-teaming framework that closes the loop between automated attack generation and hardening. The work reframes evaluation around post-training robustness rather than ASR alone. It targets the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents.

entry.title: MIRAGE: A Framework for Multi-hop Reasoning under Dynamic Knowledge Injection

author.name: Heyang Xu, HanWen Hao, Haifeng Wang, Haoyi Zhou, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: Introduces a more realistic knowledge-updating setting for multi-hop QA called Knowledge Injection, where models must simultaneously handle conflicting updates and entirely novel information. MIRAGE diagnoses failure modes — clinging to outdated parametric memory when knowledge conflicts and failing on entirely new facts — and provides a framework for evaluating multi-hop reasoning under these conditions.

entry.title: GTA: Generative Tower of Agents for Scalable Holonic Scene Generation

author.name: Zeng Tao, Yunuo Chen, Xiang Feng, Yumeng He, Peihao Li, Nanxiang Jiang, Yaowei Guo, Fanlian Zeng, Yin Yang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: GTA (Generative Tower of Agents) represents every unit at every level of an adaptive scene hierarchy as a holon, both a self-contained construction task and a composable scene unit, with parallel agents recursively planning top-down and assembling bottom-up. Uniform interfaces propagate scene-wide requirements through the hierarchy, enabling high-throughput parallel world modeling while preserving structured layouts and fine-grained assets. This addresses scalability of agentic scene and world generation, including dynamic characters.

entry.title: ReSynth: Constructing Synthetic Supervision for Multi-Image Understanding

author.name: Yilin Wang, Xin Yu, Xinyi Guo, Xiangxi Zheng, Dongxing Mao, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: ReSynth addresses the data bottleneck in multi-image understanding for VLMs by synthesizing relational supervision from single-image perception plus controllable generation: localized editing yields before-and-after pairs and viewpoint generation yields multiple views of the same instance. Verified scene contents enable cross-image relational comparisons at scale. This tackles a genuine weakness of current VLMs with a scalable data engine.

entry.title: Do Thinking VLMs Need to Keep Looking at Long Videos? Write It Down, Then Look Away

author.name: Pengyu Li, Zhitao Gao, Lingling Zhang, Heng Wang, Chengqian Ma, WenHao Wang, Wenxuan Huang, Chen Zheng, Jun Liu

entry.summary: LookAway shows that VLM dependence on video content concentrates early in long-video reasoning: the model writes timestamped notes answering the question's needs, then the video KV cache is hidden for the rest of the response. On Qwen3.6-27B, note-writing preserves accuracy better than free reasoning at the same withdrawal step, offering substantial KV-cache savings.

entry.title: RAID: Representation Autoencoder for Intrinsic Decomposition

author.name: Claudia Cuttano, Tamy Boubekeur, Elena Garces, Giuseppe Vecchio

entry.summary: RAID shows accurate single-image intrinsic decomposition does not require large diffusion priors. It decouples reconstruction from decomposition on top of DINOv3 features: an X-to-X teacher learns to reconstruct intrinsic maps from DINOv3 features with a shared decoder without paired supervision, then a lightweight student predicts teacher representations directly from RGB. This avoids large, iterative, stochastic generative models.

entry.title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot

author.name: Xinke Lyu, Bowen Yang, Zhicheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an object-centric pipeline that converts monocular egocentric human video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Its CORE representation records contact-centric object-interaction dynamics so retargeting respects physics rather than only visual appearance.

entry.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow

author.name: Rui Li, Liyang He, Zheng Zhang, Zhenya Huang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: AnyS1 is a domain-general dual-system framework that mines enumerable decision points from over 1,000 public procedural skills and trains a single lightweight System-1 model (on the Any-DP dataset) to handle candidate-selection decisions across arbitrary agent workflows, reserving the large System-2 model for the rest. Unlike prior dual-system agents, it needs no workflow-specific hooks. This substantially reduces agent cost and latency.

entry.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Jinbae Seo, Jungin Park, Hyunsung Jang, Namkoo Ha, Jiyoung Lee, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: Introduces COTEX, a method for continually adding new specialist vision tools to already-trained multimodal agents at adapter-level cost. It separates parameter directions that trigger tool calls from those that select tools, using orthogonality constraints so new adapters leave earlier tool choices unaffected. This addresses the practical problem of extending agent toolkits without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Zongyuan Wu, Xin Wang, Tongtong Feng, Yuan Meng, Zeyang Zhang, Ling Feng, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a world model that imagines over sparse relational state abstractions rather than dense pixels, using a graph of task-relevant entities to reduce error accumulation in long imagined rollouts. Tackles two challenges: forming compact state abstractions and incorporating relations for planning in embodied and web environments. Relevant to model-based RL for long-horizon decision making.

entry.title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming

author.name: Xiaoyang Xing, Wenyu Dai, Xiaoliang Gong, Asoke K Nandi, Anthony Cohn

entry.summary: This paper introduces Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided framework that evolves executable multi-agent workflows for automated red-teaming of large language models. It represents agent responsibilities, execution dependencies, and input bindings in a versioned graph to reduce redundant coordination costs while identifying which collaboration decisions should change based on target model responses.

entry.title: EnvAgent: Multi-Agent Approach to Building Science Environments in the Clouds

author.name: Yiming Cheng, Chris Low, Binrui Huang, Mengshi Zhang, Zihao Chen, Kate Keahey, Paul Marshall, Kexin Pei

entry.summary: EnvAgent is an agentic framework that automatically synthesizes, builds, and verifies repository-level Docker environments for scientific computing, replacing labor-intensive developer-maintained Dockerfiles and setup scripts. The system combines multi-agent coordination with deterministic utilities for Docker execution and state management to handle the heterogeneous and incomplete dependency requirements found in real repositories. This matters because correctly configured execution environments are a prerequisite for AI agents that generate and run scientific code, and manual environment setup does not scale.

entry.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents

author.name: Xingyang Li, Tianlang Zhao, Song Han, Ligeng Zhu

entry.summary: QDA is an agentic system in which an LLM agent designs post-training quantization recipes per model and precision through iterative build-and-evaluate loops. To overcome the cost of evaluating quantized reasoning models, QDA uses fast proxy scoring, removing the need for tens of GPU-hours per candidate and manual porting across codebases.

entry.title: MANGO Arena: Same Seeds, Different Chains Evaluating LLM Agents in a Disrupted Supply Chain

author.name: Sara Amar

entry.summary: MANGO Arena is an open-source testbed where four LLM agents each operate a company in a serial supply chain based on a classroom factory-management game. The environment enforces hard economic rules, logs rule-breaking attempts, and provides a message board where collusion is explicitly banned, allowing simultaneous measurement of economic outcomes (bullwhip effect), rule adherence, and collusion proposals. Pilot experiments with small reasoning models show all LLM agents amplified the bullwhip effect.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments

author.name: Yuze Wu, Mo Zhu, Xingxing Li, Yuheng Du, Zhaoqi Wang, Yuxin Fan, Wenjun Li, Kenghou Hoi, Zhichao Han, Xin Zhou, Fei Gao

entry.summary: Presents VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation framework for UAVs that decouples multimodal semantic reasoning from low-level control, producing 3D pose commands and navigation intentions translated into dynamically feasible actions. It targets onboard deployment with limited compute, addressing 3D data scarcity, trajectory feasibility, and long-horizon reasoning.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Johannes Hog, Neeratyoy Mallik, Steven Adriaensen, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Tom Viering, Danny Stoll, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Investigates whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style tabular foundation models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings, given that these models are pretrained on nearly unlimited synthetic data but evaluated on real datasets. The analysis finds systematic differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that good fits do not guarantee reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. Author list includes Frank Hutter and AutoML researchers.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers

author.name: Houman Mehrafarin, Ioannis Konstas

entry.summary: The paper shows that chain-of-thought hidden states encode recoverable task-solving information, and that the direct-prompt representation space contains per-question directions which, when activated, lead models to correct answers in fewer tokens than CoT. This offers a mechanistic route to cheaper direct answering on tasks where CoT underperforms or is unnecessarily verbose.

entry.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents

author.name: Alexander Boesgaard Lorup

entry.summary: Openhagen Worlds is a suite of 27 procedurally generated environments for scientific discovery agents, spanning experimental-reasoning puzzles to simulator-grounded physics and chemistry, where agents run budgeted experiments and commit answers checked by deterministic verifiers against hidden truths. Its 178 difficulty levels are explicitly calibrated using oracle success thresholds and fully stated scoring rules to eliminate recall shortcuts.

entry.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses

author.name: Jiahang Lin, Jiahao Chen, Yiding Wang, Shichun Liu, Chengjun Pan, Shihan Dou, Honglin Guo, Yuyang Hu, Changhao Jiang, Zhenhua Han, Hang Yan, Qi Zhang, Tao Gui, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: AHE-Beta introduces a requirement-centered loop for evolving agent harnesses that incorporates implicit user requirements and interaction needs, addressing the narrow patches and benchmark-specific local optima produced by existing single-agent, benchmark-score-driven evolution methods. The loop uses simulated users raising requirements as issues over multi-turn interactions, followed by team-based development and testing steps mirroring real software engineering practice. It targets the growing area of automated agent scaffolding improvement.

entry.title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses

author.name: George Giapitzakis, Ankur Moitra, Andrej Risteski, Dhruv Rohatgi

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that error accumulation in reverse diffusion sampling with imperfect learned scores can be bounded better than the polynomial-in-horizon rates arising from path-space analyses. By avoiding bounding output error by the error of the entire reverse diffusion path law, the authors (including Moitra and Risteski, strong theorists) derive improved accumulation behavior. A meaningful advance in the theoretical understanding of diffusion model sampling.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Neural Approximation of Convex, Semiconvex, and Quasiconvex Functions

author.name: Yeachan Park, Yeoneung Kim

entry.summary: This theoretical work extends input convex neural networks to semiconvex, quasiconvex, and convex-transformable functions, establishing sharp W^{1,p} minimax approximation rates for max-affine approximation and showing exact bounded-width ICNN representations. It connects architectural constraints on convexity to rigorous approximation theory.

entry.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents

author.name: Hengguang Zhou, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen, Priyanshi Shrivastava, Anastasios Angelopoulos, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: This meta-evaluation study tests whether existing user-simulator evaluation metrics reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior, deliberately perturbing simulated replays to induce failures such as altered goals, omitted constraints, and acceptance of broken work. Findings from three prior evaluation frameworks reveal what a high benchmark score actually says about simulator quality.

entry.title: Optical Neural Networks Should Be Evaluated by Function, Not Only Physics

author.name: Shi-Yuan Ma, Xingjian Bai, Ryan Hamerly, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad

entry.summary: This position/methodology paper argues that optical neural network modules should be evaluated as black-box tensor-to-tensor mappings within a digital pipeline, by replacing them with digital equivalents to isolate their true contribution to claimed throughput or energy advantages. It proposes a three-step function-oriented evaluation boundary for ONN systems.

entry.title: Every Query Routes Itself: Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers with Per-Query Routed Sparse Attention

author.name: Zhen Huang, Shuwei Li, Ruizhe Yao, Xinrui Chen, Danyi Liu, Haoyuan Liang, Zhiyu Ye, Qiuyan Sun, Bingwei Chen, Yiyuan Li, Xu Zhou, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: The paper shows that sharing key-cluster selections among clustered queries limits accuracy in sparse attention for video diffusion transformers, and proposes PQRS, a training-free method where each query independently selects its own key clusters, compensating unselected keys with centroids. Per-query routing yields higher accuracy at fixed sparsity and accelerates long-sequence video diffusion inference. This challenges a design assumption in cluster-based sparse attention.

entry.title: Localizing Text Anonymization for Trustworthy AI: Extending RAT-Bench to Malaysian Microdata and PII

author.name: David Hong Liang Chew, Zexi Yao, Nata\v{s}a Kr\v{c}o, Matthieu Meeus, Waqas Khalid Obeidy, Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye

entry.summary: Extends the RAT-Bench anonymization benchmark to Malaysia with local microdata, Malaysian PII formats, and transcripts in Malaysian English and Bahasa Malaysia. It evaluates NER- and LLM-based anonymizers using an LLM attacker measuring re-identification success and text utility, finding that LLM-based anonymizers provide the strongest explanations across both languages.

entry.title: Reference-Guided Data Curation for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pretraining

author.name: Faidra Patsatzi, Ashwin Kumar, Chong Wang, Curtis P. Langlotz, Reinhard Heckel, Akshay S. Chaudhari

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free, reference-guided data curation recipe for 3D medical VLM pretraining: a small high-quality reference set produces quality signals per modality of a large uncurated pool, merged via rank aggregation to guide sample selection. It is validated on 35k abdominal CT volume-report pairs across institutions. Data curation is increasingly recognized as a dominant factor in VLM quality, making this recipe broadly applicable.

entry.title: ACUS: An Angular Calibrated Uncertainty Score for Incomplete-View CT

author.name: Zihan Deng, Chuanzhi Xu, Quankeng Huang, Yujie Liu, Zhenzhen Gong, Junjie Huang, Tianye Niu, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: ACUS is a new evaluation metric for sparse-view and limited-arc CT reconstruction that measures how predictive reliability degrades with angular distance from acquired views. Instead of scoring projection completion against a single ground-truth image, it uses the Winkler interval score of a 90 percent predictive interval on held-out projections, binned by distance to the nearest measured view, penalizing learned priors that invent unconstrained anatomy.

entry.title: MobileWeave: Program-First Synthesis of Dependency-Linked Tasks for Training Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Ziyi He, Xian Wu, Qiyuan Chen, Haitao Li, Cehao Yang, Yinghao Zhu, Xichen Zhang, Xiao Chen, Yushi Feng, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: MobileWeave synthesizes training tasks for mobile GUI agents as executable programs derived from typed app capability abstractions in a controllable simulator, making subgoal dependencies explicit. This addresses a key gap in prior free-form task synthesis: agents may complete subtasks individually but fail to chain them into multi-goal workflows. Program-first synthesis enables scalable, dependency-aware training data for cross-app GUI automation.

entry.title: WaveView: The Novel View Is in the Noise

author.name: Kaiwen Wang, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Yinzhe Shen, Frank Bieder, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: WaveView enables generative novel view synthesis by injecting a warped source view into the phase of the initial noise of a pretrained diffusion generator using a Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Packet Transform. This constrains the generator less in disoccluded regions and along epipolar lines than prior warp-based or conditioning-based methods, adding negligible overhead with no architecture changes. A clever, low-cost trick for camera-controllable generation.

entry.title: One Shot, Any View: High-Fidelity Video Reshooting with Geometry Guidance and Visual References

author.name: Kai Huang, Runze Xu, Hui Ren, Taiyi Wu, Xinyuan Li, Xun Gao, Quande Liu, Dong Tang, Tongtong Shen, Xuefeng Su, Alan Zhao

entry.summary: This system takes a recorded clip and generates a reshot video of the same performance along a user-specified camera trajectory, conditioning generation on the source video and a point-video 3D prior from feed-forward reconstruction. It specifically targets hard human-centric cinematic footage with shallow depth of field and low-key lighting that degrades reconstruction.

entry.title: Where Should a Diffusion Transformer Meet Its Teacher?

author.name: Zhuoqi Hu, Shiwei Li, Haozhao Wang, Xiandi Luo, Yihao Ouyang, Wenting Shen, Ang Wang, Jiamang Wang, Minyi Guo, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: This paper studies Representation Alignment (REPA) for Diffusion Transformer training and finds the most effective teacher-alignment layer changes over training. AdaREPA uses gradient compatibility between flow-matching and alignment objectives to adaptively route supervision to the best layer online via a softmax sampling scheme. This improves training acceleration without costly layer search.

entry.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events

author.name: Rong Zou, Haiqing Hao, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: ALIVE incrementally updates frozen DINOv3 foundation model features between image frames using event camera data, avoiding repeated expensive encoder runs. A lightweight updater trained purely on synthetic data transfers directly to real-world event streams. This addresses feature staleness in dynamic visual scenes efficiently.

entry.title: Lossless Reversible Watermarking for AIGC with Applications in Authentication

author.name: Yupeng Qiu, Han Fang, Ee-Chien Chang

entry.summary: Introduces a lossless reversible watermarking framework for AI-generated content that allows exact recovery of the original watermarked image after permissible distortions, exploiting the low entropy of generation information. Applied to AIGC authentication and tampering detection against adaptive adversaries.

entry.title: LaST1.0: A Unified Latent World-Action Model with Control-Centric SpatioTemporal Reasoning

author.name: Hao Chen, Xuheng Zhang, Zhuangzhe Wu, Jiaming Liu, Shaobo Zhang, Jialin Gao, Zhonghao Yan, Di Wu, Sixiang Chen, Peng Jia, Chi-Wing Fu, Shanghang Zhang, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: LaST1.0 reformulates world modeling for manipulation as control-centric future prediction in latent space, predicting compact geometry-aware latent targets derived from future wrist views instead of reconstructing full videos. This focuses model capacity on the robot-object interactions that matter for fine-grained control rather than incidental appearance detail.

entry.title: Asymmetric Decomposition for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Unassigned Agents

author.name: Xi Jin, Chen Qian, Renjun Zhang, Guowei Wu, Xiaobo Li, Jun Jiang, Weiwei Shang

entry.summary: This paper introduces flow-oracle conflict-based search (FOCBS) for multi-agent path finding where unassigned, taskless robots can obstruct active ones. It routes targetless agents via a min-cost flow oracle and uses flow-conflict branching to convert blockers into constraints without sacrificing optimality, with warm-start and tie-breaking accelerations. This matters for warehouse and multi-robot deployments where idle robots are unavoidable.

entry.title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief

author.name: Cameron Mehlman, Arjun Mulchandani, Hovik Grigoryan, Anurag Koyyada, Gregory Falco

entry.summary: Inspired by card players coordinating without communication, this paper shows that anchoring decentralized agents to a shared external witness—whose reactions encode team state—enables communication-free coordination, with an allocentric belief network letting each agent independently reconstruct full team state. This avoids fragile explicit communication and complex state estimation in multi-agent systems.

entry.title: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Apoorva Vashisth, Manav Kulshrestha, Damon Conover, Zachary Kingston, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: RePlan-VLA is a VLA-agnostic execution framework that wraps short-horizon vision-language-action policies with progress monitoring and adaptive replanning, translating their manipulation competence into reliable long-horizon task execution. The framework explicitly tracks motion progress and revises future plans when errors occur, rather than burdening the VLA with full long-horizon reasoning. It targets multi-step robotic manipulation tasks.

entry.title: How Reward Gain Imbalance Shapes Ranking: Rethinking Rubric-Based Reward Aggregation

author.name: Zhengyuan Fan, Zhonghua Wu, Tianyu Cheng, Qun Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes reward gain imbalance in rubric-based RLHF — criteria contributing with differing gaps between expected scores on satisfied versus unsatisfied responses — and shows this heterogeneity can distort candidate rankings in counterintuitive ways. The work challenges the assumption that uniform aggregation of judge scores is adequate for preference alignment.

entry.title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Wenhao Li, Zhongyi Han, Yuhao Wei, Liang Han, Yilong Yin, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Identifies that few-shot VLA policies silently memorize the camera-to-base extrinsic from data collection, so small bumps to the tripod or robot base cause failures, and unifies both failure modes as extrinsic change. It proposes WACO, a world-anchored canonicalization framework that uses the robot arm positioned by forward kinematics as a metric calibration target to undo extrinsic shifts. This addresses a real robustness gap in robot learning with few demonstrations.

entry.title: Stability Does Not Mirror Plasticity: A Module-Level View of Declarative and Procedural Learning in Transformers

author.name: Jinjun Peng, Wailiang Zhao, Baishakhi Ray, Zhou Yu, Jufeng Yang

entry.summary: This study examines plasticity and stability in continual learning at the level of individual transformer modules rather than whole models, drawing on the cognitive distinction between declarative and procedural memory. In a controlled synthetic environment it shows a double dissociation: QK and VO projections are most plastic on procedural tasks while MLPs are most plastic on declarative memorization, and stability does not simply mirror plasticity. This has direct implications for targeted continual-learning interventions and model editing.

entry.title: Objective-Specialized Residual Streams in Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections

author.name: Shantanu Agarwal, Ruchita V. Maitri, Zhiqi Huang, Vivek Datla, Alfy Samuel

entry.summary: Studies whether assigning distinct learning objectives to different streams in manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), which extend the Transformer residual stream into parallel streams, improves performance. Using complementary lexical and semantic retrieval objectives, objective-specialized mHC consistently outperforms non-specialized variants across fusion ranges and model scales, with probes revealing internal specialization.

entry.title: DOCK: Dual-Stream-Inspired Self-Supervised Object-Centric Representations Grounded in Robot Kinematics

author.name: Pengju Liu, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: DOCK shows with simulator-executed futures that feature distance in six frozen DINO and V-JEPA encoders barely tracks object distance to goal (rank correlation at most 0.11 vs 0.87 for object-mask centroids), being dominated by background and robot patches. Inspired by ventral/dorsal visual streams, it learns an object representation whose changes agree with robot kinematics for latent-space planning. This is a rigorous critique of a core assumption in latent-space planners.

entry.title: Spark-H3: Adaptive Block Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Zecheng Tang, Jiaye Fu, Youtian Lin, Xinyao Rao, Liuxuan Sun, Jian Zhang, Yao Yao, Wei Li

entry.summary: Spark-Attn is a training-free block sparse attention method for video diffusion models comprising Spark-Reblock, which recursively groups tokens by attention preference while keeping GPU-friendly block shapes, and Spark-Reweight, which builds attention-weighted key-value representations anchored on the global mean query to fix underestimated compressed-block attention mass.

entry.title: ShoWorld: Shape-Faithful Multi-Hypothesis Occupancy World Model

author.name: Zhiqiang Yan, Guangfa Wang, Yuan Wu, Jian Yang, Gim Hee Lee

entry.summary: ShoWorld is an occupancy world model that addresses motion uncertainty and shape distortion in forecasting moving objects by separating motion and shape representations. A motion forecaster predicts probabilistic trajectory hypotheses that are rendered into occupancy and fused by probability, while a shape component predicts sub-voxel points that move rigidly to preserve object geometry. This avoids averaging plausible futures into implausible paths and re-voxelization shape erosion.

entry.title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Junlin Long, Xu Deng, Yiran Wang, Yue Yang, Yang Zhao, Zeyu Zhang

entry.summary: Adapts arm-pretrained world action models to language-conditioned quadrupedal loco-manipulation via cross-morphology policy adaptation, on-policy self-distillation into a fast student, and a task-specific refinement stage. Enables legged robots to manipulate with a front leg while balancing on three others following language instructions.

entry.title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers

author.name: Ramani Duraiswami, Yichao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a differentiable physical renderer that fits atoms, microscope, and detector parameters directly to recorded 4D-STEM electron counts under a Poisson likelihood, outputting atoms as Gaussian primitives with Fisher-information-based error bars. Provides per-atom uncertainty and dose requirements, which prior reconstruction codes lack.

entry.title: BEV-Diffusion: Camera-Only Traversability Navigation with BEV Memory and Efficient Cross-Robot Adaptation

author.name: Iana Zhura, Timofei Kozlov, Dmitrii Plotnikov, Ivan Valuev, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: BEV-Diffusion is a camera-only navigation model that jointly predicts bird's-eye-view traversability maps, uncertainty, and paths using a frozen DINOv2 backbone with Bayesian fusion and a transformer denoiser generating polar waypoints in few DDIM steps. It achieves graded traversability (median 0.94 vs 0.75) and supports efficient adaptation across different robots. It reduces dependence on expensive LiDAR and modular navigation stacks.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities

author.name: Hoang Pham Cong, Long D. Nguyen, Ho Viet Duc Luong, Nguyen Tran Minh Nhat, Binh P. Nguyen, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: Analyzes what portion of prediction error remains correctable when a deployed multimodal model loses modalities after weights are frozen, characterizing it via the Bayes gap between the model's prediction and the Bayes prediction on observed modalities. It shows excess risk captures this gap for cross-entropy and squared loss, and leverages predictions from richer-modality models to estimate correction without labels. A theoretically grounded approach to deployment-time robustness.

entry.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Sachith Abeywickrama, Peiliang Gong, Emadeldeen Eldele, Min Wu, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: Addresses domain-incremental adaptation of time-series foundation models, showing that under operating-condition shifts the embedding space changes non-uniformly, so global adaptation unnecessarily perturbs already-correct regions. The method adapts selectively based on this geometric structure, improving new conditions without forgetting old ones, from small calibration sets and without condition labels at inference. A principled take on continual adaptation of TSFMs.

entry.title: Reducing Inference Cost of Coding Agents with Timeout Cascades

author.name: Boxi Zhou, German Sviridov, Dmitrii Ustiugov, Haris Javaid

entry.summary: The paper evaluates 36 open-weight large and small models on a software engineering benchmark and finds recent small models nearly match large ones except on hard tasks. It then proposes timeout cascades that route between model sizes to cut coding-agent inference cost without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code

author.name: Zipeng Qiu, Shusheng Xu, Jiale Li, Yukun Zhou, Chenyue Li, Wenshuang Li, Tongkai Yang, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: The paper studies self-improving agents for real-time visual games where the agent sees only the screen, comparing model-as-policy (with real-time chunking so actions execute while the model reasons, using a trained 2B controller) against code-as-policy (the model writes, tests, and revises a program between attempts). Across 170 GameWorld tasks with at most eight one-minute attempts, it shows how agents can self-improve from few of their own attempts.

entry.title: Ephyra: A Property-Based Testing Framework for the LLM Era

author.name: Alperen Keles

entry.summary: Ephyra is a property-based testing library in Rust redesigned for the era of agent-written tests, built on customizability, observability, and generator synthesis. Users can compose testing loops from generation, mutation, and shrinking components and synthesize these to satisfy functional predicates. Applied to 14 open-source systems, it found 349 bugs with 300 reported, including in SQLite, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, DataFusion, the Cedar policy engine, and Node.js URL parsing.

entry.title: Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language

author.name: S{\o}ren Taverniers, Eric Darve, Hamdi A. Tchelepi

entry.summary: This paper presents an agentic harness for LLM-coordinated multi-physics simulation from natural-language descriptions, with explicit task allocation: LLMs interpret requests and diagnostics, generate components outside predefined rules, and propose repairs, while deterministic routines construct, check, and validate inputs and results. It is evaluated on CO2-storage problems using the GEOS simulator, up to flow-poromechanics with frictional faults.

entry.title: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates

author.name: Jiapeng Pei, Yuhang Yao, Sitan Liu, Hanxin Chen, Hao Li, Guogeng Li, Jiapei Liu, Ruijie Chen, Hongshan Lin, Yang Mo, Tianyu Shi, Shangding Gu

entry.summary: The paper presents Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation component for a personal health assistant that restricts recursive self-improvement to prompt updates while keeping weights and runtime code fixed. Proposed instruction changes are tested against benchmarks, with failing cases repeated, temporary rollbacks used to guide repairs, and safety plus task checks required before adoption. The executable benchmark spans 29 email, calendar, health, and marketplace cases with authorization probes.

entry.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Hongxu Chen, Chun Wang, Yanghao Wang, Hongxiang Li, Zhen Wang, Zhixiang Zhang, Long Chen

entry.summary: Addresses the off-manifold problem in latent diffusion VAEs caused by unregularized latent dimension expansion, proposing a dual-manifold design that regularizes the latent manifold without relying on frozen external priors like DINOv2, which the authors argue restricts generalization due to pre-training biases. The approach aims to keep generated latents on-manifold while improving reconstruction quality.

entry.title: FormalFixer: Intent-Aligned Automated Hardware Repair via Joint Refinement of Specifications, Assertions, and RTL Implementations

author.name: Changyuan Yu, Hongce Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces FormalFixer, a multi-stage automated repair system for hardware designs that jointly refines specifications, formal assertions, and RTL implementations, recognizing that failed formal property verification may stem from buggy assertions or ambiguous specifications rather than RTL defects. This addresses an alignment problem between design intent, verification intent, and implementation that existing RTL-centric repair loops ignore.

entry.title: Grading Executable Legal Rules Against Independent Records: Transitional Provisions and Korean SME Status

author.name: Jinhyung Bae

entry.summary: Introduces LexTemporis, which grades LLM-written legal rule programs against real-world records — 10,901 firm-years of Korean SME status with all governing rule versions — rather than against answers from someone reading the same law, avoiding shared-interpretation bias. An appendix adds US tax and German hospital cases, and analysis shows date changes hinge on provisions outside the main statutory text.

entry.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents

author.name: Stavros Damianakis, Konstantinos Psounis

entry.summary: Presents AutoPI, an adaptive red-teaming agent that uses PIAtlas, a taxonomy of prompt-injection techniques, to discover many distinct ways to break an LLM agent rather than maximizing attack success rate with a few reused tricks. It argues diversity of discovered attacks matters for hardening, since high ASR can mask untested technique classes. The taxonomy guides both search and coverage measurement.

entry.title: Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs

author.name: Xiaolin Lin, Kai-Chiang Wu, Bing Li, Grace Li Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SkimPrefill, which accelerates first-token latency for vision-language models on ~100K-token interleaved inputs by using a small hybrid model to identify the few relevant images or paragraphs with a single early-layer attention head, even at half image resolution. This avoids the costly self-scoring that erases the savings of input pruning. A practical efficiency contribution for long-context multimodal inference.

entry.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour

author.name: Haoran Ye, Tianrui Huo, Hangzhen Li, Xin Zhang, Guojie Song

entry.summary: Chiron is a foundation model fine-tuned from an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics, trained on 36 behavioural domains, 78 social-science experiments, and nearly 1.5 million atomic behavioural decisions. It addresses the tendency of general LLMs to misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics in behavioural simulation.

entry.title: TRACE-MAS: Diagnosing and Repairing Collaboration Failures in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zekai Chen, Yihan Sun, Xunkai Li, Xun Wu, Xinmo Jin, Yinlin Zhu, Haodong Lu, Xuaner Chen, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: TRACE-MAS is a fine-grained framework for diagnosing and repairing failures in LLM-based multi-agent systems by modeling interactions (message exchanges, task dependencies) rather than only individual agent behavior. It learns normal collaborative execution patterns from benign trajectories, detects deviations across agent state changes, message transitions, and dependency evolution, and identifies responsible execution elements for repair. Addresses a real gap as MAS safeguards to date focus on agent-level anomaly detection.

entry.title: What Interpolators Store and What They Express: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Benign Overfitting and Label-Free Model Selection

author.name: Nikolaos Nikolaou

entry.summary: This paper develops an information-theoretic framework that decomposes what an interpolating learner retains about its training labels (storage) from what reaches its predictions on fresh inputs (expression). It characterizes the ideal model via minimal sufficient complexity and connects this to benign overfitting and label-free model selection. The work also generalizes and corrects an earlier lossless maximal compression view of boosting.

entry.title: Latent Action Policies from Suboptimal Data

author.name: Donghyeon Ki, Xiaoyu Chen, Jun Ho Seo, Hayeong Lee, Kyungyoon Kim, Byung-Jun Lee, Li Zhao

entry.summary: This work studies training latent policies from latent action models learned on action-free video, showing that naive offline RL in latent action spaces is unreliable because optimization can yield unrealizable latent actions or merge physically distinct controls with different rewards. The authors derive conditions under which latent-space optimization remains valid and propose methods for policy improvement from suboptimal data.

entry.title: How Uncertain Is My Action? Self-Correcting Visual Planning with Frozen World Models

author.name: Siqing Li, Luming Yang, Yijia Jiao, Junze Deng, Alper Yilmaz

entry.summary: This work introduces a method for frozen latent world models used in visual MPC to detect and correct actuation shifts at deployment by running the model in reverse: predicting what should have been observed under a hypothesized shift and comparing against reality. The resulting shift score supports locally optimal detection and Cramer-Rao-style error bounds.

entry.title: Same Model, Different People: Numerical Execution Contracts and the Reproducibility of Fairness Audits

author.name: Erzheng Zhang, Agnes Chu

entry.summary: This paper shows that fairness audit outcomes can change solely with the numerical execution contract, varying arithmetic order and precision while holding model weights byte-identical, and separately testing reduced-precision deployment configs (BF16, FP8, 8-bit). It audits tabular model families and open-weight LLMs on public tasks to quantify reproducibility risks.

entry.title: A Fast, Programmable GPU-to-CPU Invocation Layer for GPU-Initiated Communication

author.name: Jiakun Yan, Shiksha Patel, David Sidler, Gengyu Rao, Brandon Potter, Bradford Beckmann

entry.summary: The paper presents KIWI, a programmable reverse-offload framework enabling GPU kernels to invoke host-side communication operations with sub-microsecond one-way device-to-host latency. It argues that reverse offload should be a first-class communication path rather than a fallback to GPUDirect Async, and exposes workload-specific communication as a user-facing programming interface. This is relevant to large-scale training and inference systems where device-initiated communication is increasingly important.

entry.title: Nearly Tight Almost Sure Convergence Rates for the Last iterate of SGD

author.name: Weiming Ou, Andrea Paudice, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: This work establishes almost sure convergence rates for the last iterate of stochastic (sub)gradient descent on convex objectives: k^-1/3 with a stationary minimizer and k^-1/4 without, up to polylog factors, using deterministic anytime stepsize schedules. Matching lower bounds prove these exponents optimal for the corresponding problem classes. This resolves a fundamental question in the pathwise analysis of SGD.

entry.title: ProbMedTOD: A Bayesian Network Guided Task-Oriented Dialogue System for Patient History Taking

author.name: Vishal Vivek Saley, Bhavesh Gurnani, Dinesh Raghu, Mausam

entry.summary: Proposes ProbMedTOD, a task-oriented dialogue system for patient history taking that combines small language models with Bayesian Networks to provide the deliberative System 2 reasoning needed to track diagnostic uncertainty. The Bayesian framework offers interpretable, auditable probabilistic belief updating, complementing SLM intuitions while respecting privacy, cost, and latency constraints.

entry.title: Bits, Not Boxes: Label-Free Layer Selection for Visual Localization in VLMs

author.name: Haisheng Fu, Gexin Huang, Haikai Zhao, Jie Liang, Zhenman Fang, Jingning Han, Xiaoxiao Li

entry.summary: This paper shows that attention in vision-language models can identify which layers localize a queried object without box annotations, by separating how much a head attends to the image from where the attention goes. The latter, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, yields WhereBits, a layer prior combined with per-head contrastive scores for localization. Design constants are fixed once on COCO and transfer, addressing attention-sink unreliability in VLM localization.

entry.title: Layer-Matched Sparse Attention for Low-Redundancy 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Sammam Mahdi, Fariha Binta Salim, K. M. Jubair Sami, Rakin Bin Rabbani

entry.summary: This work accelerates VGGT's feed-forward 3D reconstruction by tracing why training-free attention thinning loses pose accuracy on low-redundancy views: diffuse layers aggregate distributed context while matching layers depend on query-specific interactions. A per-layer statistic (logit variance as a row-free proxy) selects per-layer estimators, using shared importance sampling for diffuse layers and different treatment for matching layers. This preserves accuracy while reducing quadratic global attention cost.

entry.title: GaussLearner: 3D Gaussian Primitives as Self-Regulating Continual Learners

author.name: Gaoxiang Linghu, Haonan Zhou, Xuanhe Liu, Weili Xu, Kaiyue Zhou, Jun Xiao, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: GaussLearner tackles catastrophic forgetting in continual 3D Gaussian field reconstruction by treating each Gaussian primitive as its own continual learner with a closed loop of observation, self-regulation, and adaptation. This per-primitive design aims to balance adapting to scene changes against preserving still-valid content, going beyond selective optimization, replay, or parameter regularization. It is relevant for maintaining up-to-date 3D reconstructions in dynamic environments such as robotics.

entry.title: ROBIN++: Unified Copyright Protection and Tamper Localization for Diffusion Models via Dual-Domain Synergistic Watermarking

author.name: Huayang Huang, Siqi Zeng, Qian Wang, Bo Du, Yu Wu

entry.summary: ROBIN++ decouples copyright robustness and tamper-fragility into distinct domains for diffusion-generated images: a frequency-domain copyright watermark injected with adversarial optimization plus a fragile watermark, re-coupled at verification time. This resolves the inherent trade-off between copyright robustness and localization sensitivity in single-domain watermarking and unifies provenance verification with tamper localization. It addresses pressing provenance needs as generative content proliferates.

entry.title: From Restoration to Redrawing: Revitalizing Ancient Chinese Characters by SVG Code Generation and Editing

author.name: Weiguang Zhang, Linhua Dong, Bin Dong, Shanshan Jiang, Maizhen Ning, Xiaoqiang Kang, Kun Zhang, Hao Xu, Xiaowei Huang, Wei Wang, Kaizhu Huang, Qiufeng Wang

entry.summary: ReDraw reformulates restoration of damaged Han Dynasty bamboo-slip manuscripts as SVG code generation and editing using a two-stage VLM: faithful vectorization of observed strokes followed by conservative completion guided by skeleton chain-of-thought and structure-aware reinforcement learning. This preserves stroke geometry with controllable edits, mirroring expert redrawing practice. A culturally significant application combining VLMs, RL, and vector graphics.

entry.title: ViStep-RL: Stepwise Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Visual Agents

author.name: Junyang Chen, Yao Qin, Xiao Li, Ningchao Wang, Yiguo Qiao, Wenbin Li, Xin Geng

entry.summary: ViStep-RL models long-horizon visual agent execution as a dependency-linked graph of evidence-bearing subgoals, using a verifier and graph-potential changes as a net-progress reward signal. An active memory protocol preserves evidence across turns and ties retrieval to downstream use.

entry.title: CanopyKV: Remember beyond the Crop for Fast Active Visual Reasoning

author.name: Lei Yang, Dayan Wu, Yiliang Zhu, Xinze Liu, Hengjie Zhu, Zihao Zhang, Ding Wang, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin

entry.summary: CanopyKV addresses KV cache growth in active visual reasoning, where multimodal models iteratively inspect image crops and accumulate tokens. It distinguishes locally replaced evidence from complementary earlier-view information that standard attention/recency/redundancy criteria would discard, retaining evidence needed for future exploration. This reduces memory and inference cost while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate

author.name: Yuhe Liu, Qi Li, Shihua Zhang, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Jeveration shows that fast parallel-prediction models can generate high-quality images in a single forward pass, building on a frozen vision-language model. The key challenge of global consistency among parallel predictions is solved by conditioning all positions on a shared random state, with a staged training scheme to prevent the model ignoring that state. Each draw yields a different but coherent image.

entry.title: RageVLA: Augmentation-Trained Perception and Action for State-of-the-Art Robustness on LIBERO

author.name: Amrit Lal Singh, Smarak Kanjilal

entry.summary: Argues VLA policy brittleness on LIBERO-PRO stems from entanglement of what-to-do with scene layout and instruction wording rather than lack of scale. Introduces systematic data augmentation (moving/rotating objects, retasking environments, paraphrasing instructions) plus a decoupled perception engine over frozen DINOv3 features, achieving state-of-the-art robustness.

entry.title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading

author.name: Argyrios Zafeiriou, Athanasios Kallipolitis, Ilias Maglogiannis

entry.summary: Builds an interpretable prostate cancer grading system on a sparse code over pathology foundation model tokens, aligning 69 of 2048 sparse autoencoder features with multi-reader Gleason morphology annotations (e.g., cribriform glands, comedonecrosis). The same features drive both grading predictions and human-readable morphology maps, evaluated across five public datasets.

entry.title: 3DTouch: A Tactile-aware VLA Model with 3D Geometric Relations for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Xin Zhang, Shiqi Zhang, Siyuan Cao, Juncheng Cai, Yedong Shen, Yuxuan Gao, Dianlong Wen, Kaixue Long, Lu Zhang, Yao Li, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: 3DTouch augments VLA models with a shared 3D visuo-tactile representation built by expressing RGB-D scene points and dense five-finger tactile measurements in the robot-base frame, preserving taxel locations and force vectors. Hand-object and object-object geometric relations from landmarks and pose-aligned surfaces condition the policy for contact-rich dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Assessing Vision-Language Models for Early Prediction of Unsafe Situations in Robotics

author.name: Muhammad Farooq, Aitor Arrieta, Paolo Arcaini, Shaukat Ali, Thomas Peyrucain

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates general-purpose VLMs (Qwen, InternVL, LLaVA-OneVision) for predicting robot failures before they occur, across three robotic case studies using video and odometry data. It assesses classification of safe, potentially unsafe, and unsafe situations with uncertainty quantification. The work provides evidence on whether current VLMs can serve as early-warning safety monitors for robots.

entry.title: CommDreamer: Radio-Geometric World Models for Mapless Cellular-Connected UAV Trajectory Planning

author.name: Yuqi Ping, Tianhao Liang, Tingting Zhang

entry.summary: CommDreamer is a mapless radio-geometric world model that fuses onboard 3D LiDAR, cellular network reports, and relative kinematics to jointly infer obstacle clearance and signal-to-interference conditions for UAV flight in urban canyons. It avoids dependence on prior 3D city meshes and channel maps while improving sample efficiency and cross-city generalization versus model-free RL. It jointly targets connectivity and collision-free trajectory planning.

entry.title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers have equipped a flapping-wing aerial microrobot with onboard sensors and computation, enabling it to follow complex trajectories and land precisely on a sunflower outside a motion-capture lab for the first time. The robot still relies on offboard power, but the achievement points toward autonomous microrobots for precision pollination and crop monitoring where natural pollinators have declined.

entry.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs

author.name: Xi Ding, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: SpecLook is a training-free speculate-and-verify framework for multimodal agents that use zoom-in tool calls. Instead of speculating answers, a small model drafts a plausible next observation (glimpse) which can be verified and used to test the agent's answer, cutting the slow sequential tool loop. This improves both speed and reliability calibration of agentic multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Luca Lusvarghi, Javier Gozalvez

entry.summary: Brings the long-standing debate about whether attention weights reflect causal input relevance into autonomous driving, comparing attention-based relevance estimates against counterfactual analysis of object impact on driving decisions. The findings question the common practice of using attention for interpretability in AV systems. Important for safety-critical interpretability claims.

entry.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules

author.name: Mingliang Zhai, Chuanhao Li, Jiaming Tan, Zhen Li, Yuwei Wu, Yunde Jia, Zian Meng, Yuanyang Yin, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: WorldRuler addresses user-defined rule following in generative world models, identifying two challenges: Rule-State Persistence (preserving rule definitions and world state across save/load) and Rule-to-Visual Realization (realizing rule-induced changes, including on unseen objects). The system organizes rule definitions so that restored worlds continue to obey established rules beyond real-world behavior priors. This extends world models toward customizable, game-like interactive environments.

entry.title: SurgCBVR: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Content-Based Surgical Video-to-Video Retrieval

author.name: Mohammad Eslami, Mousa Moradi, Negin Ghamsarian, Nazlee Zebardast, Jennifer L Lindsey, Sophia Y. Wang, Lucia Sobrin, Rishi P Singh, Tobias Elze

entry.summary: SurgCBVR introduces the first benchmark for content-based video-to-video retrieval in surgery, integrating eight public datasets across ophthalmic, laparoscopic, robotic-assisted, and colonoscopy domains with 679 cases and 76,489 clips. It defines two retrieval tiers, Scene and Workflow, enabling retrieval of similar operative states and localization of phase transitions across cases and sites.

entry.title: The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI

author.name: Jalal Mahmud, Eser Kandogan

entry.summary: The paper proposes the Value Semantics Layer (VSL), an architectural abstraction that externalizes value-level operational semantics as persistent, planner-visible infrastructure for databases serving LLM agents. It introduces Value Semantic Types capturing distributional, relational, process, quantitative, and policy-grounded semantics, enabling planners to validate analytical operations rather than merely describe schemas. This addresses a gap in existing metadata systems for agentic data access.

entry.title: SEE: Unlocking the Hidden Perception of Frozen VLMs

author.name: Alin-Ionut Popa, Tuo Zhang, Dimitrios Dimitriadis

entry.summary: Proposes Self-Elicited Evidence (SEE), a training-free method where a frozen vision-language model, when uncertain, proposes candidate regions containing fine details, re-answers on enlarged crops, and aggregates answers via confidence-weighted voting, including self-transcription for text-rich images. This recovers fine-grained perception without any model updates.

entry.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Shiwei Wu, Yuwen Pan, Zhi Li, Yaowen Li, Yan Zhou, Xuemiao Xu, Yu Liu

entry.summary: Presents AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework where an aerial vision-language-action navigation policy learns from its own failures, judging candidate repair actions by flying onward from the policy's own failure states. Under this judging scheme, even rule-based proposals that hurt under direct imitation become reliable supervision for closed-loop flight improvement.

entry.title: Efficient Variance-Aware Reinforcement Learning in Time-Inhomogeneous Linear MDPs

author.name: Qingyue Zhao, Qiwei Di, Jiafan He, Heyang Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: The paper proposes VA-LSVI-UCB++, a computationally efficient algorithm achieving variance-dependent regret for episodic time-inhomogeneous linear MDPs, removing the polynomial O(K^1/4) additive term that persisted in prior variance-aware analyses even in deterministic environments. Building on variance-aware results for linear mixture MDPs and minimax results for linear MDPs, it closes a theoretical gap in the RL literature. A solid theoretical contribution from an established RL group (Quanquan Gu's lab).

entry.title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics

author.name: Favour Nerrise, Julian Busch, Gurpreet Singh Hora, Martin Sipka, Danielle C. Maddix, Georgia Olympia Brikis

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic benchmark of transfer behavior for neural surrogates of vehicle aerodynamics, pretraining five surrogates on DrivAerML and evaluating zero-shot and few-shot adaptation across four target datasets differing in geometry and CFD setup. The goal is pretrained surrogates that adapt to new vehicle classes with only a few simulations while remaining accurate on the pretraining domain.

entry.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm

author.name: Zhouxing Luo, Lei Wang, Xin Liu

entry.summary: This theoretical work addresses vulnerability of PCA to distributional uncertainty using distributionally robust optimization. The authors show that the infinity-Wasserstein distance yields a DRO formulation of PCA that both preserves the nominal PCA subspace and admits an exact finite-dimensional reformulation, and they identify an explicit worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. The paper also provides finite-sample generalization guarantees and an efficient algorithm, with the reformulated objective retaining samplewise residual structure.

entry.title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation

author.name: Samet Demir, Zafer Dogan

entry.summary: Analyzes two-layer networks trained with SGD on a multi-index teacher model, decomposing first-layer weights into teacher-aligned signal and orthogonal components. The paper shows that teacher-dependent spectral spikes emerge in the orthogonal complement Gram matrix, providing a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified and generalization degrades.

entry.title: Detect What You Need: Chain-of-Causal Reasoning for 3D Intent Grounding

author.name: Zihao Zhang, Aming Wu, Yang Li, Yahong Han

entry.summary: The paper introduces 3D Intention Grounding, localizing target 3D objects given abstract, non-descriptive natural-language intents rather than descriptive referring expressions. The proposed Chain-of-Causal Reasoning approach makes latent functional-requirement inference explicit, improving interpretability, robustness, and generalization over implicit intent-object matching. It connects causal reasoning with 3D grounding, pushing toward AI that understands what users want rather than what they describe.

entry.title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards

author.name: Yeongtak Oh, Donghyeok Lee, Joonhee Oh, Jaewon Jeong, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: PReMind-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark evaluating whether personalized vision-language assistants can combine visible physical hazards with personal context such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints to give appropriate advice. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, including joint success on interdependency cases. The paper exposes that current models often satisfy one requirement while failing the combination, which matters for safe personal AI assistants.

entry.title: SIGNTOK: A Text-Aligned Continuous Pose Tokenizer for Sign Language Generation

author.name: Nabeela Khan, Gaurav Rai, Bowen Wu, Sihan Tan, Benjamin Yen, Takeshi Ashizawa, Kazuhiro Nakadai

entry.summary: SIGNTOK is a continuous pose tokenizer for text-conditioned sign language generation whose latent space is shaped by auxiliary training heads aligning signing with kinematics, sentence-level text, and word-level content. The authors show existing pose and latent spaces are organized by signer identity rather than linguistic content, with nearest-neighbor matches only 2% on CSL-Daily. This improves the representation foundation for accessibility-oriented generation.

entry.title: NativeSeg: Native Vision Language Segmentation of 3D Computed Tomography via Spatial Visual Tokens and Verified Local Zoom

author.name: Chengqian Ma, Gaole Dai, Zijie Meng, Weixuan Jin, Yijie Du, Yuexiao Ma, Xiawu Zheng, Fei Chao

entry.summary: NativeSeg is a native vision-language segmentation framework for text-prompted 3D CT segmentation built on LoRA-adapted Qwen3.8-27B, performing dense mask decoding inside the VLM instead of delegating to external SAM decoders or codebooks. It uses spatial visual tokens and verified local zoom to handle volumes where most organ-prompted slices lack the queried target. This addresses full-slice context plus fine boundary precision in medical VLMs.

entry.title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models

author.name: Zejian Kang, Yeqiang Wang, Zekai Chen, Boyang Shen, Mingyu Ma, Bingqian Wu, Fan Zhou, Jianjie Zhang, Chentao Shen, Wentao Yang, Rui Qian, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: Proposes training humanoid motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated physical executions, with the insight that alignment must be judged on the motion the robot actually executes rather than the kinematic reference. Uses a differentiable world model and fixed tracking controller to backpropagate semantic evaluation through physics.

entry.title: LoRN: Low-Rank Noise Steering for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Wei Liu, Abrar Anwar, Huihua Zhao, Soha Pouya, Yan Chang

entry.summary: LoRN scales noise steering to world-action models via reinforcement learning, where a small steering actor selects directions through fixed low-rank random projections with norm-controlled construction. The work finds actions in world-action models are more sensitive to video noise than action noise, making video noise an expressive steering input without weight updates.

entry.title: RecallFlow: Episodic Memory as the Source Distribution of Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Xuji Zhang, Qilin Zhong, Zichen Zhang, Wei Zhai, Jian Di, Kun Li, Yang Cao, Wenjun Lv

entry.summary: RecallFlow reframes memory-dependent robot manipulation by treating episodic memory as the source distribution for generative visuomotor policies built on diffusion or flow matching. Instead of conditioning on a raw observation history and starting action generation from uninformative Gaussian noise, the approach initializes generation from memory-derived distributions, reducing spurious correlations when targets are no longer visible. This is a meaningful architectural contribution for imitation learning policies that must act on information outside the current view.

entry.title: The Spectral Distribution of Matrix Least Squares Solutions, and the Ellipsoid Fitting Problem

author.name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Yue M. Lu, Petar Nizi\'{c}-Nikolac

entry.summary: The authors derive closed-form descriptions of the spectral distribution support for least squares solutions to random linear systems with symmetric matrix unknowns, applying this to the ellipsoid fitting problem. They show least squares candidates exhibit a positive semi-definiteness threshold connected to the recently discovered sharp satisfiability phase transition at n approximately d^2/4.

entry.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents

author.name: Kaiwen Shi, Zheyuan Zhang, Weixiang Sun, Han Bao, Colby Nelson, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: LProp addresses the problem that LLM agents pass tentative judgments downstream as if they were facts when uncertainty is not propagated. It introduces Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator preserving revision-relevant information without verbose descriptions, and revises inherited answer distributions as new evidence arrives without extra trajectory sampling. This improves multi-step agent reliability at low cost.

entry.title: Space-X: Self-Evolving Spatial Agents Weaving Clues into Evidence Chains

author.name: Zijian Zhang, Wenqing Tian, Qiang Liu, Liang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Space-X, a spatial reasoning framework in which an Execution Agent acquires and judges evidence while a Control Agent diagnoses breaks in evidence chains from execution traces and revises tools, interfaces, skills, memory, and decision rules. Targets the problem that more tool calls do not reliably improve spatial reasoning due to inconsistent semantics and poor evidence sufficiency judgments. Part of the growing self-improving agent literature.

entry.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers

author.name: Guijia Zhang, Hongbo Qiu, Jiajun Zha, Guohao Cai, Hao Zheng, Huihao Jing, Kexu Cheng, Shipeng Luo, JinYang Huang, Shing-Chi Cheung, Changsheng Lu, Haoxuan Che, Harry Yang

entry.summary: This work benchmarks autonomous figure-text inconsistency detection on 31 full manuscripts containing reviewer-documented inconsistencies, where models must locate the figure worth checking, relate visual elements to claims, and recognize conflicts without being handed the claim or told an inconsistency exists. Six multimodal models are evaluated under neutral prompts with progressive input additions.

entry.title: When Code Works but the License Doesn't: Evaluating License Constraint Handling in Coding Agents

author.name: Sundaraparipurnan Narayanan, Sandeep Vishwakarma

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether coding agents recognize and preserve software-license constraints when developing proprietary software, testing permissive and copyleft licenses, missing information, transitive dependencies, dual licensing, vendoring, and distribution contexts. Agent traces and artifacts are evaluated against licensing ground truth, revealing a persistent gap between functional success and licensing correctness. Existing agent benchmarks prioritize functional success and ignore this compliance dimension.

entry.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games

author.name: Chaipat Tirapongprasert, Rajarshi Das, Parijat Dube

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability techniques on LLM agents playing iterated games with incomplete information, this paper finds that models form and iteratively revise internal representations of the game throughout chain-of-thought reasoning. It further finds that once a model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers, a failure visible in both the trace text and layer activations.

entry.title: Reliability is a user-specific property of large language models

author.name: Xingyu Zhao

entry.summary: Drawing on traditional software reliability engineering, the paper argues that LLM reliability should be assessed for specified users and conditions of use rather than via aggregate benchmark scores. It distinguishes fault-discovery testing from reliability assessment, identifies ten modeling considerations behind reliability claims, and proposes a six-workstream research roadmap covering claim specification, dynamic operational profiles, graded outcomes, and probabilistic robustness.

entry.title: ProtoBridge-CLIP: Observation-Masked Finding Prototypes for Medical Image--Report Representation Learning

author.name: Jinrui Wu, Yun Peng

entry.summary: Presents a medical image-report alignment framework that distinguishes affirmed findings, explicit negations, and unmentioned concepts, aligning text-derived finding prototypes with local visual tokens while excluding uncertain concepts from direct supervision. It is evaluated across three CT and five chest-radiograph benchmarks with retrieval, localization, and perturbation analyses.

entry.title: The 7th International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026): Summary and Results

author.name: Tobias Ladner, Konstantin Kaulen, Stanley Bak, Julien Girard-Satabin, Taylor T. Johnson, Edoardo Manino, ThanhVu H Nguyen, Ben Wooding, Haoze Wu

entry.summary: Summarizes VNN-COMP 2026, the seventh annual neural network verification competition held at FLoC 2026 in Lisbon, comparing state-of-the-art verification tools on scalability and speed using standardized formats (ONNX, VNNLIB), standardized AWS hardware, and author-provided tool parameters. The report documents rules, benchmarks, participating tools, results, and lessons learned.

entry.title: Temporal Rank in Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Leo Dobson, Anton Ragni

entry.summary: Identifies an information bottleneck in RNNs caused by rank-constrained hidden state dynamics, which limits the number of independent input directions preserved over time independently of vanishing/exploding gradient issues. It introduces structured high-dimensional state dynamics that preserve temporal separability to lift this constraint. A fresh architectural diagnosis relevant to the ongoing RNN-vs-transformer discussion.

entry.title: Variable Length Diffuse Everything: Arbitrary Length Generative Modeling on Arbitrary State Spaces

author.name: Kevin Rojas, Felix X. -F. Ye, Molei Tao

entry.summary: VL-DE introduces a general diffusion framework for variable-length multimodal generation on arbitrary state spaces, avoiding the padding or length-modeling tricks used in prior work. It handles mixed continuous and discrete data, such as bounding box coordinates with discrete types in layout generation, via an insertion-based mechanism. This extends diffusion and flow models beyond fixed-dimension data.

entry.title: Transferring an analysis of human brain organization to language models

author.name: Donghyeok Lee, Sangwon Yu, Sangkwon Park, Hye Youn Park, Munyoung Chang, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Applying diffusion-map embedding techniques from cortical organization analysis to matched base and reasoning-trained language models, the authors find broadly preserved gradient profiles with localized changes in a contiguous layer span. Grafting weights from these spans into instruction-tuned hosts improves mathematical reasoning, with gains tracking region overlap and the span forming during early performance rises.

entry.title: Neural Memory Orchestration

author.name: Michael Zizov, Boris Morose

entry.summary: Overseer is an end-to-end learned page-prefetching system for HPC memory hierarchies: an eBPF collector observes page faults on the host, a transformer-based predictor runs on network-attached inference hardware, and prefetch decisions feed back into the kernel. Unlike prior learned prefetchers evaluated only in simulation, this is deployed against live workloads on real hardware. It targets the growing fraction of wall time lost to page faults in mmap, swap, and tiered-memory workloads.

entry.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas

author.name: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham, Zekai Zhu

entry.summary: The authors extend a machine-learning-assisted search for modular data of 2+1D topological quantum field theories from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data using rejection gates including logistic regression classifiers. With this data they find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore on time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories and propose a refined criterion. Roughly 80% of modular data in ranks 23-42 is now identified.

entry.title: What Majority Labels Hide: Annotator Disagreement and Model Errors in Multi-Dialect Arabic Sexism Detection

author.name: Alaa Bazaid, Arkaitz Zubiaga

entry.summary: Introduces MuDAS, a dataset of YouTube comments in Saudi, Egyptian, and Moroccan Arabic labeled by three native speakers per dialect with individual annotations preserved. The study evaluates fine-tuned Arabic encoders, GPT-5.6 Terra, and Arabic-centric LLMs, finding model errors are more frequent on contested cases with annotator disagreement, and that close Macro-F1 scores hide complementary error patterns.

entry.title: MedHarness: A Unified Budgeted Runtime for Reliable Medical Imaging Agents

author.name: Haofan Wu, Le Zhang

entry.summary: MedHarness is a runtime reliability layer for medical imaging agents that reformulates post-answer control as shared decision-object attachment, deciding when to stop, open deeper evidence, repair, or reject under a limited verification budget. It replaces surface-specific evidence orders or costly always-open full-depth verification paths with one controller across modalities. Verification-under-budget is a central unsolved problem for deploying agents in high-stakes clinical settings.

entry.title: HOForce: Motion and Force Reconstruction of Hand-Object Interaction Using a Single-View RGB-D Video

author.name: Jiahui Wang, Wanqing Du, Yuanbin Zou, Zhefeng Xu, Feng Xu

entry.summary: HOForce jointly tracks hands and objects and recovers interaction forces, including bimanual fingertip forces and object-object contact forces, from single-view RGB-D video given known object properties. Reconstructed forces also serve as pose constraints in occluded regions, improving motion tracking accuracy on DexYCB and TACO benchmarks with less hand-object penetration. Recovering physical forces from ordinary video is valuable for robotics, VR, and manipulation learning.

entry.title: STAR++: A Physical-Aware Benchmark and Framework for Astronomical Super-Resolution across Multiple Filters

author.name: Guohang Zhuang, Jiaze Li, Kuo-cheng Wu, Hao Du, Jinyang Huang, Xiang Zhang, Wanli Ouyang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: STAR++ introduces a large-scale benchmark of roughly 1.7 million flux-consistent image pairs for astronomical super-resolution across multiple filters, plus a physics-aware framework that preserves stellar flux across resolutions. It addresses the ill-posedness of reconstructing high-frequency stellar components like locations and profiles that natural-image SR methods mishandle. A strong domain-specific benchmark and method contribution.

entry.title: Look Closer, Look Back, or Wait for Agentic Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Pengyu Li, Zhitao Gao, Lingling Zhang, Wenxuan Huang, YiCheng Xiao, Chen Zheng, Jun Liu

entry.summary: ActiveForager is a streaming video agent that maintains a clean short working window and, per query, chooses to answer directly, zoom into high-resolution recent frames, recall past events from memory, or wait for future frames. This addresses hallucination from diluting attention with past frames and failures of cascade retrieval when current frames are ambiguous.

entry.title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model

author.name: Chuang Wang, Rui Nie, Jie Song, Junyuan Gao, Jiahe Song, Haitao Zhou, Boyu Zhu, Xing Li, Jiang Wu, Conghui He, Qian Yu, Weijia Li

entry.summary: StrideWorld is a benchmark for interactive video world models that evaluates scene rigidity and action consistency using references fixed before motion occurs, rather than references fitted to the video under test. This prevents gradual scene deformation and pacing changes from passing undetected. It measures 3D structural stability against ground-truth start-view geometry and stability of action effects.

entry.title: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback

author.name: Jiayou Zhu, Peng Guo, Litian Zhang, Xinze Shi, Yuting Zhang, Zelong Yu, Yize Tian, Jirong Liu, Zifeng Kang

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free, inference-time defense against adversarial patches on VLA-controlled robots, using the frozen policy's own attention response to local visual interventions to guide purification during closed-loop manipulation. Avoids extra training or auxiliary models required by prior defenses.
