entry.title: Learning the Dynamics of Deformable Linear Objects Through Coupled Oscillators for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Iv\'an L\'opez-Broce\~no, Maximilian St\"olzle, Daniel Feliu-Talegon, Daniela Rus, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Proposes Phi-CON for learning force-driven dynamics of deformable linear objects, combining a floating-base coupled oscillator network with a learned diffeomorphism between observed and latent coordinates. The model is stable by construction and retains Lagrangian structure, addressing dynamic effects neglected by prior DLO learning approaches.

entry.title: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents

author.name: Jinhao Zhang, Yushen Zuo, Ke Rui, Weitao Zhou, Haibao Yu, Honglong Tian, Xiaoheng Ma, Jie Mei, Jiawei Wang, Minglei Li

entry.summary: CoT-WAM jointly trains a vision-language model and a world-action model through a learnable embedding exchanging plan latents, injecting VLM semantic competence such as open-world scene understanding and long-horizon reasoning into WAM prediction and control. It targets general robot manipulation requiring both semantics and physical foresight.

entry.title: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots

author.name: Yuhang Huang, Junchao Li, Boyang Ma, Minghui Xu, Kaidi Xu, Pengfei Hu, Xiuzhen Cheng, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a semantic consistency boundary in multi-model robot pipelines between LLM intent understanding, the small action model's translation into commands, and physical execution, showing commercial robots may act unintentionally even without explicit action commands. It introduces TARS, a black-box framework to explore and measure the command-reasoning-action pipeline.

entry.title: Remote Teleoperation of Endovascular Robots: A Network Emulation Framework for Systematic Performance Evaluation

author.name: Xingyu Chen, Nikola Fischer, Harry Robertshaw, Weiyuan Deng, Christos Bergeles, Thomas Booth

entry.summary: This work develops a network emulation and benchmarking framework for remote endovascular teleoperation, running a user study with eight clinicians and eight students performing 480 navigation attempts across 15 network conditions. It links network performance and video quality to navigation outcomes, confidence, and operator experience. The results help characterize when remote endovascular procedures remain safe and usable under network degradation.

entry.title: Where is all the AI persuasion?

author.name: Karthik Tadepalli

entry.summary: Surveys the gap between lab studies showing frontier AIs are superhumanly persuasive and the absence of observable real-world AI persuasion effects. The author argues persuasion is a rare fuzzy, hard-to-evaluate domain where we can check evaluations against reality, making it a bellwether for whether AI progress on checkable tasks generalizes to fuzzy tasks like AI research.

entry.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters

author.name: Hui Zhu, Saleh Zare Zade, Rafi Ibn Sultan, Deng Pan, Arun Ross, Dongxiao Zhu

entry.summary: The authors observe that under causal masking the BOS token's representation carries no input information despite being a widely-used attention sink, and introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query alone at one prefill layer. This lets the BOS position aggregate visual and textual input into a context representation that downstream tokens already attend to. It is an elegant, low-cost modification applicable to LVLMs and LLMs.

entry.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying

author.name: Hangle Hu, Chenyu Hou, Bin Cao, Jing Fan, Wei Luo

entry.summary: Studies Underspecified Decision Completion (UDC), where LLMs silently adopt assumptions when natural-language questions about structured data admit multiple computational interpretations, producing potentially incorrect code. It introduces Grounded Code Generation (GCG), a diagnostic protocol separating identification of unresolved decisions, their evidence-based resolution, and translation into code. Useful for understanding and improving text-to-SQL-style systems.

entry.title: KnowledgeClaw: Towards Agentic Knowledge Engineering via Omnimodal Hypergraphs

author.name: Haoran Luo, Jiapu Wang, Linhao Luo, Luu Anh Tuan

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Omnimodal Knowledge Engineering (OmniKE) and releases OmniKE-Bench, a benchmark with six tasks spanning 1,829 items over 3,960 real files in five modalities. It also proposes KnowledgeClaw, an agentic system that builds an omnimodal typed hypergraph maintained by a closed-loop lifecycle agent, addressing omnimodality, lifecycle management, and multi-granular application simultaneously.

entry.title: When Single Agent Is Enough: Rethinking Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Code Review

author.name: Jiawei Li, Hoa Khanh Dam, Iftekhar Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares multi-agent and single-agent designs for review comment generation and code refinement in automated code review. Surprisingly, single-agent approaches perform comparably to, and sometimes outperform, multi-agent systems despite far simpler architecture and lower runtime overhead. The finding challenges the prevailing assumption that specialized multi-agent coordination is needed for code review tasks.

entry.title: SIGMA: speaker-isolated, symptom-structured multimodal estimation of depression severity from clinical interviews

author.name: Zhuoyuan Tang, Tao Wang, Kai Yang, Li Yuan, Yuezhou Zhang, Rongrong Zhong, Yi Cai, Saskia C. Sanderson, Jaime Delgadillo, Richard Dobson, Angus Roberts

entry.summary: SIGMA estimates depression severity from semi-clinical interviews using speaker diarization to isolate participant speech, cross-attention fusion of text, audio, and video, and a graded-response head that jointly predicts eight questionnaire items. The design addresses confounds from interviewer speech, late fusion limits, and ignored inter-symptom correlations in prior work.

entry.title: Lodestone: Automated Semantic Discovery of Datacenter Hardware Specialization

author.name: Peizhe Liu, Akanksha Jain, Gerasimos Gerogiannis, Vidushi Dadu, Parthasarathy Ranganathan, Jovan Stojkovic

entry.summary: Lodestone uses agentic AI to automatically discover computations across large-scale datacenter software that justify dedicated hardware acceleration, identifying semantically identical computations spread across seemingly unrelated code regions. Conventional hot-function analysis misses these fine-grained specialization opportunities, and the authors argue agents with semantic reasoning can find them where rule-based approaches fail. The work comes from Google systems researchers.

entry.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping

author.name: Manav Kulshrestha, Shreyans Jain, Apoorva Vashisth, Ankush Gupta, Damon Conover, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: LAGR re-ranks candidate grasps by task suitability given language instructions, distinguishing holds appropriate to different uses (e.g., hammer by handle for hammering versus by head for handover). The authors construct a dataset of 2.68 million scored 5-DoF grasp annotations over roughly 100,000 image-task pairs across 17 object categories, addressing the scarcity of dense task-oriented grasp labels. This advances language-conditioned robotic manipulation.

entry.title: ReliFlow: Reliability-Calibrated Residual Transport for Combinatorial Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Jinrui David, Yun Peng

entry.summary: Introduces a conditional flow-matching model that estimates the reliability of single-gene perturbation effects via training-only cross-fitting and uses these estimates to calibrate the additive source distribution before learning a residual transport field. On Norman genetic perturbation data it reduces MAE for unseen combinations, including when single-perturbation evidence is withheld.

entry.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions

author.name: Luoyuan Zhang, Xuanyu Zheng, Yancheng Long, Haoyang Xu, Bin Wen, Tingting Gao

entry.summary: Introduces VideoACE, a benchmark of 1,000 multiple-choice questions testing agentic video understanding, where models must actively interact with high-frame-rate action videos to gather evidence rather than passively watch. It includes temporal evidence annotations and carefully screened hints to prevent answer leakage. It targets the underexplored question of whether interaction opportunities actually translate into better video understanding.

entry.title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams

author.name: Edoardo Chidichimo, Felix P. S. Wallis

entry.summary: Demonstrates that steering along a single neuron's output direction in Qwen3.5-4B increases decisions to conceal information, with larger effects in multi-agent team settings than solo settings, and that collective concealment rises further when all members are steered. Inter-agent messaging tempers concealment, while ablating the neuron has negligible effect. Shows that multi-agent context changes how internal interventions manifest in behavior.

entry.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game

author.name: Muhammad Rizky Wellyanto, Hajara-Yasmin Isa, Kexin Xue, Vishal Ravichandran, Wenpeng Lu, Jerry O. Talton, Ranjitha Kumar

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Personal Imitation Game, a harder variant of the Turing test asking whether a machine can imitate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. With 30 participants they establish human baselines and identify identity signals interrogators rely on, then build an LLM system replicating one author from ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators chose the system over the author's real friends in a substantial fraction of trials.

entry.title: A Rank-One Bypass of Fixed Linear Erasure

author.name: Jai Kumar Sharma, Vanshaj Khattar

entry.summary: This paper shows that linear concept erasure in open-weight models is vulnerable: if an attacker can modify upstream layers and any direction visible to a downstream classifier survives, a rank-one affine update can write the erased target score back through the erasure layer. The condition is shown to be both necessary and sufficient, and experiments on six CIFAR-10 class-pair tasks restore nearly all pre-erasure target performance. This demonstrates a fundamental fragility of fixed erasure layers in open-weight settings.

entry.title: Probing Physics in Motion Diffusion Models Against Their Own Estimate

author.name: Saeed Ghorbani

entry.summary: This paper critically re-examines claims that diffusion models know more physics than they show, arguing that since a diffusion model computes its clean-sample estimate from the same activations probed, such comparisons may reflect readout ease rather than hidden knowledge. Using kinematic text-to-motion models where physics is exactly computable, it tests whether layers genuinely look ahead of the model's own estimate.

entry.title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators

author.name: Michael Liaofan Liu, Joe Kileel

entry.summary: The paper presents a general framework for learning equivariant functions between semisimple real group representations using linear combinations of equivariant polynomial features with learnable coefficient functions of invariant features, based on minimal homogeneous generators of the invariant algebra. It ships a Python package that computes features and fits models automatically.

entry.title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch

author.name: Haoxuan Wang, Jianliang Ye, Sen Na

entry.summary: The paper proves that replacing stochastic gradients with a moving average in online sketched Newton methods mitigates, and in some cases eliminates, the known computational-statistical trade-off where sketching inflates the limiting covariance of iterates. Gradient averaging requires no additional hyperparameters and achieves optimal statistical efficiency.

entry.title: Meaning Reaches Object Choice but Not Completion: Where Is a VLA Vulnerable to Landmark Synonyms?

author.name: Ryoichi Kurihara, Kota Sunamoto

entry.summary: This study probes the released GR00T N1.7 vision-language-action model on LIBERO-Spatial tasks where only a landmark word differs, showing that unseen synonyms send the policy to the wrong object and drop success from 100% to 67.6%. By pasting landmark token vectors at different points in the pipeline, the authors localize where semantic information influences object choice versus task completion. This provides a diagnostic methodology for interpreting and intervening in VLA failures beyond aggregate success rates.

entry.title: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation

author.name: Shengxiang Lin, Jiajie Su, Pengyang Zhou, Xiang Chen, Xiaolin Zheng, Feng Tian, Chaochao Chen

entry.summary: Addresses privacy leakage in LLM-enhanced recommenders, where semantic embeddings of item text can leak sensitive attributes through inversion attacks. PGPO learns topology-aware obfuscation anchors for high-influence prototype words and propagates them through a static semantic graph, optimized with GRPO to balance privacy protection against preserving inter-item semantic relations needed for recommendation quality.

entry.title: TransFIRA+: Transfer Learning for Biometric Recognizability Assessment

author.name: Allen Tu, Kartik Narayan, Joshua Gleason, Jennifer Xu, Matthew Meyn, Tom Goldstein, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: TransFIRA grounds biometric recognizability directly in embedding space using class-center similarity and angular separation from a pretrained encoder, predicting these from images without quality annotations. This avoids visual heuristics and costly generative pipelines used by prior face-quality assessment methods, tying predictions to the encoder's actual decision geometry. The extension adds transfer learning for deployment across encoders and conditions.

entry.title: GramStatTexNet: Efficient, Interpretable, and Neuro-Inspired Texture Analysis-by-Synthesis

author.name: Vasha DuTell, Zuyu Yun, Anne Harrington, Michael Y-S Fang, Mark Hamilton, Christian K\"ovesdi, Edward H. Adelson, William T. Freeman, Ruth Rosenholtz

entry.summary: GramStatTexNet combines the multi-scale Gabor filter structure of neuroscience-informed pyramid texture models with the flexibility of Gramian-based correlations, organized into structured, named filter families. This hybrid analysis-by-synthesis framework yields interpretable, compact texture representations that support analyses difficult for opaque deep-feature methods, while remaining biologically grounded. It bridges classical and deep approaches to texture with strong author pedigree (Freeman, Adelson, Rosenholtz).

entry.title: CausalDrive: Causal Decomposition for Data-Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaobao Wei, Jingxian Wu, Lirong Yang, Qing Han, Yuan Gao, Ziwei Yang, Shuai Yang, Weiwei Liu, Chang Huang

entry.summary: CausalDrive separates nominal intention (where to go) from multimodal driving styles (how it is executed) in imitation learning for end-to-end autonomous driving, decoupling a deterministic intention predictor from a probabilistic style model. This causal decomposition disambiguates entangled expert demonstrations for more data-efficient policy learning. A conceptually clean framework for a core driving challenge.

entry.title: ART: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer

author.name: Zichen Zhang, Wei Zhai, Xuji Zhang, Yang Cao, Yu Kang

entry.summary: ART defines a new task, 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer, recognizing that affordances depend on the agent's embodiment rather than being object-intrinsic. It contributes a human-robot paired affordance dataset and methods to adapt human priors to robot end-effectors for manipulation.

entry.title: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)

author.name: Sen Fang, Yalin Feng, Yancheng Zhang, Yanxin Zhang, Zonglin Lyu, Hongbin Zhong, Liwei Che, Rui Wu, Chen Chen, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: This position-style paper proposes that all visual tasks can be reformulated as generation over World Snapshots, enabling a single World Snapshot Model to train on and perform nearly all visual tasks, analogous to how LLMs unified NLP. It formalizes the hypothesis and validates it empirically across multiple tasks. The claim is ambitious: a unified framework for computer vision.

entry.title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM

author.name: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam

entry.summary: Presents the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras, using surface primitives that triangulate directly into connected meshes. Combines geometric registration with techniques that keep displaced triangles reliable as registration targets, avoiding the slow photometric tracking of prior work.

entry.title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization

author.name: Xuanwei Liu, Guipu Cao, Zhongyi Luo, Jiafei Duan

entry.summary: Proposes a bimanual action tokenizer that shares a common motion vocabulary between the two arms while capturing complementary cross-arm coordination roles, improving on concatenated-vector tokenizers used in autoregressive VLA models. This lets the policy inherit shared movement patterns and model coordination explicitly.

entry.title: Improving While Deployed: Learning Proactive End-to-End Driving from Imperfect Human Takeover Data

author.name: Yangang Ren, Di Zeng, Jun Li, Zirui Li, Chengjiang Zhang, Xiaoqing Ye, Ji Tao, Chen Lv

entry.summary: An offline post-training framework transforms imperfect human takeover data from deployed driving models into proactive supervision by augmenting model plans and shifting recorded human corrections earlier in time, then training a scene-conditioned trajectory scorer. This avoids reinforcing late or unnecessary driver interventions.

entry.title: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors

author.name: Lequn Fu, Yufeng Hu, Yijun Zhong, Jie Zhang, Xiao Li, Lingxiang Ji, Zhiyuan Xu, Jian Tang, Shiqi Li

entry.summary: ReLoco uses behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors to learn locomotion, get-up recovery from arbitrary fallen postures, and command resumption within a single proprioceptive policy for humanoids. Training uses posture-selected expert pools, behavior-specific discriminator outputs, and simulation-based refinement of robot-executed motion.

entry.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing

author.name: Malak Gamal El-Din, Yasser Shoukry, Salma Elmalaki

entry.summary: BeFit shifts neural network capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations for time-series models on microcontrollers. It uses hardware-aware NAS to find compact Bernstein-activated CNNs, projects weights to multiplication-free codes, and recovers accuracy loss through the learnable activations. This enables accurate, energy-efficient inference on severely resource-constrained sensing hardware.

entry.title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs

author.name: Zhi Sheng, Chuyue Wang, Jiahao Ji, Yile Liang, Xuetao Ding, Jinghua Hao, Jie Feng, Yong Li

entry.summary: Introduces GLIDE for forecasting order volume at scale-effect hotspots in on-demand food delivery platforms like Meituan, handling ephemeral logistics graph topology and highly heterogeneous, zero-inflated volumes. The inductive, event-aware design targets real-time dispatch and order pooling at industrial scale. Addresses challenges that standard spatiotemporal models handle poorly.

entry.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events

author.name: Yiyang Zhu, Guangyuan Liu, Jingdi Lei, Li Wei, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: The paper identifies a fundamental flaw in multimodal alignment architectures for physical AI: compressing temporal sensor sequences into single pooled embeddings erases transient cross-modal dynamics. The authors formally prove that temporal pooling fails on twin events (distinct physical executions under identical conditions) and propose trajectory-level alignment as an alternative.

entry.title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents

author.name: Ruiqi Liu, Jinming Li, Mo Wang, Yang Lu, Yanlan Kang

entry.summary: This work introduces budget-paired counterfactual audits, an evaluation protocol for visual agents that read dense documents under a finite observation budget. By holding evidence and region bindings fixed while perturbing only remaining budget or declared task parameters, it decomposes lost expected accuracy into stepwise acquisition loss and terminal decision loss, separating planning quality from answering quality. The protocol is demonstrated across paired routing anchors and multiple open-weight models.

entry.title: Optimize the Cob, Then the Kernel: Optimizing Beam Search for Generative Recommendation Inference

author.name: Shing Wai Pun, Kai Wu, Pengfei Xia, Hui Zang, Wei Guo, Yong Liu

entry.summary: This systems paper optimizes beam search inference for generative recommendation, which differs from standard LLM serving due to long input prompts, wide beams, and few fixed output tokens. The authors use Tree Attention to concatenate beams along the sequence dimension, eliminating redundant KV cache accesses over the shared prompt prefix, and address host-side beam processing and PagedAttention block management overheads found in engines like vLLM.

entry.title: FutureBench: A Renewable Framework for Evaluating Knowledge-Context Conflict in LLMs

author.name: Yi-Cheng Lai, Hen-Hsen Huang

entry.summary: FutureBench evaluates knowledge-context conflict in LLMs using timestamped questions, controlled passage triplets, and no-context probes, with a renewable design that avoids contamination over time. Across 3,629 questions and six models it finds that a Verify prompt combining checking with passage priority raises false-answer adoption on pre-cutoff events, while passage priority without checking raises adoption on post-cutoff events.

entry.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks

author.name: Shenghan Gao, Zhiling Zheng

entry.summary: This work presents a pipeline combining a vision LLM for figure layout understanding with classical computer vision for pixel-level refinement to extract powder X-ray diffraction curves from published figures of covalent organic frameworks. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, it recovered 11,445 curves, converting decades of image-only structural evidence into machine-readable data. This enables large-scale materials science analysis and model training.

entry.title: Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Shuaidi Wang, Zhuocheng Gong, Xuejie Liu, Jianguo Li, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes LED, a post-training framework extending diffusion language models beyond replacement-only editing by adding token insertion and deletion, enabling Levenshtein-style refinement of generated sequences. This addresses inefficiency when missing or extra tokens cause sequence shifts and when errors span many positions. The contribution strengthens flexible editing for the growing diffusion-LM paradigm.

entry.title: SixthView: A Benchmark for Hidden-View Reconstruction and 3D Assembly Reasoning

author.name: Pooya Khosravi, Jen-Feng Chang, Fnu Pramono

entry.summary: Introduces SixthView, a benchmark of 602 synthetic polycube 3D assemblies where models must predict a sixth hidden orthographic view from five observed views plus component shape information. The authors exhaustively verify that each instance has a unique valid hidden view, enabling both exact-view and cell-level evaluation of 3D assembly and occlusion reasoning.

entry.title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices

author.name: Zihao Wang, Ye Tian, Tajana Rosing, Nalini Venkatasubramanian

entry.summary: Introduces LEDGE, a lightweight simulator for distributed LLM serving on heterogeneous edge devices that builds event graphs supporting non-uniform tensor and pipeline parallelism and predicts execution times via reusable calibrated performance models, without executing tensor operations. It enables fast exploration of model partitions, device placements, and network conditions that would be costly to test physically.

entry.title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL

author.name: Seungyub Han, Taehyun Cho, Dohyeong Kim, Kyungjae Lee, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes MINT, which replaces products of per-step trace coefficients in multi-step off-policy temporal-difference methods with a binary stopping indicator based on when coupled behavior and target trajectories first meet. This yields a variance bound governed by meeting-time survival and admits a model-free surrogate requiring a single sampled action. It removes a sensitive hyperparameter (maximum trace length) from off-policy RL.

entry.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Qu\'ebec French

author.name: Eeham Khan, Richard Khoury, Leila Kosseim

entry.summary: This paper presents a controlled study of continual pre-training (CPT) for adapting language models to Quebec French, spanning nine LLMs across different families and scales under a budget-matched protocol of 30M tokens per experiment. The key finding is that CPT benefits depend strongly on the starting model's existing competence in the target dialect, and when helpful, improvements are driven more by corpus composition (e.g., literary text) than by data volume. The work also questions whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture dialectal adaptation effects.

entry.title: HypoLoop: Revising Weight-Editing Plans from Scientific Feedback

author.name: Mengran Li, Xichen Yan, Bo Li, Chengyang Zhang, Jinfeng Xu, Zheng Lin, Zelin Zang, Zhen Lei, Jiebo Luo, Victor C. M. Leung, Stan Z. Li

entry.summary: HypoLoop is a family of weight-editing methods that updates model parameters in response to scientific experimental feedback, using fixed, adaptive, or LLM-guided policies to produce editing plans refined by numerical solvers and validation. Experiments span 22 scientific tasks and use both DeepSeek and Claude models, with substantial error reductions such as 58.80 percent on Burgers equations. It connects LLM-guided model editing to scientific discovery loops.

entry.title: Adaptive Action Horizon Selection via Flow-Field Uncertainty

author.name: Idan Ben-Ami, Arnon Netzer, Sarah Keren, Idit Diamant

entry.summary: DUAC is a post-hoc method for extracting action-level uncertainty from the vector field of pretrained vision-language-action models, building on a closed-form flow-posterior covariance formulation. Unlike Adaptive Action Chunking, which samples multiple action chunks and incurs extra inference cost, DUAC derives uncertainty from a single generated chunk using Jacobian-vector products. This enables reliable adaptive action horizon selection for VLA models without additional inference overhead.

entry.title: Element-Wise Femoral Stress Prediction: A Hybrid Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Finite Element Analysis

author.name: Sikha O K, Abdollah Moslemi, Elham Alizadeh, Ludovic Humbert, Miguel A. Gonzalez Ballester, Jerome Noailly

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid graph neural network framework that predicts element-wise femoral stress from graph-structured finite element mesh data, serving as a fast surrogate for computationally expensive FEA in hip fracture assessment. By preserving spatial and topological mesh structure that conventional ML surrogates discard, it aims to make biomechanical strength analysis clinically practical for aging populations.

entry.title: Variance-Optimal Counterfactual Policy Design for Sample-Efficient Online A/B Testing

author.name: Shashank Gupta, Subhadeep Maji

entry.summary: This paper redesigns the data-collection scheme for online A/B tests to reduce estimator variance, addressing the common situation where treatment and production policies take overlapping actions and add noise without informative signal. By planning counterfactual policy design upfront rather than only improving estimators post hoc, it aims to detect small treatment effects with less traffic and shorter test durations.

entry.title: Isthmus: Bridging Supervision Islands Restores Uncertainty and Stability in One-Step Flows

author.name: Luming Yang, Siqing Li, Haoxian Liu, Zhenyu Bu, Jiazheng Zhu, Alper Yilmaz

entry.summary: The paper shows that one-step flow-map samplers lose variance and stability because their training-time start/end pairs receive little or no direct supervision, causing sample collapse toward the conditional mean. It proposes bridging these supervision islands in the time-triangle of training pairs to restore uncertainty in one-step generative sampling.

entry.title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades

author.name: Abdiaziz Muse, Jiju Poovvancheri

entry.summary: This study asks whether 3D point cloud representations capture architectural function (e.g., whether a window is operable or a column is load-bearing) rather than just semantic identity, using 22 mobile-LiDAR buildings annotated with 15 functional attributes. The authors find that networks trained from scratch, including a 108M-parameter PTv3, fail to beat hand-crafted descriptors, while frozen self-supervised point transformer features substantially outperform both. The result challenges assumptions about scaling supervised 3D models and highlights the value of pretraining for function-level understanding in urban digital twins and building analysis.

entry.title: Functional Principal Component Analysis: Minimax Optimality from Sparse to Dense Designs and Beyond

author.name: Shunxing Yan, Fang Yao

entry.summary: This paper resolves a two-decade-old open problem by establishing minimax rates for functional principal component analysis with diverging spectral indices under noisy discrete observations. A sieve-based framework pools measurements across subjects and covers sampling regimes from sparse to dense, with new minimax rates for covariance estimation over general bivariate function classes. It identifies the intrinsically two-dimensional optimal rate.

entry.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures

author.name: Yan Qiu, Yuanyuan Li

entry.summary: Proposes JDPI, a jailbreak detection method that builds harmful and benign prototypes from binary safety labels using contrastively learned representations and classifies by relative prototype distance, without training a downstream classifier. It uses fewer labeled examples than classifier baselines and is evaluated across four benchmarks covering different input formats.

entry.title: Geometry-bridge flow matching for blind rigid-motion correction in head cone-beam CT

author.name: Sungho Yun, Seungryong Cho

entry.summary: The authors propose a 3D flow-matching prior for correcting patient head motion in cone-beam CT, learning motion-induced image changes via a geometry-bridge between motion-corrupted and motion-free FDK reconstructions. A plug-and-play loop combines learned image updates with spline pose estimation, data consistency, and total-variation regularization. This brings generative flow-matching priors into a clinically relevant medical imaging reconstruction problem.

entry.title: Learning What to Degrade: A Recoverability-Aware Curriculum for Reliable Smart-Glasses Super-Resolution

author.name: Yaopeng Wang, Qingliang Wang, Yilun Jin, Xiujin Liu, Han Yue, Chen Xia, Renjie Zhu, Chuang Sheng

entry.summary: This paper addresses super-resolution for smart-glasses images where degradations obscure text and fine structures needed by vision-language models for visual assistance. The authors introduce an HR-referenced semantic evaluation protocol that reveals two failure modes (generative SR hallucinating details, restoration-oriented SR leaving evidence blurred) and propose ReDiC, a recoverability-difficulty curriculum that provides hard but recoverable training inputs. It matters because it targets reliability of AI visual assistance on wearable devices, a growing application area.

entry.title: CoScan: Multi-Scale Content-Adaptive Space-Filling Scans for Causal State-Space Image Restoration

author.name: Wei Dong, Terry Ji, Yan Min, Shahram Shirani, Jun Chen, Han Zhou

entry.summary: This paper introduces CoScan, a method for learning image-dependent scan orders for selective state-space models in image restoration. Because 2D feature maps must be linearized into 1D sequences for causal SSM updates, restoration quality is sensitive to the traversal order; CoScan uses differentiable proxy supervision driven by scan-quality objectives to learn content-adaptive space-filling traversals instead of fixed, content-agnostic scans.

entry.title: Beyond Additive Composition: Interventional Modeling of State-Dependent Cross-Degradation Responses for Composite Image Restoration

author.name: Zongda Tang, Jie Feng, Wenda Zhao, Mingtao Feng, Yuping Liang, Ronghua Shang, Weisheng Dong

entry.summary: PROBE formulates composite image restoration as modeling state-dependent interactions between coexisting degradations, since one degradation dynamically shifts the manifestation of others in non-additive ways that factor-wise decomposition misses. It builds unified degradation axes and uses an interventional framework to explicitly capture cross-degradation responses. This brings causal-interventional thinking to a practical restoration problem.

entry.title: SimplePro: A Simple Baseline for Proactive Video Understanding

author.name: Yilin Wang, Xiangxi Zheng, Dongxing Mao, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: SimplePro is a training-free baseline for proactive streaming video understanding where a frozen VLM must decide what to answer and when to respond or stay silent. It shows that explicit reporting rules plus structured streaming context substantially improve proactive response behavior without task-specific reinforcement learning or triggering modules. A useful simplicity check on an emerging task.

entry.title: Freeforward4d: Annotation-free feed-forward 4d reconstruction of driving scenes

author.name: Luosong Guo, Xiang Yang, Chaoyang Li, Ao Gao, Jiangming Shi, Yanyun Qu, Zhizhong Zhang, Jingyu Gong, Yuan Xie

entry.summary: This paper introduces FreeForward4D, a method for feed-forward 4D reconstruction of driving scenes that works without dataset-provided annotations such as camera parameters, LiDAR depth, or 3D box labels. It reconciles predictions from pretrained visual models (cameras, depth, object tracks) into a single consistent metric frame, enabling reconstruction directly from unannotated RGB driving videos. This matters for autonomous driving simulation because it removes costly annotation requirements and makes scene reconstruction applicable to arbitrary unlabeled footage.

entry.title: Learning Where and How Much to Sample: Volume-Adaptive k-Space Acquisition for Accelerated MRI

author.name: Reyhaneh Neshatavar, Mohsen Yavartanoo, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: This paper proposes a volume-adaptive k-space acquisition framework for accelerated MRI that jointly learns where and how much to sample across an entire volume, using only ACS measurements to allocate sampling budgets across slices based on anatomy. It moves beyond fixed sampling patterns and uniform slice budgets, with potential to reduce MRI acquisition times. Clinically meaningful efficiency gains.

entry.title: GenRF: Generative Registration-free Image Fusion

author.name: Linfeng Tang, Zhijun Fan, Yang Chen, Zizhuo Li, Hao Zhang, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: GenRF tackles multi-modal image fusion when sources are misaligned and degraded, removing the need for explicit registration by leveraging generative foundation models. It handles geometric discrepancies and mismatched fields of view that break correspondence estimation in prior restoration-fusion pipelines.

entry.title: MLIE-CoT: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Multi-Level Image Editing

author.name: Baichuan Yang, Dongyuan Xu, Zhao Yang, Yong Liu, Bing Su

entry.summary: MLIE-CoT extends chain-of-thought reasoning to text-to-image generation by carrying reasoning through multi-level image edits rather than text-only intermediate steps, preserving visual semantic information that language descriptions lose. It exploits image-conditioned generation models such as FLUX and BAGEL to iteratively refine images. This aims to improve complex visual generation tasks requiring stepwise reasoning.

entry.title: Read Together, Answer Apart: How Earlier Questions Help Vision-Language Models Look

author.name: Xinyi Guo, Kaile Huang, Xitong Ling, Mingyi He, Chende Zheng, Jianyu Xu, Chao He, Dongqing Song

entry.summary: This large-scale study of 22 open-weight VLMs disentangles how co-asking multiple questions about one image affects individual answers, finding two opposing effects: co-asking repairs 15-30% of single-question errors on densely captioned images while also corrupting some correct answers, with corruption falling sharply for stronger models. Attention readouts and layer-wise analysis across 14 models illuminate the mechanism. The work clarifies conflicting prior reports about multi-question prompts.

entry.title: Streaming Generative Video Compression with Embedding Alignment and In-Context Propagation

author.name: Zhitao Wang, Hengyu Man, Han Liu, Wenrui Li, Debin Zhao, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: Proposes SGVC, a streaming generative video compression framework that adapts a pretrained latent video diffusion transformer into a causal pixel-space refiner, avoiding expensive VAE decoders and multi-frame buffering delays. This enables ultra-low bitrate video compression with better perceptual quality and lower latency.

entry.title: SPICE: Stochastic Policy for Interaction in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Nidhi Parayil, Benjamin Greenland, Thierry Peynot, Chris Lehnert

entry.summary: SPICE is a tactile-conditioned diffusion policy enabling robots to reach targets through dense plant canopies using only tactile sensing, handling compliant foliage, partial obstructions, and blocking branches. It targets agricultural tasks like harvesting and pruning where vision is obstructed and contact is unavoidable.

entry.title: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control

author.name: Xianhao Pan, Chi Li, Hanchao Li, Yunxin Liu, Jiankai Sun, Luhui Hu

entry.summary: JEPA Dots separates dynamics and task representations in a dual-latent world model so language instructions guide a flow-matching policy without altering predictions of fixed actions under identical observations, using masked attention to restrict world prediction to instruction-independent history. It achieves 84.9% overall success across 40 trained LIBERO tasks in closed-loop evaluation.

entry.title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors

author.name: Yoobin Shin, Jaeyoung Lee, Jieun Kang, Hyun Song, Woojin Kim, Andrew Jaeyong Choi

entry.summary: TapTacTouch reconstructs 3D object meshes from sparse tactile contacts without vision, pretraining, or category-specific models, using a multi-finger hand with fingertip pressure arrays and a multi-scale Gaussian Process Implicit framework with geometric priors. This addresses manipulation and perception in occluded or visually constrained environments. It is validated on a real 6-DoF arm with a 20-DoF hand.

entry.title: Pacing AI via Compute Reallocation

author.name: Thomas Larsen

entry.summary: A concrete policy proposal with two components: Verified Compute Allocation Disclosures (VCAD) with independent auditing, and reallocation of compute away from capabilities R&D toward serving customers and safety research. The authors estimate that a 15% reallocation cap starting January 2027 would delay an intelligence explosion by roughly a year, framing this as buying time for more durable policy regimes.

entry.title: Helping AI text detectors keep up with changing conditions

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT and Cornell researchers show that AI-text detectors can be fooled by disguised AI-generated writing and degrade as writing habits and new LLMs shift over time. They apply test-time adaptation, letting a deployed detector learn from unlabeled data on the fly, which substantially improves robustness — the commercial baseline caught only about 27 percent of disguised AI text while their approach performed far better.

entry.title: ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation

author.name: Shaobin He, Yan Gao, Quan Zheng, Zhenyang Lin, Zhen Liu, Jiyan He, Shuxin Zheng

entry.summary: ABSClaw is a zero-code agent that compiles natural-language requests into executable, reality-grounded social simulations, grounding who acts, where, and with whom in survey, census, and geospatial data rather than invented personas. Simulation logic is composed from a shared task-independent vocabulary to make results less sensitive to the backbone model and more tied to real populations.

entry.title: HydroMind: A Checkable Agent for Autonomous Hydrological Research

author.name: Zheng Fang, Yiqun Sun, Simin Qu, Shijie Jiang

entry.summary: This paper asks what happens when a coding agent, rather than the researcher, decides how a hydrological model will be evaluated: how many of its claims are supported by its own data, code, and results, and whether readers can check them. Comparing three harnesses, including the agent's own setup, an augmented harness with the HydroMind hydrological modeling tools, and a checkability-oriented variant, it measures claim support and verifiability in autonomous scientific research. This targets trustworthiness of agent-driven science.

entry.title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions

author.name: Yilong Dai, Yiming Sun, Shengyu Chen, Jiaqi Gong, Xiaowei Jia, Runlong Yu

entry.summary: PhysDial adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight 2D PDE families with changing physical conditions, injecting coefficients with noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equation text as prompts. A counterfactual test shows prior PDE foundation models trained on fixed conditions respond only partially to within-trajectory condition changes.

entry.title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow

author.name: Ojas Sanghi, Anvita Bhagavathula, Alvaro Carbonero, Priya L. Donti

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training, and perturbation-based data augmentation improve zero-shot transfer of graph neural network power flow models from small grids to an unseen 500-bus system. This addresses a key deployment barrier: training data for large grids is prohibitively expensive. The work is motivated by growing power-system uncertainty from renewables, extreme weather, and data center loads.

entry.title: Angular Conditional Distillation: Overcoming Classifier Geometry Mismatch

author.name: Xuefei Zhang, Ruoqi Wang, Lei Cui

entry.summary: Introduces Angular Conditional Distillation (ACD), which reframes knowledge distillation by reconstructing the student classifier in an angular coordinate space to remove magnitude and bias artifacts, then transferring only scale-invariant conditional non-target relations. This addresses classifier geometry mismatch that makes logit-based distillation unreliable across architectures.

entry.title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection

author.name: Yun Bian, Shihao Li, Haiquan Wang, Yi Chen, Zhao Yang, Zhe Cui

entry.summary: Identifies fix reversal in function-level vulnerability detectors, where fixed code receives higher vulnerability probability than the vulnerable original, and traces the cause to a length shortcut amplified by typical fixes lengthening functions. CFVul addresses this with sliding-window encoding and counterfactual content constraints during training. A careful diagnostic-plus-fix contribution for security-relevant code models.

entry.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving

author.name: Xuanwei Ren, Wenda Li

entry.summary: Isabelle Pool Server provides pooled warm headless Isabelle proof-verification sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing, memory-aware admission control, time budgets, checkpointed branching, and clients including Python, two MCP servers, and raw HTTP. It matches or outperforms a PIDE-frontend alternative at multiple worker counts, supporting scalable RL training and multi-agent theorem proving.

entry.title: Same Rank, Different Needs: Rethinking LoRA Redistribution in Federated Learning

author.name: Jinqian Chen, Jihua Zhu, Chang Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a mismatch in federated LoRA fine-tuning: retaining leading singular directions of an aggregated update minimizes reconstruction error but may not preserve the responses most relevant to a particular client. It formalizes the problem, shows matrix-optimal truncation can incur arbitrarily larger response error, and proposes RASA, a plug-in receiver-aware subspace adaptation framework. This improves personalized knowledge transfer under heterogeneous rank budgets.

entry.title: VESPA: Verifiable Symbolic Policy Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Paul K\"onig, Sascha Marton, Stefan L\"udtke, Christian Bartelt

entry.summary: VESPA addresses the inefficiency of the train-verify-retrain loop in safe reinforcement learning, where policies that fail formal verification must be retrained from scratch. It adapts policies using symbolic safety constraints so that candidate policies can be repaired and re-verified rather than rebuilt, targeting safety-critical domains like robotics and autonomous driving. This reduces the cost of obtaining formally verified safe policies.

entry.title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries

author.name: Dylan M Paiton, David L Schultheiss, Matthias K\"ummerer, Zac Cranko, Matthias Bethge

entry.summary: The paper introduces methods to visualize and measure neural network decision boundary geometry directly in high-dimensional input space, avoiding projection distortions, and analyzes boundary curvature and distances across architectures and training methods. Findings show boundaries sit close to inputs within large continuous subspaces with smooth, consistent curvature.

entry.title: JEPA for astronomy: multi-survey spectral alignment puts stellar parameters on the leading principal axes

author.name: Xiaosheng Zhao, Rosemary F. G. Wyse, Yuan-Sen Ting, Alexander S. Szalay

entry.summary: The paper compares alignment objectives for multi-survey stellar spectra foundation models, holding architecture fixed and varying only the loss, and finds that a JEPA-style predictive objective places stellar physics on leading principal axes recoverable by simple linear probes, outperforming contrastive alignment in this respect. Evaluation uses principal-component geometry of Gaia BP/RP spectra and linear probing of stellar parameters.

entry.title: Finetuning VLAs for Dexterous Manipulation: The Right Checkpoint Is All You Need

author.name: Artur Kuramshin, Charlotte Cloutier, Michael Przystupa, Kirsty Ellis, Mohammad S. Akhter, Glen Berseth

entry.summary: The work studies adapting vision-language-action models to multi-fingered dexterous hands, pairing supervised fine-tuning with diffusion-steering reinforcement learning on a pi0.5-style VLA and a LEAP hand. Across five fine-tuning recipes and two simulated tasks, it finds that SFT success poorly predicts post-RL success, so checkpoint selection must account for the RL stage.

entry.title: Optimal Deep Nonparametric Regression with Uniformly Bounded Lipschitz Constants

author.name: Jiaxin Shi, Ziyuan Chen, Jian Huang, Hansheng Wang

entry.summary: The paper establishes sharp approximation theory for deep ReLU networks under a split spectral norm product constraint, showing that smooth Holder functions can be uniformly approximated to arbitrary accuracy with norm-product bounds controlling the Lipschitz constant. This closes a gap where existing results under fixed norm-product bounds could not establish optimal statistical rates for stable deep nonparametric regression. It provides theoretical justification for the widely used practice of weight norm constraints for stability.

entry.title: LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers

author.name: Zizhuo Fu, Haochen Huang, Shengxuan Qiu, Linye Wei, Ziyu Tang, Runsheng Wang, Meng Li

entry.summary: LoopCache accelerates self-speculative decoding for looped (weight-shared recurrent) transformers by addressing two limitations of wave-style methods: stale drafting at fixed loops and memory blowup from batching tokens across loops. It introduces adaptive loop-aware caching to cut KV cache traffic in long-context settings. This is directly relevant to efficient inference for an increasingly popular compact architecture family.

entry.title: Trust the Ray, Not the Depth: Ray-Lateral Agreement for Multi-View 3D Human Pose Fusion

author.name: Farnoosh Koleini, Ahmed Helmy, Pu Wang, Xiwu Cao

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why multi-view fusion of monocular mesh estimates lands bodies meters apart: each estimate's error points almost entirely along its own viewing ray due to assumed focal depth. Ray-Lateral Agreement slides estimates along their own rays to remove depth bias, then fuses views point-wise under a Gaussian whose precision follows each viewing ray. The simple geometric insight yields an elegant maximum-likelihood fusion rule.

entry.title: Keep the Image in Mind: A Visual Board for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Haiming Zhu, Zhiwei Chen, Ding Cao, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces a Visual Board harness for multi-step visual reasoning that separates visual observations, uncertain interpretations, and derived reasoning in a structured, capacity-bounded, revisable workspace rather than an ever-growing dialogue. This explicit separation makes premises auditable so text-only critics can detect conflicts and trigger targeted reinspection of the original image. It targets a documented failure mode where early visual misinterpretations persist as incorrect premises.

entry.title: FlyVQA: Seeing Video Frame Interpolation Quality through Fly Eyes

author.name: Baoliang Chen, Lingyu Zhu, Zhiwei Zhong, Shiqi Wang

entry.summary: FlyVQA uses a frozen fly visual connectome circuit as a biological model for full-reference quality assessment of frame-interpolated videos, exploiting the fly's well-characterized motion pathways to detect temporal artifacts. This is a creative use of recently released fly connectomes as a tractable stand-in for the complexity of human visual circuitry. An unusual and original direction in perceptual quality assessment.

entry.title: TrajWAM: Trajectory-Conditioned Future Learning for Vision-Language Driving

author.name: Xuerui Fang, Gulimila Kezierbieke, Chen Wangxing, Hui Li

entry.summary: TrajWAM is a trajectory-conditioned world action model that improves vision-language driving via auxiliary bird's-eye-view future learning, conditioning DINOv3-aligned BEV predictions on ego-trajectory queries. Training combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with feature separation under perturbed ones to train a shared planner that generates waypoints.

entry.title: Allocentric Memory, Egocentric Acting: A Dual-Frame VLA for Urban Aerial Navigation

author.name: Haotian Xu, Yue Hu, Zhengqiu Zhu, Tuo Feng, Wenguan Wang, Quanjun Yin

entry.summary: CityNav-VLA is a dual-frame vision-language-action model for language-goal UAV navigation that accumulates egocentric observations onto a fixed north-up allocentric map with geographic and landmark priors. A dynamic query conditioned on instruction, observations, state, and motion history retrieves relevant spatial memory for long-range urban navigation.

entry.title: Retroactive Concept Bottleneck Models for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Yang Ji, Ying Sun, Yuanxin Zhuang, Yuting Zhang

entry.summary: RetroCBM improves exempl-free class-incremental learning by retaining small vocabulary-independent statistics relating frozen visual features to a pretrained vision-language model embedding space. This allows newly learned concepts to retroactively benefit old-class predictions even after earlier training images are discarded, addressing underuse of new concepts in concept bottleneck models. The approach keeps predictions interpretable through concepts.

entry.title: SCRiD: Spatial and Contextual References for Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Hao Tan, Zekai Zuo, Boyang Chen, Jinghui Qin

entry.summary: SCRiD is a framework for generalizable detection of AI-generated video that interprets video variations through spatial and contextual references. Matched-Coordinate Residual Response characterizes temporal residual associations under motion and coordinate references with matched subpixel sampling, while Real-Conditioned Score Adaptation learns a content-conditioned denoising reference from authentic videos. This improves robustness where natural motion mimics synthesis artifacts.

entry.title: Gaspard: Expressive unified speech and gesture synthesis with continuous autoregressive flow-matching and decoupled classifier-free guidance

author.name: T\'eo Guichoux, Th\'eodor Lemerle, Catherine Pelachaud, Nicolas Obin

entry.summary: Gaspard is a unified speech and co-speech gesture generation model using continuous autoregressive generation with next-step flow-matching, trained on the large-scale Seamless Interaction dataset. Modality-specific prediction heads and decoupled classifier-free guidance handle the heterogeneous temporal properties of speech and gesture, replacing cascaded pipelines where gestures follow speech. This enables more coordinated multimodal communication synthesis.

entry.title: LuxTac: A Flexible, Scalable, and Open-Source Optical Taxel Array with Distributed Three-Axis Force Sensing for Tactile Robot Learning

author.name: Md Rakibul Islam Prince, John Pelan, Zhiyuan Zhang, Adyaa Khera, Katherine Pesetski, Adeesh Desai, Akimizu Sugiyama, Minwoo Ki, Benjamin Alan Capelle, Temitope Ibrahim Amosa, Zijie Xu, Yihan Huang, Taehun Chung, Long Wang, Wei Li, Shaoting Lin, Yu She

entry.summary: Presents LuxTac, a 3.5 mm-thick flexible optical taxel array built from off-the-shelf components that senses both normal force and shear via color-coded gel cartridges. Offers a scalable, open-source alternative that fills the gap between pressure-only piezoresistive arrays and bulky camera-based tactile sensors.

entry.title: Estimation-Aware Reachability

author.name: Himanshu Paudel, Javier Borquez

entry.summary: The paper extends Hamilton-Jacobi reachability from exact states to the robot's belief, treating unexpected measurements as a bounded adversary and enlarging the unsafe set by current uncertainty so certified states are safe with prescribed probability. The resulting filters nearly eliminate collisions versus certainty-equivalent HJ while being less conservative than uncertainty-padding baselines.

entry.title: Towards Vacuum-Assisted Robotic Needle Interventions: From Fluid Aspiration to Tissue Biopsy

author.name: Sheena Shabana, Laxmi Nag Laxminarayan Nagesh, Marta Vallejo, Karen Donaldson, Maria Koskinopoulou

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified robotic framework for ultrasound-guided fluid aspiration and tissue biopsy using a single vacuum-assisted end effector, combining force-controlled ultrasound scanning, semantic target identification, and automated needle deployment. It unifies two procedures usually treated separately, sharing guidance, safe access, and sample transport requirements. This advances medical robotics toward complete interventional workflows.

entry.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops

author.name: Michael Schroeder

entry.summary: This empirical study dissects why quantizing vision CNNs below 4 bits causes catastrophic accuracy collapse, mapping degradation across ResNet and EfficientNet backbones on the full ImageNet-1k validation set. It shows collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage portions of the network, and characterizes where mixed-precision recovery stops helping. This provides actionable guidance for extreme quantization in resource-constrained deployment.

entry.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design

author.name: Sevda Ebrahimi, Mohammed Saidul Islam, Xiaodan Zhu, Elham Dolatabadi

entry.summary: GRAFT improves evolutionary search for LLM agent architectures by using parent-specific execution evidence (bounded samples of successful and failed runs) to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation, rather than relying on aggregate fitness alone. This makes automated agent design search more informed at the instance level. It represents a solid advance in evolutionary agent-architecture search.

entry.title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills

author.name: Nami Cho, Shailja Gupta

entry.summary: Argues that the right unit of trust for reusable agent skills is a Warranted Reuse Claim: a defeasible, versioned authorization tied to skill, context, evidence, assumptions, and identified defeaters. It proposes Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport, a discipline for deciding which historical validation evidence remains admissible after context changes. A conceptual/position contribution on agent skill safety and governance.

entry.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery

author.name: Marco Virgolin, Harry Desmond, Ester Bergantin, Giorgio Morales, John W. Sheppard, Luigi Romano, Alessandro Lucantonio

entry.summary: automodel is an agent skill that equips general-purpose coding agents with a model discovery recipe for finding analytical equations or neural architectures. Case studies in astrophysics, cardiovascular dynamics, agriculture, traffic flow, and tire dynamics show commercial agents with automodel can identify novel and scientifically useful models.

entry.title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software

author.name: Zhiyuan Peng (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Wei Tao (LIGHTSPEED), Chenhao Ying (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yuan Luo (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yiwen Guo (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: StatePortal is an agent that synthesizes versionable, replayable checkpoints for reaching deep states in GUI software, given a natural-language functional test case and read-only source access. This addresses a recurring testing bottleneck: deep states require long interaction histories whose cost recurs across commits, and self-rendered GUI engines expose no DOM or accessibility tree for conventional automation. Checkpoints are restored via per-application hooks bound or synthesized by an onboarding agent.

entry.title: BiMa-ECGSR: reconstructing the 12-lead ECG from reduced lead sets with bidirectional state-space models

author.name: Ugo Lomoio, Pierangelo Veltri, Pietro Hiram Guzzi

entry.summary: BiMa-ECGSR reconstructs 12-lead ECG signals from reduced lead sets using a bidirectional Mamba state-space encoder-decoder, in both regression and diffusion variants. Trained on PTB-XL across six input configurations and evaluated on over 55,000 records across three cohorts, it substantially outperforms a least-squares linear filter baseline from lead II alone.

entry.title: ExiST: Existence-Aware Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Multi-Organ Segmentation

author.name: Maxx Richard Rahman, Prakhar Kumar, Wolfgang Maass

entry.summary: ExiST identifies a self-training failure mode in semi-supervised multi-organ segmentation: when a teacher misses a small organ, confident background pseudo-labels train the student toward organ absence, extinguishing tail organs, demonstrated by gallbladder Dice dropping from 36.5 to 1.0 in a pilot. It treats a missing organ as unresolved rather than absent and builds pseudo-labels accordingly.

entry.title: NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding

author.name: Zhang Ziyue, Juwei Jian, Baiyang Song, Yunshan Zhong, Jun Peng, Yiyi Zhou, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: NullTok is a training-free method for long video understanding in multimodal LLMs that assesses the spatiotemporal distribution of query-specific evidence using an empirical-null approach to token selection. It avoids the irreversible evidence loss that occurs when noisy frame-level relevance estimates drive frame selection before token pruning. The method targets the token explosion problem in long-video MLLM inference.

entry.title: From Data to Valves: A Self-Learning, Production-Grade Edge Stack for Sustainable HVAC Control

author.name: Abbas Raza Ali, Muhammad Hamza Rehman, Xu Li, Muhammad Ajmal Siddiqui

entry.summary: Describes a production HVAC control stack where three learning components — a prequentially trained transformer forecaster, a distributional soft actor-critic controller, and self-verification — run continuously on an edge gateway per building, with multiple gates bounding the influence of corrupt readings. It demonstrates learned control deployed beyond simulation with continuous on-device adaptation.

entry.title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?

author.name: Yosuke Yamagishi, Tomohiro Kikuchi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe

entry.summary: A retrospective evaluation of two generalist CT foundation models, RADAR and Merlin, on differentiating liver tumors (HCC, cholangiocarcinoma, metastases, hemangioma) across 517 multiphase CT cases, in zero-shot and linear-probing settings. Zero-shot accuracy is reported around 54 percent for RADAR, revealing that generalist models detect lesions but struggle to characterize them.

entry.title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection

author.name: Ziyue Kang, Zixi Qi, Yuchen Dai, Nana Lv, Xirong Cheng, Liang Liu, Ying Li, Haoyan Wei, Haiyang Yao

entry.summary: Formulates visual inspection in field robotics as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, combining a compact recurrent world model with exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. A receding-horizon beam search with online replanning schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and stopping decisions under strict compute and sensing budgets. The approach targets practical inspection scenarios where exhaustive sweeps waste resources.

entry.title: Harmonic Circuit: Chord Progression Lies in a Sparse Principal Information Flow in Symbolic Music Models

author.name: Ruiji Yu, Gus Xia

entry.summary: Extends mechanistic interpretability circuit discovery to symbolic music generation, identifying a sparse principal sub-network in ChatMusician and MuPT that predicts the terminal tonic root in classical harmonic progressions. Using the Auto-Emergence algorithm, the work shows music-functional circuits analogous to those found in NLP. Opens a new domain for interpretability methodology.

entry.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge

author.name: Guilherme Guedes, Marco Apolinario Lainez, Charlotte Frenkel

entry.summary: Hypnos is an open-source platform for continual learning on edge devices, inspired by wake/sleep cycles: a wake phase for fast on-device adaptation under tight resource constraints and a sleep phase for long-term consolidation, addressing backpropagation being prohibitive on edge hardware. It targets online, sample-at-a-time operation with robustness to catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics

author.name: Zihan Wang, Jianzhe Li, Zhenyi Zhang, Peijie Zhou

entry.summary: The paper introduces horizontal flow matching, which learns cell tissue dynamics from spatial transcriptomics snapshots up to shared rigid motion, so that section rotation or translation is not misinterpreted as cell movement. It formulates dynamics via a continuity-reaction equation whose action assigns no cost to shared rigid motion and jointly estimates correspondence and dynamics through an equivalent endpoint problem.

entry.title: When Does Subspace Direction Matter for LoRA? Regime Analysis of the Magnitude Principle in Few-Shot Adaptation

author.name: Nischal Subedi, Cencheng Shen, Peng Zhao

entry.summary: The paper theoretically and empirically characterizes when the initial input-subspace direction of a LoRA adapter matters, refining the recent view that spectral initializers help only via update magnitude. Direction matters most when labeled data is scarce relative to representation dimension and the initialization subspace captures supervised task structure; a spiked-covariance perturbation analysis and first-step analysis of LoRA training explain the subspace's sensitivity. Useful guidance for parameter-efficient fine-tuning practice.

entry.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference

author.name: Shoma Yukawa, Meghna Roychowdhury, Arnab Sanyal, Chengwei Zhou, Shreyas Sen, Gourav Datta

entry.summary: EEG2MCU is a sensing-to-execution co-design framework for wearable EEG inference that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable via task-aware montage selection and generates only the INT8 tensor regions needed per first-layer tile. With halo reuse and access-aware placement across Flash, SRAM, and tightly coupled memory, it reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x on a Cortex-M7 MCU. A strong hardware-algorithm co-design result for edge biomedical inference.

entry.title: Faster to the Wrong Answer: The Price of Local Updates in Federated Optimization

author.name: Molly Wang

entry.summary: This paper provides an exact characterization of the worst-case bias introduced by local updates in federated optimization, for strongly convex quadratic objectives with Hessian eigenvalues in a given range and local updates represented by a spectral filter. It derives the exact worst-case bias per unit client heterogeneity under a conditioning bound and shows plain local gradient descent with small steps is optimal in this setting. The result quantifies the fundamental tradeoff between improved conditioning and introduced bias.

entry.title: Learning with Unlearning: Synaptic Role Partitioning for Simultaneous Continual Learning and Machine Unlearning

author.name: Mohammad Ali Vahedifar, Behzad Bozorgtabar, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: LwU unifies continual learning and machine unlearning, which conflict because both objectives pull on the same weights. It scores each weight against data to keep and data to delete, partitioning the network into four zones with distinct update rules: freezing retention-only weights, clearing deletion-only weights, and handling conflicting zones separately. This resolves the tension at the individual-synapse level rather than the model level.

entry.title: OpenGNS: An Open Dataset of the Gradient Noise Scale across Vision, Language, and Diffusion Models

author.name: Marcel Aach, Jiangtao Wang, Stefan Kesselheim, Andreas Lintermann

entry.summary: The authors release OpenGNS, a dataset of over 400 Gradient Noise Scale measurement trajectories spanning ResNets, GPTs, and Diffusion Transformers from 11M to 1B parameters, enabling systematic study of gradient signal-to-noise and critical batch size. GNS informs batch-size selection and scaling behavior, and this is the first open dataset of its kind.

entry.title: Prioritize, Don't Decide: What We Learned Auditing a Deployed Human-in-the-Loop CV Sorter

author.name: Hadi Mohammadi, Jeroen Sparla, Alexandros Paliouras, Georg Krempl, Robert A. Bagheri

entry.summary: The authors describe and audit a deployed CV priority sorter on a national academic vacancy platform that proposes a reading order while leaving all decisions to the committee, using a frozen multilingual encoder with a per-session linear model retrained after each label. Evaluation shows a committee reading in the tool's order reaches 95% of relevant candidates after half the pile versus nearly the whole pile in arbitrary order.

entry.title: Option-GRPO: Hierarchical RL Against AI Slop in Code Generation for Unseen SDKs

author.name: Prashank Kadam

entry.summary: Option-GRPO is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that adapts a code LLM to unseen SDKs from source code alone, extracting reusable code-pattern hierarchies (options) as reward structure. It explicitly optimizes both functional correctness and code elegance to reduce verbose, non-idiomatic AI-generated code.

entry.title: Rare-Tail Statistics For Learning Biased Gaussian Halfspaces with Label Noise

author.name: Arya Mazumdar, Prateeti Mukherjee, Harsh Vardhan

entry.summary: The paper revisits learning Gaussian halfspaces with label noise in the large-bias regime, where classical averaging-based estimators are provably suboptimal. It proposes the rare-tail mean estimator, which averages only the observed minority class, and shows it recovers the halfspace direction at the information-theoretic sample rate under a broad family of noise models including probit noise. This is a striking example of a simple statistic beating standard first-moment approaches.

entry.title: Training-free motion statistics match self-supervised behavior encoders

author.name: Ziwen Chen

entry.summary: This paper asks whether self-supervised animal-behavior encoders (BAMS, hBehaveMAE) actually beat simple hand-built motion features under a fair comparison protocol: frozen equal-size representations and one shared classifier, preregistered. A training-free PCA summary of generic per-frame measurements reaches 85.8 macro F1 on CalMS21 versus 82.4 for the best encoder, and leads under annotator shifts and few-video settings. This is a provocative skeptical result for the self-supervised behavior modeling literature.

entry.title: GRID-UAV: Geometry and Ray-depth Integrated Decision-making for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

author.name: Anas Anwarul Haq Khan, Amrin Kareem, Muhammad Umer Sheikh, Biplab Banerjee, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: GRID-UAV studies how 3D information should be supplied to vision-language-action policies for UAVs, showing that naively adding depth features yields no gain on long aerial routes and that explicit 3D lifting and implicit geometry alignment fail in complementary ways. The proposed integration of ray-depth and geometry aims to combine the strengths of both grounding approaches. This is a careful analysis of a key design question for aerial VLA policies.

entry.title: What Do Learned 3D Models Add to Localization from Posed References?

author.name: Jaehyun Kim, Wonseok Kang, Jeongmin Lee, Tae-Wan Kim

entry.summary: A systematic empirical study asking whether camera predictions from learned 3D models improve localization compared to classical geometric estimation from a few posed reference images. Across eight learned models and five test sets, the authors find that simple geometric estimation with one extra reference image beats every learned model on two references at fine pose-error thresholds, and results become scene-dependent with three references. This offers a sobering reality check on learned 3D approaches for camera pose tasks.

entry.title: On Demand, Not Uniformity: Adaptive Expert Orchestration for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Mengxin Qin, Kun Wei, Weitao An, Jiahua Li, Xu Yang, Cheng Deng

entry.summary: This paper improves Mixture-of-Experts approaches to multimodal continual instruction tuning by recognizing heterogeneous adaptation demands across tasks, measured via layer-wise gradient pressure and token-wise prediction difficulty. It proposes coverage-calibrated expert injection deciding where new capacity is needed, plus residual mechanisms controlling per-token expert contribution. This refines how MLLMs adapt sequentially without forgetting.

entry.title: Agreement Is Not Accuracy: LiDAR Elevation Errors Hidden in LiDAR-Camera Extrinsics

author.name: Yeon Kun Lee, Dongseok Yang, Deok-Kyeong Jang, Choongho Chung, Junyoung Lee, Hyeongseok So

entry.summary: This paper shows that systematic LiDAR elevation biases can be silently absorbed into estimated LiDAR-camera extrinsics, meaning sensor agreement does not imply geometric accuracy. It jointly estimates a shared sensor-specific elevation correction alongside per-recording extrinsics using checkerboard poses located via ray-plane intersections without reported ranges. An important cautionary result for autonomous driving sensor calibration.

entry.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ruisi Zhao, You Li, Sihan Chen, Aosong Cheng, Chixiang Ma, Sen Pei, Zhen Yang, Hehe Fan, Dongliang He, Yi Yang

entry.summary: RoughCut-Bench is the first comprehensive benchmark for automatic video rough-cutting, evaluating LVLMs on visually driven editing (highlight detection, selection, ordering, requirement adherence) and speech-driven editing (filler removal, deduplication) based on ASR transcripts. It fills an evaluation gap in a core media-production stage that LVLMs have largely ignored. Useful groundwork for a new task area.

entry.title: SEER: Semantic Evidence for Executable Region Propagation in Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Junyang Chen, Xiao Li, Yiguo Qiao, Wenbin Li

entry.summary: SEER is a training-free, test-time repair layer for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation that casts post-prediction correction as evidence-conditioned label propagation. A frozen VLM verifies regional evidence and an execution gate certifies corrections as plausible and vocabulary-legal before applying them.

entry.title: SCOUT: Risk-Guided Foundation-Model Escalation for Robust Tissue Detection in Whole-Slide Images

author.name: Cristian Tommasino, Antonio M. Rinaldi

entry.summary: SCOUT is a risk-guided cascade for whole-slide image tissue detection that uses a lightweight audit network to estimate where a cheap thumbnail-based segmentation is likely wrong, then selectively escalates uncertain regions to a frozen pathology foundation model. An asymmetric consensus rule merges predictions to reduce false positives. This addresses the cost of exhaustive foundation-model inference in computational pathology.

entry.title: Why Multi-Source Audio Fails to Compose: A Geometric Diagnosis and Its Remedy

author.name: Anurag Singh, Prajwal Singh, Shanmuganathan Raman

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why multi-source audio-to-image generation fails compositionally, identifying a geometric displacement phenomenon where audio tokens occupy positions in CLIP text-token space that the diffusion U-Net cannot reliably attend to or spatially ground. Analysis of BEATs and CLAP embeddings reveals three key geometric properties, and CLAP-based remedies are explored. The work connects embedding geometry to compositional failure.

entry.title: SCR: Detecting Backdoor-Poisoned Samples through Clean-Reference Residuals

author.name: Yi Yang, Jinyang Huang, Feng-Qi Cui, Yu-Tong Guo, Sirui Zhao, Haiming Jin, Weihua Li, Quan Bai, Meng Li

entry.summary: SCR detects backdoor-poisoned training samples by using a small set of clean reference samples to reconstruct sample-specific features that account for benign semantic variation, then flagging coherent deviations from the clean-reference residual. This addresses the problem that class-level statistics in existing detectors flag benign deviations while missing poisoned samples that blend into class distributions.

entry.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models

author.name: Zhaolu Wang, Jiacheng Xu, Lihong Wang, Shuqing Wang, Jianjie Fang, Ziyou Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Rongze Tang, Yiding Ma, Xin Zhang, Jiawei Chen, Wei Wu, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: HandWorldBench systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human, simulated, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions including visual quality, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. It fills a gap in fine-grained evaluation for embodied tasks involving hand-object interaction. This connects world model research to dexterous manipulation evaluation.

entry.title: GTI: Grounding Task Intent Throughout Long-Horizon VLA Manipulation

author.name: Tianqi Gong, Haochen Niu, Yusheng Zhao, Lantao Zhang, Haoyu Liu, Rendong Ying, Peilin Liu

entry.summary: GTI grounds global task intent in long-horizon VLA manipulation by localizing the active subtask and execution phase from observation and history, then generating phase-dependent visual targets (contact state and local completion state) that, with local instructions, condition the VLA. It also includes anomaly monitoring during execution.

entry.title: Proprioceptive Simultaneous Base and Terrain Elevation Estimation for Legged Robot Locomotion

author.name: Michael Maravgakis, Stylianos Piperakis, Panos Trahanias

entry.summary: The paper proposes SBEE, a real-time open-source framework for legged robots that couples a left-invariant EKF for floating-base estimation with a grid-based elevation map in a bidirectional loop, treating footsteps as persistent proprioceptive landmarks anchoring the vertical axis. This mitigates vertical drift that destabilizes swing-leg control in visually degraded environments. It mirrors SLAM using terrain elevation in place of landmarks.

entry.title: A Generative Model for Higher-Order Network Dynamics

author.name: Valentina S\'anchez, Theodore Papamarkou, Gonzalo N\'apoles, \c{C}i\c{c}ek G\"uven, Koen V. Haak

entry.summary: The authors introduce a generative model of stochastic network dynamics with user-specified pairwise and higher-order interactions represented by directed hyperedges, providing ground-truth systems with known generating mechanisms. This enables careful validation and comparison of higher-order information-theoretic dependence measures that previously lacked proper benchmarks.

entry.title: JEPA as a Transferable Optimizer: Learning and Understanding Black-Box Optimization from Reward-Agnostic Pretraining

author.name: Mayukh Debnath, Manan Roy Choudhury
