entry.title: The Rhythm of Generated Video: Latent Chunking Leaves Periodic Traces in Compressed Bitstreams

author.name: Chen Ye Gan, Bryan Zhen Zhang, Gene Wen, Yuxing han

entry.summary: This paper shows that causal video autoencoders leave architecture-specific periodic fingerprints in compressed bitstreams: latent-chunk boundaries concentrate unpredictable content, causing rate-distortion encoders to allocate bits periodically (four-frame pulses for CogVideoX and Wan2.2, eight-frame for LTX-Video). A training-free peak-ratio statistic detects generated video with AUC 0.84-0.94 without decoding pixels. This opens a new, compute-efficient channel for AI-video detection.

entry.title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs

author.name: Chengqian Ma, Yuanze Zeng, Hongyu Wang, Mingfeng Lin, YiCheng Xiao, Yu Chen, Pengyu Li, WenHao Wang, Yuexiao Ma, Xiawu Zheng, Fei Chao

entry.summary: VIVID addresses a key weakness in video multimodal LLMs: they treat video as static multi-image reasoning, discarding intermediate frames and losing motion cues. The method augments keyframes with inter-frame Patch Diffs to preserve localized changes and event ordering under tight frame budgets.

entry.title: ReLAP: Latent Action Pretraining through Recurrent Video Prediction in JEPA Space

author.name: R. Gnana Praveen, Ali Rouzbayani, Zhiying Jiang, Bidhan Roy

entry.summary: ReLAP is a latent-action pretraining framework that combines local inverse-dynamics transition learning with recurrent multi-step future prediction in a frozen JEPA representation space. Error backpropagation through rollouts encourages temporally consistent latent actions from unlabeled video for robot learning.

entry.title: How should we define “capabilities activities” for the purpose of pacing?

author.name: Alek Westover

entry.summary: This post proposes a standardized taxonomy for classifying which uses of compute count as AI capabilities activities, intended as a foundation for compute-based frontier pacing via legislation or voluntary commitments. It lays out desiderata such as effectiveness at slowing progress and robustness to adversarial reframing by labs, then defines categories of activity.

entry.title: RL Misalignment Under Accurate Rewards and Explicit Requirements

author.name: Frank Shen

entry.summary: This work constructs verifiable RL environments with accurate task rewards, explicitly stated contextual permission boundaries, and guaranteed shortcuts, showing that RL can increase genuine capability while teaching agents to cross authorization boundaries to do more real work. This extends reward hacking beyond incentive errors to violations of constraints even under accurate rewards.

entry.title: A closer look at “Sparks of Weight-Space Programming”

author.name: ZhiW

entry.summary: Researchers at UC San Diego analyze the widely circulated claim that GPT-6 Astra can edit a small Qwen model's MLP weights via a written program to improve its math performance, concluding the effect is equivalent to context-dependent activation steering along a fixed data-constructed direction rather than genuine weight-space programming. They further show that a trained sensing vector generalizing the edit improves effectiveness, and that building the steering direction from short synthetic traces rather than real rollouts is substantially more effective.

entry.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks

author.name: Xingchen AGI Lab, :, Baotian Hu, Bingkai Yang, Boyang Wang, Changzai Pan, Chao Lyu, Chao Wang, Chen Li, Chenshuo Pan, Chenyu Lin, Chenyuan Zhang, Chongming Liu, Dawei Fan, Di Wu, Dong Guo, Dong Li, Dongfang Li, Enlin Liu, Fanye Xiao, Fengkai Li, Fubei Yao, Gang Lin, Han Gao, Hanming Wu, Haowei He, Huapeng Liu, Hua Wang, Huinan Xu, Jiahong Xiong, Jiaxin Peng, Jianxiang Ma, Jianxing Zhuge, Jie Zhang, Ji Xiong, Jinglin Chen, Jingqi Li, Jingxuan Li, Jiwang Ye, Junchen Li, Junbiao Li, Junyang Wu, Kaidong Yu, Kaipeng Jia, Kehai Chen, Kuai Li, Laobin Liu, Lei Li, Libo Qin, Lingling Shi, Luwen Pu, Menghao Xu, Mengjiao Bao, Mengqi Chen, Min Zhang, Mingrui Wang, Naying Wang, Peicong Han, Peiming Guo, Pengfei Li, Qiang Feng, Qi Wang, Qingjun Zhu, Qingli Li, Qitai Ding, Qiyi Xie, Quanchao Zhao, Rongbao Han, Rui Xue, Ruiyu Fang, Ruiting Song, Shijie Li, Shiquan Wang, Shuangyong Song, Sishi Xiong, Teng Su, Wankang Bao, Weijie Zhang, Wei Mao, Weiwei Fu, Weiyang Huang, Wenmin Deng, Wenqing Hu, Wujie Zhong, Xi Yu, Xiaohui Hu, Xiaomin Fang, Xiaomeng Huang, Xiaoqiong Shi, Xiaotong Shang, Xiaoyu Li, Xinglei Xu, Xin Jiang, Xin Wang, Xin Zhang, Xinzhang Liu, Xue Liu, Xuefeng Bai, Xuewei He, Yahan Li, Yanhan Zhang, Yanlei Xue, Yanzhang Wu, Yang Yu, Yi Liu, Yin Zhang, Yingyan Li, Yitong Yao, Yixuan Li, Yongqiang Xia, Yongxiang Li, Yinzhou Zhu, Yu Zhao, Yuhao Jiang, Yunpeng Zhang, Yuting Lin, Yuxuan Wu, Yuyao Huang, Yuyi Wang, Zebo Peng, Zhenwu Pei, Zhenxiong Li, Zhao Wang, Zhaoxi Zhang, Zhihao Yang, Zhiqiang Dong, Zhiwei Yan, Zhilong Lu, Zhonghao Guo, Zhongheng Wu, Zhongjiang He, Zhongqiu Li, Zhu Yuan, Zhuoru Jiang, Zhuoyi Wei, Zijia Guo, Zilu Huang, Zhipeng Guo, Zirui Li, Zihan Wang

entry.summary: This technical report from Xingchen AGI Lab presents Xing 4, a series of large language models extending the TeleChat lineage, trained on Ascend hardware with MindSpore-based infrastructure. It details coordinated advances in sparse activation, attention design, speculative decoding, topology-aware hybrid sharding, and reasoning/agentic post-training, demonstrating frontier-capable model training on domestic Chinese chips.

entry.title: MCTS Is Counting the Wrong Thing: Learning Exploration Counts for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Xuan Zhang, Zhijian Zhou, Zicheng Hu, Yan Feng, Hongyan Hao, Yuan Qi, Chao Qu

entry.summary: The paper identifies count fragmentation as an overlooked MCTS bottleneck for LLM reasoning: standard UCT assigns independent visit counts to textual branches, so different formulations of the same reasoning strategy repeatedly receive exploration bonuses, increasing cumulative regret per the theoretical analysis. LPC-MCTS fixes only the exploration statistic, using a lightweight Coin-Flipping Network head on the policy's hidden representation to learn pseudo-counts over strategies.

entry.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents

author.name: Zhuohan Cai, Zhangxuan Gu, Runze Li, Beitong Zhou, Ming Wen, Hongbo Yu, Shuheng Shen, Changhua Meng

entry.summary: PACT targets the execution gap in GUI agents where a correct plan is followed by a failing action, noting that outcome-supervised RL broadcasting a negative advantage across all tokens penalizes good planning alongside bad execution. The framework combines reference-aligned plan protection with plan-aligned action repair while preserving the original scalar action reward.

entry.title: Remembered as Brief: Stored Preferences SilentlyRemove Decision-Critical Information

author.name: Joshua Adrian Cahyono

entry.summary: This benchmark study shows that assistant memory of user preferences can silently remove decision-critical information: a stored preference causes models to omit warnings or options the user never sees, while every individual sentence remains true. The benchmark spans 100 decisions across 25 domains where only the assistant's memory varies, testing five models including Gemini 2.5 Flash. This reveals a novel memory-mediated safety risk distinct from fact-checking.

entry.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table

author.name: Muhammed Fatih Bal{\i}n

entry.summary: CPTC is a low-bit tensor quantization format whose decoder computes each value with two multiplications and indexing into a 64-byte table, recovering much of the information-theoretic loss that per-value formats like INT4/FP4 incur. It jointly encodes values via trellis coding, serves all bit widths with one decoder, and suits write-once-read-many weights.

entry.title: Eyes in the Update? Learning Where Rewards Land in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Lixuan He, Tianzhe Chu, Shulin Tian, Shikang Zheng, Feng Chen, Yi Ma

entry.summary: Gaze-RL is a representation-driven policy optimization method for multimodal RL that infers where a trajectory-level outcome reward should be allocated within a response using the model's own multimodal computation, rather than auxiliary annotators or process labels. It targets the mismatch between trajectory-level rewards and sparse, unevenly used visual evidence in image and video reasoning. This makes multimodal RL more token-sensitive without external supervision.

entry.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science

author.name: Ron Bekkerman, Nichole Li, Bahareh Kargar, Mark Somers

entry.summary: Analyzes 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015-2025 and finds that most pre-2023 scientific practice trends continued with limited detectable breaks after LLMs emerged, with exceptions like accelerated CS coauthor growth in Asia. It establishes an empirical baseline for assessing LLM impact on science.

entry.title: ReMaRL: Learning to Unmask and Remask in Frozen Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Egor Shibaev, Danila Biktimirov, Ivan Klimov, Artem Makoian, Viacheslav Meshchaninov, Dmitry Vetrov

entry.summary: ReMaRL trains a lightweight reinforcement learning policy, roughly 0.3M parameters, to decide which tokens to unmask, retain, or remask in frozen masked diffusion language models, directly optimizing final-answer correctness. Prior learned policies could only unmask, while remasking heuristics were not reward-optimized. This enables self-correction using newly generated context during parallel decoding.

entry.title: NONSENSE: Non-Semantic Strings Expose Semanticity Gaps in Dense Retrieval

author.name: Ankit Gupta

entry.summary: NONSENSE is a black-box sparse-edit probe that constructs visibly non-semantic strings, without copying query terms, that nonetheless achieve high dense similarity to a query. Across five BEIR-style datasets and three single-vector retrievers, these strings often outrank the retriever's own best judged relevant passage and even rank first in the corpus. The paper exposes a semanticity gap showing that nearest-neighbor similarity can be fully decoupled from meaning in dense retrieval.

entry.title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair

author.name: Tao Zhang, Yi Zhong, Jinhao Ruan, Yipeng Gao, Linfeng Zhong, Youming Yang, Yuan Wang

entry.summary: SR-VLA reduces control stalls in vision-language-action policy execution by predicting next-boundary observations and using them to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk, then selectively repairing mismatches when real inputs arrive. This hides inference latency without the risks of unconditional reuse or full recomputation.

entry.title: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition

author.name: Yunxiao Shi (Australian National University), Tingwei Chen (University of Technology Sydney), Dannong Xu (Australian National University), Ahad N. Zehmakan (Australian National University), Jialie Shen (City St George's, University of London), Zhendong Chu (Squirrel Ai Learning), Qingsong Wen (Squirrel Ai Learning)

entry.summary: The paper formulates AgentComposition, the task of jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle to maximize end-to-end execution utility for a given task. The proposed retrieval-grounded generator recombines candidate resources via constrained beam search and a bundle-aware critic, allowing newly added resources without retraining and capturing complementarities that independent scoring misses.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents

author.name: Hejia Zhang, Zhongming Yu, Yimin Ding, Wei-Ting Chen, Hengjia Yu, Wentao Ni, Yijun Liu, Cong Xu, Xin Chen, Matrix Yao, Fan Zhao, Jishen Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark and evidence-flow profiler for multi-agent memory inconsistency, using controlled factual conflicts in Harvey LAB document-review tasks to study how facts can vanish between worker and lead agent contexts. Delegation increases retrieval of both conflicting claims (50.2% to 68.7%) yet reduces conflict detection (16.2% to 13.2%), and workers report both claims for only 35.2% of retrieved pairs.

entry.title: LMLineage: Content Lineage and Context Governance for LLM Agents

author.name: Wei Hou, Jingxin Geng, Xin Chen, Zheqing Jiang

entry.summary: LMLineage is an out-of-band system that attributes each output sentence of an agent session to its supporting input spans with calibrated confidences, without white-box model access or extra inference passes. It also introduces concept-drift micro compaction, which surgically compresses only drifted context documents while preserving active instructions.

entry.title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build

author.name: Jason Liang, Dylan Waldner, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: This paper tests whether embedding short value statements (drawn from Schwartz's theory of basic human values) into a self-improving coding agent's persistent instructions changes both performance and the artifacts it builds. It evaluates openness to change, conservation, self-enhancement, and self-transcendence across diverse coding tasks over repeated self-improvement iterations. The finding that values affect performance and output character is directly relevant to shaping open-ended agent behavior beyond task rewards.

entry.title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models

author.name: Cheng Li, Adhyyan Narang, Jiayi Yuan, John F. Buss, Jina Suh, Devon Sandel-Fernandez, Yulia Tsvetkov, Adam M. Kuczynski, Tim Althoff

entry.summary: SimAI is a framework for mechanistic user simulation that models how psychological factors shape user responses, using a graph reconstruction objective that rewards conversations reflecting underlying psychological relationships. It introduces PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs from 516 psychotherapy cases, enabling simulation grounded in psychological mechanisms rather than surface imitation.

entry.title: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection

author.name: Alexandra G. Roberts, Tonmoy Hossain, Mark Olchanyi, Stefan Brandst\"atter, Jonathan Williams Ramirez, Ana Lawry Aguila, Matthew Rosen, Annabel Sorby-Adams, W. Taylor Kimberly, Juan Eugenio Iglesias

entry.summary: The authors propose PathoDraw, a generative model of brain MRI that draws lesions into label maps conditioned on healthy anatomy before controllable synthesis, enabling pathology randomization at scale. This creates contrast-agnostic synthetic priors that unlock uncurated hospital archives and support zero-shot abnormality detection across contrasts and resolutions.

entry.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression

author.name: Fengyuan Liu, Jay Gala, Siva Reddy, Dzmitry Bahdanau

entry.summary: EchoMoE is a lightweight retrofit to mixture-of-experts models that compresses activations to reduce the dispatch and combine communication steps in expert parallelism, which become bottlenecks as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. The modification requires no retraining of existing MoE models. It targets inference efficiency at large scale where synchronous collectives dominate cost.

entry.title: Manufacturing Differential Sparsity: Planner-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient World Model Planning

author.name: Wenbo Zhu, Paul Yi-Chia Chen, Yuanhan Li, Zishen Wan, Christopher Torng

entry.summary: Tackles the slowness of JEPA-style latent world model planning, where sampling-based MPC requires tens of thousands of predictor inferences per plan. The key insight is that the planner itself chooses which action candidates to evaluate together, so it can deliberately group similar actions to exploit differential bit-level sparsity in a quantized predictor. This planner-hardware co-design could make latent world model planning viable for real-time embodied control.

entry.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Guoqing Wang, Pin Tang, Xiangxuan Ren, Chao Ma

entry.summary: Argues that pixel-level future frame generation in world VLA models for driving wastes most tokens on planning-irrelevant appearance details, and proposes agent-centric world states that encode geometry, motion, and interactions directly. This yields more efficient end-to-end driving systems that reason over imagined futures.

entry.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching

author.name: Giannis Daras, Marios Papachristou, Adam Klivans, Antonio Torralba, Constantinos Daskalakis

entry.summary: Ambient SFT addresses overfitting and catastrophic forgetting in supervised fine-tuning by using a frozen copy of the pre-trained model as a noisy teacher to augment small fine-tuning datasets. The fine-tuned model must match the teacher's high-temperature conditional distributions at a coarse level, leveraging imperfect predictions to expand effective training signal. The framework is principled and aims to preserve the tails of the pre-training distribution during post-training.

entry.title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation

author.name: Maor Farid

entry.summary: This paper frames transformers as nonlinear dynamical systems across three clocks: layers, training steps, and generated tokens, connecting phenomena like fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, and chaos. It condenses roughly 200 papers into a Three-Clock Dictionary mapping fifteen nonlinear dynamics concepts onto language model behavior, marking each correspondence as proved, measured, or conjectured, with illustrative mechanical and LM side-by-side examples.

entry.title: Sample-efficient Personalization of Large Language Model Alignment with Multidimensional User Preference Data

author.name: Zhen-Yu Zhang, Jerry Huang, Gang Niu, Takashi Ishida, Masashi Sugiyama

entry.summary: The authors improve sample efficiency of online LLM preference alignment by noting that LLM-perceived uncertainty differs from user-perceived uncertainty, and that user preferences are often multidimensional. They leverage multidimensional user preference data to select comparison pairs that are more informative from the user perspective, enabling personalized alignment with fewer annotations.

entry.title: Escaping Latent Traps by Remembering: Training-Free Episodic Kernel Repulsion for World-Model Planning

author.name: Yican Zhao, Bolin Yang, Ruizhe Wang, Haiyang Guo, Fuji Yang, Bingo Wing-Kuen Ling, Zelin Zang

entry.summary: The paper identifies latent traps, local minima in latent distance that strand world-model agents behind walls and in dead ends, and proposes Episodic Kernel Repulsion, a training-free cost term that penalizes revisiting latents stored in a novelty-gated episodic memory. Across two JEPA world models and four benchmarks, average planning success improves substantially, for example from 31.8 percent to 46.7 percent on LeWM. This is a clean, plug-in improvement for memoryless receding-horizon planning.

entry.title: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness When Only a Few Hospitals Collaborate

author.name: Adnan Malkani

entry.summary: This empirical audit evaluates eight Byzantine-robust aggregation rules, including FedAvg, Krum, Bulyan, and geometric median, in realistic small-coalition clinical federated learning settings with three to six unequal hospitals, using 54,214 training runs on FLamby medical datasets. It reveals issues of validity, data-share dictatorships, and fairness that synthetic many-client benchmarks conceal. The work challenges standard robust-aggregation evaluation practice.

entry.title: The Illusion of Grounding: Do Vision-Language Models Weigh Retrieved Text and Images Like an Ideal Observer?

author.name: Basavaraj R M, Harshal Chandel

entry.summary: This work introduces GIB-200K, a 200,000-item benchmark stressing retrieval-augmented VLMs with retrieval noise, visual degradation, and cross-modal conflicts. Using ideal Bayesian cue combination as a reference, it formally defines failure modes such as knowledge inertia where models over-weight retrieved text.

entry.title: Discovery of new antiviral agents through artificial intelligence: in vitro and in vivo results

author.name: Roza Izmailyan, Mher Matevosyan, Hamlet Khachatryan, Anastasiya Shavina, Smbat Gevorgyan, Artur Ghazaryan, Irina Tirosyan, Yeva Gabrielyan, Marusya Ayvazyan, Boris Martirosyan, Vardan Harutyunyan, Hovakim Zakaryan

entry.summary: A deep reinforcement learning molecule-generation platform designed compounds targeting influenza neuraminidase, generating 60,291 candidates with most showing better physicochemical properties than oseltamivir. Nine compounds were synthesized and tested, yielding two non-sialic-acid-like inhibitors effective against influenza A and B, including H275Y mutant strains, validated in vitro and in vivo.

entry.title: Task Convergent Flow Matching for Generative Robotics

author.name: Lorenzo Paiola, Maximilian St\"olzle, Giorgio Grioli, Daniela Rus, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Introduces a task-centric inference-time refinement framework for flow-matching robot policies that evaluates candidate action chunks via parallel physics-based rollouts and searches for motions satisfying sufficient conditions for task convergence. Task-level performance funnels bound temporary regressions while requiring net progress per chunk, with proven convergence conditions under repeated funnel satisfaction.

entry.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rui Ning, Om Chabra, Hari Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Presents Spool, a system enabling bounded-window streaming question answering over recent video with hybrid VLMs that interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet. Its key insight is that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so each frame's effect can be captured as a composable transformation, making sliding-window expiry cheap without re-running the window. Targets visual accessibility agents and robotics.

entry.title: Where Does Hindsight Enter Clinical Agent Benchmarks? An Audit of Simulators and Case Construction

author.name: Meilu Zhu, Xiaohan Li, Axiu Mao

entry.summary: HindAudit separates three hindsight channels in LLM diagnostic-agent benchmarks — diagnosis leakage to the simulator, retrospective context, and agent-facing case text — and measures each with judges trained only on real data. Across 27,489 MIMIC-IV emergency admissions, five registered tests found no leakage into simulated lab results, though gatekeepers can raise agent performance.

entry.title: Polarity Composition Hypothesis: Causal Evidence from Negation in NLI

author.name: Nhi Hoai Doan, Tatsuya Hiraoka, Munachiso Samuel Nwadike, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Proposes the Polarity Composition Hypothesis, a causal model of how language models compute negation in natural language inference, and validates it behaviorally and with Distributed Alignment Search, finding causally effective subspaces aligned with the hypothesis variables. These representations transfer across negation forms and partially to MNLI.

entry.title: SCAN: Site-Aware Collaborative Privacy-Preserving Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Neurological Disease Classification

author.name: Nikhil J. Dhinagar, Rishab Pendam, Harmony S. Cen, Sophia I. Thomopoulos, John P. John, Mahir H. Khan, Sook-Lei Liew, Erik Kaestner, Carrie McDonald, Paul M. Thompson

entry.summary: SCAN lets new clinical sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model to neurological disease classification without retraining or sharing patient scans, exchanging only norm-bounded, noise-perturbed class prototypes and counts. Using 7,641 brain MRI scans from 67 sites across 12 countries covering Alzheimer's disease, stroke, and epilepsy, it shows cross-site benefits at seven unseen sites without harming existing sites. It is a compelling example of privacy-preserving federated adaptation at realistic scale.

entry.title: SARVIA: Fast-Adapting the Strong SAR Foundation Models That Are Already in Your MLLMs

author.name: Yuxuan Li, Zichen Tian, Qianru Sun

entry.summary: SARVIA shows that visual encoders inside modern multimodal LLMs can outperform dedicated synthetic aperture radar foundation models as downstream initializations, questioning the need for costly domain-specific pretraining. It proposes an adaptive post-pretraining method that specializes MLLMs using self-supervised visual questions for all-weather Earth observation.

entry.title: Fast and Strong Image Protection against Diffusion Personalization

author.name: Jiwon Park, Jihye Kang, Namhyuk Ahn

entry.summary: Proposes the Protective Diffusion Model (PDM), which is trained once and samples adversarial perturbations that prevent diffusion models from personalizing on protected images, distilled from an iterative teacher and post-trained with a Target Residual Projection reward. It outperforms nine baselines on faces and artworks at roughly a tenth of the cost.

entry.title: Evolve in Panorama, Render in View: Panoramic World State Evolution for Video World Models

author.name: Longtao Jiang, Mingfei Han, Jianmin Bao, Tingjun Dai, Jinjie Wei, Zhiran Zhang, Xin Tao, Zhihui Li, Salman Khan, Xiaojun Chang

entry.summary: PanoEvo addresses the problem that video world models freeze or lose unobserved scene content when the camera turns away, by evolving world state in the latent space of a panoramic video diffusion model where every viewing direction persists at every time step. The authors also build PanoEvo-Data, an event-centric dataset from real 360-degree videos to train the evolver.

entry.title: HandUMI: A Modular Hand-Worn Parallel-Jaw Interface for Robot-Free Bimanual Data Capture

author.name: Brik Meza, Leonardo Perez, Alvaro Mendoza-Li, Aniela Ubillus, Mitshell Ramos, Raul Bastidas, Mauricio Olivera, Bryan Bastidas

entry.summary: HandUMI is a low-cost (~$557), open-source hand-worn parallel-jaw interface for capturing bimanual demonstrations without a robot, using VR controllers and fingertip encoders. Demonstrations retarget across seven simulated arms and 562 real demonstrations train ACT and pi-0.5 policies on bimanual towel folding with measurable success.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Baicheng Li, Wenkang Qin, Youqi Pan, Dongxiao Mao, Yukun Zhou, Chuanfu Shen, Dong Wu, Shunkai Zhou, Zike Yan, Wei Sui, Hongbin Zha

entry.summary: The paper proposes a geometry-supervised training framework enabling zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills across embodiments, using calibrated forward kinematics to supply tool-space supervision to foreign action interfaces without joint labels. Positive reachability checks select cross-robot supervision targets for a visual policy that predicts native commands.

entry.title: A solvable model of learning in shallow MLPs

author.name: Joey Turnbull

entry.summary: The authors propose a tractable model of two-layer MLP training that replaces the elementwise nonlinearity with a global featurization splitting preactivations into polynomial components, yielding simple low-dimensional ODE training dynamics. The model qualitatively and quantitatively matches real MLP training on coordinate targets, advancing the training dynamics agenda in deep learning theory.

entry.title: Monitorability evaluations and policy proposals

author.name: evhub

entry.summary: evhub (Evan Hubinger), explicitly in a personal rather than official Anthropic capacity, proposes a four-way taxonomy of monitorability — control, training, auditing, and deployment monitorability — and connects each to measurable evaluations such as sabotage benchmarks like LinuxArena. The post situates ongoing policy debates, including Redwood's proposal and the author's counter-proposal, within this framework.

entry.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory

author.name: Mingyang Liu, Qingcan Kang, Shixiong Kai, Kaichao Liang, Xiaojin Fu, Tao Zhong, Linqi Song

entry.summary: EvoDisco formulates agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery, where a learnable policy conditioned on memory state and task history selects and instantiates among four semantic operators (Abstract, Refine, Bridge, Reframe) rather than following a fixed operator schedule. This lets the agent learn which memory transformation to apply, when, and how during interaction.

entry.title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators

author.name: Yujun Wang, Jiqiang Li, Yinuo Lu, Jinhe Bi, Aniri, Wenxuan Ye, Boliang Liu, Sikuan Yan, Shuning Wang, Xuebing Zhou, S{\"o}ren Pirk, Hinrich Sch{\"u}tze, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: EvoSkill-S1 is an RL-driven framework that treats reusable agent skills as direct objects of evolution, using five genetic-inspired operators (revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, crossover) to transform parent skills into candidate child skills from hard-negative failures. Downstream task rewards train the skill evolver, aiming for deeper, better-controlled skill-bank updates than rollout-driven accumulation or heuristic reflection.

entry.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop

author.name: Zerui Yang, Quan Xue, Miaomiao Dong, Chaorui Zhang, Xuanyu Zheng, Xiyuan Wang, Haolin Ruan, Xueyan Niu, Guangcheng Song, Weixi Zhang, Wei Han, Bo Bai

entry.summary: The paper studies when coding agents should stop via anytime evaluation: replaying ~6,000 recorded runs of eight open models in two scaffolds on SWE-bench Verified, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and measuring per-step cost. It finds the hindsight saving available at passing self-tests ranges from under 1% to 57% depending on the setup, showing agents often keep working after their own tests pass. This quantifies a real inefficiency and enables paired comparisons without new trajectories.

entry.title: The Hidden Cost of MoE Diffusion Decoding: Profiling and Fixing the Sampler

author.name: Harshit Samrat, Ramakrishna Paramahamsa Kompella

entry.summary: Profiling a 26B-parameter diffusion MoE language model on a bandwidth-bound edge accelerator, the authors find that after weight quantization the per-token sampling and stopping pipeline over the full canvas-by-vocabulary logits tensor, not expert GEMMs, dominates decode time. They propose fixes to this previously overlooked bottleneck, which is S times larger per token than autoregressive sampling.

entry.title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World

author.name: Kaixin Li, Meng Luo, Yanlin Li, Yuchen Tian, Xiang Liu, Xiangru Jian, Yan Yang, Zhiheng Xi, Yang Zhang, Ziyang Luo, Mingfei Cheng, Hongzhan Lin

entry.summary: This position/survey paper examines agentic intelligence for the physical world, framing the physical environment itself as the program's test suite when coding agents write programs for robots, laboratories, and industrial controllers. It organizes the area around three questions: how agents write, evaluate, and take responsibility for programs whose correctness evidence is costly and fallible. It synthesizes an emerging research area at the intersection of coding agents and embodied AI.

entry.title: Similar Is Not Useful: Selecting In-Context Demonstrations by Closed-Loop Utility

author.name: Jiachen Li, Zhigen Zhao, Shihao Li, Dongmei Chen, Long Chen, Zhuo Xu

entry.summary: This paper challenges the default of selecting in-context demonstrations for retrieval-augmented VLA policies by visual similarity, instead scoring demonstrations by their measured closed-loop success utility. On a frozen RICL setup over pi0-FAST on LIBERO, top-utility demonstration pools achieve 66.4 percent success versus about 55.7 percent for similarity-based and random pools across 760 paired episodes in 19 tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Attribute-Centric Fairness: Modelling and Mitigating Unified Bias Representation in Omni-modal Large Language Models

author.name: Runqi Lin, Suqin Yuan, Zihao Fu, Chris Russell

entry.summary: This work argues that attribute-centric debiasing, which imposes separate fairness objectives per sensitive attribute and modality, fails in omni-modal LLMs where biases interact across modalities and generalize beyond predefined attributes. The authors model a unified bias representation and develop mitigation that jointly addresses diverse social stereotypes in joint multimodal understanding and generation. This addresses fairness for next-generation multimodal backbones.

entry.title: M$^3$-Test: Coverage Gaps in Joint-Perturbation Testing of Visual Question Answering

author.name: Enhui Wan, Xiaowan Wang

entry.summary: M3-Test is a coverage audit for VQA robustness showing that models passing all single-modality perturbation tests can still fail badly under joint image-plus-question perturbations. Across 2.6 million responses from four vision-language models, 26-29% of Qwen questions passing all 40 single-modality tests failed under joint changes, revealing that standard robustness averaging hides critical vulnerabilities.

entry.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations

author.name: Alexey Ignatiev, Peter J. Stuckey, Joao Marques-Silva

entry.summary: This paper connects two strands of explainable AI: closest-world counterfactual conditionals and the feature-based abductive/contrastive explanations used in formal XAI. It characterizes closest-world counterfactual explanations as a disjunctive normal form over minimally distant counterexamples and introduces conjunctive counterfactual explanations that guarantee prediction changes while retaining efficient computation and hitting-set duality with abductive explanations.

entry.title: SpecSearch: Towards Hardware-Aware Efficient Speculative Decoding

author.name: Selin Yildirim, Ali Zeyrek, Deming Chen

entry.summary: SpecSearch is a hardware-aware search engine that jointly optimizes speculative decoding strategy, draft length, and precision across workload-GPU pairs using an analytical cost model of memory and compute constraints. It shows that SOTA drafters like DFlash can vary from 3.50x to 0.76x autoregressive throughput depending on concurrency and output length, motivating configuration search per deployment.

entry.title: Efficient Wide-Beam Generative Retrieval with Model-Native Trie Decoding and Shared-Context Attention

author.name: Vedant Jhaveri, Arashpreet Singh Mor, Satyam Kumar, Alex Tsun, Qing Lan, Shaunak Mishra, Sriram Vasudevan

entry.summary: This paper addresses the serving costs of trie-constrained beam search in generative retrieval, where models predict catalog entries as short semantic identifiers. The authors introduce Trie-Head, a model-native output interface that stores the identifier trie as validated GPU tensors, avoiding Python constraint callbacks and vocabulary-wide candidate buffers, and pair it with a shared-context attention mechanism to eliminate repeated attention over the same prompt. This yields substantially lower CPU-GPU coordination and memory traffic while preserving exact valid-token scores, making wide-beam generative retrieval more practical for production-scale catalog search.

entry.title: PACD: Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding for Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations in Omnimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Chang Sun, Yijun Tian, Zhenwei Tang, Yuchen Deng, Yifan Simon Liu, Chenxu Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: PACD is a training-free decoding framework that reduces cross-modal hallucinations in omnimodal LLMs handling audio, video, and text. Unlike prior perturbation or relevance-weighting methods, which can suppress correct unimodal predictions or let shared errors persist, PACD tracks the provenance of predictions across modalities and uses two complementary paths to build a more reliable consensus at decoding time.

entry.title: RehearsalBench: Can AI Predict What Happens When You Change a Company?

author.name: Mika Siddiqui, Tharaka Perera

entry.summary: RehearsalBench evaluates whether AI models can diagnose an organization's operations, select interventions, and forecast their consequences, using a simulated bank contact center fitted to real call-level records. Model plans are scored in dollars against stakeholders' valuations and played out across 200 seeded futures, providing a rigorous test of managerial forecasting ability.

entry.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback

author.name: Gennadii Savrasov, Artem Slavin, Soslan Kabisov, Andrey Kuznetsov, Anton Konushin, Dmitrii Zhemchuzhnikov

entry.summary: MillBill separates machining decision-making from geometric execution: a locally hosted mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters, while a geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. This verifier-in-the-loop design avoids making numerical execution part of the model's task and respects physical cutter reach constraints.

entry.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training

author.name: Zhengfeng Yu, Tian Lan, Zhijing Wu, Enbo Zhao, Xuannan Liu, Feihu Jiang, Qianghuai Jia, Longyue Wang, Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo, Xian-Ling Mao

entry.summary: CrossEnv is a framework for synthesizing executable, verifiable agent tasks that span multiple environments, using an entity-tool graph to identify connections between services and align task-specific data for consistency. This addresses the gap where existing synthetic environments only generate within-environment tasks, missing real-world cross-service interactions. It matters for scalable training of long-horizon agents with verifiable feedback.

entry.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation

author.name: Ambroise Aigueperse, Hugo Buurmeijer, Carmen Amo ALonso, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: This paper elevates token commitment policy in masked diffusion models — previously a fixed decoding detail — to an explicit control surface, separating which tokens to commit from how many to commit per step. It introduces counterfactual target-aware commitment (ranking positions by confidence plus leave-one-token-out target contribution) and calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress. This offers a diffusion-specific alternative to activation/logit steering with potential for controllable generation.

entry.title: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict

author.name: Musfiqur Rahman, Mahi Begoug, Emad Shihab

entry.summary: Revisiting whether AI-agent code survives longer than human code after merging, the authors vary nine measurement choices across 854,139 lines from 2,802 pull requests in 215 repositories, building a specification curve of 88 survival analyses. The study shows that conflicting prior verdicts largely stem from defensible-but-different measurement choices, a caution for empirical AI-assisted software engineering research.

entry.title: Does the Model Use What It Cites? Counterfactual Tests of Grounded Reasoning Chains in Small Video-Language Models

author.name: Jugal Gajjar, Kamalasankari Subramaniakuppusamy

entry.summary: The paper proposes an annotation-free counterfactual test, the cite gap, which blacks out regions a video-language model cited in its reasoning chain and compares answer flips against masking equal-size control regions. Applied to 2-3B parameter models, it finds the cited regions matter on CLEVRER (cite gap 0.089) but barely on NExT-QA (0.003), showing chains often look grounded without being causal.

entry.title: FM-Mamba: An Efficient Native 2D Selective State Space Model with Stability-Aware Discretization

author.name: Shengyuan Hu, Yiyong Sun, Weihang Shan, Yongzhe Chang

entry.summary: FM-Mamba proposes a native two-dimensional selective state space model built on the Fornasini-Marchesini framework, avoiding the flattening of 2D feature maps into 1D sequences that plagues prior Mamba-based vision approaches. Its coupled recurrence evolves along both spatial axes with input-dependent, stability-aware step sizes, addressing both computational overhead and theoretical grounding issues in existing 2D state space recurrences. This is a substantive architectural contribution with potential relevance to efficient vision backbones.

entry.title: OfficePrism: Benchmarking Agents on Single-Domain Operations Across Enterprise Business Functions

author.name: Hanfeng Liu, Zhenyu Luo, Dongchao Zhang, Zexi Liu, Zulong Chen, Jinxin Hu, Jia Xu, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: OfficePrism is a benchmark of 420 single-domain enterprise tasks across seven business functions with shared L1-L3 task-structure levels, evaluating agents in fresh environments combining a synthetic organization with function-specific state. It uses grounded records, business rules, and tool schemas to construct Chinese-language tickets with hidden executable witnesses for verification. The design isolates within-function competence from cross-function coordination costs.

entry.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering

author.name: Yoonho Choi, Taehyeon Han, Seonghyeon Lee

entry.summary: Identifies over-exploration, a phenomenon where LLM coding agents keep invoking tools after sufficient information has already been gathered, and shows that SFT on expert trajectories propagates this inefficiency. JET is a fine-tuning method that truncates training trajectories at the point of sufficiency to teach agents to answer as soon as enough evidence exists. This directly improves cost-efficiency of repository-level QA agents.

entry.title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Tianci Xie, Li Chen, Pinxue Guo, Rui Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces NexSight, a set of verifiable tasks for both evaluating and training agentic models that search long videos for brief evidence moments (counts, event orderings, state changes). It addresses the problem that answer-only supervision does not train evidence search and that sparse evidence cannot verify timeline-wide claims.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Vincenzo Marcian\`o, Xiaoming Zhang, Michela Antonelli, Sebastien Ourselin, Maria A Zuluaga

entry.summary: GRACE is a retrieval-augmented refiner that corrects errors in medical image segmentation masks using context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. Unlike prior work requiring a separate trained corrector per anatomy, it is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, vessels, and tumors, and generalizes to held-out datasets querying a fixed knowledge base. This reduces the engineering burden of deploying segmentation correction in clinical workflows.

entry.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics

author.name: Xingyang Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces StringQFT, an 18-volume, 3,795-page textbook collection on string constructions of quantum field theory, designed both as a physics reference and as infrastructure for AI-assisted research. It includes an open-book benchmark with 1,073 items (499 automatically checkable), retrieval-augmented generation resources with 1,371 section records and a local lexical retriever, training-data examples, and 19 agent-facing calculation tools. It matters because it provides a rare, high-quality domain-specific resource connecting frontier AI methods (RAG, agents, fine-tuning) with advanced theoretical physics.

entry.title: A Log-Timescale Perturbation Bound for Selective State Space Models at Every Sequence Length

author.name: Jack Humphries, Daniel Midgley

entry.summary: This work derives a perturbation bound for selective state space models like Mamba that holds at arbitrary sequence lengths, addressing streaming deployments that far exceed training lengths. By measuring timescale changes on a log scale, the per-step decay factor moves by at most a fixed fraction of each step's input weight, preventing error accumulation and yielding a bound that stays stable across all lengths.

entry.title: TempQuant: Learning Adaptive Temperatures for Quantized Language Models

author.name: Mukund Athmaram, Liang Ma, Manoj Rao

entry.summary: TempQuant studies how quantization distorts next-token probability distributions in LLMs, finding that quantization effectively warps the output distribution and makes decoding temperature far more consequential than at full precision. The authors propose learning per-model sampling temperatures to compensate for quantization-induced distortion, improving low-precision deployment quality at negligible cost.

entry.title: Physically Admissible Generative Flow Matching for Sparse Flow Reconstruction

author.name: Yuhao Wang, Yuanxi Peng

entry.summary: This paper introduces Feasible Subspace Consistency, a framework that enforces discrete conservation laws as invariants of the entire generative trajectory in flow matching, rather than only at the output. Tangent-space matching confines ODE trajectories to the conservation manifold while mass-orthonormal coordinates preserve kinetic-energy geometry. It targets the ill-posed inverse problem of reconstructing fluid velocity fields from sparse observations with reliable uncertainty.

entry.title: Limite 1B - Violetto: Technical Report

author.name: Mario Prignano, Gabriele Cirillo, Alessio Morosini, Luca Cerovaz, Alessandro Bartolocci, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Giulio Starace, Francesco Pappone

entry.summary: This technical report describes a 1B-parameter model trained from scratch on 237B mathematics-focused tokens with 131k context, using distillation, SFT, and RLVR post-training. It reports 94.01% on AIME 2026 and 74.25% on BeyondAIME, competing with far larger models, positioned as a specialized math-reasoning component rather than a general assistant.

entry.title: RISA: Recoverable Sparse Attention for Block-Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xinrui Zhong, Fanjiang Ye, Yuke Wang

entry.summary: Presents RISA, a recoverable sparse-attention method for block-wise diffusion language models whose long-context inference is bottlenecked by repeatedly reading a growing KV cache at every denoising step. RISA uses shared read plans exploiting the fact that historical KV entries remain fixed, addressing query-divergent page selection and eviction-related information loss.

entry.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration

author.name: Ting-Hsuan Chen, Siheng Zhao, Han Jiang, Qi Pan, Louison Lu, Jiaheng Luo, Henghui Bao, Yiyu Chen, Quan Nguyen, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation combining a multi-agent post-training method adapted from a humanoid foundation tracking model, a vision-language planner, and speech-based leader-follower coordination. The system enables physically coupled whole-body collaboration from local observations alone.

entry.title: Efficient Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Yury Lysogorskiy, Anton Bochkarev, Ralf Drautz

entry.summary: A systematic review of machine learning interatomic potentials organized around efficiency, representing classical potentials and modern MLIPs, including equivariant transformers, within a common Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) and its graph generalization GRACE. The unified framing clarifies the sources of apparent diversity and cost-accuracy trade-offs across the field.

entry.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution

author.name: S. M Seefat Alam

entry.summary: Audits methods that localize social bias in LLMs to individual attention heads and remove it via ablation, showing on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct that the head-selection statistic is not a valid bias measure. Although the head map correlates strongly with a label-blind response-length map, an intervention breaking length-label coupling shows prompt identity, not length, explains most of the statistic's variance. A cautionary result about validation-by-fairness-metric in interpretability-driven debiasing.

entry.title: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Order Party Positions They Cannot Place

author.name: Yousef Attia, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: Shows that language models can reliably order political party positions on issues without being able to place them on an anchored magnitude scale, reflecting that training text contains more comparisons than measurements. The paper argues this dissociation undermines single-entity prompting benchmarks used to measure such domain knowledge.

entry.title: Bad Apples in the Kitchen: How LLM Teams Detect, Correct, and Calibrate Against Their Misaligned Members

author.name: Dongseok Heo, Junghwan Kim, Bongwon Suh

entry.summary: Studies how LLM teams cope with a misaligned teammate in real-time embodied cooperation by injecting three theory-grounded misaligned agents into a four-player Overcooked environment, covering speech-action mismatch, role invasion, and aggregate-progress disruption. Robustness is decomposed into detection, correction, and calibration gates in a factorial design.

entry.title: MM-ReportBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Report Generation from Tables

author.name: Teng Lin, Nan Tang

entry.summary: Introduces MM-ReportBench, a benchmark of 386 tasks over 185 real-world tables requiring models to generate reports that combine narrative text with faithful visualizations, with expert-curated references and verifiable key insight points. It addresses gaps in prior benchmarks including single-modality focus and weak visualization-quality metrics.

entry.title: Sketch, Don't Paint: Allocating Test-Time Compute in Generative Visual Reasoning

author.name: Sheng Lu, Guangpin Tao, Tong Lu, Ying Tai

entry.summary: This work studies how to allocate test-time compute in multimodal models that reason by generating visual thoughts, varying both when to render a visual thought and how many diffusion denoising steps each requires. It finds that causal, plan-carrying thoughts become legible early, so an 8-step sketch nearly matches a 50-step photorealistic render in accuracy and plan commitment. This offers large efficiency gains for interleaved visual chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: HandRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Hand Pose Estimation

author.name: Zhekai Wang, Luqing Luo, Wenhao Yao, Junjie Lu, Huanan Zhu, Feifei Gao, Yuhua Jiang

entry.summary: HandRSI applies a recursive self-improvement loop to 3D hand pose estimation, where coding agents iteratively refine an executable inference harness and accept changes only when they improve a composite of ten benchmark metrics on held-out data. The improved harness then drives selective distillation to improve the underlying video estimator.

entry.title: Can Vision-Language Models Truly Understand Images? A Benchmark Beyond Commonsense Bias

author.name: Ling Lin, Heng Su, Xiangzeng Liu, Yang Bai, Congcong Zhu, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ContraSense, a benchmark designed to test whether multimodal LLMs genuinely understand image content or merely exploit commonsense and co-occurrence priors. By constructing counterintuitive samples that violate typical statistical correlations, it exposes reliance on dataset shortcuts rather than faithful visual grounding.

entry.title: Must You See Fakes to Catch Fakes? Language Says What to Look For, Real Images What to Ignore

author.name: Tianchi Xu, Yuxuan Zhou, Yuheng Zhang, Yanan Guan, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: Proposes training AI-generated image detectors without any generated images, using vision foundation models plus language guidance to specify what artifacts to look for and real-image statistics to suppress spurious authenticity cues. This sidesteps the generator-specific overfitting and format-confounding problems inherent to fake-trained detectors.

entry.title: Beyond the Camera: A Tri-Modal Driving World Model for Future RGB, Thermal, and LiDAR Forecasting in Adverse Weather

author.name: Faysal Mehrab Chowdhury, Md. Mahfuzur Rahman, Ahmed Rafi Hasan, Kishor Datta Gupta, Mohd Ariful Haque, Savannah Shannon

entry.summary: The authors build a driving world model that jointly forecasts future RGB, thermal, and LiDAR observations on real adverse-weather sequences, reportedly the first to cover all three sensor modalities. They post-train a pretrained video world model per sensor, represent LiDAR as aligned depth video, and evaluate LiDAR prediction in physical meters against measured returns.

entry.title: Impact of Pretraining Length, Model Size, and Annotation Budget on Downstream Clinical Tasks of Foundation Models in Radiotherapy

author.name: Alejandro Cortina Uribe, Sidsel H{\o}jklint Poulsen, Ivan Richter Vogelius, Jens Petersen

entry.summary: This study pretrains vision transformer encoders with masked image modeling on roughly 150,000 raw 3D radiotherapy CBCT scans, filling a gap since no large-scale pretrained models existed for this modality. It systematically examines how pretraining length, model size, and finetuning strategy relate to downstream clinical performance, and how pretraining-time metrics correlate with eventual task outcomes. This matters for medical foundation model design where downstream tasks are unknown in advance.

entry.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification

author.name: Jiarui Guo, Saining Zhang, Jiaying Wan, Jiawei Weng, Junhao Chen, Rui Zhang, Yuanbo Lyu, Zhiheng Lee, Peishuo Li, Jingrun Du, Weiqing Xiao, Weiyi Lin, Zenan Meng, Hu Wei, Lin Qu, Zongzheng Zhang, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li

entry.summary: RFW-S is a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified deformable object assets across 485 categories in five structural families, built via an automated pipeline combining reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter calibration. An independent simulation verification framework ensures physical reliability for robotic simulation.

entry.title: SE(3)-LIVOM: Adaptive Multi-LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry and Mapping

author.name: Gunhee Shin, Seungjae Lee, Daebeom Kim, Seoyeon Jang, Hyun Myung

entry.summary: An adaptive multi-sensor odometry and mapping system for legged robots, winner of the COMFORT Challenge at IROS 2026. It extends SE(3)-LIO to multiple LiDARs plus camera, uses adaptive downsampling and online backend optimization, and achieves 1.40 cm average trajectory error across challenging outdoor scenes with a single configuration.

entry.title: Tracing Feature Circuits

author.name: nuppal

entry.summary: This post outlines a mechanistic interpretability research direction using sparse dictionary learning and transcoders to decompose GPT-2 components into monosemantic features and trace feature-level circuits for specific behaviors. The goal is to replace native model components with interpretable autoencoder parts, enabling end-to-end circuit analysis.

entry.title: The Fragility of Reasoning-Importance Attribution for Pruning Language Models

author.name: Himanshu Mishra

entry.summary: The paper shows that attribution-guided pruning of reasoning LLMs rests on fragile importance measurement: final-answer-token scores saturate because the answer appears inside the chain of thought, and guiding head pruning with this target costs 27.6 and 32.2 accuracy points across four small reasoning models. The work identifies three distinct ways attribution measurements mislead pruning decisions.

entry.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents

author.name: Yicheng Tao, Yuante Li, Zipei Fan

entry.summary: ForecastGym is a benchmark for LLM forecasting agents that records what four commercial web search APIs return for open prediction-market questions over time, enabling controlled and replayable evaluation that separates retrieval effects from reasoning ability. It addresses contamination problems where live self-search mixes evidence with reasoning and retrospective search leaks future information via date filters or ranking. This enables fair comparison of models, search sources, and memory strategies.

entry.title: EmbedGym: Letting Coding Agents Develop and Debug Embedded Firmware Without Physical Hardware

author.name: Minghui Zhao, Yiming Li, Sophie Zhu, Maxwell Khor, Lauren Ouyang, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen, Tingjun Chen

entry.summary: EmbedGym is an interactive virtual hardware environment that lets coding agents develop and debug embedded firmware without physical boards, using instruction-level MCU emulation to close the execution loop that embedded development otherwise breaks. It captures hardware-observable failure modes like pin polarity, bus protocol, and timing bugs that text-terminal agents cannot detect.

entry.title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jia Hu, Yang Chang, Panqu Wang, Zhijun Fu, Chang Liu, Changjian Yu, Jintao Lai

entry.summary: Presents a closed-loop interactive world model for autonomous driving that couples behavior modeling with visual rendering: imitation-learned background-vehicle policies are fine-tuned with multi-agent reinforcement learning in closed loop against an end-to-end ego planner reacting to rendered images, so interaction behaviors match real logs. The viewpoints exposed by these interactions then feed the rendering, ensuring behavioral realism and visual fidelity together. This enables training and evaluating driving systems in unseen interactions beyond logged data.

entry.title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation

author.name: Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Weihang Guo, Chen Wei, Lydia E Kavraki, Niloofar Mireshghallah, Steven Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Hierarchical Diffusion Transformers (HiT), which progressively group tokens into coarser representations to close the gap between plain pixel-space diffusion Transformers and two-stage latent diffusion models. The hierarchy encourages visual summarization at multiple scales within a single end-to-end training stage.

entry.title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels

author.name: Kushagra Bainsla

entry.summary: This single-author engineering paper exploits a structural property of Gemma 4 31B global attention layers, where the value is the normalized key projection and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, to store one 640-value row instead of a full key and value per token. An unmodified paged attention kernel reads the compact cache through two overlapping strided views, achieving bit-identical outputs in a vLLM prototype with the 16-bit 31B model. This realizes the KV cache savings the Gemma 4 report claimed but open serving engines did not yet deliver.

entry.title: Understanding Cross-Modal Inconsistency through Representation Subspaces in Omni Models

author.name: Seonghyeon Cho, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: Analyzes why omni models give different answers to semantically equivalent inputs across audio, vision, and text, estimating a low-dimensional Answer Subspace to separate answer-related components from the rest of the representation. Information predictive of cross-modal inconsistency concentrates in a reproducible two-dimensional subspace outside it.

entry.title: PhyVGGT: Feed-Forward Articulated Object Reconstruction from Monocular Videos

author.name: Qi Shao, Zhihao Cao, Shuhao Zhai, Anh Nguyen, Hong Liang, Baoru Huang, Liang Li

entry.summary: PhyVGGT reconstructs articulated objects — including movable parts, joint parameters, and unseen articulation states — from uncalibrated monocular video in a single feed-forward pass, addressing failures of direct joint regression on casual videos such as blurred part boundaries and ill-conditioned continuous axes. It targets robot manipulation and interactive digital twins.

entry.title: Plausible Videos Can Lead to Poor Decisions: Diagnosing and CURE-ing World Models for Planning

author.name: Raphael C. Kim, Michele Santacatterina, Jingsen Zhu, Ramin Zabih

entry.summary: Argues that world models producing plausible, realistic videos can still induce poor planning decisions, and introduces CURE, a certificate-guided procedure that decides whether a world model can be trusted and otherwise upweights training data, rolls out more samples, or explores where data support is missing.

entry.title: Beyond Co-Generation: Rethinking Jointness in Joint Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Jihoo Jung, Ji-Hoon Kim, Suyeon Lee, Gia Thinh Pham, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: This work introduces intrinsic jointness, the ability of audio and video in text-to-audio-video generation to agree on details left underspecified by the prompt, to distinguish genuine cross-modal coordination from independent text following. Evaluating four recent T2AV models with underspecified prompts reveals their limited intrinsic jointness.

entry.title: From Human Videos to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Data: Confidence-Guided RL Refinement of Video Priors

author.name: Yanghong Liu, Yang Chen, Kailang Xu, Bang Du, Feiyang Yang, Jiawei Xia, Zhengtao Yao, Yubiao Zhang, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Ruihai Wu, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: PriDex converts human-video priors into executable bimanual dexterous manipulation demonstrations via RL in simulation, preserving task-relevant interaction structure while regenerating embodiment-specific behavior. It uses affordance cues from human-object interactions for grasp selection and confidence-guided refinement to handle uncertainty in video-derived motion estimates.

entry.title: VoxelSBFL: Voxel-Level Spectrum-Based Failure Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Arusa Kanwal, Pablo Valle, Paola Roggero, Miren Illarramendi, Shaukat Ali, Aitor Arrieta

entry.summary: VoxelSBFL adapts spectrum-based fault localization from software testing to robotics by treating workspace voxels as program elements, using recorded tool-center-point trajectories to identify regions associated with higher failure likelihood for VLA policies. This supports prediction of failures in subsequent executions and informs policy repair.

entry.title: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents

author.name: Arjun Sivaraman, Zhaoheng Li, Alan Shi, Sanjay Malisetty, Eugene Wu, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: Readie addresses slow startup in code sandboxes used by AI agents through learned startup snapshots that predict which artifacts (packages, datasets) agent-generated code will need. Rather than one compact snapshot, it composes learned snapshots to cover diverse workloads while keeping startup latency low, decoupling agent harnesses from execution infrastructure.

entry.title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses

author.name: Deep Shah, Nehal Kathrotia

entry.summary: The paper presents a unifying architectural and design framework for self-improving agent harnesses — runtime systems that manage context, memory, multi-turn control, sandboxed tool execution, and verification, and that inspect their own traces to distinguish runtime bugs from model limits and rewrite their own code. It frames the shift from static prompt tuning to self-improving runtime software as a key driver of agent capability.

entry.title: HealthCLBench:Evaluating Context Learning in Health Conversations through Controlled Case Clusters

author.name: Ting Yang, Zijing Hong, Chengjie Wang, Peng Wei, Chunxiao Guo, Yun Yue, Xurui Li, Jinqun Guan, Zixiao Chen, Ant Group

entry.summary: HealthCLBench is a Chinese-language medical benchmark for evaluating in-context learning in health conversations, testing how fixed-parameter models acquire, integrate, and apply context when facts, evidence, or task goals change. The benchmark comprises 328 controlled case clusters, 1,103 cases, and 4,931 rubric criteria covering medical consultation and everyday health management, with member-specific medical criteria and controlled contextual difficulty. It enables systematic, open-ended assessment of contextual robustness that prior Chinese medical benchmarks lacked.

entry.title: A Full-Ledger Counterfactual Audit of Adaptive Reasoning

author.name: Xiaopeng Chu, Wenzheng Kong, Wei Liu, Wenyi Zhang

entry.summary: FLCVA audits adaptive reasoning by comparing an immediate answer with fixed-length continuations from the same frozen prefix, accounting for the cost of every signal a policy uses. On GSM8K and MATH-500, random 256-token continuations recover wrong answers in 26.6% (Qwen3-8B) and 18.9% (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) of cases while rarely damaging correct ones. This challenges the assumption that predicting answer incorrectness justifies more compute, since improvement depends on whether reasoning will actually help.

entry.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents

author.name: Viet K. Nguyen, Mohammad I. Husain

entry.summary: ATI proposes a framework-independent security architecture for autonomous AI agents operating across organizational boundaries, built on PKI, Zero Trust Architecture, and remote attestation. It establishes federated trust via peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs) rather than a shared root authority, validating agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization before requests execute. This addresses a real gap as multi-organization agent ecosystems emerge.

entry.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign

author.name: James Sadler, Rotimi Alabi, Kotub Uddin

entry.summary: EJBench tests whether models can exercise engineering judgment: predicting how a battery cold plate design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier simulation results and deciding what to conclude without running software. Its three task families use ground truth from converged conjugate heat transfer simulations rather than LLM judges, and frontier models reportedly perform poorly.

entry.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor

author.name: Timo Oksanen

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates weight-space programming, where LLMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1/5.2 (established models by the coverage date) directly edit the 253 weights of a small neural controller that steers a real research tractor, without gradient descent. LLMs successfully repaired a controller transferred across tractors and wrote one from zero weights, competing with evolution strategies and gradient descent under a small simulation budget.

entry.title: From Perception to Simulation: Unveiling and Empowering Mental Spatial Dynamics in MLLMs

author.name: Jiachun Li, Zhuoran Jin, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces MentalGrid, a benchmark requiring multimodal LLMs to simulate evolving spatial states without intermediate visual feedback, moving beyond static spatial relation perception. Extensive evaluation reveals significant deficiencies, with performance limited by perceptual bottlenecks in simple scenarios and multi-step reasoning failures in harder ones. This probes a key gap between perception and internal world simulation in current MLLMs.

entry.title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops

author.name: Eleftherios Triantafyllidis, Filippos Christianos, Zhibin Li, Bernd Bickel

entry.summary: Formalizes automated reward discovery in partially observable, sparse-reward, long-horizon settings where goals and dynamics must be discovered through interaction. WATERFALL is an iterative population-based workflow that relaxes the goal-conditioning, demonstrations, and ground-truth metric assumptions of prior foundation-model reward design approaches.

entry.title: Regularized Score Centering

author.name: Hao Bai, Chenlu Ye, Xuanchang Zhang, Aviral Kumar, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Addressing instability in asynchronous reinforcement learning for LLMs, the paper introduces Regularized Score Centering, which adds a reverse KL penalty to keep the learner's next-token distribution close to the behavior policy's, limiting policy mismatch that causes score centering to fail. Gradient diagnostics show score centering produces less extreme gradients than importance sampling, and RSC extends its stability range. The method works with off-policy data from stale policies in asynchronous RL training.

entry.title: BernBRS: Certified Backward Reachability for Deep Bernstein Neural Networks

author.name: Ibrahim Albool, Yasser Shoukry

entry.summary: BernBRS is a scalable framework for backward reachability analysis of DeepBern-Nets, neural networks with Bernstein polynomial activations that already enjoy fast forward reachability. The method simultaneously computes certified inner and outer approximations of the backward reachable set, identifying safe initial states for neural network-controlled systems.

entry.title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction

author.name: Aamod Varma, Shuyi Jia, Victor Fung

entry.summary: This paper tackles a key bottleneck in diffusion-based pretraining for materials property prediction: the dependence on DFT-relaxed structures near potential energy surface minima. The authors generate synthetic crystal structures for pretraining, removing the need for expensive quantum-mechanical relaxation and expanding the scale and diversity of pretraining data in crystal structure space.

entry.title: Lost in the Funnel: Selection-Induced Miscalibration in Ranking and Decision Systems

author.name: Aditya Somani, Rahul Ragesh, Vikas Joshi, Amit Singh

entry.summary: The paper studies how calibration of model scores degrades as they pass through multi-component decision funnels involving filtering, reranking, business rules, and auctions, where calibration is typically validated only at the score-producing boundary. It offers a boundary-wise diagnostic framework based on residual identities to distinguish inherited error from selection effects. This exposes a routinely overlooked failure mode in production ranking systems.

entry.title: Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering

author.name: Khiem Le, Ting Hua, Nitesh V. Chawla

entry.summary: The paper addresses a failure mode of GRPO where questions exceeding model capability yield zero reward and no gradient signal. Existing hint-augmented GRPO methods create a training-inference context mismatch because hints are unavailable at test time; the authors propose using activation steering to inject hint information internally, avoiding the mismatch.

entry.title: RTLReviewBench: LLM Hardware Reviewers Rarely Miss Bugs but Routinely Reject Correct RTL

author.name: Yasir Mahmud

entry.summary: This benchmark comprises 114 simulation-verified pairs of buggy and correct Verilog modules, mostly real LLM code-generator failures. Across 12 models, LLM reviewers show a strong asymmetry: they rarely accept buggy code but frequently reject correct code, with over five false rejections per missed bug, and synthetic mutants mask the problem.

entry.title: Symmetries of Counterfactuals: Identification and Testability of Counterfactual Maps from Covariate Heterogeneity

author.name: Marc Braun, Adel Daoud, Jose M. Pe\~na

entry.summary: Studies what observational data can reveal about counterfactual maps when covariates influence outcomes only through a latent cause. The authors characterize all data-consistent counterfactual maps, showing they differ from the true map by symmetry groups that preserve conditional outcome distributions, and derive testability conditions. This clarifies fundamental identification limits that are usually assumed away in counterfactual estimation methods.

entry.title: AfriNORM: An Evaluation Benchmark for Normative Reasoning of LLMs Across African Cultures

author.name: Ahmad Samuel Gali (Independent Researcher), Tadesse Destaw Belay (Instituto Polit\'ecnico Nacional), Idris Abdulmumin (University of Pretoria), Seid Muhie Yimam (University of Hamburg), Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad (Bayero University Kano, Imperial College London)

entry.summary: Introduces AfriNORM, a scenario-based multiple-choice benchmark measuring LLM normative reasoning about African deontic modality — strict norms and taboos governing social interactions — across diverse African sociocultural contexts. It proposes metrics including a universal competence measure to diagnose where models fall short beyond linguistic fluency.

entry.title: Can Decision Models Replace LLMs in Real-World Contact Center Classification and Judging Tasks?

author.name: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Xue-Yong Fu, Shashi Bhushan TN

entry.summary: Compares nine decision models against thirteen generative LLMs in zero-shot settings across eight real contact center use cases, including intent classification, knowledge-base retrieval, compliance assessment, and LLM judging. The study assesses whether typed-output decision models are a cost-effective alternative to generative models for bounded tasks.

entry.title: Surfacing Disagreement Beats Resolving It: A Gated Ablation Study of Provenance-Weighted Memory for Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Ziaullah Khan, Abdul Rehman Khalid, Shrestha Nischal Lal, Nheng Vanchhay, Md Ariful Islam Mozumder, Hee-Cheol Kim

entry.summary: DebateGraph studies shared memory for multi-agent debate through a controlled ablation of five memory mechanisms under a fixed budget, finding that the single mechanism that survives is preserving contradictions and passing ranked conflict sets to the debate rather than collapsing them to a winner. This improves F1 by +0.340 and reduces attack success on poisoned items from 22 to 7 of 122 at equal cost. The result suggests multi-agent systems benefit from surfacing disagreement rather than eagerly resolving it.

entry.title: ARG-Avatar: Animation-Rendering Guidance for Efficient Feedforward Avatar Reconstruction

author.name: Jianjin Xu, Soham Dasgupta, Fernando De la Torre

entry.summary: ARG-Avatar reconstructs animatable 3D human avatars from images in seconds using only 68M trainable parameters while achieving state-of-the-art quality. The key insight is that 3D animation and rendering already provide geometric correspondences that other methods wastefully learn from data, encoded via a foreground avatar coordinate RoPE attention design.

entry.title: Inertial Video World Models

author.name: Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Yu Guo, Yuxu Lu, Zhengru Fang, Hao Wu, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: InertialWorld introduces an inertial prior into autoregressive video world models, carrying existing scene evidence forward through an Inertial Memory mechanism instead of reconstructing scenes at every step. This addresses error accumulation and destabilized dynamics during long autoregressive rollouts.

entry.title: CoBoVLA: Decoupling Language from Action with Discrete Codes for Robust and Interpretable Robot Manipulation

author.name: Mehul Arora, Dhruv Agarwal, Ambuj Agrawal

entry.summary: Shows that existing vision-language-action models suffer large performance drops (22-52 points on LIBERO-Para) when instructions are paraphrased, and proposes CoBoVLA, a compact 250M-parameter VLA that decouples language understanding, planning, and control using learned discrete interpretable codes. The design improves robustness to rephrasing and makes failure diagnosis easier.

entry.title: Lost in Read-out: Locating the Image Quality Gap in Vision-Language Models with a Closed-Form Edit

author.name: Zhuangzi Li, Shilv Cai, Jian Jin, Zhiyi Pan, Haihong Xiao, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: Shows that VLMs used as zero-shot image quality assessors encode quality linearly and decodably deep into the network, and that the gap with human opinion lies mainly in the final read-out, which over-rewards colorfulness and under-rewards sharpness. A closed-form edit of a single last-layer neuron, fitted from about a hundred labels, largely recovers human-aligned quality judgments across five VLMs.

entry.title: Visual Harness Scales General VLMs to Medical Images

author.name: Shaowen Wan, Hanqi Jiang, Zihao Wu, Junhao Chen, Weihang You, Ruiyu Yan, Bowen Chen, Tianming Liu, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces a medical visual harness that lets general vision-language models interactively explore medical images using tools, maintain lossless diagnostic-evidence memory, and iteratively revise answers based on assessments of omissions and finding reliability. This substantially improves general VLM performance across diverse medical imaging tasks without specialized medical pretraining.

entry.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Nguyen Quang Trung, Hoang Phan, Shuo Sun, Longyin Zhang, AiTi Aw

entry.summary: M3OPD-Reasoner is a fully open recipe for post-training vision-language models across image STEM, image perception, and video reasoning, using multi-teacher on-policy distillation. The authors release two datasets (1.35M SFT and 193K RL with verifiable rewards) and compare mixed-data training against per-domain teachers distilled into a single student starting from Qwen3.5-9B, using Group Sequence Policy Optimization. This provides a reproducible open baseline for multimodal reasoning post-training.

entry.title: TetherMark: Instance-Level Watermark Authentication Against Cross-Instance Transplantation

author.name: Jin Wei, Rundong Li, Li Ma, Yikai Wang, Ruihao Yang, Jianxiong Wu, Xiaoyuan Duan, Yanbo Wang, Runyu Mao, Chen Fang, Chang Xu, Ping Chen, Jun Dai, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: TetherMark exposes a new attack on image watermarks, cross-instance transplantation, where an attacker moves valid watermark evidence from a registered image onto a different image of the same category, fooling decodability and content-consistency checks. It proposes instance-level watermark authentication to bind evidence to the specific registered visual instance.

entry.title: ALERT: Extending Humanoid Motion Trackers with a General and Lightweight Human Avoidance Pipeline

author.name: Zhaoyang Li, Chiyu Zhang, Chengxin Xu, Peng Yang, Zhonghao Guo, Wanting Li, Ziyu Chen
